They freely maintain personal relationships with any third party, whether related or not. They have the right to be visited and, where applicable, accommodated by them.

In case of difficulty, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance rules.

###### Article 599

The marriage of a person under curatorship is permitted only with the authorization of the curator or, failing that, that of the judge.
The marriage of a person under guardianship is permitted only with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the President of the Court of First Instance, and after hearing of the future spouses by the judge.

The opinion of the parents and entourage is possibly obtained by the judge.

###### Article 600

At the opening of the measure or, failing that, subsequently, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance decides on the conditions under which the curator or guardian responsible for a mission of protection of the person accounts for the diligence they perform in this capacity.

###### Sous-section 5 : Of the regularity of acts Article 601

The obligations resulting from acts performed by the protected person less than two years before the publication of the judgment opening the protection measure may be reduced on the sole proof that their inability to defend their interests, as a result of the alteration of their personal faculties, was notorious or known to the contracting party at the time the acts were executed.

These acts may, under the same conditions, be annulled if it is proven that the protected person suffered prejudice.
By way of derogation from article 2387, the action must be brought within five years from the date of the judgment opening the measure.

###### Article 602

From the publication of the opening judgment, irregularities in acts performed by the protected person or by the person responsible for the protection are sanctioned under the following conditions:
1° If the protected person has performed alone an act that they could do without the assistance or representation of the person responsible for their protection, the act remains subject to the actions for nullity or reduction provided for in Article 574 as if it had been performed by a person placed under safeguard of justice, unless it has been expressly authorized by the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance.
2° If the protected person has performed alone an act for which they should have been assisted, the act may only be annulled if it is established that the protected person has suffered harm;
3° If the protected person has performed alone an act for which they should have been represented, the act is null and void by operation of law without it being necessary to prove harm;
4° If the guardian or curator has performed alone an act that should have been done by the protected person either alone or with their assistance or that could only be performed with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance, the act is null and void by operation of law without it being necessary to prove harm.
The curator or guardian may, with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance, bring alone the action for nullity or reduction of the acts provided for in 1°, 2° and 3°.
In all cases, the action is extinguished by the period of five years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling them to exercise it.
During this period and as long as the protection measure is open, the act provided for in 4° may be confirmed with the authorization of the judge or the family council if it has been constituted.

###### Article 603

Articles 601 and 602 do not preclude the application of Articles 554 and 555.

###### Sous-section 6 : Des actes faits dans la curatelle Article 604

The person under curatorship may not, without the assistance of the curator, perform any act which, in the case of guardianship, would have required authorization from the judge or the family council.

When concluding a written act, the assistance of the curator is manifested by the affixing of their signature next to that of the protected person. If the latter does not know how to sign, the act bears their fingerprint.
On pain of nullity, any service of process made on the protected person must also be made on the curator.

###### Article 605

Capital due to the person under curatorship is paid directly into an account opened in their name alone and indicating their protection regime, with an establishment authorized to receive funds from the public.
The person under curatorship may not, without the assistance of the curator, use their capital. This assistance is also required to bring legal action or defend in it.

###### Article 606

The curator may not substitute themselves for the person under curatorship to act in their name.

However, the curator may, if they find that the person under curatorship is seriously compromising their interests, refer the matter to the judge to be authorized to perform alone a specific act or to initiate the opening of guardianship.
If the curator refuses their assistance for an act for which their cooperation is required, the person under curatorship may ask the judge for authorization to perform it alone.

###### Article 607

The person under curatorship may freely make a will subject to the provisions of Article 554. They may only make a donation with the assistance of the curator.
The curator is deemed to be in conflict of interest with the protected person when they are the beneficiary of the donation.

###### Article 608

At any time, the judge may, by way of derogation from Article 604, enumerate certain acts that the person under curatorship has the capacity to perform alone or, conversely, add other acts to those for which the assistance of the curator is required.

###### Article 609

The judge may also, at any time, order a reinforced curatorship. In this case, the curator alone receives the income of the person under curatorship in an account opened in the name of the latter. They themselves ensure the settlement of expenses with third parties and deposit the surplus in an account left at the disposal of the person concerned or pay it into their hands.
Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 598, the judge may authorize the curator to conclude alone a residential lease or an accommodation agreement ensuring the housing of the protected person.
Reinforced curatorship is subject to the provisions of Articles 630 and 639 to 644.

###### Sous-section 7 : Des actes faits dans la tutelle Article 610

Subject to cases where the law or custom authorizes the person under guardianship to act themselves, the guardian represents them in all acts of civil life.

However, the judge may, in the opening judgment or subsequently, enumerate certain acts that the person under guardianship will have the capacity to perform alone or with the assistance of the guardian.

###### Article 611

The person under guardianship is represented in acts necessary for the management of their patrimony under the conditions and according to the procedures provided for in Title XIII.

###### Article 612

The person under guardianship is represented in court by the guardian.

The guardian may not act, as plaintiff or defendant, to assert the extra-patrimonial rights of the protected person except after authorization or upon injunction of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance.
The judge or the family council may also enjoin the guardian to withdraw from the proceedings or action or to settle.

###### Article 613

The person under guardianship may, with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance, be assisted or if necessary represented by the guardian to make donations.
They may only make their will alone after the opening of the guardianship with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance, this on pain of nullity of the act. The guardian may neither assist nor represent them on this occasion.
However, they may alone revoke the will made before or after the opening of the guardianship.

The will made prior to the opening of the guardianship remains valid unless it is established that, since this opening, the cause that had determined the testator to dispose has disappeared.

##### Section V : De l'habilitation familiale Article 614

When a person is unable to express their will for one of the causes provided for in Article 565, the judge may authorize one or more persons chosen from among their ascendants or descendants, brothers and sisters or, unless the community of life has ceased between them, the spouse or cohabitant to represent them or to perform one or more acts in their name under the conditions and according to the procedures provided for in this section and those of Title XV of Book III of this code.
The authorized person must meet the conditions for exercising guardianship duties. They exercise their mission free of charge.

###### Article 615

Family authorization may only be ordered by the judge in case of necessity and when the interests of the person cannot be sufficiently provided for by the application of either the rules of common law of representation, or those relating to the respective rights and duties of spouses and the rules of matrimonial regimes, or by another less restrictive judicial protection measure.

###### Article 616

The application for the designation of an authorized person may be submitted to the judge by one of the persons mentioned in Article 614 or by the public prosecutor at the request of one of them.

The application is filed, examined and adjudicated in accordance with the rules of the Code of Civil Procedure and in compliance with the provisions of Articles 569 and 571.

###### Article 617

The person in respect of whom authorization is requested is heard or summoned according to the procedures provided for in the first paragraph of Article 572. However, the judge may, by specially reasoned decision and on the advice of the doctor mentioned in Article 571, decide that there is no need to proceed with their hearing if it is likely to harm their health or if the person is unable to express themselves.
The judge ensures the consent or, failing that, the absence of legitimate opposition to the authorization measure and to the choice of the authorized person from the relatives mentioned in Article 614 who maintain close and stable ties with the person or who show interest in them and whose existence is known to the judge at the time of ruling.

###### Article 618

The judge rules on the choice of the authorized person and the scope of the authorization by ensuring that the proposed arrangement is in accordance with the patrimonial and, where applicable, personal interests of the person concerned.

###### Article 619

The authorization may cover:
1° one or more of the acts that the guardian has the power to perform, alone or with authorization, on the property of the person concerned;
2° one or more acts relating to the person to be protected. In this case, the authorization is exercised in compliance with the provisions of Articles 595 to 598 of this Code.

The authorized person may perform an act of disposition by gratuitous title only with the authorization of the judge.
If the interest of the person to be protected so requires, the judge may issue a general authorization covering all acts or one of the two categories of acts mentioned in points 1° and 2° of this article.

###### Article 620

The authorized person may, unless the judge decides otherwise, proceed without authorization to the acts mentioned in the first paragraph of Article 567.

###### Article 621

If the person in respect of whom authorization has been issued performs alone an act whose performance has been entrusted to the authorized person, it is null and void by operation of law without the need to prove prejudice.
Obligations arising from acts performed by a person in respect of whom a family authorization measure was pronounced less than two years before the judgment issuing the authorization may be reduced or annulled under the conditions provided for in Article 601.
The authorized person may, with the authorization of the judge, bring alone the action for nullity or reduction provided for in the above paragraphs.
If the authorized person performs alone, in that capacity, an act not falling within the scope of the authorization issued to them or which could only be performed with the authorization of the judge, the act is null and void by operation of law without the need to prove prejudice.

In all cases, the action for nullity or reduction is exercised within five years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling them to exercise it. During

this period and as long as the authorization measure is in effect, the contested act may be confirmed with the authorization of the judge.

###### Article 622

The judge rules at the request of one of the persons mentioned in Article 614 or of the public prosecutor on difficulties that may arise in the implementation of the arrangement.
Seized for this purpose under the conditions provided for in the first paragraph of Article 616, the judge may, at any time, modify the scope of the authorization or terminate it, after having heard or summoned, on the one hand, the person in respect of whom the authorization has been issued, under the conditions provided for in the first paragraph of Article 617 and, on the other hand, the authorized person.

###### Article 623

In addition to the death of the person in respect of whom the family authorization has been issued, this family authorization terminates:
1° By the placement of the person concerned under safeguard of justice, under curatorship or under guardianship;
2° In case of a judgment of discharge having become res judicata pronounced by the judge at the request of one of the persons mentioned in Article 614 or of the public prosecutor, when it appears that the conditions provided for in that article are no longer met or when the execution of the family authorization is likely to harm the interests of the protected person;
3° By operation of law in the absence of renewal upon expiration of the fixed period;
4° After the performance of the acts for which the authorization had been issued.

### Titre XIII

Management of the patrimony of minors and adults under guardianship Chapter I: Procedures for management

###### Article 624

The guardian represents the protected person in acts necessary for the management of their patrimony.
They are required to exercise prudent, diligent and informed care in such management, solely in the interest of the protected person.

The list of acts that are regarded, for the application of this title, as acts of administration relating to the current management of the patrimony and as acts of disposition that commit it in a lasting and substantial manner is fixed by decree.

###### Article 625

Capital accruing to the protected person is paid directly into an account opened in their name alone and mentioning the guardianship measure, with a bank or any other organization that may legally receive funds from the public.

###### Article 626

Third parties may inform the judge of acts or omissions by the guardian that appear to them likely to harm the interests of the protected person. In this title, each time the judge is mentioned, it refers to the President of the Court of First Instance or the magistrate they have designated.
These third parties are not guarantors of the use of capital. However, if in connection with such use they become aware of acts or omissions that manifestly compromise the interest of the protected person, they notify the judge.

Third-party opposition against authorizations of the family council or of the judge may only be exercised by creditors of the protected person and in case of fraud against their rights.

##### Section unique: Decisions of the family council or of the judge Article 627

The guardian establishes the budget of the guardianship by determining, according to the importance of the property of the protected person and the operations involved in their management, the sums annually necessary for the maintenance of the person and for the reimbursement of the costs of administration of their property. The guardian informs the family council or, failing that, the judge. In case of difficulties, the budget is established by the family council or, failing that, by the judge.

The family council or, failing that, the judge may authorize the guardian to include in the management costs the remuneration of special administrators whose assistance they request under their own responsibility.
The family council or, failing that, the judge may authorize the guardian to conclude a contract for the management of securities and financial instruments of the protected person. They choose the contracting third party in consideration of their professional experience and solvency. The contract may, at any time and notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, be terminated on behalf of the protected person.

###### Article 628

The family council or, failing that, the judge determines the amount from which the obligation to invest liquid capital and excess income begins for the guardian.
The family council or, failing that, the judge prescribes all measures it deems useful regarding the investment or reinvestment of funds either in advance or on the occasion of each transaction. The investment or reinvestment is carried out by the guardian within the time limit set by the decision ordering it and in the manner it prescribes. After this time limit, the guardian may be declared debtor of the interest.

The family council or, failing that, the judge may order that certain funds be deposited in an unavailable account.

###### Article 629

The family council or, failing that, the judge rules on the authorizations that the guardian requests for acts that he cannot perform alone.

###### § 1. Acts that the guardian performs without authorization Article 630

Within three months of the opening of the guardianship, the guardian has an inventory of the property of the protected person prepared and transmits it to the judge. He ensures its updating during the measure.

He may obtain communication of all information and documents necessary for the establishment of the inventory from any public or private person, without professional secrecy or banking secrecy ever being invoked against him.
If the inventory has not been established or proves to be incomplete or inaccurate, the protected person and, after his death, his heirs may prove the value and initial composition of his property by any means.

###### Article 631

The guardian performs alone conservatory acts and, subject to the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 608, acts of administration necessary for the management of the protected person's patrimony.

He acts alone in court to assert the patrimonial rights of the protected person.
Leases granted by the guardian confer on the lessee, against the protected person who has become capable, no right of renewal and no right to remain in the premises at the expiration of the lease, even if there exist contrary legal provisions. These provisions are not, however, applicable to leases granted before the opening of the guardianship and renewed by the guardian.

###### § 2. Acts that the guardian performs with authorization Article 632

The guardian may not, without being authorized by the family council or, failing that, the judge, perform acts of disposition in the name of the protected person.
The authorization that may be given to him by the family council or, failing that, the judge, determines the stipulations and, where applicable, the price or reserve price for which the act may be executed. Authorization is not required in case of forced sale by judicial decision or in case of amicable sale upon authorization of the judge.

###### Article 633

The guardian may not settle or submit to arbitration in the name of the protected person except after having had the clauses of the settlement or arbitration agreement and, where applicable, the arbitration clause approved by the family council or, failing that, by the judge.

###### Article 634

Partition with respect to a protected person may be made amicably upon authorization of the family council or, failing that, of the judge, who designates, if necessary, a notary to proceed with it. It may be only partial.
The liquidation statement is submitted to the approval of the family council or, failing that, of the judge.

Partition may also be made in court in accordance with Articles 981 and 998. Any other partition is considered provisional.

###### Article 635

By way of derogation from Article 881, the guardian may accept a succession that has fallen to the protected person only subject to inventory. However, the family council or, failing that, the judge may, by a deliberation or decision, authorize him to accept purely and simply if the assets manifestly exceed the liabilities.
The guardian may not renounce a succession that has fallen to the protected person without authorization from the family council or, failing that, the judge.

###### Article 636

In the case where the succession that was renounced in the name of the protected person has not been accepted by another heir and as long as the State has not been sent into possession, the renunciation may be revoked, either by the guardian authorized for this purpose by a new deliberation of the family council or, failing that, a new decision of the judge, or by the protected person who has become capable.
This revocation, like the renunciation, has retroactive effect to the day of the opening of the succession, without however calling into question the rights that may be acquired by third parties over the property of the succession by prescription or by acts validly made with the curator of the vacant succession.

###### Article 637

On an exceptional basis and in the interest of the protected person, the guardian may, upon authorization of the family council or, failing that, of the judge, purchase the property of the latter or take it on lease.
For the conclusion of the act, the guardian is deemed to be in conflict of interest with the protected person.

###### § 3. Acts that the guardian may not perform Article 638

The guardian may not, even with authorization:
1° Perform acts that entail a gratuitous alienation of the property or rights of the protected person except what is said regarding donations, such as the remission of debt, the gratuitous renunciation of an acquired right, the advance renunciation of the action for reduction referred to in Articles 1085 and 1086, the release of mortgage or security without payment or the gratuitous constitution of an easement or security to guarantee the debt of a third party;
2° Acquire from a third party a right or claim that the latter holds against the protected person; 3° Engage in commerce or a liberal profession in the name of the protected person;
4° Purchase the property of the protected person as well as take it on lease, subject to the provisions of Article 637;
5° Transfer into a fiduciary patrimony the property or rights of a protected adult.

#### Chapitre II

Establishment, verification and approval of accounts Article 639
The guardian establishes each year an account of his management to which are annexed all useful supporting documents.

For this purpose, he requests from the institutions with which one or more accounts are opened in the name of the protected person an annual statement thereof, without professional secrecy or banking secrecy ever being invoked against him.
The guardian is required to ensure the confidentiality of the management account. However, a copy of the account and supporting documents is provided each year by the guardian to the protected person when he is at least sixteen years of age and, if the guardian deems it useful, to other persons responsible for the protection of the person concerned.

In addition, the judge may, after having heard the protected person and obtained his agreement, if he has reached the aforementioned age and if his condition permits, authorize the spouse, a relative, a relative by marriage of the latter or one of his close relations, if they justify a legitimate interest, to have the guardian communicate to them at their expense a copy of the account and supporting documents or a part of these documents.

###### Article 640

The tutor submits each year the management account, accompanied by supporting documents, for verification, to the Chief Registrar of the Court of First Instance.
For the verification of the account, the Chief Registrar of the Court of First Instance may make use of the right of communication provided for in the second paragraph of Article 639. He may be assisted in his mission of auditing the accounts under the conditions set by the code of civil procedure.

If he refuses to approve the account, the Chief Registrar of the Court of First Instance draws up a report of the difficulties encountered which he transmits to the judge. The latter rules on the conformity of the account.

The judge may decide that the mission of verification and approval of accounts devolved to the Chief Registrar of the Court of First Instance shall be exercised by a certified public accountant registered on the list of judicial experts.

When Article 594 is applied, the judge may decide that the family council shall verify and approve the accounts in place of the Chief Registrar of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 641

The judge may, by way of derogation from Articles 639 and 640 and in consideration of the modest nature of the income and assets of the protected person, exempt the tutor from preparing the management account and from submitting it to the approval of the Chief Registrar of the Court of First Instance director of judicial registry services.

###### Article 642

If the resources of the protected person permit and if the importance and composition of his assets justify it, the judge may decide, in consideration of the patrimonial interest at stake, that the mission of verification and approval of the management account shall be exercised, at the expense of the interested party and according to the procedures he sets, by a technician.

###### Article 643

When his mission ends for any reason whatsoever, the tutor prepares a management account of the operations that have occurred since the preparation of the last annual account and submits it to the verification and approval provided for in Articles 640 and 642.
In addition, within three months following the end of his mission, the tutor or his heirs if he has died deliver a copy of the last five management accounts and of the account mentioned in the first paragraph of this article, as the case may be, to the person who has become capable if he has not already been a recipient thereof, to the person newly charged with the management measure or to the heirs of the protected person.

The preceding paragraphs are not applicable in the case provided for in Article 641.

In all cases, the tutor delivers to the persons mentioned in the second paragraph of this article the documents necessary to continue the management or ensure the liquidation of the estate, as well as the initial inventory and the updates to which it has given rise.

#### Chapitre III : De la prescription Article 644

The action for rendering of accounts, for revendication or for payment brought by the protected person or person who has been protected or by his heirs relating to the facts of the tutorship is prescribed after five years from the end of the measure, even though the management may have continued beyond.

### Titre XIV : Des mesures de protection des victimes de violences

###### Article 645

When violence exercised within the couple or by a former spouse, or a former cohabitant endangers the person who is the victim thereof, one or more children, the judge may issue urgently to the latter a protection order.
In this title, each time mention is made of the judge, it refers to the President of the Court of First Instance or the magistrate he has designated.

###### Article 646

The protection order is issued by the judge, seized by the person in danger, if necessary assisted, or, with the agreement of the latter, by the public prosecutor.
Upon receipt of the application for a protection order, the judge summons, by all appropriate means, for a hearing, the applicant party and the respondent party, assisted, where appropriate, by a lawyer, as well as the public prosecutor. These hearings may take place separately. They must be held in chambers.

###### Article 647

The protection order is issued, as soon as possible, by the judge, if he considers, in view of the elements produced before him and debated in adversarial proceedings, that there are serious reasons to consider as plausible the commission of the alleged acts of violence and the danger to which the victim or one or more children are exposed. On the occasion of its issuance, the judge has jurisdiction to:
1° Prohibit the respondent party from receiving or meeting certain persons as well as from entering into contact with them, in any manner whatsoever;
2° Prohibit the respondent party from holding or carrying a weapon and, where appropriate, order him to surrender to the police or gendarmerie service he designates the weapons of which he is the holder with a view to their deposit at the registry;
3° Rule on the separate residence of the spouses by specifying which of the two will continue to reside in the marital home and on the procedures for covering the costs relating to this dwelling. Except in special circumstances, the enjoyment of this dwelling is attributed to the spouse who is not the perpetrator of the violence, even if he has benefited from emergency accommodation;
4° Specify which of the cohabitants will continue to reside in the common dwelling and rule on the procedures for covering the costs relating to this dwelling. Except in special circumstances, the enjoyment of this dwelling is attributed to the cohabitant who is not the perpetrator of the violence, even if he has benefited from emergency accommodation;
5° Rule on the procedures for exercising parental authority and, where appropriate, on the contribution to the charges of the marriage and on the contribution to the maintenance and education of the children;
6° Authorize the applicant party to conceal his domicile or residence and to elect domicile with the lawyer who assists or represents him or with the public prosecutor for all civil proceedings in which he is also a party. If, for the purposes of executing a judicial decision, the bailiff charged with this execution must have knowledge of the address of this person, it is communicated to him, without his being able to reveal it to his principal;

When the judge issues a protection order by reason of violence likely to endanger one or more children, he informs the public prosecutor without delay.

###### Article 648

The measures mentioned in Article 647 are ordered for a maximum duration of six months from the notification of the order. They may be extended beyond if, during this period, a petition for divorce or for legal separation has been filed or if the judge has been seized with a petition relating to the exercise of parental authority.
The judge may, at any time, at the request of the public prosecutor or of either party, or after having caused any useful investigative measure to be carried out, and after having invited each of them to express themselves, remove or modify all or part of the measures set out in the protection order, decide on new ones, grant the respondent party a temporary exemption from observing certain of the obligations that have been imposed on him or revoke the protection order.

###### Article 649

A protection order may also be issued urgently by the judge to the adult person threatened with forced marriage, under the conditions set in Article 646.

The judge has jurisdiction to take the measures mentioned in 1°, 2° and 6° of Article 647.

## BOOK II. - ON PROPERTY, AND THE DIFFERENT MODIFICATIONS OF OWNERSHIP

###### Article 650

The property of public persons is governed by the codes and laws that concern them and, in the absence of specific provisions, by the common law of property as established by this Book.

### Title I: On patrimony and the property that composes it

Subtitle I: Patrimony Article 651
Patrimony is the universality of law comprising all the property of a person, both movable and immovable, present and future, the entirety of the assets answering for the entirety of the liabilities.
Every natural or legal person holds a patrimony. Except where otherwise provided by law, a person may have only one patrimony.

###### Article 652

Property within the meaning of the preceding article means corporeal or incorporeal things that are the object of appropriation by the holder of the patrimony in question, as well as real and personal rights that are his.

###### Article 653

A real right is one that confers on its holder a direct power over property.

The holder of a real right may exercise his power over the thing in whatever hands it may be found. When it is accessory to a claim whose payment it guarantees, it confers, in addition to the right of pursuit, a right of preference over the property.

###### Article 654

A personal right is one held by the creditor of an obligation against his debtor.
Subtitle II. On the distinction of property Article 655
All property is movable or immovable.

###### Article 656

Subject to the laws that protect them, animals are subject to the legal regime of corporeal things.

###### Article 657

Except where the law provides otherwise:

-	a consumable thing is a thing that is consumed when one uses it. It cannot be used without being destroyed at first use or without leaving the patrimony of its owner;

-	a non-fungible thing or specific thing consists of a determined and individualized thing; a fungible thing or generic thing is determined only by its species and quantity;

-	when a thing gives or produces fruits periodically, it is fruit-bearing. Fruits are what a property generates, periodically or not, spontaneously or through its development, without its substance being in any way altered. They may be natural, when they come spontaneously from the land or from animals; industrial, when they are obtained through cultivation or breeding; or civil, such as rents from leases, interest on sums due, and arrears of annuities. Civil fruits are also called revenues. Products affect the very matter of the property, which is diminished when it is exploited.

Chapter I: On immovables Article 658
Corporeal property is immovable, either by its nature or by its destination. Incorporeal property is immovable by the object to which it applies.

###### Article 659

Immovable by nature are land, buildings and vegetation found thereon, as well as all other things incorporated therein, as long as the connection with the soil is thus maintained.
Pipes used to conduct water in a house or any other immovable by nature to which they are attached are immovable and form part of the land to which they are joined.

Co-ownership units are also immovable.
Houses known as plank houses are movable property, except when the State sells to its owner the land on which it is built. In that case, a land title may be established and the whole consisting of the land and the house then becomes immovable property subject to registration.

###### Article 660

Immovables by destination are a legal fiction by which the law treats as immovable a movable property. A movable is immovable by destination when two cumulative conditions are met: 1° The two properties must be owned by the same person;
2° A relationship of destination must exist between the movable and the immovable to which it is attached. This relationship of destination results either from the assignment of the movable to the operation of an immovable by nature, or from the attachment of the movable property to the immovable property by nature in perpetuity.

###### Article 661

The assignment of the movable to the operation of an immovable by nature may result from the agricultural operation of land, such as animals attached to cultivation as long as they remain attached to the land by the effect of an agreement; from the industrial operation of land, such as equipment of an industrial building used for the activity; from the commercial operation of land, such as furniture used for the operation of an immovable for hotel purposes; or from the civil operation of an immovable, such as equipment elements that allow the use of an apartment rented by its owner.

###### Article 662

The attachment of a movable to an immovable by nature in perpetuity resides in the material process of attachment implemented by the owner. This process externalizes the owner's intention to attach the movable to the immovable.
Presumed irrefutably to be attached to the immovable are movables that have been fixed thereto by means of plaster, lime or cement, or any other mode of attachment that would prevent the movables from being

detached without being broken or damaged, or without breaking or damaging the part of the land to which they are attached.

Presumed, unless proven otherwise, to be attached to the immovable are movables that have been specially designed or adapted to be integrated into the immovable by nature, or for which the owner has made a modification to the immovable in order to receive them, such as a niche made expressly to receive a statue, even if it can be removed without breakage or damage.

In other cases, the owner must establish that he intended to attach the movable in perpetuity to the immovable by nature.

###### Article 663

The owner of an immovable by destination may always terminate the relationship of destination, by his sole will, subject to the rights of third parties.

###### Article 664

Immovable by the object to which they apply are:
1° Immovable real rights:
a)	ownership of immovable property;
b)	usufruct of the same property;
c)	rights of use and habitation;
d)	emphyteusis;
e)	right of superficies;
f)	easements and land services;
g)	antichresis;
h)	privileges and mortgages.
2° Actions that tend to claim an immovable.

###### Article 665

The real rights enumerated in the preceding article are preserved and produce effect with regard to third parties only insofar as they have been made public in the forms, conditions and limits regulated in this code, without prejudice to the rights of the parties for the performance of their agreements.
By way of derogation from the rule of the preceding paragraph, creditors and legatees who request the separation of the patrimony of a deceased person retain, with regard to his heirs and representatives, to exercise their privilege over hereditary immovables, the benefit of the period of six months from the opening of the succession, notwithstanding any alienation by said heirs or representatives.

#### Chapter II: On movables Article 666

Property is movable by its nature or by determination of law.
Movable by nature are all corporeal things other than those referred to in articles 659 and 660.

Movable by determination of law are all rights other than those referred to in article 664.

###### Article 667

The word movable property, used alone in the provisions of the law or in a legal act, without any other addition or designation, does not include cash, precious stones, debts receivable, books, medals, instruments of the sciences, arts and trades, body linen, weapons, grains, wines, hay and other commodities; it also does not include what is the object of a trade.

###### Article 668

The words movable furnishings include only movable property intended for the use and ornamentation of apartments, such as beds, seats, mirrors, clocks, tables, porcelain and other objects of this nature.
The sale or gift of a furnished house includes only movable furnishings. Likewise, the sale or gift of a house, with everything found therein, does not include cash, nor debts receivable and other rights whose titles may be deposited in the house; all other movable effects are included therein.

###### Article 669

Subject to the rights of third parties, property that is currently immovable but which is intended, by the effect of the will of the contracting parties, to become movable property shortly and in the perspective of performance of the agreement, is considered as movable property. Thus: crops sold standing, products to be extracted from quarries or mines, materials to come from the demolition of a building.

### Titre II : De la propriété, de la possession et de la détention

###### Article 670

Real rights not subject to publicity, subject to the provisions relating to legal acts, are proved by all means.
In case of conflict, when no sufficiently probative title is produced, it is for the judge of the revendication claim to identify the best and most characteristic presumptions of ownership, and he retains the most likely right after having analyzed all the circumstances to decide between the litigants. If he does not succeed in doing so, the possessor in place is awarded the ownership.

For immovable property, the conflict between several persons invoking titles emanating from a common author is resolved according to the rules of land registration.

Chapitre Ier : La propriété Article 671
Ownership is the exclusive right to enjoy and dispose of things and rights.

It confers upon its holder an absolute power, subject to the laws and regulations that govern it. This power may not be used for the purpose of harming others, failing which it constitutes an abuse of right.

###### Article 672

No one may be compelled to transfer his ownership, except for reasons of public utility, and in return for just and prior compensation.

###### Article 673

The ownership of a thing, whether movable or immovable, extends to the fruits and products of the thing.

The fruits produced by the thing belong to the owner of the thing, however, only subject to reimbursement of the costs of ploughing, work and seeds done by third parties and whose value is estimated at the date of reimbursement.

The ownership of the thing also extends to everything that is united to it accessorily either naturally or artificially. This right is called the right of accession.

###### Article 674

Ownership is not lost by non-use.

The action for revendication, subject to contrary provision of the law, is perpetual.

###### Article 675

By way of derogation from the preceding articles, when the owner victim of a minor encroachment on his land does not bring an action for revendication within two years after having become aware of the encroachment, or within the limit of 10 years from the completion of the works, the author of the constructions and other works may request, if he is in good faith and if the circumstances permit, that the encroachment be attributed to him as a real right against payment of fair compensation.
The owner victim of the encroachment may, within the time limits stated above, request at his choice, either the demolition of what has been done in violation of his right, or the payment of fair compensation.

The encroachment is minor when it is less than 0.20 meters.
The compensation is fixed amicably by the owners concerned who establish an authentic act of their agreement and, failing that, determined by the judge who takes into account the value of the land occupied, the added value brought to the land of the author of the encroachment, and the harm that he has caused to the owner of the land victim of the encroachment.

###### Article 676

The ownership of a treasure belongs to the person who finds it in his own land, by virtue of the right of accession; if the treasure is found in the land of another, it belongs for half to the person who discovered it, by occupation, and for the other half to the owner of the land, by accession.
The treasure is any thing hidden or buried on which no one can justify his ownership, and which is discovered by pure chance.

###### Article 677

The rights over effects thrown into the sea, over objects that the sea casts up, of whatever nature they may be, over plants and herbage that grow on the shores of the sea, are regulated by special laws.
The same applies to lost things whose owner does not come forward.

###### Article 678

The public domain includes all property of all kinds, immovable or movable, classified or delimited in the public domain, whether or not allocated to public use. The public domain of the State is determined by a special law.
The public domain of the State comprises, on the one hand, natural sites determined by law, such as: the seashore, up to the limit of the highest tides, as well as a zone of 50 meters from this limit; islands and islets; springs as well as non-navigable and non-floatable watercourses within the limits determined by the height of the highest waters flowing at full bank before overflowing, as well as a passage zone of 25 meters wide from these limits on each bank; lakes, ponds and lagoons within the limits determined by the level of the highest waters before overflow, with a passage zone of 25 meters wide from these limits on each outer bank; underground water tables, whatever their origin, nature and depth and, on the other hand, developments and works carried out for reasons of general interest or public utility, as well as the land that supports them, determined by law or having been the subject of a classification procedure, such as: irrigation or drainage canals, aqueducts, boreholes, dams and hillside reservoirs, cemented wells, as well as the dependencies of these works, when they are executed for a purpose of public utility; railways, roads and communication routes of all kinds, ports and roadsteads, sea dikes, semaphores, lighting or beaconing works, as well as their dependencies; telegraph and telephone lines, radio stations and other telecommunications installations, as well as their dependencies; works declared of public utility for the use of hydraulic forces and the transport of electrical energy.
More generally, the public domain of the State comprises property of all kinds that Djiboutian laws declare not susceptible to private ownership.

Property that does not belong to private individuals is administered and may be alienated only in the forms and according to the rules that are specific to them.

###### Article 679

All immovable property that has no owner, and that of persons who die without heirs or whose estates are abandoned, belong to the State.
Movable property without an owner belongs to the first person who appropriates it, subject to special provisions.


This excerpt sits under: RÉPUBLIQUE DE DJIBOUTI > LIVRE II. - DES BIENS, ET DES DIFFERENTES MODIFICATIONS DE LA PROPRIETE > Titre I : Du patrimoine et des biens qui le composent > Chapitre II : Des meubles Article 666

###### Article 680

There are things that belong to no one and whose use is common to all. Police laws regulate the manner of enjoying them.
The right to hunt or fish is also regulated by special laws.

#### Chapitre II

Of possession and detention Section I: Possession

###### Article 681

Possession is the fact of exercising, with the intention of being the holder thereof, a right over a thing. It is immaterial whether the possessor is or is not the true holder of the right exercised. Possession exists only if it is public, unequivocal and peaceful. In case of violence, useful possession begins only from the day the violence ceased. It is protected, without regard to the merits of the right, against disturbance that affects it or threatens it.
However, there is no immovable possession except in the presence of a title regularly published according to the laws governing immovables.

Possession of incorporeal movables is governed by the special laws that govern them.

Payment made in good faith to the person who is in possession of the claim is valid, even if the possessor is subsequently evicted.

###### Article 682

Acts of mere faculty and those of simple tolerance cannot establish either possession or prescription.

###### Article 683

The possessor is in good faith when he possesses as the holder of the right he exercises would, by virtue of a title transferring ownership whose defects he is unaware of.
Good faith is always presumed, and it is for the person alleging bad faith to prove it. It is assessed on the day of entry into possession, unless otherwise provided.

He ceases to be in good faith from the moment these defects become known to him.

###### Article 684

One may possess by oneself or through another.

###### Article 685

Possession is proved by all means.

One is always presumed to possess for oneself, and as owner, unless it is proved that one began to possess for another.
When one has begun to possess for another, one is always presumed to possess under the same title, unless there is proof to the contrary.

###### Article 686

In the case of movables, possession in good faith instantly confers title.

It is otherwise when the person who has lost or from whom the thing was stolen intends to claim it: that person has three years, from the day of the loss or theft, to take action against the possessor. If the possessor has purchased the claimed thing in a normal circuit of commercialization of goods and services, the claimant must pay the possessor the price the thing cost him; otherwise, he shall obtain the property without having to reimburse the price to the possessor. The claimant who had to pay a price to the possessor, or the possessor who had to return the thing without obtaining reimbursement of its price, may take action for that amount against the person from whom the possessor obtained the thing, up to the finder or thief thereof.
When the possessor is in bad faith, the claimed right is acquired only after thirty years. When the period is reached, the right arises from the day possession began.

In case of an action for revendication concerning the property he possesses, the possessor shall be defendant in the action brought. The plaintiff may reverse the presumptions favorable to the possessor, by all means.

###### Article 687

The current possessor of a movable who proves having possessed it formerly is presumed to have possessed it in the intervening time, unless proved otherwise.

###### Article 688

One may always join to one's possession that of one's predecessor.

###### Article 689

The possessor in bad faith, in addition to the obligation to return the thing, owes to the owner who claims it, the interest, the fruits he has received in kind or their value estimated at the date of payment. The possessor in good faith owes them only from the day of the demand.
Every possessor has however the right to reimbursement of necessary and useful expenses for the conservation of the property within the limit of the added value provided.

###### Article 690

Articles 2401 and following are applicable during possession.

##### Section II: Detention

###### Article 691

When the person who holds a property knows that this property is subject to a real right of which he is not the holder, he is a mere detainer. Such is the case of the contractor to whom an object has been entrusted for repair, or of the usufructuary who holds the thing of the bare owner.
Detention is precarious and entails the obligation to return the thing to the holder of the real right that relates to it under the conditions of the juridical act that gave rise to it.

###### Article 692

Article 685 third paragraph is applicable to the detainer.

Possessory protection is granted to the detainer against anyone other than the person from whom he derives his rights.

##### Section III: Protection of possession and detention Article 693

Possession is protected against disturbance that affects it or threatens it.

Likewise, the detainer is protected from disturbance he suffers in the exercise of his right, from any person other than the one from whom he derives his rights.

#### Chapitre III: Of the right of accession

##### Section I: Of the right of accession in relation to immovable things Article 694

Ownership of the soil carries with it ownership of what is above and below.
Everything that is united and incorporated into the thing belongs to the owner thereof.

###### Article 695

The owner may make above all plantations and constructions, within the limits imposed by laws, regulations and juridical acts, and below, all constructions and excavations he deems appropriate, and draw from these excavations all the products they can provide, subject to modifications resulting from laws and regulations relating to mines, and laws and police regulations.

###### Article 696

All constructions, plantations and works on land or in the interior are presumed made by the owner at his expense and to belong to him, unless the contrary is proved.
The owner of the soil who has made constructions, plantations and works with materials that did not belong to him must pay their value estimated at the date of payment; he may also be ordered to pay damages, if appropriate. But the owner of the materials does not have the right to remove them.

###### Article 697

When the plantations, constructions and works have been made by a possessor in good faith and with materials belonging to him, the owner of the land must compensate the latter for the lower value of the two sums that represents, at the date of payment, the added value provided to the land or the cost of materials and labor, taking into account the state in which said constructions,

plantations and works are found. The possessor then benefits from a right of retention until complete payment of the sum due.

When the plantations, constructions and works have been made by a possessor in bad faith and with materials belonging to him, the owner of the land has the right, either to retain ownership thereof according to the conditions of the preceding paragraph, or to oblige the third party to remove them.
If the owner of the land requires the removal of the constructions, plantations and works, it is carried out at the expense of the third party, without any compensation for him; the third party may, in addition, be ordered to pay damages for any harm suffered by the owner of the land.

When the plantations, constructions and works have been made by a detainer, their fate is governed by the title that is at the origin of the possession. In the absence thereof, only the plantations, constructions and works made in the sight and knowledge of the owner fall under the application of the first paragraph above.

###### Article 698

The movement of rivers or wadis that modifies riparian land benefits the riparian properties. The riparian owner on the opposite side cannot complain when he has, on his side, lost land as a result, except when a sudden force has carried away a considerable and recognizable part of riparian land, and it remains identified at the place where it has been carried; in this case, the owner of the removed part may claim his property, provided he acts within one year of the event.

##### Section II: Of the right of accession in relation to movable property Article 699

The right of accession, when it relates to two movable things belonging to two different owners, is entirely subordinated to the principles of natural equity.

The following rules shall serve as an example to the judge in making his determination, according to the particular circumstances.

###### Article 700

There are three types of movable incorporation.

Adjunction, which is the act of uniting one movable object to another movable object for a purpose of use, ornamentation or completion of the first. Such is the case of property used to personalize cars or motorcycles.
Specification, which is the act of a person using material that does not belong to him and creating a new object from it. Such is the case of a person who takes pieces of wood and makes a table from them.

Mixture, which is the act of forming a thing by the union of several materials such that the resulting material can no longer be separated. Such is the case when two metals are mixed.

###### Article 701

In case of adjunction, the newly created property reverts in its entirety to the person whose thing was the most important in value and, failing that, in volume, regardless of whether the two things would be separable from each other. In return, the other person shall receive compensation.
It is otherwise if the thing united to the other is much more valuable than the principal thing and the operation was carried out without the knowledge of its owner; the latter may request that the united thing be separated to be returned to him, even when some deterioration of the thing to which it has been joined might result.

###### Article 702

In case of specification, ownership of the new property reverts to the owner of the materials against remuneration for the work accomplished, except when the work clearly exceeds the value of the material used.

###### Article 703

In case of mixture, division of the separable materials may be requested by the owner without whose knowledge the mixture was made. Failing that, ownership shall be common to the persons concerned, in proportion to the quantities. But when there is a manifest disproportion of the mixed quantities, the accessory shall again follow the principal.

###### Article 704

In all cases where property has been used without the knowledge of its owner, the latter has the choice of requesting the restitution of his material in the same nature, quantity, weight, measure and quality, or its value estimated at the date of restitution.

#### Chapter IV: Of collective ownership

##### Section I: Ordinary co-ownership Article 705

Co-ownership is the situation in which several persons hold a real right of the same nature over the same property or the same mass of property. None of these persons may then claim an exclusive right over the property.

This right may be ownership or another real right.

###### Article 706

Co-ownership is governed by articles 933 and following (legal co-ownership) and 2071 and following (conventional co-ownership).

##### Section II: Co-ownership of built immovable property divided into lots Article 707

Co-ownership of built immovable property divided into lots is a combination of private ownership, on the one hand, and co-ownership, on the other hand. Ownership of the immovable property is divided into lots each comprising a private part, such as an apartment, and a share of the common parts of the immovable property.

Co-ownership of built immovable property divided into lots is governed by the texts that govern it.

### Title III

Of usufruct, use and habitation, special real rights, emphyteusis and the right of superficies

Chapter I: Of usufruct

##### Section I: General provisions Article 708

Usufruct is the real right to use and enjoy things of which another has ownership, as the owner himself, but subject to preserving their substance.

###### Article 709

Usufruct is established by law, or by the will of man.

###### Article 710

The will of the parties expressed in the constitutive act determines the starting point of the right of usufruct.

Usufruct is temporary and is extinguished in accordance with the provisions of Section IV below, which govern its duration.

###### Article 711

Usufruct may be established over any kind of property or set of properties, movable or immovable, corporeal or incorporeal.

##### Section II

Of the mutual obligations of the bare owner and the usufructuary Article 712
An inventory of the property subject to usufruct and of their condition is drawn up at the latest at the time the usufructuary enters into enjoyment. The latter may not enter into enjoyment until after having had the inventory drawn up, in the presence of the owner, or the owner having been duly summoned.
In case of disagreement between them, the inventory is carried out by an independent professional chosen by mutual agreement and, failing that, designated by the president of the civil chamber of the court of first instance, ruling by order on the merits.
The usufructuary takes the things in the state in which they are.

###### Article 713

The owner may not, by his act, nor in any manner whatsoever, harm the rights of the usufructuary.

###### Article 714

Unless otherwise agreed, the owner is liable for all major works and repairs, namely works relating to the structure and general solidity of the immovable property such as the repair of load-bearing walls, dikes, retaining walls and enclosures in their entirety, or the restoration of beams or roofs, also in their entirety.
All other repairs are maintenance repairs.

###### Article 715

Maintenance and conservation works, like other periodic expenses, are the responsibility of the usufructuary.
If major repairs are the responsibility of the owner, it is otherwise when they have been caused by the lack of maintenance repairs, since the opening of the usufruct. In this case, the usufructuary is liable for them. He is also liable for expenses made necessary by his abuse of enjoyment.
In case of judicial proceedings, the usufructuary is liable only for the costs of proceedings concerning the enjoyment, and other condemnations to which these proceedings might give rise.

###### Article 716

The usufructuary may not, upon cessation of the usufruct, claim any compensation for improvements he may have made, even though the value of the thing was increased thereby. In this case, he may however, or

his heirs, remove the improvements he has made to the property, but subject to restoring the premises to their original condition.

###### Article 717

When the obligations provided for by the preceding articles are not respected, the other party may seize the judge so that he may enjoin the person who is liable to carry out the necessary works and, failing that, authorize him to have them carried out, at the expense of the person who has responsibility for them.
He may also request from the judge authorization to create a security interest over the property, in order to guarantee, as the case may be, the financing of the works by the other, or the reimbursement of the sums expended.

###### Article 718

In the case of a usufruct with a simply determinable duration, the contract may provide that upon its termination, the owner may request from the usufructuary a contribution to the expenses he has covered for major works. This contribution is calculated according to the value of the usufruct in relation to what its actual duration has been.

###### Article 719

Neither the owner nor the usufructuary is required to rebuild what has fallen into decay or what has been destroyed by fortuitous event.

###### Article 720

With regard to charges that may be imposed on the property during the duration of the usufruct, the usufructuary and the owner contribute to them as follows:
The owner is obliged to pay them, and the usufructuary must account to him for the interest; If they are advanced by the usufructuary, he has the right to recover the capital at the end of the usufruct.

##### Section III : Des droits et obligations de l'usufruitier

###### § 1. Les droits de l'usufruitier Article 721

The usufructuary has the right to use and enjoy the property of which he has the usufruct.

The right of enjoyment covers every kind of fruits that the property concerned may produce.

###### Article 722

The usufructuary exercises his right, either by himself or by granting the use and enjoyment to another.

He may transfer his right, for consideration or gratuitously, or encumber it with real security interests. In this case, the right thus created terminates, at the latest, on the date provided for the transferred usufruct.

The usufructuary may not create any real right over the property other than rights of use and habitation.

The creation or renewal of leases subject to commercial or rural lease statutes, as well as those constituting a real right, may only be carried out with the owner's agreement. Other leases may be concluded by the usufructuary alone, but if they subsist upon termination of the usufruct, the owner is bound only for the current period and, except with his written agreement, for a maximum duration of six years for real property leases and three years for movable property leases.

###### Article 723

The usufructuary uses and enjoys all the rights that the owner may use and enjoy, and he uses and enjoys them as the owner himself.

###### Article 724

He also uses and enjoys, in the same manner as the owner, the products from the exploitation of the property subject to the usufruct; such is the case with mines and quarries that are in operation at the opening of the usufruct. Nevertheless, if it involves an operation that cannot be carried out without a concession, the usufructuary may only use and enjoy it after having obtained permission from the President of the Republic.
He has no right to mines and quarries not yet opened, nor to treasure that might be discovered during the duration of the usufruct.

###### Article 725

Unless otherwise agreed, natural and industrial fruits, hanging by branches or by roots at the time the usufruct opens, belong to the usufructuary.
Those that are ripe at the time the usufruct ends belong to the owner, without compensation on either side for ploughing and seeds.

###### Article 726

Unless otherwise agreed, income provided by the property, such as rents, interest and dividends whose distribution has been voted, accrues day by day.

###### § 2. Les obligations de l'usufruitier Article 727

The usufructuary uses and enjoys the property subject to the usufruct in a manner consistent with the property's intended purpose.

If, during the duration of the usufruct, a third party commits any encroachment on the land or otherwise infringes the owner's rights, the usufructuary is required to report it to him; failing which, he is liable for all damage that may result to the owner, as he would be for damage committed by himself.
Upon termination of the usufruct, he returns the property to its owner, subject to the provisions specific to special usufructs.

###### Article 728

If the usufruct is established only over an animal that perishes without fault of the usufructuary, the latter is not required to return another one or to pay its valuation.
If the herd over which a usufruct has been established perishes entirely by accident or by disease and without fault of the usufructuary, the latter is required towards the owner only to account for the hides, or their value estimated at the date of restitution. On the other hand, if the herd does not perish entirely, the usufructuary is required to replace, up to the amount of the increase, the heads of animals that have perished.

###### Article 729

The usufructuary must provide sufficient security for compliance with the obligations mentioned in the preceding article, unless he is exempted from it by law, the act creating the usufruct, or by the owner.
However, the following are exempted: fathers and mothers having the legal usufruct of their children's property, as well as the seller or donor with reservation of usufruct.

###### Article 730

If the usufructuary does not find security, the immovable properties are leased or placed under sequestration;

The sums included in the usufruct are invested;

The commodities are sold and the price resulting therefrom is similarly invested;
The interest on these sums and prices belongs, in this case, to the usufructuary.

###### Article 731

In the absence of security from the usufructuary, the owner may require that movables that deteriorate through use be sold, so that the price be invested like that of commodities.

###### Article 732

Delay in providing security does not deprive the usufructuary of the fruits to which he may be entitled; they are due to him from the moment the usufruct opened.

###### Article 733

The universal usufructuary or usufructuary by universal title and the owner are obliged to the succession liabilities in proportion to their respective value of the usufruct and the bare ownership. They contribute to them in the same proportions, unless otherwise agreed.

###### Article 734

The usufructuary by particular title is not liable for debts that burden the land.

###### Article 735

If the usufructuary does not comply with his obligations, either by committing damage to the land or by allowing it to deteriorate for lack of maintenance, the owner may apply to the court to have it pronounce forfeiture of the usufruct right.
The usufructuary's creditors may intervene in the proceedings for the preservation of their rights; they may propose to substitute themselves for him in the performance of his obligations and by providing all guarantees.
The judges may, depending on the seriousness of the circumstances, either pronounce the absolute termination of the usufruct, or order the owner's return to enjoyment of the object encumbered by it only on condition of paying annually to the usufructuary, or to his successors in title, a determined sum, until the time when the usufruct should have ceased.

##### Section IV : La durée de l'usufruit Article 736

The usufruct is created for the life of its holder.

It may also be created for a determined or determinable duration. In this case, whether the duration of the usufruct is determined or determinable, it may not exceed thirty years.

###### Article 737

The life usufruct terminates by the death of the usufructuary, a natural person, or the dissolution of the legal person when such a person holds the right. When the usufruct is created for the benefit of a legal person, it may never exceed thirty years.
The usufruct created for a determined duration or for a determinable duration terminates by the expiration of the time for which it was granted. When the usufruct has been granted until a third party has reached a fixed age, it lasts until that time, even if the third party dies before the fixed age.

Every usufruct terminates by the union in the same person of the two capacities of usufructuary and owner.

###### Article 738

In case of transfer of the usufruct right, the right is extinguished:
- by the death or dissolution of the first holder and not by that of the transferee;
- by non-use of the right for thirty years;
- by the total loss of the thing on which the usufruct is established, except by agreement of the usufructuary and the owner to transfer it to the thing representing that which has perished.

##### Section V: Special Usufructs

###### § 1. Quasi-usufruct Article 739

If the usufruct includes consumable things, such as money, grain, the usufructuary has the right to use them, but subject to the obligation to return to the owner, at the end of the usufruct, either things of the same quantity and quality, or their value estimated at the date of restitution.

###### Article 740

If the usufruct includes things which, without being consumed immediately, deteriorate little by little through use, such as linen, furnishings, the usufructuary has the right to use them for the purpose for which they are intended, and is only obliged to return them at the end of the usufruct in the state in which they are found, not deteriorated by his fault.

###### Article 741

If the instrument creating the usufruct so provides, the usufructuary may dispose of any non-consumable movable property. The instrument creating the usufruct shall then specify the conditions under which restitution shall take place.
The usufructuary may reinvest the funds arising from the alienation. The instrument creating the usufruct may even make this an obligation on the usufructuary. The judge may also, at the request of the owner, be seized for this purpose for the preservation of his rights. The reinvestment made may be proved by any means.

At the end of the usufruct, in the absence of contractual provision, the usufructuary returns to the owner either things of the same quantity and quality, or their value estimated at the date of restitution. If there has been reinvestment, he returns the property resulting therefrom or their value estimated at the same date. When the reinvestment has been made freely and spontaneously by the usufructuary, the latter returns the greater of the sums represented by the current value of the property acquired in reinvestment or that of the property on which the quasi-usufruct was initially created.

###### § 2. Usufruct of claims Article 742

The usufruct of a claim for a sum of money gives the usufructuary the right to interest, as fruits. In case of repayment of the capital during his usufruct, the usufructuary exercises, unless otherwise agreed, his right over this capital in accordance with Article 739.

The usufruct of a life annuity gives the usufructuary, during the duration of his usufruct, the right to receive the arrears, without being required to make any restitution.

###### § 3. Usufruct of corporate rights Article 743

Dividends distributed as income belong to the usufructuary.

Unless otherwise agreed, the usufructuary exercises his right over other sums in accordance with Article 744, during the duration of his usufruct.

###### § 4. Usufruct of property forming a whole Article 744

Unless otherwise agreed, when the usufruct relates to property forming a whole, the usufructuary may dispose of each of its elements, but he shall do so by replacing them and in accordance with the purpose of that whole.

If compliance with the purpose of the whole puts his right in jeopardy, the usufructuary may ask the judge to adapt and modify that purpose.

#### Chapter II: Of Use and Habitation Article 745

The right of use, like the right of use and habitation, is that which confers on its beneficiary, within the limits of his needs and those of his family, present and future, the personal use of a property and the collection of fruits.
These rights are established and lost in the same manner as usufruct. They may be neither transferred nor leased.

###### Article 746

One may not enjoy them, as in the case of usufruct, without first giving security and without making statements and inventories.

###### Article 747

The user, and the person who has a right of habitation, must exercise their right reasonably and in compliance with the normal purpose of the property.

###### Article 748

When the user uses the entire property or receives all the fruits thereof, he is liable for maintenance expenses and, more generally, for periodic expenses that Article 715 places on the usufructuary.
If he takes only part of the fruits or occupies only part of the property, he contributes in proportion to what he enjoys.

#### Chapter III: Special Real Rights

##### Section I: Real rights conferred by leases Article 749

Certain contracts, such as emphyteutic leases or construction leases, confer on the lessee a real property right.

Such rights are transferable and susceptible to real property security interests. They confer on their holder, during the term of the contract, ownership of the constructions, plantations, or installations, the realization of which they authorize.

These contracts are governed by the laws that establish them.

##### Section II: Special real right of enjoyment Article 750

The owner may grant, subject to rules of public policy, one or more real rights conferring the benefit of special enjoyment of one or more of his properties.

###### Article 751

The special real right of enjoyment is established and lost in the same manner as usufruct.

It may not be established in perpetuity, but may be granted for the duration of existence of the person who benefits from it.

###### Article 752

The special real right of enjoyment, subject to the instrument creating it, gives its holder the right to all the rights that benefit the usufructuary and imposes, likewise, all the obligations.
It is always exercised in compliance with the normal purpose of the property concerned.

###### Article 753

Subject to contractual provisions, the special real right of enjoyment is extinguished:
- by the expiration of the time for which it was granted;
- by non-use of the right for a period established by the instrument creating it and, failing that, for a reasonable period fixed by the judge;
- by the union in the same person of the two capacities of holder of the special real right of enjoyment and owner;
- by the total loss of the thing on which the special real right of enjoyment relates.

#### Chapter IV: Of Emphyteusis Article 754

The emphyteutic lease of immovable property confers on the lessee a real right susceptible to mortgage; this right may be transferred and seized in the forms prescribed for immovable seizure.

This lease must be granted for more than eighteen years and may not exceed ninety-nine years; it may not be extended by tacit renewal.

###### Article 755

The emphyteutic lease may only be validly granted by those who have the right to alienate, and under the same conditions, as in the same forms.
Immovable property belonging to minors or adults under guardianship may be given on emphyteutic lease by virtue of a resolution of the family council.
When spouses are subject to the dotal regime, the husband may give immovable dotal property on emphyteutic lease with the consent of the wife and judicial authorization.

Concerning premises for residential use, lease contracts concluded by the emphyteuta with tenants continue automatically with the owner of the building until the end of each of the lease contracts as signed with the tenants.

###### Article 756

Proof of the emphyteusis contract is established in accordance with the rules of this code regarding leases.

###### Article 757

In the absence of contrary agreements, it is governed by the following provisions.

###### Article 758

The lessee may not request reduction of the rent on grounds of partial loss of the property, nor on grounds of sterility or deprivation of any harvest following fortuitous events.

###### Article 759

In the event of non-payment for two consecutive years, the lessor is authorized, after a demand that has remained without effect, to have the termination of the emphyteusis pronounced by the court.
Termination may also be sought by the lessor in the event of non-performance of the conditions of the contract or if the lessee has committed serious deterioration to the land.
Nevertheless, the courts may grant a period of time according to the circumstances.

###### Article 760

The lessee cannot free himself from the rent, nor evade the performance of the conditions of the emphyteutic lease by abandoning the land.
