In the absence of co-ownership funds, he may oblige his co-owners to make the necessary expenses with him.

When co-owned property is encumbered with a usufruct, these powers are enforceable against the usufructuary to the extent that the latter is liable for repairs.

###### Article 941

Co-owners may give a mandate to one or more of them or to a third party to perform a specific act, which forms a special mandate, or even to handle all the affairs of the co-ownership, which is a general mandate. The general mandate permits only acts of administration.
If one of the co-owners or a third party takes the initiative to manage the co-owned property with the knowledge of the others and without opposition on their part, he is deemed to have received a tacit mandate. This mandate permits only acts of administration; it covers neither acts of disposition nor the conclusion or renewal of leases.

The co-owner who manages one or more co-owned properties is responsible for his management. He is entitled to remuneration for his activity under the conditions fixed amicably or, failing that, by judicial decision.
If a co-owner or a third party performs an act useful to the co-ownership without the conditions provided for in the preceding paragraphs being met, he is obliged to continue his management in accordance with the rules governing management of affairs.

###### Article 942

When the situation does not permit giving a mandate, a co-owner may seek judicial authorization:
1° When another co-owner is unable to express his will: the applicant co-owner may have himself authorized by the court to represent him, both generally and for certain particular acts. The court then determines the conditions and extent of the representation;
2° In case of refusal by one of the co-owners to give his consent to an act deemed necessary by the applicant, when this refusal endangers the common interest. However, it does not fall within the power of the judge to authorize the sale in full ownership requested by a bare owner when the usufructuary opposes it;
3° For all urgent measures required by the common interest.
In cases 2° and 3°, authorization is sought before the president of the Court of First Instance who is seized and rules in summary proceedings. The president may, in particular, authorize a co-owner to receive from the debtors of the co-ownership or from depositaries of co-owned funds a provision intended to meet urgent needs, prescribing, if necessary, the conditions of use. This authorization does not entail assumption of capacity for the surviving spouse or for the heir. He may also either designate a co-owner as administrator, obliging him if necessary to provide security, or appoint a sequestrator, or prohibit the displacement of movable property except to specify those of which he grants personal use to one or another of the beneficiaries, on condition that they provide security if he deems it necessary.

###### Article 943

When a co-owned building for residential use or for mixed residential and professional use is vacant or has not been the subject of effective occupation for more than two calendar years, a co-owner may be authorized in court to carry out improvement, rehabilitation and restoration works on the building as well as to perform acts of administration and publicity formalities, having as sole purpose to lease it as a principal residence.

###### Article 944

For this purpose, a co-owner may seize the president of the Court of First Instance, so that he may designate him as mandatary. The president sets the duration of his mission as well as his remuneration. At the request of the designated co-owner, the president may extend this mission for a period that he determines.

The appointment decision is registered and published in a newspaper authorized to receive legal publications.

###### Article 945

Within the limits of the powers conferred upon him, the designated co-owner represents all the co-owners for the acts provided for in Article 943. He exercises his powers even when there is a minor or a protected adult among the other co-owners.
The acts he performs within the framework of his mission have no effect on the inheritance option of the co-owner designated as mandatary.

###### Article 946

At the request of any interested person or of the public prosecutor, the president may remove the mandatary from his mission in case of characterized failure in the exercise thereof. The president then designates another mandatary, for a period that he defines.

###### Article 947

Each heir may require the agent to allow consultation, at any time, of documents relating to the performance of his mission.
Each year and at the end of his mission, the agent submits to the judge and to each heir upon request a report on the performance of his mission.
The mission ceases automatically by operation of a co-ownership agreement that is signed between the heirs or by the signing of the partition deed. It also ceases when the judge finds that the mission entrusted to the succession agent has been fully performed.

###### § 3. Des droits et obligations des indivisaires Article 948

Each co-owner has the same right of use and enjoyment over the undivided property as the others. The co-owners determine the allocation of this right among themselves. It is possible for them to grant to a co-owner an exclusive right of use or enjoyment over the property, in return for compensation.

In the absence of agreement on the use of the undivided property, the president of the court settles the matter on a provisional basis. He is seized and rules by summary order.

###### Article 949

Each person is entitled to the benefits of the undivided property and bears the losses in proportion to his rights in the co-ownership. However, no claim relating to fruits and revenues shall be admissible more than five years after the date on which they were received or could have been received.
Any person who receives revenues or incurs expenses on behalf of the co-ownership must keep a record thereof which is available to the co-owners.

The fruits and revenues benefit the entire co-ownership; however, by express agreement, they may be allocated to one of the co-owners.
Any co-owner may request his annual share in the benefits. In case of disagreement, the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance shall rule taking into account the extent of each person's rights in the co-ownership.

###### Article 950

Claims and indemnities that replace undivided property, as well as property acquired, with the consent of all the co-owners, in employment or re-employment of undivided property, are automatically undivided by operation of subrogation in rem.

###### Article 951

When a co-owner has improved at his own expense the condition of undivided property, he must be credited for it according to equity, having regard to the amount by which the value of the property is increased at the time of partition or alienation. He must likewise be credited for necessary expenses that he has incurred from his personal funds for the preservation of said property, even though they have not improved them.
Conversely, the co-owner is liable for degradations and deteriorations that have diminished the value of the undivided property by his act or by his fault.

###### § 4. Du droit de poursuite des créanciers Article 952

The creditors of the co-ownership, who are those who could have acted against the undivided property before there was co-ownership and those whose claim arose from the fact of management of the co-ownership or from acts of preservation of which they were the authors, shall be paid from the assets of the co-ownership before any partition and, if the co-ownership should not suffice to satisfy them in their rights, they may act against each of the co-owners. The latter are held jointly and severally for the balance. The creditors of the co-ownership may also pursue the seizure and sale of the undivided property.

The personal creditors of a co-owner may not seize either the undivided property or the share of their debtor. On the other hand, they may provoke partition in the name of their debtor or intervene in the partition that the latter has provoked. The co-owners, however, have the power to stop the course of the partition action by discharging the obligation owed by the debtor. Those who exercise this option shall reimburse themselves by deduction from the undivided property.

###### § 5. Des demandes en partage Article 953

No one may be compelled to remain in co-ownership and partition may always be provoked, except by judgment or contrary agreement.

Co-owners who hold a title of ownership, bare ownership or usufruct may agree to remain in co-ownership for a limited time: this agreement cannot be binding beyond five years; but it may be renewed. Conventional co-ownership is subject to the rules of articles 2071 and following.

###### Article 954

When several co-ownerships exist exclusively between the same persons, whether they relate to the same property or to different property, a single partition may take place.

###### Article 955

Partition may be requested even when one of the co-heirs has enjoyed separately all or part of the undivided property, if there has not been a partition deed, or sufficient possession to acquire prescription when it is admitted.

###### Article 956

If a minor, an adult under guardianship or curatorship, or a presumed absentee, is called to a partition, the latter may be done amicably.

In this case, the judge authorizes the partition, even partial, and designates, if necessary, a notary to proceed with it, in the presence as the case may be of the representative or curator of the person referred to in the preceding paragraph or, if that person is himself interested in the partition, of his replacement designated in accordance with article 143. The liquidation statement is submitted to the approval of the judge.
The partition may also be done in court in accordance with the provisions of articles 981 and following. Failing compliance with these conditions, the amicable partition is considered provisional.

###### Article 957

A spouse may not, without the consent of the other, proceed with the partition of property that has devolved to the latter which falls into the community. Any partition to which he proceeds alone, as to such property, is valid only as a provisional partition.

###### Article 958

The co-owner in usufruct may request partition in kind of the undivided usufruct; if this partition in kind among the different usufructuaries is not possible, the usufruct may be sold.
When the sale of the usufruct alone cannot be envisaged under satisfactory conditions for the usufructuaries, the sale may relate to the full ownership provided that it appears to be the only measure that can preserve the interests of all holders of rights over the undivided property.

###### Article 959

The same option belongs to the co-owner in bare ownership for the undivided bare ownership. But in case of sale of the full ownership, when the property is encumbered with usufruct, the sale may not operate against the will of the usufructuary.

###### Article 960

When a person is in co-ownership over both the usufruct and the bare ownership, he has the options provided for in the two preceding articles. The contrary will of a usufructuary, if he requests the sale of the property in full ownership, may not be opposed to him.

###### Article 961

When all parties agree on the partition, it is amicable; if one of the co-heirs refuses to consent to the partition, or if disputes arise either on the manner of proceeding with it or on the manner of completing it, the partition is judicial.

###### § 6. Des attributions préférentielles Article 962

Except by decision or agreement to maintain the co-ownership, preferential allocation may be granted to the spouse or to any heir called to succeed by operation of law, whether he is a co-owner in full ownership or in bare ownership, under the conditions provided for by the following provisions.
These provisions also benefit the heir having a universal or universal title vocation to the succession by virtue of a will or contractual institution.

###### Article 963

The surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may request preferential allocation by way of partition, subject to payment of an equalisation sum if applicable, of any enterprise, or part of an agricultural, commercial, industrial, artisanal or liberal enterprise or undivided share of such an enterprise, even formed in part from property of which he or she was already owner or co-owner before the death, in the operation of which he or she participates or has effectively participated. In the case of the heir, the condition

of participation may be or have been fulfilled by his or her spouse or descendants.

If applicable, the request for preferential allocation may relate to company shares, without prejudice to the application of legal provisions or statutory clauses on the continuation of a company with the surviving spouse or one or more heirs.

###### Article 964

The surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may also request preferential allocation:
1° Of the ownership or right to the lease of the premises which effectively serve as his or her dwelling, if he or she had his or her residence there at the time of death, and of the furniture furnishing it, as well as of the deceased's vehicle provided that this vehicle is necessary for the needs of daily life. This preferential allocation is by right for the surviving spouse;
2° Of the ownership or right to the lease of the premises for professional use effectively serving for the exercise of his or her profession and of the movable objects for professional use furnishing these premises;
3° Of the ownership of any agricultural holding whose size in area makes it a family holding. Preferential allocation is by right for the surviving spouse;
4° Of all the movable elements necessary for the operation of a rural property cultivated by the deceased in a professional capacity, when the lease continues for the benefit of the applicant, or when a new lease is granted to the latter.
The rights resulting from preferential allocation do not prejudice the life rights of habitation and use, or of enjoyment, which the spouse may exercise by virtue of law or contract.

###### Article 965

If maintenance in joint ownership has not been ordered and in the absence of preferential allocation in ownership, provided for in the preceding articles, the surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may request preferential allocation of all or part of the immovable property and rights with agricultural purpose forming part of the succession with a view to constituting, with one or more co-heirs and, where applicable, one or more third parties, an agricultural land grouping.
This allocation is by right if the surviving spouse or one or more of the co-heirs fulfilling the personal conditions provided for in articles 963 and 964, require that all or part of the property of the grouping be leased to them.

In the event of multiple requests, the property of the grouping may, if its consistency permits, be the subject of several leases benefiting different co-heirs; otherwise, and in the absence of amicable agreement, the court designates the lessee taking into account the aptitude of the different applicants to manage the property concerned and to remain there. If the clauses and conditions of this lease or these leases have not been the subject of an agreement, they are fixed by the court.
The immovable property and rights that the applicants do not envisage contributing to the agricultural land grouping, as well as the other property of the succession, are allocated by priority, within the limits of their respective succession rights, to the joint owners who have not consented to the formation of the grouping. If these joint owners are not satisfied with their rights by the allocation thus made, an equalisation sum must be paid to them. Except by amicable agreement between the co-partitioners, the equalisation sum possibly due is payable within the year following the partition. It may be the subject of a payment in kind in the form of shares of the agricultural land grouping, unless the interested parties, within the month following the proposal made to them, have made known their opposition to this method of settlement.

The partition is only complete after the signature of the constitutive deed of the agricultural land grouping and, if applicable, of the long-term lease or leases.

###### Article 966

If an agricultural holding constituting an economic unit and not operated in corporate form is not maintained in joint ownership and has not been the subject of preferential allocation under the conditions provided for in the preceding articles, the surviving spouse or any co-owner heir who wishes to continue the operation in which he or she participates or has effectively participated may require, notwithstanding any request for sale by auction, that the partition be concluded on the condition that his or her co-partitioners grant him or her a long-term lease on the lands of the holding which fall to them. In the case of the heir, the condition of participation may be or have been fulfilled by his or her spouse or descendants. Except by amicable agreement between the parties, the person who requests to benefit from these provisions receives by priority in his or her share the operating and dwelling buildings.
The preceding provisions are applicable to a part of the agricultural holding that may constitute an economic unit. This economic unit may be formed, in part, from property of which the surviving spouse or heir was already owner or co-owner before the death.

Account is taken, if applicable, of the depreciation due to the existence of the lease in the valuation of the lands included in the different lots.
If, by reason of the manifest inaptitude of the applicant or applicants to manage all or part of the holding, the interests of the co-heirs risk being compromised, the court may decide that there is no ground to apply the first three paragraphs of this article.

###### Article 967

In the absence of amicable agreement, the request for preferential allocation is brought before the court, which rules, except contrary provision, according to the interests at stake.
Preferential allocation may be requested jointly by several successors in order to preserve together the undivided property.
In the event of multiple opposing requests concerning a holding or an enterprise, the court designates the allocatee or joint allocatees according to the interests at stake and the aptitude of the different applicants to manage this holding or this enterprise and to remain there and in particular the duration of their personal participation in the activity of the holding or the enterprise.

###### Article 968

The property subject to allocation is valued at its value on the day of partition.

Except by amicable agreement between the co-partitioners, the equalisation sum possibly due is payable in cash. However, when the allocatee is the surviving spouse, he or she may require from his or her co-partitioners for the payment of a fraction of the equalisation sum, equal at most to half, periods not exceeding ten years. Except contrary agreement, the sums remaining due bear interest at the legal rate.

In the event of sale of the totality of the allocated property, the fraction of equalisation sum remaining due becomes immediately payable; in the event of partial sales, the proceeds of these sales are paid to the co-partitioners and credited against the fraction of equalisation sum still due.

###### Article 969

The beneficiary of preferential allocation only becomes exclusive owner of the allocated property on the day of final partition.
Until that date, he or she may only renounce the allocation when the value of the property, as determined on the day of that allocation, has increased by more than a quarter on the day of partition independently of his or her personal act.

###### § 7. De la constitution des parts et lots et du partage

A.	Dispositions communes

###### Article 970

The divisible estate comprises the property existing at the opening of the succession, or that which has been subrogated thereto, and which the deceased has not disposed of by reason of death, as well as the fruits pertaining thereto.
It is increased by the values subject to collation or reduction, as well as by the debts of the co-partitioners towards the deceased or towards the undivided estate.

###### Article 971

The partition of undivided property is carried out per capita. However, it is done per stirpes when there is a case for representation. Once the partition per stirpes has been carried out, within each stirpes, the partition is done, where applicable, per capita among the heirs of each stirpes.
When a person dies, his heirs come to the succession of the person from whom he would have inherited if he had not died before him. The heirs come by representation of their predecessor. Thus, grandchildren succeed to their grandparents by representation of their predeceased father or mother. These heirs by representation constitute "a stirpes".

###### Article 972

When the debtor of a balancing payment has obtained payment delays, and when, as a result of economic circumstances, the value of the property placed in his lot has increased or decreased by more than one quarter since the partition, the sums remaining due increase or decrease in the same proportion.
The parties may however agree that the amount of the balancing payment will not vary.

###### Article 973

Any person, even a relative of the deceased, who is not his successor, and to whom a co-heir would have transferred his right to the succession, may be excluded from the partition, either by all his co-heirs, or by one alone, by reimbursing him the price of the transfer.
This power granted to the co-heirs or to one of them to exclude from the partition any person not entitled to succeed to whom a co-heir would have transferred his right to the succession, also belongs to the undivided co-owner of an immovable, to the superficiary for the acquisition of the land, and to the owner of the land, for the acquisition of the superficies; any withdrawal without distinction must be exercised within a period of three months from the day the sale was made public.

###### Article 974

In the formation and composition of lots with a view to partition, one must avoid fragmenting the land and dividing economic units and other sets of property whose division would result in depreciation.

B.	Amicable partition

###### Article 975

Amicable partition may be total or partial. It is partial when it leaves the undivided ownership subsisting with regard to certain property or certain persons.

###### Article 976

If all the co-owners are present and capable, the partition may take place in the form and according to the procedures chosen by the parties.
When the undivided ownership relates to property subject to land registration publicity, the deed of partition is executed by notarial deed.

###### Article 977

If a co-owner is presumed absent or, as a result of distance, is unable to express his will, an amicable partition may take place under the conditions provided for in article 146.
Similarly, if a co-owner is subject to a protective regime, an amicable partition may take place in compliance with the provisions of the titles On minority, guardianship and emancipation and On majority and adults protected by law.

###### Article 978

If a co-owner is in default, without however being in one of the cases provided for in the preceding article, he may, at the instance of a co-partitioner, be formally notified, by extrajudicial act, to be represented at the amicable partition.
If this co-owner fails to appoint a representative within three months of the formal notice, a co-partitioner may request the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance to designate any qualified person who will represent the defaulter until the complete completion of the partition. This person may only consent to the partition with the authorization of the judge.

###### Article 979

The co-owners compose the lots at their convenience, and agree on the distribution of the lots among themselves. Failing that, the lots once constituted shall be drawn by lot.
Each lot must, as far as possible, be composed, either in whole or in part, of movables or immovables, rights or claims of equivalent value, subject to respect for the proportion of each person's rights in the undivided estate. In case of inequality of the lots constituted, this inequality is compensated, either by annuity or in money.

The equality of all in the partition, understood as the rights that each holds proportionally, in the undivided estate, is a rule of public policy.

###### Article 980

The co-owners freely proceed with the valuations of the value of the undivided rights and property.

The property is valued at its value on the date of divided enjoyment, taking into account, where applicable, the charges encumbering it. The determination of the day corresponding to the divided enjoyment of the property by the co-owners is the subject of a special clause in the deed of partition.

The date selected must be as close as possible to the partition. However, the judge may set the divided enjoyment at an earlier date if the choice of this date appears more favorable to the achievement of equality.

C.	Judicial partition

###### Article 981

The partition is made in court when one of the co-owners refuses to consent to the amicable partition or if disputes arise over the manner of proceeding with it or completing it or when the amicable partition has not been authorized or approved in one of the cases provided for in articles 977 and 978.
In these cases, the affixing of seals on the effects of the succession carried out as soon as possible, either at the request of the heirs, or at the instance of the public prosecutor at the Court of First Instance, or ex officio by the judge of the court within whose jurisdiction the succession is opened.

###### Article 982

Creditors may also request the affixing of seals, by virtue of an enforceable title or a permission from the judge.

###### Article 983

When the seal has been affixed, all creditors may form opposition to it, even if they have neither an enforceable title nor permission from the judge. The formalities for the removal of seals and the preparation of the inventory are regulated by the code of civil procedure.

###### Article 984

The action for partition and the disputes that arise, either on the occasion of the maintenance of the undivided estate, or during the partition operations, are submitted to the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of the place of opening of the succession which has exclusive jurisdiction to hear them. Any other judge must raise his lack of jurisdiction ex officio.
It is before this court that the sales by auction are carried out and that applications relating to the warranty of lots between co-partitioners and those for nullity of the partition or for additional share must be brought.

###### Article 985

If it considers that the settlement of the partition is simple, the court orders the partition; if it appears complex to it, it designates, on the one hand, a notary to carry out the partition operations and, on the other hand and from within itself, a judge to supervise these operations.
The notary certifies the property rights of each person, establishes the accounts of the undivided estate, forms the mass to be partitioned and constitutes the lots.

If the appointed notary encounters the inertia of a co-owner, he formally notifies him, by extrajudicial act, to be represented. If the co-owner fails to appoint a representative within three months of the formal notice, the notary requests, without formality, the judge who designated him to appoint any qualified person who will represent the defaulter until the complete completion of the operations.

###### Article 986

A co-owner may request that certain property be allocated to him or her on a preferential basis. In the event of opposition from another co-owner, the difficulty is resolved by the judge responsible for supervising the operations. This judge, for property that cannot be easily divided or allocated, orders the sale by auction of said property, under the conditions he or she determines.

###### Article 987

When the lots are constituted, each co-partitioner is permitted to submit his or her objections against their formation.
When the objections are resolved or settled by the judge, the notary proposes to the co-partitioners to agree on the allocation of the lots. Failing that, a drawing of lots is carried out.

###### Article 988

At any time, the co-partitioners may abandon the judicial route to pursue an amicable partition if the conditions provided for a partition of this nature are met.

###### § 8. Judicial maintenance in co-ownership Article 989

At the request of a co-owner, the court may stay the partition for up to two years if its immediate completion is likely to adversely affect the value of the undivided property or if one of the co-owners can only take over the agricultural, commercial, industrial, artisanal or professional enterprise forming part of the

estate upon the expiration of this period. This stay may apply to all of the undivided property or to only some of it.

If necessary, the request for a stay of partition may relate to company shares.

###### Article 990

In the absence of an amicable agreement, the judge may order the maintenance of co-ownership of any agricultural, commercial, industrial, artisanal or professional enterprise, the operation of which was carried out by the deceased or by his or her spouse, as well as residential or professional premises actually used by the deceased or his or her spouse, and movable objects furnishing the residential premises or used in the exercise of the profession.
If necessary, the request for maintenance of co-ownership may relate to company shares.

###### Article 991

In all these cases, when there are one or more minor descendants, the request may be submitted by the surviving spouse, by any heir or by the legal representative of the minor heirs; if there are no minor descendants, the action belongs to the surviving spouse alone.
Two conditions are then added: the surviving spouse must have had the status of co-owner of the property in question, whether this status predated the death or is linked to it, and, in the case of residential premises, this surviving spouse must have resided in the premises at the time of death.

###### Article 992

The court rules according to the interests at stake and the means of subsistence that the family can derive from the undivided property.
It may order the maintenance of co-ownership for up to five years, renewable as the case may be until the death of the surviving spouse and until the majority of the youngest of the descendants.

###### Article 993

When only one co-owner requests partition, the court may, at the request of one or more of the co-owners who on the contrary intend to remain in co-ownership, according to the interests at stake and without prejudice to the application of articles 962 and following of this code, allocate after appraisal his or her share to the one who requested the partition, either in kind if this share is easily detachable from the rest of the undivided property, or in value.
If there is not a sufficient sum in the co-ownership, the balance is paid by those co-owners who joined in the request, without prejudice to the possibility for the other co-owners to participate, if they express the wish. Each person's share in the co-ownership is increased in proportion to his or her payment.

##### Section II

Accounting for, imputation and reduction of liberalities made to successors Article 994
Every heir, even having accepted the estate subject to inventory, coming to an estate, must account to his or her co-heirs for everything he or she has received from the deceased, by inter vivos gifts, directly or indirectly; he or she may not retain gifts made to him or her by the deceased, unless they were expressly made to him or her outside the estate share.

Legacies made to an heir are deemed made outside the estate share, unless the testator has expressed a contrary intention, in which case the legatee may only claim his or her legacy by taking less.

###### Article 995

Gifts made outside the estate share may not be retained nor legacies claimed by the heir coming to partition except up to the amount of the disposable portion: the excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 996

The heir who renounces the estate may nevertheless retain the inter vivos gift or claim the legacy made to him or her up to the amount of the disposable portion, unless the disposer has expressly required accounting in case of renunciation.
In this case, the accounting is made in value. When the value accounted for exceeds the rights he or she should have had in the partition if he or she had participated, the renouncing heir compensates the accepting heirs up to the amount of this excess.

###### Article 997

The donee who was not a presumptive heir at the time of the gift, but who is found to be a successor on the day of the opening of the estate, does not owe accounting, unless the donor has expressly required it.

###### Article 998

Gifts and legacies made to the son or daughter of the one who is found to be a successor at the time of the opening of the estate are always deemed made with dispensation from accounting.
The father or mother coming to the estate of the donor is not required to account for them.

###### Article 999

Similarly, the son or daughter coming in his or her own right to the estate of the donor is not required to account for the gift made to his or her father or mother, even when he or she has accepted the estate; but if this child comes only by representation, he or she must account for what had been given to his or her father or mother, even in the case where he or she has renounced his or her estate.

###### Article 1000

Gifts and legacies made to the spouse of a successor spouse are deemed made with dispensation from accounting.

If the gifts and legacies are made jointly to two spouses, only one of whom is a successor, the latter accounts for half; if the gifts are made to the successor spouse, he or she accounts for them in full.

###### Article 1001

Accounting is only made to the estate of the donor.

###### Article 1002

Accounting is owed for what has been used for the establishment of one of the co-heirs or for the payment of his or her debts.
It is also owed in case of a gift of fruits or revenues, unless the liberality was made expressly outside the estate share.

###### Article 1003

Expenses for food, maintenance, education, apprenticeship, ordinary equipment expenses, wedding expenses and customary gifts, need not be accounted for, unless the disposer has expressed a contrary intention.
The character of a customary gift is assessed at the date when it is granted and taking into account the fortune of the disposer.

###### Article 1004

The same applies to profits that the heir has been able to derive from agreements entered into with the deceased, if these agreements presented no indirect advantage when they were made.

###### Article 1005

Similarly, no accounting is owed for partnerships formed without fraud between the deceased and one of his or her heirs, when the conditions thereof have been settled by an authentic act.

###### Article 1006

Property that has perished by fortuitous event and without the fault of the donee is not subject to accounting.
However, if this property has been reconstituted by means of compensation received by reason of its loss, the donee must account for it in the proportion in which the compensation was used for its reconstitution.

If the compensation has not been used for this purpose, it is itself subject to accounting.

###### Article 1007

The fruits of things subject to collation are due only from the day of the opening of the succession. Interest is due only from the day on which the amount of collation is determined.

###### Article 1008

Collation is due only by a co-heir to his co-heir; it is not due to legatees or to creditors of the succession.

###### Article 1009

Collation is made by taking less, thus the donee retains the property received but takes, in return, less than the others in the mass to be divided in order to restore equality in figures, except in the case of the second paragraph of Article 996.
It cannot be required in kind except by contrary stipulation in the deed of donation.

In the case of such a stipulation, alienations and constitutions of real rights granted by the donee shall be extinguished by the effect of collation unless the donor has consented thereto.

###### Article 1010

The heir also has the option to collate in kind the donated property which still belongs to him provided that this property is free of any charge or occupation with which it had not already been encumbered at the time of the donation.

###### Article 1011

Collation is due of the value of the donated property at the time of partition, according to its condition at the time of the donation.
If the property has been alienated before the partition, account is taken of the value it had at the time of the alienation. If a new property has been subrogated to the alienated property, account is taken of the value of this new property at the time of partition, according to its condition at the time of acquisition. However, if the depreciation of the new property was, by reason of its nature, inevitable on the day of its acquisition, no account is taken of the subrogation.
All subject to contrary stipulation in the deed of donation.

If it results from such a stipulation that the value subject to collation is less than the determined value of the property, this difference forms an indirect advantage acquired by the donee outside the succession share.

###### Article 1012

Collation of a sum of money is equal to its amount. However, if it has been used to acquire a property, collation is due of the value of this property, under the conditions provided for in the preceding article.

###### Article 1013

When collation is made in kind and the condition of the donated objects has been improved by the act of the donee, account must be taken thereof, having regard to the amount by which their value is increased at the time of partition or alienation.
Account must likewise be taken to the donee of the necessary expenses he has incurred for the preservation of the property, even though they have not improved it.

###### Article 1014

The co-heir who makes collation in kind may retain possession of the donated property until the effective reimbursement of the sums due to him for expenses or improvements.

###### Article 1015

The donee, for his part, must, in case of collation in kind, account for the degradations and deteriorations which have diminished the value of the donated property by his act or by his fault.

##### Section III: Payment of Debts

###### § 1. Debts of Co-partitioners Article 1016

When the mass to be divided includes a claim against one of the co-partitioners, whether due or not, the latter is allotted it in the partition up to the amount of his rights in the mass.

To the corresponding extent, the debt is extinguished by confusion. If its amount exceeds the debtor's rights in this mass, he owes payment of the balance under the conditions and time limits which affected the obligation.

###### Article 1017

Except when it relates to undivided property, the claim is not due before the closing of partition operations. However, the debtor heir may decide at any time to discharge it voluntarily.

###### Article 1018

Sums subject to collation bear interest at the legal rate, except by contrary stipulation.

This interest runs from the opening of the succession when the heir was debtor thereof to the deceased and from the day on which the debt becomes due, when it arose during the indivision.

###### Article 1019

When the co-partitioner himself has a claim to assert, he is allotted his debt only if, balance having been struck, the account shows a balance in favour of the undivided mass.

###### § 2. Other Debts Article 1020

Co-heirs contribute among themselves to the payment of debts and charges of the succession, each in proportion to what he takes therein.

###### Article 1021

The universal legatee contributes with the heirs, in proportion to his emolument; but the particular legatee is not liable for debts and charges, except however for the hypothecary action on the immovable bequeathed.

###### Article 1022

When immovables of a succession are encumbered with annuities by special hypothec, each of the co-heirs may require that the annuities be reimbursed and the immovables rendered free before proceeding to the formation of lots.
If the co-heirs divide the succession in the state in which it is found, the encumbered immovable must be valued at the same rate as the other immovables; deduction is made of the capital of the annuity from the total price; the heir in whose lot this immovable falls remains solely charged with the service of the annuity and he must guarantee his co-heirs therefor.

###### Article 1023

Heirs are liable for debts and charges of the succession, personally for their succession share, and hypothecarily for the whole; subject to their recourse either against their co-heirs, or against universal legatees, by reason of the share for which they must contribute thereto.

###### Article 1024

The particular legatee who has discharged the debt with which the bequeathed immovable was encumbered remains subrogated to the rights of the creditor against the heirs and universal successors.

###### Article 1025

The co-heir or universal successor who, by the effect of the hypothec, has paid beyond his share of the common debt, has recourse against the other co-heirs or universal successors, only for the share which each of them must personally bear, even in the case where the co-heir who paid the debt has had himself subrogated to the rights of the creditors; without prejudice however to the rights of a co-heir who, by the effect of the benefit of inventory, has retained the power to claim payment of his personal claim, like any other creditor.

###### Article 1026

In case of insolvency of one of the co-heirs or universal successors, his share in the hypothecary debt is apportioned among all the others, proportionately.

###### Article 1027

Executory titles against the deceased are likewise executory against the heir personally, eight days after service of these titles has been made upon him.

###### Article 1028

Creditors of the deceased and legatees of sums of money may demand to be preferred on the succession assets over any personal creditor of the heir.
Reciprocally, personal creditors of the heir may demand to be preferred over any creditor of the deceased on the property of the heir not received by way of succession.

The right of preference gives rise to the privilege on immovables provided for in Article 2354, and it is subject to registration.

###### Article 1029

This right of preference may be exercised by any act by which a creditor manifests to the competing creditor his intention to be preferred on a determined property.
The right of preference cannot be exercised when the claimant creditor has renounced it.

###### Article 1030

The right of preference is prescribed, with respect to movables, by the lapse of three years.

With respect to immovables, the action may be exercised as long as they exist in the hands of the heir.

###### Article 1031

The creditors of a co-sharer, to prevent the partition from being made in fraud of their rights, may oppose it being proceeded with outside their presence: they have the right to intervene at their own expense; but they may not challenge a completed partition, unless however it was proceeded with without them and in prejudice of an opposition they had filed.

##### Section IV: Effects of partition and warranty of shares Article 1032

Each co-owner is deemed to have succeeded alone and immediately to all the assets included in his share, or allotted to him by bidding, and never to have had ownership of the other assets of the succession.
The same applies to property that came to him by any other act having the effect of terminating the co-ownership. No distinction is made according to whether the act terminates the co-ownership in whole or in part, with regard to certain property or certain co-owners only.
However, acts validly performed either by virtue of a mandate from the co-owners, or by virtue of a judicial authorization, retain their effects whatever the allocation, at the time of partition, of the property that was the subject thereof.

###### Article 1033

The co-owners remain respectively warranted, one towards the other, for disturbances and evictions only that proceed from a cause prior to the partition. They are also warranted for the insolvency of the debtor of a debt placed in the share of a co-sharer, revealed before the partition.
The warranty does not apply if the type of eviction suffered was excepted by a particular and express clause of the partition deed; it ceases if it is by his fault that the co-owner suffers the eviction.

###### Article 1034

Each of the co-owners is personally obliged, in proportion to his benefit, to indemnify the evicted co-owner for the loss he has suffered. This loss is valued at the day of the eviction.
If one of the co-owners is found to be insolvent, the portion for which he is liable must be equally distributed between the warranted party and all the solvent co-owners.

###### Article 1035

The action for warranty is prescribed after two years from the eviction or the discovery of the disturbance.

##### Section V: Actions for nullity of partition or for supplement of share

###### § 1. Actions for nullity of partition Article 1036

The partition may be annulled for cause of violence or fraud.
It may also be annulled for cause of error, if the error related to the existence or amount of the rights of the co-sharers or to the ownership of property included in the divisible mass.

The action for nullity is prescribed after five years from the discovery of the defect or the cessation of the violence.

However, if it appears that the consequences of the violence, fraud or error can be remedied otherwise than by annulment of the partition, the court may, at the request of one of the parties, order a supplementary or corrective partition.

###### Article 1037

The partition may also be annulled if one of the co-owners was omitted from it.

The omitted co-owner may however request to receive his share, either in kind or in value, without annulment of the partition.
To determine this share, the property and rights on which the partition already carried out related are revalued in the same manner as if it were a new partition.

###### Article 1038

The co-sharer who has alienated his share in whole or in part, is no longer admissible to bring the action for nullity for error, fraud or violence, if the alienation he made is subsequent to the discovery of the error or fraud or to the cessation of the violence.

###### § 2. Action for supplement of share Article 1039

When one of the co-sharers establishes, to his prejudice, a lesion of more than one quarter, the supplement of his share is provided to him, at the choice of the defendant, either in cash or in kind.

To judge whether there has been lesion, the objects are valued according to their value at the time of the partition, which corresponds to the date of divided enjoyment.
The action for supplement of share is prescribed after two years from the partition.

###### Article 1040

The action for supplement of share is admitted against any act that has the object of terminating the co-ownership, independently of the qualification that the parties may have given to that act.
But after the partition, or the act that takes its place, the action for supplement of share is no longer admitted against the transaction made on the difficulties presented by that partition or that act.

###### Article 1041

The action is not admitted against a sale of succession rights made without fraud to a co-owner by his co-owners or by one of them, when the assignment includes a contingency defined in the deed and expressly accepted by the assignee.

###### Article 1042

The simple omission of an object of the succession gives rise to a supplementary partition relating to that property.

### Title II: Inter vivos donations and wills

Chapter I: General provisions Article 1043
A liberality is an act by which a person disposes gratuitously of all or part of his property or his rights for the benefit of another person.

A liberality may take the form only of these two categories of acts which are the inter vivos donation and the will.

###### Article 1044

The inter vivos donation is an act by which a person, the donor, transfers gratuitously to another person, the donee, who accepts it, the ownership of property.
The donor may, without being deprived of his liberal intention, impose on the donee the obligation to perform a specified prestation; the act is then called a donation with charges.

###### Article 1045

The will is an act by which the testator disposes, for the time when he will no longer exist, of all or part of his property, in full ownership or in the form of any other real right. If it is not full ownership, the right transmitted is so only for the time provided in the deed and in the absence of such provision, with regard to the legatee, the object of the legacy reverting, upon its extinction, to the succession of the testator.
The will may be revoked by the testator, but the revocation is valid only insofar as it was made by authentic deed or by a deed entirely written and signed by the hand of the testator.

The legacy may, after the death of the testator and at the latest two months after the notification of the will to the legatee, be refused, totally or in part, by the latter or by his agent. The silence of the legatee during this period constitutes acceptance; if the legatee dies within this period, his heirs exercise the rights of their predecessor from the notification of the will made to them. The decision of the legatee is final, unless the heirs consent to his modifying it.

###### Article 1046

Any disposition by which a person is charged with preserving and returning to a third party produces effect only in the case where it is authorized by law.

###### Article 1047

Parents may impose upon the child whom they gratify the obligation to preserve and transfer the property received to his or her own children.
A person without descendants may burden a gift made to his or her brothers or sisters with an obligation requiring them to transmit the property received to their children and thereby ensure the retention of the property within the family.
However, clauses of inalienability affecting property given or bequeathed are valid only if they are temporary and justified by a serious and legitimate interest. Even in such case, the donee or legatee may be judicially authorized to dispose of the property if the interest that had justified the clause has disappeared or if a more important interest so requires.

The provisions of this article do not prejudice gifts made to legal persons or even to natural persons subject to the establishment of legal persons.

Any clause by which the donor deprives of the gift the person who would challenge the validity of a clause of inalienability or request authorization to alienate shall be deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1048

Any gratified person may request that the conditions and charges burdening the donations or legacies he or she has received be judicially revised when, as a result of a change in circumstances, their performance has become either extremely difficult or seriously detrimental to him or her.

The application for revision is made by principal action; it may also be made by counterclaim, in response to the action for performance or revocation brought by the heirs of the donor. It is brought against the heirs and, at the same time, against the public prosecutor if there is doubt as to the existence or identity of some of them; if there is no known heir, it is brought against the public prosecutor. The public prosecutor must, in all cases, be given notice of the matter.

The application is admissible only ten years after the death of the donor or, in case of successive applications, ten years after the judgment ordering the previous revision. The gratified person must provide evidence of the efforts he or she has made, in the interim, to perform his or her obligations.

###### Article 1049

The judge hearing the application for revision may, as the case may be and even of his or her own motion, either reduce in quantity or frequency the obligations burdening the gift, or modify their object in accordance with the intention of the donor, or even consolidate them with similar obligations resulting from other gifts.

He or she may authorize the alienation of all or part of the property subject to the gift by ordering that the proceeds be used for purposes consistent with the will of the donor.
He or she shall prescribe measures appropriate to maintain, as far as possible, the designation that the donor had intended to give to his or her gift.

###### Article 1050

Third-party opposition to the judgment granting the application for revision is admissible only in case of fraud attributable to the donee or legatee.
The retraction or reformation of the judgment challenged does not give rise to any action against the third-party purchaser in good faith.

###### Article 1051

If, subsequent to the revision, the performance of the conditions or charges, as originally provided, becomes possible again, it may be requested by the heirs.

###### Article 1052

The clause by which the author of a gift designates a second-ranking beneficiary in the event that the beneficiary designated in the first place has predeceased or, in case of survival, refuses the gift, is authorized.
The same applies to the inter vivos or testamentary disposition by which the usufruct will be given to one person and the bare ownership to another.

###### Article 1053

In any inter vivos or testamentary disposition, impossible conditions and those that are contrary to law or morals shall be deemed unwritten.
If the thing bequeathed perishes before the death of the donor, or if it is claimed after having been recognized as being the property of a third party, nothing is owed to the donee or legatee. If only part of the thing bequeathed perishes or is claimed after having been recognized as being the property of a third party, the donee or legatee receives the remainder.

#### Chapitre II

Of the capacity to dispose or receive by inter vivos donation or by will Article 1054
Any person may dispose and receive, either by inter vivos donation or by will, except for persons whom the law declares incapable thereof. The author of such a gift must be of sound mind. If

the donation or will was made while consent was vitiated by error, fraud or duress, the act is null.

The donation as well as the will made in favor of a foreigner is valid subject to the legal provisions in force.

###### Article 1055

The will made by a minor is valid, provided it is approved by the judge.

###### Article 1056

To be capable of receiving inter vivos, it is sufficient to be conceived at the time of the donation.

To be capable of receiving by will, it is sufficient to be conceived at the time of the death of the testator.

Nevertheless, the donation or will shall have effect only insofar as the child is born viable.

When the testator dies before the delivery of the child already conceived at the date of the will and in whose favor the will was made, from the death of the testator until the delivery, the fruits shall be subject to conservatory measures.

###### Article 1057

A minor may not, even by will, dispose for the benefit of his or her guardian.

A minor who has reached majority or been emancipated may not dispose, either by inter vivos donation or by will, for the benefit of the person who was his or her guardian, if the final account of the guardianship has not been previously rendered and settled.
Excepted, in the two cases above, are the ascendants of minors, who are or have been their guardians.

###### Article 1058

Members of the medical and pharmacy professions, as well as medical auxiliaries who have provided care to a person during the illness from which he or she dies, may not benefit from inter vivos or testamentary dispositions that he or she may have made in their favor during the course of that illness.
Judicial representatives for the protection of adults and the legal persons on whose behalf they exercise their functions likewise may not benefit from inter vivos or testamentary dispositions that the persons whose protection they ensure may have made in their favor regardless of the date of the gift.

Excepted are:
1° Remunerative dispositions made on a particular basis, having regard to the means of the donor and the services rendered;
2° Universal dispositions, in the case of relationship up to and including the fourth degree, provided however that the deceased has no heirs in the direct line; unless the person for whose benefit the disposition was made is himself or herself among those heirs.
The same rules shall be observed with regard to the minister of religion.

###### Article 1059

Inter vivos or testamentary dispositions for the benefit of health establishments, medical-social establishments, or public utility establishments shall have effect only insofar as they have been authorized by decree.

However, inter vivos or testamentary dispositions for the benefit of foundations, places dedicated to worship and legally constituted associations and associations are freely accepted by them. If religious establishments are involved, the gift is valid even if the donor and the person receiving the property are not of the same faith.

###### Article 1060

Any disposition in favor of a person, natural or legal, who is subject to an incapacity to receive by gratuitous title, whether it is disguised in the form of an onerous contract or made in the name of interposed persons, is sanctioned by absolute nullity.
The father and mother, children and descendants, as well as the spouse of the incapable person shall be deemed interposed persons, until proof to the contrary.

#### Chapitre III

De la réserve héréditaire, de la quotité disponible, et de la réduction Section I : De la réserve héréditaire et de la quotité disponible

###### Article 1061

The hereditary reserve is the share of property and succession rights of which the law ensures the devolution free of charges to certain heirs called reserve heirs, if they are called to the succession and if they accept it.
The beneficiaries of the reserve are:
-	the descendants of the deceased, that is to say: children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren;
-	in the absence of descendants, the ascendants of the deceased, that is to say: the father and mother, grandparents, great-grandparents;
-	the surviving spouse, in the absence of descendants and ascendants.

The available portion is the share of property and succession rights that is not reserved by law and which the deceased was able to dispose of freely through liberalities.

###### Article 1062

Liberalities, whether by acts inter vivos or by will, may not exceed half of the disposer's property if he leaves only one child at his death; one-third if he leaves two children; one-quarter if he leaves three or a greater number;
The child who renounces the succession is included in the number of children left by the deceased only if he is represented or if he is bound to account for a liberality in application of the provisions of article 900.

###### Article 1063

Included in article 1062, under the name of children, are descendants in whatever degree, even though they should only be counted for the child whose place they take in the succession of the disposer.

###### Article 1064

Liberalities, by acts inter vivos or by will, may not exceed three-quarters of the property if, in the absence of descendants, the deceased leaves a surviving spouse who is not divorced.

###### Article 1065

In the absence of a surviving spouse and heirs, liberalities by acts inter vivos or testamentary may exhaust the entirety of the property.

###### Article 1066

If the liberality consists of a usufruct or a life annuity whose value exceeds the available portion, the heirs for whose benefit the law makes a reserve shall have the option either to execute this disposition or to make the abandonment of the ownership of the available portion.

##### Section II : De la réduction des libéralités excessives Article 1067

The value in full ownership of property alienated, whether subject to a life annuity, as a pure loss, or with reservation of usufruct to one of the successors in direct line, is charged against the available portion. Such acts are requalified, irrefutably, as liberalities outside the succession share.
Any excess is brought back to the mass and therefore gives rise to reduction of the excessive liberality. This charging and this reduction may only be requested by those of the other successors in direct line who did not consent to these alienations.

###### Article 1068

The available portion may be given in whole or in part either by act inter vivos or by will to the children or other successors of the donor, without being subject to accounting by the donee or legatee coming to the succession, provided that with regard to donations the disposition was made expressly outside the succession share.
The declaration that the donation is outside the succession share may be made either by the act that will contain the disposition or subsequently, in the form of dispositions inter vivos or testamentary.

###### Article 1069

Liberalities made as an advance on the succession share to a reserve heir who accepts the succession are charged against his reserve share and, subsidiarily, against the available portion, unless otherwise agreed in the act that provides for them. The excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 1070

Liberalities made as an advance on the succession share to a reserve heir who renounces the succession are treated as a liberality made outside the succession share.
However, when he is bound to account in application of the provisions of article 900, the heir who renounces is treated as an accepting heir for the notional reunion of all the property of the deceased, the charging and, where applicable, the reduction of the liberality granted to him. This principle is derogated from for:
-	premiums of a life insurance policy taken out for the benefit of a specified third party, unless they prove to be manifestly excessive in relation to the means of the insured or the transaction was merely a pure investment;
-	expenses for food, maintenance, education, apprenticeship, ordinary equipment expenses, wedding expenses and customary gifts, which need not be accounted for unless the disposer wills otherwise, in accordance with article 1003;
-	fruits and revenues accrued between the day of the donation and the death, in accordance with article 1081.

###### Article 1071

The liberality made outside the succession share is charged against the available portion. The excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 1072

The liberality made to a successor, or to successors jointly, that exceeds the available portion may be retained in its entirety by the beneficiaries, whatever the excess, subject to compensating the co-heirs in money.
When the reducible portion does not exceed the reserve share of the interested party, he may always claim all the bequeathed objects and therefore execute the reduction in kind when the donated or bequeathed property still belongs to him and it is free of any charge with which it had not already been encumbered at the date of the liberality, as well as any occupation to which it had not already been subject at that same date. This option expires if he does not express his choice for this method of reduction within three months from the date on which a reserve heir gave him formal notice to take a position.

###### Article 1073

When the value of donations inter vivos exceeds or equals the available portion, all testamentary dispositions shall lapse.

###### Article 1074

The reduction compensation is calculated, in all cases, according to the value of the property at the time of partition or alienation by the donee and according to their condition on the day the liberality took effect. If there has been subrogation, the calculation of the reduction compensation takes into account the value of the new property at the time of partition, according to their condition at the time of acquisition. However, if the depreciation of the

new property was, by reason of their nature, inevitable on the day of their acquisition, the subrogation is not taken into account.

The reduction compensation is payable at the time of partition, unless there is agreement between the co-heirs. However, when the liberality has as its object one of the property that may be the subject of a preferential attribution, time periods may be granted by the court, taking into account the interests involved, if they have not been granted by the disposer. The granting of these time periods may not, in any case, have the effect of deferring payment of the compensation beyond ten years from the opening of the succession. The provisions of Article 972 are then applicable to the payment of sums due.
In the absence of a contrary agreement or stipulation, these sums bear interest at the legal rate in civil matters. The advantages resulting from the time periods and payment terms granted do not constitute a liberality.

In case of sale of the entirety of the property given or bequeathed, the sums remaining due become immediately payable; in case of partial sales, the proceeds of these sales are paid to the co-heirs and credited against the sums still due.

###### Article 1075

Liberalities, direct or indirect, which exceed the disposable portion, are reducible to that portion upon the opening of the succession.

###### Article 1076

The reduction of dispositions inter vivos may only be requested by those for whose benefit the law creates the reserve, by their heirs or successors in title.
The donees, legatees, and creditors of the deceased may not request this reduction, nor benefit from it.
The limitation period for the action for reduction is set at five years from the opening of the succession, or two years from the day the heirs became aware of the infringement of their reserve, without ever being able to exceed ten years from the death.

###### Article 1077

The reduction is determined by forming a mass of all property existing at the death of the donor or testator.
There are notionally added to it, after deducting debts, those of which disposition has been made by inter vivos donation according to their condition at the time of the donation and their value at the opening of the succession. If the property has been alienated, account is taken of their value at the time of alienation and, if there has been subrogation, of the value of the new property on the day of the opening of the succession according to their condition at the time of acquisition; however, if the depreciation of the new property was, by reason of their nature, inevitable on the day of their acquisition, the subrogation is not taken into account.
There is calculated on all this property, having regard to the quality of heirs that he leaves, what is the portion of which the deceased was able to dispose.

###### Article 1078

The reduction of inter vivos donations presupposes that the value of all property included in testamentary dispositions has been previously determined. Once the reunion of property has been accomplished, the reduction is carried out beginning with the last donation, and so on going back from the most recent to the oldest.

###### Article 1079

When the testamentary dispositions exceed either the disposable portion, or the portion of that portion which would remain after deducting the value of inter vivos donations, the reduction shall be made proportionally, without any distinction between universal legacies and particular legacies.

###### Article 1080

Nevertheless in all cases where the testator has expressly declared that he intends that a particular legacy be satisfied in preference to the others, this preference shall take place; and the legacy which is the object thereof shall be reduced only to the extent that the value of the others would not fill the legal reserve.

###### Article 1081

When the reduction is executed in kind, the donee restores the fruits of that which exceeds the disposable portion, from the day of the death of the donor if the demand for reduction was made within the year; otherwise from the day of the demand.

###### Article 1082

Real rights created by the donee shall be extinguished by the effect of the reduction. These rights shall nevertheless retain their effects when the donor has consented to them in the very act of creation or in a subsequent act. The donee shall then be liable for the resulting depreciation.

###### Article 1083

The action for reduction or revendication may be exercised by the heirs against third party holders of immovables forming part of the donations and alienated by the donees, in the same manner and in the same order as against the donees themselves, and after prior discussion of their property. This action must be exercised according to the order of dates of the alienations, beginning with the most recent.
When the donor has consented to the alienation with the agreement of all reservees born and living at the time thereof, the action may no longer be exercised against third party holders.

###### Article 1084

After prior discussion of the property of the debtor of the reduction compensation and in case of insolvency of the latter, the reserve heirs may exercise the action for reduction or revendication against third party holders of immovables forming part of the liberalities and alienated by the beneficiary. The action is exercised in the same manner as against the beneficiaries themselves and according to the order of dates of the alienations, beginning with the most recent. It may be exercised against third party holders of movables when Article 2276 (number to be added when file No. 15 is numbered) cannot be invoked.
When, on the day of the donation or subsequently, the donor and all presumptive reserve heirs have consented to the alienation of the property given, no reserve heir, even born after the consent of all interested heirs has been obtained, may exercise the action against third party holders. With regard to property bequeathed, this action may no longer be exercised when the reserve heirs have consented to the alienation.

###### Article 1085

Any presumptive reserve heir may renounce, totally or partially, for example targeting only the reduction of a liberality relating to a determined property, exercising an action for reduction in a succession not yet opened, for the benefit of one or more determined persons. The renunciation binds the renouncer only from the day it has been accepted by the person from whom he has a vocation to inherit; but it may not create obligations chargeable to the person from whom one has a vocation to inherit or be conditioned on an act emanating from the latter.

###### Article 1086

The act of renunciation is, on pain of nullity, established by specific authentic act received by two notaries and mentions precisely its future legal consequences for the renouncer. The renunciation may be made in the same act by several reserve heirs, but they then sign separately before the notaries who receive the act.

The capacity required of the renouncer is that required to consent to an inter vivos donation. However, the emancipated minor may not renounce in advance the action for reduction.
The renunciation, whatever its terms, does not constitute a liberality. It is enforceable against the representatives of the renouncer.

###### Article 1087

The waiver produces no effect if the forced heirship reserve of the renouncing party has not been infringed. If the infringement of the forced heirship reserve has been exercised only partially, the waiver produces effects only to the extent of the infringement of the renouncing party's reserve resulting from the liberality granted. If the infringement of the reserve relates to a fraction greater than that provided for in the waiver, the excess is subject to reduction.
The waiver relating to the reduction of a liberality relating to a specific property lapses if the liberality infringing the reserve does not relate to that property. The same applies if the liberality was not made for the benefit of the specified person or persons.

###### Article 1088

The renouncing party has the possibility to revoke his waiver, but only in the following cases: 1° When the person from whom he has a vocation to inherit does not fulfill his maintenance obligations towards him;
2° When on the day of the opening of the succession, he is in a state of need which would disappear if he had not waived his rights as forced heir;
3° When the beneficiary of the waiver has been guilty of a crime or offence against his person.

###### Article1089

In case of dispute, the renouncing party shall seize the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, within one year from the day of the opening of the succession when the revocation is based on point 2° of the preceding article, and within one year from the act imputed by the renouncing party or from the day when the act could have been known by his heirs, if it is based on point 2° or 3° of the preceding article.
Revocation pursuant to 2° of the preceding article shall be pronounced only to the extent of the needs of the person who had waived.

#### Chapter IV: Inter vivos donations

##### Section I: Conditions and effects of inter vivos donations Article 1090

To be valid, any donation must be executed by authentic instrument.

In case of defect of form, an inter vivos donation cannot be the subject of confirmation: it must be remade in legal form.
After the death of the donor, confirmation or voluntary execution of a donation by the heirs or successors in title of the donor entails their waiver to oppose defects of form or any other cause of nullity.

###### Article 1091

An inter vivos donation shall not bind the donor, and shall produce no effect, except from the day it has been accepted in express terms.

Acceptance may be made during the lifetime of the donor by a subsequent and authentic instrument, of which a minute shall remain; but then the donation shall have effect, with regard to the donor, only from the day when the instrument recording such acceptance has been notified to him.

###### Article 1092

If the donee is of full age, acceptance must be made by him or, in his name, by a representative endowed with express power to accept the donation made, or with general power to accept donations which have been or might be made.
This power of attorney must be executed before a notary; and a copy must be annexed to the minute of the donation or to the minute of the acceptance which would be made by separate instrument.

###### Article 1093

A donation made to an unemancipated minor or to an adult under guardianship must be accepted by his guardian, in accordance with article 600, under the title Of minority, guardianship and emancipation.
Nevertheless, the father and mother of the unemancipated minor, or other ascendants, even during the lifetime of the father and mother, although they are not guardians of the minor, may accept on his behalf.

###### Article 1094

A deaf-mute who can write may accept himself or through a representative.

If he cannot write, acceptance must be made by a curator appointed for that purpose, according to the rules established under the title Of minority, guardianship and emancipation.

###### Article 1095

Donations made for the benefit of the establishments referred to in article 1059 shall be accepted by the administrators of those establishments, after having been duly authorized.
A donation made by a terminally ill patient is deemed a legacy.

###### Article 1096

A donation duly accepted shall be perfected by the mere consent of the parties; and ownership of the objects donated shall be transferred to the donee, without any other delivery being necessary.
If delivery of the thing donated has not taken place, the donee has the right to require it.

###### Article 1097

When there is a donation of property susceptible to mortgages, publication of the instruments containing the donation and acceptance, as well as notification of acceptance which would have taken place by separate instrument, must be made at the mortgage office of the place where the property is situated.
When the donation is made to minors, adults under guardianship, or public establishments, publication is made at the instance of the guardians, curators or administrators.

###### Article 1098

Failure to publish may be opposed by all persons having an interest, except however those who are responsible for having publication made, or their successors in title, and the donor.

###### Article 1099

Minors and adults under guardianship cannot request that the effects of failure to accept or publish donations not operate against them, even though said guardians are found to be insolvent. Minors and adults under guardianship may however obtain compensation; against their guardians, at least if the abstention of the latter has caused them prejudice.

###### Article 1100

An inter vivos donation may comprise only the present property of the donor; if it comprises future property, it is null in that respect.

###### Article 1101

Any inter vivos donation made subject to conditions the performance of which depends on the sole will of the donor is null.
The same applies to a donation made subject to the condition of discharging debts or charges other than those which existed at the time of the donation.

###### Article 1102

When the donor has reserved the freedom to dispose of a property included in the donation or of a fixed sum on the donated property, if he dies without having disposed of it, said property or said sum belongs to the heirs of the donor, notwithstanding any clause to the contrary.

###### Article 1103

The three preceding articles do not apply to donations mentioned in chapters VIII and IX of this title.

###### Article 1104

Any instrument of donation of movable property shall be valid only for property of which an estimated statement, signed by the donor and the donee, or by those who accept on his behalf, has been annexed to the minute of the donation.

###### Article 1105
