The absence of consent and defects of consent are a cause of relative nullity of the contract.

###### Article 1285

Error of law or of fact, unless it is inexcusable, is a cause of nullity of the contract when it relates to the essential qualities of the performance owed by one or the other of the parties.
Error is not a cause of nullity when it relates only to the person with whom one intends to contract, unless the consideration of that person is the principal cause of the agreement.

Essential are the qualities in consideration of which both parties have contracted, or, similarly, the qualities in consideration of which one of them has contracted, to the knowledge of the other. These expected qualities are those which have been expressly or tacitly agreed upon by the parties to the act.

The acceptance of a risk concerning a quality of the performance excludes error relating to that quality.

###### Article 1286

Error as to a simple motive, unrelated to the essential qualities of the performance owed or of the contracting party, is not a cause of nullity, unless the parties, rather than erecting this motive into a condition of their agreement, have expressly made it a determining element of their consent.

###### Article 1287

Error as to value by which, without being mistaken as to the essential qualities of the performance, a contracting party merely makes an inaccurate economic assessment of it, is not a cause of nullity.

###### Article 1288

Fraud is the act by a party of surprising the consent of the other by maneuvers or lies in order to obtain the conclusion of a legal act.
Also constitutes fraud the concealment by one of the parties of information which it knows to be of determining character for the other. Nevertheless, the fact that a party does not disclose to its contracting party its estimation of the value of the performance does not constitute fraud.

###### Article 1289

Fraud is also constituted if it emanates from the representative, manager of affairs, agent or surety of a party.
It is also constituted when it emanates from a third party in collusion.

###### Article 1290

Error resulting from fraud is always excusable; it is a cause of nullity even if it relates to the value of the performance or to a simple motive of the contract.

###### Article 1291

The victim of fraud may bring an action for nullity, seek only damages, or, where appropriate, both.

###### Article 1292

Duress is the act by a party or by a third party of infringing upon the free consent of another, by inspiring in him the fear of exposing his person, his fortune or those of his relatives to considerable harm.

###### Article 1293

The mere reverential fear towards the father, mother, or other ascendant, without violence having been exercised, is not sufficient to annul the contract.

###### Article 1294

The threat of legal action does not constitute duress, except in case of abuse. Abuse is characterized when the legal action is diverted from its purpose or when it is invoked or exercised to obtain a manifestly excessive advantage.

###### Article 1295

There is also duress when a party, abusing the situation of weakness in which its contracting party finds itself, obtains from him a commitment that he would not have undertaken in the absence of such constraint and derives a manifestly excessive advantage from it.

###### Article 1296

The period for the action for nullity runs, in case of error or fraud, only from the day on which they were discovered and, in case of duress, only from the day on which it ceased.
A contract may no longer be challenged if, since the defect of error or fraud was discovered by the person who was the victim of it or since the duress ceased, that contract has been approved by him, either expressly, or tacitly, or by allowing the time for restitution fixed by law to pass.

##### Section II : De la capacité des parties contractantes Article 1297

Any natural person may contract except in case of incapacity provided for by law.

Legal persons contract through their representatives. In this regard, the capacity of legal persons is limited to acts useful for the realization of their object as defined by their statutes and to acts which are accessory to them, in compliance with the rules applicable to each of them.

###### Article 1298

Are incapable of contracting, to the extent defined by law:
1° Unemancipated minors;
2° Protected adults within the meaning of Article 565 of this Code.

###### Article 1299

Any person incapable of contracting may nevertheless accomplish alone routine acts authorized by law or custom.

###### Article 1300

Routine acts accomplished by a minor may be annulled for simple lesion. But nullity is not incurred when the lesion results from an unforeseeable event.

The simple declaration of majority made by the minor does not prevent annulment. Likewise, an incapable person cannot be reproached for having remained silent or for having made a false declaration about his status.

A minor cannot escape the commitments he has made in the exercise of his profession.

###### Article 1301

Acts accomplished by protected adults are governed by Articles 574, 602 and 621 without prejudice to Articles 1299, 1304 and 1581.

###### Article 1302

Incapacity to contract is a ground for relative nullity that only the incapable contracting party may invoke.

###### Article 1303

Except with judicial authorization, it is prohibited, on pain of nullity, for anyone exercising a function or occupying a position in an establishment housing elderly persons or providing psychiatric care to become the purchaser, directly or through an intermediary, of property or assignee of a right belonging to a person admitted to the establishment, nor to take a lease on the dwelling occupied by that person before his admission to the establishment.
For the application of this article, the spouse, ascendants and descendants of the persons to whom the prohibitions set out above apply are deemed to be intermediaries.

###### Article 1304

The contracting party of the incapable person may prevent the action for nullity brought against him by establishing that the act was useful to the protected person and free from lesion or that it benefited that person.
He may also oppose to the action for nullity the confirmation of the act by his contracting party who has become or become again capable.

###### Article 1305

The prescription of the action runs:
1° With regard to acts done by a minor, from the day of majority or emancipation;
2° With regard to acts done by a protected adult, from the day he became aware of them while he was in a position to redo them validly;
3° With regard to the heirs of the person under guardianship or curatorship or of the person subject to family habilitation, from the day of death if it had not begun to run previously.

##### Section III: Of the object and subject matter of contracts Article 1306

The object of the contract is constituted by what the parties have obligated themselves to. It may be an obligation to do, not to do, or to give.

###### Article 1307

Only things that are in commerce may be the object of a juridical act. A juridical act may not derogate from public policy either by its stipulations or by its purpose, whether or not the latter was known by all the parties.

###### Article 1308

The obligation has as its object a present or future performance. One cannot, however, renounce an unopened succession, nor make any stipulation concerning such a succession, even with the consent of the person whose succession is concerned.

The performance must be possible and determined or determinable.

The performance is determinable when it can be deduced from the contract or by reference to customs or to the prior relations of the parties, without a new agreement of the parties being necessary.

###### Article 1309

Lesion, economic imbalance between reciprocal performances, opens the way to an action for nullity only when the law so provides.

###### Article 1310

In framework contracts and contracts with successive performance, it may be agreed that the price will be fixed unilaterally by one of the parties, provided that it justifies the amount in case of dispute.
In case of abuse in fixing the price, the judge may be seized with a request seeking to obtain damages and if applicable the resolution of the contract. Seizing the judge suspends payment of the fixed price.

###### Article 1311

In service contracts, in the absence of agreement of the parties before their performance, the price may be fixed by the creditor, provided that he justifies the amount in case of dispute.
In case of abuse in fixing the price, the judge may be seized with a request for damages. Seizing the judge suspends payment of the fixed price.

###### Article 1312

When the quality of the performance is not determined or determinable by virtue of the contract, the debtor must offer a performance of quality conforming to the legitimate expectations of the parties in consideration of its nature, customs and the amount of the consideration.

###### Article 1313

When the price or any other element of the contract must be determined by reference to an index that does not exist or has ceased to exist or to be accessible, it is replaced by the index that most closely approximates it.

##### Section IV: Of the cause Article 1314

An obligation without cause, or on a false cause, or on an unlawful cause, can have no effect.

###### Article 1315

Any clause that deprives the debtor's essential obligation of its substance is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1316

A contract for valuable consideration is null when, at the time of its formation, the consideration agreed upon for the benefit of the person who commits himself is illusory or derisory.

###### Article 1317

In a contract of adhesion, any clause that creates a significant imbalance between the rights and obligations of the parties to the contract is deemed unwritten.
The assessment of significant imbalance does not relate either to the principal object of the contract or to the adequacy of the price to the performance.

###### Article 1318

The agreement is no less valid, although the cause is not expressed therein.

###### Article 1319

The cause is unlawful when it is prohibited by law, when it is contrary to good morals or to public policy.

##### Section V

Of the sanction for non-compliance with the conditions of validity of contracts Subsection 1: Nullity

###### Article 1320

A contract that does not fulfill the conditions required for its validity is null. Nullity must be pronounced by the judge, unless the parties acknowledge it by mutual agreement.
The annulled contract is deemed never to have existed.
Performances executed give rise to restitution under the conditions provided for in Articles 1577 to 1585.

Independently of the annulment of the contract, the injured party may request reparation for the damage suffered under the conditions of the general law of extra-contractual liability.

###### Article 1321

Nullity is absolute when the violated rule has as its object the safeguarding of the general interest. It is relative when the violated rule has as its sole object the safeguarding of a private interest.
When the rule that offends a private interest proceeds from a fundamental value, such as the protection of the human body, the nullity is absolute.

###### Article 1322

Absolute nullity may be requested by any person justifying an interest, as well as by the public prosecutor.
It can never be cured by confirmation of the contract.

###### Article 1323

Relative nullity may be requested only by the party that the law intends to protect. It may be cured by confirmation.
If the action for relative nullity has several holders, the renunciation of one does not prevent the others from acting.

###### Article 1324

Confirmation is the act by which a person who could invoke nullity renounces it. This act mentions the object of the obligation and the defect affecting the contract.
Confirmation can only take place after the conclusion of the contract.

Voluntary performance of the contract, with knowledge of the ground for nullity, constitutes confirmation. In case of duress, confirmation can only take place after the duress has ceased.

Confirmation entails renunciation of the means and defences that could have been raised, without prejudice however to the rights of third parties.

###### Article 1325

A party may request in writing from the party who could invoke nullity either to confirm the contract or to bring an action for nullity within six months on pain of forfeiture. The ground for nullity must have ceased.
The writing expressly mentions that in the absence of an action for nullity brought before the expiry of the six-month period, the contract shall be deemed confirmed.

###### Article 1326

Where the ground for nullity affects only one or more clauses of the contract, it entails nullity of the entire act only if that clause or those clauses constituted a determining element of the commitment of the parties or of one of them.
The contract is maintained where the law deems the clause unwritten, or where the purposes of the rule breached require its maintenance.
Except where a provision of law confers this power upon him, the judge may not modify a clause or an amount provided for by the contract.

###### Article 1327

The defence of nullity is not subject to prescription if it relates to a contract that has received no performance.

###### Sous-section 2 : La caducité Article 1328

A validly formed contract becomes lapsed if one of its essential elements disappears.

Where the performance of several contracts is necessary for the completion of a single operation and one of them disappears, those contracts whose performance is rendered impossible by this disappearance and those for which the performance of the disappeared contract was a determining condition of the consent of a party become lapsed.

Lapse only occurs, however, if the contracting party against whom it is invoked knew of the existence of the overall operation when he gave his consent.

###### Article 1329

Lapse terminates the contract.

It may give rise to restitution under the conditions provided for in articles 1577 to 1585.

#### Chapitre IV : De l'interprétation des actes juridiques Article 1330

Where the will of the parties is expressed in a clear and precise manner, the judge may not, under cover of interpretation, modify the clauses, on pain of misrepresentation.

###### Article 1331

The judge must in agreements seek what was the common intention of the contracting parties, rather than stopping at the literal meaning of the terms.
Where this intention cannot be discerned, the contract is interpreted according to the meaning that a reasonable person placed in the same situation would give it. But even where the terms in which an

agreement is drafted are general, it comprises only those things on which it appears that the parties intended to contract.

###### Article 1332

Terms capable of two meanings must be taken in the meaning that best suits the subject matter of the contract and the coherence of this act as a whole.
Where, in the common intention of the parties, several contracts contribute to a single operation, they are interpreted in light of it.

###### Article 1333

In case of doubt, a freely negotiated contract is interpreted against the creditor and in favour of the debtor, and a contract of adhesion against the party who proposed it.

###### Article 1334

Where a clause is capable of two meanings, the one that confers an effect upon it prevails over the one that produces no effect.

#### Chapitre V : Les effets du contrat

##### Section I

Les effets du contrat entre les parties Sous-section 1 : Force obligatoire

###### Article 1335

Contracts may be modified or revoked only by mutual consent of the parties, or for the grounds that the law authorises.

###### Article 1336

Contracts bind not only to what is expressed therein, but also to all the consequences given to them by equity, usage or law.

###### Article 1337

If an unforeseeable change of circumstances at the time of conclusion of the contract renders performance excessively onerous for a party who had not agreed to assume the risk, that party may request a renegotiation of the contract from its co-contracting party. It continues to perform its obligations during the renegotiation.
In case of refusal or failure of the renegotiation, the parties may agree to the termination of the contract at the date and under the conditions they determine. Failing that, one of the parties may apply to the judge to terminate the contract, at the date and under the conditions he sets.

###### Article 1338

There is simulation where the parties conclude an apparent contract that contradicts a hidden contract. In this case, the latter, also called a counter-letter, produces effect between the contracting parties.
However, any counter-letter having as its object an increase in the price stipulated in the deed of transfer of a ministerial office is null.

Similarly, any contract having the purpose of concealing part of the price is null, where it relates to a sale of immovables, a transfer of a business or clientele, a transfer of a right to a lease, or the benefit of a promise of lease relating to all or part of an immovable and all or part of the

balancing payment of an exchange or partition comprising immovable property, a business or a clientele.

###### Sous-section 2 : Effet translatif Article 1339

In contracts having as their object the alienation of ownership or the transfer of another right, the transfer takes place upon conclusion of the contract.
This transfer may be deferred by the will of the parties, the nature of things or by operation of law.

The transfer of ownership entails transfer of the risks of the thing. However, the debtor of the obligation to deliver recovers the burden thereof from the time of his default, either by a summons or an act containing sufficient demand, or, if the contract so provides, by the mere enforceability of the obligation, all subject to the rules provided for in article 1364, paragraph 3.

###### Article 1340

The obligation to deliver the thing entails an obligation to preserve it until delivery, by exercising all the care of a reasonable person.
This obligation is more or less extensive in relation to certain contracts, whose effects, in this respect, are explained under the titles that concern them.

###### Article 1341

Where two successive purchasers of the same corporeal movable derive their right from the same person, the one who took possession of this movable first is preferred, even if his right is later, provided that he is in good faith.
Where two successive purchasers of rights relating to the same immovable derive their right from the same person, the one who first published his deed of acquisition executed in authentic form in the land registry is preferred, even if his right is later, provided that he is in good faith.

##### Section II

Les effets du contrat à l'égard des tiers Sous-section 1 : Dispositions générales

###### Article 1342

The contract creates obligations only between the parties.

Third parties may neither request performance of the contract nor be compelled to perform it, subject to the provisions of this section and those of articles 1526 to 1529.

###### Article 1343

Third parties must respect the legal situation created by the contract, which is enforceable against them. They may rely on it in particular for evidentiary purposes.

###### Article 1344

In case of simulation, the counter-letter is not enforceable against third parties, who may nevertheless rely on it.

###### Article 1345

When a person acts on behalf of another but without informing the person with whom he enters into the contract, the latter, upon learning of the existence of the nominee agreement, may rely on the act that had been concealed from him or on the act entered into with the nominee. On the other hand, if this contracting third party participated in the establishment of the simulation, he may only rely on the hidden contract.
In such a case, in the presence of a contract transferring ownership, the nominee agreement operates a transfer directly from the estate of the nominee to that of the principal, without passing through the estate of the nominee.

###### Sous-section 2 : Le porte-fort et la stipulation pour autrui Article 1346

One may undertake in one's own name only for oneself.

###### Article 1347

One may act as guarantor by promising the act of a third party.

The promisor is released from all obligation if the third party performs the promised act. Otherwise, he may be ordered to pay damages.

When the guarantee has as its object the ratification of an undertaking, the latter is retroactively validated by the ratification made by the third party, as of the date on which the guarantee was entered into, without prejudice however to the rights of third parties.

###### Article 1348

One may stipulate for another.

One of the contracting parties, the stipulator, may have the other, the promisor, promise to perform a benefit for the benefit of a third party, the beneficiary. The third party beneficiary may be a future person but must be precisely designated or capable of being determined at the time of performance of the promise. The stipulator may reserve the right to designate the third party beneficiary when the time comes.

###### Article 1349

The third party beneficiary is vested with a direct right to the benefit against the promisor from the time of the stipulation.

Nevertheless the stipulator may freely revoke the stipulation as long as the third party beneficiary has not accepted it.

The stipulation becomes irrevocable at the moment when the acceptance reaches the stipulator or the promisor.

###### Article 1350

The revocation may only emanate from the stipulator or, after his death, from his heirs. The latter may only proceed with it upon the expiration of a period of three months from the day on which they gave formal notice to the third party beneficiary to accept it.
If it is not accompanied by the designation of a new beneficiary, the revocation benefits, as the case may be, the stipulator or his heirs.

The revocation takes effect as soon as the third party beneficiary or the promisor has become aware of it. When it is made by will, it takes effect at the time of death.

The third party initially designated as beneficiary is then deemed never to have benefited from the stipulation made for his benefit.

###### Article 1351

The acceptance may emanate from the beneficiary or, after his death, from his heirs. It may occur even after the death of the stipulator or the promisor.
The acceptance may be express or tacit.

###### Article 1352

The stipulator may himself require from the promisor the performance of his undertaking towards the beneficiary.

##### Section III : La durée du contrat Article 1353

Perpetual undertakings are prohibited.

Each contracting party may terminate them under the conditions provided for contracts of indefinite duration.

###### Article 1354

When the contract is concluded for an indefinite duration, each party may terminate it at any time, subject to observing the contractually provided notice period or, failing that, a reasonable period.

###### Article 1355

When the contract is concluded for a fixed duration, each party must perform it until its term.
The contract may be extended if the contracting parties express their intention to do so before its expiration. The initial term of the contract is thus postponed to a later date. The extension may not, however, affect the rights of third parties.

###### Article 1356

No one may require the renewal of the contract, except as provided by law or by agreement of the parties.

In case of renewal, a new contract succeeds the previous one. Their content is identical but, except as otherwise provided by law, the duration of the new contract is indefinite.

###### Article 1357

When upon the expiration of the term of a contract concluded for a fixed duration, the contracting parties continue to perform its obligations, there is tacit renewal.
This produces the same effects as the renewal of the contract.

##### Section IV : La cession de contrat Article 1358

A contracting party, the assignor, may assign his status as a party to the contract to a third party, the assignee, with the agreement of his co-contracting party, the party to whom assignment is made.

This agreement may be given in advance, in particular in the contract concluded between the future assignor and the party to whom assignment is made, in which case the assignment takes effect with respect to the party to whom assignment is made when the contract concluded between the assignor and the assignee is notified to him or when he acknowledges it.
The assignment must be recorded in writing, on pain of nullity.

###### Article 1359

If the party to whom assignment is made has expressly consented thereto, the assignment of contract releases the assignor for the future.

In the absence of such express consent, the assignor is jointly and severally liable for the performance of the contract. It is possible for the parties to exclude certain rights and obligations from the assignment.

###### Article 1360

By the effect of the assignment carried out, the assignee becomes a party to the initial contract.

The assignee may raise against the party to whom assignment is made the defenses inherent in the debt, such as payment, prescription, nullity that is not purely personal to the assignor, the defense of non-performance, termination or set-off of related debts. He may not raise against him defenses personal to the assignor, such as incapacity or a defect of consent affecting the latter's will.

The party to whom assignment is made may raise against the assignee all the defenses that he could have raised against the assignor.

###### Article 1361

If the assignor is not released by the party to whom assignment is made, the security interests that may have been granted subsist. Otherwise, the security interests granted by third parties subsist only with their agreement.
If the assignor is released, his joint and several co-debtors remain liable after deduction of his share in the debt.

##### Section V : L'inexécution du contrat Article 1362

The debtor bound by an obligation of means has undertaken to implement all the means necessary to perform his obligation, without undertaking to obtain that result. Non-performance of the contract presupposes that the creditor demonstrates fault on the part of the debtor in the performance of his obligation.
The debtor bound by an obligation of result has undertaken to obtain the result contractually provided for. He is at fault by the mere demonstration of the absence of the promised result, unless he proves that the non-performance is due to an event of force majeure.

###### Article 1363

The party towards whom the undertaking has not been performed, or has been imperfectly performed, may:
-	refuse to perform or suspend the performance of his own obligation;
-	pursue the forced performance in kind of the obligation;
-	request or, when the law authorizes him to do so, notify the other party of a reduction in price;
-	bring about the termination of the contract;
-	seek reparation for the consequences of the non-performance.
Sanctions that are not incompatible may be cumulated; forced performance of the contract and termination are not compatible. Damages may always be added to the sanction pronounced.

In case of non-performance of a contractual obligation, neither the debtor nor the creditor may evade the application of the provisions specific to contractual liability in order to opt in favor of the rules specific to extra-contractual liability.

###### Article 1364

In contractual matters, an external cause may result from a fortuitous event, the act of a third party or the act of the co-contractor. The external cause constitutes a case of force majeure when it prevents

the performance of his obligation by the debtor, results from an event which, being beyond his control, could not reasonably have been foreseen at the time of the conclusion of the contract and whose effects cannot be avoided by appropriate measures.

If the impediment is temporary, the performance of the obligation is suspended, unless the resulting delay would justify the termination of the contract.

If the impediment is definitive, as the case may be, the impossibility of performing the obligation either releases the debtor to the corresponding extent, or, if it constitutes a case of force majeure, results in termination of the contract by operation of law and releases the parties from their obligations. However, the debtor remains bound if he has agreed to assume the external cause or if he has been previously given formal notice. In the latter case, when the impossibility of performance results from the loss of the thing owed, the debtor given formal notice is nevertheless released if he proves that the loss would have occurred in the same way if the obligation had been performed. In all cases, the debtor is bound to assign to his creditor the rights and actions attached to the thing.

###### Sous-section 1 : L'exception d'inexécution Article 1365

A party to a synallagmatic contract may refuse to perform his obligation, totally or partially, even though it is due, if the other does not perform his own.
The refusal to perform must not be disproportionate to the breach attributed to the other.

###### Article 1366

A party may, subject to the same reservation, suspend the performance of his obligation where it is manifest that his co-contractor will not perform at the due date and the consequences of such non-performance are sufficiently serious for him.
This suspension must be notified as soon as possible.

###### Sous-section 2 : L'exécution forcée en nature Article 1367

The creditor of an obligation may, after formal notice, pursue its performance in kind, unless such performance is impossible or there exists a manifest disproportion between its cost for the debtor and its interest for the creditor.

###### Article 1368

After formal notice, the creditor may also, within a reasonable time and at a reasonable cost, have the obligation performed himself or, with prior authorization of the judge, destroy what has been done in violation thereof. He may request from the debtor reimbursement of the sums expended for this purpose.
He may also request in court that the debtor advance the sums necessary for such performance or such destruction.

###### Sous-section 3 : La réduction du prix Article 1369

The creditor may, after formal notice, accept imperfect performance of the contract and request a proportional reduction of the price.
If he has not yet paid, the creditor notifies the debtor as soon as possible of his decision to reduce the price.

###### Sous-section 4 : La résolution

###### Article 1370

Termination results either from the application of a termination clause or, in case of sufficiently serious non-performance, from a notification by the creditor to the debtor or from a court decision.

###### Article 1371

The termination clause specifies the commitments whose non-performance will result in termination of the contract.

Termination is subject to an unsuccessful formal notice, if it has not been agreed that it would result from the mere fact of non-performance. The formal notice produces effect only if it expressly mentions the termination clause.

The termination clause must be implemented in good faith by the creditor. However, in case of non-performance of his commitment by the debtor, his good faith has no effect on the acquisition of the termination clause.

###### Article 1372

The creditor may, at his own risk, terminate the contract by way of notification. Except in case of urgency, he must first give formal notice to the defaulting debtor to satisfy his commitment within a reasonable time.
The formal notice expressly mentions that in the absence of the debtor satisfying his obligation, the creditor will be entitled to terminate the contract.

When the non-performance persists, the creditor notifies the debtor of the termination of the contract and the reasons motivating it.

The debtor may at any time seize the judge to contest the termination. The creditor must then prove the seriousness of the non-performance.

###### Article 1373

Termination may, in any event, be requested in court.

It is however possible to waive in advance the right to request judicial termination of the contract.

###### Article 1374

The judge may, according to the circumstances, find or pronounce the termination, or order the performance of the contract possibly granting a time period to the debtor, or award only damages.

###### Article 1375

Termination puts an end to the contract.

Termination takes effect, as the case may be, either under the conditions provided for by the termination clause, or on the date of receipt by the debtor of the notification made by the creditor, or on the date fixed by the judge or, failing that, on the day of the summons to court.
When the exchanged performances could find their utility only through the complete performance of the terminated contract, the parties must restore the entirety of what they procured from one another. When the exchanged performances found their utility progressively through the reciprocal performance of the contract, there is no need for restitution for the period prior to the last performance not having received its counterpart; in this case, the termination is qualified as rescission.

Restitutions take place under the conditions provided for in articles 1577 to 1585.

###### Article 1376

Termination does not affect clauses relating to the settlement of disputes, nor those intended to produce effect even in case of termination, such as confidentiality and non-competition clauses.

###### Sous-section 5

La réparation du préjudice résultant de l'inexécution du contrat Article 1377
The reparation of prejudice resulting from non-performance of the contract falls under the provisions of articles 1403 and following.

Sous-titre II : La responsabilité civile

Chapitre Ier : Dispositions préliminaires Article 1378
Prejudices resulting from bodily harm are always repaired on the basis of the rules of extra-contractual liability, even though they may be caused on the occasion of the performance of the contract.
However, the victim may invoke the express stipulations of the contract when they are more favorable to him.

###### Article 1379

When non-performance of the contract causes damage to a third party, the latter may request reparation of its consequences from the debtor only on the basis of extra-contractual liability. He must then demonstrate the reality of one of the generative facts referred to in section II of chapter II.
However, when the third party has a legitimate interest in the proper performance of a contract, he may invoke, on the basis of contractual liability, a contractual breach provided that it has caused him damage. The conditions and limits of liability that apply in the relations between the contracting parties are then opposable to him. However, any clause that limits the contractual liability of a contracting party towards third parties is deemed unwritten.

#### Chapitre II : Les conditions de la responsabilité civile

##### Section I

Dispositions communes aux responsabilités contractuelles et extracontractuelles Sous-section 1 : Le fait générateur de responsabilité

###### Article 1380

The triggering event of extra-contractual liability is defined by Articles 1391 and following. The triggering event of contractual liability is defined by Articles 1403 and following.

###### Article 1381

A person who performs an act is not civilly liable:
-	prescribed or authorized by legislative or regulatory provisions;

-	ordered by legitimate authority, unless such act is manifestly illegal;
-	ordered by the necessity of legitimate defense of themselves, others, or their property;
-	necessary to safeguard the person or property in response to a current or imminent danger threatening themselves, others or property.
All subject to the limits placed on these acts by the criminal code.

###### Article 1382

Nor does a harmful act give rise to liability where it infringes a right or interest which the victim could dispose of, if the victim consented thereto.

###### Sous-section 2 : Le préjudice réparable Article 1383

Any certain loss resulting from damage and consisting of the infringement of a lawful interest, whether patrimonial or extra-patrimonial, is recoverable.

Future loss is recoverable as soon as it is certain and direct.

###### Article 1384

Expenses incurred by the claimant to prevent the imminent occurrence of damage or to avoid its aggravation, as well as to reduce its consequences, constitute recoverable loss provided they were reasonably incurred.

###### Article 1385

Only the present and certain disappearance of a favorable eventuality constitutes recoverable loss of chance.
The compensation corresponds to the lost chance and not to the advantage that this chance would have provided had it materialized.

###### Sous-section 3 : Le lien de causalité Article 1386

A causal link must exist between the act imputed to the defendant and the damage. Proof of the causal link is established by any means.

###### Article 1387

Where bodily harm is caused by an unidentified person among identified persons acting jointly or carrying on a similar activity, they are jointly and severally liable to answer for the whole. However, each of the co-responsible parties may demonstrate that they cannot have caused the damage.
The responsible parties contribute among themselves in proportion to the probability that each caused the damage.

###### Sous-section 4 : Les clauses limitatives ou exclusives de responsabilité Article 1388

Clauses having the object or effect of excluding or limiting liability are in principle valid, both in contractual and extra-contractual matters.

However, liability may not be limited or excluded by contract in case of bodily harm.

###### Article 1389

In contractual matters, clauses limiting or excluding liability have no effect in case of gross or fraudulent fault.
They are deemed unwritten when they deprive the debtor's essential obligation of its substance.

###### Article 1390

In extra-contractual matters, one may not exclude or limit liability for fault.

##### Section II : Dispositions propres à la responsabilité extracontractuelle

###### § 1. La responsabilité pour faute Article 1391

Any act whatsoever of man, which causes damage to another, obliges the person by whose fault it occurred to make reparation.

Each person is liable for the damage they have caused not only by their act, but also by their negligence or imprudence.

###### § 2. La responsabilité du fait des choses Article 1392

Any harmful act of a thing automatically engages the liability of the person who has custody of it.

The custodian is the person who has the use, control and direction of the thing at the time of the harmful act. The owner is presumed to be the custodian of the thing.
The act of the thing and its causal role are presumed when it, in motion, came into contact with the seat of the damage. In other cases, it is for the victim to prove the act of the thing, by establishing either its defect, or the abnormality of its position, state or behavior, and its role in causing the damage.

###### Article 1393

The owner of an animal, or the person using it, while it is in their use, is liable for the damage caused by the animal, whether the animal was under their custody, or had strayed or escaped.

###### Article 1394

The owner of a building is liable for damage caused by its collapse, when it occurred as a result of lack of maintenance or a defect in its construction.
A person who holds, under any title whatsoever, all or part of the immovable property or movable property in which a fire originated shall be liable, vis-à-vis third parties, for damage caused by that fire only if it is proved that it must be attributed to their fault or to the fault of persons for whom they are responsible.

The preceding paragraph does not apply to relations between owners and tenants, which remain governed by the laws concerning them.

###### § 3. La responsabilité du fait d'autrui

###### Article 1395

Liability for the acts of another requires proof of an act capable of engaging the personal liability of the direct author of the damage.

###### Article 1396

The following are automatically liable for the acts of a minor:
-	their parents, insofar as they exercise parental authority;
-	their guardian or guardians, insofar as they are responsible for the person of the minor;
-	the natural or legal person charged by judicial or administrative decision with organizing and controlling on a permanent basis the minor's way of life. In this case, the liability of the parents of that minor may not be engaged.

###### Article 1397

The natural or legal person charged by judicial or administrative decision with organizing and controlling on a permanent basis their way of life is automatically liable for the acts of a major placed under their supervision.

###### Article 1398

Other persons who, by contract, assume, in a professional capacity, such as teachers and craftsmen with regard to their pupils and apprentices, a mission of supervision of another or of organization and control of another's activity, are liable for the acts of the natural person supervised, during the time they are under their supervision.
They may be exonerated from this liability by demonstrating that, in the exercise of their mission, they did not commit any fault of supervision or of organization and control.

###### Article 1399

The principal is automatically liable for damage caused by their agent. The relationship of agency presupposes the power of the principal to give the agent orders or instructions in relation to the performance of their functions.
In case of transfer of the relationship of agency, this liability rests on the beneficiary of the transfer.

The principal or the beneficiary of the transfer is not liable if they prove that the agent acted outside the functions for which they were employed, without authorization and for purposes unrelated to their duties. Nor are they liable if they establish collusion between the agent and the victim.

The agent engages their personal liability in case of intentional fault, or when, without authorization, they acted for purposes unrelated to their duties. They engage it only in these cases.

###### § 4. La responsabilité du fait de troubles anormaux de voisinage Article 1400

No one must cause another an abnormal disturbance of neighborhood.

###### Article 1401

Neighbourhood disturbance is sanctioned by the judge as soon as it is excessive.

Where it concerns a fault committed in the performance of an obligation arising from a contract, the rules of contractual liability apply between the parties to the act. In other cases, the measure of liability is that of the excessive nature of the disturbance without any regard to the existence or not of a fault of the defendant.

###### Article 1402

Where a harmful activity is carried out lawfully, the judge may nevertheless order reasonable measures to stop the disturbance and, failing the ability to do so without jeopardising the activity, award damages to the victim of the disturbance.
However, compensation for damage caused by nuisances resulting from an agricultural, industrial, artisanal, commercial or aeronautical activity that is carried out in compliance with legislation is excluded, as soon as the claimant settled in the location concerned after the activities started.

##### Section III: Provisions specific to contractual liability Article 1403

Any non-performance of the contract having caused damage to the creditor obliges the debtor to be liable for it.

###### Article 1404

Unless the non-performance is final, damages are only due if the debtor has previously been given notice to perform within a reasonable time.

###### Article 1405

The debtor is condemned, if appropriate, to the payment of damages either by reason of the non-performance of the obligation, or by reason of delay in performance, if he does not prove that performance was prevented by an external cause.

###### Article 1406

The damages due to the creditor are, in general, the loss he has suffered and the gain of which he has been deprived, subject to the exceptions and modifications below.

###### Article 1407

The debtor is only liable for damages that were foreseen or could have been foreseen at the time of conclusion of the contract, except where the non-performance is due to gross or intentional fault.
Fault is gross when its author adopts behaviour of extreme gravity, bordering on fraud, and denoting his inability to fulfil his obligations.

Fault is intentional when, deliberately, the debtor refuses to perform his contractual obligations, even if this refusal is not dictated by the intention to harm his co-contractor.

###### Article 1408

Even where the non-performance of the contract results from gross or intentional fault, damages only include what is an immediate and direct consequence of the non-performance.

###### Article 1409

A penalty clause is one by which a person, to ensure the performance of an agreement, undertakes to pay damages agreed in advance in the event of non-performance of his obligations.
In the presence of a penalty clause, no greater or lesser penalty may be awarded to the other party. Nevertheless, the judge may, even of his own motion, moderate or increase the amount thus agreed, in cases where it is manifestly excessive or derisory.

Where the undertaking has been performed in part, the agreed penalty may be reduced by the judge, even of his own motion, in proportion to the benefit that the partial performance has provided to the creditor, without prejudice to the application of the preceding paragraph.

Any stipulation contrary to the two preceding paragraphs is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1410

Whether or not the original obligation contains a term within which it must be performed, the penalty is only incurred when the person who is obliged is in default, unless the non-performance is final.

###### Article 1411

The creditor, instead of demanding the penalty stipulated against the debtor who is in default, may pursue the performance of the principal obligation. The creditor may not, however, demand both the principal and the penalty at the same time, unless it is on a subsidiary basis, unless it was stipulated for mere delay.

###### Article 1412

The nullity of the principal obligation entails that of the penalty clause. The nullity of the latter does not entail that of the principal obligation.

###### Article 1413

Damages due by reason of delay in payment of a monetary obligation consist of interest at the legal rate. They are only due from the day of notice, except in the case where the law makes them run automatically.
Accrued income, such as rents, arrears of perpetual or life annuities, bears interest from the day of the claim or the agreement.

These damages are due without the creditor being required to prove any loss.
The creditor to whom his debtor in default has caused harm independent of this delay, may obtain damages distinct from default interest.

###### Article 1414

In all matters, the award of compensation carries interest at the legal rate even in the absence of a request or special provision in the judgment. Unless otherwise provided by law, this interest runs from the pronouncement of the judgment, unless the judge decides otherwise.
In the event of pure and simple confirmation by the court of appeal of a decision awarding compensation in reparation for damage, it bears interest at the legal rate automatically from the first instance judgment. In other cases, the compensation awarded on appeal bears interest from the appeal decision. The court of appeal may always derogate from the provisions of this paragraph.

#### Chapter III: Exemption from liability Article 1415

In extra-contractual matters, the external cause resides in fortuitous event, the act of a third party or of the victim. The external cause is totally exonerating if it has the characteristics of force majeure. This is the case when the event escapes the control of the defendant or the person for whom he must answer, and the occurrence or consequences of which they could not avoid by appropriate measures.
In contractual matters, force majeure and its effects are defined in Article 1364.

###### Article 1416

The victim's breach of his contractual obligations, his fault or that of a person for whom he must answer are partially exonerating when they contributed to the occurrence of the damage.
In the case of bodily injury, only gross fault may result in partial exemption.

###### Article 1417

Unless it has the characteristics of force majeure, the fault committed by the victim deprived of discernment has no exonerating effect.

###### Article 1418

The fault or contractual non-performance that may be raised against the direct victim may also be raised against victims of consequential loss.

#### Chapter IV

The effects of civil liability Section I: General rules

###### Sub-section 1: The sanction

###### § 1. Reparation Article 1419

Reparation has the purpose of erasing the consequences of the harmful act and aims at complete restoration. The victim must derive neither loss nor profit from it.
Reparation may take the form of reparation in kind or by monetary equivalent. These two forms of reparation may be combined in order to ensure full reparation of the victim's loss.

###### Article 1420

Reparation in kind must make it possible to eliminate, reduce or compensate for the damage. It cannot be imposed on the victim.
Nor can it be ordered in the event of impossibility or manifest disproportion between its cost for the person liable and its benefit for the victim. Subject to the same reservations, the judge may authorise the victim to take reparation measures in kind himself at the expense of the person liable. The latter may be ordered to advance the necessary sums.

###### Article 1421

Damages are assessed at the date of the judgment, taking into account all circumstances that may have affected the nature and value of the harm since the date the damage manifested, as well as its reasonably foreseeable evolution.
In the event of aggravation of the damage subsequent to the judgment, the victim may request additional compensation for the resulting harm.
Each head of damage is assessed separately.

###### Article 1422

Except in the case of bodily injury, damages are reduced whenever the victim has not taken useful and reasonable measures, particularly in light of their contributory capacity, to prevent the aggravation of their harm.

###### § 2. Cessation of the unlawful act

###### Article 1423

In non-contractual matters, independently of compensation for any harm suffered, the judge may always order reasonable measures to prevent damage or to stop the unlawful interference to which the claimant is exposed.

###### § 3. Civil fine Article 1424

In non-contractual matters, where the author of the damage has deliberately committed a fault with a view to obtaining a gain or saving, the judge may order them, at the request of the victim or the public prosecutor and by a specially reasoned decision, to pay a civil fine.

###### Article 1425

This fine is proportionate to the seriousness of the fault committed, the contributory capacity of the author and the profits they have derived from it.
The civil fine may not exceed ten times the amount of the profit realized.
If the person liable is a legal person, the fine may be increased to 5% of the amount of the highest turnover excluding taxes realized in Djibouti during one of the financial years closed since the financial year preceding that during which the fault was committed.

###### Article 1426

This civil fine is allocated to the Public Treasury. It is not insurable.

###### Subsection 2: The effect of plurality of liable persons Article 1427

Where several persons are liable for the same damage, they are jointly and severally liable to make reparation to the victim.

###### Article 1428

If all or some of the persons liable for the same damage have committed a fault, they contribute among themselves in proportion to the seriousness and causal role of the generative act attributable to them.
If none of them has committed a fault, they contribute in proportion to the causal role of the generative act attributable to them and, failing that, in equal shares.

##### Section II: Special rules

###### Subsection 1

Special rules for compensation for harm resulting from bodily injury

###### Article 1429

Any stipulation contrary to the provisions of this subsection is deemed unwritten, unless it is more favorable to the victim.

###### Article 1430

Harm must be assessed without taking into account any predispositions of the victim where the condition resulting therefrom was only caused or revealed by the harmful act.

###### Article 1431

Subject to special provisions, patrimonial and extra-patrimonial harm resulting from bodily injury gives rise to full compensation.

###### Article 1432

Sums paid to the victim for compensatory purposes by third-party payers give rise to no action or subrogatory recourse against the person liable or their insurer except in the cases and under the conditions provided by law.
In the event that the insolvency of the person liable would prevent full compensation of the victim, the victim shall have priority over the third-party payer for what remains owed to them by the person liable.

The fault of the victim may only reduce their right to compensation in respect of the portion of their harm that has not been repaired by the benefits of the third-party payer. The third-party payer is entitled to the balance of the debt charged to the person liable.

###### Subsection 2

Special rules for compensation for harm resulting from material damage

###### Article 1433

In the event of damage to a corporeal thing, the compensation is the lesser of the two sums representing the cost of restoration and that of replacement of the thing, without taking into account its wear and tear or any capital gain inherent in the repair.
Where the thing can be neither restored nor replaced, the compensation is the value that the thing would have had at the date of the decision, in its condition prior to the damage.

If, at the request of the victim, the damaged thing is not returned to the person liable in its current condition, its residual value is deducted from the compensation.

###### Article 1434

Where applicable, the compensation also covers the deprivation of enjoyment of the damaged thing, loss of profits or any other harm.

###### Subsection 3

Special rules for compensation for harm resulting from environmental damage

###### Article 1435

Any person liable for ecological harm is required to repair it.

###### Article 1436

Reparable ecological harm is that which consists of a non-negligible impairment of the elements or functions of ecosystems or of the collective benefits derived by man from the environment.

###### Article 1437

The action for reparation of ecological harm is open to any person having standing and interest to act, such as the State or any public authority and public establishments as well as approved associations or associations created at least five years before the date of commencement of proceedings which have as their object the protection of nature and the defense of the environment.
Independently of the action for reparation of harm possibly suffered or in parallel with it, the judge may always order reasonable measures to prevent damage or to stop the unlawful interference to which the environment is exposed.

###### Article 1438

Reparation of ecological harm is effected as a priority in kind.

In the event of impossibility or insufficiency of reparation measures, the judge orders the person liable to pay damages, allocated to the reparation of the environment, to the claimant or, if the claimant cannot take the measures useful for that purpose, to the State.

The assessment of ecological harm takes into account reparation measures that have, where applicable, already been able to take place.

###### Article 1439

In the event of a penalty payment, it is liquidated by the judge for the benefit of the claimant, who allocates it to the reparation of the environment or, if the claimant cannot take the measures useful for that purpose, for the benefit of the State, which allocates it to that same purpose.
The judge who orders a penalty payment with a view to the reparation of ecological harm has the power to liquidate it.

###### Subsection 4

Special rules for liability and compensation of victims of bodily injury traffic accidents

###### Article 1440

Liability for motor land vehicles is governed by the provisions of the Law on liability and compensation of victims of bodily injury traffic accidents (Law No. 40/AN/99/4th L of 8 June 1999).

###### Subsection 5

Special rules for liability for defective products Article 1441
The provisions of this subsection apply to the reparation of damage resulting from injury to the person or that, exceeding 100,000 FD, resulting from damage to property other than the defective product itself.

###### Article 1442

A product within the meaning of this subsection is any movable property, even if it is incorporated into immovable property, including products of the soil, livestock, hunting and fishing. Electricity is considered a product.
Such a product is deemed defective within the meaning of this subsection when it does not offer the safety which one is legitimately entitled to expect having regard to all the circumstances and in particular the presentation of the product, the use to which it could reasonably be expected that the product would be put and the time when the product was put into circulation. A product may not, however, be considered defective for the sole reason that a better product was subsequently put into circulation.

###### Article 1443

The producer is liable for damage caused by a defect in a product which he has put into circulation, whether or not the producer is bound by a contract with the victim.
A product is put into circulation when the producer has voluntarily parted with it. A product is put into circulation only once.

###### Article 1444

A producer within the meaning of these provisions is, when acting in a professional capacity, the manufacturer of a finished product, the producer of a raw material, the manufacturer of a component part. Any person acting in a professional capacity who presents himself as a producer by affixing to the product his name, trademark or other distinguishing feature is treated as a producer for the purposes of this chapter;
Persons whose liability may be sought on the basis of articles 1954 to 1962 and 1819 are not considered producers within the meaning of this chapter.

If the producer cannot be identified, the seller, the lessor, with the exception of the lessor under a finance lease or a lessor similar to a lessor under a finance lease, or any other professional supplier, is liable for the lack of safety of the product, under the same conditions as the producer, unless he identifies his own supplier or the producer, within three months from the date on which the victim's claim was notified to him.

The supplier may bring a claim for indemnity against the producer, in which case his recourse against the producer is subject to the same rules as the claim brought by the direct victim of the defect. However, he must do so within one year from the date of his being summoned to court.

###### Article 1445

In the case of damage caused by a defect in a product incorporated into another product, the producer of the component part and the person who carried out the incorporation are jointly and severally liable.
The producer of the component part is not, however, liable if he establishes that the defect is attributable to the design of the product into which the component part has been incorporated or to the instructions given by the producer of that product.

###### Article 1446

The claimant must prove the damage, the defect and the causal link between the defect and the damage.

The producer is liable as of right unless he proves:
1° That he had not put the product into circulation;
2° That, having regard to the circumstances, it is probable that the defect which caused the damage did not exist at the time when the product was put into circulation by him or that this defect came into being afterwards;
3° That the product was not intended for sale or any other form of distribution;
4° That the state of scientific and technical knowledge at the time when he put the product into circulation was not such as to enable the existence of the defect to be discovered; this ground of exoneration is excluded when the damage was caused by an element of the human body or by products derived from it;
5° Or that the defect is due to compliance of the product with mandatory rules of a legislative or regulatory nature.

The producer may not be exonerated on the ground that the product was manufactured in accordance with the rules of the art or existing standards or that it was the subject of an administrative authorisation.

###### Article 1447

The liability of the producer may be reduced or excluded, having regard to all the circumstances, when the damage is caused jointly by a defect in the product and by the fault of the victim or of a person for whom the victim is responsible.

The liability of the producer towards the victim is not reduced by the act of a third party who contributed to the occurrence of the damage.

###### Article 1448

Clauses which seek to exclude or limit liability for defective products are prohibited and deemed unwritten.
However, for damage caused to property which is not used by the victim principally for his private use or consumption, clauses stipulated between professionals are valid.

###### Article 1449

Except in the case of fault of the producer, the liability of the producer, based on the provisions of this chapter, is extinguished ten years after the putting into circulation of the actual product which caused the damage unless, during that period, the victim has brought legal proceedings.

###### Article 1450

The action for compensation based on the provisions of this subsection is prescribed after three years from the date on which the claimant became aware, or should have become aware, of the damage, the defect and the identity of the producer.

###### Article 1451

The provisions of this chapter do not affect the rights which the victim of damage may invoke under the law of contractual or non-contractual liability or under a special liability regime.
The producer remains liable for the consequences of his fault and that of persons for whom he is responsible.

Sous-titre III : Les quasi-contrats Article 1452
Quasi-contracts are purely voluntary acts which result in an obligation on the part of the person who benefits from them without being entitled to do so, and sometimes an obligation on the part of their author towards another person.
The quasi-contracts governed by this subtitle are: management of another's affairs, undue payment and unjust enrichment.
Chapitre Ier : La gestion d'affaires

###### Article 1453

A person who, without being obliged to do so, knowingly and usefully manages the affairs of another, without the knowledge or without the opposition of the owner of those affairs, is subject, in the performance of the legal and material acts of his management, to all the obligations of a mandatary.
The usefulness of the act of the manager is assessed at the date when it was performed.

###### Article 1454

This manager of another's affairs is required to bring to his management all the care of a reasonable person. He must continue the management begun, until the owner of the affairs or his successor is in a position to provide for it.

The judge may, according to the circumstances, mitigate the damages which would result from the faults or negligence of the manager.

###### Article 1455

The person whose affairs have been usefully managed must fulfil the obligations contracted in his interest by the manager.
He reimburses the manager for useful or necessary expenses incurred in his interest, and indemnifies him for the damage he has suffered by reason of his management.
The sums advanced by the manager bear interest from the day of payment.

###### Article 1456

Ratification of the management by the owner is equivalent to express mandate.

###### Article 1457

The fact that the manager has a personal interest in taking charge of the affairs of another does not exclude the application of the rules on management of another's affairs.
In that case, the burden of obligations, expenses and damage is apportioned in proportion to the interests of each in the common affair.

###### Article 1458

If the action of the manager does not meet the conditions for management of another's affairs but nevertheless benefits the owner of those affairs, the latter must indemnify the manager according to the rules on unjust enrichment.

#### Chapter II: Payment of the Undue Article 1459

Every payment presupposes a debt; what has been received without being due is subject to restitution.
Restitution is not admitted with regard to natural obligations that have been voluntarily discharged.

###### Article 1460

He who receives by error or knowingly what is not due to him must restore it to him from whom he unduly received it.

###### Article 1461

He who by error or under duress has discharged the debt of another may bring an action for restitution against the creditor.
Nevertheless this right ceases in the case where the creditor, following the payment, has destroyed his title or abandoned the securities that guaranteed his claim.
Restitution may also be demanded from him whose debt has been discharged by error.

###### Article 1462

Restitution is subject to the rules set out in articles 1577 to 1585. It may be reduced if the payment proceeds from a fault.

#### Chapter III: Unjust Enrichment

###### Article 1463

Outside the cases of management of affairs and payment of the undue, he who benefits from an enrichment without cause to the detriment of another owes, to him who finds himself impoverished thereby, an indemnity equal to the lesser of the two values of the enrichment and the impoverishment.

###### Article 1464

Enrichment is without cause when it proceeds neither from the performance of an obligation by the impoverished party nor from his gratuitous intention.

###### Article 1465

There is no ground for indemnification if the impoverishment proceeds from an act performed by the impoverished party with a view to personal profit.
Indemnification may be moderated by the judge if the impoverishment proceeds from a fault of the impoverished party.

### Title IV: General Regime of Obligations

Chapter I: Modalities of the Obligation

##### Section I: The Conditional Obligation Article 1466

An obligation is conditional when it depends on a future and uncertain event, or on an event that has already occurred but is still unknown to the parties.
In the first case, the condition is either suspensive, when the birth of the obligation depends on its fulfillment, or resolutory, when its fulfillment brings about the annulment of the juridical act it concerns.
In the second case, the obligation has its effect from the day on which it was contracted.

###### Article 1467

Any condition of an impossible thing, or contrary to good morals, or prohibited by law is null, and renders null the agreement that depends on it. This nullity is absolute.
The condition not to do an impossible thing does not render null the obligation contracted under this condition.

###### Article 1468

Any obligation is null when it has been contracted under a condition whose realization depends on the sole will of the debtor.
This nullity, which is relative, may not however be invoked when the obligation has been performed with full knowledge by him who was bound by it.

###### Article 1469

Every condition must be fulfilled in the manner that the parties probably wished and intended that it be fulfilled.
The suspensive condition is deemed fulfilled when it is the debtor, obligated under this condition, who has prevented its fulfillment.

The resolutory condition is deemed to have failed if its fulfillment has been provoked by the party who had an interest therein.

###### Article 1470

When an obligation is contracted under the condition that an event will occur within a fixed time, this condition is deemed to have failed when the time has expired without the event having occurred. If there is no fixed time, the condition may always be fulfilled; and it is deemed to have failed only when it has become certain that the event will not occur.

###### Article 1471

When an obligation is contracted under the condition that an event will not occur within a fixed time, this condition is fulfilled when that time has expired without the event having occurred: it is also fulfilled, if before the term it is certain that the event will not occur; and if there is no determined time, it is fulfilled only when it is certain that the event will not occur.

###### Article 1472

A party is free to renounce the condition stipulated in his exclusive interest, as long as it is not fulfilled.

###### Article 1473

The fulfilled condition has a retroactive effect to the day on which the engagement was contracted. If the creditor died before the fulfillment of the condition, his rights pass to his heir.

###### Article 1474

Before the suspensive condition is fulfilled, the debtor must refrain from any act that would prevent the proper performance of the obligation.
The creditor may, before the condition is fulfilled, exercise all conservatory acts of his right and challenge the acts of the debtor performed in fraud of his rights.
What has been paid may be recovered as long as the suspensive condition has not been fulfilled.

###### Article 1475

When the obligation has been contracted under a suspensive condition, the thing that is the subject matter of the agreement remains at the risk of the debtor of the obligation to deliver this thing and this, until the fulfillment of the condition. He retains the administration thereof and has the right to the fruits until the fulfillment of the condition.
If the thing has entirely perished without the fault of the debtor, the obligation is extinguished.

If the thing has deteriorated without the fault of the debtor, the creditor has the choice either to rescind the obligation, or to demand the thing in the state in which it is found, without reduction of the price.
If the thing has deteriorated by the fault of the debtor, the creditor has the right either to rescind the obligation, or to demand the thing in the state in which it is found, with damages.

###### Article 1476

The fulfillment of the suspensive condition gives rise to all the effects that were linked to its realization. However, the parties may provide that the fulfillment of the condition will retroact to the day of the contract.

###### Article 1477

In case of failure of the suspensive condition, the obligation is deemed never to have existed; if the suspensive condition concerned all the effects of the contract, the latter becomes lapsed.

###### Article 1478

In case of a resolutory condition, the resolution must be sought in court. The judge may grant the defendant a delay according to the circumstances.
The fulfillment of the resolutory condition extinguishes the obligation retroactively, without calling into question, where applicable, the conservatory and administrative acts and the collection of fruits. If the thing has perished before the fulfillment of the condition, the realized risks are for the creditor of the obligation to deliver this thing.

Retroactivity does not take place if such is the agreement of the parties or if the exchanged performances have found their utility as the reciprocal performance of the contract progressed.

##### Section II: The Obligation with a Term Article 1479

An obligation is with a term when its enforceability is deferred until the occurrence of a future and certain event, even though the date thereof is uncertain.

###### Article 1480

The term may be express or tacit.

###### Article 1481

What is due only at a term, may not be demanded before the expiry of the term; but what has been paid in advance may not be recovered.
The creditor of the obligation affected by a term may exercise all conservatory acts of his right and act against the acts of the debtor performed in fraud of his rights.

###### Article 1482

The term benefits the debtor, unless it results from the law, the will of the parties or the circumstances that it has been established in favor of the creditor or of both parties.
The party for whose exclusive benefit the term has been fixed may renounce it without the consent of the other.

###### Article 1483

The debtor may no longer claim the benefit of the term when he has become bankrupt, or if he does not provide the security promised to the creditor or diminishes that which guarantees the obligation.

###### Article 1484

The forfeiture of the term incurred by a debtor may not be invoked against his co-obligors, even if they are jointly and severally liable.

##### Section III : L'obligation plurale

###### Sous-section 1 : La pluralité d'objets Article 1485

An obligation is facultative when it has as its object a certain performance but the debtor has the option, in order to discharge himself, of providing another.

A facultative obligation is extinguished if the performance of the initially agreed performance becomes impossible by reason of force majeure.

###### Article 1486

An obligation is alternative when it has as its object several performances and the performance of one of them discharges the debtor.
The choice between the performances to be executed belongs to the debtor, if it has not been expressly granted to the creditor. The debtor may discharge himself by delivering one of the things promised; but he may not force the creditor to receive part of one and part of another.

If the choice is not exercised within the agreed time or within a reasonable period, the other party may, after formal notice, exercise that choice or terminate the contract.
The choice, once it is exercised, is final and causes the obligation to lose its alternative character. The alternative obligation then becomes pure and simple.

###### Article 1487

When the obligation is alternative and the choice has been exercised, the impossibility of performing the chosen performance by reason of force majeure discharges the debtor.
If the debtor has not made his choice known at the time when the impossibility materializes, he must, if one of the performances becomes impossible, perform one of the others. When the performances become impossible, the debtor is discharged only if the impossibility proceeds, for each, from force majeure.

If the creditor has not made his choice known, he must, if one of the performances becomes impossible to perform as a result of force majeure, be satisfied with one of the others.

###### Article 1488

When the performances become impossible, the debtor is discharged only if the impossibility proceeds, for each, from force majeure.

###### Sous-section 2 : La pluralité de sujets

###### Article 1489

An obligation that binds several creditors or debtors is divided by operation of law between them. The division also takes place between their successors, even if the obligation is joint and several. If it is not otherwise regulated by law or by contract, the division takes place in equal shares.
Each of the creditors is entitled only to his share of the common claim; each of the debtors is liable only for his share of the common debt.
It is otherwise, in the relations between the creditors and the debtors, only if the obligation is joint and several or if the performance due is indivisible.

###### § 1. De l'obligation solidaire Article 1490

Joint and several liability is legal or conventional; it is not presumed.

###### Article 1491

Joint and several liability between creditors allows each of them to demand and receive payment of the entire claim. Payment made to one of them, who must account for it to the others, discharges the debtor with respect to all.
The debtor may pay one or the other of the joint and several creditors as long as he is not sued by one of them.
The remission granted by one of the joint and several creditors discharges the debtor only for the share of that creditor.

###### Article 1492

Any act that interrupts or suspends prescription with respect to one of the joint and several creditors benefits the other creditors.

###### Article 1493

Joint and several liability between debtors obliges each of them for the entire debt.
The obligation may be joint and several, although one of the debtors is obliged differently from the other for payment of the same thing; for example, if one is obliged only conditionally, while the engagement of the other is pure and simple, or if one has taken a term that is not granted to the other.

The creditor may demand payment from the joint and several debtor of his choice, without the latter being able to invoke against him the benefit of division.
Proceedings brought against one of the joint and several debtors do not prevent the creditor from bringing similar proceedings against the others.

Payment made by one of them discharges them all towards the creditor.

###### Article 1494

Proceedings brought against one of the joint and several debtors interrupt prescription with respect to all.

###### Article 1495

A demand for interest made against one of the joint and several debtors causes interest to run with respect to all.

###### Article 1496

A joint and several debtor sued by the creditor may raise defenses that are common to all the co-debtors, such as nullity that is not purely personal to that debtor or termination, and those that are personal to him such as incapacity or a defect of consent affecting his will.
He may not raise defenses that are personal to other co-debtors, such as the granting of a term. However, when a defense personal to another co-debtor extinguishes the divided share of the latter, particularly in case of set-off or remission of debt, he may rely on it to have it deducted from the total debt.

###### Article 1497

If the thing due has perished through the fault of one or more of the joint and several debtors or at a date when one or more of the joint and several debtors were in default in performing, the other co-debtors remain liable to pay the price of the thing; but these other co-debtors are not liable to pay damages.

###### Article 1498
