Personal claims that spouses have to exercise against each other do not give rise to withdrawal and bear interest only from the day of formal demand.

Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, these personal claims that spouses have to exercise against each other are valued according to the rules of Article 1697, in the cases provided for therein; interest then runs from the day of liquidation.

###### Article 1708

Gifts that one spouse may have made to the other are executed only on the donor's share in the community and on his or her personal assets.

###### § 3

De l'obligation et de la contribution au passif après la dissolution Article 1709
Each spouse may be sued for the totality of debts existing on the day of dissolution that had entered the community on his or her behalf.

###### Article 1710

Each spouse may be sued only for half of the debts that had entered into the community on account of his or her spouse.
After partition and except in case of concealment, the spouse who is not personally bound is liable only up to the amount of his or her emolument, that is to say up to the amount of the active share of the community that he or she receives, provided that an inventory has been made, and subject to accounting for both the contents of that inventory and what has fallen to him or her by partition as well as the common liabilities already discharged.

###### Article 1711

The inventory provided for in Article 1710 must take place in the forms prescribed by the code of civil procedure, adversarially with the other spouse or with him or her duly summoned. It must be closed within nine months from the day on which the community was dissolved, except for an extension granted by the judge in summary proceedings. It must be affirmed sincere and true before the public officer who received it.

###### Article 1712

Each spouse contributes half to the community debts for which no compensation was due, as well as to the costs of sealing, inventory, sale of movables, liquidation, licitation and partition.
When the debt was definitively incumbent on only one of the spouses and the other spouse nevertheless contributed, the latter is entitled to corresponding compensation.

###### Article 1713

The spouse who may avail himself or herself of the benefit of Article 1710, second paragraph, does not contribute for more than the active share of the community that he or she receives, to the debts that had entered into the community on account of the other spouse, unless they are debts for which he or she would have owed compensation.

###### Article 1714

The spouse who has paid beyond the portion for which he or she was liable by application of the preceding articles has, against the other, recourse for the excess.

###### Article 1715

He or she has no claim, for that excess, against the creditor, unless the receipt expresses that he or she intends to pay only within the limit of his or her obligation.

###### Article 1716

The one of the two spouses who, by the effect of a mortgage exercised on the immovable fallen to him or her in partition, is sued for the totality of a community debt, has by right his or her recourse against the other for half of that debt.

###### Article 1717

The provisions of the preceding articles do not prevent a clause of the partition from obliging one or the other of the spouses to pay a quota of debts other than that which is fixed above, or even to discharge the liabilities entirely, without prejudice to the rights of third parties.

###### Article 1718

The heirs of the spouses exercise, in case of dissolution of the community, the same rights as the spouse whom they represent and are subject to the same obligations.

##### Section II : De la communauté conventionnelle Article 1719

The spouses may, in their marriage contract, modify the legal community by any kind of agreements not contrary to Articles 1633, 1635 and 1636.
They may, in particular, agree:
1° That the community shall include movables and acquests; 2° That the rules concerning administration shall be derogated from;
3° That one of the spouses shall have the power to withdraw certain property subject to compensation; 4° That one of the spouses shall have received sums or property outside the succession share;
5° That the spouses shall have unequal shares;
6° That there shall be universal community between them.

The rules of the legal community remain applicable in all points that have not been the subject of the agreement of the parties.

###### Sous-section 1 : De la communauté de meubles et acquêts Article 1720

When the spouses agree that there shall be between them community of movables and acquests, the common assets include, in addition to the property that would form part of it under the legal community regime, the movable property of which the spouses had ownership or possession on the day of the marriage or which has fallen to them since by succession or liberality, unless the donor or testator has stipulated otherwise.

Nevertheless, those of these movable properties that would have formed separate property by their nature under Article 1651, under the legal regime, if they had been acquired during the community, remain separate.
If one of the spouses had acquired an immovable since the marriage contract, containing a stipulation of community of movables and acquests, and before the celebration of the marriage, the immovable acquired in that interval shall enter into the community, unless the acquisition was made in execution of some clause of the marriage contract, in which case it would be governed according to the agreement.

###### Article 1721

Enter into the common liabilities, under this regime, in addition to the debts that would form part of it under the legal regime, a fraction of those with which the spouses were already burdened when they married, or with which the successions and liberalities that fall to them during the marriage are charged.
The fraction of liabilities that the community must bear is proportional to the fraction of assets that it receives according to the rules of Article 1720, either in the patrimony of the spouse on the day of the marriage, or in the totality of the property that is the subject of the succession or liberality.

For the establishment of this proportion, the composition and value of the assets are proved in accordance with Article 1649.

###### Article 1722

The debts for which the community is liable in consideration of the property it receives are its definitive charge.

###### Article 1723

The distribution of liabilities prior to the marriage or burdening successions and liberalities may not prejudice creditors. They retain, in all cases, the right to seize the property that formerly formed their security. They may even pursue their payment on the whole of the community when the movables of their debtor have been merged into the common patrimony and can no longer be identified according to the rules of Article 1649.

###### Sous-section 2 :De la clause d'administration conjointe Article 1724

The spouses may agree that they shall administer the community jointly.
In that case acts of administration and disposition of common property are made under the joint signature of the two spouses. This double signature entails by operation of law joint and several liability for the obligations subscribed. Conservatory acts may be made separately by each spouse.

###### Sous-section 3 : De la clause de prélèvement moyennant indemnité Article 1725

The spouses may stipulate that the survivor of them or one of them if he or she survives, or even one of them in all cases of dissolution of the community, shall have the power to withdraw certain common property, subject to accounting for it to the community according to the value they shall have on the day of partition, if it has not been otherwise agreed.

###### Article 1726

The marriage contract may fix bases of valuation and terms of payment of the possible balancing payment. Taking into account these clauses and in the absence of agreement between the parties, the value of the property shall be fixed by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 1727

The power of withdrawal lapses if the beneficiary spouse has not exercised it by a notification made to the other spouse or to his or her heirs within a period of one month from the day on which they shall have put him or her on notice to take a position. This notice itself may not take place before the expiration of the periods provided for in Article 906 for making an inventory and deliberating.

###### Article 1728

The withdrawal is a partition operation: the property withdrawn is imputed to the share of the beneficiary spouse; if their value exceeds that share, there is occasion for the payment of a balancing payment.
The spouses may agree that the compensation due by the author of the withdrawal shall be imputed subsidiarily to his or her rights in the succession of the predeceased spouse.

###### Sous-section 4

The attribution, to the spouse, of sums or property outside the succession share Article 1729
It may be agreed, in the marriage contract, that the survivor of the spouses, or one of them if he or she survives, shall be authorized to withdraw from the community, before any partition, either a certain sum, or certain property in kind, or a certain quantity of a specified type of property.

###### Article 1730

This attribution outside the succession share is not regarded as a donation, either as to substance or as to form, but as a marriage contract and between partners.

###### Article 1731

When the community is dissolved during the lifetime of the spouses, there is no place for the delivery of the sums and property whose attribution is provided for outside the succession share; but the spouse in whose favor it was stipulated retains his or her rights in the event of survival, subject to Article 291.
He or she may require security from his or her spouse as a guarantee of his or her rights.

###### Article 1732

The creditors of the community always have the right to have the property included outside the succession share sold, subject to the spouse's recourse against the remainder of the community.

###### Sous-section 5: On the stipulation of unequal shares Article 1733

The spouses may derogate from the equal partition established by law.

###### Article 1734

When it has been stipulated that the spouse or his or her heirs shall have only a certain share in the community, such as one-third or one-quarter, the spouse thus reduced or his or her heirs bear the debts of the community only in proportion to the share they take in the assets.
The agreement is null if it obliges the spouse thus reduced or his or her heirs to bear a greater share, or if it exempts them from bearing a share in the debts equal to that which they take in the assets.

###### Article 1735

The attribution of the entire community may be agreed only for the event of survival, either in favor of a designated spouse, or in favor of whichever spouse survives. The spouse who thus retains the totality of the community is obliged to pay all its debts.
It may also be agreed, for the event of survival, that one of the spouses shall have, in addition to his or her half, the usufruct of the share of the predeceased. In this case, he or she shall contribute to the debts, as to the usufruct, according to the rules of Articles 714 and following of this code.
The provisions of Article 1731 are applicable to these clauses when the community is dissolved during the lifetime of both spouses.

###### Article 1736

The stipulation of unequal shares and the clause of full attribution are not deemed to constitute donations, either as to substance or as to form, but simply marriage contracts and between partners. Unless otherwise stipulated, they do not prevent the heirs of the predeceased spouse from recovering the contributions and capital that fell into the community from their predecessor.

###### Sous-section 6: On universal community

The spouses may establish by their marriage contract a universal community of their property both movable and immovable, present and future. However, unless otherwise stipulated, the property that Article 1651 declares separate by its nature does not fall into this community.

The universal community definitively bears all the debts of the spouses, present and future.

##### Section III

Provisions common to the first two sections of Chapter II Article 1738
The advantages that either spouse may derive from the clauses of a conventional community, as well as those that may result from the merger of movable property or debts, are not regarded as constituting donations.

Nevertheless, in the event that there are children who are not issue of both spouses, any agreement that would have the consequence of giving to one of the spouses beyond the portion regulated by Article 1228, under the title Of Donations Inter Vivos and Testaments, shall be without effect for the entire excess; but the simple benefits resulting from common work and savings made from the respective incomes, although unequal, of the two spouses, are not considered as an advantage made to the prejudice of children of another marriage.

#### Chapter III: On the regime of separation of property Article 1739

When the spouses have stipulated in their marriage contract that they would be separated as to property, each of them retains the administration, enjoyment and free disposal of his or her personal property.

Each of them remains solely liable for debts arising in his or her person before or during the marriage, except in the case of Article 228.

###### Article 1740

The spouses contribute to the charges of the marriage according to the agreements contained in their contract; and, if none exist in this regard, in the proportion determined in Article 222.

###### Article 1741

Both with regard to his or her spouse and to third parties, a spouse may prove by all means that he or she has exclusive ownership of property.
The presumptions of ownership stated in the marriage contract have effect with regard to third parties as well as in relations between spouses, unless otherwise agreed. Proof to the contrary shall be permitted, and it shall be made by all means proper to establish that the property does not belong to the spouse whom the presumption designates, or even, if it belongs to him or her, that he or she acquired it by a liberality from the other spouse.

Property over which neither spouse can establish exclusive ownership is deemed to belong to them jointly, to each for one-half.

###### Article 1742

If, during the marriage, one of the spouses entrusts to the other the administration of his or her personal property, the rules of mandate are applicable. The mandatary spouse is, however, dispensed from accounting for the fruits, when the power of attorney does not expressly oblige him or her to do so.

When one of the spouses takes in hand the management of the property of the other, with the knowledge of the latter, and nevertheless without opposition on his or her part, he or she is deemed to have received a tacit mandate, covering acts of administration and management, but not acts of disposition.

This spouse is responsible for his or her management to the other as a mandatary. He or she is, however, accountable only for existing fruits; for those that he or she neglected to collect or fraudulently consumed, he or she may be pursued only within the limit of the last five years.

If it is in defiance of a recorded opposition that one of the spouses interfered in the management of the property of the other, he or she is responsible for all the consequences of his or her interference, and accountable without limitation for all the fruits that he or she collected, neglected to collect or consumed.

###### Article 1744

A spouse is not guarantor of the failure to invest or reinvest the property of the other, unless he or she interfered in the operations of alienation or collection, or unless it is proved that the monies were received by him or her, or were used for his or her benefit.

###### Article 1745

After the dissolution of the marriage by the death of one of the spouses, the partition of undivided property between spouses separated as to property, with respect to all that concerns its forms, the maintenance of the indivision and preferential attribution, the sale by auction of property, the effects of partition, the warranty and the balancing payments, is subject to all the rules that are established under the title Of Successions for partitions between co-heirs.
The same rules apply after divorce or legal separation. However, preferential attribution is never of right. It may always be decided that the totality of any balancing payment due shall be payable in cash.

###### Article 1746

The rules of Article 1707 are applicable to claims that one of the spouses may have to exercise against the other.

#### Chapter IV: Of the participation in acquisitions regime Article 1747

When spouses have declared that they are marrying under the participation in acquisitions regime, each of them retains the administration, enjoyment and free disposal of their personal property, without distinguishing between that which belonged to them on the day of marriage or came to them since by succession or liberality and that which they acquired during the marriage for valuable consideration. During the marriage, this regime functions as if the spouses were married under the separation of property regime. Upon dissolution of the regime, each spouse has the right to participate for half in value in the net acquisitions found in the patrimony of the other, and measured by the double valuation of the original patrimony and the final patrimony.
The right to participate in acquisitions is not transferable as long as the matrimonial regime is not dissolved. If dissolution occurs by the death of a spouse, their heirs have, over the net acquisitions made by the other, the same rights as their predecessor.

###### Article 1748

The original patrimony includes the property that belonged to the spouse on the day of marriage and that which they acquired since by succession or liberality, as well as all property which, in the legal community regime, forms separate property by nature without giving rise to compensation. No account is taken of the fruits of this property, nor of those of this property which would have had the character of fruits or which the spouse disposed of by inter vivos donation during the marriage.

The composition of the original patrimony is proved by a descriptive statement, even under private signature, established in the presence of the other spouse and signed by them. In the absence of a descriptive statement or if it is incomplete, proof of the composition of the original patrimony can only be provided by the means of article 1649.

###### Article 1749

Original property is valued according to its condition on the day of marriage or acquisition, and according to its value on the day the matrimonial regime is liquidated. If it has been alienated, its value on the day of alienation is retained. If new property has been subrogated to the alienated property, the value of this new property is taken into consideration.
From the original assets are deducted the debts with which it was encumbered, revalued, if applicable, according to the rules of article 1697. If the liabilities exceed the assets, this excess is fictitiously added to the final patrimony.

###### Article 1750

The final patrimony includes all property that belongs to the spouse on the day the matrimonial regime is dissolved, including, where applicable, that which they would have disposed of by reason of death and without excluding the sums of which they may be creditor towards their spouse. If there is divorce, legal separation or early liquidation of acquisitions, the matrimonial regime is deemed dissolved on the day of the application.
The composition of the final patrimony is proved by a descriptive statement, even under private signature, which the spouse or their heirs must establish in the presence of the other spouse or their heirs or they being duly summoned. This statement must be drawn up within nine months of the dissolution of the matrimonial regime, except for extension by the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance ruling in summary proceedings.

Proof that the final patrimony would have included other property may be provided by all means, even by testimony and presumptions.

Each spouse may, as to the property of the other, require the affixing of seals and inventory according to the rules provided in the code of civil procedure.

###### Article 1751

To existing property are fictitiously added property that does not appear in the original patrimony and which the spouse disposed of by inter vivos donation without the consent of their spouse, as well as that which they would have alienated fraudulently. Alienation subject to life annuity or as a life interest is presumed made in fraud of the rights of the spouse, if the latter did not consent to it.

###### Article 1752

Existing property is valued according to its condition at the time of dissolution of the matrimonial regime and according to its value on the day of liquidation thereof. Property that has been alienated by inter vivos donations, or in fraud of the rights of the spouse, is valued according to its condition on the day of alienation and the value it would have had, if it had been preserved, on the day of liquidation.
From the assets thus reconstituted, all debts that have not yet been paid are deducted, including sums that might be owed to the spouse. The value, on the day of alienation, of improvements that had been made during the marriage to original property given by a spouse without the consent of their spouse before the dissolution of the matrimonial regime must be added to the final patrimony.

###### Article 1753

If the final patrimony of a spouse is less than their original patrimony, the deficit is borne entirely by that spouse. If it is greater, the increase represents the net acquisitions and gives rise to participation.

If there are net acquisitions on both sides, they must first be offset. Only the excess is shared
: the spouse whose gain was the lesser is creditor of their spouse for half of this excess.

To the participation claim are added, to subject them to the same settlement, the sums of which the spouse may be otherwise creditor towards their spouse, for values provided during the marriage and other compensation, after deduction, if applicable, of what they may owe to them.

###### Article 1754

The participation claim gives rise to payment in money. If the debtor spouse encounters serious difficulties in discharging it entirely upon closure of the liquidation, the judges may grant them delays that shall not exceed five years, subject to providing security and paying interest. The amount of this interest is determined by mutual agreement and, failing that, the legal interest rate shall apply.
The participation claim may however give rise to settlement in kind, either with the consent of both spouses, or by virtue of a decision of the judge, if the debtor spouse justifies serious difficulties that prevent them from discharging in money.
The settlement in kind provided for in the preceding paragraph is considered a partition transaction when the property attributed was not included in the original patrimony or when the attributee spouse succeeds to the other.

The liquidation is not enforceable against the creditors of the spouses: they retain the right to seize the property attributed to the spouse of their debtor.

###### Article 1755

The creditor spouse pursues recovery of their participation claim first on existing property and, subsidiarily, beginning with the most recent alienations, on the property mentioned in article 1751 that had been alienated by inter vivos donation or in fraud of the rights of the spouse.

###### Article 1756

Upon dissolution of the matrimonial regime, if the parties do not agree to proceed with liquidation by agreement, one of them may request the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance to proceed with it.
Applicable to this application, as appropriate, are the rules prescribed to arrive at judicial partition of successions and communities.

The parties are required to communicate to each other reciprocally, and to communicate to the experts appointed by the judge, all information and documents useful for the liquidation. The action for liquidation is prescribed after three years from the dissolution of the matrimonial regime. Actions brought against third parties by virtue of article 920, paragraph 4, are prescribed after two years from the closure of the liquidation.

###### Article 1757

If the application of the valuation rules provided for by Articles 1749 and 1752 were to lead to a result manifestly contrary to equity, which the judge must specifically justify, the court may derogate therefrom at the request of one of the spouses.

###### Article 1758

If the disorder of a spouse's affairs, his or her poor administration or misconduct, give rise to fear that the continuation of the matrimonial regime may compromise the interests of the other spouse, the latter may request early liquidation of his or her participation claim.
The rules of separation of property apply to this request. When the request is granted, the spouses are placed under the regime of Articles 1739 to 1744.

###### Article 1759

By stipulating participation in acquests, the spouses may adopt any clauses not contrary to Articles 1633, 1635 and 1636. They may in particular agree to a clause of unequal division, or stipulate that the survivor of them or one of them if he or she survives, shall be entitled to all of the net acquests made by the other. It may also be agreed between the spouses that the one of them who, upon liquidation of the regime, will have a participation claim against the other, may require payment in kind of certain property of his or her spouse, if he or she establishes that he or she has an essential interest in having them attributed to him or her.

### Titre VII : De la vente

Chapitre Ier. De la nature et de la forme de la vente Article 1760
Sale is a contract by which one party undertakes to deliver a thing, and the other to pay for it. It may be made by authentic deed, by private signature, or verbally.

###### Article 1761

The sale is perfect between the parties, and ownership is acquired by right by the buyer with regard to the seller, as soon as the parties have agreed on the thing and on its price, even if the thing has not yet been delivered nor the price paid.

###### Article 1762

The sale may be made purely and simply, or subject to a condition, which may be suspensive or resolutory.
It may also have as its object two or more alternative things.

In all these cases, its effect is governed by the general principles provided for by this code and which govern the contract.

###### Article 1763

When goods are not sold in bulk, but by weight, count or measure, the sale is not perfect: the things sold remain at the seller's risk until they are weighed, counted or measured; but, in case of non-performance of his undertaking by the seller, the buyer may request delivery of the thing or damages, if applicable.
On the other hand, if the goods have been sold in bulk, the sale is perfect, regardless of the fact that the goods have not yet been weighed, counted or measured.

###### Article 1764

In case of sale on trial, as for wine, oil, and other things which one is in the habit of tasting before purchasing them, there is no sale until the buyer has tasted and approved them.
Such a sale is always presumed to be made subject to a suspensive condition.

###### Article 1765

A promise to sell is equivalent to a sale, as soon as there is mutual consent of both parties on the thing and on the price.
When a unilateral promise to sell land already subdivided or to be subdivided is signed, the exercise of the option necessarily results from payment of part of the price by the beneficiary of the promise, whatever

the name given by the parties to this payment, provided that he has taken possession of the immovable property which is the subject of the deed.

The date of the agreement, even if subsequently formalized, shall be that of payment of the first instalment.

###### Article 1766

Any unilateral undertaking entered into with a view to acquiring immovable property or an immovable right for which a payment is required or received from the person undertaking it, whatever its cause and form, is null and void.

###### Article 1767

If it is not evidenced by an authentic deed or by a deed under private signature registered within ten days from the date of its acceptance by the beneficiary, any unilateral promise to sell relating to an immovable, an immovable right, a business, a right to a lease relating to all or part of an immovable, or to shares of companies whose shares or units confer on their holders the right to enjoyment of immovables or fractions of immovables and to those of companies which have, in fact, as their sole purpose either the construction or acquisition of immovables or groups of immovables with a view to their division into fractions intended to be allocated to the members in ownership or enjoyment, or the management of these immovables or groups of immovables thus divided, or the lease on behalf of one or more members of the company of all or part of the immovables or fractions of immovables belonging to each of these members, is null and void.
The same applies to any assignment relating to said promises which has not been the subject of an authentic deed or a deed under private signature registered within ten days of its date.

###### Article 1768

If the promise to sell has been made with a deposit each of the contracting parties has the possibility of withdrawing from the contract:
The one who gave it, by forfeiting the sum represented by the deposit paid, And the one who received the deposit, by returning double the sum received.
Unless otherwise stipulated, for any contract of sale or provision of services concluded between a professional and a consumer, sums paid in advance are deposits.

###### Article 1769

The price of the sale must be determined and designated by the parties.

###### Article 1770

The parties to the contract may however designate a third party to estimate the price of the sale; if the third party does not wish or cannot make the estimate, there is no sale.
If the expert has not been designated due to the silence or conduct of one of the parties to the contract, its non-performance is resolved in damages.
The price fixed by the expert may only be challenged in case of gross error on his part in its determination.

###### Article 1771

Unless otherwise stipulated, the costs of deeds and other accessories to the sale are borne by the buyer.

#### Chapitre II. Qui peut acheter ou vendre Article 1772

All those whom the law does not prohibit may buy or sell.

###### Article 1773

The contract of sale may not take place between spouses except in the following three cases:
1° Where one of the two spouses transfers property to the other, judicially separated from him or her, in payment of his or her rights;
2° Where the transfer that the husband makes to his wife, even if not separated, has a legitimate cause, such as the reinvestment of her alienated immovables, or of money belonging to her, if these immovables or money do not fall into community property;
3° Where the wife transfers property to her husband in payment of a sum which she would have promised him as a dowry, and when there is exclusion of community property;
subject, in these three cases, to the rights of the heirs of the contracting parties, if there is an indirect advantage.

###### Article 1774

May not become purchasers, on pain of nullity, either by themselves or through intermediaries:
-	guardians, of the property of those of whom they have guardianship;
-	mandataries, of the property which they are charged with selling;
-	administrators, of those of the communes or public establishments entrusted to their care;
-	public officers, of the national property the sales of which are made through their ministry.
-	fiduciaries, of the property or rights composing the fiduciary patrimony.

###### Article 1775

It is prohibited for persons invested with judicial functions, such as judges, their deputies, public prosecutors, court clerks, bailiffs, notaries, lawyers or any other person authorized to represent others in court, to acquire rights or actions that may be contested before the court within whose jurisdiction they exercise their functions.

#### Chapitre III. Des choses qui peuvent être vendues Article 1776

Unless otherwise provided by law, anything that is in commerce may be sold.

###### Article 1777

The following are null and void:
1° The sale of another person's property. Such a sale may give rise to damages when the buyer was unaware that the property belonged to another;
2° The succession of a living person, even with their consent;
3° The sale of a thing that did not exist or no longer existed at the time of the sale. The purchaser may then, at their choice, abandon the sale or request the preserved part of the thing with a reduction in price in a proportion analogous to that of the loss incurred.

#### Chapitre IV. De la vente d'immeubles à construire Article 1778

The sale of immovable property to be constructed is that by which the seller undertakes to erect an immovable property within a time period determined by the contract.
It may be concluded on a fixed term basis or in a future state of completion.

###### Article 1779

The fixed term sale is the contract by which the seller undertakes to deliver the immovable property upon its completion, the buyer undertakes to take delivery of it and to pay the price on the date of delivery. The transfer of

ownership takes effect by operation of law upon the recording by authentic deed of the completion of the immovable property; it produces its effects retroactively to the day of the sale.

###### Article 1780

The sale in a future state of completion is the contract by which the seller immediately transfers to the purchaser their rights over the land as well as the ownership of existing constructions. Future works become the property of the purchaser as and when they are executed; the purchaser is required to pay the price as the works progress.
The seller retains the powers of project owner until acceptance of the works.

###### Article 1781

The assignment by the purchaser of the rights they hold from a sale of immovable property to be constructed substitutes by operation of law the assignee in the purchaser's obligations towards the seller.
If the sale was accompanied by a mandate, it continues between the seller and the assignee.
These provisions apply to any transfer inter vivos, voluntary or forced, or upon death.

#### Chapitre V. Des obligations du vendeur

##### Section I : Dispositions générales Article 1782

The seller is required to explain clearly what they undertake to do. Any obscure or ambiguous clause is interpreted against the seller.
In contracts proposed by professionals to consumers, the clauses must be presented and drafted in a clear and comprehensible manner. In case of doubt, they are interpreted in the sense most favorable to the consumer.

###### Article 1783

The seller has two principal obligations: that of delivering and that of guaranteeing the thing they sell.

##### Section II : De la délivrance Article 1784

Delivery consists in making available to the buyer the thing sold so that the buyer may use it, enjoy it and dispose of it materially.
Delivery must take place at the location where, at the time of the sale, the thing that was the object thereof was located, unless otherwise agreed.

###### Article 1785

The obligation to deliver immovable property is fulfilled on the part of the seller when they have handed over the keys, if it is a building, or when they have handed over the title deeds.

###### Article 1786

Delivery of movable property takes place:
-	by handing over the thing to the purchaser;
-	by handing over the keys to the buildings that contain them;

-	or by the mere consent of the parties, if the transport thereof cannot take place at the time of the sale, or if the buyer already had them in their possession under another title.

###### Article 1787

Delivery of incorporeal rights takes place by handing over the title deeds, signing transfer orders, or by the use that the purchaser makes of them with the seller's consent.

###### Article 1788

Unless otherwise stipulated, the costs of delivery are borne by the seller, and those of removal are borne by the buyer.

###### Article 1789

If the seller fails to make delivery within the time agreed between the parties, the purchaser may, at their choice, request the resolution of the sale or their being put in possession, if the delay arises only from the seller's act.
The burden of proof that they made the thing sold available to the buyer within the agreed time period lies with the seller.

###### Article 1790

In all cases where the purchaser suffers damage due to failure to deliver at the agreed term, the seller is ordered to pay them compensatory damages.

###### Article 1791

The seller is not required to deliver the thing if the buyer does not pay the price thereof, and the seller has not granted them a time period for payment.
They will also not be obliged to deliver, even though they had granted a time period for payment, if, since the sale, the buyer has become bankrupt, so that the seller is in imminent danger of losing the price; unless the buyer gives them security to pay at the term.

###### Article 1792

The thing must be delivered in the state in which it is at the time of the sale.

From that day, unless otherwise agreed, all fruits belong to the purchaser.

###### Article 1793

The obligation to deliver the thing includes its accessories and everything that has been intended for its perpetual use.

###### Article 1794

The seller is required to deliver the area as it is stated in the contract, subject to the modifications set out below.

###### Article 1795

If the sale of an immovable property has been made with indication of the area, at a rate of so much per unit of measurement, the seller is obliged to deliver to the purchaser, if they require it, the quantity indicated in the contract; if this is not possible or if the purchaser does not require it, the seller is obliged to suffer a proportional reduction in the price.
If, on the contrary, the area is greater than that expressed in the contract, the purchaser has the choice of providing the additional price, or of withdrawing from the contract, if the excess is one-twentieth above the declared area.

###### Article 1796

In all other cases of sale of immovable property, which have therefore not been made at a rate of so much per unit of measurement, the deficiency in area can only give rise, in favor of the purchaser, to a reduction in price when the shortfall reaches one-twentieth, and, in favor of the seller, to an increase in price when the excess reaches one-twentieth, all subject to any stipulation to the contrary.

###### Article 1797

In the case where, according to Article 1796, there is ground for an increase in price for excess measurement, the purchaser has the choice either of withdrawing from the contract or of providing the additional price, together with interest if they have kept the immovable property.

###### Article 1798

In all cases where the purchaser has the right to withdraw from the contract, the seller is required to return to them, in addition to the price, if they have received it, the costs of that contract.

###### Article 1799

The action for additional price on the part of the seller of the immovable property, and that for reduction in price or for termination of the contract on the part of the purchaser of that property, must be brought within one year, from the day of the contract, on pain of forfeiture.

###### Article 1800

If two properties have been sold by the same contract, and for one and the same price, with designation of the measurement of each, and there is found to be less area in one and more in the other, compensation is made up to due concurrence; and the action, either for supplement or for reduction of the price, takes place only according to the rules established above.

###### Article 1801

The question of knowing upon which, of the seller or the purchaser, must fall the loss or deterioration of the thing sold before delivery, is decided according to the rules prescribed in the title On obligations.

##### Section III: On the warranty of the seller Article 1802

The warranty that the seller owes to the purchaser of any right of property, corporeal or incorporeal, has two objects:
-	the first is the peaceful possession of the thing sold;
-	the second, the hidden defects of this thing or the redhibitory vices.

###### § 1. On the warranty in case of eviction

###### Article 1803

Even if the sale contains no stipulation on the warranty, the seller is obliged by law to warrant the purchaser against the eviction that he suffers in the totality or part of the object sold, or of the charges claimed on this object, and not declared at the time of the sale.

###### Article 1804

The parties may, by particular agreements, add to this obligation by law, or diminish its effect.

The parties may even agree that the seller shall be subject to no warranty; in this case, the seller nevertheless remains liable for the warranty that results from an act personal to him. Any contrary agreement is null.

###### Article 1805

Even if a clause of non-warranty has been stipulated, the seller, in case of eviction, is nevertheless bound to the restitution of the price, unless the purchaser knew at the time of the sale of the danger of eviction or unless he purchased at his own peril and risk.

###### Article 1806

When the warranty has been promised, or when nothing has been stipulated on this subject, if the purchaser is evicted, he has the right to demand against the seller the reparation of all the prejudice caused by the non-performance of the contract, namely:
1° The restitution of the price;
2° The restitution of the fruits, when he is obliged to render them to the owner who evicts him;
3° The costs incurred on the demand for warranty of the purchaser, and those incurred by the original claimant; 4° Finally, the damages and interest, as well as the costs and loyal expenses of the contract.

###### Article 1807

When at the time of eviction, the thing sold is found to be diminished in value, or considerably deteriorated, either by the negligence of the purchaser, or by accidents of force majeure, the seller is nonetheless bound to restore the totality of the price.
But if the purchaser has drawn profit from the degradations made by him, for example, by selling the materials that he removed from the thing or the decorative elements, the seller has the right to retain from the price a sum equal to this profit.
Conversely, the seller is bound to reimburse or to have reimbursed to the purchaser, by the one who evicts him, all the useful repairs and improvements that he shall have made to the property.

###### Article 1808

On the other hand, if the thing sold is found to have increased in price at the time of eviction, independently even of the act of the purchaser, the seller is bound to pay him the amount of this increase in value in relation to the price of the sale.

###### Article 1809

If the seller has sold in bad faith the property of another, he is obliged to reimburse to the purchaser all the expenses, even voluptuary or of amenity, that the latter has made to the property.

###### Article 1810

If the purchaser is evicted only of a part of the thing but it is so essential that the purchaser would not have purchased without it, he may have the sale rescinded.
In this case of partial eviction, when the sale is not rescinded, the value of the part of which the purchaser is evicted is reimbursed to him according to the estimation at the time of eviction, and not proportionally to the total price of the sale, regardless of whether the thing sold has increased or diminished in value.

###### Article 1811

If the property that has been sold is found to be burdened, without any declaration having been made thereof, with non-apparent servitudes, and they are of such importance that there is reason to presume that the purchaser would not have purchased if he had been informed thereof, he may demand, at his choice, the rescission of the contract or an indemnity.

The other questions to which the damages and interest resulting for the purchaser from the non-performance of the sale may give rise must be decided according to the general rules established in the title On obligations.

###### Article 1812

The warranty for cause of eviction ceases when the purchaser has allowed himself to be condemned by a judgment in last resort, or from which appeal is no longer admissible, without calling his seller, if the latter proves that there existed sufficient means to have the claim rejected.

###### § 2. On the warranty for defects of the thing sold Article 1813

The seller is bound to the warranty by reason of the hidden defects of the thing sold which render it unfit for the use for which it is intended, or which so diminish this use that the purchaser would not have acquired it, or would have given only a lesser price, if he had known them.

###### Article 1814

The seller is not bound for apparent vices and of which the purchaser could have convinced himself.

###### Article 1815

The seller of an immovable to be constructed cannot be discharged, either before the reception of the works, or before the expiration of a period of one month after taking possession by the purchaser, of the vices of construction or the defects of conformity then apparent.
There is no ground for rescission of the contract or for reduction of the price if the seller undertakes to repair the vice.

###### Article 1816

The seller is bound for hidden vices, even though he did not know them, unless, in this case, he has stipulated that he shall be obliged to no warranty.

###### Article 1817

In the case of articles 1813 and 1816, the purchaser has the choice of returning the thing and having the price restituted to him, or of keeping the thing and having part of the price returned to him, such as it shall be fixed by the judge who may, where appropriate, appoint an expert.

###### Article 1818

If the seller knew the vices of the thing, he is bound, in addition to the restitution of the price that he received for it, for all the damages and interest towards the purchaser.
If the seller was unaware of the vices of the thing, he is bound only to the restitution of the price, and to reimburse to the purchaser the costs occasioned by the sale.

###### Article 1819

The seller of an immovable to be constructed is bound, from the reception of the works, by the obligations of which the architects, contractors and other persons bound to the owner by a contract of lease of work are themselves bound in application of articles 1950 and following of the present code.
These warranties benefit the successive owners of the immovable.

There shall be no ground for rescission of the sale or for reduction of the price if the seller undertakes to repair the damage defined in articles 1953, 1954 and 1955 of the present code and to assume the warranty provided for in article 1956.

###### Article 1820

If the thing which had vices has perished as a result of its bad quality, the loss is for the seller, who shall be bound towards the purchaser to the restitution of the price and to the other compensations explained in articles 1818 and 1819.
But the loss occurring by fortuitous event shall be for the account of the purchaser.

###### Article 1821

The action resulting from redhibitory vices must be brought by the purchaser, within a brief period, according to the nature of the redhibitory vices, and the usage of the place where the sale was made.
In the case provided for by article 1815, the action must be brought, on pain of foreclosure, within the year following the date on which the seller may be discharged from apparent vices.

###### Article 1822

It does not take place in sales made by judicial authority.

#### Chapitre VI. Des obligations de l'acheteur Article 1823

The principal obligation of the buyer is to pay the price on the day and at the place stipulated by the sale.

###### Article 1824

If nothing has been stipulated in this regard at the time of sale, the buyer must pay at the place and at the time when delivery is to be made.

###### Article 1825

The buyer owes interest on the sale price until payment of the principal, in the following three cases:
-	if it was so agreed at the time of sale;
-	if the thing sold and delivered produces fruits or other revenues;
-	if the buyer has been summoned to pay. In this last case, interest runs only from the summons.

###### Article 1826

If the buyer is disturbed or has just cause to fear being disturbed by an action, whether hypothecary or in revendication, he may suspend payment of the price until the seller has caused the disturbance to cease, unless the seller prefers to give security, or unless it has been stipulated that, notwithstanding the disturbance, the buyer shall pay.

###### Article 1827

If the buyer does not pay the price, the seller may demand the resolution of the sale.

###### Article 1828

The resolution of the sale of immovables is pronounced immediately, if the seller is in danger of losing the thing and the price.
If this danger does not exist, the judge may grant the purchaser a longer or shorter period depending on the circumstances.

Once this period has passed without the purchaser having paid, the resolution of the sale shall be pronounced.

###### Article 1829

If it has been stipulated at the time of the sale of immovables that, for failure to pay the price within the agreed term, the sale would be resolved by operation of law, the purchaser may nevertheless pay after the expiration of the period, as long as he has not been put on notice by a summons; but, after this summons, the judge cannot grant him this period.

###### Article 1830

In the matter of the sale of commodities and movable effects, the resolution of the sale shall take place by operation of law and without summons, for the benefit of the seller, after the expiration of the term agreed for withdrawal.

#### Chapitre VII. De la nullité et de la résolution de la vente Article 1831

Independently of the causes of nullity or resolution already explained in this title, and of those which are common to all contracts, the contract of sale may be resolved by the exercise of the right of redemption and by the inadequacy of the price.

##### Section I : De la faculté de rachat Article 1832

The right of redemption is a pact by which the seller reserves the right to take back the thing sold, upon restitution of the principal price and the reimbursement set out in article 1843.

###### Article 1833

The right of redemption cannot be stipulated for a term exceeding five years. The fixed term is strict and cannot be extended by the judge.
If it has been stipulated for a longer term, it is reduced to this term of five years.

###### Article 1834

For failure by the seller to have exercised his action of redemption within the prescribed term, the purchaser remains irrevocable owner.
The period runs against all persons, even against minors, subject, if applicable, to recourse against the person to whom this omission is attributable.

###### Article 1835

The seller with a pact of redemption may exercise his action against a second purchaser, even if the right of redemption had not been declared in the second contract.

###### Article 1836

The purchaser with a pact of redemption exercises all the rights of his seller; he may prescribe both against the true owner and against those who would claim rights or hypothecs on the thing sold.

###### Article 1837

He may raise the benefit of discussion against the creditors of his seller.

###### Article 1838

If the purchaser with a pact of redemption of a part of an undivided property has become the successful bidder for the whole on a licitation brought against him, he may oblige the seller to take back the whole when the latter wishes to use the pact.

###### Article 1839

If several persons have sold jointly, and by a single contract, a property common among them, each may exercise the action of redemption only for the share he had in it.
The same applies if the person who sold a property alone has left several heirs. But each of these coheirs may use the right of redemption only for the share he takes in the succession.

###### Article 1840

However, in the case of the preceding article, the purchaser may require that all the co-sellers or all the coheirs be made parties, in order to reconcile among themselves for the taking back of the thing sold in its entirety; and, if they do not reconcile, the purchaser may retain the thing in its entirety, subject to the person who exercised the action of redemption who has not obtained the agreement of the others, exercising the action for the whole and paying the entirety of the price and the costs of the sale.

###### Article 1841

If the sale of a property belonging to several persons has not been made jointly and as a whole, and each has therefore sold only the share he had in it, these persons may separately exercise the action of redemption on the portion that belonged to them.
The purchaser, in this case, cannot force the person who exercises the action for his share to take back the whole.

###### Article 1842

If the purchaser has left several heirs, the action of redemption may be exercised against each of them only for his share, in the case where it is still undivided, and in the case where the thing sold has been divided among them.
But if there has been a partition of the succession and the thing sold has fallen to the lot of one of the heirs, the action of redemption may be brought against him for the whole.
The parties may stipulate that in case of death of the purchaser leaving several heirs, the redemption shall be effected, against these heirs, only for the whole. Likewise, several persons acquiring jointly with a pact of redemption, may stipulate that the seller shall not exercise partial redemption.

###### Article 1843

The seller who uses the pact of redemption must reimburse not only the principal price, but also the costs and lawful expenses of the sale, the necessary repairs, and those which have increased the value of the property, up to the amount of this increase. He may not enter into possession of the property until he has satisfied all these obligations.
When the pact of redemption has been duly published at the mortgage office, all charges and hypothecs with which the purchaser would have encumbered it subsequent to the sale, are unenforceable against the seller who redeems his property. He is however bound to perform the leases made without fraud by the purchaser.

##### Section II : De l'annulation de la vente pour cause de lésion Article 1844

If the seller has been injured by more than seven twelfths in the price of an immovable, he has the right to demand the nullity of the sale, even in the case where he had expressly renounced in the contract the right to demand this annulment and had declared to give the surplus value.

The sanction of lesion does not take place in favor of the purchaser.

###### Article 1845

To know whether there is lesion of more than seven twelfths, the immovable must be valued according to its condition and its value at the time of the sale.
In case of a unilateral promise of sale, the lesion is assessed on the day of realization, that is to say at the time of the exercise of the option.

###### Article 1846

The claim is no longer admissible after the expiration of two years, from the day of the sale.

This period runs against spouses and against absentees, adults under guardianship and minors coming from a major who has sold.
This period also runs and is not suspended during the duration of the time stipulated for the pact of redemption.

###### Article 1847

In case of disagreement between the parties on the existence of lesion, the judge may only order an expert assessment if the claimant sets forth facts sufficiently serious for the lesion to appear possible if not probable. In this case, the judge appoints, either ex officio or by joint and unanimous choice of the parties for each of the experts, a panel of three experts. They must establish a joint report, in which they shall express a single opinion on the existence or non-existence of lesion, by majority vote.
If nevertheless different opinions remain, the report shall contain the reasons therefor, without it being permitted to disclose which opinion each expert held.

###### Article 1848

In the case where the action for nullity is allowed, the purchaser has the choice:
1° to return the thing by withdrawing the price he paid for it;
2° to keep the property by paying the supplement of the fair price, less one-tenth of the total price. The third-party possessor has the same right, subject to his warranty against his seller.

###### Article 1849

If the purchaser prefers to keep the thing by providing the supplement regulated by the preceding article, he owes interest on the supplement from the day of the demand for nullity.
If he prefers to return it and receive the price, he returns the fruits from the day of the demand.

Interest on the price he paid is also counted to him from the day of the same demand, or from the day of payment, if he has received no fruits.

###### Article 1850

Sales that must be made by judicial authority cannot be the subject of an action for nullity for lesion.

###### Article 1851

The rules explained in the preceding section for cases where several persons have sold jointly or separately, and for the case where the seller or the purchaser has left several heirs, are likewise observed for the exercise of the action for nullity.

#### Chapitre VIII. De la licitation

###### Article 1852

Licitation consists in the sale by auction, in a voluntary manner, of undivided movable or immovable property, by the holders of real rights over that thing.
The sale is followed by a distribution of its proceeds by allocation to each co-owner of a portion corresponding to his undivided rights.

###### Article 1853

Each of the co-owners has the right to request that third parties be admitted to participate in the auction. They are necessarily called when one of the co-owners is a minor.

###### Article 1854

The method and formalities to be observed for licitation are explained in the Title on Successions and in the Code of Civil Procedure.

#### Chapitre IX. Du transport des créances et autres droits incorporels Article 1855

In the transfer of a right or action against a third party, delivery is effected between the assignor and the assignee by the handing over of the title.

###### Article 1856

The assignee is seized with respect to third parties only by notification of the transfer made to the debtor.

Nevertheless, the assignee may also be seized by acceptance of the transfer made by the debtor in an authentic act.

###### Article 1857

If, before the assignor or the assignee had notified the transfer to the debtor, the latter had paid the assignor, he shall be validly discharged.

###### Article 1858

One who sells an incorporeal right must warrant its existence at the time of the transfer, even though it is made without warranty.

###### Article 1859

One who sells a succession without specifying in detail the objects thereof is only bound to warrant his quality as heir.
If he had already enjoyed the fruits of a thing present in that succession, or received the amount of a claim found therein, or sold property nevertheless belonging to the succession, he is bound to reimburse them to the purchaser, unless otherwise stipulated at the time of sale.

The purchaser must for his part reimburse to the seller of the succession what the latter has paid for the debts and charges thereof, and any claim that the latter could have against the succession, unless otherwise stipulated.

###### Article 1860

The assignment of litigious rights effects transfer of the assignor's right to the assignee by substituting the latter for the former in the pending proceedings.

Nevertheless, the person against whom a litigious right has been assigned may, either by extrajudicial act or by way of principal submissions filed in the pending proceedings, have himself discharged of it by the assignee, by reimbursing him the actual price of the assignment together with costs and proper expenses, and with interest from the day on which the assignee paid the price of the assignment made to him.

###### Article 1861

A thing is deemed litigious as soon as there is a lawsuit and contestation on the merits of the right.

###### Article 1862

The assigned debtor may not benefit from the right of litigious redemption:
1° In the case where the assignment was made to a co-heir or co-owner of the assigned right; 2° When it was made to a creditor in payment of what is due to him;
3° When it was made to the possessor of the property subject to the litigious right.

###### Article 1863

Articles 1855 to 1858 do not apply to assignments governed by Articles 1507 to 1512 of this Code.

### Titre VIII : De l'échange

###### Article 1864

Exchange is a contract by which the parties respectively give each other one thing for another.

###### Article 1865

Exchange is effected by consent alone, in the same manner as sale.

###### Article 1866

If one of the co-exchangers has already received the thing given to him in exchange, and he subsequently proves that the other contracting party is not the owner of that thing, he cannot be forced to deliver that which he promised in counter-exchange, but only to return that which he received.

###### Article 1867

The co-exchanger who is evicted from the thing he received in exchange has the choice of claiming damages or compelling the other party to restore his thing to him.

###### Article 1868

Rescission for cause of lesion does not take place in the contract of exchange.

###### Article 1869

All other rules prescribed for the contract of sale apply to exchange.

### Titre IX : Du contrat de louage

Chapitre Ier. Dispositions générales Article 1870
There are two kinds of contracts of lease:
-	that of things,
-	and that of work and industry.

###### Article 1871

The lease of things is a contract by which one of the parties undertakes to give the other the enjoyment of a thing for a certain time, and for a certain price which the latter undertakes to pay him.

The contract of lease confers on the lessee only a movable and personal right.
The rules applicable to the contract of lease do not apply to the emphyteutic lease, which is subject to its own rules.

###### Article 1872

The lease of work and industry is a contract by which one of the parties undertakes to do something for the other, for a price agreed between them.
Estimates, contracts or fixed prices, for the undertaking of a work for a determined price, are also a lease, when the material is supplied by the person for whom the work is done.

###### Article 1873

Leases of national property, property of communes and public establishments are subject to special regulations.

#### Chapitre II. Du louage des choses Article 1874

All movable and immovable property that is in commerce may be the subject of a contract of lease.

##### Section I : Dispositions communes aux baux Article 1875

The lease contract may be entered into in writing or verbally.
If the lease made without writing has not yet received any performance, and one of the parties denies it, proof may not be received by witnesses, even if the announced price is modest. The possible payment of a sum of money, without further specification, does not constitute commencement of performance of the verbal lease. The oath may only be deferred to the person who denies the lease.

###### Article 1876

When there is a dispute over the price of a verbal lease whose execution has begun and where no receipt exists, the lessee has the choice between two modes of proof to establish the price of the lease: oath or expert assessment. If he opts for the oath, the owner shall be believed on his word; if he opts for expert assessment, the costs thereof shall remain at the lessee's expense if the valuation exceeds the price he declared.
The judge may neither apply the provisions of the preceding paragraph of his own motion nor, when seized of the matter, fix the rent on the basis of elements other than those provided for by the text.

###### Article 1877

The lessee has the right to sublet, and even to assign his lease to a third party, if this option has not been prohibited to him, in whole or in part, by the contract.
When the clause prohibiting subletting or assignment of the lease is pure and simple, it applies absolutely and the lessee must comply with it, even if he were to demonstrate that the lessor has no interest in requiring its application and that he himself has an important interest in subletting or assigning his lease

###### Article 1878

Article 722, paragraph 4, is applicable to leases of property of minors.

###### Article 1879

The lessor is obliged, by the nature of the contract, and without any particular stipulation being necessary: 1° To deliver to the lessee the thing leased;
2° To maintain this thing in a condition to serve the use for which it was leased;
3° To ensure the lessee peaceful enjoyment of the thing leased throughout the duration of the lease; 4° To ensure, if there are any, the permanence and quality of plantations.

###### Article 1880

The lessor is required to deliver the thing in good repair of every kind.

He must carry out therein, during the duration of the lease, all repairs that may become necessary, other than tenancy repairs. The owner thus bears the cost of major repairs due to age or poor workmanship; he must also guarantee his lessee against all defects or faults of the thing leased that prevent its use, even if the lessor was not aware of them at the time of the lease. If any loss should result to the lessee from these defects or faults, the lessor would be required to compensate him.

###### Article 1881

The tenant cannot claim reimbursement from his owner for major repairs that he carried out without the latter's prior agreement.

###### Article 1882

It is otherwise if, during the lease, the thing leased needs urgent repairs that cannot be deferred, when the lessor cannot be reached or is slow to react: the tenant may then have the works carried out without requesting prior authorization from his owner; he may subsequently obtain reimbursement.
Conversely, if such repairs are undertaken by the lessor during the lease, the lessee must tolerate them, whatever inconvenience they cause him, and even if he must be deprived, while they are being carried out, of part of the thing leased.

But, if these repairs last more than thirty days, the price of the lease shall be reduced in proportion to the time and the part of the thing leased of which he has been deprived. And, if the repairs are of such a nature that they render uninhabitable what is necessary for the accommodation of the lessee and his family, the latter may have the lease terminated.

###### Article 1883

The lessor may not, during the duration of the lease, change the form of the thing leased.

###### Article 1884

The lessee is subject to two principal obligations:
1° To use the thing leased as a normally diligent person, and according to the purpose given to it by the lease, or according to that presumed from the circumstances, in the absence of agreement;
2° To pay the rent, price of the lease, at the agreed terms.

###### Article 1885

If the lessee uses the thing leased contrary to the obligations imposed upon him, or according to a use from which damage to the lessor could result, the latter may, depending on the circumstances, have the lease terminated.

###### Article 1886

If an inventory of fixtures has been made between the lessor and the lessee, the latter must return the thing as he received it, according to this inventory.
If no inventory of fixtures has been made, the lessee is presumed to have received them in good repair for tenancy purposes, and must return them in such condition, subject to proof to the contrary.

In both cases, the lessee is not liable for what has perished or been damaged during the lease, when the harmful event occurred without his fault, for example, due to age, a break-in causing the damage, a fortuitous event or fault of the lessor.

###### Article 1887

The lessee must ensure the premises he occupies are maintained in their condition. He must therefore bear the cost of minor repairs and tenancy repairs, that is to say the routine maintenance of the accommodation and its equipment elements.
The lessee must bear the cost of major repairs when the damage is due to poor maintenance on his part, excluding age, poor workmanship, construction defect, fortuitous event or force majeure. He is likewise not liable for deterioration related to normal use of equipment and premises.

###### Article 1888

The lessee is however liable for damage and losses that occur through the act of persons of his household or his subtenants.

###### Article 1889

The lessee is also liable for fire, unless he proves that the fire occurred by fortuitous event or force majeure, by construction defect, or that the fire was communicated from a neighboring house.
If there are several tenants, they are jointly and severally liable for the fire, in proportion to the rental value of the part of the building they occupy, unless they prove either that the fire started in the dwelling of one of them, in which case that one alone is liable for it, or that certain ones succeed in proving that the fire could not have started in their premises, in which case those ones are not liable for it.

###### Article 1890

If the lease was made without writing, the lease ends by notice given by one party to the other, observing a reasonable period.
If it was made in writing, it ceases by operation of law at the expiration of the fixed term, without it being necessary to give notice.

###### Article 1891

If, at the expiration of written leases, the lessee remains in the premises and is left in possession by the lessor, a new lease is created whose effect is governed by Article 1890 first paragraph relating to leases made without writing.
In this case, the security given for the lease does not extend to obligations resulting from the extension.

###### Article 1892

The lessor is not required to guarantee the lessee against disturbance that third parties bring by acts of fact to his enjoyment, without moreover claiming any right over the thing leased; subject to the lessee pursuing them in his personal name.
The perpetrators of an act of fact cannot justify it on the pretext of a right they might have over the thing. The judge shall order restoration and cessation of the disturbance, and shall invite the interested parties to proceed according to legal channels.
If, on the contrary, the tenant has been disturbed in his enjoyment as a result of an action concerning the ownership of the property, he is entitled to a proportionate reduction in the price of the lease, provided that the disturbance and impediment have been reported to the owner.

###### Article 1893

If the lessee is himself summoned to court by a third party who intends to have him condemned to vacate all or part of this thing, or to suffer the exercise of some servitude, this lessee must call the lessor as guarantor, and must be removed from the proceedings, if he so requires, by naming the lessor for whom he possesses.

###### Article 1894

If, during the term of the lease, the leased thing is destroyed or lost in its entirety by fortuitous event, the lease is terminated by operation of law; if it is only partially destroyed, the lessee may, depending on the circumstances, request either a reduction in the price, or even the termination of the lease. In either case, there is no entitlement to any compensation.

###### Article 1895

The lease contract is terminated by the respective failure of the lessor and the lessee to fulfill their obligations.

###### Article 1896

The lease contract is not terminated by the death of the lessor nor by that of the lessee.

###### Article 1897

If the lessor sells the leased thing, the purchaser may not evict the lessee who has an authentic lease or whose date is certain, unless he has reserved this right in the lease contract.

###### Article 1898

If it has been agreed, at the time of the lease, that in case of sale the purchaser may evict the lessee, and no stipulation has been made regarding damages, the lessor is obliged to compensate the lessee:
1° In case of lease of a house, apartment or shop, a sum equal to the rent price, for the time which, according to local custom, is granted between notice and departure.
2° In the case of rural property, a sum equal to one third of the lease price for all the time remaining to run.
The amount of compensation is, in case of dispute, fixed by the judge who may, where appropriate, appoint an expert.
As long as the compensation has not been paid, the lessee may remain on the premises.

###### Article 1899

If the lease is not made by authentic deed, or does not have a certain date, the purchaser is not liable for any damages.

###### Article 1900

The purchaser with a redemption clause may not use the power to evict the lessee, until, by the expiration of the time limit set for redemption, he becomes the definitive owner, except with the agreement of his seller.

###### Article 1901

The purchaser who wishes to use the power reserved by the lease, to evict the lessee in case of sale is obliged to give notice to the lessee, for a duration as provided in the lease contract for notices in case of termination and, failing that, for a reasonable duration.

##### Section II: Special rules

###### Article 1902

The lease with option to purchase is a lease contract providing that at its term, the tenant may acquire the property at a price fixed in advance.
When the contract concerns an individual, the transaction is a lease with promise of sale or lease-purchase; when it concerns professionals, it is a lease-credit contract governed by the provisions of Law No. 183/AN/17/7th L on lease-credit, of 29 May 2017.

###### § 1

Relations between lessors and tenants of residential premises or premises for professional use without industrial or commercial character

###### Article1903

These provisions are applicable to relations between lessors and tenants or occupants of premises belonging to the following categories:
1° Premises for residential use, with the exception of hotels and boarding houses; 2° Premises for professional use without commercial and industrial character;
3° Premises leased by a legal person under public law to install services or agents;
4° Premises leased by legal persons carrying out a non-profit activity, in particular by registered associations and professional unions;
5° Premises leased by commercial or industrial enterprises for the exclusive residential use of their personnel.
These provisions do not apply either to relations between legal persons under public law and their agents or to relations between commercial or industrial enterprises and their personnel, with regard to premises assigned to the housing of these agents or this personnel, when housing constitutes a benefit in kind accessory to remuneration within the framework of the regulatory status of civil servants, or the provisions of the labor code for private sector employees.

A.	Rent

###### Article1904

The amount of rent for leases covered by this section, as well as the conditions for its revision, are freely fixed by agreement of the parties upon conclusion of the initial lease between the lessor and the tenant.

###### Article1905

When the lease does not provide for special conditions for the revision of the rent, the latter, except contrary stipulations in the lease contract, may be revised at the request of one of the parties when a change in the inflation rate has occurred since the conclusion of the lease or since the last revision of the rent, likely to cause this rate to vary by more than ten percent.
The revision requested may not exceed the justified variation in the inflation rate during the period considered.

The request for revision must specify the new rent requested or offered and give all details on the elements taken into consideration to justify the amount of the revision.

###### Article1906

The request for revision of the rent made pursuant to Article 1905 may not, in any event, be made less than two years after the date of entry into enjoyment of the tenant, or after the starting point of the renewed lease, or after the last revision.

###### Article 1907

In addition to the elements mentioned in Article 1905 that may justify a revision, a request for revision may be made by the owner who has made improvements in the substance, comfort or amenity of the leased premises, with the express agreement of the tenant. This agreement must also cover the increase in rental value that will result from these improvements. The new rent thus revised may take effect upon completion of these improvements.
However, if the owner wishes to make improvements to the premises dictated by hygiene concerns, the prior agreement of the tenant is not necessary. The increase in rental value that will result from these improvements will justify a revision of the rent in proportion to the expenses incurred.

On the other hand, improvements made by the tenant may not be taken into account for a revision of the rent.

###### Article1908

In the absence of agreement between the parties on the revision requested pursuant to Articles 1905 and 1907 (second paragraph), disputes are brought before the President of the Court of First Instance or before the judge who replaces him, who shall rule on the request.

###### Article1909

The lease contract may provide for payment by the tenant, upon entry into the premises, of a security deposit as guarantee for possible damages and payment of rent due. The amount of the security deposit, which may not exceed two months' rent, shall be returned to the lessee at the expiration of the lease, except in case of renewal.

###### Article 1910

In the case of subletting, the amount of the subletting rent may not exceed the amount of the rent owed by the principal tenant to the owner, unless the premises have been furnished or have received improvements by the principal tenant, in which case the rent increase must be proportionate to the expenses incurred.
The subtenant is only liable to the owner up to the amount of his subletting rent which he may owe at the time of seizure, and without being able to set off payments made in advance.
