Payments made by the subtenant, either by virtue of a stipulation contained in his lease, or as a consequence of the use of the premises, are not deemed to have been made in advance.
In the case of partial subletting, the rent must be at most equal to a fraction of the principal rent proportionate to the size of the sublet premises, subject, as in the preceding paragraph, to the furniture provided and improvements made by the principal tenant which will justify increases proportionate to the expenses incurred.

###### Article1911

If the lease or sublease relates to premises furnished by the owner or by the principal tenant, the rent may be increased by a rental price for the furniture proportionate to the price of the latter, provided that this additional price may not exceed the amount of the rent for the unfurnished premises.

###### Article1912

In the case where the tenant or occupant is authorized, either amicably or by court order, to carry out maintenance or repair work normally the responsibility of the owner, he may offset the expenses incurred against future rents. In case of departure from the premises before the expiration of the debt, he may pursue the owner for reimbursement of the balance owed.

###### Article1913

Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, the clause inserted in the lease providing for termination by operation of law for failure to pay rent at the agreed due dates only takes effect one month after the date of the formal notice or payment order that has remained unsuccessful.

The formal notice or order must, on pain of nullity, mention this period.

The president of the court, seized by the lessee within the aforementioned one-month period, may by order grant him additional periods for payment of the rent within the limit of three months.

###### Article 1914

In case of termination of the lease due to the fault of the tenant, the latter is required to pay the agreed rent for the time necessary for reletting by the owner, provided that this period may not exceed two months, without prejudice to damages that may have resulted from his fault.

B.	Right to remain in the premises

###### Article 1915

The right to the lease of premises, without professional or commercial character, which effectively serves as housing for two spouses, whatever their matrimonial regime and notwithstanding any provision to the contrary and even if the lease was concluded before the marriage.
In case of divorce or legal separation, this right may be attributed, in consideration of the social and family interests at stake, by the court seized of the application for divorce or legal separation, to one of the spouses, subject to rights to compensation or indemnity for the benefit of the other spouse.

In case of death of one of the spouses, the surviving spouse, co-holder of the lease, has an exclusive right to it unless he expressly renounces it.

###### Article1916

1° Occupants in good faith of premises, unfurnished or furnished, defined in Article 1903, if they have lived there for at least one year, benefit by operation of law and without the completion of any formality from the right to remain in the leased premises, under the terms and conditions of the original contract not contrary to the provisions of this deliberation, the lease continuing by tacit renewal beyond the term fixed by the contract, except for notice given by either party with three months' notice, by extrajudicial act or by bailiff;
2° Notice given by the tenant does not need to be justified;
3° Notice given by the owner must specify, on pain of nullity, the reason for which it is given and apply Articles 1917, 1918 and 1920, subject to the provisions of Articles 1919 and 1921;
4° Tenants, subtenants, assignees of leases are deemed to be in good faith during the term and after the expiration of their contract, as well as occupants who, living in the premises by virtue of or following a written or verbal lease, a regular sublease of a regular assignment of a prior lease, fulfill their obligations;
5° However, to be enforceable against the owner, the subletting of premises or the assignment of a lease must have had his express or tacit consent. For this purpose, and except for special provisions in this regard in the lease contract, the proposed subletting or assignment of lease must be served on the owner by extrajudicial act two months before the subtenant or assignee enters the premises. Within the month following service, the owner must make known whether he intends to participate in the act. After this period, he is deemed to have given his tacit agreement;
6° The benefit of the right to remain in the premises for the premises referred to in Article 1903 belongs, in case of abandonment of domicile or death of the occupant, to his relatives or in-laws in the first degree who have habitually lived with him for more than six months;
7° In case of divorce or legal separation proceedings, the court seized attributes to one of the spouses the possible right to remain in the premises in consideration of the social or family interests at stake.

If the spouse who is the beneficiary is not the one in whose name the receipts were issued, notification of the decision must be made to the lessor within three months of its pronouncement by extrajudicial means;
8° However, the right to remain in the premises may not benefit the persons referred to in the two preceding paragraphs for premises used exclusively for professional purposes, unless one of these persons continues to practice there the profession for which these premises were allocated;
9° The right to remain in the premises is granted to legal entities occupying premises for professional use as well as to legal entities carrying out non-profit activities, in particular to registered associations and professional unions if these persons meet the conditions provided for in paragraphs 1 and 4 of this article. However, the right to remain in the premises thus recognized for legal entities is not enforceable against the owner who wishes to occupy the premises himself or have it occupied by his spouse, his ascendants or descendants, or those of his spouse.

###### Article1917

The following legal or natural persons are not entitled to remain in the premises:
1° Those who have been or will be the subject of a final judicial decision ordering their eviction by application of ordinary law, or who will be the subject of a similar decision for one of the causes and under the conditions admitted by this deliberation;
2° Those who have several dwellings, except for those constituting their principal establishment, unless they justify that their functions or profession require them to do so;
3° Those who have not effectively occupied the rented premises themselves or have not had them occupied by relatives or in-laws in the first degree who habitually lived with them;
4° Those who inhabit premises subject to an administrative injunction for reasons of hygiene or public utility requiring their evacuation;
5° Those who cease or have ceased the functions of which the title of occupation was an accessory;
6° Those who have at their disposal or can recover, by exercising their right of repossession, another premises meeting their needs and those of their relatives or in-laws in the first degree in their care;
7° Those installed in the premises by the principal tenant or any other beneficiary of the right to remain in the premises, without the consent of the lessor given under the conditions specified in point 5° of Article 1916;
8° Those who occupy premises located in buildings acquired or expropriated following a public declaration, subject to the administration ensuring the rehousing of evicted tenants or occupants.

C.	Right of repossession

###### Article1918

The right of repossession may be exercised by the owner who has obtained authorization to rebuild or raise the building, or to make modifications to it requiring its evacuation. The exercise of this right of repossession is however subject to the following conditions.
The owner:
1° Must give the occupants, by extra-judicial act, three months' notice which shall indicate precisely the reason or reasons justifying the exercise of the right of repossession and shall refer to the administrative decision authorizing the works, all on pain of nullity;
2° Shall be required to commence the works within a maximum period of three months from the evacuation of the premises by the last occupant;
3° Must, to the extent of his means, proceed with the rehousing of the evicted occupants if he possesses other premises;
4° May not re-let, occupy or have occupied the premises before completion of the works;
5° Must, upon completion of the works, grant to the evicted occupant a right of priority over any applicants.

###### Article1919

The owner who has not satisfied the obligations prescribed by the provisions of paragraphs 2, 3, 4 and 5 of Article 1918 above shall be liable, towards the evicted occupants, for payment for

unjustified deprivation of enjoyment, of compensation which may not be less than the amount of the annual rent.

###### Article1920

The right of repossession also belongs to the owner who wishes to repossess the building to occupy it himself or have it occupied by his spouse or by his relatives or in-laws in the first degree.
The owner who wishes to benefit from the above provisions must, by extra-judicial act, give three months' notice to the occupant whose premises he proposes to repossess.
The owner must, within a maximum period of two months from the evacuation of the premises, occupy them himself or have them occupied by the beneficiary of the right of repossession for a minimum period of one year.

The owner who has not occupied or had the premises occupied under the conditions defined in the preceding paragraphs of this article, shall be liable for payment towards the evicted occupant, of compensation which may not be less than the amount of the annual rent.

###### Article1921

The owner may not exercise the right of repossession provided for in Article 1920:
1° If he is the owner of another vacant premises corresponding to his needs and those of the beneficiaries of the right of repossession;
2° If he is the owner of another premises corresponding to his needs and those of the beneficiaries of the right of repossession, of which he can repossess from occupants who do not benefit from the right to remain in the premises.

D.	Miscellaneous provisions

###### Article1922

Any demand by the lessor or his agents, any agreement, tending to impose on the lessee, in an indirect form (handing over of money, repurchase of furniture, provision of service, etc.) a rental price higher than that which has been stipulated in the lease contract or than that which will result from the application of the provisions of point B. of this section, shall be null and void.

###### Article1923

A presidential decree may, in all or part of the territory of the Republic, subject to prior authorization the conversion of premises for residential use into premises for all other uses.
Offenders shall be punished by a civil fine which may not be less than 100,000 FD nor more than three times the annual rent provided for prior to the offence. In all cases, the court shall order the reallocation and restoration of the premises at the expense of the offender within the time limit it shall set. In the event of failure to execute within the time limits set, the fine provided for may be doubled.

###### Article1924

Any lessor of premises for residential use let unfurnished, convicted of having refused to let a vacant premises to a prospective tenant, on the grounds of the existence or number of children in the latter's care, shall be punished by a civil fine equal to at least one quarter and at most three times the rent payable at the time of the refusal.
The perpetrator of the offence shall, in addition, be required to grant to the evicted family, for a minimum period of two years, a lease on the refused building, unless the premises have already been let, in which case the said perpetrator of the offence shall be condemned, towards the injured party, to all damages and interest.

###### Article 1925

The tenant repairs or minor maintenance for which the tenant is liable, if there is no clause to the contrary, are those designated as such by the usage of the premises and, failing that, by the general provisions of the first section of this chapter.

###### Article 1926

The lease of furniture provided to furnish the rented premises is deemed made for the ordinary duration of leases, according to the usage of the premises.

###### Article 1927

The lease of a furnished apartment is deemed subscribed annually, when it has been made at so much per year; Monthly, when it has been made at so much per month;
Daily, when it has been made at so much per day.
If nothing establishes that the lease is made at so much per year, per month or per day, the lease is deemed made according to the usage of the premises.

###### Article 1928

If the tenant of a house or apartment continues his enjoyment after the expiration of the written lease, without opposition from the lessor, there is tacit renewal of the original contract.

###### § 2. Emphyteutic lease and building lease

A.	Emphyteutic lease

###### Article 1929

The emphyteutic lease of immovable property is a contract by which the lessor confers on the lessee, called emphyteuta, a real immovable right called emphyteusis.
The lease is granted for a duration which is between eighteen and ninety-nine years. It may not be extended by tacit renewal; in case of express renewal, the total duration of the lease may not exceed 99 years.

The right thus conferred is susceptible to mortgage, transferable and seizable in the forms prescribed for immovable seizure.

###### Article 1930

The emphyteutic lease may only be validly granted by those who have the right to alienate, and under the same conditions, as in the same forms. It is enforceable against third parties from the date of publication at the mortgage registry.
Properties belonging to minors or adults under guardianship may be granted under emphyteutic lease by virtue of a resolution of the family council.

Concerning premises for residential use, lease contracts concluded by the emphyteuta with tenants automatically continue with the owner of the property until the end of each of the lease contracts signed with the tenants and under the same conditions.
In the absence of contrary agreements, the emphyteutic lease is governed by the following provisions.

###### Article 1931

The lessee is liable for a periodic rent, called redevance, in the form of a sum of money or a portion of fruits and products.

The lessee may not request the reduction of this redevance on grounds of partial loss of the property.
In the absence of payment for six consecutive months, the lessor is authorized, after a demand that has remained without effect, to have the resolution of the emphyteusis pronounced in court.

###### Article 1932

The lessee may not make any change to the property that diminishes its value. Conversely, if he makes improvements or constructions that increase the value of the property, he may not destroy them, nor claim any compensation in this regard from the lessor.
Resolution may also be requested by the lessor in case of non-performance of the conditions of the contract or if the lessee has committed serious deterioration to the property.
Nevertheless, the courts may grant a delay according to the circumstances.

###### Article 1933

The lessee is liable for all contributions and charges weighing on the property.

He is liable for the maintenance and repairs of all kinds on the constructions that exist at the time of the lease and those that will have been erected in execution of the agreement, but he is not obliged to rebuild the buildings, if he proves that they were destroyed by fortuitous event, by force majeure or that they perished by defect of construction prior to the lease.

He is liable for fire, in accordance with Article 1394, paragraphs 2 and 3, of the Civil Code.

###### Article 1934

The lessee may acquire for the benefit of the property active easements, and encumber them, by title, with passive easements, for a time that will not exceed the duration of the lease, subject to notifying the owner.
If the lessee has concluded agreements with third parties, they terminate with the extinction of the emphyteusis, without possibility for the lessee's contracting parties to claim extension or compensation.

###### Article 1935

The lessee benefits from the right of accession during the duration of the emphyteusis.

B.	Construction lease

###### Article 1936

The construction lease is the lease contract by which the lessee undertakes, as a principal obligation, to erect constructions on the lessor's land and to keep them in good state of maintenance throughout the duration of the lease.
The construction lease is subject, subject to the provisions below, to the rules provided for the emphyteutic lease.

When the lease provides for a possibility of purchase of the land by the lessee and the lessee exercises the option, the lease terminates on the date of the sale.

###### Article 1937

The parties agree on their respective ownership rights over existing constructions and over constructions erected. In the absence of such an agreement, the lessor becomes the owner at the end of the lease and benefits from the improvements.

###### Article 1938

The construction lease confers on the lessee a real property right.

This right may be mortgaged, as well as the constructions erected on the leased land; it may be seized in the forms prescribed for real property seizure.

The lessee may assign all or part of his rights or contribute them to a company. The assignees or the company are subject to the same obligations as the assignor who remains guarantor until the completion of all the constructions that the lessee has undertaken to erect pursuant to Article 1936.

The lessee may grant passive easements essential to the realization of the constructions provided for in the lease.

The provisions of the two preceding paragraphs are of public policy.

###### Article 1939

The lessee is liable for all charges, taxes and duties relating to both the constructions and the land. Unless otherwise stipulated in the lease, he may demolish, with a view to rebuilding them, existing buildings.

###### Article 1940

The price of the lease may consist, in whole or in part, in the delivery to the lessor, at agreed dates and under agreed conditions, of immovable property or fractions of immovable property or securities giving entitlement to ownership or enjoyment of such immovable property.
If a periodic rent payable in cash is stipulated, this rent is affected by a coefficient revisable by three-year periods counted from the completion of the works. However, the first revision takes place at the latest upon expiration of the first six years of the lease.
The variation of the coefficient is proportional to that of the gross income of the immovable property. The income taken as the basis for the variation of the coefficient is that of the first calendar year following that of the completion of the works.

Disputes relating to the application of the provisions of the two preceding paragraphs are brought before the President of the Court of First Instance.

In case of loss of the buildings, the rent is maintained at the rate it had reached on the date of this loss until possible reconstruction of the destroyed buildings.

###### Article 1941

Passive easements, other than those mentioned in the fourth paragraph of Article 1938, privileges, mortgages or other charges arising from the lessee and, in particular, leases and occupancy titles of any kind relating to the constructions, are extinguished at the expiration of the lease except for lease contracts for residential premises.
However, when the lease provides for a possibility of purchase of the land by the lessee and the lessee exercises the option in accordance with the fourth paragraph of Article 1936, the privileges and mortgages from the lessee registered before the exercise of the option are not extinguished at the expiration of the lease but retain their effects, until their date of extinction, on the immovable property that has become the property of the grantor. They extend by operation of law to the land and may guarantee loans granted for the acquisition of said land.

Moreover, if the lease terminates by judicial or amicable termination, the privileges and mortgages mentioned in the first paragraph and registered, as the case may be, before the publication of the legal claim seeking to obtain this termination or before the publication of the act or agreement recording it, are only extinguished on the date originally agreed for the expiration of the lease.

###### Article 1942

If during the duration of the lease the constructions are destroyed by fortuitous event or force majeure, termination may, at the request of either party, be pronounced by judicial decision, which also rules on the compensation that may be due.

#### Chapter III. Lease of work and industry Article 1943

There are three main types of lease of work and industry:
1° Lease of service;
2° That of carriers, both by land and by water, who undertake the transport of persons or goods;
3° That of architects, contractors of works and technicians following studies, estimates or contracts.

##### Section I: On the hiring of services Article 1944

One may engage one's services only for a fixed time, or for a specified undertaking.
In the case of a contract concluded for an indefinite duration, the hiring of services may always cease by the will of one of the contracting parties.

Nevertheless, this right of unilateral termination may give rise to damages when, by the conditions in which it occurs, the termination has caused prejudice to the other party.

For the fixing of the indemnity to be awarded, if applicable, account is taken of customs, the nature of the services engaged, the time elapsed, the deductions made and the payments made with a view to a retirement pension, and, in general, all the circumstances which may justify the existence and determine the extent of the prejudice caused.

The parties may not renounce in advance the potential right to claim damages by virtue of the above provisions.

The disputes to which the application of the preceding paragraphs may give rise, when they are brought before the civil courts and before the courts of appeal, shall be heard and judged urgently.

##### Section II: On the hiring of carriers by land and by water

###### Article 1945

Carriers by land and by water are subject, for the custody and preservation of things entrusted to them, to the same obligations as innkeepers, of which mention is made in the title On deposit and sequestration.
With regard to their liability, carriers are subject to the regime provided for in articles L.2223-1 et seq. of the commercial code (

##### Section 3 On the liability of the carrier of the commercial code)

###### Article 1946

They are liable not only for what they have already received in their vessel or vehicle, but also for what has been delivered to them at the port or in the warehouse, to be placed in their vessel or vehicle.

###### Article 1947

They are liable for the loss and damage of things entrusted to them, unless they prove that they were lost and damaged by fortuitous event or force majeure.

###### Article 1948

The operators of public vehicles by land and by water, and those of public haulage, must keep a register of the money, effects and packages with which they are entrusted.

###### Article 1949

The operators and directors of public vehicles and haulage, the masters of barges and ships, are further subject to particular regulations.

##### Section III: On estimates and contracts Article 1950

When one entrusts someone to make a work, one may agree that he will provide only his labour or his industry, or else that he will also provide the material.

###### Article 1951

When the contractor provides the material and the thing perishes, in whatever manner, before being delivered, the loss falls upon the contractor, unless the master of the work was in default in receiving the thing.

###### Article 1952

When the contractor provides only his labour or his industry and the thing perishes, the risks of the thing fall upon its owner, except in case of fault of the contractor who, in that case, is liable for the loss.
The contractor who undertakes to manufacture an object with the material provided by the master of the work has no right to remuneration if the object perishes, even in the absence of fault on his part, before he has delivered it.

###### Article 1953

If the building perishes in whole or in part through defect of construction, even through defect of the soil, the architects, contractors and other persons bound to the master of the work by a contract for the hiring of work are liable for it for ten years.

###### Article 1954

Is deemed a constructor of the work:
1° Any architect, contractor, technician or other person bound to the master of the work by a contract for the hiring of work;
2° Any person who sells, after completion, a work which he has constructed or had constructed;
3° Any person who, although acting in the capacity of agent of the owner of the work, performs a mission comparable to that of a hirer of work.

###### Article 1955

The presumption of liability established by article 1953 extends equally to damage which affects the solidity of the equipment elements of a work, but only when these form an indissociable whole with the works of access, foundation, framework, enclosure or roofing.

An equipment element is considered as forming an indissociable whole with one of the works of access, foundation, framework, enclosure or roofing when its removal, dismantling or replacement cannot be carried out without deterioration or removal of material from that work.

###### Article 1956

The other equipment elements of the work are subject to a guarantee of proper functioning for a minimum duration of two years from its acceptance.

###### Article 1957

The manufacturer of a work, of a part of a work or of an equipment element designed and produced to satisfy, in service condition, precise and predetermined requirements, is jointly and severally liable for the obligations placed by articles 1953, 1955 and 1956 upon the hirer of work who has implemented, without modification and in accordance with the rules laid down by the manufacturer, the work, part of work or equipment element in question.
Are assimilated to manufacturers for the application of this article:
-	one who has imported a work, a part of a work or an equipment element manufactured abroad
;
-	one who has presented it as his work by placing on it his name, his trademark or any other distinctive sign.

###### Article 1958

Any natural or legal person whose liability may be engaged by virtue of articles 1953 to 1957 of this code is discharged from the liabilities and guarantees weighing upon him, in application of articles 1953 to 1955, after ten years from the acceptance of the works or, in application of article 1956, upon expiry of the period referred to in that article.

###### Article 1959

Actions in liability brought against a subcontractor by reason of damage affecting a work or equipment elements of a work mentioned in articles 1953 and 1955 are prescribed after ten years from the acceptance of the works and, for damage affecting those equipment elements of the work mentioned in article 1956, after two years from that same acceptance.

###### Article 1960

Apart from the actions governed by articles 1956, 1958 and 1959, actions in liability brought against the constructors designated in articles 1953 and 1954 and their subcontractors are prescribed after ten years from the acceptance of the works.

###### Article 1961

Any clause of a contract which has as its object, either to exclude or to limit the liability provided for in articles 1953, 1954 and 1955, or to exclude the guarantees provided for in articles 1956 and 1962 or to limit their scope, or to set aside or to limit the joint and several liability provided for in article 1957, is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1962

Reception is the act by which the client declares acceptance of the work with or without reservations. It takes place at the request of the most diligent party, either amicably or, failing that, judicially. It is, in any event, pronounced after adversarial proceedings.
The guarantee of perfect completion, for which the contractor is liable for a period of one year from reception, extends to the repair of all defects reported by the client, either by means of reservations mentioned in the reception report, or by written notification for those revealed after reception.

The time periods necessary for the execution of repair works are fixed by mutual agreement between the client and the contractor concerned.

In the absence of such agreement or in case of non-performance within the fixed period, the works may, after unsuccessful formal notice, be executed at the expense and risk of the defaulting contractor.
The execution of works required under the guarantee of perfect completion is recorded by mutual agreement, or, failing that, judicially.

The guarantee does not extend to works necessary to remedy the effects of normal wear and tear or use.

###### Article 1963

Equipment elements of a work within the meaning of Articles 1953, 1955, 1956 and 1957 do not include equipment elements, including their accessories, whose exclusive function is to permit the exercise of a professional activity in the work.

###### Article 1964

When an architect or contractor has undertaken the construction of a building at a fixed price, according to a plan settled and agreed with the owner of the land, he may not demand any increase in price, either on the pretext of an increase in labour or materials, or on that of changes or additions made to that plan, if such changes or additions have not been authorised in writing, and the price agreed with the owner.

###### Article 1965

The client may terminate, by his sole will, the fixed-price contract, even though the work has already begun, by compensating the contractor for all his expenses, all his works, and all that he could have earned in this undertaking.

###### Article 1966

The contract for work is dissolved by the death of the architect or the contractor.

The death of the client only results in the termination of the contract if his person was a determining element in the conclusion of the contract.
The dissolution of the contract by death does not, however, allow the client to retain without consideration the unfinished work, in the state in which it is: the client is obliged to pay in proportion to the price stated in the agreement, to the estate of the architect or the contractor, the value of the works done and that of the materials prepared, but only when such works or materials can be useful to him. In the case of paragraph 2, the same effect applies to the heirs of the client.

###### Article 1967

The contractor is liable for the acts of the persons he employs.

###### Article 1968

Employees and subcontractors who have been employed in the construction of a building or other works done under contract, have no action against the person for whom the works were done, except up to the amount of which he is found to be a debtor to the contractor, at the time when their action is brought.

### Titre X : De la société

Chapitre Ier. Dispositions générales Article 1969

A company is established by two or more persons who agree by contract to devote to a common enterprise property or their industry with a view to sharing the profit or benefiting from the economy that may result therefrom.

A company may also be established, in cases provided for by law, by the act of will of a single person.

The partners undertake to contribute to losses.

Even if they use only community property for contributions to a company or for the acquisition of shares, two spouses alone or with other persons may be partners in the same company and participate together or not in the management of the company.

###### Article 1970

Every company must have a lawful object, and be contracted for the common interest of the partners.

###### Article 1971

The provisions of this chapter are applicable to all companies unless otherwise provided by law by reason of their form or object.

###### Article 1972

The articles of association must be established in writing. They determine, in addition to the contributions of each partner, the form, object, name, registered office, share capital, duration of the company and the terms of its operation.

###### Article 1973

The articles of association may not be modified, in the absence of a clause to the contrary, except by unanimous agreement of the partners.

In no case may the commitments of a partner be increased without his consent.

###### Article 1974

Every company whose registered office is situated on the territory of the Republic of Djibouti is subject to the provisions of Djiboutian law.
Third parties may rely on the registered office stated in the articles, but it may not be relied upon against them by the company if the real registered office is situated in another place.

###### Article 1975

The duration of the company may not exceed ninety-nine years.

###### Article 1976

If the articles of association do not contain all the particulars required by legislation or if a formality prescribed by it has been omitted or irregularly performed, any interested person is entitled to apply to the court for an order, subject to penalty, for the regularisation of the formation. The public prosecutor may act for the same purposes.
The same rules are applicable in case of modification of the articles of association.

The action for regularisation provided for in the first paragraph is barred after three years from the registration of the company or the publication of the deed modifying the articles of association.

###### Article 1977

The founders, as well as the first members of the management, direction or administration bodies are jointly and severally liable for the damage caused either by the absence of a compulsory mention in the articles of association, or by the omission or irregular performance of a formality prescribed for the formation of the company.
In case of modification of the articles of association, the provisions of the preceding paragraph are applicable to the members of the management, direction or administration bodies then in office.

The action is barred after three years from the day of performance of the omitted or irregularly performed formality. The disappearance of the omission or irregularity does not preclude the exercise of the action for damages seeking reparation for the damage caused thereby. This action is barred after three years from the day on which the nullity was cured.

###### Article 1978

Companies other than the joint ventures referred to in Chapter III enjoy legal personality from their registration.
Until registration, relations between the partners are governed by the company contract and by the general principles of law applicable to contracts and obligations.

###### Article 1979

Persons who have acted in the name of a company in formation before registration are bound by the obligations arising from the acts thus performed, jointly and severally if the company is commercial, without joint and several liability in other cases.
The company duly registered may assume the commitments undertaken, which are then deemed to have been from the outset contracted by it.

###### Article1980

The contribution of property or a right subject to publication for its enforceability against third parties may be published even before registration and subject to the condition that such registration takes place.
From the date of registration of the company, the effects of the formality are retroactive to the date of completion of said formality.

###### Article 1981

The rights of each partner in the share capital are proportional to their contributions upon the formation of the company or during its existence.
Contributions in industry do not contribute to the formation of the share capital but give rise to the allocation of shares conferring the right to share in profits and net assets, subject to contributing to losses.

###### Article 1982

Each partner is a debtor to the company for everything they have promised to contribute to it in kind, in cash or in industry.
Contributions in kind are made by the transfer of the corresponding rights and by the effective placing at disposal of the property.
When the contribution is in ownership, the contributor is guarantor to the company as a seller to their buyer.
When it is in enjoyment, the contributor is guarantor to the company as a lessor to their lessee. However, when the contribution in enjoyment relates to fungible things or to any other property

normally intended to be renewed during the life of the company, the contract transfers to the company the ownership of the contributed property, subject to returning a similar quantity, quality and value; in this case, the contributor is guarantor under the conditions provided for in the preceding paragraph.

The partner who was to contribute a sum to the company and who has not done so becomes by operation of law and without demand, debtor of the interest on that sum from the day on which it was to be paid, without prejudice to further damages, if applicable. Furthermore, when calls for funds have not been made to achieve the full payment of the capital, any interested party may request the president of the court of first instance sitting in summary proceedings either to order under penalty the administrators, managers and directors to make these calls for funds, or to appoint a representative responsible for carrying out this formality.

The partner who has undertaken to contribute their industry to the company must account to it for all gains they have made through the activity that is the subject of their contribution.

###### Article 1983

I. In cases where the law refers to this article to set the conditions of price for a transfer of the social rights of a partner, or the repurchase thereof by the company, the value of these rights is determined, in case of dispute, by an expert designated either by the parties or, failing agreement between them, by order of the president of the court of first instance sitting in summary proceedings and without possible recourse.
II. In cases where the articles of association provide for the transfer of the social rights of a partner or the repurchase of these rights by the company without their value being either determined or determinable, the value is determined, in case of dispute, by an expert designated under the conditions of the first paragraph.

III. In the cases provided for in points I. and II., the expert thus designated is required to apply, where they exist, the rules and methods for determining the value provided for by the articles of association of the company or by any agreement binding the parties.

###### Article 1984

In addition to the action for compensation for damage suffered personally, one or more partners may bring the corporate liability action against the managers. The claimants are authorized to seek compensation for the damage suffered by the company; in case of conviction, the damages are awarded to the company.
Any clause in the articles of association having the effect of making the exercise of the corporate action subject to prior opinion or authorization of the general meeting or which would constitute advance waiver of the exercise of this action is deemed unwritten.
No decision of the general meeting of partners may have the effect of extinguishing a liability action against the managers for fault committed in the performance of their mandate.

###### Article 1985

Every partner has the right to participate in collective decisions.

The co-owners of an undivided share are represented by a single representative, chosen from among the co-owners or from outside them. In case of disagreement, the representative is designated by court order at the request of the most diligent.
If a share is subject to a usufruct, the voting right belongs to the bare owner, except for decisions concerning the allocation of profits, where it is reserved to the usufructuary.

The articles of association may derogate from the provisions of the two preceding paragraphs.

###### Article 1986

The share of each partner in the profits and their contribution to losses are determined in proportion to their share in the share capital, and the share of the partner who has contributed only their industry is equal to that of the partner who has contributed the least, all subject to a clause to the contrary.

However, the stipulation attributing to a partner the totality of the profit generated by the company or exempting them from all losses, as well as that totally excluding a partner from profit or placing on them the totality of losses, are deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1987

A mortgage or any other real security interest on the property of the company may be granted by virtue of powers resulting from resolutions or delegations established under private signature even though the creation of the mortgage or security interest must be by authentic instrument.

###### Article 1988

The regular transformation of a company into a company of another form does not result in the creation of a new legal person. The same applies to the extension or any other amendment to the articles of association.

###### Article 1989

A company, even in liquidation, may be absorbed by another company or participate in the formation of a new company, by way of merger. It may also transfer its assets by way of division to existing companies or to new companies.
These operations may take place between companies of different forms.

They are decided by each of the companies concerned, under the conditions required for the amendment of its articles of association.
If the operation involves the creation of new companies, each of them is formed according to the rules specific to the form of company adopted.

###### Article 1990

The consolidation of all shares in a single hand does not result in the automatic dissolution of the company. Any interested party may request such dissolution if the situation has not been regularised within a period of one year. The court may grant the company a maximum period of six months to regularise the situation. It may not order dissolution if, on the day it rules on the merits, such regularisation has taken place.
The ownership of the usufruct of all shares by the same person has no consequence on the existence of the company.

In the event of dissolution, it results in the universal transfer of the company's assets to the sole member, without the need for liquidation.

Creditors may oppose the dissolution within thirty days from its publication. A court decision shall reject the opposition or order either the repayment of debts or the provision of guarantees if the company offers them and if they are deemed sufficient. The transfer of assets is only effected and the legal person only ceases to exist at the end of the opposition period or, where applicable, when the opposition has been rejected at first instance or when the repayment of debts has been made or the guarantees provided.

The provisions of the two preceding paragraphs do not apply to companies whose sole member is a natural person.

###### Article 1991

The extension of the company is decided unanimously by the members or, if the articles of association so provide, by the majority required for amending them.

At least one year before the expiry date of the company, the members must be consulted to decide whether the company should be extended.

In default thereof, any member may apply to the president of the court of first instance, ruling on application, for the appointment of a judicial representative responsible for initiating the consultation provided for above.

###### Article 1992

The company comes to an end:
1° By the expiry of the period for which it was formed, unless extended in accordance with Article 1991;
2° By the achievement or extinction of its object; 3° By the annulment of the company contract;
4° By early dissolution decided by the members;
5° By early dissolution ordered by the court of first instance at the request of a member for just cause, in particular in the event of failure by a member to perform his obligations, or disagreement between members paralysing the operation of the company;
6° By early dissolution ordered by the court of first instance in the case provided for in Article 1990;
7° By the effect of a judgment ordering the closure of judicial liquidation for insufficiency of assets; 8° For any other cause provided for in the articles of association.

###### Article 1993

The dissolution of the company results in its liquidation, except in the cases provided for in Article 1989 and in the third paragraph of Article 1990. It has effect with regard to third parties only after its publication.
The liquidator is appointed in accordance with the provisions of the articles of association. In the absence thereof, he is appointed by the members or, if the members have been unable to make such appointment, by court decision. The liquidator may be removed under the same conditions. The appointment and removal are only enforceable against third parties from their publication. Neither the company nor third parties may, in order to avoid their commitments, rely on an irregularity in the appointment or removal of the liquidator, provided that it has been duly published.

The legal personality of the company subsists for the purposes of liquidation until the publication of its closure.
If the closure of the liquidation has not occurred within three years from the dissolution, the public prosecutor or any interested party may refer the matter to the court of first instance, which shall have the liquidation carried out or, if it has been commenced, its completion.

###### Article 1994

After payment of debts and repayment of the share capital, the distribution of assets is made among the members in the same proportions as their participation in profits, unless otherwise provided by clause or agreement.
The rules concerning the division of estates, including preferential allocation, apply to divisions among members.
However, the members may validly decide, either in the articles of association or by a separate decision or act, that certain assets shall be allocated to certain members. In default thereof, any contributed asset found in kind in the mass to be divided is allocated, upon his request, and subject to equalisation payment if applicable, to the member who had made the contribution. This option is exercised before any other right to preferential allocation.

All the members, or only some of them, may also remain in joint ownership for all or part of the company's assets. Their relations are then governed, at the closure of liquidation, with regard to such assets, by the provisions relating to joint ownership.

###### Article 1995

The nullity of the company may only result from the violation of the provisions of Articles 1969 and 1970, or from one of the grounds for nullity of contracts in general.
Any clause in the articles of association contrary to a mandatory provision of this title whose violation is not sanctioned by the nullity of the company, is deemed unwritten.
The nullity of acts or resolutions of the company's organs may only result from the violation of a mandatory provision of this title or from one of the grounds for nullity of contracts in general.

###### Article 1996

The action for nullity is extinguished when the ground for nullity has ceased to exist on the day the court rules on the merits at first instance, unless such nullity is based on the unlawfulness of the company's object.

###### Article 1997

In the event of nullity of a company or of acts or resolutions subsequent to its formation, based on a defect of consent or the incapacity of a member, and where regularisation may occur, any person having an interest therein may give formal notice to the person capable of effecting it, either to regularise or to bring an action for nullity within six months on pain of forfeiture. This formal notice is served on the company.
The company or a member may submit to the court seized within the period provided for in the preceding paragraph, any measure likely to eliminate the applicant's interest, in particular by the redemption of his membership rights. In such case, the court may either order nullity or make the proposed measures mandatory if they have been previously adopted by the company under the conditions provided for statutory amendments. The vote of the member whose redemption of rights is requested has no influence on the company's decision.

In the event of dispute, the value of the membership rights to be reimbursed to the member is determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 1983.

###### Article 1998

The court, seized of an application for nullity, may, even of its own motion, set a period to allow nullities to be cured. It may not order nullity less than two months after the date of the writ initiating proceedings.
If, to cure a nullity, a meeting must be convened, or a consultation of members be carried out, and if proof is provided of proper convocation of such meeting or of the sending to members of the text of draft decisions accompanied by documents that must be communicated to them, the president of the court of first instance seized by way of summary proceedings, shall grant the time necessary for the members to make a decision.

###### Article 1999

Actions for nullity of the company or of acts and resolutions subsequent to its formation are prescribed after three years from the day the nullity is incurred.

###### Article 2000

When the nullity of the company is pronounced, it terminates, without retroactive effect, the performance of the company contract.

With regard to the legal person that may have come into existence, the nullity of the company produces the effects of a dissolution pronounced by court.

###### Article 2001

Neither the company nor the partners may invoke a nullity against third parties acting in good faith.

However, nullity resulting from incapacity or from one of the defects of consent may be invoked even against third parties acting in good faith by the incapacitated person and their legal representatives, or by the partner whose consent was obtained through error, fraud or duress.

###### Article 2002

The action for liability based on the annulment of the company or of acts and resolutions subsequent to incorporation is barred after three years from the day on which the decision of annulment became res judicata.
The disappearance of the cause of nullity does not prevent the exercise of the action for damages seeking compensation for the harm caused by the defect with which the company, act or resolution was tainted. This action is barred after three years from the day on which the nullity was cured.

#### Chapitre II. De la société civile

##### Section I : Dispositions générales Article 2003

The provisions of this chapter apply to all civil companies, unless derogated from by the particular legal status to which some of them are subject.

All companies to which the law does not attribute another character by reason of their form, nature, or object have civil character.

###### Article 2004

The capital is divided into equal shares.

The provisions of Chapter I of Title II of Book III of the Commercial Code relating to the variable capital of companies apply to civil companies.

##### Section II : De la gérance Article 2005

The company is managed by one or more persons, whether partners or not, appointed either by the articles of association, or by a separate instrument, or by a decision of the partners.
The articles of association set the rules for appointing the manager or managers and the method of organizing the management.

Unless otherwise provided in the articles of association, the manager is appointed by a decision of the partners representing more than half of the company shares.
In the absence of provisions in the articles of association, and if the partners have not decided otherwise at the time of appointment, managers are deemed appointed for the duration of the company.

If, for any reason whatsoever, the company finds itself without a manager, any partner may apply to the president of the court of first instance ruling on petition for the appointment of a representative responsible for convening the partners with a view to appointing one or more managers.

###### Article 2006

Apart from the cases referred to in Article 1992, the company is terminated by early dissolution that may be pronounced by the court of first instance at the request of any interested party, when it has been without a manager for more than one year.

###### Article 2007

The appointment and termination of office of managers must be published.

Neither the company nor third parties may, in order to avoid their commitments, invoke an irregularity in the appointment of managers or in the termination of their office, when these decisions have been duly published.

###### Article 2008

If a legal person exercises management, its directors are subject to the same conditions and obligations and incur the same civil and criminal liabilities as if they were managers in their own name, without prejudice to the joint and several liability of the legal person they direct.

###### Article 2009

In relations between partners, the manager may perform all management acts required by the interest of the company.
If there are several managers, they exercise these powers separately, subject to the right of each to oppose an operation before it is concluded.
All of the foregoing, in the absence of provisions in the articles of association on the method of administration.

###### Article 2010

In relations with third parties, the manager binds the company by acts falling within the corporate object.

In case of plurality of managers, they hold separately the powers provided for in the preceding paragraph. Opposition by one manager to the acts of another manager has no effect with regard to third parties, unless it is established that they had knowledge of it.

Statutory clauses limiting the powers of managers are unenforceable against third parties, unless it is established that they had knowledge of them.

###### Article 2011

Each manager is individually liable to the company and to third parties, whether for violations of laws and regulations, or for breach of the articles of association, or for faults committed in their management.
If several managers participated in the same acts, their liability is joint and several with regard to third parties and partners. However, in their relations among themselves, the court determines the contributory share of each in the compensation for the damage.

###### Article 2012

Unless otherwise provided in the articles of association, the manager is removable by a decision of the partners representing more than half of the company shares. If the removal is decided without just cause, it may give rise to damages.
The manager is also removable by the courts for legitimate cause, at the request of any partner.

Unless otherwise stipulated, the removal of a manager, whether a partner or not, does not result in the dissolution of the company. If the removed manager is a partner, they may, unless otherwise agreed in the articles of association, or unless the other partners decide on the early dissolution of the company, withdraw from it and claim reimbursement of the value of their company rights determined, in the absence of amicable agreement, by expert opinion, in accordance with Article 1983.

##### Section III : Des décisions collectives Article 2013

Decisions that exceed the powers recognized to managers are taken according to the statutory provisions or, in the absence of such provisions, unanimously by the partners.

###### Article 2014

Decisions are taken by the partners meeting in assembly. The articles of association may also provide that they result from a written or electronic consultation.

###### Article 2015

Decisions may also result from the consent of all partners expressed in an instrument.

##### Section IV : De l'information des associés Article 2016

Partners have the right to obtain, at least once a year, access to the books and company documents, and to pose questions in writing concerning company management to which answers must be provided in writing within one month.

###### Article 2017

Managers must, at least once a year, account for their management to the partners. This rendering of account must include a comprehensive written report on the activity of the company during the past year or financial period including an indication of the profits realized or foreseeable and the losses incurred or anticipated.

##### Section V : Des engagements des associés à l'égard des tiers

###### Article 2018

With regard to third parties, partners are liable indefinitely for company debts in proportion to their share in the company capital at the date of maturity or on the day of cessation of payments.
The partner who has contributed only their industry is liable as the one whose participation in the company capital is the smallest.

###### Article 2019

Creditors may not pursue payment of company debts against a partner except after having previously and unsuccessfully pursued the legal person.

###### Article 2020

All actions against non-liquidating partners or their heirs and successors are barred after three years from the publication of the dissolution of the company.

###### Article 2021

If there is insolvency, personal bankruptcy, liquidation of assets or judicial settlement affecting one of the partners, unless the others unanimously decide to dissolve the company in advance or unless such dissolution is provided for in the articles of association, the reimbursement of the social rights of the person concerned shall be carried out under the conditions set out in Article 1983, and that person shall then lose the status of partner.

##### Section VI: Transfers of social shares Article 2022

Social shares may only be transferred with the approval of all the partners.

The articles of association may, however, provide that such approval shall be obtained by a majority determined by them, or granted by the managers. They may also dispense with approval for transfers made to partners or to the spouse of one of them. Unless otherwise provided in the articles of association, transfers made to ascendants or descendants of the transferor are not subject to approval.

The proposed transfer is notified, with a request for approval, to the company and to each of the partners. It is notified only to the company when the articles of association provide that approval may be granted by the managers.
When two spouses are simultaneously members of a company, transfers made by one of them to the other must, to be valid, result from a notarial deed or from a deed under private signature having acquired certain date otherwise than by the death of the transferor.

###### Article 2023

When several partners express their intention to acquire, they are, unless otherwise provided by clause or agreement, deemed to be purchasers in proportion to the number of shares they previously held.
If no partner comes forward as purchaser, the company may have the shares acquired by a third party designated by the unanimous consent of the other partners or according to the procedures provided for in the articles of association. In case of deadlock, Article 2024, paragraph 1 applies. The company may also proceed with the repurchase of the shares with a view to their cancellation.

The name of the proposed purchaser or purchasers, partners or third parties, or the offer of repurchase by the company, as well as the price offered, are notified to the transferor. In case of dispute over the price, it is fixed in accordance with the provisions of Article 1983, all without prejudice to the right of the transferor to retain his shares.

###### Article 2024

If no offer to purchase is made to the transferor within six months from the last of the notifications provided for in the third paragraph of Article 2022, approval of the transfer is deemed to have been obtained, unless the other partners decide, within the same period, on the early dissolution of the company.
In the latter case, the transferor may render this decision null and void by making known that he renounces the transfer within one month from the said decision.

###### Article 2025

The provisions of the two preceding articles may only be derogated from to modify the six-month period provided for in the first paragraph of Article 2024, and provided that the period stipulated in the articles of association does not exceed one year or is not less than one month.

###### Article 2026

The transfer of social shares must be recorded in writing. It is made enforceable against the company by service of the transfer made or, if the articles of association so stipulate, by transfer on the registers of the company.
It is only enforceable against third parties after completion of these formalities and after publication.

###### Article 2027

Social shares may be the subject of a pledge recorded either by authentic deed or by deed under private signatures served on the company or accepted by it in an authentic deed, and giving rise to publication the date of which determines the rank of pledgee creditors. Those whose titles are published on the same day rank concurrently.
The privilege of the pledgee creditor subsists on the pledged social rights by the mere fact of publication of the pledge.

###### Article 2028

Any partner may obtain from the other partners their consent to a proposed pledge under the same conditions as their approval for a transfer of shares.
Consent given to the proposed pledge entails approval of the transferee in case of forced realization of the social shares on condition that such realization is notified one month before the sale to the partners and to the company.

Each partner may substitute himself for the purchaser within five clear days from the sale. If several partners exercise this option, they are, unless otherwise provided by clause or agreement, deemed to be purchasers in proportion to the number of shares they previously held. If no partner exercises this option, the company may repurchase the shares itself, with a view to their cancellation.

###### Article 2029

Forced realization that does not proceed from a pledge to which the other partners have given their consent must likewise be notified one month before the sale to the partners and to the company.
The partners may, within this period, decide on the dissolution of the company or the acquisition of the shares under the conditions provided for in Articles 2023 and 2024.
If the sale has taken place, the partners or the company may exercise the option of substitution recognized to them by Article 2028. Failure to exercise this option entails approval of the purchaser.

##### Section VII: Withdrawal or death of a partner

###### Article 2030

Without prejudice to the rights of third parties, a partner may withdraw totally or partially from the company, under the conditions provided for in the articles of association or, failing that, after authorization given by a unanimous decision of the other partners. This withdrawal may also be authorized for just cause by a court decision.
Unless certain assets of the company of equivalent value are allocated to him, the partner who withdraws is entitled to reimbursement of the value of his social rights, fixed, failing amicable agreement, by expert determination, in accordance with Article 1983.

###### Article 2031

The company is not dissolved by the death of a partner, but continues with his heirs or legatees, unless it is provided in the articles of association that they must be approved by the partners.
It may, however, be agreed that such death shall result in the dissolution of the company or that it shall continue with the surviving partners only.

It may also be agreed that the company shall continue either with the surviving spouse, or with one or more of the heirs, or with any other person designated by the articles of association or, if they so authorize, by testamentary disposition.

Unless otherwise provided in the articles of association, when the succession devolves to a legal person, the latter may only become a partner with the approval of the other partners, given according to the conditions in the articles of association or, failing that, by unanimous agreement of the partners.

###### Article 2032

Heirs or legatees who do not become partners are only entitled to the value of the social shares of their predecessor. This value must be paid to them by the new holders of the shares or by the company itself if it has repurchased them with a view to their cancellation.
The value of these social rights is determined on the day of death by expert determination, unless there is amicable agreement, under the conditions provided for in Article 1983.

#### Chapter III: Partnership Article 2033

The partners may agree that the company shall not be registered. The company is then called a "partnership". Such a company is not a legal person and is not subject to publicity. Its existence may be proved by any means.

The partners freely agree on the object, operation and conditions of the partnership, subject to the mandatory rules of the common law of companies.

###### Article 2034

Unless a different organization has been provided for, relations between partners are governed, as appropriate, either by the provisions applicable to civil partnerships, if the partnership has a civil character, or, if it has a commercial character, by those applicable to general partnerships.

###### Article 2035

With regard to third parties, each partner remains the owner of the property that he places at the disposal of the partnership.

Property acquired through the use or reinvestment of undivided funds during the duration of the partnership and property that was undivided before being placed at the disposal of the partnership are deemed to be held in co-ownership between the partners.

The same applies to property that the partners have agreed to place in co-ownership.

It may further be agreed that one of the partners is, with regard to third parties, the owner of all or part of the property that he acquires with a view to achieving the corporate purpose.

###### Article 2036

Each partner contracts in his own name and is alone bound with regard to third parties.

However, if the participants act in their capacity as partners in the sight and knowledge of third parties, each of them is liable to the latter for obligations arising from acts performed in that capacity by one of the others, jointly and severally if the partnership is commercial, without joint and several liability in other cases.

The same applies to a partner who, by his interference, has led the contracting party to believe that he intended to bind himself to him, or whose commitment is proven to have benefited him.
In all cases, with respect to property deemed to be held in co-ownership pursuant to Article 2035 (paragraphs 2 and 3), the provisions of Chapter VI of Title I of Book III of this Code (Articles 933 et seq.) apply in relations with third parties, or, if the formalities provided for in Article 2037 have been completed, those of Title XI of this Book (

###### article 2071

et seq.), all partners then being, unless otherwise agreed, deemed to be managers of the co-ownership.

###### Article 2037

When the partnership in participation is of indefinite duration, its dissolution may result at any time from a notification sent by one of them to all the partners provided that such notification is made in good faith and not at an inopportune time.
Unless otherwise agreed, no partner may request the partition of undivided property pursuant to the rules applicable to co-ownership under Article 2035 as long as the partnership has not been dissolved.

###### Article 2038

The provisions of this chapter are applicable to partnerships created de facto.

#### Chapitre IV

De la société civile professionnelle Section I : Dispositions générales

###### Article 2039

Civil professional partnerships may be formed between natural persons exercising the same liberal profession subject to a legislative or regulatory status or whose title is protected, and in particular between public officers and ministerial officers, which enjoy legal personality and are subject to the provisions of this Chapter III.
These civil professional partnerships have as their purpose the joint exercise of the profession of their members, notwithstanding any legislative or regulatory provision reserving the exercise of that profession to natural persons.

Registration of the partnership may not take place until after approval thereof by the competent authority or its registration on the list or roll of the professional order.

The conditions for application of this Chapter III to each profession are determined by the laws and regulations applicable to each of the professions concerned.

###### Article 2040

A decree may authorize, under the conditions it determines, natural persons exercising a liberal profession referred to in the preceding article to form partnerships governed by this Chapter III with natural persons exercising other liberal professions with a view to the joint exercise of their respective professions.
Members of the professions referred to in Article 2039 may only enter into a civil professional partnership grouping persons belonging to liberal professions not referred to in Article 2039 on condition that they have been authorized to do so by the body exercising disciplinary jurisdiction over them. In the event of refusal of authorization, an appeal may be made to the Civil Chamber of the Court of Appeal.

Partnerships referred to in this article may only perform the acts of a particular profession through one of their members qualified to exercise that profession.

###### Article 2041

Only persons who, prior to the formation of the partnership, regularly exercised the profession as well as those who, meeting all the conditions required by the laws and regulations in force, are qualified to exercise it may be partners, subject to the provisions of Article 2062.

###### Article 2042

Unless otherwise provided by the regulations specific to each profession, any partner may only be a member of one civil professional partnership and may not exercise the same profession on an individual basis.

###### Article 2043

Natural persons holding a public or ministerial office and exercising the same profession may also form civil professional partnerships among themselves for the joint exercise of their profession, without such partnerships themselves being appointed holders of an office.
The application of the preceding paragraph is subject to the provisions of Article 2039, paragraph 3.

The provisions of Article 2040 are applicable to partnerships formed pursuant to this article.

##### Section II : Constitution de la société Article 2044

Civil professional partnerships are freely formed under the conditions provided for by the regulations specific to each profession, which shall determine the approval or registration procedure and the role of professional bodies.
With regard to public and ministerial offices, the partnership must be approved or appointed to the office under the conditions to be provided for by decree.

###### Article 2045

The articles of association of the partnership must be drawn up in writing. The regulations specific to each profession determine the information that must be included in the articles of association.

The corporate name of the partnership must be immediately preceded or followed by the words:
"société civile professionnelle" or the initials: "SCP", themselves followed by an indication of the profession exercised.
The name of one or more partners may be included in the corporate name.

###### Article 2047

The share capital is divided into equal shares which may not be represented by negotiable instruments. The regulations specific to each profession may limit the number of partners.

###### Article 2048

The shares must be subscribed in full by the partners. Those representing contributions in kind must be fully paid up upon formation of the partnership.
The distribution of shares is stated in the articles of association. It takes into account contributions in cash and, according to the valuation made thereof, contributions in kind and in particular contributions of intangible rights.
The articles of association may, by unanimous decision of the partners, establish the principles and procedures applicable to determining the value of shares.

Unless otherwise provided by the regulations specific to each profession, the value of shares takes into consideration a value representing the civil clientele. However, by unanimous decision of the partners, the articles of association may exclude this value representing the civil clientele from the valuation of shares.

##### Section III: Operation of the company Article 2049

All partners are managers unless otherwise stipulated in the articles of association, which may designate one or more managers from among the partners or provide for their designation by a subsequent act.
The conditions for appointment and removal of managers, their powers and the duration of their term are determined by the articles of association. The powers of managers may in no case have the effect of creating subordination of the partners to the company for the performance of their professional acts.

###### Article 2050

Managers are liable, individually or jointly as the case may be, towards the company or towards third parties, either for infringements of laws and regulations, or for violation of the articles of association, or for faults committed in their management. If several managers have cooperated in the same acts, the court shall determine the contributory share of each in the apportionment of the damage.

###### Article 2051

Decisions that exceed the powers of managers are made by the partners.

Each partner has, unless otherwise provided by the specific decree for each profession or, failing that, by the articles of association, one vote only, regardless of the number of shares he holds.
The regulations specific to each profession and, failing that, the articles of association determine the method of consultation of the partners, the quorum and majority rules required for the validity of their decisions and the conditions under which they are informed of the state of company affairs.

Remuneration of any kind, paid in consideration of the professional activity of the partners, constitutes receipts of the company and is received by it.

The regulations specific to each profession and, failing that, the articles of association may determine methods of distribution of profits that are not proportional to capital contributions.

In the absence of regulatory provision or statutory clause, each partner is entitled to the same share in the profits.

###### Article 2053

Partners are liable indefinitely for company debts towards third parties. This provision does not prevent two spouses from being partners in the same professional civil company.
Creditors of the company may not pursue payment of company debts against a partner except after having unsuccessfully served formal notice on the company and on condition of joining it as a party.
The articles of association may stipulate that, in relations between partners, each of them is liable for company debts in the proportion they determine.

###### Article 2054

Each partner is liable on his entire patrimony for the professional acts he performs. The company is jointly and severally liable with him for the damaging consequences of these acts.
The company or the partners must take out professional civil liability insurance, under the conditions provided for by the regulations specific to each profession.

###### Article 2055

The regulations specific to each profession determine the attributions and powers of each partner and of the company for the exercise of the profession, and proceed, where appropriate, to adapt the rules of professional ethics and discipline applicable to them.

###### Article 2056

A partner may withdraw from the company, either by transferring his shares, or by the company reimbursing him the value of his shares.
Upon the withdrawal of a partner, the professional civil company is subject to the modifications of registration and the transferee of the shares to the approval procedure, provided for by the regulations specific to each profession.

With regard to public offices and ministerial offices, the regulations specific to each profession determine the conditions under which the transferee of the shares must be approved by the appointing authority and the withdrawal of the partner to whom the value of his shares is reimbursed must be approved.

###### Article 2057

Shares may be transferred or assigned to third parties with the consent of partners representing at least three-quarters of the votes. However, the articles of association may require a higher majority or unanimity of the partners.
The transfer or proposed assignment is notified to the company and to each of the partners. If the company has not made its decision known within two months from the last of the notifications provided for in this paragraph, consent is implicitly given.

If the company has refused to give its consent, the partners are required, within six months from such refusal, to acquire or have acquired the shares at a price representing their value

determined in application of the third and fourth paragraphs of Article 2048 or, when the articles of association do not provide for the methods of determining the price, a price fixed under the conditions provided for by Article 1983 of the Civil Code.

###### Article 2058

Unless otherwise provided in the articles of association, shares are freely transferable between partners.

If the articles of association contain a clause limiting freedom of transfer, the provisions of Article 2057, paragraphs 2 and 3, are applicable in the absence of statutory stipulations.

###### Article 2059

When a partner so requests, the company is required either to have his shares acquired by other partners or third parties, or to acquire them itself, under the conditions determined by the regulations specific to each profession. In the second case, the company is required to reduce its capital by the amount of the nominal value of these shares.

###### Article 2060

The transfer of shares must be recorded in writing. It is made enforceable against the company in the forms provided for in Article 1994.
