The simple or joint and several surety is discharged when subrogation to the creditor's rights and guarantees can no longer operate in its favor, by act of the creditor. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.

If the act imputed to the creditor only limits this subrogation, the surety is discharged to the extent of the insufficiency of the guarantee preserved.

###### Article 2283

The surety who, upon first proceedings brought against it, requests the benefit of discussion must indicate to the creditor the property of the principal debtor capable of being immediately seized on national territory and, if the creditor so requests, advance sufficient sums to conduct the discussion.

###### Article 2284

Whenever the surety has made the indication of property authorized by the preceding article, and has provided sufficient sums for the discussion, the creditor is, up to the value of the property indicated, liable to the surety for the insolvency of the principal debtor arising from failure to pursue.

###### Article 2285

If there are several sureties for the same debtor and the same debt, unless there is a stipulation of solidarity between them or waiver by them of this benefit, each of them may, upon first proceedings by the

creditor, request division of the debt among the solvent sureties on the day the defense is invoked.

The surety is not liable for the insolvencies of the other sureties arising after the division.
The creditor who voluntarily divides its action when it could have avoided doing so, may not reverse this division and bears the insolvency of the sureties pursued without being able to transfer it to the other sureties.

###### § 2. Effect of suretyship between the debtor and the surety Article 2286

As soon as it is pursued the surety must notify the principal debtor or join it as a party before paying the debt to the pursuing creditor.
If the surety has paid without having notified or joined the principal debtor as a party, it loses its recourse against the debtor if, at the time of payment by it or subsequent to this payment, the debtor had the means to have the debt declared extinguished or if it had paid in ignorance of the surety's payment. Nevertheless, the surety retains its action for restitution against the pursuing creditor.

###### Article 2287

The surety who has paid has recourse against the principal debtor, even if the suretyship was given without the debtor's knowledge.
This recourse applies both to the principal and to interest and costs; nevertheless the surety only has recourse for costs incurred by it since it notified the principal debtor of the proceedings brought against it.
It also has recourse for damages, if applicable in case of prejudice it may have suffered from the creditor's proceedings.

###### Article 2288

The surety who has paid the debt is subrogated to all the rights and guarantees of the pursuing creditor against the debtor.
If there are several principal debtors jointly and severally liable for the same debt, the surety is subrogated against each of them for all that it has paid, even if it only stood surety for one. If the debtors are joint, it must divide its recourses.

###### Article 2289

The surety, even before having paid, may act against the debtor to be indemnified by the debtor, or request preservation of its rights in the debtor's patrimony:
1° As soon as it is pursued in court for payment; 2° When the debtor is in cessation of payments;
3° When the debtor has not discharged it within the agreed period;
4° When the debt has become due by expiry of the term under which it was contracted.

###### § 3. Effect of suretyship among the various sureties Article 2290

When several persons have stood surety for the same debtor for the same debt, the surety who has discharged the debt has recourse against the other sureties, each for its share and portion;

But this recourse only applies when the surety has paid in one of the cases set out in the preceding article.

##### Section III: Extinction of suretyship Article 2291

The obligation resulting from suretyship is extinguished by the same causes as under the general law of contracts.
Payment in kind definitively releases the surety, even if the creditor is subsequently evicted from the thing accepted by it. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.
Novation of the principal obligation by change of object or cause releases the surety unless it agrees to transfer its guarantee to the new debt. Any clause to the contrary stipulated before the novation is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2292

The surety's undertaking is extinguished independently of the principal obligation:
-	when in proceedings brought against it, the surety pleads set-off for a personal claim against the pursuing creditor;
-	when the creditor has granted a release of debt to the surety alone;
-	when confusion occurs between the person of the creditor and the surety;
-	when the creditor has voluntarily accepted immovable property or any effect in payment of the principal debt, even if subsequently the creditor were to be evicted therefrom;
-	for debts arising after the death of the surety;
-	in the case of article 2282.

###### Article 2293

The simple extension of time granted by the creditor to the principal debtor, or the modification of the security interests accompanying the principal obligation into new equivalent security interests, does not discharge the surety, who may, in such case, pursue the debtor to compel payment.

#### Chapitre II: De la lettre de garantie ou « garantie autonome » Article 2294

A letter of guarantee or autonomous guarantee is a necessarily written undertaking by which the guarantor binds himself, in consideration of an obligation entered into by a third party giving the order, to pay a sum either on first demand or according to agreed terms.
Such a contract may not be entered into, on pain of nullity, by natural persons; and may not, for legal persons, be stipulated for a purpose unrelated to the commercial or professional activity of the borrower. In such case, the letter of guarantee is governed by articles L.2281-201 et seq. of the commercial code.

#### Chapitre III: De la lettre d'intention

###### Article 2295

The letter of intent is an undertaking to do or not to do having as its object the support provided to a debtor in the performance of his obligation towards his creditor.

Sous-Titre II: Les sûretés réelles Chapitre I: Dispositions générales

###### Article 2296

Any real security interest may be created, registered, managed and enforced on behalf of the creditors of the guaranteed obligation by a person whom they designate for that purpose in the instrument evidencing such obligation.

###### Article 2297

A privilege is a right which the quality of the claim gives to a creditor to be preferred over other creditors, even secured creditors. It may be over movables or over immovables.
As between privileged creditors, preference is determined by the different qualities of the privileges. When they are of the same rank, privileged creditors are paid proportionately.

###### Article 2298

The privilege in respect of rights of the Public Treasury and the order in which it is exercised are governed by the laws concerning them.
The Public Treasury may not, however, obtain a privilege to the prejudice of rights previously acquired by third parties.

###### Article 2299

Privileges, like security interests, may be over movables or over immovables.

#### Chapitre II: Des sûretés sur les meubles Article 2300

Real security interests over movables include: the right of retention, the pledge, privileges and ownership retained or transferred by way of security.

##### Section I: Du droit de rétention Article 2301

A creditor who lawfully holds property of the debtor may retain it until full payment of what is owed to him, independently of any other security interest.
When the same property is the subject of several successive pledges without dispossession, the rank of creditors is determined by the order of their registration. When property given in pledge without dispossession is subsequently the subject of a pledge with dispossession, the preference right of the prior pledgee is enforceable against the subsequent pledgee when it is duly published notwithstanding the latter's right of retention.

###### Article 2302

The right of retention may only be exercised:
-	before any seizure;
-	if the claim is certain, liquidated and due;
-	if there exists a connection between the arising of the claim and the thing retained.

##### Section II: Du nantissement Article 2303

A pledge is a contract by which a debtor delivers a thing to his creditor as security for the debt.

Pledges without dispossession which relate to: rights of partners and securities; business goodwill; professional equipment; stocks of raw materials and merchandise, are governed by the provisions of the commercial code.
The pledge of a movable thing is called a gage. That of an immovable thing is called an immovable pledge.

###### Article 2304

Heavy equipment purchased by a private individual may be the subject of a pledge for the benefit of the seller, of the third party having guaranteed the purchaser's commitments towards the seller, or of any person having lent the sums necessary for the purchase.
Such a security interest is enforceable against third parties only if it is registered in the register of movable security interests.

###### Article 2305

A gage is a contract by which a debtor delivers a thing or a set of things of a movable nature to his creditor as security for the debt.
The secured claims may be present, future or contingent; in the latter two cases, they must be determinable and not be tainted with nullity.

The gage confers upon the creditor the right to be paid from the thing which is its object, by privilege and in preference to other creditors.

###### Article 2306

The gage may be granted by the debtor or by a third party; in the latter case, the creditor has recourse only against the property assigned as security.
Except for a gage granted by a third party, the gage of another's thing is null and may give rise to damages when the creditor was unaware that the thing belonged to another. If the thing does not belong to the grantor, the pledgee in good faith may oppose the owner's claim for recovery under the conditions provided for a possessor in good faith.

###### Article 2307

Any movable property, corporeal or incorporeal, is capable of being given in gage.

Movable security interests subject to publicity are the subject of registration, at the initiative of the creditor, in the register of movable security interests.

###### Article 2308

The parties may agree to the substitution during performance of the gage contract of the pledged thing by another thing.
The gage may also relate to sums or securities deposited as security by civil servants, ministerial officers or any other person to guarantee abuses for which they might be liable and loans granted for the constitution of such security.

###### Article 2309

The gage contract provided with dispossession produces effect only if the pledged thing is actually delivered to the creditor or to a third party agreed between the parties.

The promise of gage, in particular of future things, obliges the promisor to deliver the thing under the agreed conditions.

###### Article 2310

When it is without dispossession of the debtor, the gage is enforceable against third parties by the publicity given to it. This is effected at the initiative of the creditor in the register of movable security interests.

###### Article 2311

The gage contract is enforceable against third parties only if it is evidenced by a writing, authentic or under private signature, duly registered, and containing indication of the sum owed as well as the kind, nature and quantity of the movable property given in gage, unless otherwise provided by law.
The drafting of the instrument in writing and its registration are nevertheless required only for matters exceeding the value of 100,000 FD.
The gage is also enforceable against third parties by the dispossession into the hands of the creditor or of an agreed third party of the property which is its object.
If the gage is created over incorporeal movable property, such as a movable claim, the instrument, registered, is served on the debtor of the claim given in gage.

###### Article 2312

A debtor who pledges his claim against a named third party must deliver to the pledgee creditor his title to the claim and notify his own debtor of the transfer of his claim in that capacity; failing this, the pledgee creditor may proceed with such notification.
This pledge is realized by the demand for payment that the pledgee creditor addresses to the transferred debtor. The latter may raise against the pledgee creditor defenses based on his personal relations with his own creditor as well as defenses which he may assert against the pledgee creditor. It is otherwise if the transferred debtor has made a written commitment to pay the pledgee creditor directly, in which case he may not raise against the pledgee creditor defenses based on his personal relations with his own creditor.

The creditor of the transferred debtor remains liable, jointly and severally with the latter, for payment of the pledged claim.
The pledgee creditor who has obtained payment must account for it to his own debtor.

###### Article 2313

In other areas, if there are no specific legal provisions or contractual stipulations defining the methods of pledging the intangible property given as security, delivery to the creditor of the document evidencing the existence of the right effects dispossession of the grantor.

###### Article 2314

The deposit or consignment of sums, instruments or securities, ordered judicially as security or as a conservatory measure, entails special allocation and privilege under Article 2305 paragraph 3.

###### Article 2315

The pledgee creditor retains or causes to be retained the pledged thing by the agreed third party until full payment, in principal, interest and costs, of the debt for which the pledge was constituted.
If there arises on the part of the same debtor towards the same creditor, one or more other debts contracted subsequent to the pledging, and becoming due before payment of the first debt, the creditor may retain or cause to be retained the pledged thing until complete payment of all debts, even in the absence of any stipulation to that effect.

###### Article 2316

The privilege subsists on the pledge only insofar as the pledge has been placed and remains in the possession of the creditor, or of a third party agreed between the parties.
But if he has been dispossessed against his will, the creditor may claim the pledged thing as a possessor in good faith.

###### Article 2317

Until expropriation of the debtor, if applicable, the grantor remains owner of the pledge, which is, in the hand of the creditor, only a deposit securing the latter's privilege.

###### Article 2318

The creditor or the agreed third party must watch over the thing and ensure its preservation, as must a remunerated depositary. He is liable for the loss or deterioration of the pledge that occurs through his negligence.
He may not, except by contrary stipulation, use the pledged thing or collect its fruits. If he is authorized to collect the fruits, he must apply them, except by contrary clause, to what is owed to him in interest and principal. When the pledged thing is a claim, the provisions of Article 2320 apply.

If the thing threatens to perish, the creditor or the agreed third party may, upon authorization, as the case may be, from the Civil Chamber or the Commercial Chamber of the Court of First Instance, sell it and the effects of the pledge are then transferred to the price.
The agreed third party and, if applicable, the bad faith purchaser of the pledged thing are jointly and severally liable with the pledgee creditor for non-performance of these obligations.
The pledging of a consumable thing authorizes the creditor or the agreed third party to return an equivalent thing.

When the pledge has as its object fungible things, the creditor or the agreed third party may alienate them only if the agreement so provides, subject to replacing them with the same quantity of equivalent things. In the absence of a stipulation to that effect, he must keep them separate from things of the same nature belonging to him. If the creditor or the agreed third party fails to do so, the grantor may claim restitution of the pledged property, without prejudice to damages, if the creditor or the agreed third party does not satisfy his obligation to preserve the pledge. When the agreement dispenses the creditor from the obligation to separate the pledged property from his things of the same nature, he acquires ownership thereof subject to returning the same quantity of equivalent things.

###### Article 2319

For his part, when he has fully paid him the principal, interest and costs, the debtor must account to the creditor for the useful and necessary expenses that the latter incurred for the preservation of the pledge.

###### Article 2320

When the thing given as pledge is a claim:
-	if the maturity of the claim given as pledge is prior to the maturity of the secured claim, the pledgee creditor is entitled to collect the amount thereof in principal and interest, except by contrary clause;
-	if the maturity of the secured claim is prior to the maturity of the claim given as pledge, the pledgee creditor is required to wait for the maturity of the latter to collect the amount thereof.
In both cases, the pledgee creditor collects the amount of the pledged claim subject to accounting, in the capacity of agent, for the surplus collected in favor of the grantor of the pledge.
In addition, except by contrary agreement, if this claim bears interest, the creditor applies this interest to that which may be owed to him in interest and principal.
If the debt for security of which the claim was given as pledge does not itself bear interest, the application is made to the principal of the debt.

###### Article 2321

In default of payment at maturity, the pledgee creditor may, eight days after simple notification made to the debtor and to the third party who holds the thing delivered as pledge, if there is one, cause the pledged thing to be sold at public sale.
The sale is conducted by a bailiff at least eight days after publication of a notice in a newspaper authorized to receive legal announcements mentioning the date, time and place of the sale, the place where the objects may be viewed, the reserve price or prices, the description of the object and the costs.

The creditor may also apply, as the case may be, to the Civil Chamber or the Commercial Chamber of the Court of First Instance to request that the pledge be attributed to him or sold to a third party up to the amount of his claim and according to valuation following market rates or by expert opinion.
Any clause that would authorize the creditor to appropriate the pledge or to dispose of it without the above formalities is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2322

In case of sale or loss or destruction of the pledged thing, the pledgee creditor has priority over the price of the thing sold or over the insurance indemnity for the amount of the secured claim in principal, interest and costs.
He exercises his right of preference in accordance with Article 2331 of this code. If there are several pledgee creditors, they are ranked in the order of registration of successive pledges or, in the absence of registration, in the order of constitution.

###### Article 2323

The pledge is indivisible notwithstanding the divisibility of the debt towards the heirs of the debtor or those of the creditor.
The heir of the debtor who has paid his portion of the debt may not demand restitution of his portion in the pledge, even if it is divisible by nature, as long as the debt is not entirely discharged.

Reciprocally, the heir of the creditor who has received his share of the claim may not release the pledge, even if it is divisible, to the prejudice of those of his co-heirs who are not paid.

###### Article 2324

The commercial pledge is governed by the provisions of the commercial code.

###### Article 2325

The pledge relating to a registered motor vehicle or trailer is governed by this article and articles 2326 to 2329 below.
This pledge is enforceable against third parties by the declaration made to the Mining Service. This declaration is recorded in a special register with counterfoils and mentions the creation of the pledge to which the vehicle or trailer is subject, the name of the owner of the property and that of the creditor, and the date of registration of the contract.

A receipt for this declaration is issued to the pledgee creditor, repeating verbatim the particulars appearing on the counterfoil. By possession of this receipt, the pledgee creditor is deemed to have retained the vehicle or trailer in his possession.

###### Article 2326

In the case of a pledge relating to a new vehicle or trailer, the registration of the pledge by the seller, assignee of the debt, discounter or lender of money for the purchase made, must be done within three months from the issue of the receipt for the declaration of putting the vehicle into circulation.

###### Article 2327

The cancellation of the pledge notation may be requested either by the creditor or by the debtor.

When it is done by the creditor, indication of the cancellation is recorded on the receipt that was issued to him. In this case, the debtor may request to obtain a certificate of cancellation.
When it is done by the debtor, the latter must justify the extinction of the guaranteed debt or produce the deed giving release of the registration. A certificate of cancellation is then issued to him.

###### Article 2328

In the absence of payment of the guaranteed debt, the creditor may have the sale of the pledged property ordered by the court. This sale takes place according to the procedures provided for enforcement proceedings without the pledge agreement being able to derogate therefrom.
The creditor may also have it ordered by the court that the property shall remain with him in payment. When the value of the property exceeds the amount of the guaranteed debt, the sum equal to the difference is paid to the debtor or, if there are other pledgee creditors, is deposited.

###### Article 2329

It may be agreed, at the time of creation of the pledge or subsequently, that in the absence of performance of the guaranteed obligation the creditor shall become owner of the pledged property.
The value of the property is determined on the day of transfer by an expert appointed amicably or judicially. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.
When this value exceeds the amount of the guaranteed debt, the sum equal to the difference is paid to the debtor or, if there are other pledgee creditors, is deposited.

##### Section III: Privileges over movable property

###### Article 2330

Privileges are either general, or special over certain movable property.

###### § 1. General privileges over movable property Article 2331

Privileged claims over all movable property are those expressed below, and are exercised in the following order, without formality of publicity:
1° Court costs; 2° Funeral expenses;
3° Any costs of the last illness preceding the seizure of property, whatever its outcome, concurrently among those to whom they are owed;
4° Without prejudice to the possible application of the provisions of articles 152 to 155 of the labour code, the privileges of wages, which relate to:
-	sums owed to workers and apprentices for performance and termination of their contract during the last six months preceding the death of the debtor, the seizure of property or the judicial decision opening collective proceedings;
-	compensation owed for paid leave;
-	severance compensation owed;

5° Supplies of subsistence provided to the debtor and his family during the last year

6° Sums owed to authors of intellectual, literary and artistic works for the last three years preceding the death of the debtor, the seizure of property or the judicial decision opening collective proceedings;

7° Up to a limit of one million Djibouti Francs, the sums for which the debtor is liable in respect of tax and customs claims and to the National Social Security Fund.

###### Article 2332

It is recalled that, in accordance with article 2298, the privilege, by reason of the rights of the Public Treasury and the order in which it is exercised, are governed by the laws concerning them. The same applies to claims for contributions to the National Social Security Fund.
Special texts creating general privileges must specify the rank thereof by determining it in relation to the provisions of this article. Failing this, the rank of these privileges is the last of that established by this article.

###### § 2. Privileges over certain movable property Article 2333

Creditors holding special privileges have, over the movable property assigned to them as a basis by law, a right of preference.

This right of preference is also exercised, by subrogation, over the insurance indemnity for the movable property that has perished or disappeared, as long as it is not paid.

###### Article 2334

Privileged claims over certain movable property are, without prejudice to special texts establishing others, those:
1° Of the lessor of immovable property, who has a privilege over the fruits and income of the year, and over the price of everything that furnishes the leased property.
This privilege guarantees, in addition to the damages that may be awarded to him, the claims of the lessor against the lessee for the twelve months elapsed preceding the seizure and for the twelve months to fall due after it.
The lessee or any person who, by fraudulent manoeuvres, deprives the lessor of his privilege totally or partially, commits a criminal offence punished by the penalties for breach of trust.
The owner may seize the movable property furnishing his house or farm, when they have been moved without his consent, and he retains his privilege over them, provided that he has made the claim in the deed of seizure; however, the lessor who thus claims the movable property moved without his consent must reimburse the purchaser the price they cost him.
2° Of the pledgee creditor, over the pledge he realizes;

3° Of the person who has incurred expenses or provided services for the preservation of the thing;

4° Of the seller, who has, over the movable property sold, a privilege to guarantee payment of the unpaid price, if it is still in the possession of the debtor or over the price still owed by the sub-purchaser.
5° The hotelier for his supplies, over the effects of the traveller that have been transported to his hotel; 6° The carrier, for carriage costs and ancillary expenses, over the thing transported;
7° Holders of claims resulting from abuses and malfeasance committed by public officials in the exercise of their functions, over the funds of their security deposit and over the interest that may be owed thereon;
8° Holders of claims arising from an accident for the benefit of third parties injured by this accident or their successors in title, over the indemnity for which the civil liability insurer acknowledges itself or has been judicially recognized as debtor by reason of the insurance agreement.

No payment made to the insured shall be liberatory as long as the privileged creditors have not been satisfied.

##### Section V: Ownership retained or transferred as security

###### § 1. Ownership retained as security Article 2335

Ownership of property may be retained as security by the effect of a retention of title clause. The effect of a retention of title clause is to suspend the transfer effect of a contract until complete payment of the obligation that constitutes the consideration therefor.

The ownership thus reserved is accessory to the claim whose payment it guarantees.

###### Article 2336

Retention of title must necessarily be agreed in writing.

###### Article 2337

Reserved ownership of a fungible good may be exercised, up to the amount of the debt remaining due, over goods of the same nature and same quality held by the debtor or on his account.

###### Article 2338

The incorporation of a movable subject to reservation of ownership into another good does not prevent the creditor's rights when these goods can be separated without suffering damage.

###### Article 2339

In the absence of full payment at maturity, the creditor may demand the restitution of the good in order to recover the right to dispose of it.
The value of the good repossessed is imputed, as payment, on the balance of the secured debt.

When the value of the good repossessed exceeds the amount of the secured debt still due, the creditor owes the debtor a sum equal to the difference.

###### Article 2340

The right of ownership transfers to the debtor's claim against the sub-purchaser or to the insurance indemnity subrogated to the good.

###### § 2. Ownership transferred as security Article 2341

Ownership of a movable good or a right may be transferred as security for an obligation by virtue of a fiduciary contract concluded in application of articles 2205 to 2245.

###### Article 2342

In case of fiduciary concluded as security, the contract mentions on pain of nullity, in addition to the provisions provided for in article 2210, the secured debt and the estimated value of the good or right transferred into the fiduciary patrimony.

###### Article 2343

In the absence of payment of the secured debt and unless otherwise stipulated in the fiduciary contract, the fiduciary, when he is the creditor, acquires free disposal of the good or right transferred as security.
When the fiduciary is not the creditor, the latter may require from him the delivery of the good, which he may then freely dispose of, or, if the fiduciary contract so provides, the sale of the good or right transferred and the delivery of all or part of the price.

The value of the good or right transferred is determined by an expert designated amicably or judicially, unless the good is a sum of money. Any contrary clause is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2344

If the beneficiary of the fiduciary has acquired free disposal of the good or right transferred in application of article 2343, he pays to the settlor, when the value mentioned in the last paragraph of that article exceeds the amount of the secured debt, a sum equal to the difference between that value and the amount of the debt, subject to prior payment of debts arising from the conservation or management of the fiduciary patrimony.
Subject to the same reservation, if the fiduciary proceeds with the sale of the good or right transferred in application of the fiduciary contract, he restores to the settlor the part of the proceeds of that sale exceeding, where applicable, the value of the secured debt.

###### Article 2345

The ownership transferred in application of article 2341 may be subsequently allocated to the security of debts other than those mentioned by the constitutive act provided that it expressly so provides.
The settlor may offer it as security, not only to the original creditor, but also to a new creditor, even though the first has not been paid. When the settlor is a natural person, the fiduciary patrimony may then be allocated as security for a new debt only within the limit of its value estimated on the day of the recharge.

On pain of nullity, the agreement established according to the provisions of article 2342 is registered in the form provided for in article 2213. The date of registration determines, between them, the rank of creditors.

The provisions of this article are of public order and any clause contrary to them is deemed unwritten.

#### Chapter III: Securities over immovables Article 2346

Securities over immovables are: privileges, immovable pledge (or antichresis), and mortgages.
Ownership of the immovable may also be retained or transferred as security.

##### Section I: Immovable pledge or "antichresis" Article 2347

Immovable pledge, or antichresis, is the allocation, by the debtor or by a third party for the debtor, of an immovable as security for an obligation; it entails dispossession of the one who constitutes it.
Immovable pledge is established only in writing.

The creditor acquires by this contract only the faculty to collect the fruits of the immovable, with the obligation to impute them annually on the interest, if any is owed to him, and then on the principal of his debt. He may for this purpose, without losing possession of the good, lease the immovable, either to a third party or to the debtor himself.

###### Article 2348

The creditor is bound, unless otherwise agreed, to pay the contributions and annual charges of the immovable that he holds as immovable pledge.
He must also, on pain of damages, provide for the maintenance and useful and necessary repairs of the immovable, and may deduct for this purpose, from the fruits, all expenses relating to these various matters. He may, at any time, free himself from this obligation by restoring the good to its owner.

###### Article 2349

The debtor may not claim enjoyment of the immovable that he has delivered as immovable pledge before the full discharge of his debt.

###### Article 2350

The creditor does not become owner of the immovable by the mere default of payment at the agreed term; any contrary clause is null.

The creditor, in case of default of payment at the agreed term may however pursue the expropriation of his debtor by legal means.

###### Article 2351

The provisions of article 2323 apply to immovable pledge.

###### Article 2352

Everything provided in this chapter does not prejudice the rights that third parties might have over the land of the immovable delivered as immovable pledge. Indeed, immovable pledge being only a delegation of fruits as they fall due or are collected, third parties may acquire and exercise their rights over the pledged immovable.
If the creditor, provided with this title, has over the land privileges or mortgages legally established and preserved, he exercises them in his order and like any other creditor.

###### Article 2353

The rights of the creditor holding an immovable pledge right are extinguished notably: 1° By the extinction of the principal obligation;
2° By the early restitution of the immovable to its owner.

##### Section II: Immovable Privileges

###### § 1. Special Privileges on Immovables Article 2354

Privileged creditors on immovables are:

1° The vendor, on the immovable sold, for payment of the price;

If there are several successive sales of which the price is owed in whole or in part, the first vendor is preferred to the second, the second to the third, and so on;
2° Those who have provided funds for the acquisition of an immovable, provided that it is authentically established, by the loan agreement, that the sum was intended for that use and, by the vendor's receipt, that this payment was made from the borrowed funds;

3° Co-heirs, on the immovables of the succession, for the guarantee of partitions made between them, and of balancing payments or returns of lots;

4° Architects, contractors and artisans who have built, rebuilt or repaired buildings, canals or any other works whatsoever, provided nevertheless that, by an expert appointed ex officio by the court of first instance within whose jurisdiction the buildings are situated, a report has been drawn up beforehand, for the purpose of establishing the state of the premises in relation to the works that the owner will declare his intention to have done, and that the works have been, within six months at most of their completion, received by an expert also appointed ex officio. But the amount of the privilege cannot exceed the values established by the second report, and it is reduced to the increased value existing at the time of alienation of the immovable and resulting from the works that have been done thereon;

5° Those who have lent the funds to pay or reimburse the workers, enjoy the same privilege, provided that this use is authentically established by the loan agreement, and by the workers' receipt, as stated above for those who have lent the funds for the acquisition of an immovable;

6° The creditors of the deceased and the legatees of sums of money on the immovables of the succession, as well as the personal creditors of the heir on the immovables of the latter, for the guarantee of the rights they hold from article 1028.

###### Article 2355

The privileges enumerated in articles 2331 and 2354 of the civil code, with the exception however of the privilege for costs of justice, incurred for the realization of the immovable and the distribution of the price, only provide a right of preference to the beneficiaries called to exercise them on the immovable mass over unsecured creditors.

###### § 2. General Privileges on Immovables Article 2356

The privileges that extend over movables and immovables are those set out in article 2331.

###### Article 2357

When, for lack of movable property, the privileged creditors set out in the preceding article present themselves to be paid on the price of an immovable in competition with other privileged creditors on the immovable, payments are made in the following order:
1° The costs of justice and others set out in article 2331; 2° The claims designated in article 235

###### 4. §

3. How Immovable Privileges are Preserved Article 2358
As between creditors, privileges only produce effect with regard to immovables insofar as they are made public by registration in the registers of the keeper of mortgages, in the manner determined by law, and from the date of that registration, subject only to the following exceptions.

###### Article 2359

The claims enumerated in article 2331 are excepted from the formality of registration.

###### Article 2360

If their privilege is established by a notarial deed to be published in the land register:
1° The privileged vendor preserves his privilege by the transcription of the title that transferred ownership to the purchaser, and which establishes that all or part of the price is owed to him; for which purpose, the transcription of the contract made by the purchaser shall be valid as registration for the vendor and for the lender who has provided him with the sums paid, and who will be subrogated to the rights of the vendor by the same contract. In this case, the keeper of mortgages shall nevertheless be required, on pain of all damages and interest towards third parties, to make ex officio the registration in his register, of the claims resulting from the deed transferring ownership, both in favor of the vendor and in favor of the lenders, who may also have made, if it has not been done, the transcription of the sale contract, for the purpose of acquiring the registration of what is owed to them on the price.

2° The co-heir or co-partitioner preserves his privilege on the property of each lot or on the property sold by licitation for the balancing payments and returns of lots or for the price of the licitation, by registration made at his initiative, within sixty days, from the date of the partition deed or the adjudication by licitation; during which time no mortgage may take place on the property charged with the balancing payment or adjudicated by licitation, to the prejudice of the creditor of the balancing payment or of the price.

###### Article 2361

Architects, contractors, masons and other workers employed to build, rebuild or repair buildings, canals, or other works, and those who have, to pay and reimburse them, lent the sums whose use has been established, preserve by the double registration made:

1° Of the report that establishes the state of the premises;

2° Of the report of receipt, their privilege at the date of registration of the first report.

###### Article 2362

Creditors and legatees who request the separation of the patrimony of the deceased, in accordance with article 665 of the title On Successions, preserve, with regard to the creditors of the heirs or representatives of the deceased, their privilege on the immovables of the succession, by registrations made on each of these properties, within six months from the opening of the succession.
Before the expiration of this period, no mortgage may be established with effect on these properties by the heirs or representatives to the prejudice of these creditors or legatees.

###### Article 2363

The assignees of these various privileged claims exercise all the same rights as the assignors in their place and stead.

###### Article 2364

All privileged claims subject to the formality of registration, with regard to which the conditions prescribed above to preserve the privilege have not been fulfilled, do not nevertheless cease to be secured by mortgage, but the mortgage only dates, with regard to third parties, from the time of the registrations that must have been made as will be explained hereinafter.

##### Section III: Mortgages Article 2365

Applicable, in a general manner and subject to the provisions that follow, to registered immovables and to the real rights relating thereto, are the provisions of Law No. 177/AN/91/2ème L on the organization of land ownership.

###### Article 2366

A mortgage is a real right on immovables assigned to the discharge of an obligation.

It is, by its nature, indivisible, and subsists in its entirety on all the immovables assigned, on each and on each portion of these immovables.

It follows them into whatever hands they pass.

###### Article 2367

A mortgage only takes place in the cases and according to the forms authorized by law.

###### Article 2368

Only the following are susceptible to mortgages:
1° Lands built or unbuilt that are in commerce and with them, their accessories deemed immovable;
2° The usufruct of the same properties, during the time of its duration;
3° The rights of emphyteusis, during the time of its duration, and of superficies, established on the same properties. Movables have no right of pursuit by mortgage.

Ships and seagoing vessels are governed by the provisions specific to them.

###### Article 2369

A mortgage is either legal, judicial, or conventional. A legal mortgage is one that results from the law.
A judicial mortgage is one that results from judgments or judicial acts. A mortgage may likewise result from judgments rendered in foreign countries, if they have been declared enforceable by a Djiboutian court, subject to special laws or treaties. Similarly, arbitral awards give rise to a mortgage only insofar as they are vested with the exequatur.
A conventional mortgage is one that results from contracts and other juridical acts. It is granted by notarial deed; the transfer and release of the mortgage take place in the same forms.

###### Article 2370

A conventional mortgage may be granted only by those who have the capacity to alienate the immovable property they subject to it. The property of minors, adults under guardianship, and that of absentees as long as possession is granted only provisionally, may be mortgaged only for the causes and in the forms established by law, or by virtue of judgments; those who have over the immovable property only a right suspended by a condition, or resolvable in certain cases, or subject to rescission, may grant only a mortgage subject to the same conditions or to the same rescission.
The authentic instrument specifically declares the nature and location of each of the immovable properties currently belonging to the debtor, on which he grants the mortgage of the debt.

###### Article 2371

Future property cannot be mortgaged.

Nevertheless, if the present and unencumbered property of the debtor is insufficient for the security of the debt, he may, by acknowledging this insufficiency, consent that each of the properties he subsequently acquires be specially assigned thereto as acquisitions are made.

###### Article 2372

If the present immovable property or properties subject to the mortgage perish or suffer deterioration to such an extent that they become insufficient for the security of the creditor, the creditor may obtain a supplementary mortgage or, failing that, pursue his reimbursement forthwith.

###### Article 2373

A conventional mortgage is valid only insofar as the sum for which it is granted is certain and determined by the deed: if the debt resulting from the obligation is conditional as to its existence, or indeterminate in its value, the creditor may require the registration of which mention will be made hereinafter, only up to an estimated value expressly declared by him, and which the debtor shall have the right to have reduced, if appropriate.

###### Article 2374

Mortgages and privileges that have given rise to registration are extinguished: 1° By the extinction of the obligation of which they constitute the guarantee;
2° By the creditor's renunciation of his right;
3° By the completion of the procedure for purging mortgages by the third-party holder upon forced expropriation or upon expropriation for reasons of public utility, in accordance with the requirements of Article 51 of Law No. 177/AN/91/2nd L on the organization of land ownership.

##### Section IV: Immovable property transferred as security

###### Article 2375

The provisions of this chapter are not applicable to fiduciary arrangements constituted as security by legal persons.

###### Article 2376

Ownership of immovable property may be transferred as security for an obligation by virtue of a fiduciary contract concluded in application of Articles 2205 to 2245.

###### Article 2377

In the case of a fiduciary arrangement concluded as security, the contract must mention, on pain of nullity, in addition to the provisions provided for in Article 2210, the secured debt and the estimated value of the immovable property transferred into the fiduciary estate.

###### Article 2378

In the absence of payment of the secured debt and unless otherwise stipulated in the fiduciary contract, the fiduciary, when he is the creditor, acquires free disposal of the property transferred as security.
When the fiduciary is not the creditor, the latter may require from him the delivery of the property, which he may then freely dispose of, or, if the agreement so provides, the sale of the property and the delivery of all or part of the price.

The value of the property is determined by an expert appointed amicably or judicially. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2379

If the beneficiary of the fiduciary arrangement has acquired free disposal of the property in application of Article 2378, he pays to the settlor, when the value mentioned in the last paragraph of that article exceeds the amount of the secured debt, a sum equal to the difference between that value and the amount of the debt, subject to the prior payment of debts arising from the preservation or management of the fiduciary estate.
Subject to the same reservation, if the fiduciary proceeds with the sale of the property in application of the fiduciary contract, he returns to the settlor the portion of the proceeds of that sale exceeding, where applicable, the value of the secured debt.

###### Article 2380

The ownership transferred in application of Article 2376 may be subsequently assigned as security for debts other than those mentioned in the constitutive deed provided that the latter expressly so provides.
The settlor may offer it as security, not only to the original creditor, but also to a new creditor, even though the first has not been paid. When the settlor is a natural person, the fiduciary estate may then be assigned as security for a new debt only within the limit of its value estimated on the day of the recharge.

On pain of nullity, the agreement established according to the provisions of Article 2377 is published in the form provided for in Article 2213. The date of publication determines, among them, the rank of the creditors.
The provisions of this article are of public order and any clause contrary to them is deemed unwritten.

### TITRE XX: Immovable revendication and forced sale of immovable property

###### Article 2381

The action for revendication of an immovable property and the forced sale of immovable property is pursued in compliance with the provisions of the code of civil procedure and those of Law No. 177/AN/91/2nd L on the organization of land ownership.

### Titre XXI: Prescription

Chapitre Ier: General provisions Article 2382
Prescription is a means of acquiring or being released by a certain lapse of time, and under the conditions determined by law.

Time limits for forfeiture are not, except for contrary provisions provided by law, governed by this title.

The provisions of this title do not preclude the application of special rules provided by other texts or special laws.

###### Article 2383

Extinctive prescription is a mode of extinction of a right resulting from the inaction of its holder for a time defined by law.
It is subject to the law governing the right it affects.

###### Article 2384

Acquisitive prescription is a means of acquiring property or a right by the effect of possession, when the law authorizes such an effect.

###### Article 2385

Prescription can in no case constitute a mode of acquisition of real rights over immovable property or of release from charges encumbering the same immovable property.

###### Article 2386

In movable matters, possession may produce an acquisitive effect of right under the conditions set forth in Article 686 and following.

###### Article 2387

One cannot renounce prescription in advance; one may renounce acquired prescription.

Renunciation of prescription is express or tacit; tacit renunciation results from a fact that presupposes the abandonment of the acquired right.

One who cannot exercise his rights by himself cannot alone renounce acquired prescription.

###### Article 2388

Except in case of waiver, prescription may be raised at any stage of the proceedings, even before the court of appeal.

Creditors, or any other person having an interest in the prescription being acquired, may raise it, even if the debtor or the owner has said he waives it.
Judges may not raise the defense of prescription of their own motion.

###### Article 2389

Payment made to extinguish a debt may not be reclaimed on the sole ground that the prescription period had expired.

###### Article 2390

The State, public establishments and communes are subject to the same prescriptions as private individuals, and may also raise them.

###### Article 2391

However, the following are imprescriptible, subject to the texts that govern them:
1° Property belonging to the public domain within the meaning of the law (specifically referred to here are Law No. 171/AN/91/2nd L establishing and organizing the public domain and Law No. 173/AN/91/2nd L organizing the private domain of the State);
2° Things that are not in commerce;
3° In accordance with Article 674, the right of ownership as well as the rights and actions that are attributes of the right of ownership, such as for example the right to acquire joint ownership of a wall, the right to use running water of which one is a riparian owner, the right to claim passage for the owner of a landlocked property, the right to enclose, or the right to request partition.

#### Chapitre II : Des causes qui empêchent la prescription mobilière Article 2392

One cannot change for oneself the cause and basis of one's possession, so that one prescribes according to the obligation one has contracted. Thus, those who possess for another never prescribe by any lapse of time whatsoever. Such is the case, for example, of the depositary or the usufructuary, and of all others who hold the thing of the owner precariously, cannot prescribe it.

The heirs of those who held the thing under any such precarious titles cannot prescribe either.

###### Article 2393

It is otherwise in case of interversion of title, namely when the person whom the owner designates as precarious holder considers that his holding has been changed into possession or ownership.

###### Article 2394

Those to whom the thing has been transferred by a precarious holder by a title transferring ownership may nevertheless prescribe it when the conditions of possession are fulfilled.

#### Chapitre III

Du cours de la prescription Section I : Dispositions générales

###### Article 2395

Prescription runs against all persons, unless they are within some exception established by law.

###### Article 2396

Prescription is counted by days, and not by hours.

It is acquired when the last day of the term is completed.

###### Article 2397

When a new law lengthens the duration of a prescription period or a forfeiture period, it has no effect on a prescription or forfeiture already acquired. Subject to any transitional provisions it may provide, such a law applies immediately to the situation when the prescription period or forfeiture period had not expired on the date of its entry into force; the time already elapsed is then taken into account.

If the new law reduces the duration of a prescription period or a forfeiture period, this new period runs from the day of entry into force of this new law, without the total duration being able to exceed the duration provided for by the former law.

###### Article 2398

The prescription period may be interrupted or suspended according to the causes indicated by law.

Interruption of prescription erases the period already acquired and starts a new period running. This new period is of the same duration as the former one.
Suspension of prescription temporarily stops its running without erasing the period already elapsed.

##### Section II : Du délai de droit commun et de certains délais particuliers Article 2399

Except where otherwise provided:

1° Personal or movable actions are prescribed after three years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling him to exercise it;

2° Real immovable actions are prescribed after thirty years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling him to exercise it.

3° The prescription period is:
a.	10 years in case of bodily injury for the victim, from the date of consolidation of the injury;
b.	10 years for ecological damage;
c.	20 years in case of harm related to an act of torture or barbarity, or violence or sexual assault against minors.
d.	Architects, contractors and other persons bound to the owner by a contract for work are discharged from the warranty of the works they have made or directed after ten years if they are major works, after two years for minor works.
e.	The action of bailiffs, for the salary of the acts they serve and the commissions they execute; the action of notaries for payment of their acts; the action of doctors, surgeons, dental surgeons, midwives and pharmacists, for their visits, operations and medicines, are prescribed after two years.
f.	The action of lawyers, for payment of their costs and fees, is prescribed after two years, from the judgment of the proceedings or the settlement of the parties, or since the revocation of said lawyers. With regard to unfinished matters, they may not make claims for their costs and fees going back more than five years.
g.	Prescription, in the above cases, takes place, even though there has been continuation of supplies, deliveries, services and works.
It ceases to run only when there has been a settled account, note or obligation, or legal summons not lapsed.
h.	Nevertheless, those against whom these prescriptions are raised may defer the oath to those who raise them, on the question of whether the thing has actually been paid.
The oath may be deferred to the widows and heirs, or to the guardians of the latter, if they are minors, so that they may declare whether they do not know that the thing is due.

i.	Judges, bailiffs as well as persons who have represented or assisted the parties are discharged from the documents five years after the judgment or the cessation of their involvement.
j.	The action of workers for payment of salary, salary accessories, bonuses and allowances of any kind as well as, more generally, any sum due by the employer to the worker, and that for provision of benefits in kind and possibly their reimbursement, are prescribed after one year. Prescription runs from the date from which the salary is payable. It is suspended or interrupted under the conditions provided for in Section III below.

###### Article 2400

All actions, both real and personal, are prescribed after thirty years, without the person alleging this prescription being obliged to produce a title or being able to be met with the exception derived from bad faith.
The thirty-year extinctive prescription established by the preceding paragraph is not applicable to cases where the law sets a shorter period running from the day of knowledge of the fact, act or event.

##### Section III : Des causes qui interrompent ou suspendent la prescription

###### § 1. Des causes qui interrompent le cours de la prescription Article 2401

Prescription is interrupted:
1° When the possessor is deprived for more than one year of the enjoyment of the thing, either by the purported owner, or even by a third party;
2° By the acknowledgment that the debtor or the possessor makes of the right of the person against whom he was prescribing.

###### Article 2402

A legal claim, even in summary proceedings, a formal demand or a seizure, served on the person one wishes to prevent from acquiring by prescription, also interrupts the limitation period as well as the foreclosure period.
The same applies when the legal claim is brought before an incompetent court, or when the summons is void by reason of a defect in form.
The interruption resulting from the legal claim produces its effects until the extinction of the proceedings.

###### Article 2403

The interruption is regarded as having not occurred:
-	if the claimant withdraws his claim;
-	if he allows the proceedings to lapse;
-	or if his claim is definitively rejected.

###### Article 2404

A formal demand made to one of the joint and several debtors by a legal claim, or by an act of forced execution, or the acknowledgment by the debtor of the right of the person against whom he was acquiring by prescription, interrupts prescription against all the others, even against their heirs.
On the other hand, a formal demand made to one of the heirs of a joint and several debtor, or the acknowledgment of that heir, does not interrupt prescription with regard to the other co-heirs, even in the case of a mortgage debt, if the obligation is divisible. That formal demand or that acknowledgment interrupts prescription, with regard to the other co-debtors, only for the share for which that heir is liable.
To interrupt prescription for the whole, with regard to the other co-debtors, formal demand made to all the heirs of the deceased debtor, or acknowledgment by all those heirs, is required.

###### Article 2405

A formal demand made to the principal debtor, or his acknowledgment, interrupts prescription against the surety.

###### § 2. Des causes qui suspendent le cours de la prescription Article 2406

By way of exception to Article 2395, prescription does not run against a person who cannot validly act, by reason of an impediment resulting from the law, from an agreement, or from force majeure.

###### Article 2407

Prescription does not run against unemancipated minors and adults under guardianship, with the exception of cases determined by law.
Thus and by way of exception, prescription runs against unemancipated minors and adults under guardianship, subject to their recourse against their guardians: prescriptions relating to the payment or recovery of wages, arrears of annuities, maintenance payments, rents, rental charges, interest on sums lent and, generally, actions for payment of everything that is payable by years or at shorter periodic terms.

###### Article 2408

Prescription does not run between spouses, one against the other.

###### Article 2409

Prescription does not run:
-	with regard to a claim that depends on a condition, until the condition occurs;
-	with regard to an action in warranty, until eviction has taken place;
-	with regard to a claim at a fixed date, until that date has arrived.

###### Article 2410

Prescription does not run against the beneficiary heir, with regard to claims he has against the estate.
On the other hand, it runs against a vacant estate, even in the case where it is not provided with a curator.

###### Article 2411

When the law grants a person a grace period, the prescription of the property and rights concerned is suspended during that legally granted time.

Article final Dispositions transitoires générales

All texts contrary to the provisions of this code are repealed, except when they create texts derogating from the common law, in consideration of their domain.
References to provisions repealed, amended or moved by this code and contained in provisions of any nature, legislative as well as regulatory, are replaced by references to provisions having the same subject matter.

Contracts and other legal acts that were entered into under the previous code are valid if they complied with the conditions then required.

Prescriptions commenced at the time of publication of this code are governed in accordance with the former texts. Nevertheless, prescriptions then commenced, and for which, according to the former laws, more than thirty years would still be required from the same time, shall be completed by that period of thirty years, all subject to Article 2400, paragraph 2.

This law shall be executed upon its promulgation.
RÉPUBLIQUE DE DJIBOUTI
Unité-Egalité-Paix

Final Article
General transitional provisions

Civil Code of the Republic of Djibouti

Preliminary Title: On the publication, effects and application of laws in general

###### Article 1

Laws are enforceable in Djiboutian territory by virtue of their promulgation by the President of the Republic, and enter into force on the day they specify or, failing that, the day after their publication in the Official Journal of the Republic of Djibouti.
Publication within the meaning of this text means the first publication in date made by the National Printing Office or by dematerialised means.

###### Article 2

The law applies only for the future; it has no retroactive effect.

###### Article 3

Laws of police and security bind all those who inhabit the territory.

Immovable property, even that owned by foreigners, is governed by Djiboutian law.
Laws concerning the status and capacity of persons govern Djiboutians, even residing in a foreign country.

###### Article 4

A judge who refuses to adjudicate, on the pretext of the silence, obscurity or insufficiency of the law, may be prosecuted as guilty of denial of justice.

###### Article 5

Judges are prohibited from ruling by way of general and regulatory provision on the cases submitted to them.

###### Article 6

One cannot derogate, by private agreements, from laws that concern public order and good morals.

## BOOK I: ON PERSONS

Title I: On civil rights and the individual

Chapter I: On the enjoyment of civil rights

###### Article 7

The exercise of civil rights is independent of the exercise of political rights, which are acquired and retained in accordance with constitutional and electoral laws.

###### Article 8

Every person enjoys legal personality.

###### Article 9

Everyone has the right to respect for their private life.
Judges may, without prejudice to compensation for damage suffered, prescribe all measures, such as sequestration, seizure and others, appropriate to prevent or stop an infringement of the privacy of private life; these measures may, if there is urgency, be ordered in summary proceedings.

###### Article 10

Everyone has the right to respect for the presumption of innocence.
When a person is, before any conviction, publicly presented as being guilty of facts that are the subject of an investigation or judicial inquiry, the judge may, even in summary proceedings, without prejudice to compensation for damage suffered, prescribe all measures, such as the insertion of a correction or the dissemination of a statement, for the purpose of stopping the infringement of the presumption of innocence, at the expense of the person, natural or legal, responsible for this infringement.

###### Article 11

Every Djiboutian shall enjoy civil rights.

A foreigner shall enjoy in Djibouti the same civil rights as those granted by treaty to Djiboutians by the State of which the foreigner is a national.

The provisions of the Family Code form the ordinary law regime of the family (marriage, divorce, filiation, successions and liberalities) and fall under the Personal Status Court; the provisions of the Civil Code relating to family law fall under the jurisdiction of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 12

A foreigner, even not residing in Djibouti, may be summoned before Djiboutian courts for the performance of obligations contracted by him in Djibouti with a Djiboutian; he may be brought before the courts of Djibouti for obligations contracted by him in a foreign country towards Djiboutians.

###### Article 13

A Djiboutian may be brought before Djiboutian courts for obligations contracted by him in a foreign country, even with a foreigner.

#### Chapter II: On respect for the human body Article 14

The law ensures the primacy of the person, prohibits any infringement of the dignity thereof and guarantees respect for the human being from the beginning of life.

###### Article 15

Everyone has the right to respect for their body.

###### Article 16

The human body is inviolable.

The human body, its elements and its products cannot be the subject of a property right.

###### Article 17

The respect due to the human body does not cease with death.

The remains of deceased persons, including the ashes of those whose body has been cremated, must be treated with respect, dignity and decency.

###### Article 18

The judge may prescribe all measures appropriate to prevent or stop an unlawful infringement of the human body or unlawful acts concerning elements or products thereof, including after death.

###### Article 19

The integrity of the human body may only be infringed in case of medical necessity for the person or exceptionally in the therapeutic interest of another.
The consent of the person concerned must be obtained beforehand except in the case where their condition makes necessary a therapeutic intervention to which they are not able to consent.

###### Article 20

No one may infringe the integrity of the human species.

Any eugenic practice tending to organise the selection of persons is prohibited.

Any intervention aimed at causing the birth of a child genetically identical to another living or deceased person is prohibited.
Without prejudice to research aimed at the prevention and treatment of genetic diseases, no transformation may be made to genetic characteristics for the purpose of modifying the person's descendants.

###### Article 21

Agreements having the effect of conferring a property value on the human body, its elements or its products are null and void.

###### Article 22

No remuneration may be granted to one who submits to experimentation on their person, to the removal of elements of their body or to the collection of products thereof.

###### Article 23

Any agreement concerning procreation or gestation on behalf of another is null and void.

###### Article 24

No information allowing the identification of both the person who donated an element or product of their body and the person who received it may be disclosed. The donor cannot know the identity of the recipient nor the recipient that of the donor.
In case of therapeutic necessity, only the doctors of the donor and the recipient may have access to information allowing their identification.

###### Article 25

The provisions of this chapter are of public order.

### Title II: On nationality

Chapter I: General provisions

###### Article 26

Djiboutian nationality is acquired according to the provisions set out in this title subject to the application of treaties and other international commitments of the Republic of Djibouti.

###### Article 27

Djiboutian nationality by filiation is that which an individual possesses, from birth, by virtue of the origin of their parents of Djiboutian nationality.
Djiboutian nationality by acquisition is that which an individual obtains after birth, either by operation of law or by decision of the public authority.

###### Article 28

The acquisition of Djiboutian nationality is governed by the laws in force at the time of the act or fact to which the law attaches its effects.

#### Chapitre II : Nationalité djiboutienne par filiation Article 29

A person whose father and mother are Djiboutian is Djiboutian.

###### Article 30

A person born in the Republic of Djibouti or abroad whose father or mother is Djiboutian is also Djiboutian.

###### Article 31

An individual born in the Republic of Djibouti whose parents are unknown is also Djiboutian.
He shall be deemed never to have been Djiboutian if, before reaching the age of majority, his filiation is established with respect to a foreigner.

###### Article 32

An individual who is Djiboutian by virtue of the provisions of articles 29 to 31 is deemed to have been Djiboutian from birth, even if the existence of the conditions required by law for the attribution of Djiboutian nationality is established only subsequently. However, the establishment of Djiboutian status subsequent to birth does not affect the validity of acts previously acquired by third parties on the basis of the person's apparent nationality.

#### Chapitre III : Nationalité djiboutienne par acquisition Article 33

Djiboutian nationality may be acquired by decision of the public authority. It results from naturalization granted by decree and upon application by the interested party.

###### Article 34

Marriage does not, by operation of law, have any effect on the nationality of the foreign spouse.

###### Article 35

The acquisition of a foreign nationality does not result in the loss of Djiboutian status, unless the individual renounces his Djiboutian nationality by his own will.

###### Article 36

In case of naturalization, minor children born of the marriage are, by operation of law, Djiboutian.

###### Article 37

The adoption of a child does not, by operation of law, have any effect on the nationality of the adoptee, except in case of full adoption in which case the child is, by operation of law, Djiboutian.

###### Article 38

A commission is created to give a prior opinion on all applications for naturalization.

This commission, whose seat is at the Palace of Justice, comprises:
-	a magistrate, president;
-	a representative of the Ministry of the Interior, member;
-	a representative of the Ministry of Health, member;
-	the Director of Population, member;
-	the prefect of the place of residence of the person applying for naturalization, member.

The commission is appointed by the President of the Republic. It meets upon convocation by its president.

###### Article 39

Subject to the exceptions provided for in articles 36 and 40, naturalization may be granted only to a foreigner who can prove habitual residence in the Republic of Djibouti during the ten years preceding the filing of his application.

###### Article 40

The period provided for in article 39 is reduced to five years for individuals who have rendered or who can render, by their capacity and talent, important services to the Republic of Djibouti.

###### Article 41

No one may apply for naturalization if he has not reached the age of eighteen years.

###### Article 42

No one may be naturalized if he is not of good character and morals or if he has been subject to a conviction referred to in article 45 of this code. Convictions pronounced abroad may be taken into consideration.
A medical certificate must attest that he is in good health.

###### Article 43

No one may be naturalized if he does not demonstrate his assimilation into the Djiboutian community, in particular, by sufficient knowledge of one of the languages used in the Republic of Djibouti.

###### Article 44

No one may acquire Djiboutian nationality if he is subject to an expulsion order or residence assignment not withdrawn in the forms in which it was issued at the time of the fact or act likely to determine the acquisition.
The same applies to an individual who has been subject to a decree opposing the acquisition of Djiboutian nationality.

###### Article 45

No one may acquire Djiboutian nationality if he has been subject either to a conviction for an act qualified as a crime or offense against the security of the State, or to a conviction not erased by rehabilitation for an act qualified as a crime, or to a conviction not erased by rehabilitation to a sentence of more than six months' imprisonment for one of the offenses provided for in articles 131 to 150 of the penal code and the offenses of theft, fraud, breach of trust, receiving stolen goods, extortion and blackmail, forgery and use of forgery, provided for in articles 485 to 498, 509 to 510, 520 to 521, 533 to 540, 499 to 508 of the same code.

###### Article 46

An individual who has acquired nationality enjoys, from the day of this acquisition, all the rights attached to the status of Djiboutian.

#### Chapitre IV

Actes relatifs à l'acquisition par naturalisation de la nationalité djiboutienne Article 47
Any application for naturalization is filed and addressed to the Ministry of the Interior (Director of Population). A receipt for the filing of the file is issued. Every application must be registered. Mention of this registration is made on this file.

###### Article 48

The applicant produces civil status documents, documents and titles required of him, of a nature: 1° To establish that his application is admissible in the terms of the law;
2° To enable the commission responsible for giving a prior opinion on naturalization to assess whether the favor requested is justified, from the national point of view, in particular by reason of the filiation, the profession of the interested party and the duration of his stay in the Republic of Djibouti;
3° To establish that he has not been convicted in the Republic of Djibouti or in his country of origin; 4° To establish that the applicant is in good health by producing a medical certificate.

###### Article 49

In the event that the interested party is unable to produce the civil status documents necessary for the admissibility of the naturalization application, these documents may be replaced by certificates of notoriety issued by the judge designated in accordance with article 62.

###### Article 50

Any application for naturalization must be the subject of a police investigation. This investigation concerns the morality, conduct and loyalty of the applicant and the interest that the granting of naturalization would present from the national point of view.

###### Article 51

Within six months of the filing of the naturalization application, the Minister of the Interior must transmit to the president of the naturalization commission the complete file of the application as well as the results of the investigation and his reasoned opinion.

###### Article 52

The naturalization commission must be seized within two months following receipt of the file by the president of the commission.

###### Article 53

Decrees granting naturalization to Djiboutian nationality are published in the Official Journal.

###### Article 54

If the application does not give rise to naturalization or if the application is deemed inadmissible by the president of the commission after its opinion, the Minister of the Interior notifies the rejection of the application.
The notification pronouncing the rejection of the application does not have to be reasoned.

#### Chapitre V : Contentieux de la nationalité Article 55

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance has sole jurisdiction to hear disputes concerning nationality.

Questions of nationality are preliminary before any other administrative or judicial jurisdiction.

###### Article 56

Any person has the right to bring an action in court to have it determined that they have or do not have the status of Djiboutian.
The Prosecutor of the Republic and the Attorney General have the same right with regard to any person. The Public Prosecutor's Office is a necessary defendant in any declaratory action concerning nationality. It must be joined whenever a question of nationality is raised incidentally before a court having jurisdiction to hear it.

###### Article 57

The Prosecutor of the Republic and the Attorney General are required to act if so requested by a public administration or by a third party who has raised the exception of nationality before a court that has stayed proceedings pursuant to Article 62. The third party applicant must be joined.

###### Article 58

Judgments and rulings rendered in matters of Djiboutian nationality have effect even with regard to those who were neither parties nor represented therein.
However, any interested party may challenge them by third-party opposition on condition of joining the Prosecutor of the Republic or the Attorney General, depending on the level of the court to be seized.

#### Chapitre VI : Preuve de la nationalité devant les tribunaux judiciaires Article 59

The burden of proof in matters of Djiboutian nationality lies with the person whose nationality is in question.
However, this burden lies with the person who contests the status of Djiboutian of a third party who holds a certificate of nationality issued in accordance with Articles 62, 63 and 64 below.

###### Article 60

Where Djiboutian nationality is attributed or acquired otherwise than by naturalization, proof can only be made by establishing the existence of all the conditions required by law.

###### Article 61

Proof of the foreign status of an individual may be established by demonstrating that the person concerned does not fulfill any of the conditions required by law to have the status of Djiboutian.

#### Chapitre VII : Des certificats de nationalité

###### Article 62

The President of the Court of First Instance of Djibouti, or a judge specially designated for this purpose by him, alone has authority to issue a certificate of Djiboutian nationality to any person proving that they have this nationality.
Before ruling on any application for a certificate of nationality, the file must be the subject of a police investigation and be sent to the Directorate of Population for opinion.

###### Article 63

The certificate of nationality indicates, by reference to the articles of this code, the legal provisions by virtue of which the person concerned is Djiboutian as well as the documents that made it possible to establish it. It constitutes evidence until proof to the contrary.

###### Article 64
