When the judge rejects the application and refuses to issue a certificate of nationality, the person concerned may seize the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of Appeal who decides, after having conducted a new police investigation, whether or not to proceed with this issuance. The decision of refusal by the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of Appeal is subject to appeal before the Supreme Court.

### Titre III : Des actes de l'état civil

Chapitre Ier : Dispositions générales Article 65
Civil status records state the year, day and hour when they are received, the given names, surnames, professions and domiciles of all those named therein.

The dates and places of birth of the following persons are indicated in civil status records, when they are known:
1° Of the father and mother in birth and acknowledgment records; 2° Of the child in acknowledgment records;
3° Of the spouses in marriage records; 4° Of the deceased in death records.

When the date of birth of the person concerned is not known, the age of said persons shall be designated by their number of years, as shall be, in all cases, the age of the declarants. With regard to witnesses, only their status as adults shall be indicated.

###### Article 66

Civil status officers may not insert anything in the records they receive, either by note or by any statement, other than what must be declared by the appearing parties.

###### Article 67

In cases where the interested parties are not required to appear in person, they may be represented by an agent holding a special and authentic power of attorney.

###### Article 68

Witnesses produced for civil status records must be at least eighteen years of age, relatives or others, without distinction of sex; they are chosen by the interested persons.

###### Article 69

The civil status officer reads the records to the appearing parties, or to their agent holding a power of attorney, and to the witnesses; he invites them to take direct knowledge thereof before signing them.
Mention is made on the records of the completion of these formalities.

###### Article 70

These records are signed by the civil status officer, by the appearing parties and the witnesses; or mention shall be made of the reason preventing the appearing parties and the witnesses from signing.

###### Article 71

Civil status records are entered, in each commune, in one or more registers kept in duplicate.

###### Article 72

The registers are numbered and initialed on each page by the president of the court of first instance or by the judge he shall mandate for this purpose.

###### Article 73

The records are entered in the registers consecutively, without any blank spaces. Erasures and marginal notes are approved and signed in the same manner as the body of the record. Nothing may be written therein by abbreviation, and no date shall be written in figures.

###### Article 74

The registers are closed and finalized by the civil status officer at the end of each year; and, within one month, one of the duplicates shall be deposited in the archives of the commune, the other at the registry of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 75

Powers of attorney and other documents that must remain annexed to civil status records are deposited, after they have been initialed by the person who produced them and by the civil status officer, at the court registry, with the duplicate of the registers.

###### Article 76

Any person may obtain from the depositaries of civil status registers extracts from these registers. Extracts issued in conformity with the registers, and authenticated by the President of the Court of First Instance, or by the judge who shall replace him, constitute evidence until forgery is established.

###### Article 77

When registers have not existed, or they are lost, proof thereof shall be received both by documents and by witnesses; and, in these cases, marriages, births and deaths may be proved both by registers and papers emanating from deceased fathers and mothers, and by witnesses.

###### Article 78

Any civil status record of Djiboutians and foreigners, made in a foreign country, constitutes evidence if it is drawn up in the forms customary in said country.

###### Article 79

Any civil status record of Djiboutians in a foreign country is valid if it was received, in accordance with Djiboutian laws, by diplomatic agents or by consuls.
A duplicate of the civil status registers kept by these agents is sent at the end of each year to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which ensures their safekeeping and may issue extracts therefrom.

###### Article 80

In all cases where the notation of an act relating to civil status must be made in the margin of an act already registered, it is made ex officio.
The civil registrar who has drawn up or transcribed the act giving rise to the notation makes this notation, within three days, on the registers in his or her possession, and, if the duplicate of the register on which the notation must be made is at the registry, he or she sends a notice to the public prosecutor.

If the act in the margin of which this notation must be made was drawn up or transcribed in another commune, the notice is sent, within three days, to the civil registrar of that commune and the latter immediately notifies, if the duplicate of the register is at the registry, the public prosecutor.
If the act in the margin of which a notation must be made was drawn up or transcribed abroad, the civil registrar who drew up or transcribed the act giving rise to the notation notifies, within three days, the Minister of Foreign Affairs.

###### Article 81

Any contravention of the preceding articles, on the part of the officials named therein, shall be prosecuted before the Court of First Instance, and punished by a fine of 20,000 Djibouti francs (FD) to 200,000 FD.

###### Article 82

Every custodian of registers is civilly liable for alterations that occur therein, without prejudice to his or her recourse, if applicable, against the authors of said alterations.

###### Article 83

Any alteration, any forgery in civil status acts, any registration of these acts made on a loose sheet and otherwise than on the registers intended for that purpose, gives rise to the award of damages for the benefit of the parties who are victims thereof, without prejudice to the penalties provided for in the penal code.

###### Article 84

The public prosecutor is required to verify the state of the registers when they are deposited at the registry; he or she draws up a summary report of the verification, reports contraventions or offences committed by civil registrars, and applies for their conviction to fines.

###### Article 85

In all cases where the Court of First Instance has jurisdiction over acts relating to civil status, the interested parties may appeal against the judgment.

#### Chapitre II : Des actes de naissance Article 86

Declarations of birth are made within three days of delivery, to the civil registrar of the place.
When a birth has not been declared within the legal time limit, the civil registrar may only record it on his or her registers by virtue of a judgment rendered by the court of the place where the child was born, and a summary notation thereof is made in the margin at the date of birth. If the place of birth is unknown, the competent court is that of the domicile of the applicant.

In a foreign country, declarations to diplomatic agents or consuls are made within ten days of delivery. However, this time limit may be extended in certain consular districts by virtue of a decree of the President of the Republic which sets the extent and conditions of this extension.

###### Article 87

The birth of the child is declared by the father, or in the absence of the father, by doctors of medicine or surgery, midwives, health officers or other persons who have attended the delivery; and when the mother has given birth outside her domicile, by the person at whose home she gave birth.
The birth certificate is drawn up immediately.

###### Article 88

The birth certificate states the day, time and place of birth, the sex of the child and the given names assigned to him or her, the given names, surnames, ages, occupations and domiciles of the father and mother and, if applicable, those of the declarant. If the father and mother of the illegitimate child, or one of them, are not identified to the civil registrar, no mention is made of this in the registers.
If the act drawn up concerns an illegitimate child, the civil registrar gives notice thereof, within one month, to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or to the judge delegated for that purpose.
The judgment is rendered and published under the conditions provided for in articles 129 and 131 of this code.

###### Article 89

Any person who finds a newborn child is required to make a declaration thereof to the civil registrar of the place of discovery. If he or she does not consent to take charge of the child, he or she must hand over the child, together with the clothing and other effects found with it, to an approved centre for the reception of abandoned children. If on the other hand, he or she consents to take charge of the child, he or she must make a declaration thereof to the public prosecutor and initiate proceedings for placement or adoption.
A detailed report is drawn up which, in addition to the information provided for in article 65 of this code, states the date, time, place and circumstances of the discovery, the apparent age and sex of the child, any particularity that may contribute to his or her identification as well as the authority or person to whom he or she is entrusted. This report is registered on its date in the civil status registers.

Following and separately from this report, the civil registrar establishes an act in lieu of a birth certificate. In addition to the information provided for in article 65, this act states the sex of the child as well as the given names and surname assigned to him or her; it sets a date of birth that may correspond to his or her apparent age and designates as place of birth the commune where the child was discovered.
A similar act must be established, upon declaration by the child welfare services, for children placed under their guardianship and lacking a known birth certificate or for whom secrecy of birth has been requested.
Copies and extracts of the discovery report or the provisional birth certificate are issued under the conditions and according to the distinctions made in article 88 of this code.

If the child's birth certificate is found or if his or her birth is judicially declared, the discovery report and the provisional birth certificate are annulled at the request of the public prosecutor or the interested parties.

###### Article 90

The act of recognition of an illegitimate child is registered in the registers on its date; mention thereof is made in the margin of the birth certificate, if one exists, and notice thereof is given, within one month, to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 91

Every person is individualized by his or her given name followed by his or her traditional family name or patronymic name. The choice is made at the time of drafting the birth certificate of the first child, subsequent children being identified according to the same method. In the absence of an expressed choice, the traditional family name system is adopted.
The traditional family name is composed of the father's given name to which is added the paternal grandfather's given name.

The patronymic family name is the family name of the child's father, transmitted by filiation from generation to generation.

###### Article 92

Any person who demonstrates a legitimate interest may apply to change his or her given name. The addition or deletion of a given name may likewise be requested.
When the application concerns a minor, the petition is presented by his or her legal representative. If the child is over thirteen years of age, his or her personal consent is required.
The application is brought before the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance at the petition of the interested party or, in the case of a minor or an adult under guardianship, at the petition of his or her legal representative. The application is communicated for opinion to the public prosecutor.

The decision to change a given name is registered in the civil status register.

###### Article 93

Any person who establishes a legitimate interest may apply to change their patronymic name.

An application to change patronymic name may have the purpose of avoiding the extinction of the name borne by an ancestor or collateral relative of the applicant up to the fourth degree.
An application to change name may also have the purpose of abandoning the traditional family name in favour of a patronymic name, which shall be transmitted by filiation from generation to generation.

A change of name is authorised by decree.

###### Article 94

Any interested party may lodge an opposition before the Administrative Court to the decree ordering a change of name, within two months from its publication in the Official Gazette.
A decree ordering a change of name takes effect, if there has been no opposition, upon expiry of the period during which opposition is admissible or, otherwise, after rejection of the opposition.

###### Article 95

A change of name extends automatically to the children of the beneficiary when they are under thirteen years of age.

###### Article 96

Any change of name of a child over thirteen years of age requires their personal consent when such change does not result from the establishment or modification of a filiation link.
The establishment or modification of a filiation link does not, however, entail a change of family name of adult children except subject to their express consent.

###### Article 97

Any person who establishes a name registered in the civil status register of another State may apply to the civil status officer holding their birth certificate established in Djibouti for a change of name in order to bear the name acquired in that other State. When the person is a minor, the declaration is made jointly by both parents exercising parental authority or by the parent exercising parental authority alone, with their personal consent if they are over thirteen years of age.
The change of name is authorised by the civil status officer, who records it in the current birth register.
In case of difficulties, the civil status officer refers the matter to the public prosecutor, who may oppose the application. In such case, the interested party is notified.
Referred to under the same conditions, the public prosecutor of the place of birth may himself order the change of name.
A change of name acquired under the conditions set out in the first four paragraphs extends automatically to the children of the beneficiary when they are under thirteen years of age.

###### Article 98

Mention of decisions to change given names and name is recorded in the margin of the civil status records of the interested party and, where applicable, of those of their spouse and children.
Similarly, decisions to change given names and name lawfully acquired abroad are recorded in the margin of the civil status records of Djibouti, on instructions from the public prosecutor.

The provisions of Articles 130 and 131 are applicable to modifications of given names and name.

#### Chapter III. Marriage certificates Article 99

Before the celebration of marriage, the civil status officer makes a publication by means of a notice posted on the door of the town hall. This publication states the given names, names, professions, domiciles and residences of the future spouses, as well as the place where the marriage is to be celebrated.

The civil status officer may not proceed with the publication provided for in the above paragraph nor, in case of dispensation from publication, with the celebration of the marriage, until after the submission by each of the future spouses of a medical certificate dated less than two months previously, certifying, to the exclusion of any other indication, that the interested party has been examined with a view to marriage.

The civil status officer who does not comply with the requirements of the preceding paragraph shall be prosecuted before the criminal chamber of the Court of First Instance and punished by a fine of 20,000 FD to 200,000 FD.
The civil status officer receives the declaration of the future spouses as to whether they intend their union to be governed by the family code or by the provisions of this code.

###### Article 100

The notice provided for in Article 99 shall remain posted on the door of the town hall for ten days.

The marriage may not be celebrated before the tenth day from and not including the day of publication.

If the posting is interrupted before the expiry of this period, mention is made thereof on the notice which has ceased to be posted on the door of the town hall.

###### Article 101

If the marriage has not been celebrated within one year from the expiry of the publication period, it may no longer be celebrated except after a new publication made in the above form.

###### Article 102

Acts of opposition to marriage are signed on the original and on the copy by the opponents or by their agents holding a special and authentic power of attorney; they are served, together with a copy of the power of attorney, on the person or at the domicile of the parties, and on the civil status officer, who places his endorsement on the original.

###### Article 103

The civil status officer makes, without delay, a summary mention of oppositions in the marriage register; he also makes mention, in the margin of the registration of said oppositions, of judgments or acts of withdrawal of which an authenticated copy has been delivered to him.

###### Article 104

In case of opposition, the civil status officer may not celebrate the marriage before he has been provided with the withdrawal thereof, on pain of a fine of 100,000 FD, and damages.

###### Article 105

The authenticated copy of the birth certificate submitted by each of the future spouses to the civil status officer who is to celebrate their marriage conforms to the provisions of Article 88 of this code, with, where applicable, an indication of the status as spouses of his or her father and mother or, if the future spouse is a minor, an indication of the acknowledgement of which he or she has been the subject.
This certificate must not have been issued more than three months previously.

###### Article 106

A future spouse who is unable to obtain this certificate may substitute for it a certificate of notoriety issued by the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of the place of his or her birth or by that of his or her domicile.
The certificate of notoriety contains the declaration made by three witnesses of either sex, related or unrelated, of the given names, name, profession and domicile of the future spouse, and of those of his or her father and mother, if they are known; the place, and, as far as possible, the time of his or her birth, and the reasons preventing the production of the certificate thereof. The witnesses sign the certificate of notoriety with the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance; and if there are any who cannot or do not know how to sign, mention is made thereof.

###### Article 107

Neither the certificate of notoriety nor the refusal to issue it is subject to appeal.

###### Article 108

The authentic act of consent of fathers and mothers or grandfathers and grandmothers, or, in their absence, that of the family council, contains the given names, names, professions and domiciles of the future spouses and of all those who participated in the act, as well as their degree of kinship.
Except in the case provided for by Article 170 of the Civil Code, this act of consent is drawn up either by a notary or by the civil status officer of the domicile or residence of the ascendant and, abroad, by Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agents. When it is drawn up by a civil status officer, it need only be authenticated, subject to contrary international conventions, when it is to be produced before foreign authorities.

###### Article 109

The marriage is celebrated in the commune where one of the two spouses has his or her domicile or residence established by at least one month of continuous habitation on the date of the publication provided for by law.

###### Article 110

On the day designated by the parties, after the publication period, the civil registrar, at the town hall, in the presence of at least two witnesses or at most four, whether or not related to the parties, reads to the future spouses articles 220 (paragraph 1), 221, 222 (paragraph 1) and 223 (paragraph 1) of this code.
However, in case of serious impediment, the public prosecutor of the place of marriage may require the civil registrar to go to the domicile or residence of one of the parties to celebrate the marriage. In case of imminent danger of death of one of the future spouses, the civil registrar may go there before any requisition or authorization from the public prosecutor, to whom he must then, as soon as possible, report the necessity of this celebration outside the town hall.

Mention thereof shall be made in the marriage certificate.
The civil registrar questions the future spouses, and, if they are minors, their ascendants present at the celebration and authorizing the marriage, to declare whether a marriage contract has been made and, if so, the date of that contract, as well as the name and place of residence of the notary who received it.

If the documents produced by one of the future spouses do not agree with each other as to the first names or as to the spelling of the surnames, he questions the person concerned, and, if he is a minor, his closest ascendants present at the celebration, to declare that the lack of agreement results from an omission or an error.

He receives from each party, one after the other, the declaration that they wish to take each other as husband and wife; he pronounces, in the name of the law, that they are united by marriage and he draws up the certificate immediately.

###### Article 111

The marriage certificate states:

1° The first names, surnames, professions, ages, dates and places of birth, domiciles and residences of the spouses; 2° The first names, surnames, professions and domiciles of the fathers and mothers;
3° The consent of the fathers and mothers, grandfathers or grandmothers and that of the family council, in cases where they are required;

4° The first names and surname of the previous spouse of each of the spouses;

5° The declaration of the contracting parties to take each other as spouses, and the pronouncement of their union by the civil registrar;
6° The first names, surnames professions, domiciles of the witnesses and their status as adults;

7° The declaration, made that a marriage contract has or has not been made and, as far as possible, the date of the contract, if it exists, as well as the name and place of residence of the notary who received it;

8° The option provided for in article 99 of this code.

In the margin of the birth certificate of each spouse, mention shall be made of the celebration of the marriage and the name of the spouse.

#### Chapitre IV. Des actes de décès

###### Article 112

No burial may take place without an authorization on plain paper and without charge from the civil registrar, or from a doctor, who may only issue it after going to the deceased person, to ascertain the death.
If the circumstances reveal a doubt about the identity of the person or the causes of death, the doctor shall proceed as provided in article 116 of this code.

###### Article 113

The death certificate is drawn up by the civil registrar of the municipality where the death occurred, on the declaration of a relative of the deceased or on that of a person possessing the most accurate and complete information possible on his civil status.

###### Article 114

The death certificate states:

1° The day, time and place of death;

2° The first names, surname, date and place of birth, profession and domicile of the deceased person; 3° The first names, surnames professions and domiciles of his father and mother;
4° The first names and surname of the other spouse, if the deceased person was married, widowed or divorced;
5° The first names, surname, age, profession and domicile of the declarant and, if applicable, his degree of relationship with the deceased person.

All of the above, as far as can be known.
Mention of the death is made in the margin of the birth certificate of the deceased person.

###### Article 115

When a death has occurred elsewhere than in the municipality where the deceased was domiciled, the civil registrar who drew up the death certificate sends, as soon as possible, to the civil registrar of the last domicile of the deceased a copy of this certificate, which is immediately transcribed in the registers.
In case of death in hospitals or other public establishments, the directors of these hospitals or establishments must give notice thereof, within ten hours, to the civil registrar or to the person performing his functions.

The latter goes there to ascertain the death and draws up the certificate, in accordance with the preceding article, on the declarations that have been made to him and on the information he has obtained.

A register is kept in said hospitals and establishments on which these declarations and information are recorded.

###### Article 116

When there are signs or indications of violent death, or other circumstances that give reason to suspect it, burial may not take place until a police officer, assisted by a doctor of medicine, has drawn up a report on the state of the body and the circumstances relating thereto, as well as the information he has been able to gather on the first names, surname, age, profession, place of birth and domicile of the deceased person.

###### Article 117

The police officer is required to transmit immediately to the civil registrar of the place where the person died, all the information stated in his report, according to which the death certificate is drawn up.
The civil registrar sends a copy thereof to that of the domicile of the deceased person, if it is known: this copy is recorded in the registers.

###### Article 118

In case of death in a prison or detention facility, notice thereof is given immediately, by the head of the establishment, to the civil registrar, who goes there as stated in article 115, and draws up the death certificate.

###### Article 119

When the body of a deceased person is found and that person can be identified, a death certificate must be drawn up by the civil registrar of the presumed place of death, regardless of the time elapsed between the death and the discovery of the body.
If the deceased cannot be identified, the death certificate must include his most complete description; in case of subsequent identification, the certificate is corrected under the conditions provided for in article 129 of this code.

###### Article 120

May be judicially declared, at the request of the public prosecutor or interested parties, the death of any Djiboutian who disappeared in Djibouti or outside the country, in circumstances likely to endanger his life, when his body could not be found.
May, under the same conditions, be judicially declared the death of any foreigner who disappeared either on a territory under the authority of Djibouti, or abroad if he had his domicile or habitual residence in Djibouti.
The procedure for judicial declaration of death is also applicable when the death is certain but the body could not be found.

###### Article 121

The application is submitted to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

If several persons disappeared during the same event, a collective application may be submitted to him.

###### Article 122

When it does not originate from the public prosecutor, the application is transmitted through him to the court. The case is heard and judged in chambers. Legal representation is not mandatory and all procedural acts, as well as certified copies and extracts of said acts, are exempt from stamp duty and registered free of charge.
If the court considers that the death is not sufficiently established, it may order any additional investigative measure and in particular require an administrative inquiry into the circumstances of the disappearance.
If the death is declared, its date must be fixed taking into account the presumptions drawn from the circumstances of the case and, failing that, on the day of the disappearance. This date must never be indeterminate.

###### Article 123

The operative part of the declaratory judgment of death is transcribed in the civil status registers of the actual or presumed place of death and, where applicable, in those of the place of the deceased's last domicile.

Mention of the transcription is made in the margin of the registers at the date of death. In the case of a collective judgment, individual extracts of the operative part are transmitted to the civil status officers of the last domicile of each of the missing persons, for transcription.
Declaratory judgments of death serve as death certificates and are enforceable against third parties, who may only obtain their rectification in accordance with Article 129 of this code.

###### Article 124

If the person whose death has been judicially declared reappears after the declaratory judgment, the public prosecutor or any interested party may seek, in the forms provided for in Articles 121 and following, the annulment of the judgment.

He shall recover his property in the state in which it is found, as well as the price of property that has been alienated and property acquired through the use of capital or income accrued for his benefit.
The matrimonial regime which the declaratory judgment had terminated shall resume. If a liquidation of the spouses' rights that has become final had been carried out, the restoration of the matrimonial regime shall not affect rights acquired, on the basis of the apparent situation, by persons other than the spouse, heirs, legatees or any holders of rights whose acquisition was subject to the death of the missing person.
Mention of the annulment of the declaratory judgment shall be made in the margin of its transcription.

#### Chapitre V

Civil status acts concerning military personnel and sailors in certain special cases Article 125
Civil status acts concerning military personnel and sailors of the State are drawn up as stated in the preceding chapters.
However, outside the territory of the Republic of Djibouti and in case of war, peacekeeping and pacification operations or stationing of Djiboutian troops in foreign territory, these acts may also be received by military civil status officers designated by order of the Minister of Defence.

On the territory of the Republic of Djibouti, the civil status officers referred to above may receive acts concerning military personnel and non-military personnel, in parts of the territory where, as a result of mobilization or siege, the municipal civil status service is no longer regularly provided.

Birth declarations in the armed forces are made within ten days following childbirth.
Death certificates may be drawn up in the armed forces by way of derogation from Article 112 above, even though the civil status officer was unable to go to the deceased person, and, by way of derogation from Article 113, they may only be drawn up there on the attestation of two declarants.

###### Article 126

Marriage publications of military personnel and employees attached to the armed forces are made at the place of their last domicile: they are also posted, twenty-five days before the celebration of the marriage, in the daily orders of the army or army corps, for officers without troops, and for employees who are part of it.

###### Article 127

In the cases provided for in paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 125, civil status acts are drawn up in a special register, the maintenance and preservation of which are regulated by order of the Minister of Defence.

When a marriage is celebrated in one of the cases provided for in paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 125, the publications are made, to the extent that circumstances permit, at the place of the last domicile of the future spouse; they are also ensured, in the unit to which the person concerned belongs, under the conditions set by order of the Minister of Defence.

###### Article 128

Death certificates received by the military authority, in all cases provided for in Article 125 above, or by the civil authority for members of the armed forces, civilians participating in their action, on official duty, or persons employed with the armed forces, may be subject to administrative rectification under conditions set by decree, in the periods and on the territories where the military authority is authorized, by said Article 125, to possibly receive these acts.

#### Chapitre VI. De la rectification des actes de l'état civil Article 129

The rectification of civil status acts is ordered by the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.
The rectification of acts drawn up or transcribed by diplomatic agents and consuls is ordered by the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of Djibouti. This magistrate may also hear applications for rectification of acts of which one copy is deposited in the archives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The rectification of declaratory or supplementary judgments of civil status acts is ordered by the court that rendered the judgment.

The president or the court territorially competent to order the rectification of an act or judgment is also competent to prescribe the rectification of all acts, even drawn up or transcribed outside its jurisdiction, which reproduce the error or contain the original omission.
The application for rectification may be submitted by any interested person or by the public prosecutor; the latter is required to act ex officio when the error or omission concerns an essential indication of the act or the decision that serves in its place. When the application does not originate from the public prosecutor, it must be communicated to him for an opinion.

The public prosecutor may proceed with the administrative rectification of purely material errors and omissions in civil status acts; for this purpose, he gives useful instructions directly to the custodians of the registers.

###### Article 130

Any judicial or administrative rectification of an act or judgment relating to civil status is enforceable against all.

###### Article 131

The operative part of the order, judgment or ruling ordering rectification is transmitted immediately by the public prosecutor to the civil status officer or to the custodian of the registers of the place where the amended act is recorded; mention of this operative part is immediately made in the margin of said act.
A certified copy of the act may only be issued with the ordered rectifications, on pain of a fine of 20,000 FD to 200,000 FD pronounced by the Court of First Instance and all damages against the custodian of the registers.

### Titre IV : Du domicile

###### Article 132

The domicile of every Djiboutian, as regards the exercise of his civil rights, is at the place where he has his principal establishment.
The place of exercise of civil rights of a person without stable domicile is that where he has elected domicile. This election of domicile must be either with a communal centre, or with an organization approved for this purpose, or with a notary or a lawyer.

###### Article 133

A change of domicile shall be effected by actual residence in another place, together with the intention to establish one's principal establishment there.

###### Article 134

Proof of intention shall result from an express declaration made both to the town hall of the place being left and to that of the place to which domicile has been transferred.
In the absence of an express declaration, proof of intention shall depend on the circumstances.

###### Article 135

Husband and wife may have separate domiciles without thereby affecting the rules relating to community of life.
Any notification made to a spouse, even if separated from bed and board, in matters of status and capacity of persons, must also be addressed to his or her spouse, on pain of nullity.

###### Article 136

The separate residence of spouses during divorce or legal separation proceedings automatically results in separate domicile.

###### Article 137

An unemancipated minor is domiciled with his or her father and mother.

If the father and mother have separate domiciles, he or she is domiciled with the parent with whom he or she resides.

###### Article 138

An adult under guardianship is domiciled with his or her guardian.

###### Article 139

Adults who habitually serve or work for others shall have the same domicile as the person they serve or for whom they work, when they reside with that person in the same house.

###### Article 140

The place where a succession opens shall be determined by the domicile of the deceased.

###### Article 141

When a deed contains, on the part of the parties or one of them, an election of domicile for the performance of that same deed in a place other than that of the actual domicile, notifications, demands and proceedings relating to that deed may be made at the agreed domicile and before the judge of that domicile.

### Titre V: Of absent persons

#### Chapitre I. Of the presumption of absence Article 142

When a person has ceased to appear at the place of his or her domicile or residence without any news having been received, the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or the judge delegated by him or her for that purpose may, at the request of interested parties or the public prosecutor, find that there is a presumption of absence.

###### Article 143

The judge may designate one or more relatives or relatives by marriage, or, where appropriate, any other persons to represent the person presumed absent in the exercise of his or her rights or in any act in which he or she would have an interest, as well as to administer all or part of his or her property; the representation of the presumed absentee and the administration of his or her property are then subject to the rules applicable to the guardianship of adults without a family council, and further subject to the following modifications.

###### Article 144

Without prejudice to the special jurisdiction attributed to other courts for the same purposes, the judge determines, where appropriate, according to the value of the property, the sums that should be allocated annually to the maintenance of the family or to the charges of marriage. He or she determines how provision is made for the establishment of the children. He or she also specifies how administrative expenses are settled as well as, where applicable, the remuneration that may be granted to the person responsible for representing the presumed absentee and administering his or her property.

###### Article 145

The judge may, at any time and even of his or her own motion, terminate the mission of the person so designated; he or she may also proceed with his or her replacement.

###### Article 146

If the presumed absentee is called to a partition, the latter may be made amicably. In that case, the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance authorizes the partition, even partial, and designates, if necessary, a notary to proceed with it, in the presence of the representative of the presumed absentee or his or her replacement designated in accordance with Article 143, if the initial representative is himself or herself interested in the partition. The liquidation statement is subject to the approval of the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance. The partition may also be made in court. Any other partition is considered provisional.

###### Article 147

The public prosecutor is specially charged with protecting the interests of presumed absentees. He or she is heard on all applications concerning them; he or she may require of his or her own motion the application or modification of the measures provided for in this title.

###### Article 148

If a presumed absentee reappears or gives news, the measures taken for his or her representation and the administration of his or her property are terminated by the judge at his or her request; he or she then recovers the property managed or acquired on his or her behalf during the period of absence.

###### Article 149

Rights acquired without fraud, on the basis of the presumption of absence, are not called into question when the death of the absentee comes to be established or judicially declared, whatever the date adopted for the death.

###### Article 150

The foregoing provisions relating to the representation of presumed absentees and the administration of their property are also applicable to persons who, as a result of distance, find themselves despite themselves unable to express their will.

###### Article 151

These same provisions are not applicable to presumed absentees or to the persons mentioned in Article 120 when they have left a sufficient power of attorney for the purpose of representing them and administering their property.
The same applies if the spouse can sufficiently provide for the interests at stake through the application of the matrimonial regime, and in particular through the effect of a decision obtained pursuant to Articles 225 and 227, and 1671 and 1674.

#### Chapitre II: Of the declaration of absence Article 152

When ten years have elapsed since the judgment that found the presumption of absence, either according to the procedures set by Article 142, or on the occasion of one of the judicial proceedings provided for by Articles 225 and 227, and 1671 and 1674, the absence may be declared by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance at the request of any interested party or the public prosecutor. The same shall apply when, in the absence of such a finding, the person has ceased to appear at the place of his or her domicile or residence, without any news having been received for more than twenty years.

###### Article 153

Extracts from the application for declaration of absence, after having been endorsed by the public prosecutor, are published in a newspaper authorized to receive legal publications and in a newspaper of the country of domicile or last residence of the person who has remained without giving news when the domicile or last residence is located outside the territory of the Republic of Djibouti. The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, seized of the application, may further order any other publicity measure in any place it deems useful.
These publicity measures are ensured by the party presenting the application.

###### Article 154

As soon as the extracts have been published, the application is transmitted, through the intermediary of the public prosecutor, to the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, which rules on the basis of the documents and papers produced and having regard to the conditions of the disappearance, as well as to the circumstances that may explain the lack of news. The Civil Chamber may order any additional investigative measure and prescribe, if necessary, that an inquiry be conducted adversarially in any place it deems useful.

###### Article 155

The application initiating proceedings may be presented from the year preceding the expiration of the time limits provided for in Article 152. The judgment declaring absence is rendered at least one year after the publication of the extracts from that application. It finds that the person presumed absent has not reappeared during the time limits referred to in Article 152.

###### Article 156

The petition for a declaration of absence is deemed to have lapsed when the absentee reappears or when the date of his death is established, prior to the pronouncement of the judgment.

###### Article 157

When the declaratory judgment of absence is rendered, extracts thereof are published according to the procedures provided for in Article 153, within the time limit set by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance. The decision is deemed to have lapsed if it has not been published within that time limit.
When the judgment has become res judicata, its operative part is transcribed at the request of the Public Prosecutor in the death registers of the place of domicile of the absentee or of his last residence. Mention of this transcription is made in the margin of the registers at the date of the judgment declaring the absence; it is also made in the margin of the birth certificate of the person declared absent. The transcription makes the judgment enforceable against third parties who may only obtain its rectification or annulment, in accordance with Article 129.

###### Article 158

The declaratory judgment of absence produces, from the transcription, all the effects that the established death of the absentee would have had. The measures taken for the administration of the property of the absentee, in accordance with Chapter I of this title, come to an end, unless otherwise decided by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance. The spouse of the absentee may contract a new marriage.

###### Article 159

If the absentee reappears or if his existence is proven subsequent to the declaratory judgment of absence, the annulment of that judgment may be pursued, at the request of the Public Prosecutor or of any interested party.
However, if the interested party intends to be represented, he may only be represented by a lawyer duly registered with the bar.

The operative part of the annulment judgment is published without delay, according to the procedures set by Article 153.

Mention of this decision is made, upon its publication, in the margin of the declaratory judgment of absence and on any register that refers to it.

###### Article 160

The absentee whose existence is judicially established recovers his property and that which he should have received during his absence in the state in which it is found, the price of that which has been alienated or the property acquired in exchange for capital or revenues accrued to his benefit.

###### Article 161

Any interested party who has fraudulently provoked a declaration of absence shall be required to restore to the absentee whose existence is judicially established the revenues from the property of which he has had enjoyment and to pay him legal interest thereon from the day of receipt, without prejudice, where applicable, to additional damages.

If the fraud is attributable to the spouse of the person declared absent, the latter shall be entitled to challenge the liquidation of the matrimonial regime which the declaratory judgment of absence has terminated.

###### Article 162

If the missing person reappears while his wife has not yet remarried, she becomes his wife again by operation of law. Whereas if she has remarried, she remains the wife of the second husband.

### Title VI: On marriage

#### Chapter I

On the qualities and conditions required to be able to contract marriage Article 163
A man and a woman may not contract marriage before eighteen years of age.

Nevertheless, the Public Prosecutor of the place of celebration of the marriage may grant age dispensations for serious reasons.
The civil registrar receives the declaration of the future spouses if they intend their union to be governed by the provisions of this code, failing which it shall be governed by the family code.

###### Article 164

There is no marriage when there is no consent.

###### Article 165

A second marriage may not be contracted before the dissolution of the first.

###### Article 166

Minors may not contract marriage without the consent of their father and mother. In case of disagreement between the father and the mother, this division constitutes consent.
In case of refusal by both parents and persistence of the matrimonial intention of the two minors, the marriage is authorized by the judge.

###### Article 167

If one of the two parents is dead or if he is unable to express his will, the consent of the other suffices.
It is not necessary to produce the death certificate of the father or mother of one of the future spouses when the spouse or the father and mother of the deceased attest to this death under oath.
If the current residence of the father or mother is unknown, and if he has not given news of himself for one year, the celebration of the marriage may proceed if the child and the one of his father and mother who gives his consent makes a declaration to that effect under oath.

All of this shall be mentioned on the marriage certificate.

False oath taken in the cases provided for in this article and in the following articles of this chapter shall be punished by the penalties prescribed by Article 266 of the Criminal Code.

###### Article 168

If the father and mother are dead or if they are both unable to express their will, the grandfathers and grandmothers replace them; if there is disagreement between the grandfather and grandmother of the same line or if there is disagreement between the two lines, this division constitutes consent.

If the current residence of the father and mother is unknown and if they have not given news of themselves for one year, the celebration of the marriage may proceed if the grandfathers and grandmothers as well as the child himself make a declaration to that effect under oath. The same applies if, one or more grandfathers or grandmothers giving their consent to the marriage, the current residence of the other grandfathers or grandmothers is unknown and if they have not given news of themselves for one year.

###### Article 169

The provisions contained in Articles 166 and 167 are applicable to legally recognized natural children.
If one of the two parents is dead or if he is unable to express his will, the consent of the other suffices. The provisions of paragraphs 3, 4 and 5 of Article 167 are applicable to the minor natural child.

###### Article 170

If there is no father, mother, grandfathers or grandmothers, or if they are all unable to express their will, minors under eighteen years of age may not contract marriage without the consent of the family council.
The natural child who has not been recognized, and the one who, after having been recognized, has lost his father and mother or whose father and mother cannot express their will, may not, before the age of eighteen years, marry without having obtained the consent of the family council.

###### Article 171

If the current residence of those ascendants of the minor under eighteen years of age whose death is not established is unknown and if these ascendants have not given news of themselves for one year, the minor shall make a declaration to that effect under oath before the President of the Court of First Instance of his residence, assisted by his clerk, in his chambers, and this judge shall record it.
The President of the Court of First Instance shall notify this oath to the family council, which shall rule on the application for authorization to marry. However, the minor may take the oath directly in the presence of the members of the family council.

###### Article 172

Civil registrars who have proceeded with the celebration of marriages contracted by sons or daughters who have not reached the age of eighteen years without the consent of the fathers and mothers, that of the grandfathers or grandmothers and that of the family council, in the case where it is required, being stated in the marriage certificate, shall, at the instance of the interested parties or of the Public Prosecutor, be sentenced to a fine of 100,000 FD.

###### Article 173

In the direct line, marriage is prohibited between all legitimate or natural ascendants and descendants, and relatives by marriage in the same line.

###### Article 174

In the collateral line, marriage is prohibited between legitimate or natural brother and sister.

###### Article 175

Marriage is further prohibited between uncle and niece, aunt and nephew, whether the relationship is legitimate or natural.

###### Article 176

Nevertheless, the President of the Republic may, for serious reasons, lift the prohibitions set out:
-	by Article 173 on marriages between relatives by marriage in the direct line when the person who created the relationship has died;
-	by Article 175 on marriages between uncle and niece, aunt and nephew.

#### Chapitre II. Des formalités relatives à la célébration du mariage Article 177

The marriage shall be celebrated publicly before the civil registrar of the municipality where one of the spouses has his or her domicile or residence on the date of the publication provided for by Article 99 and, in case of dispensation from publication, on the date of the dispensation provided for in Article 178 below.

The man and the woman may attend their marriage in person or by proxy. The person who consents to the marriage of a minor may also do so by power of attorney. The guardian may also exercise his rights by power of attorney. The power of attorney must, on pain of nullity, be established by authentic instrument and expressly contain the designation of the two future spouses.

###### Article 178

The publication ordered in Article 99 shall be made at the town hall of the place of marriage and at that of the place where each of the future spouses has his or her domicile or, in the absence of domicile, his or her residence.

###### Article 179

The Public Prosecutor may dispense, for serious reasons, with the publication and any time period or with the posting of the publication only.
He may also in exceptional cases dispense the future spouses or only one of them from submitting the medical certificate required by the second paragraph of Article 99.

The medical certificate is not required from either of the future spouses in the case of imminent danger of death of one of them, provided for in the second paragraph of Article 110 of this code.

###### Article 180

A marriage contracted in a foreign country between Djiboutians and between a Djiboutian and a foreigner shall be valid if it was contracted in the forms customary in that country, provided that it was preceded by the publication prescribed by Article 99, under the heading Civil Status Records, and that the Djiboutian has not contravened the provisions contained in the preceding chapter of this code.
The same shall apply to a marriage contracted in a foreign country between a Djiboutian and a foreign woman, if it was celebrated by diplomatic agents or by consuls of Djibouti, in accordance with Djiboutian laws.

A marriage contracted in accordance with the two preceding paragraphs is enforceable against third parties in Djibouti only if the marriage certificate has been transcribed in the Djiboutian civil status registers. In the absence of transcription, the marriage of a Djiboutian, validly celebrated by a foreign authority, produces its civil effects in Djibouti with respect to the spouses and children. The request for transcription is made to the consular or diplomatic authority having jurisdiction over the place of celebration of the marriage.

###### Article 181

The President of the Republic may, for serious reasons, authorize the celebration of the marriage if one of the future spouses died after the completion of official formalities unequivocally marking his or her consent.
In this case, the effects of the marriage go back to the date of the day preceding that of the death of the spouse.

However, this marriage does not entail any right of intestate succession in favor of the surviving spouse and no matrimonial regime is deemed to have existed between the spouses.

#### Chapitre III. Des oppositions au mariage Article 182

The right to form an opposition to the celebration of the marriage belongs to the person bound by marriage to one of the two contracting parties.

###### Article 183

The father, the mother, and, in the absence of father and mother, the grandfathers and grandmothers may form an opposition to the marriage of their children and descendants, even if of age.
After judicial removal of an opposition to marriage formed by an ascendant, no new opposition formed by an ascendant is admissible nor may delay the celebration.

###### Article 184

In the absence of any ascendant, the brother or sister, uncle or aunt, first cousin, of age, may not form any opposition except in the following two cases:
1° When the consent of the family council required by application, as the case may be, of Articles 170 or 171 has not been obtained;

2° When the opposition is based on the state of insanity of the future spouse: this opposition, of which the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may pronounce pure and simple removal, shall never be received except on condition that the opponent initiate guardianship of adults, and have a decision made thereon within the time period to be fixed by the judgment.

###### Article 185

In the two cases provided for by the preceding article, the guardian or curator may, during the duration of the guardianship or curatorship, form an opposition only insofar as he has been authorized to do so by a family council, which he may convene.

###### Article 186

Every act of opposition shall state the capacity that gives the opponent the right to form it and shall be signed, on the original and on the copy, by the latter or his proxy holding a special and authentic power of attorney; it shall contain election of domicile in the place where the marriage is to be celebrated; it must also contain the grounds for the opposition and reproduce the text of the law on which the opposition is based; all on pain of nullity and temporary suspension of the bailiff who signed the act containing the opposition. The suspension is pronounced following the procedure provided for by Order No. 86-069/PR/J of 11 September 1986 relating to the discipline of bailiffs, auctioneers and notaries. The bailiff may, however, only be responsible for the formal regularity of the act and does not have to judge the capacity claimed by the opponent or the accuracy of the facts alleged by him. The bailiff may, without incurring liability, refuse his services if the opponent is not one of the persons listed by law, or if the opposition is not based on a cause provided for by law.
After one full year, the act of opposition ceases to have effect. It may be renewed, except in the case referred to in the second paragraph of Article 183 above.

###### Article 187

The Civil Chamber shall rule within ten days on the application for removal filed by the future spouses, even if minors.

###### Article 188

The decision of the Civil Chamber may be referred to the Court of Appeal, which rules within the same period of ten days.

###### Article 189

If the opposition is rejected, the opponents, other than ascendants however, may be ordered to pay damages.
Default judgments and rulings rejecting oppositions to marriage are not subject to opposition.

#### Chapitre IV. Des demandes en nullité de mariage Article 190

A marriage that was contracted without the free consent of both spouses, or of one of them, may be challenged only by the spouses, or by the one of the two whose consent was not free, or by the Public Prosecutor.

The exercise of coercion on the spouses or one of them, including reverential fear towards an ascendant, constitutes a ground for nullity of the marriage.
If there has been an error as to the person, or as to essential qualities of the person, the other spouse may request the nullity of the marriage.

###### Article 191

In the case of the preceding article, the application for nullity is no longer admissible after a period of two years from the marriage, or from the time when the spouse acquired full freedom or when the error was recognized by him.

###### Article 192

A marriage contracted without the consent of the father and mother, ascendants, or the family council, in cases where such consent was necessary, may only be challenged by those whose consent was required, or by the one of the two spouses who needed such consent.

###### Article 193

The action for nullity may no longer be brought either by the spouses or by the relatives whose consent was required, whenever the marriage has been approved expressly or tacitly by those whose consent was necessary, or when two years have elapsed without objection on their part, since they became aware of the marriage. The action for nullity may not be brought by the spouse either, when two years have elapsed without objection on his part, since he reached the competent age to consent by himself to the marriage.

###### Article 194

Any marriage contracted in contravention of the provisions contained in articles 163, 164, 165, 173, 174 and 175 may be challenged, within a period of thirty years from its celebration, either by the spouses themselves, or by all those who have an interest, or by the public prosecutor.
Nevertheless, a marriage contracted by spouses who had not yet reached the required age, or one of whom had not reached that age, may no longer be challenged:

1° when six months have elapsed since that spouse or the spouses reached the competent age;

2° when the woman who had not reached that age conceived before the expiry of six months.

The father, mother, ascendants and family who consented to the contracted marriage are not entitled to request its nullity.

###### Article 195

In all cases where, in accordance with article 194, the action for nullity may be brought by all those who have an interest therein, it may not be brought by collateral relatives, or by children born of another marriage, during the lifetime of both spouses, but only when they have a vested and current interest.

###### Article 196

The spouse to whose prejudice a second marriage was contracted may request its nullity, even during the lifetime of the spouse who was bound to him.

###### Article 197

If the new spouses oppose the nullity of the first marriage, the validity or nullity of that marriage must be determined first.

###### Article 198

The public prosecutor, in all cases to which article 194 applies, may and must request the nullity of the marriage, during the lifetime of both spouses, and have them condemned to separate.

###### Article 199

A marriage that was celebrated in fraud of the law may be annulled at the request of the spouse in good faith or of the public prosecutor, made within one year of the marriage.

###### Article 200

Any marriage that was not contracted publicly, and that was not celebrated before the competent public officer, may be challenged, within a period of thirty years from its celebration, by the spouses themselves, by the father and mother, by the ascendants, and by all those who have a vested and current interest therein, as well as by the public prosecutor.
The period is reduced to fifteen years when there is possession of status as spouses during that period and a certificate of celebration registered in the civil status register is produced.

###### Article 201

If the marriage was not preceded by the required publication or if the dispensations permitted by law were not obtained or if the intervals prescribed between publications and celebrations were not observed, the public officer and the contracting parties, or those under whose authority they acted, are liable to a fine of 20,000 FD to 50,000 FD.

###### Article 202

The penalties pronounced by the preceding article shall be incurred by the persons designated therein, for any contravention of the rules prescribed by article 177, even if such contraventions are not deemed sufficient to result in the nullity of the marriage being pronounced.

###### Article 203

No one may claim the title of spouse and the civil effects of marriage, if he does not produce a certificate of celebration registered in the civil status register, except in the cases provided for by article 77, under the title Of civil status records.

###### Article 204

Possession of status cannot dispense the alleged spouses who invoke it respectively, from producing the certificate of celebration of the marriage before the civil status officer.

On the other hand, subsequent publicity cures prior or concomitant clandestinity to the marriage when possession of status as spouses exists.

###### Article 205

When there is possession of status, and the certificate of celebration of the marriage before the civil status officer is produced, the spouses are respectively not entitled to request the nullity of that certificate.

###### Article 206

If nevertheless, in the case of articles 203 and 204, there exist children born of two individuals who lived publicly as husband and wife, and who are both deceased, the legitimacy of the children cannot be contested on the sole pretext of failure to produce the certificate of celebration, whenever such legitimacy is proved by possession of status that is not contradicted by the birth certificate.

###### Article 207

When proof of a lawful celebration of the marriage is obtained by the result of criminal proceedings, the registration of the judgment in the civil status registers ensures to the marriage, from the day of its celebration, all civil effects, both with regard to the spouses and with regard to the children born of that marriage.

###### Article 208

If the spouses or one of them died without having discovered the fraud, the criminal action may be brought by all those who have an interest in having the marriage declared valid, and by the public prosecutor.
The court ruling on the criminal matter must, in order to enter into condemnation, recognize that the incriminated act resulted in suppressing the proof of a marriage actually celebrated.

###### Article 209

If the public officer is deceased at the time of the discovery of the fraud, the action shall be brought in civil court against his heirs by the public prosecutor, in the presence of the interested parties and upon their denunciation.

###### Article 210

A marriage that has been declared null nevertheless produces its effects with regard to the spouses, when it was contracted in good faith.
If good faith exists only on the part of one of the spouses, the marriage produces its effects only in favor of that spouse.

###### Article 211

It also produces its effects with regard to the children, even if neither of the spouses was in good faith.
The exercise of parental authority is determined as in matters of divorce.

#### Chapitre V. Des obligations qui naissent du mariage Article 212

The spouses contract together, by the mere fact of marriage, the obligation to feed, maintain and educate their children.

###### Article 213

Children owe maintenance to their father and mother or other ascendants who are in need.

###### Article 214

Sons-in-law and daughters-in-law likewise owe, and in the same circumstances, maintenance to their father-in-law and mother-in-law, but this obligation ceases when the one of the spouses who produced the affinity and the children born of his union with the other spouse are deceased.

###### Article 215

The obligations resulting from these provisions are reciprocal.

Nevertheless, when the creditor has himself seriously failed in his obligations towards the debtor, the judge may discharge the latter from all or part of the maintenance debt.

###### Article 216

Alimony is granted only in proportion to the need of the person claiming it, and to the fortune of the person who owes it.
The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may, even of its own motion, and according to the circumstances of the case, attach to the alimony a variation clause permitted by the laws in force.

###### Article 217

When the person who provides or the person who receives alimony is placed in a state such that the one can no longer give it or that the other no longer needs it in whole or in part, discharge or reduction may be requested.

###### Article 218

If the person who must provide alimony proves that he cannot pay the alimony, the Civil Chamber may, with full knowledge of the facts, order that he shall receive into his dwelling, that he shall feed and maintain the person to whom he owes alimony.

###### Article 219

The Civil Chamber shall also decide whether the father or mother who offers to receive, feed and maintain in his dwelling, the child to whom he owes alimony, shall in that case be exempted from paying the alimony.

#### Chapitre VI. Des devoirs et des droits respectifs des époux Article 220

Spouses owe each other mutual fidelity, support, assistance.

Each spouse may bear, for use, the name of the other spouse, by substitution or addition to his own name in the order he chooses.

If one of the spouses complains of any act causing him prejudice on the part of the other spouse without being able to provide proof thereof, and if the judge cannot determine the responsible spouse, he must appoint two persons to whom he gives the mission of reconciling the spouses. After having studied the situation, the conciliators must, as far as possible, reconcile the spouses and, in all cases, report on their mission to the judge.

###### Article 221

The spouses jointly ensure the moral and material direction of the family. They provide for the education of the children and prepare their future.

###### Article 222

If the matrimonial agreements do not regulate the contribution of the spouses to the charges of the marriage, they contribute to it in proportion to their respective means.

If one of the spouses does not fulfill his obligations, he may be compelled to do so by the other in the forms provided for in the code of civil procedure.

###### Article 223

The spouses mutually undertake to a community of life.

The residence of the family is at the place they choose by mutual agreement.

The spouses cannot, one without the other, dispose of the rights by which the family dwelling is secured, nor of the household furniture with which it is furnished. The one of the two who has not given his consent to the act may request its annulment: the action for nullity is open to him within one year from the day on which he became aware of the act, without ever being able to be brought more than one year after the matrimonial regime has been dissolved.

###### Article 224

Each spouse has full legal capacity; but his rights and powers may be limited by the effect of the matrimonial regime and the provisions of this chapter.

###### Article 225

A spouse may be authorized by justice to perform alone an act for which the cooperation or consent of his spouse would be necessary, if the latter is unable to manifest his will or if his refusal is not justified by the interest of the family.
The act performed under the conditions fixed by the judicial authorization is enforceable against the spouse whose cooperation or consent was lacking, without resulting in any personal obligation on his part.

###### Article 226

A spouse may give a mandate to the other to represent him in the exercise of the powers that the matrimonial regime attributes to him.

###### Article 227

If one of the spouses is unable to manifest his will, the other may be authorized by justice to represent him, in a general manner, or for certain particular acts, in the exercise of the powers resulting from the matrimonial regime. The conditions and extent of this representation are fixed by the judge.
In the absence of legal power, mandate or authorization by justice, acts performed by one spouse in representation of the other have effect, with regard to the latter, according to the rules of management of affairs.

###### Article 228

Each of the spouses has power to enter alone into contracts which have as their object the maintenance of the household or the education of the children: any debt thus contracted by one binds the other jointly and severally.
Solidarity does not apply, however, for manifestly excessive expenses, having regard to the lifestyle of the household, the utility or inutility of the operation, the good or bad faith of the third party contracting.
It does not apply either for obligations resulting from installment purchases if they have not been concluded with the consent of both spouses.

###### Article 229

If one of the spouses seriously fails in his duties and thereby endangers the interests of the family, the president of the Court of First Instance may prescribe all urgent measures required by these interests.

He may in particular prohibit that spouse from making, without the consent of the other, acts of disposition on his own property or on that of the community, movable or immovable. He may also prohibit the displacement of movables, except to specify those of which he attributes personal use to one or the other of the spouses.

The duration of the measures provided for in this article must be determined. It cannot, including any extension, exceed three years.

###### Article 230

If the order prohibits acts of disposition on property whose alienation is subject to publicity, it must be published at the diligence of the applicant spouse. This publication ceases to have effect at the expiration of the period determined by the order, except for the interested party to obtain in the meantime a modifying order, which shall be published in the same manner.
If the order prohibits disposing of corporeal movables, or moving them, it is served by the applicant on his spouse, and has the effect of making the latter a responsible custodian of the movables under the same conditions as a person under seizure.
When the spouse brings the order to the knowledge of a third party, that third party, if he nevertheless contracts with the other spouse, is in bad faith.

###### Article 231

Subject to annulment, at the request of the applicant spouse, are all acts accomplished in violation of the order, if they were performed with a third party in bad faith, or even in the case of property whose alienation is subject to publicity, if they are simply subsequent to the publication provided for by the preceding article.
The action for nullity is open to the applicant spouse for two years from the day on which he became aware of the act, without ever being able to be brought, if that act is subject to publicity, more than two years after its publication.

###### Article 232

Each of the spouses may open, without the consent of the other, any deposit account and any securities account in his personal name.
The depositing spouse is deemed, with regard to the depositary, to have free disposal of the funds and securities on deposit.

###### Article 233

If one of the spouses appears alone to perform an act of administration, enjoyment or disposition on movable property that he holds individually, he is deemed, with regard to third parties in good faith, to have the power to perform that act alone.
This provision is not applicable to household furniture referred to in Article 223, paragraph 3, nor to corporeal movables whose nature creates a presumption of ownership by the other spouse in accordance with Article 1651.

###### Article 234

Each spouse has the right to exercise a profession without the consent of the other spouse, and may always, for the needs of that profession, alienate and encumber alone his or her personal property in full ownership.

Each spouse administers, encumbers and alienates alone his or her personal property. The origin and composition of personal property are established both with regard to third parties and to the spouse, according to the rules of Article 1649.

###### Article 235

Each spouse receives his or her earnings and salary and may dispose of them freely after having discharged the charges of the marriage.

###### Article 236

Creditors to whom a spouse has become obligated may exercise their claims against his or her personal property, even when the obligation was not contracted by him or her in the exercise of his or her profession.

###### Article 237

The provisions of this chapter, in all points where they do not reserve the application of matrimonial agreements, are applicable, by the sole effect of marriage, whatever the matrimonial regime of the spouses.

#### Chapitre VII. De la dissolution du mariage Article 238

Marriage is dissolved:

1° By the death of one of the spouses;

2° By legally pronounced divorce.

#### Chapitre VIII. Des seconds mariages Article 239

A woman may not contract a new marriage until three hundred days have elapsed since the dissolution of the previous marriage. A woman may however, before the expiration of this period of widowhood, contract marriage with her former spouse. The period is extended to four months and ten days elapsed from the death of the husband, for the widow, and from the judgment referred to in Article 158 of this code, for the spouse of the missing person.

This period ends in case of childbirth after the dissolution of the marriage. It also ends if the woman produces a medical certificate attesting that she is not pregnant.
The President of the Court of First Instance in whose jurisdiction the marriage is to be celebrated may, by order rendered on simple petition, shorten the period provided for by this article when it is evident from the circumstances that, for three hundred days, the previous husband has not cohabited with his wife. The petition is communicated to the public prosecutor. In case of rejection of the petition, an appeal may be lodged.

### Titre VII : Du divorce

#### Chapitre I. Des cas de divorce Article 240

Divorce may be pronounced in case of:
-	either mutual consent;
-	or definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond;
-	or fault.

##### Section I : Du divorce par consentement mutuel

###### § 1. Du divorce sur demande conjointe des époux Article 241

When the spouses jointly request divorce, they do not have to make known the cause thereof; they must only submit for the judge's approval a draft agreement which settles the consequences thereof.
The application may be presented either by the parties themselves, or by their respective lawyers, or by a lawyer chosen by mutual agreement.
Divorce by mutual consent may not be requested during the first six months of marriage.

###### Article 242

The judge examines the application with each of the spouses, then brings them together. He then calls the lawyer or lawyers, if one or both spouses have made such a choice.
If the spouses persist in their intention to divorce, the judge indicates to them that their application must be renewed after a reflection period of one month.
In the absence of renewal within three months following the expiration of this reflection period, the joint application shall lapse.

###### Article 243

The judge approves the agreement and pronounces the divorce if he has acquired the conviction that the will of each of the spouses is real and that their consent is free and informed.
