The judge may refuse approval and not pronounce the divorce if he finds that the agreement insufficiently preserves the interests of the children or of one of the spouses.

###### § 2. Du divorce accepté Article 244

Divorce may be requested by either spouse or by both when they accept the principle of the breakdown of the marriage without consideration of the facts at the origin thereof.

This acceptance is not susceptible to retraction. Once it has been validly given, it can no longer be called into question, even by the exercise of a means of appeal.

###### Article 245

If he has acquired the conviction that each of the spouses has given his or her agreement freely, the judge pronounces the divorce and rules on its consequences.

##### Section II : Du divorce pour altération définitive du lien conjugal Article 246

Divorce may be requested by one of the spouses when the conjugal bond is definitively broken down.

###### Article 247

The definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond results from the cessation of the community of life between the spouses, when they have been living separately for two years at the time of the divorce summons.
Notwithstanding these provisions, divorce is pronounced for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond in the case provided for in the second paragraph of Article 251, as soon as the application presented on this ground is made by way of counterclaim.

##### Section III : Du divorce pour faute Article 248

Divorce may be requested by one of the spouses when facts constituting a serious or repeated violation of the duties and obligations of marriage are imputable to his or her spouse and render intolerable the maintenance of the common life.

###### Article 249

In case of reconciliation of the spouses occurring since the alleged facts, these facts can no longer be invoked as a cause of divorce. If this should nevertheless be the case, the judge would have the obligation to declare the application inadmissible.
A new application may however be made by reason of facts occurring or discovered since the reconciliation, the old facts being able then to be recalled in support of this new application.
The maintenance or temporary resumption of the common life are not considered as a reconciliation if they result only from necessity, from an effort at conciliation, or from the needs of the education of the children.

###### Article 250

The faults of the spouse who took the initiative for the divorce do not prevent examination of his or her application; they may, however, remove from the facts which he or she reproaches to his or her spouse the character of seriousness which would have made them a cause of divorce.
These faults may also be invoked by the other spouse in support of a counterclaim for divorce. If both applications are granted, the divorce is pronounced on shared fault.

Even in the absence of a counterclaim, the divorce may be pronounced on the shared fault of both spouses if the proceedings reveal faults chargeable to one and the other.

###### Article 251

If an application for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond and an application for fault are concurrently presented, the judge examines first the application for fault.
In this case, if he rejects the application for divorce for fault, the judge rules without delay on the application for divorce for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond.

##### Section IV : Des modifications du fondement d'une demande en divorce

###### Article 252

The spouses may, at any moment of the proceedings, request the judge to note their agreement to have the divorce pronounced by mutual consent by presenting to him an agreement settling the consequences thereof.

###### Article 253

The spouses may also, at any moment of the proceedings, when the divorce has been requested for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond or for fault, request the judge to note their agreement to have the divorce pronounced for acceptance of the principle of the breakdown of the marriage.

###### Article 254

If, in the context of proceedings instituted for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond, the defendant requests by way of counterclaim divorce for fault, the plaintiff may invoke the faults of his or her spouse to modify the ground of his or her application.

#### Chapter II

Divorce Procedure Section I: General Provisions

###### Article 255

Proceedings on the grounds, consequences of divorce and interim measures are not public.

###### Article 256

In the case of divorce for fault, and at the request of the spouses, the court may limit itself to finding in the reasons for the judgment that there are facts constituting grounds for divorce, without having to state the wrongs and grievances of the parties.

###### Article 257

If an application for divorce must be made in the name of an adult under guardianship, it is submitted by the guardian with the authorization of the family council, after obtaining the opinion of the attending physician.
An adult under curatorship exercises the action himself with the assistance of the curator.

###### Article 258

If the spouse against whom the application is made is under guardianship, the action is brought against the guardian; if he is under curatorship, he defends himself, with the assistance of the curator.

###### Article 259

A special guardian or curator is appointed when the guardianship or curatorship had been entrusted to the spouse of the incapacitated person.

###### Article 260

If one of the spouses is placed under judicial protection, the application for divorce may not be examined until after the organization of guardianship or appointment of a special curator.

###### Article 261

When one of the spouses is placed under one of the protection regimes provided for in Chapter II Legal Protection Measures for Adults of Title XII Majority and Adults Protected by Law(

###### art. 565

et seq.), no application for divorce by mutual consent may be submitted.

##### Section II: Procedure Applicable to Divorce by Mutual Consent

###### Article 262

The application for divorce is submitted by the parties themselves or their lawyers. The spouses may be represented by a lawyer chosen by mutual agreement.
This application takes the form of an initial petition to which is annexed an agreement containing the interim measures that the spouses will observe during the course of the proceedings, as well as a draft final agreement intended to settle the consequences of the divorce.
The judge examines the application with each of the spouses, then brings them together. He then calls the lawyer or lawyers if they have so chosen.

###### Article 263

When the conditions provided for in Article 243 are met, the judge approves the agreement settling the consequences of the divorce and, by the same decision, pronounces it.

###### Article 264

In case of refusal to approve the agreement settling the consequences of the divorce, the judge may nevertheless approve the interim measures envisaged by the parties under Article 262, paragraph 2, and take any measure provided for in Articles 272 and 273, until the date on which the divorce judgment becomes final, ensuring in particular that these measures are in accordance with the interest of the child or children.
A new agreement settling the consequences of the divorce may then be submitted by the spouses within a maximum period of three months.

###### Article 265

In the absence of submission of a new agreement within the time limit set in the preceding article or if the judge refuses approval again, the application for divorce lapses.

##### Section III: Procedure Applicable to Other Cases of Divorce

###### § 1. Initial Petition Article 266

The spouse who files an application for divorce submits, himself or through a lawyer, a petition to the judge, without indicating the grounds for divorce.

###### § 2. Conciliation Article 267

The judge must organize a conciliation hearing. In case of failure, the conciliation attempt may be renewed and attempted at any time during the divorce proceedings which may be initiated by a spouse in accordance with Article 276.

The judge invites the spouses to consider renouncing the divorce and, if he finds their will to continue the proceedings, the judge seeks to reconcile the spouses both on the principle of divorce and on its consequences.

###### Article 268

When the judge seeks to reconcile the spouses, he must meet personally with each of them separately before bringing them together in his presence.
The lawyers are then called to attend and participate in the meeting.

In the case where the spouse who did not file the application does not appear at the hearing or is unable to express his will, the judge meets with the other spouse and invites him to reflect.

###### Article 269

The conciliation attempt may be suspended and resumed without formality, allowing the spouses time for reflection within a limit of eight days.
If a longer period seems useful, the judge may decide to suspend the proceedings and resort to a new conciliation attempt within six months at most. He orders, if necessary, the necessary interim measures.

###### Article 270

When the judge finds that the petitioner maintains his application, he encourages the spouses to settle amicably the consequences of the divorce.
He asks them to submit for the trial hearing a draft settlement of the effects of the divorce.

To this end, he may take any interim measure within the meaning of Articles 272 and 273 of this code, until the date on which the divorce judgment becomes final, ensuring in particular that these measures are in accordance with the interest of the child or children.

###### Article 271

What has been said or written on the occasion of a conciliation attempt, in whatever form it took place, may never be invoked for or against a spouse or a third party in the continuation of the proceedings.

###### § 3. Interim Measures Article 272

Upon the appearance of the spouses in the case referred to in Article 244, or the non-conciliation order in other cases, the judge prescribes the measures that are necessary to ensure the existence of the spouses and children until the date on which the judgment becomes final.

###### Article 273

The judge may in particular:
1° Propose to the spouses a mediation measure and, after obtaining their agreement, appoint a mediator to proceed with it;
2° Enjoin the spouses to meet with a mediator who will inform them about the purpose and conduct of mediation;
3° Rule on the terms of the separate residence of the spouses;
4° Allocate to one of them the enjoyment of the dwelling and furniture of the household, or share this enjoyment between them, specifying its gratuitous nature or not and, where applicable, recording the spouses' agreement on the amount of an occupancy indemnity; failing that, fix this amount;
5° Order the return of clothing and personal objects and, in case of dispute over the ownership of these goods, decide provisionally on their allocation;
6° Fix the maintenance allowance and the provision for costs of proceedings that one of the spouses must pay to his spouse, designate which spouse or spouses must ensure the provisional settlement of all or part of the debts;
7° Grant to one of the spouses advances to be credited against his rights in the liquidation of the matrimonial regime if the situation makes it necessary;
8° Rule on the allocation of the enjoyment or management of common or undivided property other than those referred to in 4°, subject to the rights of each of the spouses in the liquidation of the matrimonial regime
;

9° Appoint any qualified professional with a view to drawing up an estimated inventory or making proposals regarding the settlement of the pecuniary interests of the spouses;
10° Appoint a notary with a view to preparing a draft liquidation of the matrimonial regime and formation of lots to be divided.

###### Article 274

If there are minor children, the judge shall rule on their custody, as well as on visitation and accommodation rights. The judge shall fix the contribution due for their maintenance and education by the spouse who does not have custody.
Parental authority is exercised by the spouse to whom the court has entrusted custody of the child, subject to the visitation and supervision rights of the other.

###### Article 275

The judge may take emergency measures from the initial application.

For this purpose, the judge may authorize the applicant spouse to reside separately, if necessary with his or her minor children; the judge may then, where applicable, determine, with the agreement of the spouses and failing that by decision, the financial arrangements between spouses to facilitate this separate residence.

The judge may also, to guarantee the rights of a spouse, order any conservatory measures such as the affixing of seals on common property. The provisions of Article 240 and the other safeguards established by the matrimonial regime remain applicable, however.

###### § 4. Del'introduction de l'instance en divorce Article 276

After the non-conciliation order, a spouse may initiate proceedings or file a counterclaim for acceptance of the principle of the breakdown of the marriage, for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond or for fault.
However, when at the conciliation hearing the spouses have declared that they accept the principle of the breakdown of the marriage and the pronouncement of divorce on the basis of Article 244, proceedings may only be initiated on that same basis.

###### Article 277

On pain of inadmissibility, the application initiating proceedings must include a proposal for the settlement of the pecuniary and patrimonial interests of the spouses.

###### Article 278

When the judge definitively dismisses the application for divorce, the judge may rule on the contribution to the charges of the marriage, the residence of the family and the terms of the exercise of parental authority.

###### § 5. Des preuves Article 279

The facts invoked as grounds for divorce or as defenses to an application may be established by any mode of proof, including admission. However, descendants may never be heard on the grievances invoked by the spouses.

###### Article 280

A spouse may not submit to the proceedings any evidence that he or she obtained by violence or fraud.

###### Article 281

Reports drawn up at the request of a spouse outside judicial proceedings are excluded from the proceedings if there has been a violation of domicile or unlawful interference with the privacy of private life.

###### Article 282

The spouses must communicate to each other and communicate to the judge as well as to the experts appointed by him, all useful information and documents to fix the benefits and pensions and liquidate the matrimonial regime.
The judge may have any useful investigations carried out with debtors or those who hold securities on behalf of the spouses without professional secrecy being invoked. Any contravention of the judge's order shall be prosecuted before the Court of First Instance, and punished by a fine of 20,000 to 200,000 FD.

#### Chapitre III : Des conséquences du divorce

##### Section I : De la date à laquelle se produisent les effets du divorce Article 283

The decision pronouncing the divorce dissolves the marriage on the date on which it acquires the force of res judicata.

###### Article 284

To contract a new marriage, the woman must observe the period of three hundred days as provided for in Article 250.
If the spouses have been authorized to reside separately during the proceedings, this period begins to run from the day of the decision authorizing the separate residence or approving, in the case of a joint application, the temporary agreement entered into for this purpose.
The woman may remarry without delay when the divorce has been pronounced in the cases provided for in Articles 246 and 247.

###### Article 285

The period referred to in the preceding article ends if a childbirth takes place after the decision authorizing or approving the separate residence or, failing that, after the date on which the divorce judgment has become res judicata.
If the husband dies before the divorce judgment has become res judicata, the period runs from the day after the day on which the death is officially recorded.

###### Article 286

The divorce judgment is enforceable against third parties, with regard to the property of the spouses, from the day on which the formalities of marginal notation prescribed by the rules of civil status have been completed.

###### Article 287

The agreement or divorce judgment takes effect in the relations between the spouses, with regard to their property:
-	when it is pronounced by mutual consent in accordance with Article 263, on the date of approval of the agreement settling all the consequences of the divorce, unless the agreement provides otherwise;
-	when it is pronounced for acceptance of the principle of the breakdown of the marriage, for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond or for fault, on the date of the non-conciliation order.

One of the spouses may request that the effect of the judgment be brought forward to the date when, through the fault of the other, their cohabitation and collaboration ceased.

###### Article 288

Any obligation contracted by one of the spouses to the charge of the community, any alienation of common property made by one of them within the limits of his or her powers, subsequent to the initial application, shall be declared null and void if it is proved that there has been fraud against the rights of the other spouse.

##### Section II : Des conséquences du divorce pour les époux

###### § 1. Dispositions générales Article 289

If the divorced spouses wish to contract another union between themselves, a new celebration of the marriage is necessary.

###### Article 290

Following the divorce, each of the spouses loses the use of the name of his or her spouse.

One of the spouses may nevertheless retain the use of the name of the other, either with the latter's agreement, or with the authorization of the judge, if he or she justifies a particular interest for himself or herself or for the children.

###### Article 291

The divorce has no effect on matrimonial benefits that take effect during the marriage and on gifts of present property whatever their form.
The divorce entails revocation by operation of law of matrimonial benefits that only take effect upon the dissolution of the matrimonial regime or upon the death of one of the spouses and of dispositions upon death, granted by one spouse to his or her spouse by marriage contract or during the union, unless the spouse who granted them wills otherwise. This will is recorded in the agreement signed by the spouses and approved by the judge, or by the judge at the time of pronouncing the divorce; in these cases, the benefit or disposition maintained are irrevocable.

However, if the marriage contract so provides, the spouses may always take back the property that they have contributed to the community.

###### Article 292

The divorce has no effect on the rights that either spouse derives from the law or from agreements entered into with third parties.

###### Article 293

The spouses may, during the divorce proceedings, enter into any agreements for the liquidation and partition of their matrimonial regime.
When the liquidation relates to property subject to land registration, the agreement must be executed by notarial deed.

###### § 2

Consequences specific to divorces other than by mutual consent Article 294

Without prejudice to the application of Article 297, damages may be awarded to a spouse in compensation for consequences of particular gravity which he or she suffers as a result of the dissolution of the marriage:
1° either when he or she was defendant in a divorce pronounced for definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond and had not himself or herself filed any petition for divorce;
2° or when the divorce is pronounced on the exclusive fault of his or her spouse. This claim may only be made in connection with the divorce action.

###### Article 295

In the absence of a conventional settlement by the spouses, the judge rules on their applications for maintenance in joint ownership, preferential allocation and advance on share of community property or undivided property.
The judge rules on applications for liquidation and partition of patrimonial interests, under the conditions set out in Articles L.624-5 to L.624-11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, if disagreements persisting between the parties are proven by any means, in particular by producing:
-	a joint declaration of acceptance of a judicial partition, indicating the points of disagreement between the spouses;
-	the draft prepared by the notary designated on the basis of 10° of Article 273.

He may, even of his own motion, rule on the determination of the matrimonial regime applicable to the spouses.

###### Article 296

The spouses may, during the proceedings, submit to the judge for approval agreements settling all or part of the consequences of the divorce.
The judge, after having verified that the interests of each of the spouses and of the children are preserved, approves the agreements by pronouncing the divorce.

###### § 3. Compensatory allowances Article 297

Divorce terminates the duty of support between spouses.

One of the spouses may be required to pay the other an allowance intended to compensate, as far as possible, for the disparity that the breakdown of the marriage creates in their respective living conditions.
However, the judge may refuse to grant such an allowance if equity so requires, either in consideration of the criteria provided for in Article 298, or when the divorce is pronounced on the exclusive fault of the spouse who requests the benefit of this allowance, having regard to the particular circumstances of the breakdown.

###### Article 298

The compensatory allowance is fixed according to the needs of the spouse to whom it is paid and the resources of the other, taking into account the situation at the time of the divorce and the evolution thereof in a foreseeable future.
For this purpose, the judge takes into consideration, in particular:
-	the duration of the marriage;
-	the age and state of health of the spouses;
-	their qualifications and their professional situations;
-	the consequences of professional choices made by one of the spouses during the common life for the education of the children and the time that will still have to be devoted thereto or to promote the career of his or her spouse to the detriment of his or her own;

-	the estimated or foreseeable patrimony of the spouses, both in capital and in income, after the liquidation of the matrimonial regime;
-	their existing and foreseeable rights;
-	their respective situation with regard to retirement pensions, having estimated, as far as possible, the reduction in retirement rights which may have been caused, for the spouse creditor of the compensatory allowance, by the circumstances referred to in the sixth paragraph.

###### Article 299

In the context of the fixing of a compensatory allowance, by the judge or by the parties, or on the occasion of an application for revision, the parties provide the judge with a declaration certifying on their honour the accuracy of their resources, income, patrimony and living conditions.

###### Article 300

The compensatory allowance has a lump-sum character. It may not be revised even in the event of an unforeseen change in the resources or needs of the parties, except if the absence of revision would have consequences of exceptional gravity for one of the spouses.

###### Article 301

When the composition of the assets of the spouse debtor of the compensatory allowance so permits, it takes the form of a capital sum the amount of which is fixed by the judge.

###### Article 302

The judge decides on the terms according to which the allocation or assignment of property in capital will be executed:
1° Payment of a sum of money;
2° Abandonment of property in kind, movable or immovable, but for the usufruct only, the judgment operating forced transfer in favour of the creditor;

3° Deposit of income-producing securities with a third party responsible for paying the income to the spouse creditor of the allowance until the fixed term.
The divorce judgment may be made conditional upon the actual payment of the capital or the provision of the guarantees provided for in Article 306.

###### Article 303

If the spouse debtor of the compensatory allowance does not have immediate liquid assets, he or she may be authorized, subject to the guarantees provided for in Article 306, to constitute the capital in three annual instalments.
In the absence of capital or if it is not sufficient, the compensatory allowance takes the form of an annuity.

###### Article 304

When the compensatory allowance takes the form of an annuity, this annuity is awarded for a period equal to or less than the life of the spouse creditor.
The annuity is indexed; the index is determined as in matters of maintenance.
The amount of the annuity before indexation is fixed uniformly for its entire duration or may vary by successive periods according to the probable evolution of resources and needs.

###### Article 305

Upon the death of the spouse debtor, the burden of the annuity passes to his or her heirs.

###### Article 306

Independently of the legal or judicial mortgage, the judge may require the spouse debtor to provide a personal or real security to guarantee the annuity.

###### Article 307

In the event of a joint application, the spouses fix the amount and terms of the compensatory allowance in the agreement which they submit to the judge for approval.
The judge, however, refuses to approve the agreement if it inequitably fixes the rights and obligations of the spouses.

###### Article 308

The approved agreement has the same executory force as a court decision.

It may only be modified by a new agreement between the spouses, also subject to approval.
The spouses nevertheless have the option of providing in their agreement that each of them may, in the event of an unforeseen change in his or her resources and needs, request the judge to revise the compensatory allowance.

###### Article 309

The transfers and abandonments provided for in this paragraph are considered as participating in the matrimonial regime. They are not treated as gifts.

###### Article 310

The spouse on whose exclusive fault the divorce is pronounced is not entitled to any compensatory allowance.

However, he or she may obtain compensation on an exceptional basis, if, taking into account the duration of the common life and the collaboration provided to the profession of the other spouse, it appears manifestly contrary to equity to refuse him or her any pecuniary compensation following the divorce.

###### § 4. The duty of support after divorce Article 311

When divorce is pronounced for breakdown of common life, the spouse who took the initiative for the divorce remains fully bound by the duty of support.

In the case of Article 247, the duty of support covers everything necessary for the medical treatment of the sick spouse.

###### Article 312

The performance of the duty of support takes the form of maintenance. This may always be revised according to the resources and needs of each of the spouses.

###### Article 313

Maintenance ceases to be due by operation of law if the spouse who is the creditor thereof enters into a new marriage.
It is terminated if the creditor lives in a state of notorious cohabitation.

###### Article 314

Upon the death of the debtor spouse, the burden of maintenance passes to his or her heirs.

###### Article 315

Where the assets of the debtor spouse so permit, maintenance is replaced, in whole or in part, by the constitution of capital, according to the rules of Articles 301 to 303, first paragraph, and 309.
If this capital becomes insufficient to cover the needs of the creditor spouse, the latter may request a supplement in the form of maintenance.

###### § 5. Du logement Article 316

If the premises serving as the family dwelling belong in ownership or personally to one of the spouses, the judge may grant a lease thereof to the other spouse:
1° Where custody of one or more children has been entrusted to the latter;
2° Where the divorce has been pronounced at the request of the owner spouse, for breakdown of cohabitation.

In the case provided for in 1° above, the judge fixes the duration of the lease and may renew it until the youngest of the children reaches the age of majority.
In the case provided for in 2°, the lease may not be granted for a period exceeding nine years, but may be extended by a new decision. It terminates, by operation of law, in the event of remarriage of the person to whom it was granted. It is terminated if the latter lives in a state of notorious cohabitation.
In all cases, the judge may terminate the lease if new circumstances justify it.

##### Section III : Des conséquences du divorce pour les enfants Article 317

Divorce leaves intact the rights and duties of the father and mother towards their children, subject to the rules that follow.

###### Article 318

According to the interests of minor children, their custody is entrusted to one or the other of the spouses.
Exceptionally and if the interests of the children so require, such custody may be entrusted: 1° either to another person chosen preferably from among their relatives;
2° or, if this proves impossible, to an educational establishment or to a recognised association in this field.

###### Article 319

Before ruling on the custody of children, provisional or final, and on visiting rights, the judge may give a mission to any qualified person to carry out a social inquiry. The purpose of this inquiry is to gather information on the material and moral situation of the family, on the conditions in which the children live and are educated and on the measures to be taken in their interests.
If one of the spouses contests the conclusions of the social inquiry, he or she may request a counter-inquiry. The social inquiry may not be used in the debate on the cause of the divorce.

###### Article 320

The spouse to whom custody of the children has not been entrusted retains the right to supervise their maintenance and education. He or she contributes thereto in proportion to his or her resources.

A right of visit and accommodation may only be refused to him or her for serious reasons.
He or she may be charged with administering, under judicial supervision, all or part of the children's patrimony, by way of derogation from Articles 480 and 518 paragraph 2, if the interest of proper administration of this patrimony so requires.

###### Article 321

The judge rules on the award of custody and on the modalities of the exercise of parental authority, at the request of one of the spouses, a member of the family or the public prosecutor.

###### Article 322

The judge takes into account:
1° Agreements entered into between the spouses;
2° Information that has been gathered in the inquiry and the social counter-inquiry provided for in Article 319;
3° Sentiments expressed by minor children where their hearing has appeared necessary and does not entail disadvantages for them.

###### Article 323

Decisions relating to the exercise of parental authority may be modified or supplemented at any time by the judge, at the request of a spouse, a member of the family or the public prosecutor.

###### Article 324

In the case of divorce by joint application, the provisions of the convention approved by the judge relating to the exercise of parental authority may be revised, for serious reasons, at the request of one of the spouses or the public prosecutor.

###### Article 325

The contribution to the maintenance and education of children provided for in Article 320 takes the form of maintenance paid to the person who has custody thereof.
The modalities and guarantees of this maintenance are fixed by the judgment or, in the case of divorce by joint application, by the convention of the spouses approved by the judge.

###### Article 326

Where the assets of the debtor so permit, maintenance may be replaced, in whole or in part, according to the rules of Articles 301 to 303, first paragraph, and 309, by the payment of a sum of money into the hands of an accredited body charged with granting in return to the child an indexed annuity, the abandonment of property in usufruct or the allocation of income-producing property.

###### Article 327

If the capital thus constituted becomes insufficient to cover the needs of the children, the person who has custody may request the award of a supplement in the form of maintenance.

###### Article 328

The parent who assumes primary responsibility for the care of adult children who cannot themselves provide for their needs may request his or her spouse to pay him or her a contribution to their maintenance and education.

#### Chapitre IV : De la séparation de corps

##### Section I : Des cas et de la procédure de la séparation de corps

###### Article 329

Judicial separation may be pronounced at the request of one of the spouses in the same cases and on the same conditions as divorce.

###### Article 330

The spouse against whom an application for divorce is presented may file a counterclaim for judicial separation. However, where the principal application for divorce is based on the definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond, the counterclaim may only seek divorce.
The spouse against whom an application for judicial separation is presented may file a counterclaim for divorce.

###### Article 331

Where an application for divorce and an application for judicial separation are concurrently presented, the judge examines first the application for divorce. He or she pronounces the latter as soon as the conditions therefor are met. Failing that, he or she rules on the application for judicial separation.
However, where these applications are based on fault, the judge examines them simultaneously and, if he or she grants them, pronounces divorce on shared fault in respect of both spouses.

###### Article 332

The rules contained in Article 250 as well as in Chapter II above are applicable to the procedure for judicial separation.

##### Section II : Des conséquences de la séparation de corps Article 333

Judicial separation does not dissolve the marriage but it terminates the duty of cohabitation.

###### Article 334

Judicial separation allows each of the spouses who was using the name of the other to retain such use for the future. However, the judgment of judicial separation, or a subsequent judgment, may prohibit a spouse from retaining the use of his or her spouse's name.

###### Article 335

In the event of the death of one of the spouses who are judicially separated, the other spouse retains the rights that the law grants to the surviving spouse. Where judicial separation is pronounced by mutual consent, the spouses may include in their convention a renunciation of the succession rights conferred upon them by Articles 858 et seq. and 872 et seq. of this Code.

###### Article 336

Judicial separation always entails separation of property.

With regard to property, the date on which judicial separation takes effect is determined in accordance with the provisions of Articles 286 to 288.

###### Article 337

Judicial separation leaves the duty of support subsisting; the judgment granting it or a subsequent judgment fixes the maintenance allowance that is owed to the spouse in need.

This allowance is granted without consideration of fault. The debtor spouse may nevertheless invoke, where applicable, the provisions of Article 215, paragraph 2.

This allowance is subject to the rules of maintenance obligations; the provisions of Article 315 are however applicable to it.

###### Article 338

Subject to the provisions of this section, the consequences of judicial separation are governed by the same rules as the consequences of divorce set out in Chapter III above.

##### Section III: On the termination of judicial separation Article 339

The voluntary resumption of common life terminates judicial separation.

To be enforceable against third parties, this must either be recorded by notarial deed or be the subject of a declaration to the civil registrar. Mention thereof is made in the margin of the marriage certificate.
The separation of property subsists unless the spouses adopt a new matrimonial regime following the rules of Article 1642.

###### Article 340

At the request of one of the spouses, the judgment of judicial separation is converted by operation of law into a judgment of divorce when the judicial separation has lasted three years.

###### Article 341

In all cases of judicial separation, it may be converted into divorce by joint application.
When judicial separation has been granted on joint application, it may be converted into divorce only by a new joint application.

###### Article 342

By virtue of the conversion, the ground for judicial separation becomes the ground for divorce; the attribution of fault is not modified.
The judge fixes the consequences of the divorce. Benefits and allowances between spouses are determined according to the rules specific to divorce.

###### Article 343

The wife may contract a new marriage as soon as the conversion decision has become res judicata.

#### Chapter V

On the conflict of laws relating to divorce and judicial separation Article 344
Divorce and judicial separation are governed by Djiboutian law:
-	when both spouses are of Djiboutian nationality;
-	when the spouses both have their domicile on Djiboutian territory;
-	when no foreign law recognizes itself as competent, while the Djiboutian courts have jurisdiction to hear the divorce or judicial separation.

### Title VIII: On filiation

Chapter I: Provisions common to legitimate filiation and natural filiation Section I: On presumptions relating to filiation

###### Article 345

The law presumes that the child was conceived during the period extending from the three hundredth to the one hundred and eightieth day, inclusive, before the date of birth.
Conception is presumed to have occurred at any moment of this period, according to what is required in the interest of the child.

Proof to the contrary is admissible to rebut these presumptions.

###### Article 346

Possession of status is established by a sufficient combination of facts that indicate the relationship of filiation and kinship between an individual and the family to which he is said to belong.
Possession of status must be continuous.

###### Article 347

The principal of these facts are:
-	that the individual has always borne the name of those from whom he is said to be descended;
-	that they have treated him as their child, and that he has treated them as his father and mother;
-	that they have, in that capacity, provided for his education, maintenance and establishment;
-	that he is recognized as such in society and by the family;
-	that the public authority considers him as such.

###### Article 348

The parents or the child may request from the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or from the judge designated for that purpose that there be issued to them, under the conditions provided for in Articles 106 and 107 of this code, a certificate of notoriety constituting proof of possession of status until proof to the contrary; this without prejudice to all other means of proof to which they could resort to establish its existence in court, if it were to be contested.

##### Section II: On actions relating to filiation Article 349

No action is received as to the filiation of a child who was not born viable.

###### Article 350

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance has sole jurisdiction to hear actions relating to filiation under the Civil Code. The Personal Status Court of First Instance has jurisdiction to hear disputes relating to personal status matters of persons governed by the Family Code.

###### Article 351

In case of an offense affecting the filiation of an individual, the criminal action may be decided only after the judgment that has become res judicata on the question of filiation.

###### Article 352

Whenever they are not confined by law within shorter terms, actions relating to filiation are prescribed after thirty years from the day on which the individual would have been deprived of the status he claims, or began to enjoy the status that is contested.

###### Article 353

The action that belonged to an individual as to his filiation may be exercised by his heirs only in cases where that individual died a minor or within five years after his majority or emancipation.
His heirs may also pursue the action he had already initiated, unless there has been withdrawal or lapse of proceedings.

###### Article 354

Actions relating to filiation may not be the subject of waiver.

###### Article 355

Judgments rendered in matters of filiation are enforceable against any person, even those who were not parties to the proceedings; but persons who were not parties to the proceedings have the right to file third-party opposition against said judgments.
The judges may of their own motion order that all interested parties to whom they consider the judgment should be made common be joined as parties.

###### Article 356

Similarly when, in one of the actions opened by Articles 418 and 436 below, a plea of inadmissibility or a defense is raised on the ground that the mother had, during the legal period of conception, relations with a third party, the judge may order that the latter be called to the case.

###### Article 357

The courts settle conflicts of filiation for which the law has not fixed any other principle, by determining by all means of proof the most probable filiation.
In the absence of sufficient elements of conviction, they have regard to possession of status.

###### Article 358

In the case where they are led to reject the claim of the party who was, in fact, taking care of the education of the minor child, the courts may, nevertheless, taking into account the interest of the child, grant to that party a right of visitation.

##### Section III

On the conflict of laws relating to the establishment of filiation Article 359
Filiation is governed by the personal law of the mother on the day of the child's birth; if the mother is not known, by the personal law of the child.

###### Article 360

However, if the legitimate child and his father and mother, the natural child and one of his father or mother have in Djibouti their habitual residence, common or separate, possession of status produces all the consequences that flow from it according to Djiboutian law, this even in the case where the other elements of filiation could have depended on a foreign law.

###### Article 361

Marriage entails legitimation when, on the day the union was celebrated, this consequence is recognized either by the law governing the effects of marriage, or by the personal law of one of the spouses, or by the personal law of the child.

Legitimation by judicial authority is governed, at the choice of the applicant, either by the personal law of the applicant or by the personal law of the child.

###### Article 362

Voluntary acknowledgment of paternity or maternity is valid if it was made in conformity either with the personal law of its author or with the personal law of the child.

###### Article 363

The action for maintenance is governed, at the choice of the child, either by the law of his or her habitual residence or by the law of the habitual residence of the debtor.

#### Chapter II: Legitimate Filiation

##### Section I: Presumption of Paternity Article 364

A child conceived or born during marriage has the husband as father.

Nevertheless, the husband may disavow the child in court if he establishes facts demonstrating that he cannot be the father.

###### Article 365

In the event of a judgment or even an application for either divorce or legal separation, the presumption of paternity does not apply to a child born more than three hundred days after the order authorizing the spouses to reside separately, and less than one hundred and eighty days since the final rejection of the application or since the reconciliation.
The presumption of paternity nevertheless recovers its force by operation of law:
1° If the child, with regard to the spouses, has the status possession of a legitimate child and does not have paternal filiation already established with regard to a third party.
2° If, upon application brought by either spouse before the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance during the child's minority, proof is provided that the husband is indeed the father of the child. This action is also available to the child during the ten years following his or her majority.

###### Article 366

The presumption of paternity is set aside when the child, registered without indication of the husband's name, has status possession only with regard to the mother.

###### Article 367

When the presumption of paternity is set aside under the conditions provided for in the preceding articles, the child's filiation is established with regard to the mother as if there had been a disavowal admitted in court.
Either spouse may request that the effects of the presumption of paternity be restored by establishing that, during the legal period of conception, a factual reunion took place between them that makes the husband's paternity plausible.

###### Article 368

A child born before the one hundred and eightieth day of marriage is legitimate and deemed to have been so from conception.

The husband, however, may disavow the child according to the rules of Article 312.

He may even disavow the child on the sole proof of the date of delivery, unless he knew of the pregnancy before the marriage or behaved as the father after the birth.

###### Article 369

The presumption of paternity is not applicable to a child born more than three hundred days after the dissolution of the marriage, nor, in the case of declared absence of the husband, to one born to a married woman more than one year after the absence or death of her husband or the date of divorce.

###### Article 370

The husband must bring the action for disavowal within six months of the birth, when he is present at the place.
If he was not present at the place, within six months of his return.

And within six months following the discovery of the fraud, if the birth of the child had been concealed from him.

###### Article 371

If the husband died before bringing the action, but while still within the time limit to do so, his heirs shall have standing to contest the legitimacy of the child.
Their action, however, shall cease to be admissible when six months have elapsed from the time when the child took possession of the alleged paternal property, or from the time when they were disturbed by him in their own possession.

###### Article 372

Any extrajudicial act containing disavowal on the part of the husband or contestation of legitimacy on the part of the heirs shall be deemed null and void if it is not followed by a court action within six months.

###### Article 373

The action for disavowal is directed, in the presence of the mother, against a guardian ad litem appointed to the child by the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or by the judge designated for this purpose.

###### Article 374

Even in the absence of disavowal, the mother may contest the husband's paternity, but only for the purposes of legitimation, when she has, after dissolution of the marriage, remarried the true father of the child.

###### Article 375

On pain of inadmissibility, the action, directed against the husband or his heirs, is joined to an application for legitimation made in the terms of Article 390 below.
It must be brought by the mother and her new spouse within six months of their marriage and before the child has reached the age of seven years.

###### Article 376

Both applications are decided by a single judgment, which may grant the contestation of paternity only if legitimation is admitted.

##### Section II: Proof of Legitimate Filiation Article 377

The filiation of legitimate children is proved by birth certificates registered in the civil status registers.

###### Article 378

In the absence of such title, possession of the status of legitimate child is sufficient.

###### Article 379

There is possession of the status of legitimate child only insofar as it connects the child indivisibly to his or her father and mother.

###### Article 380

No one may claim a status contrary to that given by his or her birth certificate and possession consistent with that certificate.
And conversely, no one may contest the status of one who has possession consistent with his or her birth certificate.

###### Article 381

However, if it is alleged that there was a false representation of a child, or substitution, even involuntary, either before or after the drafting of the birth certificate, proof thereof shall be admissible and may be made by all means.

###### Article 382

In the absence of title and possession of status, or if the child was registered either under false names or without indication of the mother's name, proof of filiation may be made by witnesses.
Proof by witnesses may, however, be admitted only when there exists either a commencement of proof in writing or presumptions or indications serious enough to warrant its admission.

###### Article 383

Commencement of proof in writing results from family documents, registers and domestic papers, as well as from all other public or private writings emanating from a party involved in the dispute or who would have an interest therein if alive.

###### Article 384

Counter-proof may be made by all means capable of establishing that the claimant is not the child of the mother he or she claims to have, or even, maternity being proved, that he or she is not the child of the mother's husband.
If the husband was not made a party to the status claim proceedings, he may contest his paternity within six months from the day he became aware of the judgment having acquired the force of res judicata granting the child's application.

###### Article 385

Without waiting for a status claim to be brought by the child, the husband may, by all means, contest his paternity within six months from the day he learned of the birth.

###### Article 386

After the husband's death, his heirs shall likewise have the right to contest his paternity either preventively if the husband was still within the time limit to do so, or in defense to a status claim action.

###### Article 387

Spouses, separately or jointly, may, by providing the proof required under Article 382 above, claim a child as their own; but if the child already has another established filiation, they must first demonstrate its inaccuracy, assuming that one is in one of the cases where the law authorizes such demonstration.

##### Section III: Of legitimation Article 388

Legitimation is the act by which a lawfully married couple confers upon a natural child the status of legitimate child.

Legitimation may benefit all natural children, as soon as, either by voluntary recognition or by judgment, their filiation has been legally established.

Legitimation takes place either by marriage of the parents or by authority of justice.

###### § 1. Of legitimation by marriage Article 389

All children born out of wedlock are legitimated by operation of law by the subsequent marriage of their father and mother.

If their filiation was not already established, these children are the subject of recognition at the time of the celebration of the marriage. In this case, the civil registrar who performs the celebration records the recognition and legitimation in a separate act.

###### Article 390

When the filiation of a natural child has been established with respect to his father and mother or one of them only after their marriage, legitimation can only take place by virtue of a judgment.
This judgment must establish that the child has had, since the celebration of the marriage, the possession of status of common child.

###### Article 391

Every legitimation is noted in the margin of the birth certificate of the legitimated child.
This notation may be requested by any interested party. In the case of Article 389, the civil registrar provides for it himself, if he has had knowledge of the existence of the children.

###### Article 392

Legitimation may take place after the death of the child, if he has left descendants; it then benefits them.

###### Article 393

Legitimation confers upon the legitimated child the rights and duties of the legitimate child. It takes effect on the date of the marriage.

###### § 2. Of legitimation by authority of justice

###### Article 394

If it appears that marriage is impossible between the two parents, the benefit of legitimation may still be conferred upon the child by authority of justice provided that he has, with respect to the parent who requests it, the possession of status of natural child.

###### Article 395

The application for legitimation is made by one of the two parents or by both jointly before the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 396

If one of the parents of the child was, at the time of conception, in the bonds of a marriage that is not dissolved, his application is admissible only with the consent of his spouse.

###### Article 397

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance verifies whether the conditions of the law are met and, after having received or solicited, as the case may be, the observations of the child himself, of the other parent when he is not a party to the application, as well as of the spouse of the applicant, it pronounces, if it deems it justified, the legitimation.

###### Article 398

Legitimation by authority of justice takes effect on the date of the decision that pronounces it definitively.

If it took place at the request of only one of the parents, it has no effect with respect to the other; it does not entail modification of the child's name, except by contrary decision of the Civil Chamber.

###### Article 399

If legitimation by authority of justice has been pronounced with respect to both parents, the child takes the name of the father; if he is a minor, his custody is decided upon by the Civil Chamber, as in matters of divorce.

###### Article 400

The provisions of Articles 391 to 393, paragraph 1 are applicable to legitimation by authority of justice.

#### Chapter III: Of natural filiation

##### Section I

Of the effects of natural filiation and its modes of establishment in general Article 401
Every natural child falls under the regime of the civil code whenever his parents have expressed their will to subject this child to this regime at the time of the declaration of his birth to the civil registrar.
The parent who, alone, makes the declaration is deemed to act in agreement with the other to this effect. The one who has not made the declaration has one month, from the declaration made to the civil registrar to contest its meaning. In case of disagreement between the two parents, the regime of the family code shall then be applicable to the child.
If the parents of this child give birth to one or more other common children, these shall be subject to the choice made for the first common child.

###### Article 402

The natural child has in principle the same rights and the same duties as the legitimate child in his relations with his father and mother.

He enters into the family of his author.

###### Article 403

The natural child acquires the name of that one of his two parents with respect to whom his filiation is established first; the name of his father, if the filiation is established simultaneously with respect to one and the other.

###### Article 404

Even in the case where his filiation was established only second with respect to the father, the natural child may take the name of the latter by substitution, if, during his minority, his two parents make the joint declaration before the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or the judge delegated for this purpose.

If the child is more than fifteen years old, his personal consent is necessary.

###### Article 405

In all other cases, the change of name of the natural child must be requested from the Court of First Instance.
The action is available during the minority of the child and in the two years that will follow either his majority or a modification made to his status.

###### Article 406

The substitution of name extends by operation of law to the minor children of the interested party. It extends to adult children only with their consent.

###### Article 407

In the absence of established paternal filiation, the husband of the mother may confer, by substitution, his own name on the child by a declaration that he will make jointly with the mother, under the conditions provided for in Article 404 above.
The child may however request to resume the name he bore previously by a request that he will submit to the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, within two years following his majority.

###### Article 408

The rules of attribution of name provided for in the preceding articles do not prejudice the effects of possession of status.

###### Article 409

In the case provided for in the third paragraph of Article 401 above, the natural child may be raised at the conjugal domicile only with the consent of the spouse of his author.

###### Article 410

Natural filiation is legally established either by voluntary recognition or by judicial declaration, following an action in search of paternity or maternity.
Natural filiation may also be legally established by the necessary effect of a judgment, notably following an action in disavowal or in contestation of legitimacy.

###### Article 411

Any recognition is null, any request in search is inadmissible, when the child has a legitimate filiation already established by possession of status.

###### Article 412

If there exists between the father and mother of the natural child one of the impediments to marriage provided for by Articles 173 and 174 for reason of kinship, the filiation being already established with respect to one, it is prohibited to establish the filiation with respect to the other.

##### Section II: Recognition of natural children Article 413

Recognition of a natural child shall be made by authentic act, when it has not been made in the birth certificate.

###### Article 414

Recognition by the father, without indication and acknowledgment of the mother, has effect only with regard to the father.

###### Article 415

The birth certificate bearing indication of the mother is valid as recognition, when it is corroborated by possession of status.

###### Article 416

As long as it has not been contested in court, a recognition renders inadmissible the establishment of another natural filiation that would contradict it.

###### Article 417

Recognition may be contested by all persons who have an interest therein, even by its author.
The action is also open to the public prosecutor, if indications drawn from the acts themselves render the declared filiation implausible.

When there exists a possession of status consistent with the recognition and which has lasted at least ten years since the latter, no contestation is any longer admissible, except on the part of the other parent, of the child himself or of those who claim to be the true parents.

##### Section III: Actions for establishment of paternity and maternity Article 418

In the absence of title and possession of status, establishment of maternity is admitted. The mother may however, at the time of delivery, request that the secrecy of her admission and her identity be preserved.
The child who brings the action is required to prove that he is the one of whom the alleged mother gave birth.

He may prove it by establishing that he has, with regard to the latter, the possession of status of natural child. In the absence thereof, proof of filiation may be made by witnesses, if there exist either serious presumptions or indications, or a commencement of proof in writing, within the meaning of Article 383.

###### Article 419

Paternity outside marriage may be judicially declared in the presence of established facts which render the filiation plausible.

###### Article 420

The action belongs only to the child.
The parent, even if a minor, with regard to whom filiation is established has, during the minority of the child, sole capacity to bring the action for establishment of maternity or paternity.

If no filiation link is established or if that parent is deceased or unable to express his will, the action is brought by the guardian in accordance with the provisions of Article 542, paragraph 2.

###### Article 421

The action for establishment of paternity is brought against the alleged parent or against his heirs. In the absence of heirs or if they have renounced the succession, it is directed against the State. The renouncing heirs are called to the proceedings to assert their rights therein.

###### Article 422

The action must, on pain of forfeiture, be brought within two years following the birth.

However, when the alleged father and the mother lived during the legal period of conception in a state of concubinage, implying, in the absence of community of life, stable and continuous relations, or when the alleged father has provided for or participated in the maintenance, education or establishment of the child in the capacity of father, the action may be brought until the expiration of two years following the cessation, either of the concubinage, or of the acts of participation in the maintenance and education of the child.

If it has not been brought during the minority of the child, the latter may still bring it during the two years following his majority.

###### Article 423

When it grants the action, the court may, at the request of the mother, order the father to reimburse her for all or part of her maternity and maintenance expenses during the three months preceding and the three months following the birth, without prejudice to the damages to which she might be entitled by application of Article 1391.

###### Article 424

The court rules, if appropriate, on the attribution of the name and on the exercise of parental authority, in accordance with Articles 405 and 486.

###### Article 425

In rejecting the claim, the judges may, nevertheless, award maintenance to the child, if relations between the mother and the defendant have been demonstrated under the conditions provided for in Articles 426 and following.

##### Section IV: Action for maintenance Article 426

Any natural child whose paternal filiation is not legally established, may claim maintenance from the person who had relations with his mother during the legal period of conception.

The action is admissible even if the father or the mother was at the time of conception, bound in the bonds of marriage with another person, or if there existed between them one of the impediments to marriage governed by Articles 173 to 176 of this code.

###### Article 427

The action for maintenance may also be brought by the child of a married woman, if his title of legitimate child is not corroborated by possession of status.

###### Article 428

Maintenance is determined, in the form of a pension, according to the needs of the child, the resources of the debtor, the family situation of the latter.

The pension may be due beyond the majority of the child, if he is still in need, unless that state is attributable to his fault.

###### Article 429

When there is occasion for the application of Article 356 above, the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, in the absence of other elements of decision, has the power to place an indemnity intended to ensure the maintenance and education of the child on the defendants, if faults are established against them, or if commitments have been made previously by them.
The president determines the period within which the indemnity must be paid to the legal representative of the child; in case of default of payment within the indicated period, the creditor may seize that judge by simple petition with a view to accompanying the condemnation with a penalty which shall be, here, immediately final.

The provisions governing maintenance are, for the remainder, applicable to this indemnity.

###### Article 430

The defendant may dismiss the claim, by proving that he could not be the father of the child.

###### Article 431

The burden of maintenance is transmitted to the succession of the debtor within the limits of Articles 216 to 219.

###### Article 432

Articles 420 to 423 above are applicable to the action for maintenance.

###### Article 433

The judgment which awards maintenance creates between the debtor and the beneficiary, as well as, where appropriate, between each of them and the relatives or spouse of the other, the impediments to marriage governed by Articles 161 to 164 of this code.

###### Article 434

The res judicata on the action for maintenance raises no bar to a subsequent action for establishment of paternity.
The award of maintenance shall cease to have effect if the paternal filiation of the child comes to be established subsequently with regard to a person other than the debtor.

### Title IX: Adoptive filiation

Chapter I: Full adoption

##### Section I: Conditions required for full adoption Article 435

Adoption, according to the regime established by the civil code, may be requested after five years of marriage by two spouses not legally separated.

###### Article 436

If the adopter is married and not legally separated, the consent of his spouse is necessary unless that spouse is unable to express his will.

###### Article 437

The adopters must be fifteen years older than the children they propose to adopt. If the latter are the children of their spouse, the required age difference is only ten years.

However, the court may, if there are just grounds, grant the adoption when the age difference is less than those provided for in the preceding paragraph.

###### Article 438

Adoption is permitted only in favour of children under fifteen years of age, received into the home of the adoptive parent or parents for at least six months.
However, if the child is over fifteen years of age and was received before reaching that age by persons who did not meet the legal conditions for adoption or if the child was the subject of a simple adoption before reaching that age, full adoption may be requested, if the conditions are met, throughout the child's minority.

If the child is over thirteen years of age, the adoptee must personally consent to his or her full adoption.

###### Article 439

No person may be adopted by several persons except by two spouses.

However, a new adoption may be pronounced either after the death of the adoptive parent, or of both adoptive parents, or after the death of one of the two adoptive parents, if the application is submitted by the new spouse of the survivor.

###### Article 440

May be adopted:
1° Children for whom the father and mother or the family council have validly consented to the adoption;
2° Children who have been legally entrusted to a duly registered association for at least five years from the date on which consent is given, whose statutory purpose includes the defence or assistance of children and which effectively works in this field. This association must also be recognised by the Ministry of Justice, and communicate a copy of the ministerial order of recognition to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or to the judge delegated for this purpose.
3° Children declared abandoned under the conditions provided for in Article 448.

###### Article 441

When the filiation of a child is established with respect to his or her father and mother, both must consent to the adoption.
If one of them is deceased or unable to express his or her will, if he or she has lost parental authority rights, the consent of the other is sufficient.

###### Article 442

When the filiation of a child is established with respect to only one of his or her parents, that parent gives consent to the adoption.

###### Article 443

When the father and mother of the child are deceased, unable to express their will or if they have lost their parental authority rights, consent is given by the family council, after obtaining the opinion of the person who, in fact, takes care of the child.

The same applies when the filiation of the child is not established.

###### Article 444

Consent to adoption is given before the president of the Civil Chamber of First Instance or the judge delegated for this purpose of the domicile or residence of the person consenting, or before a Djiboutian or foreign notary, or before Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agents. It may also be received by a duly registered association for at least five years from the date on which consent is given, whose statutory purpose includes the defence or assistance of children and which effectively works in this field. This association must also be recognised by the Ministry of Justice, and communicate a copy of the ministerial order of recognition to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or to the judge delegated for this purpose.
Consent to adoption may be retracted within three months. The retraction must be made by any means allowing confirmation of its receipt by the person or service that had received the consent to adoption. The return of the child to his or her parents upon request, even verbal, also constitutes proof of retraction.

If at the expiration of the three-month period, the consent has not been retracted, the parents may still request the return of the child provided that the child has not been placed with a view to adoption. If the person who has received the child refuses to return him or her, the parents may seize the court which assesses, taking into account the interest of the child, whether it is appropriate to order the return. The return renders the consent to adoption null and void.

###### Article 445

The father and mother or the family council may consent to the adoption of the child leaving the choice of the adoptive parent to an association as designated in Article 444 or to an authorised adoption agency which would provisionally receive the child.

###### Article 446

Except in the case where there is a relationship of kinship or affinity up to and including the sixth degree between the adoptive parent and the adoptee, consent to the adoption of children under two years of age is valid only if the child has been effectively handed over to an association as designated in Article 444 or to an authorised adoption agency.

###### Article 447

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may pronounce the adoption if it considers abusive the refusal of consent opposed by the legitimate and natural parents or by only one of them, when they have shown no interest in the child at the risk of compromising his or her health or morality.
The same applies in case of abusive refusal of consent by the family council.

###### Article 448

A child received by a private individual, a private agency or an association as designated in Article 444, whose parents have manifestly shown no interest during the year preceding the filing of the application for declaration of abandonment, may be declared abandoned by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.
Parents who have not maintained with the child the relations necessary for the maintenance of emotional ties are considered to have manifestly shown no interest in their child.
The simple retraction of consent to adoption, the request for news or the intention expressed but not followed by effect to take back the child, is not a sufficient mark of interest to automatically justify the rejection of an application for declaration of abandonment.

Abandonment is not declared if, during the period provided for in the first paragraph of this article, a member of the family has requested to assume responsibility for the child and if this request is deemed to be in the interest of the child.

When it declares the child abandoned, the court delegates by the same decision the parental authority rights over the child to an association as designated in Article 444 or to the private individual guardian of the child.

Third-party opposition is admissible only in case of fraud, deceit or error as to the identity of the child.

##### Section II

Placement with a view to full adoption and judgment of full adoption Article 449
Placement with a view to adoption is carried out by the effective delivery to the prospective adoptive parents of a child for whom consent to adoption has been validly and definitively given, or of a child declared abandoned by judicial decision.

When the filiation of the child is not established, there may be no placement with a view to adoption during a period of three months from the receipt of the child.
Placement may not take place when the parents have requested the return of the child until a decision has been made on the merits of this request at the application of the most diligent party.

###### Article 450

Placement with a view to adoption prevents any return of the child to his or her family of origin. It precludes any declaration of filiation and any acknowledgement.
If the placement with a view to adoption ceases or if the court has refused to pronounce the adoption, the effects of this placement are retroactively resolved.

###### Article 451

Adoption is pronounced upon the application of the adopter by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, which verifies whether the conditions of the law are met and whether the adoption is in the best interest of the child.
In the case where the adopter has descendants, the court further verifies whether the adoption is not of a nature to compromise family life.

If the adopter dies after having lawfully taken in the child with a view to adoption, the application may be presented in his or her name by the surviving spouse or one of the heirs of the adopter.

The judgment pronouncing the adoption is not reasoned.

###### Article 452

Third-party opposition against the adoption judgment is admissible only in case of fraud or deceit attributable to the adopters.

###### Article 453

Within fifteen days from the date on which it becomes final, the decision pronouncing full adoption is transcribed in the civil status registers of the place of birth of the adopted person, at the request of the Public Prosecutor.

The transcription states the day, time and place of birth, the sex of the child as well as his or her given names, as they result from the adoption judgment, the given names, surnames, date and place of birth, profession and domicile of the adopter or adopters. It contains no indication relating to the actual filiation of the child.

The transcription serves as birth certificate for the adopted person.

The original birth certificate and, where applicable, the birth certificate drawn up pursuant to Article 89 are, at the initiative of the Public Prosecutor, endorsed with the mention adoption and considered null and void.

##### Section III : Des effets de l'adoption plénière Article 454

Adoption produces its effects from the day of filing of the application for adoption.

###### Article 455

Adoption confers upon the child a filiation which replaces his or her filiation of origin: the adopted person ceases to belong to his or her family by blood, subject to the prohibitions on marriage referred to in Articles 161 to 164.
However, adoption of the child of the spouse allows his or her filiation of origin to subsist with respect to that spouse and his or her family. It produces, for the remainder, the effects of an adoption by two spouses.

###### Article 456

Adoption confers upon the child the name of the adopter and, in case of adoption by two spouses, the name of the husband.

Upon the request of the adopter or adopters, the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may modify the given names of the child.

If the adopter is a married woman, the Civil Chamber may, in the adoption judgment, deduce from the consent of the adopter's husband that the name of the latter shall be conferred upon the adopted person; if the husband is deceased or unable to express his will, the court assesses at its discretion after having consulted the heirs of the husband or his closest successors.

###### Article 457

The adopted person has, in the family of the adopter, the same rights and the same obligations as a legitimate child.

###### Article 458

Adoption is irrevocable.

#### Chapitre II : De l'adoption simple

##### Section I : Des conditions requises et du jugement Article 459

Simple adoption is permitted regardless of the age of the adopted person.

If the adopted person is over fifteen years of age, he or she must personally consent to the adoption.

###### Article 460

The provisions of Articles 435 to 437, 439 to 448, 451, 452, 454 and 456, last paragraph, are applicable to simple adoption.

###### Article 461

Within fifteen days from the date on which it becomes final, the decision pronouncing simple adoption is mentioned or transcribed in the civil status registers at the request of the Public Prosecutor.

##### Section II : Des effets de l'adoption simple Article 462

Simple adoption confers the name of the adopter upon the adopted person by adding it to the name of the latter. The court may however decide that the adopted person shall bear only the name of the adopter.

###### Article 463

The adopted person remains in his or her family of origin and retains all his or her rights therein, in particular his or her inheritance rights.

The prohibitions on marriage provided for in Articles 173 to 176 of this code apply between the adopted person and his or her family of origin.

###### Article 464

The adopter alone is vested with respect to the adopted person with all the rights of parental authority, including that of consenting to the marriage of the adopted person, unless he or she is the spouse of the father or mother of the adopted person; in that case, the adopter has parental authority concurrently with his or her spouse, but the latter retains the exercise thereof.
The rights of parental authority are exercised by the adopter or adopters under the same conditions as with respect to the legitimate child.
The rules of legal administration and guardianship of the legitimate child apply to the adopted person.

###### Article 465

The relationship of kinship resulting from adoption extends to the legitimate children of the adopted person.

Marriage is prohibited:
1° Between the adopter, the adopted person and his or her descendants;
2° Between the adopted person and the spouse of the adopter; reciprocally between the adopter and the spouse of the adopted person; 3° Between the adoptive children of the same individual;
4° Between the adopted person and the children of the adopter.

Nevertheless, the prohibitions on marriage set out in 3° and 4° above may be lifted by dispensation of the President of the Republic, if there are serious causes.
