The prohibition on marriage set out in 2° above may be lifted under the same conditions when the person who created the affinity is deceased.

###### Article 466

The adopted person owes maintenance to the adopter if he or she is in need and, reciprocally, the adopter owes maintenance to the adopted person.
The obligation to provide maintenance continues to exist between the adopted person and his or her father and mother. However, the father and mother of the adopted person are bound to provide him or her with maintenance only if he or she cannot obtain it from the adopter.

###### Article 467

The adopted person and his or her legitimate descendants have in the family of the adopter the same succession rights as a legitimate child without however acquiring the status of forced heir with respect to the ascendants of the adopter.

###### Article 468

If the adopted person dies without descendants, the property given by the adopter or received in his or her succession returns to the adopter or to his or her descendants, if they still exist in kind at the time of the death of the adopted person, subject to contribution to debts and subject to rights acquired by third parties. The property that the adopted person had received gratuitously from his or her father and mother likewise returns to the latter or to their descendants.
The remainder of the property of the adopted person is divided in half between the family of origin and the family of the adopter, without prejudice to the rights of the spouse over the entire succession.

###### Article 469

Adoption retains all its effects, notwithstanding the subsequent establishment of a filiation link.

###### Article 470

If serious grounds are established, adoption may be revoked, at the request of the adopter or of the adopted person.
The application for revocation made by the adopter is admissible only if the adopted person is over fifteen years of age.
When the adopted person is a minor, the father and mother by blood or, in their absence, a member of the family of origin up to and including the fourth degree, may also apply for revocation.

###### Article 471

The judgment revoking adoption must be reasoned.
The operative part of the judgment is mentioned in the margin of the birth certificate or of the transcription of the adoption judgment, under the conditions provided for in Article 461.

###### Article 472

Revocation terminates for the future all the effects of adoption.

### Titre X : De l'autorité parentale

Chapitre Ier : De l'autorité parentale relativement à la personne de l'enfant

###### Article 473

The child, at any age, owes honour and respect to his or her father and mother.

###### Article 474

He or she remains under their authority until his or her majority or emancipation.

###### Article 475

Authority belongs to the father and mother to protect the child in his or her safety, health and morality. They have the right and duty towards him or her of custody, supervision and education.

###### Article 476

The child may not, without permission of the father and mother, leave the family home and he or she may only be removed from it in cases of necessity as determined by law.

###### Article 477

The father and mother may not, except for serious reasons, obstruct the personal relations of the child with his or her grandparents. In the absence of agreement between the parties, the terms of these relations are settled by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.
In consideration of exceptional situations, the Civil Chamber may grant a right of correspondence or visitation to other persons, whether related or not.

##### Section I : De l'exercice de l'autorité parentale Article 478

During marriage, the father and mother exercise their authority jointly.

###### Article 479

If the father and mother cannot agree on what the interest of the child requires, the practice they may have previously followed on similar occasions shall serve as their rule.
In the absence of such practice or in case of dispute as to its existence or validity, the more diligent spouse may apply to the president of the Court of First Instance or the judge he or she delegates for this purpose, who shall rule after having attempted to reconcile the parties.

###### Article 480

With regard to third parties in good faith, each spouse is deemed to act with the agreement of the other when he or she alone performs a usual act of parental authority relating to the person of the child.

###### Article 481

Loses the exercise of parental authority or is temporarily deprived of it that one of the father and mother who is in one of the following cases:
1° If he or she is unable to express his or her will, by reason of incapacity, absence, remoteness or any other cause;
2° If he or she has consented to a delegation of his or her rights according to the rules established in section III of this chapter; 3° If he or she has been convicted under one of the various heads of family abandonment, as long as he or she has not resumed his or her obligations for a period of at least six months;
4° If a judgment of forfeiture or withdrawal has been pronounced against him or her, for those of his or her rights which have been withdrawn.

###### Article 482

If one of the father and mother dies or is in one of the cases enumerated in the preceding article, the exercise of parental authority is devolved entirely to the other.

###### Article 483

If the father and mother are divorced or legally separated, parental authority is exercised by the one of them to whom the court has entrusted custody of the child, subject to the right of visitation and supervision of the other.
When custody has been entrusted to a third party, the other attributes of parental authority continue to be exercised by the father and mother. But the court, in designating a third party as provisional guardian, may decide that he or she must request the opening of a guardianship.

When ruling, the judge always does so taking into consideration the best interest of the child.

###### Article 484

Divorce or legal separation does not prevent the devolution provided for in article 482, even if the one of the father and mother who remains able to exercise parental authority had been deprived of custody by the effect of the judgment pronounced against him or her.
Nevertheless, the Civil Chamber which had last ruled on custody may always be applied to by the family or by the public prosecutor, in order to designate a third party as guardian of the child, with or without opening of a guardianship, as stated in the preceding article.
In exceptional circumstances, the Civil Chamber ruling on custody of the child after divorce or legal separation may decide, even during the lifetime of the spouses, that it shall not pass to the survivor in case of death of the custodial spouse. It may, in this case, designate the person to whom custody shall be provisionally devolved.

###### Article 485

If there remains neither father nor mother able to exercise parental authority, there shall be grounds for opening a guardianship.

###### Article 486

Concerning the natural child, parental authority is exercised by the one of the father and mother who has voluntarily recognized him or her, if he or she has been recognized by only one of them.
If both have recognized him or her, parental authority is exercised entirely by the mother. The court may, nevertheless, at the request of either one or the other, or of the public prosecutor, decide that it shall be exercised either by the father alone, or by the father and mother jointly, to whom articles 478 to 480 shall then be applicable, as if the child were a legitimate child.

##### Section II : De l'assistance éducative Article 487

If the health, safety or morality of an unemancipated minor is in danger, or if the conditions of his or her education are seriously compromised, educational assistance measures may be ordered by the court at the request of the father and mother jointly, or of one of them, of the guardian or tutor, of the minor himself or herself or of the public prosecutor. The judge may take up the matter on his or her own initiative on an exceptional basis.

These educational assistance measures may be ordered at the same time for several children subject to the same parental authority.

The president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, or the judge he or she delegates for this purpose, has jurisdiction, subject to appeal, for all matters concerning educational assistance.

The president or the delegated judge must always endeavor to obtain the family's agreement to the measure envisaged.

###### Article 489

Whenever possible, the minor must be maintained in his or her current environment. In this case, the judge designates either a qualified person or an association as designated in article 444, giving the designated person or association the mission of providing aid and advice to the family, in order to overcome the material or moral difficulties it encounters. This person or association is responsible for monitoring the development of the child and reporting on it to the judge periodically.
The president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may also make the child's maintenance in his or her environment subject to particular obligations, such as that of regularly attending an educational establishment, or of engaging in a professional activity.

###### Article 490

If it is necessary to remove the child from his or her current environment, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may decide to entrust him or her:
1° To the one of the father and mother who did not have custody;
2° To another member of the family or to a trustworthy third party; 3° To an association as designated in article 444.
However, when a petition for divorce has been filed or a divorce judgment rendered between the father and mother, these measures may only be taken if a new fact likely to result in danger for the minor has been revealed subsequent to the decision ruling on custody of the child. They may not prevent the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge from deciding, by application of article 302, to whom the child must be entrusted. The same rules are applicable to legal separation.

###### Article 491

In the cases specified in paragraphs 1° and 2° of the preceding article, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may instruct a qualified person, an association as designated in Article 444, or an observation, education or re-education service in an open environment, to provide assistance and advice to the guardian as well as to the family and to monitor the development of the child.
In all cases, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may attach to the return of the child the same conditions as under Article 489, paragraph 2. He may also decide that he shall be given periodic reports on the situation of the child.

###### Article 492

On a provisional basis but subject to appeal, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may, during the proceedings, take one of the measures provided for in Articles 490 and 491.
In case of urgency, the public prosecutor of the place where the minor was found has the same power, subject to referring the matter within eight days to the president of the Civil Chamber, who shall maintain, modify or withdraw the measure.

###### Article 493

Decisions taken in matters of educational assistance may be, at any time, modified or withdrawn by the judge who rendered them either on his own motion, or at the request of the father and mother jointly, or of one of them, of the guardian or of the tutor, of the minor himself or of the public prosecutor.

The father and mother whose child has given rise to an educational assistance measure retain their parental authority over him and exercise all the attributes thereof that are not incompatible with the application of the measure. They may not emancipate the child without authorization from the children's judge, as long as the educational assistance measure is being applied.
If it has been necessary to place the child outside his parents' home, they retain a right of correspondence and a right of visit. The judge shall determine the conditions thereof and may, if the interest of the child so requires, decide that the exercise of these rights, or of one of them, shall be provisionally suspended.

###### Article 495

The costs of maintenance and education of the child who has been the subject of an educational assistance measure continue to be borne by his father and mother as well as by the ascendants from whom maintenance may be claimed, except for the power of the judge to discharge them therefrom in whole or in part.

##### Section III: De la délégation de l'autorité parentale Article 496

No renunciation, no assignment relating to parental authority, may have effect, except by virtue of a judgment and in the cases determined below.

###### Article 497

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may, when it is called upon to rule on the custody or education of a minor child, have regard to the agreements that the father and mother may have freely concluded between themselves on this subject, unless one of them justifies serious grounds that would authorize him to revoke his consent.

###### Article 498

The father and mother, together or separately, or the tutor authorized by the family council, may, when they have entrusted the minor child of sixteen years to a trustworthy individual or to an establishment approved for this purpose, or an association as designated in Article 444, renounce in whole or in part the exercise of their authority.
In this case, delegation, total or partial, of parental authority shall result from the judgment that shall be rendered by the Civil Chamber on the joint application of the delegators and the delegatee.

The same delegation may be decided, at the sole request of the delegatee, when the parents have lost interest in the child for more than one year.

###### Article 499

The delegation of parental authority may also take place when the minor of sixteen years has been taken in without the intervention of the father and mother or of the tutor. But it is necessary, in this case, that the individual, the establishment or the association, after having taken in the child, has made a declaration thereof to the administrative authority of the place.
This declaration is made within one week. The administrative authority, within the month that follows, gives notice thereof to the father and mother or to the tutor. The notification that is thus made to them opens a new period of three months at the expiration of which, failing by them to claim the child, they are presumed to renounce exercising their authority over him.

The individual, the establishment or the association that has taken in the child may then present an application to the Civil Chamber for the purpose of having parental authority delegated to it totally or partially.

###### Article 500

The delegation may, in all cases, come to an end or be transferred by a new judgment, if new circumstances are justified.

In the case where the restitution of the child is granted to the father and mother, the Civil Chamber shall charge them, if they are not indigent, with the reimbursement of all or part of the maintenance costs.
When the application for restitution has been rejected, it may not be renewed except after six months from the day on which the decision of rejection became final.

###### Article 501

The right to consent to the adoption of the minor is never delegated.

##### Section IV

De la déchéance et du retrait partiel de l'autorité parentale Article 502
May be deprived of parental authority by an express provision of the criminal judgment the father and mother who are convicted, either as perpetrators, co-perpetrators or accomplices of a crime or offence committed against the person of their child, or as co-perpetrators or accomplices of a crime or offence committed by their child.

This deprivation is applicable to ascendants other than the father and mother for the share of parental authority that may fall to them over their descendants.

###### Article 503

May be deprived of parental authority, outside of any criminal conviction, the father and mother who, either by ill-treatment, or by harmful examples of habitual drunkenness, notorious misconduct or delinquency, or by a lack of care or a lack of direction, manifestly endanger the safety, health or morality of the child.
May likewise be deprived thereof, when an educational assistance measure had been taken with regard to the child, the father and mother who, for more than two years, have voluntarily refrained from exercising the rights and fulfilling the duties that Article 494 left to them.
The action for deprivation is brought before the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, either by the public prosecutor, or by a member of the family or the tutor of the child.

###### Article 504

The deprivation pronounced by virtue of one of the two preceding articles applies by operation of law to all the attributes, both patrimonial and personal, relating to parental authority; in the absence of other determination, it extends to all minor children already born at the time of the judgment.
It entails, for the child, exemption from the maintenance obligation, by way of derogation from Articles 212 to 214, except for a contrary provision in the judgment of deprivation.

###### Article 505

The judgment may, instead of total deprivation, confine itself to pronouncing a partial withdrawal of rights, limited to the attributes that it specifies. It may also decide that the deprivation or the withdrawal shall have effect only with regard to certain of the children already born.

###### Article 506

In pronouncing the deprivation or the withdrawal of the right of custody, the court seized must, if the other parent is deceased or if he has lost the exercise of parental authority, either designate a third party who shall provisionally assume the custody of the child subject to his requesting the organization of the tutorship, or entrust the child to an association as designated in Article 444.

The court seized may take the same measures when parental authority is devolved to one of the parents by the effect of the deprivation pronounced against the other.

###### Article 507

Fathers and mothers who have been subject to forfeiture or withdrawal of rights for one of the causes provided for in Articles 502 and 503, may, by petition, obtain from the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, by demonstrating new circumstances, that all or part of the rights of which they had been deprived be restored to them.
The application for restoration may not be made until six months from the day on which the judgment pronouncing the forfeiture or withdrawal became final; in case of rejection, this application may not be renewed until after a new period of one year. No application shall be admissible when, before the filing of the petition, the child has been placed with a view to adoption.

If restoration is granted, the public prosecutor shall request, where applicable, educational assistance measures.

#### Chapitre II : De l'autorité parentale relativement aux biens de l'enfant Article 508

Fathers and mothers have, subject to the distinctions that follow, the administration and enjoyment of their child's property.

###### Article 509

Legal administration is exercised in accordance with the provisions of Articles 518 et seq. of this code.

###### Article 510

The right of enjoyment ceases:
1° As soon as the child has reached the age of sixteen, or even earlier when he or she contracts marriage;
2° By the causes that terminate parental authority, or even more specifically by those that terminate legal administration;
3° By the causes that bring about the extinction of any usufruct.

###### Article 511

The charges of this enjoyment are:
1° Those to which usufructuaries are generally bound;
2° The food, maintenance and education of the child, according to his or her fortune;
3° The debts encumbering the succession received by the child insofar as they should have been paid from the income.

###### Article 512

This enjoyment shall not take place for the benefit of the surviving spouse who has failed to make an inventory, authentic or under private signature, of the property accruing to the minor.

###### Article 513

Legal enjoyment does not extend to property that the child may acquire through his or her work, nor to property given or bequeathed to him or her on the express condition that the father and mother shall not enjoy it.

### Titre XI : De la minorité, de la tutelle et de l'émancipation

###### Article 514

In this title, whenever mention is made of the judge, it refers to the president of the Court of First Instance or the magistrate he or she has designated.

Chapitre Ier : De la minorité Article 515
A minor is an individual of either sex who has not yet reached the age of eighteen years.

###### Article 516

In any proceedings concerning him or her, a minor capable of discernment may, without prejudice to provisions providing for his or her intervention or consent, be heard by the judge or, when his or her interest so requires, by the person designated by the judge for that purpose.
This hearing is a matter of right when the minor so requests. When the minor refuses to be heard, the judge assesses the merits of this refusal. He or she may be heard alone, with a lawyer or a person of his or her choice.

###### Article 517

The legal administrator represents the minor in all acts of civil life, except in cases where the law or custom authorizes minors to act themselves.

#### Chapitre II : De l'administration légale Article 518

Legal administration belongs to the parents.
If parental authority is exercised jointly by both parents, each of them is a legal administrator. In other cases, legal administration belongs to the parent who exercises parental authority.

###### Article 519

When legal administration is exercised jointly by both parents, each of them is deemed, with respect to third parties, to have received from the other the power to perform alone acts of administration relating to the minor's property.
The list of acts that are regarded as acts of administration is defined by presidential decree.

###### Article 520

When the interests of the sole legal administrator or, as the case may be, of both legal administrators are in conflict with those of the minor, the latter request the appointment of an ad hoc administrator by the judge. In the absence of diligence by the legal administrators, the judge may proceed with this appointment at the request of the public prosecutor, the minor himself or herself or of his or her own motion.
When the interests of one of the two legal administrators are in conflict with those of the minor, the judge may authorize the other legal administrator to represent the child for one or more specified acts.

###### Article 521

Property given or bequeathed to the minor on condition that it be administered by a third party is not subject to legal administration.

The third-party administrator has the powers conferred upon him or her by the donation, the will or, failing that, those of a legal administrator.

When the third-party administrator refuses this function or is legally unable to exercise it, the judge designates an ad hoc administrator to replace him or her.

###### Article 522

The legal administrator is required to exercise prudent, diligent and informed care in the management of the minor's property, in the sole interest of the minor.

###### Article 523

The legal administrator is liable for any damage resulting from any fault he or she commits in the management of the minor's property.
If legal administration is exercised jointly, both parents are jointly and severally liable.

The action for liability is prescribed after five years from the coming of age of the person concerned or from his or her emancipation.

#### Chapitre III : De la tutelle

##### Section I : Des cas d'ouverture et de fin de la tutelle Article 524

Tutorship opens when the father and mother are both deceased or are deprived of the exercise of parental authority.
It also opens with respect to a child whose filiation is not legally established.

###### Article 525

In case of legal administration, the judge may, at any time and for serious cause, either of his or her own motion or at the request of relatives or in-laws or the public prosecutor, decide to open tutorship after having heard or summoned, except in case of urgency, the legal administrator. The latter may not perform any act of disposition from the day he or she is informed of the application and until the final judgment except in case of urgency.
If tutorship is opened, the judge convenes the family council, which may either appoint the legal administrator as tutor or designate another tutor.

###### Article 526

If a child comes to be recognized by one of his or her two parents after the opening of tutorship, the judge may, at the request of that parent, decide to substitute legal administration for tutorship.

###### Article 527

Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 526, tutorship ends upon the emancipation of the minor or upon his or her majority. It also ends in case of a judgment of discharge having become res judicata or in case of death of the person concerned.

##### Section II : De l'organisation et du fonctionnement de la tutelle

###### § 1. Des charges tutélaires

###### Article 528

Tutorship, protection owed to the child, is a public charge. It is a duty of families and the public community.

###### Article 529

The following may not exercise the various charges of tutorship:
1° Unemancipated minors, except if they are the father or mother of the minor under tutorship
2° Adults who benefit from a legal protection measure provided for by this code; 3° Persons from whom parental authority has been withdrawn;
4° Persons who have been prohibited from exercising tutorship charges by court decision.

###### Article 530

Any tutorship duty may be withdrawn by reason of the unfitness, negligence, misconduct or fraud of the person to whom it has been entrusted. The same applies when a dispute or a conflict of interest prevents the holder of the duty from exercising it in the interest of the minor.
Any person to whom a tutorship duty has been entrusted may be replaced in the event of a significant change in their situation or in that of the minor.

###### Article 531

The family council rules on impediments, withdrawals and replacements concerning the tutor.
The judge rules on those concerning the other members of the family council.

A tutorship duty may be withdrawn, by the person who entrusted it, only after its holder has been heard or summoned.
The judge may, if they consider that there is urgency, prescribe provisional measures in the interest of the minor.

###### § 2. Of the family council Article 532

Even in the presence of a testamentary tutor and except in case of vacancy, the tutorship is organized with a family council.

###### Article 533

The judge appoints the members of the family council for the duration of the tutorship.

The family council is composed of at least four members, including the tutor. The judge is not included in this number.
The relatives and in-laws of the minor's father and mother as well as any person, residing in Djibouti or abroad, who shows an interest in the minor may be members of the family council.

The members of the family council are chosen in consideration of the interest of the minor and according to their aptitude, the habitual relations they maintained with the minor's father or mother, the emotional ties they have with the minor as well as their availability.

The judge must avoid, as far as possible, leaving one of the two branches, paternal or maternal, without representation.

###### Article 534

The family council is chaired by the judge. Its deliberations are adopted by vote of its members.

However, the tutor does not vote.

In case of a tie, the judge's vote is decisive.

###### Article 535

The family council settles the general conditions of the maintenance and education of the minor having regard to the wishes that the father and mother may have expressed.
It assesses the allowances that may be granted to the tutor.

It makes the decisions and gives the tutor the necessary authorizations for the management of the minor's property in accordance with the provisions of Title XIII of this code.

###### Article 536

The deliberations of the family council are null and void when they have been obtained by deceit or fraud or when substantial formalities have been omitted.
The action for nullity may be brought by the tutor, the other members of the family council and the public prosecutor within two years of the deliberation as well as by the minor who has become of age or emancipated within two years of their majority or emancipation. The limitation period does not run if there has been deceit or fraud as long as the fact which is at its origin is not discovered.

Acts performed pursuant to an annulled deliberation are annulled upon simple request by any of the persons entitled to act pursuant to the preceding paragraph. However, the period runs from the act and not from the deliberation.

###### § 3. Of the tutor Article 537

The individual right to choose a tutor, whether or not related to the minor, belongs only to the last surviving of the father and mother if they retained, on the day of their death, the exercise of parental authority.
This designation may only be made in the form of a will or a special declaration before a notary.
It is binding on the family council unless the interest of the minor requires that it be set aside. In that case, the family council decides to refer the matter to the judge, who will assess.

The tutor designated by the father or mother is not required to accept the tutorship.

###### Article 538

If there is no testamentary tutor, or if the person designated in that capacity ceases their functions, or refuses the tutorship, the family council appoints a tutor to the minor.

###### Article 539

The family council may, in consideration of the situation of the minor, the aptitudes of the interested parties and the composition of the estate to be administered, appoint several tutors to exercise the protective measure jointly. Each tutor is deemed, with regard to third parties, to have received from the others the power to act alone for acts for which a tutor would not need any authorization.
The family council may decide that the exercise of the tutorship will be divided between a tutor responsible for the person of the minor and a tutor responsible for the management of their property. Unless otherwise decided by the family council, these tutors are independent of each other, and are not responsible to each other. However, they inform each other of the decisions they make

###### Article 540

The tutor is appointed for the duration of the tutorship.

###### Article 541

Tutorship is a personal duty.

It is not transmitted to the heirs of the tutor.

###### Article 542

The tutor takes care of the person of the minor and represents them in all acts of civil life, except in cases where the law or custom authorizes the minor to act themselves.
The tutor represents the minor in court. However, they may not act, as plaintiff or defendant, to assert non-patrimonial rights except after authorization or upon injunction of the family council. The family council may also enjoin the tutor to withdraw from the proceedings or action, or to settle.

The tutor manages the property of the minor and accounts for their management in accordance with the provisions of Title XIII.

###### § 4. Of the vacancy of the tutorship Article 543

The President of the Court of First Instance and the public prosecutor exercise general supervision over the tutorships within their jurisdiction.

Tutors and other tutorship bodies are required to comply with their summons and to communicate to them any information they require.
The judge may issue injunctions against them and impose a civil fine of 50,000 to 200,000 FD on those who have not complied.

###### § 5. Of liability Article 544

All bodies of the tutorship are liable for damage resulting from any fault they commit in the exercise of their function.

When the fault at the origin of the damage was committed in the organization and operation of the tutorship by the judges or the clerk, the action for liability is directed against the State, which has a right of recourse.

###### Article 545

The action for liability is barred after five years from the majority of the interested party, even if the management continued beyond, or from the end of the measure if it ceases before.

#### Chapter IV: Of emancipation Article 546

The minor is emancipated by operation of law by marriage.

###### Article 547

The minor, even if not married, may be emancipated when they have reached the age of sixteen years.

After hearing the minor, this emancipation shall be pronounced, if there are just grounds, by the judge, at the request of the father and mother or one of them.
When the request is made by only one of the parents, the judge decides, after having heard the other parent unless the latter is unable to express their will.

###### Article 548

The minor left without father or mother may be emancipated at the request of the family council, convened by the tutor or by the court at the request of a member of the family council or of the minor themselves. Paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 547 are then applicable.

###### Article 549

The account of the administration, if applicable, or of the tutorship is rendered to the emancipated minor in accordance with the provisions of Title XIII.

###### Article 550

The emancipated minor is capable, like an adult, of all acts of civil life.

However, in order to marry or consent to adoption, he must observe the same rules as if he were not emancipated.

###### Article 551

The emancipated minor ceases to be under the authority of his father and mother.
They are not liable as of right, in their sole capacity as father or mother, for damage he may cause to others subsequent to his emancipation.

###### Article 552

The emancipated minor may not be a merchant.

### Titre XII : De la majorité et des majeurs protégés par la loi

Chapitre Ier : Dispositions générales Article 553
The age of majority is fixed at eighteen years completed; at that age, everyone is capable of exercising the rights which he enjoys.

##### Section I : Des dispositions indépendantes des mesures de protection Article 554

To make a valid act, one must be of sound mind. It is for those who bring an action for nullity on this ground to prove the existence of a mental disorder at the time of the act.

###### Article 555

During his lifetime, the action for nullity belongs only to the person concerned.

After his death, acts done by him, other than inter vivos gifts and wills, may be challenged by his heirs, for unsoundness of mind, only in the following cases:

1° If the act bears in itself proof of a mental disorder;
2° If it was done while the person concerned was placed under safeguard of justice;
3° If an action was brought before his death for the purpose of opening a curatorship or tutorship or for the purpose of family habilitation.
The action for nullity is available within a period of five years, to the person concerned from the cessation of his condition and, after his death, to the heirs, from the day of death.

###### Article 556

A person who has caused damage to another while under the influence of a mental disorder is nonetheless obliged to make reparation.

##### Section II : Des dispositions communes aux majeurs protégés Article 557

Adult persons receive protection of their person and their property that their condition or situation makes necessary according to the procedures provided for in this title.
This protection is established and ensured in respect of individual freedoms, fundamental rights and the dignity of the person.
Its purpose is the interest of the protected person. It promotes, as far as possible, the autonomy of that person. It is a duty of families and the public community.

###### Article 558

The president of the Court of First Instance and the public prosecutor exercise general supervision of protective measures in their jurisdiction. They may visit or have visited the protected persons and those who are the subject of an application for protection, whatever the measure pronounced or sought.
Persons responsible for protection are required to comply with their summons and to communicate to them any information they require.

###### Article 559

The president of the Court of First Instance may issue injunctions against persons responsible for protection and impose a civil fine of 10,000 FD to 100,000 FD on those who have not complied.
He may also remove them from their mission in the event of a characterized failure in the exercise thereof, after having heard them or summoned them.

###### Article 560

Without prejudice to the application of the rules of management of affairs, the death of the protected person puts an end to the mission of the person responsible for protection.

###### Article 561

Persons exercise judicial protective measures without remuneration.
However, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance may authorize, according to the importance of the property managed or the difficulty of exercising the measure, the payment of an allowance to the person responsible for protection. He fixes the amount thereof. This allowance is borne by the protected person.

###### Article 562

All organs of the judicial protective measure are liable for damage resulting from any fault they commit in the exercise of their function.

However, when the person designated as an organ of judicial protection exercises his mission without remuneration, he incurs liability, for acts performed with his assistance, only in the event of fraud or gross negligence.

###### Article 563

When the fault causing the damage was committed in the organization and operation of the protective measure by the judge or the clerk, the action for liability brought by the protected person or person who has been protected or by his heirs is directed against the State, which has a right of recourse.

###### Article 564

The action for liability is prescribed after five years from the end of the protective measure even though the management may have continued beyond.
However, when the curatorship has ceased by the opening of a tutorship measure, the period runs only from the expiration of the latter.

#### Chapitre II

Des mesures de protection juridique des majeurs Section I : Des dispositions générales

###### Article 565

Any person unable to provide for his interests alone by reason of an impairment, medically established, either of his mental faculties or of his bodily faculties such as to prevent the expression of his will, may benefit from a legal protective measure provided for in this chapter.
Unless otherwise provided, the measure is intended for the protection of both the person and the patrimonial interests of that person. It may however be expressly limited to one of these two missions.

###### Article 566

The dwelling of the protected person and the furniture with which it is furnished, whether it is a principal or secondary residence, are kept at the disposal of that person as long as possible.
The power to administer the property mentioned in the first paragraph permits only precarious enjoyment agreements which cease, notwithstanding any provisions or stipulations to the contrary, upon the return of the protected person to his dwelling.

If it becomes necessary or if it is in the interest of the protected person that the rights relating to his dwelling or his furniture be disposed of by alienation, termination or conclusion of a lease, the act is authorized by the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, by the president of the Court of First Instance, without prejudice to the formalities that the nature of the property may require. If the purpose of the act is the reception of the person concerned in an establishment, the prior opinion of a doctor, not exercising a function or occupying a position in that establishment, is required. In all cases, souvenirs, objects of a personal nature, those essential for disabled persons or intended for the care of sick persons are kept at the disposal of the person concerned, where appropriate by the care of the establishment in which he is accommodated.


This excerpt sits under: RÉPUBLIQUE DE DJIBOUTI > LIVRE I : DES PERSONNES > Titre XI : De la minorité, de la tutelle et de l'émancipation > Chapitre IV : De l'émancipation Article 546

###### Article 567

The person responsible for the protective measure may not proceed with the modification of accounts or passbooks opened in the name of the protected person, nor with the opening of another account or passbook with a bank or any other organization legally authorized to receive funds from the public. The family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance may however authorize it if the interest of the protected person so requires.

A special account is opened in the name of the protected person with a local bank by the person responsible for the protection if the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance deems it necessary.
When the protected person holds no account or passbook, the person responsible for the protective measure opens one for them.

Banking operations for collection, payment and asset management carried out in the name and on behalf of the protected person are performed exclusively by means of accounts opened in the name of the protected person; the fruits, products and capital gains generated by the funds and securities belonging to the protected person accrue exclusively to them.
If the protected person has been subject to a prohibition on issuing checks, the person responsible for the protective measure may nevertheless, with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the president of the Court of First Instance, operate under their signature the accounts of which the protected person is the holder and have access to all usual means of payment.

##### Section II: Provisions common to judicial measures Article 568

The protective measure may be ordered by the judge only in case of necessity and when the interests of the person cannot be sufficiently provided for by the application of either the rules of common law of representation, or those relating to the respective rights and duties of spouses and the rules of matrimonial regimes, or by another less restrictive judicial protective measure.

The measure is proportionate and individualized according to the degree of impairment of the personal faculties of the person concerned.

###### Article 569

A judicial protective measure may be opened for an emancipated minor as well as for an adult.

For a non-emancipated minor, the application may be filed and adjudicated in the last year of their minority. The judicial protective measure takes effect, however, only from the day of their majority.

###### Article 570

The application for opening of the measure may be presented to the judge by the person who needs to be protected or, as the case may be, by their spouse, or by a relative or in-law, a person maintaining close and stable ties with the adult, or the person exercising legal protective measures over them.
It may also be presented by the public prosecutor either on their own initiative or at the request of a third party.

###### Article 571

The application must be accompanied, on pain of inadmissibility, by a detailed certificate drafted by a doctor chosen from the list of judicial experts provided for in Article L.356-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This doctor may seek the opinion of the treating physician of the person who needs to be protected.

###### Article 572

The judge rules after the person has been heard or summoned. The person concerned may be accompanied by a lawyer or, subject to the judge's agreement, by any other person of their choice.
The judge may however, by specially reasoned decision and on the advice of a doctor registered on the list mentioned in Article 571, decide that there is no need to proceed with the hearing of the person concerned if such hearing is likely to harm their health or if they are unable to express their will.

##### Section III: Safeguard of justice Article 573

The judge may place under safeguard of justice the person who, for one of the causes provided for in Article 565, needs temporary legal protection or to be represented for the performance of certain specified acts.

This measure may also be pronounced by the judge, seized of curatorship or guardianship proceedings, for the duration of the proceedings.

###### Article 574

The person placed under safeguard of justice retains the exercise of their rights. However, they may not, on pain of nullity, perform an act for which a special agent has been designated pursuant to Article 576.
The acts they have performed and the commitments they have entered into during the duration of the measure may be annulled for simple lesion or reduced in case of excess. The courts take into account in particular the usefulness or uselessness of the transaction, the importance or consistency of the protected person's assets and the good or bad faith of those with whom they have contracted.

The action for nullity or reduction belongs only to the protected person and, after their death, to their heirs. It is extinguished by the period of five years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling them to exercise it.

###### Article 575

The mandate by which the protected person has entrusted another person with the administration of their property continues to produce its effects during the safeguard of justice unless it is revoked or suspended by the president of the Court of First Instance; the agent being heard or summoned.
In the absence of a mandate, the rules of management of affairs are applicable.

Those who have standing to request the opening of a curatorship or guardianship are required to perform the conservatory acts essential to the preservation of the protected person's assets as soon as they become aware both of their urgency and of the opening of the protective measure. The same provisions are applicable to the person or establishment that accommodates the person placed under safeguard.

###### Article 576

If there is need to act outside the cases defined in Article 570, any interested party may give notice thereof to the judge.

The judge may designate a special agent for the purpose of performing one or more specified acts, even acts of disposition, made necessary by the management of the protected person's assets.
The special agent is required to account for the execution of their mandate to the protected person and to the judge under the conditions provided for in Articles 639 to 644.

###### Article 577

The special agent may also be entrusted with a mission to protect the person in accordance with Articles 595 to 600.

###### Article 578

On pain of lapse, the safeguard of justice measure may not exceed one year, renewable once under the conditions set out in the fourth paragraph of Article 581.
The judge may, at any time, order its lifting if the need for temporary protection ceases.

In the absence of lifting, the safeguard of justice ends upon expiration of the period or after the performance of the acts for which it was ordered. It also ends with the opening of a curatorship or guardianship measure from the day the new legal protective measure takes effect.

##### Section IV: On curatorship and guardianship Article 579

A person who, without being incapable of acting themselves, needs, for one of the causes provided for in Article 565, to be assisted or supervised in a continuous manner in important acts of civil life may be placed under curatorship.
Curatorship is only ordered if it is established that safeguard of justice cannot ensure sufficient protection.

A person who, for one of the causes provided for in Article 565, must be represented in a continuous manner in acts of civil life, may be placed under guardianship.
Guardianship is only ordered if it is established that neither safeguard of justice nor curatorship can ensure sufficient protection.

###### Subsection 1: On the duration of the measure Article 580

The President of the Court of First Instance sets the duration of the measure without it being able to exceed five years.

The judge who orders a guardianship measure may, by specially reasoned decision and on the conforming opinion of a doctor registered on the list of judicial experts in accordance with Article L.356-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure finding that the alteration of the personal faculties of the person concerned described in Article 565 does not manifestly appear likely to experience improvement according to acquired scientific data, set a longer duration, not exceeding ten years.

###### Article 581

The judge may renew the measure for the same duration.

However, when the alteration of the personal faculties of the person concerned described in Article 565 does not manifestly appear likely to experience improvement according to acquired scientific data, the judge may, by specially reasoned decision and on the conforming opinion of a doctor registered on the list mentioned in Article 571, renew the measure for a longer duration that they determine, not exceeding twenty years.
The judge may, at any time, terminate the measure, modify it or substitute another measure provided for in this title, after having obtained the opinion of the person responsible for the protection measure.
They rule of their own motion or at the request of one of the persons mentioned in Article 570, in view of a medical certificate and under the conditions provided for in Article 572. However, they may only strengthen the protection regime of the person concerned if they are seized with a request to that effect satisfying Articles 570 and 571.

###### Article 582

The measure ends, in the absence of renewal, upon expiration of the set period, in case of a judgment of discharge having become res judicata or in case of death of the person concerned.
The judge may also terminate it when the protected person resides outside the national territory, if this distance prevents the monitoring and supervision of the measure.

###### Subsection 2: On publicity of the measure Article 583

Judgments ordering the opening, modification or discharge of curatorship or guardianship are only enforceable against third parties two months after the mention has been made in the margin of the birth certificate of the protected person according to the procedures provided for by the Code of Civil Procedure.

However, even in the absence of this mention, they are enforceable against third parties who have personal knowledge of them.

###### Subsection 3: On protection bodies Article 584

Curatorship and guardianship duties are subject to the conditions provided for guardianship duties of minors by Articles 529 to 531. However, the powers conferred by Article 531 on the family council are exercised by the judge in the absence of constitution of this body.

Members of the medical and pharmacy professions, as well as medical auxiliaries may not exercise a curatorship or guardianship duty with respect to their patients.
The fiduciary designated by the fiduciary contract may not exercise a curatorship or guardianship duty with respect to the settlor.

###### § 1. On the curator and the guardian Article 585

A curator or a guardian is designated for the protected person under the conditions provided for in this paragraph and subject to the powers conferred on the family council if it has been constituted.

###### Article 586

The curator or the guardian is designated by the judge.

The latter may, in consideration of the situation of the protected person, the aptitudes of the persons concerned and the consistency of the patrimony to be administered, designate several curators or several guardians to exercise the protection measure jointly. Each curator or guardian is deemed, with respect to third parties, to have received from the others the power to act alone for acts for which a guardian would not need any authorization.
The judge may divide the protection measure between a curator or a guardian responsible for the protection of the person and a curator or a guardian responsible for patrimonial management.
Unless the judge has decided otherwise, the persons designated pursuant to the preceding paragraph are independent of each other, and are not responsible to each other. However, they inform each other of the decisions they make.

###### Article 587

The designation by a person of one or more persons responsible for exercising the functions of curator or guardian in the event that they are placed under curatorship or guardianship is binding on the judge, unless the designated person refuses the mission or is unable to exercise it, or if the interest of the protected person requires their exclusion. In case of difficulty, the judge rules.
The same applies when the parents or the last surviving of the father and mother, not subject to a curatorship or guardianship measure, who exercise parental authority over their minor child or assume the material and emotional care of their adult child designate one or more persons responsible for exercising the functions of curator or guardian from the day when they themselves die or can no longer continue to care for the person concerned.

###### Article 588

In the absence of designation made pursuant to Article 587, the judge appoints, as curator or guardian, the spouse of the protected person, unless common life has ceased between them or another cause prevents entrusting them with the measure.
In the absence of appointment made pursuant to the preceding paragraph and subject to the last reservation mentioned therein, the judge designates a relative, a person related by marriage or a person residing with the protected adult or maintaining close and stable ties with them.

The judge takes into consideration the feelings expressed by the latter, their usual relationships, the interest shown in them and any recommendations of their relatives and persons related by marriage as well as their entourage.

###### Article 589

When no family member or close person can assume the curatorship or guardianship, the judge designates a judicial representative for the protection of adults. This representative may not refuse to perform urgent acts required by the interest of the protected person, in particular indispensable conservatory acts for the preservation of their patrimony.

###### Article 590

If the interest of the person accommodated or cared for in a health establishment justifies it, the judge may designate, as curator or guardian, a person or a service agent of the establishment registered on the list of judicial representatives for the protection of adults.
The mission entrusted to the representative extends to the protection of the person, unless otherwise decided by the judge.

###### Article 591

No one is required to retain the curatorship or guardianship of a person beyond five years, with the exception of the spouse, the children of the person concerned as well as judicial representatives for the protection of adults.

###### § 2. Of the ad hoc curator and the ad hoc guardian

###### Article 592

The curator or guardian whose interests are, on the occasion of an act or a series of acts, in opposition with those of the protected person or who cannot provide assistance or act on their behalf due to the limitations of their mission, shall have appointed by the judge or by the family council if one has been constituted an ad hoc curator or guardian, that is to say a curator or guardian for the act or series of acts in question.
This appointment may also be made at the request of the Public Prosecutor, any interested party or of the court's own motion.

###### § 3. Of the family council for adults under guardianship Article 593

The judge may organize the guardianship with a family council if the necessities of protecting the person or the extent of their estate justify it and if the composition of their family and entourage permit it.
The judge appoints the members of the family council in consideration of the feelings expressed by the protected person, their usual relationships, the interest shown towards them and any recommendations from their relatives and in-laws as well as their entourage.

The family council appoints the guardian, and, where applicable, the ad hoc guardian in accordance with articles 584 to 591.
The rules prescribed for the family council of minors apply, with the exception of those provided for in article 532, in the fourth paragraph of article 533 and in the first paragraph of article 535. For the application of the third paragraph of article 536, the time limit runs, when the action is brought by the protected adult, from the day the protection measure ends.

###### Article 594

The judge may authorize the family council to meet and deliberate outside their presence, when the latter has appointed a judicial representative for the protection of adults as guardian. The family council then appoints a president and a secretary from among its members, excluding the guardian.
The president of the family council transmits to the judge in advance the agenda of each meeting.

The decisions taken by the family council only take effect in the absence of opposition filed by the judge, under the conditions set by the code of civil procedure.
The president exercises the duties assigned to the judge for the convening, meeting and deliberation of the family council. The judge may however, at any time, convene a meeting of the family council under their presidency.

###### Sous-section 4

Of the effects of curatorship and guardianship as regards the protection of the person Article 595
The protected person receives from the person responsible for their protection, according to methods adapted to their condition and without prejudice to the information that third parties are required to provide them by virtue of the law, all

information about their personal situation, about the acts that the person responsible for their protection wishes to carry out, their usefulness, their degree of urgency, their effects and the consequences of a refusal on their part.

###### Article 596

Subject to the special provisions provided for by law, the performance of acts whose nature implies a strictly personal consent can never give rise to assistance or representation of the protected person.

The declaration of birth of a child, their recognition, acts of parental authority relating to the person of a child, the declaration of the choice or change of name of a child and the consent given to their own adoption or to that of their child are deemed strictly personal.

###### Article 597

Except in the cases provided for in article 596, the protected person alone makes decisions relating to their person to the extent that their condition permits.
When the condition of the protected person does not allow them to make an informed personal decision alone, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance may provide that they will benefit, for all acts relating to their person or those among them that it enumerates, from the assistance of the person responsible for their protection. In the event that this assistance would not suffice, that same person may, if necessary after the opening of a guardianship measure, authorize the guardian to represent the interested party.

However, except in an emergency, the person responsible for the protection of the adult may not, without the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the president of the Court of First Instance, make a decision having the effect of seriously affecting the bodily integrity of the protected person or the privacy of their private life.

The person responsible for the protection of the adult may take with regard to them the protection measures strictly necessary to put an end to the danger that their own behavior would pose to the interested party.
They inform the family council without delay and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 598

The protected person chooses the place of their residence.

They freely maintain personal relationships with any third party, whether related or not. They have the right to be visited and, where applicable, accommodated by them.

In case of difficulty, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance rules.

###### Article 599

The marriage of a person under curatorship is permitted only with the authorization of the curator or, failing that, that of the judge.
The marriage of a person under guardianship is permitted only with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the president of the Court of First Instance, and after hearing of the future spouses by the judge.

The opinion of the parents and entourage is possibly obtained by the judge.

###### Article 600

At the opening of the measure or, failing that, subsequently, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the president of the Court of First Instance decides on the conditions under which the curator or guardian responsible for a mission of protection of the person accounts for the diligence they accomplish in this capacity.

###### Sous-section 5 : Of the regularity of acts Article 601

The obligations resulting from acts performed by the protected person less than two years before the publication of the judgment opening the protection measure may be reduced on the sole proof that their inability to defend their interests, as a result of the impairment of their personal faculties, was notorious or known to the contracting party at the time the acts were entered into.

These acts may, under the same conditions, be annulled if it is proven that the protected person suffered prejudice.
By way of derogation from article 2387, the action must be brought within five years from the date of the judgment opening the measure.


This excerpt sits under: RÉPUBLIQUE DE DJIBOUTI > LIVRE I : DES PERSONNES > Titre XII : De la majorité et des majeurs protégés par la loi > Chapitre II > Section IV : De la curatelle et de la tutelle Article 579

###### Article 602

From the publication of the opening judgment, irregularity of acts performed by the protected person or by the person responsible for the protection is sanctioned under the following conditions:
1° If the protected person has performed alone an act that he or she could do without the assistance or representation of the person responsible for his or her protection, the act remains subject to the actions for nullity or reduction provided for in Article 574 as if it had been performed by a person placed under safeguard of justice, unless it has been expressly authorized by the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance.
2° If the protected person has performed alone an act for which he or she should have been assisted, the act may be annulled only if it is established that the protected person has suffered harm;
3° If the protected person has performed alone an act for which he or she should have been represented, the act is null and void by operation of law without it being necessary to prove harm;
4° If the guardian or curator has performed alone an act that should have been done by the protected person either alone or with his or her assistance or that could only be performed with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance, the act is null and void by operation of law without it being necessary to prove harm.
The curator or guardian may, with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance, bring alone the action for nullity or reduction of the acts provided for in 1°, 2° and 3°.
In all cases, the action is extinguished by the period of five years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling him or her to exercise it.
During this period and as long as the protection measure is open, the act provided for in 4° may be confirmed with the authorization of the judge or the family council if it has been constituted.

###### Article 603

Articles 601 and 602 do not preclude the application of Articles 554 and 555.

###### Sous-section 6 : Des actes faits dans la curatelle Article 604

The person under curatorship may not, without the assistance of the curator, perform any act which, in the case of guardianship, would have required authorization from the judge or the family council.

When concluding a written act, the assistance of the curator is manifested by the affixing of his or her signature next to that of the protected person. If the latter does not know how to sign, the act bears his or her fingerprint.
On pain of nullity, any service of process made on the protected person must also be made on the curator.

###### Article 605

Capital due to the person under curatorship is paid directly into an account opened in his or her name alone and indicating his or her protection regime, with an establishment authorized to receive funds from the public.
The person under curatorship may not, without the assistance of the curator, use his or her capital. This assistance is also required to bring legal action or defend in it.

###### Article 606

The curator may not substitute himself or herself for the person under curatorship to act in his or her name.

However, the curator may, if he or she finds that the person under curatorship is seriously compromising his or her interests, refer the matter to the judge to be authorized to perform alone a specific act or to initiate the opening of guardianship.
If the curator refuses his or her assistance for an act for which his or her cooperation is required, the person under curatorship may ask the judge for authorization to perform it alone.

###### Article 607

The person under curatorship may freely make a will subject to the provisions of Article 554. He or she may make a donation only with the assistance of the curator.
The curator is deemed to be in conflict of interest with the protected person when he or she is the beneficiary of the donation.

###### Article 608

At any time, the judge may, by way of derogation from Article 604, list certain acts that the person under curatorship has the capacity to perform alone or, conversely, add other acts to those for which the assistance of the curator is required.

###### Article 609

The judge may also, at any time, order a reinforced curatorship. In this case, the curator alone receives the income of the person under curatorship in an account opened in the name of the latter. He or she personally ensures the settlement of expenses with third parties and deposits the surplus in an account left at the disposal of the person concerned or pays it into his or her hands.
Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 598, the judge may authorize the curator to conclude alone a residential lease or an accommodation agreement ensuring the housing of the protected person.
Reinforced curatorship is subject to the provisions of Articles 630 and 639 to 644.

###### Sous-section 7 : Des actes faits dans la tutelle Article 610

Subject to cases where the law or custom authorizes the person under guardianship to act himself or herself, the guardian represents him or her in all acts of civil life.

However, the judge may, in the opening judgment or subsequently, list certain acts that the person under guardianship will have the capacity to perform alone or with the assistance of the guardian.

###### Article 611

The person under guardianship is represented in acts necessary for the management of his or her patrimony under the conditions and according to the procedures provided for in Title XIII.

###### Article 612

The person under guardianship is represented in court by the guardian.

The guardian may not act, as plaintiff or defendant, to assert the extra-patrimonial rights of the protected person except after authorization or upon order of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance.
The judge or the family council may also order the guardian to withdraw from the proceedings or action or to settle.

###### Article 613

The person under guardianship may, with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance, be assisted or if necessary represented by the guardian to make donations.
He or she may not make his or her will alone after the opening of the guardianship except with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance, this on pain of nullity of the act. The guardian may neither assist nor represent him or her on this occasion.
However, he or she may alone revoke the will made before or after the opening of the guardianship.

The will made prior to the opening of the guardianship remains valid unless it is established that, since this opening, the cause that had determined the testator to dispose has disappeared.

##### Section V : De l'habilitation familiale Article 614

When a person is unable to express his or her will for one of the causes provided for in Article 565, the judge may authorize one or more persons chosen from among his or her ascendants or descendants, brothers and sisters or, unless the community of life has ceased between them, the spouse or cohabitant to represent him or her or to perform one or more acts in his or her name under the conditions and according to the procedures provided for in this section and those of Title XV of Book III of this code.
The authorized person must meet the conditions for exercising guardianship duties. He or she exercises his or her mission free of charge.

###### Article 615

Family authorization may be ordered by the judge only in case of necessity and when the interests of the person cannot be sufficiently provided for by the application of either the rules of common law of representation, or those relating to the respective rights and duties of spouses and the rules of matrimonial regimes, or by another less restrictive judicial protection measure.

###### Article 616

The application for the designation of an authorized person may be submitted to the judge by one of the persons mentioned in Article 614 or by the public prosecutor at the request of one of them.

The application is filed, examined and adjudicated in accordance with the rules of the Code of Civil Procedure and in compliance with the provisions of Articles 569 and 571.

###### Article 617

The person in respect of whom authorization is sought is heard or summoned according to the procedures provided for in the first paragraph of Article 572. However, the judge may, by specially reasoned decision and on the advice of the doctor mentioned in Article 571, decide that there is no need to proceed with their hearing if it is likely to harm their health or if the person is unable to express themselves.
The judge ensures the consent or, failing that, the absence of legitimate opposition to the authorization measure and to the choice of the authorized person from the relatives mentioned in Article 614 who maintain close and stable ties with the person or who show interest in them and whose existence is known to the judge at the time of ruling.

###### Article 618

The judge rules on the choice of the authorized person and the scope of the authorization by ensuring that the proposed arrangement is in accordance with the property interests and, where applicable, personal interests of the person concerned.

###### Article 619

The authorization may cover:
1° one or more of the acts that the guardian has the power to perform, alone or with authorization, on the property of the person concerned;
2° one or more acts relating to the person to be protected. In this case, the authorization is exercised in compliance with the provisions of Articles 595 to 598 of this Code.

The authorized person may perform an act of gratuitous disposition only with the authorization of the judge.
If the interest of the person to be protected so requires, the judge may issue a general authorization covering all acts or one of the two categories of acts mentioned in points 1° and 2° of this article.

###### Article 620

The authorized person may, unless the judge decides otherwise, proceed without authorization to the acts mentioned in the first paragraph of Article 567.

###### Article 621

If the person in respect of whom authorization has been issued performs alone an act whose performance has been entrusted to the authorized person, it is null and void by operation of law without the need to prove prejudice.
Obligations resulting from acts performed by a person in respect of whom a family authorization measure was pronounced less than two years before the judgment issuing the authorization may be reduced or annulled under the conditions provided for in Article 601.
The authorized person may, with the authorization of the judge, bring alone the action for nullity or reduction provided for in the above paragraphs.
If the authorized person performs alone, in that capacity, an act not falling within the scope of the authorization issued to them or which could only be performed with the authorization of the judge, the act is null and void by operation of law without the need to prove prejudice.

In all cases, the action for nullity or reduction is brought within five years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling them to bring it. During

this period and as long as the authorization measure is in effect, the contested act may be confirmed with the authorization of the judge.

###### Article 622

The judge rules at the request of one of the persons mentioned in Article 614 or the public prosecutor on difficulties that may arise in the implementation of the arrangement.
Seized for this purpose under the conditions provided for in the first paragraph of Article 616, the judge may, at any time, modify the scope of the authorization or terminate it, after having heard or summoned, on the one hand, the person in respect of whom the authorization has been issued, under the conditions provided for in the first paragraph of Article 617 and, on the other hand, the authorized person.

###### Article 623

In addition to the death of the person in respect of whom the family authorization has been issued, this family authorization terminates:
1° By the placement of the person concerned under safeguard of justice, under curatorship or under guardianship;
2° In case of a judgment of discharge having become res judicata pronounced by the judge at the request of one of the persons mentioned in Article 614 or the public prosecutor, when it appears that the conditions provided for in that article are no longer met or when the execution of the family authorization is likely to harm the interests of the protected person;
3° By operation of law in the absence of renewal upon expiration of the fixed period;
4° After the performance of the acts for which the authorization had been issued.

### Titre XIII

Management of the property of minors and adults under guardianship Chapter I: Procedures for management

###### Article 624

The guardian represents the protected person in acts necessary for the management of their property.
They are required to exercise prudent, diligent and informed care in such management, solely in the interest of the protected person.

The list of acts that are regarded, for the application of this title, as acts of administration relating to the current management of property and as acts of disposition that commit it in a lasting and substantial manner is fixed by decree.

###### Article 625

Capital due to the protected person is paid directly into an account opened in their name alone and mentioning the guardianship measure, with a bank or any other organization that may legally receive funds from the public.

###### Article 626

Third parties may inform the judge of acts or omissions by the guardian that appear to them likely to harm the interests of the protected person. In this title, each time the judge is mentioned, it refers to the President of the Court of First Instance or the magistrate they have designated.
These third parties are not guarantors of the use of capital. However, if in connection with such use they become aware of acts or omissions that manifestly compromise the interest of the protected person, they notify the judge.

Third-party opposition to authorizations of the family council or the judge may only be exercised by creditors of the protected person and in case of fraud against their rights.

##### Section unique: Decisions of the family council or the judge Article 627

The guardian establishes the guardianship budget by determining, according to the importance of the protected person's property and the operations involved in their management, the sums annually necessary for the maintenance of that person and the reimbursement of the costs of administering their property. The guardian informs the family council or, failing that, the judge. In case of difficulties, the budget is established by the family council or, failing that, by the judge.

The family council or, failing that, the judge may authorize the guardian to include in the management costs the remuneration of particular administrators whose assistance they request under their own responsibility.
The family council or, failing that, the judge may authorize the guardian to enter into a contract for the management of securities and financial instruments of the protected person. They choose the contracting third party in consideration of their professional experience and solvency. The contract may, at any time and notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, be terminated on behalf of the protected person.

###### Article 628

The family council or, failing that, the judge determines the amount from which the obligation to invest liquid capital and excess income begins for the guardian.
