Thus the servitude of drawing water from another's fountain necessarily carries with it the right of passage.

##### Section III

Rights of the owner of the land to which the servitude is due Article 804
The person to whom a servitude is due has the right to carry out all works necessary to use it and to preserve it.

###### Article 805

These works are at his expense, and not at the expense of the owner of the servient land, unless the title establishing the servitude provides otherwise.

###### Article 806

Even in the case where the owner of the servient land is charged by the title to carry out at his expense the works necessary for the use or preservation of the servitude, he may always free himself from the charge by abandoning the servient land to the owner of the land to which the servitude is due.

###### Article 807

If the land for which the servitude was established comes to be divided, the servitude remains due for each portion, without however the condition of the servient land being aggravated.
Thus, for example, if it concerns a right of passage, all the co-owners shall be obliged to exercise it by the same place.

###### Article 808

The owner of the land subject to the servitude may not do anything that tends to diminish its use or to make it more inconvenient.
Thus, he may not change the state of the premises, nor transfer the exercise of the servitude to a place different from that where it was originally assigned.

But however, if this original assignment had become more onerous to the owner of the servient land, or if it prevented him from making advantageous repairs thereto, he could offer to the owner of the other land a place equally convenient for the exercise of his rights, and the latter could not refuse it.

###### Article 809

For his part, the person who has a right of servitude may only use it in accordance with his title, without being able to make, either in the land that owes the servitude or in the land to which it is due, any change that aggravates the condition of the former.

##### Section IV: How servitudes are extinguished Article 810

Servitudes cease when things are in such a state that they can no longer be used.

They revive if things are restored in such a manner that they can be used.

###### Article 811

Any servitude is extinguished when the land to which it is due and the land that owes it are united in the same hand.

###### Article 812

The servitude is extinguished by non-use for thirty years, unless it is registered in the Land Register.

The period begins to run from the day on which the holder of the dominant land ceased to enjoy it, in the case of discontinuous servitudes, and from the day on which an act contrary to the servitude was performed, in the case of continuous servitudes.

###### Article 813

If the land in favour of which the servitude is established belongs to several persons in undivided ownership, the enjoyment by one prevents extinctive prescription with regard to all.
If, among the co-owners, there is one against whom prescription could not run, such as a minor, he shall have preserved the right of all the others.

## BOOK III. THE DIFFERENT WAYS IN WHICH PROPERTY IS ACQUIRED

General provisions

###### Article 814

Ownership of property is acquired and transferred by succession, by inter vivos or testamentary donation, by the effect of obligations, by accession or incorporation, by occupation, by tradition, by prescription, or any other mode of acquisition provided for by law.

Title I: Successions
Chapter I: Opening of successions and seisin of heirs Article 815
Successions open, upon death, at the last domicile of the deceased.

They are devolved, when the deceased has not disposed of his property by liberalities or will, according to the present provisions of the civil code whenever the spouses have opted for the civil code regime at the time of their marriage or an unmarried person has expressed his or her wish to the civil registrar. Liberalities and wills are authorized to the extent compatible with the hereditary reserve.

The provisions of this title apply to the succession of a person subject to bankruptcy proceedings, subject to the special provisions provided for in this area.

###### Article 816

Agreements that have the purpose of creating rights or renouncing rights over all or part of a succession not yet open or of property dependent thereon produce effect only in cases where they are authorized by law.

###### Article 817

The law regulates the order of succession among the different heirs and the surviving spouse.

Universal legatees and donees are seised under the conditions provided for in Title II, Inter vivos donations and wills, of this book.
In their absence, the succession is acquired by the State.

###### Article 818

Heirs and the surviving spouse are vested by operation of law with the property, rights and actions of the deceased, subject to the obligation to discharge all the charges of the succession.
The State must be sent into possession.

###### Article 819

The provisions of this title, in particular those concerning indivision and partition, apply as appropriate to universal legatees and legatees by universal title, or donees by universal title, when not derogated from by a particular rule.

#### Chapter II

Qualifications required to inherit - Proof of the status of heir

##### Section I: Qualifications required to inherit Article 820

To inherit, it is necessary to exist at the moment of the opening of the succession or, having already been conceived, to be born viable.
A person whose absence is presumed within the meaning of articles 142 et seq. may inherit.

###### Article 821

Where several persons who had a vocation to inherit from one another perish in the same event, the order of deaths is established by all means.
Persons who die without it being possible to establish which survived the other are deemed to have died at the same instant, if at least one of them is called to the succession of the other.
The succession of each of them is then devolved to the persons who would have been called to receive it in their default.

###### Article 822

The following are unworthy to inherit, and, as such, excluded from successions:
1° A person who is convicted of having, alone or with others, voluntarily caused or attempted to cause the death of the deceased;
2° A person who is convicted of having, alone or with others, voluntarily inflicted blows or violence resulting in the death of the deceased, without intention to cause it;
3° A person who is convicted of having voluntarily refrained from preventing the commission of an offence against the bodily integrity of the deceased resulting in death, when he could have done so without risk to himself or to third parties;
4° A person who, in criminal proceedings, has brought against the deceased an accusation or testimony found to be false or defamatory;

5° An heir of full age who, having been informed of the murder of the deceased, has not reported it to the authorities. However, failure to report may not be invoked against ascendants and descendants of the murderer, nor against his relatives in the same degree, nor against his spouse, nor against his brothers or sisters, nor against his uncles and aunts, nor against his nephews and nieces.

###### Article 823

Where, by reason of their death, criminal proceedings could not be pursued to their conclusion against persons who committed the acts mentioned in 1° and 2°, they may nevertheless be declared unworthy by the court on application by any heir and, failing that, by the public prosecutor. The application must be made within six months of the death.

###### Article 824

Where the deceased, subsequent to the facts constituting the cause of unworthiness, became aware of them and expressly stated, in testamentary form, that he intended to maintain the heir in his rights or made him a universal or universal title liberality, that successor affected by a cause of unworthiness is not excluded from the succession.

###### Article 825

The heir excluded from the succession on grounds of unworthiness is bound to return all fruits and all revenues of which he has had enjoyment since the opening of the succession.

###### Article 826

The children of the unworthy person are not excluded by the fault of their author, whether they come to the succession in their own right, or by the effect of representation; but the unworthy person may not, in any case, claim, over the property of that succession, the usufruct that the law grants to fathers and mothers over the property of their children.

##### Section II: Proof of the status of heir Article 827

Proof of the status of heir is established by all means.
This does not derogate from usages concerning the delivery of certificates of ownership or inheritance by judicial or administrative authorities.

###### Article 828

Proof of the status of heir may result from a certificate of notoriety drawn up by a notary, at the request of one or more persons entitled.
The certificate of notoriety must refer to the death certificate of the person whose succession is open and mention the supporting documents that could be produced, such as civil status documents and, where applicable, documents concerning the existence of liberalities mortis causa that may have an impact on succession devolution.

It contains the affirmation, signed by the person or persons entitled who are the authors of the application, that they have a vocation, alone or with others whom they designate, to receive all or part of the succession of the deceased.

Any person whose statements would appear useful may be called to the act.
Mention is made of the existence of the certificate of notoriety in the margin of the death certificate.

###### Article 829

The certificate of notoriety thus established is evidence until proof to the contrary.

A person who relies on it is presumed to have hereditary rights in the proportion indicated therein, and the heirs designated in the certificate of notoriety or their common agent are deemed, in relation to third parties holding property of the succession, to have free disposal of such property and, in the case of funds, free disposal thereof in the proportion indicated in the act.
The certificate of notoriety does not, in itself, entail acceptance of the succession.

###### Article 830

A person who knowingly and in bad faith relies on an inaccurate certificate of notoriety incurs the sanctions provided for in article 888, without prejudice to damages.

#### Chapter III: Order of successions Article 831

Successions are devolved to the relatives and to the spouse entitled to inherit from the deceased, in the order and according to the rules determined hereinafter.
A spouse entitled to inherit is the surviving spouse who is not divorced.

##### Section I: Rights of relatives in the absence of a spouse entitled to inherit

###### § 1. General provisions Article 832

The law does not distinguish according to the modes of establishment of filiation in regulating succession.

The rights resulting from adoptive filiation are regulated in Title IX of this code, relating to adoption under the Civil Code.

###### Article 833

In the absence of a spouse entitled to inherit, relatives are called to inherit as follows: 1° Children and their descendants;
2° Father and mother; brothers and sisters and the descendants of the latter; 3° Ascendants other than father and mother;
4° Collaterals other than brothers and sisters and the descendants of the latter. Each of these four categories constitutes an order of heirs which excludes the following ones.

###### Article 834

Children or their descendants succeed to their father and mother or other ascendants, without distinction of sex or primogeniture, even if they are issue of different unions.

###### Article 835

Where the deceased leaves neither issue, nor brother, nor sister, nor descendants of the latter, his father and mother succeed to him, each for one half.

###### Article 836

Where the father and mother died before the deceased and the latter leaves no issue, the brothers and sisters of the deceased or their descendants succeed to him, to the exclusion of other relatives, ascendants or collaterals.

###### Article 837

Where the father and mother survive the deceased and the latter has no issue, but has brothers and sisters or descendants of the latter, the succession is devolved, for one quarter, to each of the father and mother and, for the remaining half, to the brothers and sisters or to their descendants.

Where only one of the father and mother survives, the succession is devolved for one quarter to that person and for three quarters to the brothers and sisters or to their descendants.

###### Article 838

When only the father or mother survives and the deceased has neither issue nor brothers or sisters nor descendants of the latter, but leaves one or more ascendants of the other branch than that of his or her surviving father or mother, the succession devolves one half to the father or mother and one half to the ascendants of the other branch.

###### Article 839

When the father and mother or one of them survive the deceased and the latter has no issue, they may in all cases exercise a right of return, up to the shares fixed in the first paragraph of Article 837, over property that the deceased had received from them by gift.
The value of the portion of property subject to the right of return is credited primarily against the succession rights of the father and mother.

When the right of return cannot be exercised in kind, it is executed in value, within the limit of the succession assets.

###### Article 840

In the absence of heirs of the first two orders, the succession devolves to ascendants other than the father and mother.

###### Article 841

In the absence of heirs of the first three orders, the succession devolves to the collateral relatives of the deceased other than brothers and sisters and the descendants of the latter.

###### § 2. Des degrés et des branches Article 842

Proximity of relationship is established by the number of generations; each generation is called a degree.

###### Article 843

The sequence of degrees forms the line. The direct line is the sequence of degrees between persons who descend one from the other, and the collateral line is the sequence of degrees between persons who do not descend from one another but who descend from a common ancestor.
The direct line is distinguished into direct descending line and direct ascending line. The first is that which connects the head with those who descend from him; the second is that which connects a person with those from whom he descends.

###### Article 844

In the direct line, there are as many degrees as there are generations between the persons. Thus, the child is, in relation to the father and mother, in the first degree; the grandson or granddaughter in the second; and reciprocally from the father and mother in relation to the child and from the grandparents in relation to the grandson or granddaughter; and so on.
In the collateral line, degrees are counted by generation, from one of the relatives up to but not including the common ancestor, and from the latter to the other relative. Thus, brothers and sisters are in the

second degree; the uncle or aunt and the nephew or niece are in the third degree; first cousins in the fourth degree; and so on.

###### Article 845

In each order, the nearest heir excludes the more remote heir in degree. Where degrees are equal, heirs succeed in equal portions and per capita.
All subject to what will be said hereafter concerning division by branches and representation.

###### Article 846

Collateral relatives belonging to the order of heirs mentioned in 4° of Article 833 do not succeed beyond the sixth degree.

###### Article 847

Relationship is divided into two branches, according to whether it proceeds from the father or the mother.
When the succession devolves to ascendants, it is divided in half between those of the paternal branch and those of the maternal branch.

###### Article 848

In each branch succeeds, to the exclusion of all others, the ascendant who is in the nearest degree.
Ascendants in the same degree succeed per capita.

In the absence of an ascendant in one branch, the ascendants of the other branch take the entire succession.

###### Article 849

When the succession devolves to collaterals other than brothers and sisters or their descendants, it is divided in half between those of the paternal branch and those of the maternal branch.

###### Article 850

In each branch succeeds, to the exclusion of all others, the collateral who is in the nearest degree.
Collaterals in the same degree succeed per capita.
In the absence of a collateral in one branch, the collaterals of the other branch take the entire succession.

###### § 3. De la représentation Article 851

Representation is a legal fiction, the effect of which is to call the representatives to the succession, in the place, in the degree and in the rights of the person represented.

###### Article 852

Representation takes place indefinitely in the direct descending line.

It is admitted in all cases, whether the children of the deceased compete with the descendants of a predeceased child, or whether all the children of the deceased having died before him, the descendants of said children find themselves among themselves in equal or unequal degrees.

###### Article 853

Representation does not take place in favour of ascendants; the nearest, in each of the two lines, always excludes the more remote.

###### Article 854

In the collateral line, representation is admitted in favour of the children and descendants of brothers or sisters of the deceased, whether they come to his succession concurrently with uncles or aunts, or whether all the brothers and sisters of the deceased having predeceased, the succession is devolved to their descendants in equal or unequal degrees.

###### Article 855

In all cases where representation is admitted, the partition is effected per stirpes, as if the person represented were coming to the succession: if the same stirps has produced several branches, the subdivision is also made per stirpes in each branch. Within a stirps or a subdivision of a stirps, the partition is made per capita.

###### Article 856

Living persons are not represented, but only those who are dead; one may represent a person whose succession one has renounced.
Renunciants are represented only in successions devolved in the direct or collateral line.
The children of the renunciant conceived before the opening of the succession from which the renunciant was excluded bring back to the succession of the latter the property they inherited in his stead, if they come in competition with other children conceived after the opening of the succession. The bringing back is made according to the provisions set out in Articles 994 et seq. of this Code.

Unless the donor wills otherwise, in case of representation of a renunciant, gifts made to the latter are credited, where applicable, against the reserved portion that should have gone to him had he not renounced.

The law does not distinguish, for the exercise of representation, between legitimate filiation and natural filiation.

###### Article 857

Representation is admitted in favour of the children and descendants of the unworthy person, even though the latter is living at the opening of the succession.
The provisions set out in the second paragraph of Article 856 are applicable to the children of the unworthy person during his lifetime.

##### Section II : Des droits du conjoint survivant

###### § 1. De la nature des droits, de leur montant et de leur exercice Article 858

The successor spouse is called to the succession, either alone or in competition with the relatives of the deceased.

###### Article 859

If the predeceased spouse leaves children or descendants, the surviving spouse takes, at his or her choice, the usufruct of all the existing property or ownership of one quarter of the property when all the children are issue of both spouses and ownership of one quarter in the presence of one or more children who are not issue of both spouses.

###### Article 860

If, in the absence of children or descendants, the deceased leaves his father and mother, the surviving spouse takes one half of the property. The other half devolves one quarter to the father and one quarter to the mother.

When the father or mother has predeceased, the share that would have gone to him or her passes to the surviving spouse.

###### Article 861

In the absence of children or descendants of the deceased and of his father and mother, the surviving spouse takes the entire succession.

###### Article 862

By way of derogation from Article 861, in the event of the predeceased father and mother, property that the deceased had received from his or her ascendants by succession or donation and which is found in kind in the estate is, in the absence of descendants, devolved for one half to the brothers and sisters of the deceased or to their descendants, themselves descendants of the predeceased parent or parents from whom the transmission originated.

###### Article 863

When the surviving spouse receives all or three quarters of the property, the ascendants of the deceased, other than the father and mother, who are in need benefit from a maintenance claim against the estate of the predeceased.
The time limit for claiming it is one year from the death or from the time when the heirs cease to provide the benefits they previously furnished to the ascendants. The time limit is extended, in case of joint ownership, until the completion of the partition.
The pension is taken from the estate. It is borne by all the heirs and, in case of insufficiency, by all the particular legatees, in proportion to their emolument.

However, if the deceased expressly declared that a particular legacy shall be satisfied in preference to the others, Article 1080 shall apply.

###### Article 864

When the spouse has the choice of ownership or usufruct, his or her rights are non-transferable as long as he or she has not exercised his or her option.

###### Article 865

The spouse's option between usufruct and ownership is proved by any means.

Any heir may invite the spouse in writing to exercise his or her option. Failing to have taken a position in writing within three months, the spouse is deemed to have opted for the usufruct.

The spouse is deemed to have opted for the usufruct if he or she dies without having taken a position.

###### Article 866

The calculation of the right in full ownership of the spouse provided for in Articles 859 and 860 shall be made on a mass consisting of all the property existing at the death of his or her spouse to which shall be notionally reunited those of which he or she had disposed, either by act inter vivos or by testamentary act, for the benefit of successors, without dispensation from bringing into account.
The spouse may exercise his or her right only on the property of which the predeceased had not disposed either by act inter vivos or by testamentary act, and without prejudice to the rights of reserve or to the rights of return.

###### Article 867

Liberalities received from the deceased by the surviving spouse are imputed to the rights of the latter in the succession. When the liberalities thus received are less than the rights defined in Articles 859 and 860,

the surviving spouse may claim the complement, without ever receiving a portion of the property greater than the available portion defined in Article 1228.

###### § 2. De la conversion de l'usufruit Article 868

Any usufruct belonging to the spouse on the property of the predeceased, whether it results from the law, a will or a donation of property to come, gives rise to a power of conversion into a life annuity, at the request of one of the bare owner heirs or of the successor spouse himself or herself.

The power of conversion is not susceptible to renunciation. The co-heirs cannot be deprived of it by the will of the predeceased.

###### Article 869

In the absence of agreement between the parties, the request for conversion is submitted to the judge. The request for conversion may be brought until the final partition.
If he grants the request for conversion, the judge determines the amount of the annuity, the securities that the debtor co-heirs must provide, as well as the type of indexation appropriate to maintain the initial equivalence of the annuity to the usufruct.
However, the judge cannot order against the will of the spouse the conversion of the usufruct relating to the dwelling that he or she occupies as a principal residence, as well as on the furniture furnishing it.

###### Article 870

By agreement between the heirs and the spouse, the conversion of the spouse's usufruct into capital may be carried out.

###### Article 871

The conversion of the usufruct is included in the partition operations. It does not produce retroactive effect, except by contrary stipulation of the parties.

###### § 3

Du droit au logement temporaire et du droit viager au logement Article 872
If, at the time of death, the successor spouse effectively occupies, as a principal dwelling, a dwelling belonging to the spouses or depending totally on the estate, he or she has by operation of law, for one year, the free enjoyment of this dwelling, as well as of the furniture, included in the estate, which furnishes it.

If his or her dwelling was provided by means of a lease or a dwelling belonging in part undivided to the deceased, the rents or the occupancy indemnity shall be reimbursed to him or her by the estate during the year, as and when they are paid.
The rights provided for in this article are deemed direct effects of marriage and not succession rights. This article is of public policy.

###### Article 873

In addition, except contrary will of the deceased expressed in the conditions of Article 1127, the successor spouse who effectively occupied, at the time of death, as a principal dwelling, a dwelling belonging to the spouses or depending totally on the estate, has on this dwelling and on the furniture included in the estate which furnishes it, until his or her death, a right of habitation and a right of use.

When the dwelling is the subject of a lease, the successor spouse, if he or she effectively occupied the premises as a principal dwelling at the time of death, benefits from the right of use on the furniture included in the estate furnishing it.
The deprivation of these rights of habitation and use expressed by the deceased in the conditions mentioned in the first paragraph is without effect on the usufruct rights that the spouse receives by virtue of the law or of a liberality, which continue to obey their own rules.

These rights of habitation and use are exercised in the conditions provided for in Articles 745 paragraph 3, 747 and 748.

The spouse, the other heirs or one of them may require that an inventory of the movables and a statement of the immovable subject to the rights of use and habitation be drawn up.
By way of derogation from Article 745, paragraph 3, when the situation of the spouse is such that the dwelling burdened with the right of habitation is no longer adapted to his or her needs, the spouse or his or her representative may lease it for use other than commercial or agricultural in order to generate the resources necessary for new accommodation conditions.

###### Article 874

The value of the rights of habitation and use is imputed to the value of the succession rights received by the spouse.
If the value of the rights of habitation and use is less than that of his or her succession rights, the spouse may take the complement from the existing property.

If the value of the rights of habitation and use is greater than that of his or her succession rights, the spouse is not required to compensate the estate for the excess.

###### Article 875

The spouse has one year from the death to manifest his or her will to benefit from these rights of habitation and use.
The successor spouse and the heirs may, by agreement, convert the rights of habitation and use into a life annuity or into capital.

If there is among the successors parties to the agreement a minor or a protected adult, the agreement must be authorized by the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### § 4. Du droit à pension Article 876

The estate of the predeceased spouse owes a pension to the surviving spouse who is in need. The time limit to claim it is one year from the death or from the moment when the heirs cease to provide the benefits they previously furnished to the spouse. The time limit is extended, in case of joint ownership, until the completion of the partition.
The maintenance pension is taken from the estate. It is borne by all heirs and, in case of insufficiency, by all particular legatees, proportionally to their emolument.

However, if the deceased has expressly declared that a particular legacy shall be paid in preference to others, Article 1080 shall apply.

#### Chapitre IV. Des droits de l'Etat

###### Article 877

In the absence of heirs, surviving spouse, universal legatees or donees, the estate passes to the State.
The State is required to have seals affixed and, if the inventory of property has not already been carried out within the framework of the procedure provided for unclaimed estates, the domain authority shall have it carried out in the forms prescribed for acceptance of estates under benefit of inventory.

###### Article 878

It must request delivery of possession from the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance in whose jurisdiction the estate is opened.
The State is exempted from using the services of a lawyer; the court rules on the application three months and forty days after publication and posting in the customary forms, and after hearing the Public Prosecutor.

###### Article 879

In the case where vacancy had been regularly declared, and the domain administration appointed as curator, it may, before making its application, proceed by itself with the publicity formalities provided for.

###### Article 880

The domain administration that has not fulfilled the formalities prescribed to it may be ordered to pay damages to the heirs, if any come forward.

#### Chapitre V : De l'option de l'héritier

##### Section I : Dispositions générales Article 881

Every successor, the heir with regard to the succession as the legatee with regard to the legacy that falls to him, may:
-	either accept it purely and simply,
-	or accept it under benefit of inventory, when he has a universal or universal title vocation,
-	or renounce it.

###### Article 882

The option is indivisible. However, the successor who combines more than one succession vocation has, for each of them, a separate right of option.

###### Article 883

This option cannot be exercised before the opening of the succession, nor by marriage contract nor with the consent of the person whose succession is at issue.
A conditional or term option is null and void.

###### Article 884

The heir of subsequent rank has the same rights as the heir when the latter renounces the succession or is struck by unworthiness, from the day he became aware of the renunciation or unworthiness. The same applies to the heirs of one who dies without having opted, from the death of his predecessor; these heirs of one who dies without having opted exercise the option separately, each for his share.

###### Article 885

The power to accept or renounce a succession is prescribed by ten years. At the end of this period, the successor is deemed to have renounced the succession. One who claims to have accepted this succession before the expiration of this period must provide proof thereof.

###### Article 886

The subsequent heir of an heir whose acceptance is annulled only sees the ten-year period run against him from the final decision establishing this nullity.
The heir who has left the surviving spouse in enjoyment of the hereditary property only sees the period run against him from the death of the latter.

The period does not run either against one who, legitimately, was unaware of the birth of his right, in particular the opening of the succession.

Moreover, as long as the prescription of the right to accept is not acquired against the heirs who have renounced, they have the power to still accept the succession, if it has not already been accepted by other heirs; without prejudice however to the rights that may be acquired by third parties over the property of the succession.

###### Article 887

The option exercised has retroactive effect to the day of the opening of the succession.

However, error, fraud as well as duress are a cause of nullity of the option exercised by the heir. The action for nullity is prescribed by five years from the day on which the error or fraud was discovered or the day on which the duress ceased.

###### Article 888

The heir who, knowingly and in bad faith, has concealed property or rights of a succession, or concealed the existence of a co-heir, or omitted to include in the inventory property or rights of the succession, is deprived of the benefit of inventory and the right of renunciation: he is an unconditional heir, without prejudice to the damages that the victims of his actions could claim.
The heir cannot however claim any share in the property or rights misappropriated or concealed. Likewise, when the concealment related to a donation subject to collation or reduction, the heir owes the collation or reduction of this donation without being able to claim any share therein. The concealing heir is moreover required to return all the fruits and revenues of the concealed property which he has enjoyed since the opening of the succession.

###### Article 889

The personal creditors of one who abstains from accepting a succession or who renounces a succession to the prejudice of their rights may be authorized in court to accept the succession on behalf of their debtor, in his place and stead.
The acceptance takes place only in favor of these creditors and up to the amount of their claims. It produces no other effect with regard to the heir.

###### Article 890

The acceptance of a succession that would be absorbed or diminished by more than half, by the discovery of a will unknown at the time of acceptance, is voidable for lesion.

##### Section II : De l'acceptation de la succession

###### Article 891

Successions that have fallen to minors and adults under guardianship may only be validly accepted in accordance with the provisions of the title On minority, guardianship and emancipation.

###### Article 892

The acceptance of the succession may be express or tacit: it is express when the successor takes the title or quality of heir in an authentic or private act; it is tacit when the successor performs an act that necessarily presupposes his intention to accept and that he would only have the right to perform in his quality as heir.
Acts that are purely conservatory, of supervision and provisional administration are not, by themselves, acts constituting acceptance on the part of the heir. If the successor wishes to take another act without however taking the title or quality of heir, he must request authorization from the judge to perform it.

###### Article 893

The following are deemed purely conservatory:
1° The payment of funeral and last illness expenses, taxes owed by the deceased, rents and other succession debts whose settlement is urgent;
2° The collection of fruits and revenues of succession property or the sale of perishable property, subject to justifying that the funds were used to extinguish the debts referred to in 1° or were deposited with a notary or placed in escrow;
3° Any act intended to prevent the aggravation of the succession liabilities;
4° Acts related to the termination of the employment contract of the employee of the deceased private employer, the payment of wages and compensation owed to the employee as well as the delivery of end-of-contract documents.

###### Article 894

The following are deemed to be provisional administration acts:
1° The renewal, whether as lessor or lessee, of leases which, in the absence thereof, would give rise to the payment of compensation;
2° The implementation of administration or disposition decisions initiated by the deceased and necessary for the proper functioning of the business;
3° Acts which are routine operations necessary for the short-term continuation of the activity of the business forming part of the estate.

###### Article 895

The heir who, whether gratuitously or for consideration, transfers his rights in the estate, either to a third party, or to all his co-heirs, or to some of them, accepts the estate by that fact alone.
The same applies when the heir has renounced the estate, gratuitously or not, in favour of one, several or all of his co-heirs, or in favour of one, several or all heirs of subsequent rank.

###### Article 896

Where a person to whom an estate has devolved has died before being able, expressly or tacitly, to express his choice, his heirs may accept it or renounce it on his behalf. In the absence of unanimity among them, the estate must be accepted subject to inventory.

###### Article 897

When the heir accepts the estate, the effect of the acceptance relates back to the day of the opening of the estate.

##### Section III: Renunciation of estates Article 898

Renunciation of an estate is not presumed. It is enforceable against all from the day on which it is made at the registry of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the estate was opened, in a special register kept for that purpose.

###### Article 899

The heir who renounces is deemed never to have been an heir.

###### Article 900

The estate which the heir renounces is distributed among his heirs in the direct line; in the absence of heirs in the direct line, it passes to the co-heirs and otherwise to the next degree.
The heir who renounces the estate may nevertheless retain the inter vivos gift or claim the legacy made to him up to the amount of the available portion, unless the disposer has expressly required contribution in the event of renunciation. In that case, contribution is made in value; where the value contributed exceeds the rights he should have had in the partition had he participated in it, the renouncing heir compensates the accepting heirs to the extent of that excess.

##### Section IV: Acceptance subject to inventory

###### § 1. Formalities to be observed Article 901

The declaration by an heir that he intends to take that capacity only subject to inventory must be made at the registry of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the estate was opened. It must be entered in the register intended to receive acts of renunciation.

###### Article 902

The declaration states the surnames, first names, occupation of the heir and the capacity by virtue of which he is called to the estate.
It also includes the election of a single domicile located in Djibouti, which may be the domicile of one of the acceptors subject to inventory or that of the person responsible for settling the estate. It is to this address that creditors shall declare their claims.

###### Article 903

The heir's declaration is registered by the registry, which gives him a receipt for it, and opens a file. The receipt informs the declarant of the need to comply with the publication provided for by the following article.

###### Article 904

The declaration is published, within fifteen days, in a newspaper authorised to receive legal publications.
Where the law refers to the declaration as the starting point of a time limit, that time limit runs from the date of the publication made.

###### Article 905

The heir's declaration has effect only insofar as it is preceded or followed by a faithful and accurate inventory of the property of the estate and within the time limits to be determined hereinafter.

###### Article 906

The heir has, first, three months to make an inventory, from the day of the opening of the estate.

He may however apply to the judge for an additional time limit if he justifies serious and legitimate reasons which delay the filing of the inventory. In that case, the time limit is suspended from the date of the application for extension.

The heir then has forty days to deliberate on his acceptance or not of the estate. This second time limit begins to run from the day of expiry of the time limit to which the heir is subject to make the inventory, or from the day of closure of the inventory if it was completed before the three months.

###### Article 907

The inventory is descriptive and estimative of the elements present, item by item, in the deceased's estate.
It is drawn up by a bailiff or a notary, according to the rules applicable to those professions.

###### Article 908

A copy of the inventory is delivered against receipt by the heir to the competent registry, which adds it to the file. The heir must carry out this formality within two months of the inventory being made. Failing this, he is deemed to have accepted the estate purely and simply.

###### Article 909

The inventory gives rise to the same publication as the initial declaration.
Any person who justifies his status as creditor against the deceased may take cognisance of its contents and obtain a copy at the registry.

###### § 2. Effects of acceptance subject to inventory Article 910

The declaration made by the heir to accept the estate subject to inventory entails:
1° Separation of estates: the heir's personal property is not merged with that of the estate;
2° Preservation of all the rights which the heir previously had over the deceased's property; 3° Limitation of the acceptance of the estate to the estate assets: the heir is only liable to pay the debts of the estate within the limit of the assets collected and not from his personal estate. The heir may only be held liable for his acts on his personal property where provisions of this paragraph so provide;
4° Supervision of the management of the estate assets by the heir, who is required to administer the estate.

###### Article 911

During the period of the time limits for making an inventory and for deliberating, the heir cannot be compelled to exercise his option. No judgment can be obtained against him.
As long as the prescription of the right to accept has not been acquired against him, the heir may revoke his acceptance and accept the estate purely and simply. He is then deemed to have accepted it from the opening of the estate.

Acceptance subject to inventory prevents any renunciation of the estate.

###### Article 912

If the heir does not file the inventory within the time limits provided for making it, or does not exercise his option within the time limit offered for deliberating, he retains the power to make an inventory and to opt.

It is otherwise if he has in other respects performed an act manifesting his intention to accept the estate purely and simply or if there exists against him a judgment which has become res judicata condemning him in his capacity as heir purely and simply.

###### Article 913

However, upon expiration of the time limits provided for making an inventory and for deliberating, the heir who has not made an election may be summoned, by extrajudicial act, to take a position. The summons may be issued by a creditor of the succession, a co-heir, an heir of subsequent rank, or the State.
Within two months following the summons, the heir must take a position or request an additional time limit from the judge when he has not been able to complete the inventory begun or when he justifies other serious and legitimate reasons. This time limit is suspended from the request for extension until the decision of the judge seized of the matter.

In the absence of having taken a position upon expiration of the two-month time limit or the additional time limit granted, the heir is deemed to have accepted unconditionally.

###### Article 914

From the publication of the declaration of the heir who accepts the succession subject to inventory, the creditors of the succession have a period of twelve months to claim what is owed to them. They must declare their claim within this time limit, by notifying their title to the elected domicile of the succession.
In case of late declaration or absence of declaration, claims not secured by security interests on the property of the succession are extinguished with respect to the succession.

This provision also benefits sureties and co-obligors, as well as persons having granted an independent guarantee relating to the claim thus extinguished.

###### Article 915

From the publication of the declaration of acceptance subject to inventory and for a period of twelve months, it stays or prohibits any means of execution and any new registration of security interest by the creditors of the succession, relating to both movables and immovables.
However, seizing creditors are considered as holders of security interests on the property and rights previously seized.

###### Article 916

When the succession has been accepted by one or more heirs unconditionally and by one or more others up to the net assets, the rules applicable to the latter option are binding on all heirs until the day of partition.
The creditors of a succession accepted by one or more heirs unconditionally and by others up to the net assets may provoke the partition when they justify difficulties in the recovery of the share of their claim incumbent upon the heirs accepting up to the net assets.

###### Article 917

The heir accepting up to the net assets has the obligation to administer the property he receives in the succession, and must account for his management.
He is liable for serious faults he would commit in this administration.

He must present the account to any succession creditor who requests it and respond within a period of two months to the summons, served by extrajudicial act, to disclose to him where the property and

rights received in the succession that he has neither alienated nor retained are located. In default, he may be compelled on his personal property.

If he does not wish to personally administer the property of the succession, or if he is in default, a representative may be appointed judicially at the request of any interested party. The President of the Court of First Instance is seized of the matter and rules by summary order.

###### Article 918

The heir is the owner of the assets of the succession and has the power to dispose of the property of the succession.
If there are in the succession objects liable to perish or too costly to preserve, the heir may proceed with the sale of these objects. If the heir has decided to retain such property in kind, at the end of the acceptance procedure subject to inventory, he is liable only for the depreciation or deterioration caused by his negligence.

###### Article 919

For other property, within the period of twelve months from the publication provided for in Article 904, the heir may declare:
1° that he intends to retain in kind certain property of the succession. He then owes to the succession the value of this property as it was estimated in the inventory;
2° that he is selling certain property, movable or immovable.
This property is excluded from the succession estate and withdrawn from the security of succession creditors. On the other hand, its value is recorded in the assets of the succession. All without prejudice to the rights of creditors holding security interests.
Other succession property that has not been the subject of such a declaration remains in the security of the creditors of the succession.

###### Article 920

The declaration of the alienation or retention of one or more properties is made within fifteen days at the registry of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance. The heir ensures its publication in a newspaper authorized to receive legal publications.
Without prejudice to the rights reserved to creditors holding security interests, any succession creditor may contest before the judge, within a period of three months after the publication mentioned in the first paragraph, the value of the property retained or, when the sale was made amicably, the price of the alienation by proving that the value of the property is higher.

When the creditor's claim is granted, the heir is liable for the supplement on his personal property, except to restore to the succession the property retained.
The creditor may also act in his own name to have declared unenforceable against him the acts done by his debtor in fraud of his rights, provided he establishes, if it is an act for valuable consideration, that the third party co-contractor had knowledge or should have had knowledge of the fraud.

###### Article 921

The declaration to retain a property is not enforceable against creditors as long as it has not been published.

The failure to declare the alienation of a property within the time limit provided for in the preceding article binds the heir on his personal property up to the amount of the price of the alienation.

###### Article 922

The heir settles the liabilities of the succession. He draws up for this purpose a draft settlement of liabilities.

The costs of seals, if any have been affixed, of inventory and of account, are borne by the succession. The public officer or ministerial officer having settled the succession or enabled the preservation of succession property shall be paid before the other creditors.
Registered creditors are paid according to the rank of the security interest securing their claim.

Other creditors who have declared their claim are satisfied in the order of declarations. Legacies of sums of money are delivered after payment of creditors.

###### Article 923

The draft settlement of liabilities is filed at the registry which adds it to the file. A notice is published according to the publication procedures provided for in Article 904. Creditors who are not fully satisfied in view of this draft may, within one month of the publication, seize the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance in order to contest the settlement draft.

###### Article 924

In the absence of contestation at the end of the one-month period from the publication provided for in the preceding article, the heir must pay the creditors within the two months that follow, in accordance with the draft settlement of liabilities.
When, conversely, the settlement draft is not validated due to a contestation relating to the order or nature of the claims, the heir deposits the available sums as long as the contestation subsists.

###### Article 925

The personal creditors of the heir may only pursue recovery of their claims against the assets of the estate after the expiry of a twelve-month period from the publication of the declaration of acceptance of the estate subject to inventory and after the full satisfaction of estate creditors and legatees.
Creditors who have not declared their claim within the period referred to in the preceding article, and who come forward only after the exhaustion of the assets, have recourse only against the legatees who have been satisfied in their rights.

##### Section V: Vacant Estates Article 926

An estate is vacant when, after the expiry of the periods for making an inventory and for deliberating: 1° No person comes forward claiming an estate and there is no known heir;
2° All known heirs have renounced the estate;
3° Known heirs have been summoned to take a position in accordance with the provisions of Article 913 and have renounced the estate or remained silent;
4° In the absence of a summons, known heirs have not opted, either expressly or tacitly, for ten years.
When heirs come forward during the proceedings, their hereditary prerogatives take precedence. They may then exercise their legal right of option: if they accept the estate unconditionally, the vacancy automatically ends; if they renounce it, it continues; and if they accept subject to inventory, the proceedings continue according to the rules set out in Section IV of this chapter.

###### Article 927

The President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance in whose jurisdiction the estate is opened, appoints a curator upon the application of any interested person or upon the requisition of the Public Prosecutor.

His decision is, at the initiative of the curator, within fifteen days of its pronouncement, published in a newspaper authorized to receive legal notices.

In the context of vacant estates, the curatorship is necessarily entrusted to the administrative authority responsible for state property.

###### Article 928

The curator is required, first of all, to have its condition recorded by an inventory: he exercises and pursues its rights; he responds to claims brought against the estate; he administers, under the obligation to have the sums of money found in the estate, as well as the amounts from the sale price of movables or immovables sold, deposited in the National Treasury, for the preservation of rights and under the obligation to account to whom it may concern.
The provisions of Section IV of this chapter, on the forms of inventory, on the mode of administration and on the accounts to be rendered by the beneficiary heir, as well as on the rights and obligations of creditors, are common to curators of vacant estates, subject to the following reservations.

###### Article 929

Creditors must declare their claim to the curator, by notifying him of their title, within a period of nine months.
The curator establishes a draft settlement of liabilities respecting the order provided for in Article 922, with the costs related to the administration of the curatorship being paid before other claims. The curator may only provide for the payment of estate debts up to the amount of the assets.

The curator may however pay, without waiting for the draft settlement of liabilities, the costs necessary for the preservation of the estate, funeral and last illness expenses, taxes owed by the deceased, rents and other estate debts whose settlement is urgent.

###### Article 930

The draft settlement of liabilities is filed with the registry of the Court of First Instance which adds it to the file. A notice is published according to the publication procedures provided for in Article 904.

###### Article 931

Creditors who are not fully satisfied under this draft may, within one month of publication, seize the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance to contest the settlement draft.
Those who have not declared their claim after the submission of the draft may only claim the remaining assets. In case of insufficiency of these assets, they have recourse only against the legatees who have been satisfied in their rights. This recourse is prescribed after one year from the realization of all remaining assets.

###### Article 932

In the absence of recourse against the draft or after the president's decision has become final, the curator proceeds with the final realization of the remaining assets.
Any surplus is handed over upon their request to heirs who come forward, if they are within the useful period to claim the estate.

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance in whose jurisdiction the estate is opened, seized by the curator, sends the State into possession of the estate.

#### Chapter VI. Partition

##### Section I: The Legal Regime of Co-ownership

###### § 1. General Provisions Article 933

Co-ownership arises when several persons have a real right of the same nature over the same property or the same mass of property. This right may be ownership or another dismembered real right.
Co-ownership does not have legal personality.
Each co-owner has over the undivided property the same right shared with the others. The extent of each person's rights in the co-ownership is defined by the law or the agreement that gives rise to it. In the absence of another title, it results from a certificate of notoriety or an inventory heading established by the notary.

###### Article 934

Each co-owner holds his share. However, when a co-owner intends to transfer all or part of his undivided rights, for consideration and to a person outside the co-ownership, the other co-owners have a right of pre-emption.
Any transfer project must be notified beforehand to the other co-owners, with all useful information, such as the price, the conditions of the transfer and the identifying elements of the purchaser. This notification, made by extra-judicial act, opens a one-month period for the co-owners to bring to the knowledge of the transferring co-owner their decision to exercise their right of pre-emption under the conditions brought to their knowledge.
The person who decides to pre-empt has two months to complete the transfer, from the sending of his decision to the transferring co-owner. After this period, he is formally notified to respond and, if he remains silent for fifteen days, his declaration of pre-emption is null and void by operation of law, without prejudice to damages that may be claimed by the transferor.

When the transferor has granted payment terms and, as a result of economic circumstances, the value of the property that has fallen to him has increased or decreased by more than one quarter since the partition, the sums remaining due increase or decrease in the same proportion, unless this variation is excluded by the parties.

###### Article 935

When a creditor seizes all or part of the rights of a co-owner in the co-ownership with a view to subjecting them to a forced sale, there is no right of pre-emption but a right of substitution for the successful bidder. The lawyer of the pursuing creditor or the notary notifies all other co-owners one month before the scheduled date of the sale. The latter have a period of one month from the adjudication, to substitute themselves for the purchaser.
This right is exercised by declaration at the registry of the Court of First Instance or with the notary in charge of the sale. It is recorded in the schedule of conditions of sale established for the sale.

###### Article 936

For both amicable and forced transfers, compliance with notification and time limit rules is required on pain of nullity of the transaction. This nullity, of private interest, is available for five years to the persons

to whom the notifications should have been made or to their heirs.

The notifications provided for by the two articles and the preceding paragraph must be addressed to every bare owner and to every usufructuary. But a usufructuary may acquire a share in bare ownership only if no bare owner comes forward as purchaser; a bare owner may acquire a share in usufruct only if no usufructuary comes forward as purchaser.

###### § 2. Rules for management of co-ownership Article 937

In co-ownership, decisions are made unanimously, subject to the following exceptions.

###### Article 938

When they fall within the normal operation of co-owned property, decisions concerning the following may be made by the holders of two-thirds of the co-ownership rights:
1° Acts of administration of co-owned property;
2° The designation of a co-owner or a third party under a general management mandate;
3° The conclusion and renewal of leases other than those relating to property for agricultural, commercial, industrial or artisanal use;
4° The decision to sell movable co-owned property when this transaction is necessary for the payment of debts and charges of the co-ownership. The sale of co-owned property outside this purpose requires unanimity, except by judicial authorization.

###### Article 939

Except in case of division of ownership of the property or if one of the co-owners is in one of the cases provided for in article 863, the alienation of co-owned property may be authorized by the Court of First Instance, at the request of one or more co-owners holding at least two-thirds of the co-ownership rights, according to the conditions and procedures defined in the following paragraphs.
The co-owner or co-owners holding at least two-thirds of the co-ownership rights express before a notary, by this majority, their intention to proceed with the alienation of the co-owned property. Within the month that follows, the notary serves notice of this intention on the other co-owners.
In the absence of opposition within three months of service, the decision to alienate the co-owned property is confirmed, unless the service provided for in the second paragraph has not been effected. In case of opposition, the Court of First Instance may authorize the alienation of the co-owned property if it does not excessively infringe the rights of the other co-owners.

This alienation is effected by licitation. The sums derived therefrom may not be reinvested except to pay the debts and charges of the co-ownership.

###### Article 940

Any co-owner may take the measures necessary for the preservation of co-owned property, even if there is no urgency.
These conservatory acts may be of a material nature, such as an act of occasional maintenance, or legal, such as serving formal notice on a debtor in default. They may be directed both against another co-owner and against a third party to the co-ownership.

The co-owner may use for this purpose the co-ownership funds held by him and he is deemed to have free disposal thereof with regard to third parties.

In the absence of co-ownership funds, he may oblige his co-owners to make the necessary expenditures with him.

When co-owned property is encumbered with a usufruct, these powers are enforceable against the usufructuary to the extent that the latter is liable for repairs.

###### Article 941

Co-owners may give a mandate to one or more of them or to a third party to perform a specific act, which constitutes a special mandate, or even to handle all the affairs of the co-ownership, which is a general mandate. The general mandate permits only acts of administration.
If one of the co-owners or a third party takes the initiative to manage the co-owned property with the knowledge of the others and without opposition on their part, he is deemed to have received a tacit mandate. This mandate permits only acts of administration; it covers neither acts of disposition nor the conclusion or renewal of leases.

The co-owner who manages one or more co-owned properties is responsible for his management. He is entitled to remuneration for his activity under the conditions fixed amicably or, failing that, by judicial decision.
If a co-owner or a third party performs an act useful to the co-ownership without the conditions provided for in the preceding paragraphs being met, he is obliged to continue his management in accordance with the rules governing management of affairs.

###### Article 942

When the situation does not permit giving a mandate, a co-owner may seek judicial authorization:
1° When another co-owner is unable to express his will: the applicant co-owner may have himself authorized by the court to represent him, both generally and for certain particular acts. The court then determines the conditions and extent of the representation;
2° In case of refusal by one of the co-owners to give his consent to an act deemed necessary by the applicant, when this refusal endangers the common interest. However, it does not fall within the power of the judge to authorize the sale in full ownership requested by a bare owner when the usufructuary opposes it;
3° For all urgent measures required by the common interest.
In cases 2° and 3°, authorization is sought before the president of the Court of First Instance who is seized and rules in summary proceedings. The president may, in particular, authorize a co-owner to collect from the debtors of the co-ownership or from depositaries of co-owned funds a provision intended to meet urgent needs, prescribing, if necessary, the conditions of use. This authorization does not entail assumption of status for the surviving spouse or for the heir. He may also either designate a co-owner as administrator, obliging him if necessary to provide security, or appoint a sequestrator, or prohibit the displacement of movable property except to specify those of which he grants personal use to one or another of the beneficiaries, on condition that they provide security if he deems it necessary.

###### Article 943

When co-owned immovable property for residential use or for mixed residential and professional use is vacant or has not been the subject of effective occupation for more than two calendar years, a co-owner may be authorized in court to carry out improvement, rehabilitation and restoration works on the property as well as to perform acts of administration and publicity formalities, having as sole purpose to lease it as a principal residence.

###### Article 944

For this purpose, a co-owner may seize the president of the Court of First Instance, so that he may designate him as mandatary. The president fixes the duration of his mission as well as his remuneration. At the request of the designated co-owner, the president may extend this mission for a period that he determines.

The appointment decision is registered and published in a journal authorized to receive legal publications.

###### Article 945

Within the limits of the powers conferred upon him, the designated co-owner represents all the co-owners for the acts provided for in article 943. He exercises his powers even when there is a minor or a protected adult among the other co-owners.
The acts he performs within the framework of his mission have no effect on the hereditary option of the co-owner designated as mandatary.

###### Article 946

At the request of any interested person or of the public prosecutor, the president may remove the mandatary from his mission in case of characterized failure in the exercise thereof. The president then designates another mandatary, for a period that he defines.

###### Article 947

Each heir may require the agent to allow consultation, at any time, of documents relating to the performance of his mission.
Each year and at the end of his mission, the agent submits to the judge and to each heir upon request a report on the performance of his mission.
The mission ceases automatically by the effect of an indivision agreement that is signed between the heirs or by the signing of the partition deed. It also ceases when the judge finds the complete performance of the mission entrusted to the succession agent.

###### § 3. Des droits et obligations des indivisaires Article 948

Each co-owner has the same right of use and enjoyment over undivided property as the others. The co-owners settle the distribution of this right among themselves. It is possible for them to grant to a co-owner an exclusive right of use or enjoyment over the property, in return for compensation.

In the absence of agreement on the use of undivided property, the president of the court settles the matter on a provisional basis. He is seized and rules by summary order.

###### Article 949

Each person is entitled to the benefits of undivided property and bears the losses in proportion to his rights in the indivision. No claim relating to fruits and revenues shall, however, be admissible more than five years after the date on which they were received or could have been received.
Any person who receives revenues or incurs expenses on behalf of the indivision must keep a record thereof which is available to the co-owners.

The fruits and revenues benefit the entire indivision; they may however, by express agreement, be attributed to one of the co-owners.
Any co-owner may request his annual share in the benefits. In case of disagreement, the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance shall rule taking into account the extent of each person's rights in the indivision.

###### Article 950

Are automatically undivided, by the effect of real subrogation, claims and indemnities that replace undivided property, as well as property acquired, with the consent of all the co-owners, in employment or re-employment of undivided property.

###### Article 951

When a co-owner has improved at his own expense the condition of undivided property, he must be given credit for it according to equity, having regard to the amount by which the value of the property is increased at the time of partition or alienation. He must likewise be given credit for necessary expenses that he has incurred from his personal funds for the preservation of said property, even though they have not improved them.
Conversely, the co-owner is liable for degradations and deteriorations that have diminished the value of undivided property by his act or by his fault.

###### § 4. Du droit de poursuite des créanciers Article 952

The creditors of the indivision, who are those who could have acted on the undivided property before there was indivision and those whose claim arose from the fact of management of the indivision or from acts of preservation of which they were the authors, shall be paid from the assets of the indivision before any partition and, if the indivision should not suffice to satisfy them in their rights, they may act against each of the co-owners. The latter are held jointly and severally for the balance. The creditors of the indivision may also pursue the seizure and sale of undivided property.

The personal creditors of a co-owner may not seize either the undivided property or the share of their debtor. On the other hand, they may provoke partition in the name of their debtor or intervene in the partition that the latter has provoked. The co-owners have however the power to stop the course of the partition action, by discharging the obligation owed by the debtor. Those who exercise this option shall reimburse themselves by deduction from the undivided property.

###### § 5. Des demandes en partage Article 953

No one may be compelled to remain in indivision and partition may always be provoked, except by judgment or contrary agreement.

Co-owners who hold a title of ownership, bare ownership or usufruct may agree to remain in indivision for a limited time: this agreement cannot be binding beyond five years; but it may be renewed. Conventional indivision is subject to the rules of articles 2071 and following.

###### Article 954

When several indivisions exist exclusively between the same persons, whether they relate to the same property or to different property, a single partition may take place.

###### Article 955

Partition may be requested even when one of the co-heirs has enjoyed separately all or part of the undivided property, if there has not been a partition deed, or sufficient possession to acquire prescription when it is admitted.

###### Article 956

If a minor, an adult under guardianship or curatorship, or a presumed absentee, is called to a partition, the latter may be done amicably.

In this case, the judge authorizes the partition, even partial, and designates, if necessary, a notary to proceed with it, in the presence as the case may be of the representative or curator of the person referred to in the preceding paragraph or, if that person is himself interested in the partition, of his replacement designated in accordance with article 143. The liquidation statement is submitted to the approval of the judge.
The partition may also be done judicially in accordance with the provisions of articles 981 and following. Failing to fulfill these conditions, the amicable partition is considered provisional.

###### Article 957

A spouse may not, without the consent of the other, proceed with the partition of property that has fallen to the latter which falls into the community. Any partition to which he proceeds alone, as to such property, is valid only as provisional partition.

###### Article 958

The co-owner in usufruct may request partition in kind of the undivided usufruct; if this partition in kind among the different usufructuaries is not possible, the usufruct may be sold.
When the sale of the usufruct alone cannot be envisaged under satisfactory conditions for the usufructuaries, the sale may relate to full ownership provided that it appears as the only measure that can preserve the interests of all holders of rights over the undivided property.

###### Article 959

The same option belongs to the co-owner in bare ownership for the undivided bare ownership. But in case of sale of full ownership, when the property is encumbered with usufruct, this may not operate against the will of the usufructuary.

###### Article 960

When a person is in indivision both over the usufruct and over the bare ownership, he has the options provided for in the two preceding articles. The contrary will of a usufructuary, if he requests the sale of the property in full ownership, may not be opposed to him.

###### Article 961

When all parties agree on the partition, it is amicable; if one of the co-heirs refuses to consent to the partition, or if disputes arise either over the manner of proceeding with it or over the manner of completing it, the partition is judicial.

###### § 6. Des attributions préférentielles Article 962

Except by decision or agreement to maintain the indivision, preferential attribution may be granted to the spouse or to any heir called to succeed by virtue of law, whether he is co-owner in full ownership or in bare ownership, under the conditions provided for by the following provisions.
These provisions also benefit the heir having a universal or universal title vocation to the succession by virtue of a will or contractual institution.

###### Article 963

The surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may request preferential allocation by way of partition, subject to payment of an equalisation sum if applicable, of any enterprise, or part of an agricultural, commercial, industrial, artisanal or liberal enterprise or undivided share of such an enterprise, even formed in part from property of which he or she was already owner or co-owner before the death, in the operation of which he or she participates or has effectively participated. In the case of an heir, the condition

of participation may be or may have been fulfilled by his or her spouse or descendants.

If applicable, the request for preferential allocation may relate to company shares, without prejudice to the application of legal provisions or statutory clauses on the continuation of a company with the surviving spouse or one or more heirs.

###### Article 964

The surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may also request preferential allocation:
1° Of the ownership or right to the lease of the premises which effectively serve as his or her dwelling, if he or she had his or her residence there at the time of death, and of the furniture furnishing it, as well as of the deceased's vehicle provided that this vehicle is necessary for the needs of daily life. This preferential allocation is by right for the surviving spouse;
2° Of the ownership or right to the lease of the premises for professional use effectively serving for the exercise of his or her profession and of the movable objects for professional use furnishing these premises;
3° Of the ownership of any agricultural holding whose size in area makes it a family holding. Preferential allocation is by right for the surviving spouse;
4° Of all the movable elements necessary for the operation of a rural property cultivated by the deceased in a professional capacity, when the lease continues for the benefit of the applicant, or when a new lease is granted to the latter.
The rights resulting from preferential allocation do not prejudice the life rights of habitation and use, or of enjoyment, which the spouse may exercise by virtue of law or contract.

###### Article 965

If maintenance in undivided ownership has not been ordered and in the absence of preferential allocation in ownership, provided for in the preceding articles, the surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may request preferential allocation of all or part of the immovable property and rights with agricultural purpose forming part of the succession with a view to constituting, with one or more co-heirs and, where applicable, one or more third parties, an agricultural land grouping.
This allocation is by right if the surviving spouse or one or more of the co-heirs fulfilling the personal conditions provided for in articles 963 and 964, require that all or part of the property of the grouping be leased to them.

In the event of multiple requests, the property of the grouping may, if its composition permits, be the subject of several leases benefiting different co-heirs; otherwise, and in the absence of amicable agreement, the court designates the lessee taking into account the aptitude of the different applicants to manage the property concerned and to remain there. If the clauses and conditions of this lease or these leases have not been the subject of an agreement, they are fixed by the court.
The immovable property and rights that the applicants do not envisage contributing to the agricultural land grouping, as well as the other property of the succession, are allocated by priority, within the limits of their respective succession rights, to the undivided co-owners who have not consented to the formation of the grouping. If these undivided co-owners are not satisfied with their rights by the allocation thus made, an equalisation sum must be paid to them. Except by amicable agreement between the co-partitioners, the equalisation sum possibly due is payable within the year following the partition. It may be the subject of a payment in kind in the form of shares of the agricultural land grouping, unless the interested parties, within the month following the proposal made to them, have made known their opposition to this method of settlement.

The partition is only complete after the signature of the constitutive deed of the agricultural land grouping and, if applicable, of the long-term lease or leases.

###### Article 966

If an agricultural holding constituting an economic unit and not operated in corporate form is not maintained in undivided ownership and has not been the subject of preferential allocation under the conditions provided for in the preceding articles, the surviving spouse or any co-owner heir who wishes to continue the operation in which he or she participates or has effectively participated may require, notwithstanding any request for sale by auction, that the partition be concluded on the condition that his or her co-partitioners grant him or her a long-term lease on the lands of the holding which fall to them. In the case of an heir, the condition of participation may be or may have been fulfilled by his or her spouse or descendants. Except by amicable agreement between the parties, the person who requests to benefit from these provisions receives by priority in his or her share the operating and dwelling buildings.
The preceding provisions are applicable to a part of the agricultural holding that may constitute an economic unit. This economic unit may be formed, in part, from property of which the surviving spouse or heir was already owner or co-owner before the death.

Account is taken, if applicable, of the depreciation due to the existence of the lease in the valuation of the lands included in the different lots.
