If, by reason of the manifest inaptitude of the applicant or applicants to manage all or part of the holding, the interests of the co-heirs risk being compromised, the court may decide that there is no ground to apply the first three paragraphs of this article.

###### Article 967

In the absence of amicable agreement, the request for preferential allocation is brought before the court, which rules, except contrary provision, according to the interests at stake.
Preferential allocation may be requested jointly by several successors in order to preserve together the undivided property.
In the event of multiple opposing requests concerning a holding or an enterprise, the court designates the allocatee or joint allocatees according to the interests at stake and the aptitude of the different applicants to manage this holding or this enterprise and to remain there and in particular the duration of their personal participation in the activity of the holding or the enterprise.

###### Article 968

The property subject to allocation is valued at its value on the day of partition.

Except by amicable agreement between the co-partitioners, the equalisation sum possibly due is payable in cash. However, when the allocatee is the surviving spouse, he or she may require from his or her co-partitioners for the payment of a fraction of the equalisation sum, equal at most to half, delays not exceeding ten years. Except contrary agreement, the sums remaining due bear interest at the legal rate.

In the event of sale of the whole of the allocated property, the fraction of equalisation sum remaining due becomes immediately payable; in the event of partial sales, the proceeds of these sales are paid to the co-partitioners and credited against the fraction of equalisation sum still due.

###### Article 969

The beneficiary of preferential allocation only becomes exclusive owner of the allocated property on the day of final partition.
Until that date, he or she may only renounce the allocation when the value of the property, as determined on the day of this allocation, has increased by more than a quarter on the day of partition independently of his or her personal act.

###### § 7. De la constitution des parts et lots et du partage

A.	Dispositions communes

###### Article 970

The divisible estate comprises the property existing at the opening of the succession, or that which has been subrogated thereto, and which the deceased has not disposed of by reason of death, as well as the fruits pertaining thereto.
It is increased by the values subject to collation or reduction, as well as by the debts of the co-partitioners towards the deceased or towards the undivided estate.

###### Article 971

The partition of undivided property is effected per capita. However, it is done per stirpes when there is representation. Once partition per stirpes has been effected, within each stirpes, partition is done, where applicable, per capita among the heirs of each stirpes.
When a person dies, his heirs succeed to the succession of the person from whom he would have inherited if he had not died before him. The heirs succeed by representation of their predecessor. Thus, grandchildren succeed to their grandparents by representation of their predeceased father or mother. These heirs by representation constitute "a stirpes".

###### Article 972

When the debtor of an equalizing payment has obtained payment delays, and when, as a result of economic circumstances, the value of the property placed in his lot has increased or decreased by more than one quarter since the partition, the sums remaining due increase or decrease in the same proportion.
The parties may however agree that the amount of the equalizing payment shall not vary.

###### Article 973

Any person, even a relative of the deceased, who is not his successor, and to whom a co-heir has assigned his right to the succession, may be excluded from the partition, either by all his co-heirs, or by one alone, by reimbursing him the price of the assignment.
This power granted to the co-heirs or to one of them to exclude from the partition any person not entitled to succeed to whom a co-heir has assigned his right to the succession, also belongs to the undivided co-owner of an immovable, to the superficiary for the acquisition of the land, and to the owner of the land, for the acquisition of the superficies; any withdrawal without distinction must be exercised within a period of three months from the day the sale was made public.

###### Article 974

In the formation and composition of lots for partition, one must avoid fragmenting the land and dividing economic units and other sets of property whose division would result in depreciation.

B.	Amicable partition

###### Article 975

Amicable partition may be total or partial. It is partial when it leaves the undivided ownership subsisting with regard to certain property or certain persons.

###### Article 976

If all the undivided co-owners are present and capable, partition may take place in the form and according to the procedures chosen by the parties.
When the undivided ownership relates to property subject to land registration publicity, the deed of partition is executed by notarial deed.

###### Article 977

If an undivided co-owner is presumed absent or, by reason of remoteness, is unable to express his will, an amicable partition may take place under the conditions provided for in article 146.
Similarly, if an undivided co-owner is subject to a protective regime, an amicable partition may take place in compliance with the provisions of the titles On minority, guardianship and emancipation and On majority and adults protected by law.

###### Article 978

If an undivided co-owner is in default, without however being in one of the cases provided for in the preceding article, he may, at the instance of a co-partitioner, be formally notified, by extrajudicial act, to be represented at the amicable partition.
If this undivided co-owner fails to appoint a representative within three months of the formal notice, a co-partitioner may request the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance to designate any qualified person who shall represent the defaulter until the complete completion of the partition. This person may only consent to the partition with the authorization of the judge.

###### Article 979

The undivided co-owners compose the lots at their convenience, and agree on the distribution of the lots among themselves. Failing that, the lots once constituted shall be drawn by lot.
Each lot must, as far as possible, be composed, either in whole or in part, of movables or immovables, rights or claims of equivalent value, subject to respect for the proportion of each person's rights in the undivided ownership. In case of inequality of the lots constituted, this inequality is compensated, either by annuity or in money.

Equality of all in the partition, understood as the rights that each holds proportionally in the undivided ownership, is a rule of public policy.

###### Article 980

The undivided co-owners freely proceed with the valuations of the value of the undivided rights and property.

The property is valued at its value on the date of divided enjoyment, taking into account, where applicable, the charges encumbering it. The determination of the day corresponding to the divided enjoyment of the property by the undivided co-owners is the subject of a special clause in the deed of partition.

The date selected must be as close as possible to the partition. However, the judge may fix the divided enjoyment at an earlier date if the choice of this date appears more favorable to the achievement of equality.

C.	Judicial partition

###### Article 981

Partition is made in court when one of the undivided co-owners refuses to consent to amicable partition or if disputes arise over the manner of proceeding with it or completing it or when amicable partition has not been authorized or approved in one of the cases provided for in articles 977 and 978.
In these cases, the affixing of seals on the effects of the succession carried out as soon as possible, either at the request of the heirs, or at the instance of the public prosecutor at the Court of First Instance, or ex officio by the judge of the court within whose jurisdiction the succession is opened.

###### Article 982

Creditors may also request the affixing of seals, by virtue of an enforceable title or a permission from the judge.

###### Article 983

When the seal has been affixed, all creditors may form opposition thereto, even though they have neither an enforceable title nor permission from the judge. The formalities for the removal of seals and the preparation of the inventory are regulated by the code of civil procedure.

###### Article 984

The action for partition and the disputes that arise, either in connection with the maintenance of the undivided ownership, or during partition operations, are submitted to the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of the place of opening of the succession which has exclusive jurisdiction to hear them. Any other judge must raise ex officio his lack of jurisdiction.
It is before this court that sales by auction are conducted and that applications relating to the warranty of lots between co-partitioners and those for nullity of partition or for additional share must be brought.

###### Article 985

If it considers that the settlement of the partition is simple, the court orders the partition; if it appears complex to it, it designates, on the one hand, a notary to carry out the partition operations and, on the other hand and from within itself, a judge to supervise these operations.
The notary attests to the property rights of each, establishes the accounts of the undivided ownership, forms the estate to be partitioned and constitutes the lots.

If the appointed notary encounters the inertia of an undivided co-owner, he formally notifies him, by extrajudicial act, to be represented. If the undivided co-owner fails to appoint a representative within three months of the formal notice, the notary requests, without formality, the judge who designated him to appoint any qualified person who shall represent the defaulter until the complete completion of the operations.

###### Article 986

A co-owner may request that certain property be allocated to him or her on a preferential basis. In the event of opposition from another co-owner, the difficulty is resolved by the judge responsible for supervising the operations. This judge, for property that cannot be easily divided or allocated, orders the sale by auction of said property, under the conditions he or she determines.

###### Article 987

When the lots are constituted, each co-partitioner is permitted to submit his or her objections against their formation.
When the objections are resolved or decided by the judge, the notary proposes to the co-partitioners to agree on the allocation of the lots. Failing that, a drawing of lots is carried out.

###### Article 988

At any time, the co-partitioners may abandon the judicial route to pursue an amicable partition if the conditions provided for a partition of this nature are met.

###### § 8. Judicial maintenance in co-ownership Article 989

At the request of a co-owner, the court may stay the partition for up to two years if its immediate completion is likely to harm the value of the undivided property or if one of the co-owners can only take over the agricultural, commercial, industrial, artisanal or professional enterprise forming part of the

estate upon the expiry of that period. This stay may apply to all of the undivided property or to only some of it.

If necessary, the application for a stay of partition may relate to company shares.

###### Article 990

In the absence of an amicable agreement, the judge may order the maintenance of co-ownership of any agricultural, commercial, industrial, artisanal or professional enterprise, the operation of which was carried out by the deceased or by his or her spouse, as well as residential or professional premises actually used by the deceased or his or her spouse, and movable objects furnishing the residential premises or used in the exercise of the profession.
If necessary, the application for maintenance of co-ownership may relate to company shares.

###### Article 991

In all these cases, when there is one or more minor descendants, the application may be submitted by the surviving spouse, by any heir or by the legal representative of the minor heirs; if there are no minor descendants, the action belongs to the surviving spouse alone.
Two conditions are then added: the surviving spouse must have had the status of co-owner of the property in question, whether this status predated the death or is linked to it, and, in the case of residential premises, this surviving spouse must have resided in the premises at the time of death.

###### Article 992

The court rules according to the interests at stake and the means of subsistence that the family can derive from the undivided property.
It may order the maintenance of co-ownership for up to five years, renewable as the case may be until the death of the surviving spouse and until the youngest descendant reaches the age of majority.

###### Article 993

When only one co-owner requests partition, the court may, at the request of one or more of the co-owners who intend on the contrary to remain in co-ownership, according to the interests at stake and without prejudice to the application of articles 962 and following of this code, allocate after expert valuation his or her share to the person who requested the partition, either in kind if this share is easily detachable from the rest of the undivided property, or in value.
If there is not a sufficient sum in the co-ownership, the balance is paid by those co-owners who joined in the application, without prejudice to the possibility for the other co-owners to participate, if they express the wish to do so. Each person's share in the co-ownership is increased in proportion to his or her payment.

##### Section II

Accounting for, imputation and reduction of liberalities made to successors Article 994
Every heir, even having accepted the estate subject to an inventory, coming to an estate, must account to his or her co-heirs for everything he or she has received from the deceased, by inter vivos gifts, directly or indirectly; he or she may not retain the gifts made to him or her by the deceased, unless they were expressly made to him or her outside the estate share.

Legacies made to an heir are deemed to be made outside the estate share, unless the testator has expressed a contrary intention, in which case the legatee may only claim his or her legacy by taking less.

###### Article 995

Gifts made outside the estate share may not be retained nor legacies claimed by the heir coming to partition except up to the amount of the available portion: the excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 996

The heir who renounces the estate may nevertheless retain the inter vivos gift or claim the legacy made to him or her up to the amount of the available portion, unless the disposer has expressly required accounting in the event of renunciation.
In this case, the accounting is made in value. When the value accounted for exceeds the rights he or she should have had in the partition if he or she had participated in it, the renouncing heir compensates the accepting heirs up to the amount of this excess.

###### Article 997

The donee who was not a presumptive heir at the time of the donation, but who is found to be a successor on the day of the opening of the estate, does not owe accounting, unless the donor has expressly required it.

###### Article 998

Gifts and legacies made to the son or daughter of the person who is found to be a successor at the time of the opening of the estate are always deemed to be made with dispensation from accounting.
The father or mother coming to the estate of the donor is not required to account for them.

###### Article 999

Similarly, the son or daughter coming in his or her own right to the estate of the donor is not required to account for the gift made to his or her father or mother, even when he or she has accepted the estate; but if this child comes only by representation, he or she must account for what had been given to his or her father or mother, even in the case where he or she has renounced his or her estate.

###### Article 1000

Gifts and legacies made to the spouse of a successor spouse are deemed to be made with dispensation from accounting.

If the gifts and legacies are made jointly to two spouses, only one of whom is a successor, the latter accounts for half; if the gifts are made to the successor spouse, he or she accounts for them in full.

###### Article 1001

Accounting is only made to the estate of the donor.

###### Article 1002

Accounting is owed for what has been used for the establishment of one of the co-heirs or for the payment of his or her debts.
It is also owed in the case of a gift of fruits or revenues, unless the liberality was made expressly outside the estate share.

###### Article 1003

Expenses for food, maintenance, education, apprenticeship, ordinary equipment expenses, wedding expenses and customary gifts, need not be accounted for, unless the disposer wishes otherwise.
The character of a customary gift is assessed at the date when it is granted and taking into account the fortune of the disposer.

###### Article 1004

The same applies to profits that the heir may have derived from agreements entered into with the deceased, if these agreements presented no indirect advantage when they were made.

###### Article 1005

Similarly, no accounting is owed for partnerships formed without fraud between the deceased and one of his or her heirs, when the conditions thereof were settled by an authentic act.

###### Article 1006

Property that has perished by fortuitous event and without the fault of the donee is not subject to accounting.
However, if this property has been reconstituted by means of compensation received by reason of its loss, the donee must account for it in the proportion in which the compensation was used for its reconstitution.

If the compensation has not been used for this purpose, it is itself subject to accounting.

###### Article 1007

The fruits of things subject to collation are due only from the day of the opening of the succession. Interest is due only from the day on which the amount of collation is determined.

###### Article 1008

Collation is due only by a co-heir to his co-heir; it is not due to legatees or to creditors of the succession.

###### Article 1009

Collation is made by taking less, thus the donee retains the property received but takes, in return, less than the others in the mass to be divided in order to restore equality in figures, except in the case of the second paragraph of Article 996.
It may not be required in kind except by contrary stipulation in the deed of donation.

In the case of such a stipulation, the alienations and constitutions of real rights granted by the donee shall be extinguished by the effect of collation unless the donor has consented thereto.

###### Article 1010

The heir also has the option to collate in kind the donated property which still belongs to him provided that this property is free of any charge or occupation with which it had not already been encumbered at the time of the donation.

###### Article 1011

Collation is due of the value of the donated property at the time of partition, according to its condition at the time of the donation.
If the property has been alienated before the partition, account is taken of the value it had at the time of the alienation. If a new property has been subrogated to the alienated property, account is taken of the value of this new property at the time of partition, according to its condition at the time of acquisition. However, if the depreciation of the new property was, by reason of its nature, inevitable on the day of its acquisition, no account is taken of the subrogation.
All subject to contrary stipulation in the deed of donation.

If it results from such a stipulation that the value subject to collation is less than the determined value of the property, this difference forms an indirect advantage acquired by the donee outside the succession share.

###### Article 1012

The collation of a sum of money is equal to its amount. However, if it has been used to acquire a property, collation is due of the value of this property, under the conditions provided for in the preceding article.

###### Article 1013

When collation is made in kind and the condition of the donated objects has been improved by the act of the donee, account must be taken thereof, having regard to the amount by which their value is increased at the time of partition or alienation.
Account must likewise be taken to the donee of the necessary expenses he has incurred for the preservation of the property, even though they have not improved it.

###### Article 1014

The co-heir who makes collation in kind may retain possession of the donated property until the effective reimbursement of the sums due to him for expenses or improvements.

###### Article 1015

The donee, for his part, must, in case of collation in kind, account for the degradations and deteriorations which have diminished the value of the donated property by his act or by his fault.

##### Section III: Payment of Debts

###### § 1. Debts of Co-partitioners Article 1016

When the mass to be divided includes a claim against one of the co-partitioners, whether due or not, the latter is allotted it in the partition up to the amount of his rights in the mass.

To the corresponding extent, the debt is extinguished by confusion. If its amount exceeds the debtor's rights in this mass, he owes payment of the balance under the conditions and time limits which affected the obligation.

###### Article 1017

Except when it relates to undivided property, the claim is not due before the closing of partition operations. However, the debtor heir may decide at any time to discharge it voluntarily.

###### Article 1018

Sums subject to collation bear interest at the legal rate, unless otherwise stipulated.

This interest runs from the opening of the succession when the heir was a debtor thereof to the deceased and from the day on which the debt becomes due, when it arose during the indivision.

###### Article 1019

When the co-partitioner himself has a claim to assert, he is allotted his debt only if, balance having been struck, the account shows a balance in favour of the undivided mass.

###### § 2. Other Debts Article 1020

Co-heirs contribute among themselves to the payment of the debts and charges of the succession, each in proportion to what he takes therein.

###### Article 1021

The universal legatee contributes with the heirs, in proportion to his emolument; but the particular legatee is not liable for debts and charges, except however for the hypothecary action on the immovable bequeathed.

###### Article 1022

When immovables of a succession are encumbered with annuities by special hypothec, each of the co-heirs may require that the annuities be redeemed and the immovables rendered free before proceeding to the formation of lots.
If the co-heirs divide the succession in the state in which it is found, the encumbered immovable must be valued at the same rate as the other immovables; deduction is made of the capital of the annuity from the total price; the heir in whose lot this immovable falls remains solely charged with the service of the annuity and he must guarantee his co-heirs therefor.

###### Article 1023

Heirs are liable for the debts and charges of the succession, personally for their succession share, and hypothecarily for the whole; subject to their recourse either against their co-heirs or against the universal legatees, by reason of the share for which they must contribute thereto.

###### Article 1024

The particular legatee who has discharged the debt with which the bequeathed immovable was encumbered remains subrogated to the rights of the creditor against the heirs and universal successors.

###### Article 1025

The co-heir or universal successor who, by the effect of the hypothec, has paid beyond his share of the common debt, has recourse against the other co-heirs or universal successors only for the share which each of them must personally bear, even in the case where the co-heir who paid the debt has had himself subrogated to the rights of the creditors; without prejudice however to the rights of a co-heir who, by the effect of the benefit of inventory, has retained the faculty to claim payment of his personal claim, like any other creditor.

###### Article 1026

In case of insolvency of one of the co-heirs or universal successors, his share in the hypothecary debt is apportioned among all the others, proportionally.

###### Article 1027

Executory titles against the deceased are likewise executory against the heir personally, eight days after service of these titles has been made upon him.

###### Article 1028

The creditors of the deceased and the legatees of sums of money may request to be preferred on the succession assets over any personal creditor of the heir.
Reciprocally, the personal creditors of the heir may request to be preferred over any creditor of the deceased on the property of the heir not received by way of succession.

The right of preference gives rise to the privilege on immovables provided for in Article 2354, and it is subject to registration.

###### Article 1029

This right of preference may be exercised by any act by which a creditor manifests to the competing creditor his intention to be preferred on a determined property.
The right of preference may not be exercised when the claimant creditor has renounced it.

###### Article 1030

The right of preference is prescribed, with respect to movables, by the lapse of three years.

With respect to immovables, the action may be exercised as long as they exist in the hands of the heir.

###### Article 1031

The creditors of a co-sharer, to prevent the partition from being made in fraud of their rights, may oppose it being proceeded with outside their presence: they have the right to intervene at their own expense; but they may not challenge a completed partition, unless however it was proceeded with without them and to the prejudice of an opposition they had filed.

##### Section IV: Effects of partition and warranty of allotments Article 1032

Each co-owner is deemed to have succeeded alone and immediately to all the assets included in his allotment, or fallen to him by licitation, and never to have had ownership of the other assets of the succession.
The same applies to property that came to him by any other act having the effect of terminating the co-ownership. No distinction is made according to whether the act terminates the co-ownership in whole or in part, with regard to certain property or certain co-owners only.
However, acts validly performed either by virtue of a mandate from the co-owners, or by virtue of a judicial authorization, retain their effects whatever may be, at the time of partition, the allocation of the property that was the subject thereof.

###### Article 1033

The co-owners remain respectively warranted, one towards the other, for disturbances and evictions only that proceed from a cause prior to the partition. They are also warranted for the insolvency of the debtor of a debt placed in the allotment of a co-sharer, revealed before the partition.
The warranty does not apply if the type of eviction suffered was excepted by a particular and express clause of the partition deed; it ceases if it is by his fault that the co-owner suffers the eviction.

###### Article 1034

Each of the co-owners is personally obliged, in proportion to his share, to indemnify the evicted co-owner for the loss he has suffered. This loss is valued at the day of eviction.
If one of the co-owners is found to be insolvent, the portion for which he is liable must be equally distributed between the warranted party and all the solvent co-owners.

###### Article 1035

The action for warranty is prescribed after two years from the eviction or the discovery of the disturbance.

##### Section V: Actions for nullity of partition or for supplement of share

###### § 1. Actions for nullity of partition Article 1036

The partition may be annulled for cause of violence or fraud.
It may also be annulled for cause of error, if the error related to the existence or amount of the rights of the co-sharers or to the ownership of property included in the partitionable mass.

The action for nullity is prescribed after five years from the discovery of the defect or the cessation of the violence.

However, if it appears that the consequences of the violence, fraud or error can be remedied otherwise than by annulment of the partition, the court may, at the request of one of the parties, order a supplementary or corrective partition.

###### Article 1037

The partition may also be annulled if one of the co-owners was omitted from it.

The omitted co-owner may however request to receive his share, either in kind or in value, without annulment of the partition.
To determine this share, the property and rights on which the partition already carried out related are revalued in the same manner as if it were a new partition.

###### Article 1038

The co-sharer who has alienated his allotment in whole or in part, is no longer entitled to bring the action for nullity for error, fraud or violence, if the alienation he made is subsequent to the discovery of the error or fraud or to the cessation of the violence.

###### § 2. Action for supplement of share Article 1039

When one of the co-sharers establishes, to his prejudice, a lesion of more than one quarter, the supplement of his share is provided to him, at the choice of the defendant, either in cash or in kind.

To judge whether there has been lesion, the objects are valued according to their value at the time of the partition, which corresponds to the date of divided enjoyment.
The action for supplement of share is prescribed after two years from the partition.

###### Article 1040

The action for supplement of share is admitted against any act that has the object of terminating the co-ownership, independently of the qualification that the parties may have given to that act.
But after the partition, or the act that takes its place, the action for supplement of share is no longer admitted against the transaction made on the difficulties presented by that partition or that act.

###### Article 1041

The action is not admitted against a sale of succession rights made without fraud to a co-owner by his co-owners or by one of them, when the transfer includes a contingency defined in the deed and expressly accepted by the transferee.

###### Article 1042

The simple omission of an object of the succession gives rise to a supplementary partition relating to that property.

### Title II: Inter vivos donations and wills

Chapter I: General provisions Article 1043
A liberality is an act by which a person disposes gratuitously of all or part of his property or his rights for the benefit of another person.

A liberality may take the form only of these two categories of acts which are the inter vivos donation and the will.

###### Article 1044

The inter vivos donation is an act by which a person, the donor, transfers gratuitously to another person, the donee, who accepts it, the ownership of property.
The donor may, without being deprived of his liberal intention, impose on the donee the obligation to perform a specified prestation; the act is then called a donation with charges.

###### Article 1045

The will is an act by which the testator disposes, for the time when he will no longer exist, of all or part of his property, in full ownership or in the form of any other real right. If it is not full ownership, the right transmitted is so only for the time provided in the act and in the absence of such provision, with regard to the legatee, the object of the legacy reverting, upon its extinction, to the succession of the testator.
The will may be revoked by the testator, but the revocation is valid only insofar as it was made by authentic act or by an act entirely written and signed by the hand of the testator.

The legacy may, after the death of the testator and at the latest two months after the notification of the will to the legatee, be refused, totally or in part, by the latter or by his agent. The silence of the legatee during this period constitutes acceptance; if the legatee dies within this period, his heirs exercise the rights of their predecessor from the notification of the will made to them. The decision of the legatee is final, unless the heirs consent to his modifying it.

###### Article 1046

Any disposition by which a person is charged with preserving and returning to a third party produces effect only in the case where it is authorized by law.

###### Article 1047

Parents may impose upon the child whom they gratify the obligation to preserve and transfer the property received to his or her own children.
A person without descendants may burden a gift made to his or her brothers or sisters with an obligation requiring them to transmit the property received to their children and thereby ensure the maintenance of the property within the family.
However, clauses of inalienability affecting property given or bequeathed are valid only if they are temporary and justified by a serious and legitimate interest. Even in such case, the donee or legatee may be judicially authorized to dispose of the property if the interest that had justified the clause has disappeared or if a more important interest so requires.

The provisions of this article do not prejudice gifts made to legal persons or even to natural persons subject to the establishment of legal persons.

Any clause by which the donor deprives of the gift the person who would challenge the validity of a clause of inalienability or request authorization to alienate shall be deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1048

Any gratified person may request that the conditions and charges burdening the donations or legacies he or she has received be judicially revised when, as a result of a change in circumstances, their performance has become either extremely difficult or seriously detrimental to him or her.

The application for revision is made by principal action; it may also be made by counterclaim, in response to the action for performance or revocation brought by the heirs of the donor. It is brought against the heirs and, at the same time, against the public prosecutor if there is doubt as to the existence or identity of certain of them; if there is no known heir, it is brought against the public prosecutor. The public prosecutor must, in all cases, be given notice of the matter.

The application is admissible only ten years after the death of the donor or, in case of successive applications, ten years after the judgment ordering the previous revision. The gratified person must provide evidence of the efforts he or she has made, in the interim, to perform his or her obligations.

###### Article 1049

The judge hearing the application for revision may, as the case may be and even of his or her own motion, either reduce in quantity or periodicity the obligations burdening the gift, or modify their object in accordance with the intention of the donor, or even consolidate them with similar obligations resulting from other gifts.

He or she may authorize the alienation of all or part of the property that is the subject of the gift by ordering that the proceeds be used for purposes consistent with the will of the donor.
He or she shall prescribe measures appropriate to maintain, as far as possible, the designation that the donor had intended to give to his or her gift.

###### Article 1050

Third-party opposition to the judgment granting the application for revision is admissible only in case of fraud attributable to the donee or legatee.
The retraction or reformation of the judgment challenged does not give rise to any action against the third-party purchaser in good faith.

###### Article 1051

If, subsequent to the revision, the performance of the conditions or charges, as originally provided, becomes possible again, it may be requested by the heirs.

###### Article 1052

The clause by which the author of a gift designates a second-ranking beneficiary in the event that the beneficiary designated in the first place has predeceased or, in case of survival, refuses the gift, is authorized.
The same applies to the inter vivos or testamentary disposition by which the usufruct will be given to one person and the bare ownership to another.

###### Article 1053

In any inter vivos or testamentary disposition, impossible conditions, those that are contrary to law or morals, shall be deemed unwritten.
If the thing bequeathed perishes before the death of the donor, or if it is claimed after having been recognized as being the property of a third party, nothing is owed to the donee or legatee. If only part of the thing bequeathed perishes or is claimed after having been recognized as being the property of a third party, the donee or legatee receives the remainder.

#### Chapitre II

Of the capacity to dispose or receive by inter vivos donation or by will Article 1054
Any person may dispose and receive, either by inter vivos donation or by will, except for persons whom the law declares incapable thereof. The author of such a gift must be of sound mind. If

the donation or will was made while consent was vitiated by error, fraud or duress, the act is null.

The donation as well as the will made in favor of a foreigner is valid subject to the legal provisions in force.

###### Article 1055

The will made by a minor is valid, provided it is approved by the judge.

###### Article 1056

To be capable of receiving inter vivos, it is sufficient to be conceived at the time of the donation.

To be capable of receiving by will, it is sufficient to be conceived at the time of the death of the testator.

Nevertheless, the donation or will shall have effect only insofar as the child is born viable.

When the testator dies before the delivery of the child already conceived at the date of the will and in whose favor the will was made, from the death of the testator until the delivery, the fruits shall be subject to conservatory measures.

###### Article 1057

A minor may not, even by will, dispose in favor of his or her guardian.

A minor who has become of age or emancipated may not dispose, either by inter vivos donation or by will, in favor of the person who has been his or her guardian, if the final account of the guardianship has not been previously rendered and settled.
Excepted, in the two cases above, are the ascendants of minors, who are or have been their guardians.

###### Article 1058

Members of the medical and pharmacy professions, as well as medical auxiliaries who have provided care to a person during the illness from which he or she dies, may not benefit from inter vivos or testamentary dispositions that he or she may have made in their favor during the course of that illness.
Judicial representatives for the protection of adults and the legal persons on whose behalf they exercise their functions may likewise not benefit from inter vivos or testamentary dispositions that the persons whose protection they ensure may have made in their favor regardless of the date of the gift.

Excepted are:
1° Remunerative dispositions made on a particular basis, having regard to the means of the donor and the services rendered;
2° Universal dispositions, in the case of relationship up to and including the fourth degree, provided however that the deceased has no heirs in the direct line; unless the person in whose favor the disposition was made is himself or herself among those heirs.
The same rules shall be observed with respect to the minister of religion.

###### Article 1059

Inter vivos or testamentary dispositions in favor of health establishments, medical-social establishments, or public utility establishments shall have effect only insofar as they have been authorized by decree.

However, inter vivos or testamentary dispositions in favor of foundations, places dedicated to worship and legally constituted associations and associations, are freely accepted by them. If religious establishments are concerned, the gift is valid even if the donor and the person receiving the property are not of the same faith.

###### Article 1060

Any disposition in favor of a person, natural or legal, subject to an incapacity to receive by gratuitous title, whether it is disguised in the form of an onerous contract or made in the name of interposed persons, is sanctioned by absolute nullity.
The following shall be deemed interposed persons, until proof to the contrary: the father and mother, the children and descendants, as well as the spouse of the incapable person.

#### Chapitre III

De la réserve héréditaire, de la quotité disponible, et de la réduction Section I : De la réserve héréditaire et de la quotité disponible

###### Article 1061

The hereditary reserve is the share of property and succession rights of which the law ensures the devolution free of charges to certain heirs called reserve heirs, if they are called to the succession and if they accept it.
The beneficiaries of the reserve are:
-	the descendants of the deceased, that is to say: the children, the grandchildren, the great-grandchildren;
-	in the absence of descendants, the ascendants of the deceased, that is to say: the father and mother, the grandparents, the great-grandparents;
-	the surviving spouse, in the absence of descendants and ascendants.

The disposable portion is the share of property and succession rights that is not reserved by law and which the deceased was able to dispose of freely through liberalities.

###### Article 1062

Liberalities, whether by acts inter vivos or by will, may not exceed one-half of the property of the disposer, if he leaves at his death only one child; one-third, if he leaves two children; one-quarter, if he leaves three or a greater number;
The child who renounces the succession is included in the number of children left by the deceased only if he is represented or if he is bound to the return of a liberality in application of the provisions of article 900.

###### Article 1063

Included in article 1062, under the name of children, are descendants in whatever degree, even though they should be counted only for the child whose place they take in the succession of the disposer.

###### Article 1064

Liberalities, by acts inter vivos or by will, may not exceed three-quarters of the property if, in the absence of descendants, the deceased leaves a surviving spouse, not divorced.

###### Article 1065

In the absence of a surviving spouse and heirs, liberalities by acts inter vivos or testamentary may exhaust the totality of the property.

###### Article 1066

If the liberality consists of a usufruct or a life annuity whose value exceeds the disposable portion, the heirs for whose benefit the law makes a reserve shall have the option either to execute this disposition or to make the abandonment of the ownership of the disposable portion.

##### Section II : De la réduction des libéralités excessives Article 1067

The value in full ownership of property alienated, whether subject to a life annuity, at a loss, or with reservation of usufruct to one of the successors in direct line, is charged against the disposable portion. Such acts are requalified, irrefutably, as liberalities outside the succession share.
Any excess is returned to the mass and therefore gives rise to reduction of the excessive liberality. This charging and this reduction may be requested only by those of the other successors in direct line who did not consent to these alienations.

###### Article 1068

The disposable portion may be given in whole or in part either by act inter vivos or by will, to the children or other successors of the donor, without being subject to return by the donee or the legatee coming to the succession, provided that with regard to donations the disposition was made expressly outside the succession share.
The declaration that the donation is outside the succession share may be made either by the act that will contain the disposition or subsequently, in the form of dispositions inter vivos or testamentary.

###### Article 1069

Liberalities made as an advance on the succession share to a reserve heir who accepts the succession are charged against his reserve share and, subsidiarily, against the disposable portion, if it has not been otherwise agreed in the act that provides for them. The excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 1070

Liberalities made as an advance on the succession share to a reserve heir who renounces the succession are treated as a liberality made outside the succession share.
However, when he is bound to return in application of the provisions of article 900, the heir who renounces is treated as an accepting heir for the fictitious reunion of all the property of the deceased, the charging and, where applicable, the reduction of the liberality that was granted to him. This principle is derogated from for:
-	the premiums of a life insurance policy taken out for the benefit of a specified third party, unless they prove to be manifestly excessive in relation to the means of the insured or the transaction was merely a pure investment;
-	the costs of food, maintenance, education, apprenticeship, ordinary costs of equipment, wedding costs and customary gifts, which need not be returned unless the disposer wills otherwise, in accordance with article 1003;
-	the fruits and revenues accrued between the day of the donation and the death, in accordance with article 1081.

###### Article 1071

The liberality made outside the succession share is charged against the disposable portion. The excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 1072

The liberality made to a successor, or to successors jointly, that exceeds the disposable portion, may be retained in totality by the gratified parties, whatever the excess, subject to compensating the coheirs in money.
When the reducible portion does not exceed the reserve share of the interested party, he may always claim the totality of the bequeathed objects and therefore, execute the reduction in kind when the donated or bequeathed property still belongs to him and it is free of any charge with which it had not already been encumbered at the date of the liberality, as well as of any occupation to which it had not already been subject at that same date. This faculty is extinguished if he does not express his choice for this method of reduction within a period of three months from the date on which a reserve heir put him on notice to take a position.

###### Article 1073

When the value of donations inter vivos exceeds or equals the disposable portion, all testamentary dispositions shall lapse.

###### Article 1074

The reduction compensation is calculated, in all cases, according to the value of the property at the time of partition or alienation by the donee and according to their condition on the day the liberality took effect. If there has been subrogation, the calculation of the reduction compensation takes into account the value of the new property at the time of partition, according to their condition at the time of acquisition. However, if the depreciation of the

new property was, by reason of their nature, inevitable on the day of their acquisition, the subrogation is not taken into account.

The reduction compensation is payable at the time of partition, unless otherwise agreed between the co-heirs. However, when the liberality has as its object one of the property that may be the subject of a preferential attribution, time periods may be granted by the court, taking into account the interests involved, if they have not been granted by the disposer. The granting of these time periods may not, in any case, have the effect of deferring payment of the compensation beyond ten years from the opening of the succession. The provisions of Article 972 are then applicable to the payment of the sums due.
In the absence of agreement or stipulation to the contrary, these sums bear interest at the legal rate in civil matters. The advantages resulting from the time periods and payment terms granted do not constitute a liberality.

In case of sale of the entirety of the property given or bequeathed, the sums remaining due become immediately payable; in case of partial sales, the proceeds of these sales are paid to the co-heirs and credited against the sums still due.

###### Article 1075

Liberalities, direct or indirect, which exceed the disposable portion, are reducible to that portion upon the opening of the succession.

###### Article 1076

The reduction of inter vivos dispositions may only be requested by those for whose benefit the law makes the reserve, by their heirs or successors in title.
The donees, the legatees, and the creditors of the deceased may not request this reduction, nor benefit from it.
The limitation period for the action for reduction is set at five years from the opening of the succession, or two years from the day the heirs became aware of the infringement of their reserve, without ever being able to exceed ten years from the death.

###### Article 1077

The reduction is determined by forming a mass of all property existing at the death of the donor or testator.
There are notionally added to it, after deducting debts, those of which disposition has been made by inter vivos donation according to their condition at the time of the donation and their value at the opening of the succession. If the property has been alienated, account is taken of their value at the time of alienation and, if there has been subrogation, of the value of the new property on the day of the opening of the succession according to their condition at the time of acquisition; however, if the depreciation of the new property was, by reason of their nature, inevitable on the day of their acquisition, the subrogation is not taken into account.
There is calculated on all this property, having regard to the quality of the heirs he leaves, what is the portion of which the deceased was able to dispose.

###### Article 1078

The reduction of inter vivos donations presupposes that the value of all property included in testamentary dispositions has previously been determined. Once the reunion of property has been carried out, the reduction is effected beginning with the last donation, and so on going back from the most recent to the oldest.

###### Article 1079

When the testamentary dispositions exceed either the disposable portion, or the portion of that portion which would remain after deducting the value of inter vivos donations, the reduction shall be made proportionally, without any distinction between universal legacies and particular legacies.

###### Article 1080

Nevertheless in all cases where the testator has expressly declared that he intends that a particular legacy be satisfied in preference to the others, this preference shall take place; and the legacy which is the object thereof shall be reduced only to the extent that the value of the others would not fill the legal reserve.

###### Article 1081

When the reduction is executed in kind, the donee restores the fruits of that which exceeds the disposable portion, from the day of the death of the donor if the request for reduction was made within the year; otherwise from the day of the request.

###### Article 1082

Real rights created by the donee shall be extinguished by the effect of the reduction. These rights shall nevertheless retain their effects when the donor has consented to them in the very act of creation or in a subsequent act. The donee shall then be liable for the resulting depreciation.

###### Article 1083

The action for reduction or revendication may be exercised by the heirs against third party holders of immovables forming part of the donations and alienated by the donees, in the same manner and in the same order as against the donees themselves, and after prior discussion of their property. This action must be exercised according to the order of the dates of the alienations, beginning with the most recent.
When the donor has consented to the alienation with the agreement of all the reserve heirs born and living at the time thereof, the action may no longer be exercised against third party holders.

###### Article 1084

After prior discussion of the property of the debtor of the reduction compensation and in case of insolvency of the latter, the reserve heirs may exercise the action for reduction or revendication against third party holders of immovables forming part of the liberalities and alienated by the beneficiary. The action is exercised in the same manner as against the beneficiaries themselves and according to the order of the dates of the alienations, beginning with the most recent. It may be exercised against third party holders of movables when Article 2276 (number to be added when file No. 15 is numbered) cannot be invoked.
When, on the day of the donation or subsequently, the donor and all the presumptive reserve heirs have consented to the alienation of the property given, no reserve heir, even born after the consent of all the interested heirs has been obtained, may exercise the action against third party holders. With regard to bequeathed property, this action may no longer be exercised when the reserve heirs have consented to the alienation.

###### Article 1085

Any presumptive reserve heir may renounce, totally or partially, for example targeting only the reduction of a liberality relating to a determined property, exercising an action for reduction in a succession not yet opened, for the benefit of one or more determined persons. The renunciation binds the renouncer only from the day it has been accepted by the person from whom he has a vocation to inherit; but it may not create obligations chargeable to the person from whom one has a vocation to inherit or be conditioned on an act emanating from the latter.

###### Article 1086

The act of renunciation is, on pain of nullity, established by specific authentic act received by two notaries and mentions precisely its future legal consequences for the renouncer. The renunciation may be made in the same act by several reserve heirs, but they then sign separately before the notaries who receive the act.

The capacity required of the renouncer is that required to consent to an inter vivos donation. However, the emancipated minor may not renounce in advance the action for reduction.
The renunciation, whatever its terms, does not constitute a liberality. It is opposable to the representatives of the renouncer.

###### Article 1087

The renunciation produces no effect if the hereditary reserve of the renouncing party has not been infringed. If the infringement of the hereditary reserve has been exercised only partially, the renunciation produces effects only to the extent of the infringement of the reserve of the renouncing party resulting from the liberality granted. If the infringement of the reserve relates to a fraction greater than that provided for in the renunciation, the excess is subject to reduction.
The renunciation relating to the reduction of a liberality concerning a specific property lapses if the liberality infringing the reserve does not concern that property. The same applies if the liberality was not made for the benefit of the specified person or persons.

###### Article 1088

The renouncing party has the possibility to revoke his renunciation, but only in the following cases: 1° When the person from whom he has a vocation to inherit does not fulfill his maintenance obligations towards him;
2° When on the day of the opening of the succession, he is in a state of need that would disappear if he had not renounced his reserved rights;
3° When the beneficiary of the renunciation has been guilty of a crime or offence against his person.

###### Article1089

In case of dispute, the renouncing party shall bring the matter before the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, within one year from the day of the opening of the succession when the revocation is based on point 2° of the preceding article, and within one year from the act imputed by the renouncing party or from the day when the act could have been known by his heirs, if it is based on point 2° or 3° of the preceding article.
Revocation pursuant to 2° of the preceding article shall be pronounced only to the extent of the needs of the person who had renounced.

#### Chapter IV: Gifts inter vivos

##### Section I: Conditions and effects of gifts inter vivos Article 1090

To be valid, any gift must be executed by authentic instrument.

In case of defect in form, a gift inter vivos cannot be the subject of confirmation: it must be remade in legal form.
After the death of the donor, confirmation or voluntary execution of a gift by the heirs or successors in title of the donor entails their renunciation to oppose defects in form or any other cause of nullity.

###### Article 1091

A gift inter vivos shall bind the donor, and shall produce no effect, except from the day it has been accepted in express terms.

Acceptance may be made during the lifetime of the donor by a subsequent and authentic instrument, of which a minute shall remain; but then the gift shall have effect, with regard to the donor, only from the day when the instrument recording such acceptance has been notified to him.

###### Article 1092

If the donee is of full age, acceptance must be made by him or, in his name, by a representative endowed with express power to accept the gift made, or with general power to accept gifts that have been or might be made.
This power of attorney must be executed before a notary; and a copy must be annexed to the minute of the gift or to the minute of the acceptance that would be made by separate instrument.

###### Article 1093

A gift made to an unemancipated minor or to an adult under guardianship must be accepted by his guardian, in accordance with article 600, under the title On minority, guardianship and emancipation.
Nevertheless, the father and mother of the unemancipated minor, or other ascendants, even during the lifetime of the father and mother, although they are not guardians of the minor, may accept on his behalf.

###### Article 1094

A deaf-mute who can write may accept himself or through a representative.

If he cannot write, acceptance must be made by a curator appointed for that purpose, according to the rules established under the title On minority, guardianship and emancipation.

###### Article 1095

Gifts made for the benefit of the establishments referred to in article 1059 shall be accepted by the administrators of those establishments, after having been duly authorized.
A gift made by a terminally ill patient is deemed a legacy.

###### Article 1096

A gift duly accepted shall be perfected by the mere consent of the parties; and ownership of the objects given shall be transferred to the donee, without any other delivery being necessary.
If delivery of the thing given has not taken place, the donee has the right to require it.

###### Article 1097

When there is a gift of property susceptible to mortgages, publication of the instruments containing the gift and acceptance, as well as notification of acceptance that would have taken place by separate instrument, must be made at the mortgage office of the place where the property is situated.
When the gift is made to minors, adults under guardianship, or public establishments, publication is made at the instance of the guardians, curators or administrators.

###### Article 1098

Failure to publish may be opposed by all persons having an interest, except however those who are charged with having publication made, or their successors in title, and the donor.

###### Article 1099

Minors and adults under guardianship cannot request that the effects of failure to accept or publish gifts not operate against them, even if said guardians are found to be insolvent. Minors and adults under guardianship may however obtain compensation; against their guardians, at least if the abstention of the latter has caused them prejudice.

###### Article 1100

A gift inter vivos may comprise only the present property of the donor; if it comprises future property, it is null in that respect.

###### Article 1101

Any gift inter vivos, made subject to conditions the performance of which depends on the sole will of the donor, is null.
The same applies to a gift made subject to the condition of discharging debts or charges other than those that existed at the time of the gift.

###### Article 1102

When the donor has reserved the freedom to dispose of a property included in the gift or of a fixed sum on the property given, if he dies without having disposed of it, said property or said sum belongs to the heirs of the donor, notwithstanding any clause to the contrary.

###### Article 1103

The three preceding articles do not apply to gifts mentioned in chapters VIII and IX of this title.

###### Article 1104

Any instrument of gift of movable property shall be valid only for property of which an estimated statement, signed by the donor and the donee, or by those who accept on his behalf, has been annexed to the minute of the gift.

###### Article 1105

It is permitted for the donor to make a reservation for his own benefit or to dispose, for the benefit of another, of the enjoyment or usufruct of the movable or immovable property given.

###### Article 1106

When a gift of movable property is made with reservation of usufruct, the donee shall be required, upon expiration of the usufruct, to take the property given that will be found in kind, in the state in which it will be; and he shall have an action against the donor or his heirs, by reason of non-existing objects, up to the amount of the value given to them in the estimated statement.

###### Article 1107

The donor may stipulate the right of return of the objects given either for the case of predeceasing of the donee alone, or for the case of predeceasing of the donee and his descendants.
This right may be stipulated only for the benefit of the donor alone.

###### Article 1108

The effect of the right of return is to resolve all alienations of the property given, and to cause such property to revert to the donor, free of all charges and mortgages, except however the mortgage of the spouses, if the other property of the donee spouse is not sufficient, and only in the case where the gift will have been made to him by the same marriage contract from which these charges and mortgages result.

###### Article 1109

The donor guarantees against eviction only if he has intentionally concealed the cause of eviction or if the donation was made with charges. In the first case, the donee shall be awarded fair compensation for the damage he has suffered; in the second case, the donor is liable only up to the value of the charges performed by the donee, all subject to any contrary agreement.
In case of eviction, the donee is subrogated to the rights and actions of the donor.

###### Article 1110

The donor does not guarantee against defects in the thing donated.
However, if the donor has intentionally concealed the defect or if he has guaranteed its absence, he shall owe the donee compensation for the damage thereby caused. He shall also be liable for damages if the donation is made with charges, provided that the amount of damages does not exceed, in that case, the value of the charges performed by the donee.

##### Section II

Exceptions to the rule of irrevocability of inter vivos donations Article 1111
An inter vivos donation may be revoked only on grounds of non-performance of the conditions under which it was made, on grounds of ingratitude, and on grounds of the birth of children.

###### Article 1112

In the case of revocation on grounds of non-performance of conditions, the property shall return to the hands of the donor, free of all charges and mortgages on the part of the donee; and the donor shall have, against third-party holders of the immovable property donated, all the rights he would have against the donee himself.

###### Article 1113

An inter vivos donation may be revoked on grounds of ingratitude only in the following cases: 1° If the donee has made an attempt on the life of the donor;
2° If he has been guilty towards him of violence, offences or serious insults; 3° If he refuses him maintenance.

###### Article 1114

Revocation on grounds of non-performance of conditions, or on grounds of ingratitude, shall never take place by operation of law.

###### Article 1115

The claim for revocation on grounds of ingratitude must be brought within one year from the day of the offence imputed by the donor to the donee or from the day the offence could have been known by the donor.
This revocation may not be claimed by the donor against the heirs of the donee, nor by the heirs of the donor against the donee, unless, in the latter case, the action was brought by the donor, or he died within the year of the offence.

###### Article 1116

Revocation on grounds of ingratitude does not prejudice either the alienations made by the donee, or the mortgages and other real charges he may have imposed on the object of the donation, provided that all of this is prior to the publication, at the mortgage registry of the location of the property, of the claim for revocation.
In the case of revocation, the donee is ordered to restore the value of the alienated objects, having regard to the time of the claim, and the fruits, from the day of that claim.

###### Article 1117

Donations in favour of marriage are not revocable on grounds of ingratitude.

###### Article 1118

All inter vivos donations made by persons who had no children or descendants actually living at the time of the donation, of whatever value those donations may be, and under whatever title they were made, and even if they were mutual or remuneratory, even those which would have been made in favour of marriage by persons other than the spouses to each other, may be revoked, if the deed of donation so provides, by the birth of a child born to the donor, even after his death, or adopted by him in the forms and conditions provided for in Chapter I of Title IX of Book I.

###### Article 1119

This revocation may take place even if the child of the donor or the female donor was conceived at the time of the donation.

###### Article 1120

The donation may likewise be revoked even if the donee has entered into possession of the donated property, and has been left there by the donor since the birth of the child. However, the donee is not required to restore the fruits he has received, of whatever nature they may be, except from the day on which the birth of the child or his adoption in plenary form was notified to him by writ or other act in due form, even if the claim to recover the donated property was made after that notification.

###### Article 1121

The property included in the revoked donation returns to the patrimony of the donor, free of all charges and mortgages on the part of the donee, without being able to remain subject, even subsidiarily, to the mortgage of the spouses; which shall take place even if the donation was made in favour of the marriage of the donee and inserted in the contract, and the donor bound himself as surety, by the donation, to the performance of the marriage contract.

###### Article 1122

The death of the donor's child has no effect on the revocation of donations provided for in Article 1118.

The donor may renounce the exercise of revocation for the birth of a child, at any time, that is to say before or after the birth of the child.

###### Article 1123

The action for revocation is barred by limitation after five years from the birth or adoption of the last child.
It may be exercised only by the donor.

#### Chapitre V

Testamentary dispositions Section I: General rules

###### Article 1124

Any person may dispose by will, whether under the title of institution of heir, or under the title of legacy, or under any other designation appropriate to manifest his will.

###### Article 1125

A will may not be made in the same act by two or more persons, whether for the benefit of a third party or as a reciprocal or mutual disposition.

###### Article 1126

To be valid, a will must be made by an authentic act or by an act entirely written and signed by the hand of the testator.

###### Article 1127

A will by authentic act is received either by two notaries, or by one notary assisted by two witnesses who may be neither the legatees, in whatever capacity, nor their relatives or in-laws up to and including the fourth degree, nor the clerks of the notaries by whom the acts are received.
In both circumstances, the will is dictated by the testator and, as the case may be, one of the two notaries or the notary writes it himself or has it written by hand or mechanically.
It is then obligatorily read to the testator.
When the testator cannot express himself in French or Arabic, the dictation and reading may be accomplished by an interpreter whom the testator chooses from the list of judicial experts provided for in Article L.356-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The interpreter ensures the exact translation of the statements made. The notary is not required to use an interpreter when he himself as well as, as the case may be, the other notary or the witnesses understand the language in which the testator expresses himself.

When the testator can write in French or Arabic but cannot speak, the notary writes the will himself or has it written by hand or mechanically from notes drafted before him by the testator, then reads it to the latter. When the testator cannot hear, he takes cognizance of the will by reading it himself, after reading by the notary. When the testator can neither speak or hear, nor read or write, the dictation or reading are accomplished, when possible, through the intermediary of a sign language interpreter and according to the same procedures.

The act expressly mentions compliance with the above-mentioned requirements.

###### Article 1128

This will by authentic act must be signed by the testator in the presence, as the case may be, of the witnesses and the notary or the two notaries; if the testator declares that he does not know how or cannot sign, the act bears his fingerprint.
It is also signed, as the case may be, by the witnesses and by the notary or the two notaries.

###### Article 1129

The mystic will is the will whose content remains hidden until the death of the person. When the testator wishes to make a mystic will, the paper containing the dispositions or the paper serving as an envelope, if there is one, is delivered closed, sealed and stamped, either to a notary before two witnesses, or to two notaries, or closed, sealed and stamped in their presence. The testator then declares that the content of this paper is his will, signed by him, and written by him or by another, affirming, in the latter case, that he has personally verified the wording. He indicates, in all cases, the mode of writing he has used (by hand or mechanical).
As the case may be, the notary or the notaries, write or have written by hand or mechanically on this paper or on the sheet that will serve as an envelope intended to contain it, the date and indication of the place where the mystic will is executed, the description of the fold and the impression of the seal, and mention of all the above formalities; this act is signed both by the testator and by the notary and the witnesses, or by the two notaries. If the testator, either by an impediment arising since the signing of the will, or because he does not know how to sign, has not been able to sign this act, mention is made of it as well as the reason he has given for it.

All of these operations must be carried out in one continuous action and without interruption.

###### Article 1130

Those who do not know how or cannot read cannot make dispositions in the form of a mystic will.
On the other hand, the testator who cannot speak but who knows how to write, may make a mystic will, on the express condition that the will be signed by him and written by him or by another, that he present it to the notary and the witnesses, or to the two notaries, and that at the top of the superscription act he write, in their presence, that the paper he presents is his will, this before signing the act. As the case may be, the notary or the notaries, write on this act that the testator has written and signed these words in his presence and that of the witnesses, or in their presence. The provisions of Article 1129, except those contrary to this article, are applicable.

In all cases provided for in this article or in the preceding articles, the mystic will in which the legal formalities have not been observed, and which will be null as such, shall nevertheless be valid as a holographic will if all the conditions required for its validity as a holographic will are fulfilled, even if it has been qualified as a mystic will.

###### Article 1131

The witnesses called to be present at wills must be Djiboutian and of age, know how to sign and have the enjoyment of their civil rights. They may be of either sex, but husband and wife may not be witnesses in the same act.

###### Article 1132

The wills of military personnel, sailors of the State and persons employed in the service of the armies may be received in the cases and conditions provided for in Article 125 in one of the following forms:
1° by a senior officer or military doctor of a corresponding rank, in the presence of two witnesses;
2° by two officials of the intendancy or commissariat officers or by one of these officials or officers in the presence of two witnesses;
3° in case of an isolated detachment and if there does not exist in this detachment a senior officer or military doctor of a corresponding rank, an official of the intendancy or a commissariat officer, by the officer commanding this detachment assisted by two witnesses;
4° if the testator is sick or wounded and staying in a military hospital or health formation, by the chief physician, whatever his rank, assisted by the managing administrative officer. In the absence of this administrative officer, the presence of two witnesses is necessary.
The will of the officer commanding an isolated detachment may be received by the officer who comes after him in the order of service.

The faculty to make a will under the conditions provided for in this article extends to prisoners with the enemy.
In all cases, a duplicate original of the wills thus established is made. If this formality of the duplicate cannot be fulfilled by reason of the state of health of the testator, a copy of the will is drawn up to take the place of the second original; this copy is signed by the witnesses and by the instrumenting officers. Mention is made therein of the causes that prevented the drawing up of the second original.

As soon as communication is possible, and within the shortest time, the two originals or the original and the copy of the will are sent, separately and by different couriers, under closed and sealed cover, to the Minister of Defence, to be deposited with the notary indicated by the testator or, in the absence of indication, with the president of the chamber of notaries.

The will made in the form established above is null by operation of law six months after the testator has arrived in a place where he has the freedom to employ the ordinary forms, unless, before the expiration of this period, he has again been placed in one of the special situations provided for in Article 125. The will is then valid for the duration of this special situation and for a new period of six months after its expiration.

All the formalities provided for must be observed on pain of nullity.

###### Article 1133

During a maritime voyage, both en route and during a stop in a port, when it is impossible to communicate with land or when there is no Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agent invested with the functions of a notary in the port, if one is abroad, the wills of persons present on board shall be received, in the presence of two witnesses:
1° on State vessels, by the administrative officer or, in his absence, by the commander or the person performing his functions. The will of the administrative officer is received by the commander or by the person performing his functions, and, if there is no administrative officer, the will of the commander is received by the person who comes after him in the order of service;
2° on other vessels, by the captain, master or skipper, assisted by the ship's mate, or, in their absence, by those who replace them. The will of the captain, master or skipper, or that of the mate, is received by the persons who come after them in the order of service.
The instrument indicates which of the circumstances provided for above it is received in.

In all cases, a duplicate original of the wills thus drawn up is made. If this formality of the duplicate cannot be fulfilled by reason of the state of health of the testator, a copy of the will is drawn up to take the place of the second original; this copy is signed by the witnesses and by the instrumental officers. Mention is made therein of the causes which prevented the drawing up of the second original.

At the first stop in a foreign port where there is a Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agent, one of the originals or the copy of the will is delivered, under sealed cover, into the hands of this official, who forwards it to the Minister of Defence, to be deposited with the notary indicated by the testator or, in the absence of an indication, with the president of the chamber of notaries.
And, upon the arrival of the vessel in a port of Djibouti, the two originals of the will or the original and its copy, or the original that remains, in case of transmission or delivery effected during the course of the voyage, shall be deposited, under sealed cover, for State vessels, at the armaments office, and for other vessels at the maritime registration office. Each of these documents shall be forwarded, separately and by different couriers, to the Minister of Defence, who shall transmit them as stated in the preceding paragraph.

The will made during a maritime voyage, in the form prescribed by Article 1132, shall be valid only insofar as the testator dies on board or within six months after he has disembarked in a place where he was able to remake it in the ordinary forms. However, if the testator undertakes a new maritime voyage before the expiration of this period, the will is valid for the duration of that voyage and for a new period of six months after the testator has disembarked again.
All the formalities provided for must be observed on pain of nullity.

###### Article 1134

Provisions inserted in a will made, during a maritime voyage, for the benefit of the officers of the vessel other than those who are relatives or relations by marriage of the testator, are null and void.

###### Article 1135
