The testator, in the cases of Articles 1132 and 1133, is informed, in the presence of the witnesses, that his will shall be null and void by operation of law six months after he has arrived in a place where he has the freedom

to employ the ordinary forms, unless, before the expiration of this period, he is again placed in a situation that falls under the said articles.

###### Article 1136

On pain of nullity, wills must be signed by the testator, by those who have received them and by the witnesses.
If the testator declares that he cannot or does not know how to sign, mention shall be made of his declaration, as well as of the cause which prevents him from signing.
In the case where the presence of two witnesses is required, the will shall be signed by at least one of them, and mention shall be made of the reason why the other has not signed.

###### Article 1137

A Djiboutian who is in a foreign country may make his testamentary dispositions by private instrument or by authentic instrument, with the forms customary in the place where that instrument is executed.
Such wills made in a foreign country may be executed on property situated in Djibouti only after having been registered at the office of the testator's domicile, if he has retained one, otherwise at the office of his last known domicile in Djibouti. In the case where the will contains dispositions of immovable property situated therein, it must, in addition, be registered at the office of the location of such immovable property, without a double duty being chargeable.

##### Section II: Institutions of heirs and legacies in general Article 1138

Testamentary dispositions are either universal, or by universal title, or by particular title.

Each of these dispositions shall produce its effect according to the rules established hereinafter for universal legacies, for legacies by universal title, and for particular legacies.

###### Article 1139

Unless the disposer wills otherwise, when the succession has been accepted by at least one heir designated by law, the legatee may confine his emolument to a part of the property disposed of in his favour. This confinement does not constitute a liberality made by the legatee to the other successors.
Unless the disposer wills otherwise, any person gratified with a legacy may decide to receive only a part of the property provided, provided that the succession has been accepted by at least one heir designated by law. This decision of the legatee is not considered as a liberality from the legatee to the other successors.

###### Sous-section 1: Universal legacy Article 1140

The universal legacy is the testamentary disposition by which the testator gives to one or more persons the universality of the property he will leave at his death.

###### Article 1141

When at the death of the testator there are heirs to whom a portion of his property is reserved by law, these heirs are seized by operation of law, by his death, of all the property of the succession; and the universal legatee is required to request from them the delivery of the property included in the will.

Nevertheless, in the same cases, the universal legatee shall have the enjoyment of the property included in the will, from the day of death, if the request for delivery was made within the year from that time; otherwise, this enjoyment shall begin only from the day of the request made in court, or from the day that the delivery was voluntarily consented to.

###### Article 1142

When at the death of the testator there are no heirs to whom a portion of his property is reserved by law, the universal legatee shall be seized by operation of law by the death of the testator. If the will was executed by authentic instrument, he is not required to request delivery by a sending into possession; in the contrary case, the legatee is required to have himself sent into possession, by an order of the president, placed at the bottom of a petition, to which is attached the instrument of deposit.

###### Article 1143

Every will under private signature is, before being executed, deposited with a notary. The will is opened if it is sealed. The notary immediately draws up a report of the opening and the condition of the will, specifying the circumstances of the deposit. The will as well as the report are kept among the records of the depositary.
Within one month following the date of the report, the notary sends a copy thereof and a facsimile copy of the will to the clerk of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of the place where the succession is opened, who acknowledges receipt of these documents and keeps them among his records.

###### Article 1144

The universal legatee, who is in concurrence with an heir to whom the law reserves a portion of the property, is liable for the debts and charges of the testator's succession, personally for his share and portion and by mortgage for the whole; and he is required to discharge all legacies, except in the case of reduction, as explained in Articles 1079 and 1080.

###### Sous-section 2 : Du legs à titre universel Article 1145

A legacy by general title is one by which the testator bequeaths a share of the property which the law permits him to dispose of, for example, one half, one third, or all his immovable property, or all his movable property, or a fixed portion of all his immovable property or of all his movable property.

Any other legacy constitutes only a disposition by particular title.

###### Article 1146

Legatees by general title must request delivery from the heirs to whom a portion of the property is reserved by law; in their absence, from the universal legatees and, in the absence of the latter, from the heirs called in the order established in the title On Successions.
The delivery of legacies may be effected amicably; it may be recorded by an instrument under private signature: a written, dated and signed document. However, an authentic instrument must be drawn up when immovable property is involved. Whether it is an instrument under private signature or an authentic instrument, the delivery of legacies specifies the property concerned.

###### Article 1147

The legatee by general title is liable, like the universal legatee, for the debts and charges of the testator's succession, personally for his share and portion, and by mortgage for the whole.

When the testator has disposed of only a portion of the disposable portion, and has done so by general title, this legatee is required to discharge particular legacies by contribution with the natural heirs.

###### Sous-section 3 : Des legs particuliers Article 1148

Every pure and simple legacy gives the legatee, from the day of the testator's death, a right to the thing bequeathed, a right transmissible to his heirs or successors in title.
Nevertheless, the particular legatee cannot take possession of the thing bequeathed, nor claim the fruits or interest thereof, except from the day of his demand for delivery, made according to the order established in the title On Successions, or from the day on which such delivery was voluntarily granted to him.

###### Article 1149

The interest or fruits of the thing bequeathed accrue to the benefit of the legatee, from the day of death, and without his having made his demand in court:
1° When the testator has expressly declared his will, in this regard, in the will; 2° When a life annuity or pension has been bequeathed as maintenance.

###### Article 1150

The costs of the demand for delivery are chargeable to the succession, without however resulting in any reduction of the legal reserve.
Registration fees are payable by the legatee. All of the foregoing, unless otherwise stipulated in the will.
Each legacy may be registered separately, without such registration being able to benefit anyone other than the legatee or his successors in title.

###### Article 1151

The heirs of the testator, or other debtors of a legacy, are personally bound to discharge the legacy, each in proportion to the share and portion in which they will benefit from the succession.
They are bound, by mortgage for the whole, to deliver the thing bequeathed with the necessary accessories and in the condition in which it will be found on the day of the donor's death, up to the value of the immovable property of the succession of which they are holders. However, if the person who bequeathed the ownership of an immovable property subsequently increased it by acquisitions, these acquisitions, even if they are contiguous, shall not be deemed, without a new disposition, to form part of the legacy. On the other hand, embellishments, or new constructions made on the bequeathed property are necessarily included in the legacy.

###### Article 1152

If, before the will or since, the thing bequeathed has been the subject of a real right by the testator, the legatee receives the bequeathed property in the condition in which it is at the time of the disposer's death and the person who must deliver the legacy is not required to free this property before delivering it.

###### Article 1153

When the testator has bequeathed the thing of another, the legacy is null, even if the testator did not know that it did not belong to him.

###### Article 1154

When the legacy relates to an indeterminate thing, the heir is not obliged to give it of the best quality, and he cannot offer it of the worst.

###### Article 1155

A legacy made to a creditor is not deemed to be in compensation for his debt, nor is a legacy made to a servant in compensation for his wages.

###### Article 1156

The particular legatee is not liable for the debts of the succession, except for the reduction of the legacy as stated above, and except for the mortgage action of creditors.

##### Section III : Des mandataires et exécuteurs testamentaires Article 1157

The heirs may, by mutual agreement, entrust the administration of the succession to one of them or to a third party. The mandate is governed by the provisions of Articles 2175 and following.
When at least one heir has accepted the succession up to the net assets, the mandatory cannot, even with the agreement of all the heirs, be designated except by the judge.
The judge may also be petitioned by any interested party or by the public prosecutor to designate a qualified person as succession mandatory, for the purpose of provisionally administering the succession by reason of the inertia, failure or fault of one or more heirs in this administration, their disagreement, a conflict of interests between them or the complexity of the succession situation.

###### Article 1158

In the preceding cases, the mandate or the judge, as the case may be, fixes the duration of the mission of the appointed mandatory, the limit of his powers and his remuneration.
The appointment of a testamentary mandatory is the subject of publication at the mortgage registry.

###### Article 1159

At the request of any interested party or the public prosecutor, the judge may remove the succession mandatory, and designate another, when the first has failed in his mission.
The mission ceases by operation of law by the effect of an agreement of joint ownership between the heirs or by the signing of the deed of partition. It also ceases when the judge finds the complete execution of the mission entrusted to the succession mandatory.

###### Article 1160

As soon as the succession has been accepted by at least one heir, either purely and simply, or subject to inventory, the judge who designated the succession mandatory may authorize him to perform all acts of administration of the succession.

He may also authorize him, at any time, to carry out acts of disposition necessary for the proper administration of the succession and determine the prices and stipulations thereof.

###### Article 1161

The testator may appoint one or more testamentary executors, enjoying full civil capacity, to oversee or carry out the execution of his wishes.
The testamentary executor who has accepted his mission is bound to perform it in the same capacity as a gratuitous agent. He assumes responsibility for it. He ensures that the will is executed; and, in case of dispute over its validity or execution, he must be made a party or intervene as the case may be to uphold its validity or require the execution of the disputed provisions.

The testamentary executor exercises his mission gratuitously, except for a particular legacy made having regard to the means of the disposer and the services rendered.

###### Article 1162

The testator may authorize the testamentary executor to take possession of all or only part of the movable property of the estate, and to sell it if necessary to discharge particular legacies within the limit of the available portion; this possession may not last beyond a year and a day from the opening of the will.
The heir may terminate the possession by offering to deliver to the testamentary executors a sum sufficient for the payment of movable legacies or by proving such payment.

###### Article 1163

In the absence of an accepting forced heir, the testator may authorize, for a period of two years from the opening of the will, the testamentary executor to dispose of all or part of the immovable property of the estate, receive and invest capital, pay debts and charges and proceed with the allocation or partition of the remaining property among the heirs and legatees.
On pain of being unenforceable, the sale of an immovable property of the estate may only take place after the heirs have been informed by the testamentary executor.

###### Article 1164

The authorizations provided for in the two preceding articles may, by decision of the judge, be extended by one year at most.

###### Article 1165

If there are several testamentary executors who have accepted their mission, only one may act in the absence of the others, unless the testator has provided otherwise or has divided their functions. In case of joint acceptance, they are jointly and severally liable for the account of the property entrusted to them.

###### Article 1166

The testamentary executor takes all conservatory measures useful for the proper execution of the will.
He may make, in the presence of the presumptive heir, or the heir duly summoned, the inventory of the property of the estate.

He arranges for the sale of movable property in the absence of sufficient liquid assets to discharge the legacies and urgent debts of the estate.

###### Article 1167

In case of dispute over the validity or execution of the will, the testamentary executor must be made a party or intervene as the case may be, to uphold its validity or require the execution of the disputed provisions.

###### Article 1168

The mission of the testamentary executor ends:
-	upon completion of his mission;
-	by decision of the judge, who relieves him of his mission for serious reasons;
-	by his death, his powers not being transmissible to his heirs.

The testamentary executor renders account within six months following the end of his mission; in case of death, this obligation is imposed on his heirs.

###### Article 1169

The expenses incurred by the testamentary executor in the exercise of his mission are chargeable to the estate. He is reimbursed before the delivery of legacies.

##### Section IV : De la révocation des testaments et de leur caducité Article 1170

Wills may be revoked, in whole or in part, only by a subsequent will or by an act before a notary declaring the change of intention.

###### Article 1171

In the absence of express revocation, the testator is deemed to have tacitly revoked his will:

1° By a subsequent will whose provisions prove incompatible with the previous ones. In this case, the new provisions replace the old ones;
2° By the voluntary alienation of the thing bequeathed when the legacy is particular and has as its object a specific thing, even if the alienation should subsequently be called into question, subject to the contrary intention expressed by the testator in the act of alienation;

3° By the destruction or voluntary alteration of the will. In case of erasure or tearing of only part of the paper containing the testamentary provisions, there is no revocation of the provisions mentioned on the preserved part, at least if these fulfill the formal conditions provided by law.

###### Article 1172

The revocation made in a subsequent will has full effect, even if this new act should remain without execution due to the incapacity of the instituted heir or the legatee, or by their refusal to take the succession or the legacy.
The revocation of a will does not revive the previously established will in the absence of a clearly manifested intention to that effect by the deceased.

###### Article 1173

Any testamentary provision lapses if the person in whose favor it is made does not survive the testator.
The same applies when the testamentary provision had been made under a condition, and the instituted heir or the legatee dies before the fulfillment of this condition, except in the case of a

suspensive condition whose right was immediately acquired by the instituted heir, or the legatee and who, in this case, transmits this right to his heirs.

###### Article 1174

The testamentary provision lapses:
1° If the thing bequeathed has totally perished during the life of the testator;
2° If the thing bequeathed has perished since the death of the testator, without the act and fault of the heir, although the heir has been put in default to deliver it, when it would equally have had to perish in the hands of the legatee;
3° When the instituted heir or the legatee renounces it or is incapable of taking it.

###### Article 1175

In the absence of provision in the testamentary provisions, the revocation, lapse or nullity of a legacy benefits the debtors of the revoked, lapsed or null legacy or legacies, that is to say, as the case may be, the heir, the universal legatee or the legatee by general title. Thus, the ineffectiveness of a universal legacy benefits the heirs; in the absence of a forced heir, the ineffectiveness of a particular legacy benefits the universal legatee.
By exception, the property included in the legacy deprived of effect may be transmitted to the other legatees. There is thus accretion when the legacy has been made to several persons jointly. Two types of legacies are deemed joint within the meaning of this article, namely:
-	the legacy made by one and the same provision of the will and without assignment of shares to each of the co-legatees;
-	the legacy, to several persons, of a thing that can be divided without deterioration.

###### Article 1176

After the death of the testator, the legacies he had established may be revoked judicially if the legatee:
1° Has not performed the charges incumbent upon him; 2° Has made an attempt on the life of the testator;
3° Has been guilty towards the testator of abuse, offenses or serious insults; 4° Has uttered a serious insult against the memory of the testator.
The action for revocation belongs to all those who have an interest in it: the heirs of the testator, the universal legatees, and by indirect action the creditors of the testator, the heirs or the legatees. The testamentary executor is also entitled to seek revocation for non-performance of charges. On the other hand, the beneficiary of the legacy, as well as the beneficiary of the charge may only bring the action for performance.

In case 4°, the action must be brought within one year, from the day of the offense.

#### Chapter VI

Gradual and residual liberalities Section I: Gradual liberalities

###### Article 1177

A liberality may be burdened with a charge requiring the donee or legatee to preserve the property or rights that are its object and to transmit them, upon his death, to a second beneficiary designated in the instrument.

###### Article 1178

The liberality thus granted may only take effect on property or rights identifiable at the date of transmission and subsisting in kind at the death of the person burdened.

When it relates to securities, the liberality also takes effect, in case of alienation, on the securities that have been subrogated thereto.

When it concerns immovable property, the charge burdening the liberality is subject to publication.

###### Article 1179

The rights of the second beneficiary open at the death of the person burdened.

However, the person burdened may relinquish, for the benefit of the second beneficiary, the enjoyment of the property or right that is the object of the liberality.
This anticipated relinquishment may not prejudice the creditors of the person burdened prior to the relinquishment, nor third parties having acquired, from the latter, a right over the property or right relinquished.

###### Article 1180

The second beneficiary is deemed to hold his rights from the author of the liberality. The same applies to his heirs when they receive the liberality under the conditions provided for in Article 1066.

###### Article 1181

It is for the disposer to prescribe guarantees and securities for the proper performance of the charge.

###### Article 1182

The second beneficiary may not be subjected to the obligation to preserve and transmit.

If the charge has been stipulated beyond the first degree, it remains valid but for the first degree only.

###### Article 1183

If the person burdened is a forced heir of the disposer, the charge may only be imposed on the disposable portion.
The donee may however accept, in the deed of donation or subsequently in an instrument established by specific authentic act received by two notaries, that the charge burdens all or part of his forced share. The instrument is signed in the presence of the notaries alone and mentions precisely its future legal consequences for the donee, on pain of nullity.
The legatee may, within one year from the day on which he became aware of the will, request that his forced share be, in whole or in part, freed from the charge. Failing this, he must assume its performance.
The charge relating to the forced share of the person burdened, with his consent, benefits by operation of law, to that extent, all his children born and to be born.

###### Article 1184

The author of a gradual donation may revoke it with respect to the second beneficiary as long as the latter has not notified, in the forms required for donations, his acceptance to the donor.
By way of derogation from Article 1091, the gradual donation may be accepted by the second beneficiary after the death of the donor.

###### Article 1185

When the second beneficiary dies before the person burdened or renounces the benefit of the gradual liberality, the property or rights that were its object form part of the succession of the person burdened, unless the instrument expressly provides that his heirs may receive it or designates another second beneficiary.

##### Section II: Residual liberalities Article 1186

It may be provided in a liberality that a person will be called to receive what will remain of the gift or legacy made to a first beneficiary at the death of the latter.

###### Article 1187

The residual liberality does not oblige the first beneficiary to preserve the property received. It obliges him to transmit the subsisting property.
When the property, objects of the residual liberality, have been alienated by the first beneficiary, the rights of the second beneficiary do not transfer either to the proceeds of these alienations or to new property acquired.

###### Article 1188

The first beneficiary may not dispose by will of the property given or bequeathed on a residual basis.

The residual liberality may prohibit the first beneficiary from disposing of the property by inter vivos donation.

However, when he is a forced heir, the first beneficiary retains the possibility of disposing inter vivos or upon death of the property that has been given as an advancement on his succession share.

###### Article 1189

The first beneficiary is not required to account for his management to the disposer or to his heirs.

###### Article 1190

The provisions set forth in Articles 1178, 1180, 1181, 1184 and 1185 are applicable to residual liberalities.

#### Chapter VII

Partition donations and partition wills Section I: General provisions

###### Article 1191

Any person may make, among his presumptive heirs, the distribution and partition of his property.

This instrument may be made in the form of a partition donation or a partition will. It is subject to the formalities, conditions and rules prescribed for inter vivos donations in the first case and wills in the second, subject to the application of the provisions that follow.

###### Article 1192

Any person may also make the distribution and partition of his property and rights among descendants of different degrees, whether or not they are his presumptive heirs. The agreement of the forced heirs is then necessary.

###### Article 1193

The action for supplement of share on grounds of lesion may not be brought against partition donations and partition wills.

The provisions of Article 972, first paragraph, are applicable to balancing payments charged to the donees, notwithstanding any provision to the contrary.

###### Article 1195

If all the property that the disposer leaves at the day of his death has not been included in the partition, those of his property that have not been included therein are allocated or partitioned in accordance with the law.

##### Section II: Partition donations

###### § 1. Partition donations made to presumptive heirs Article 1196

The partition donation may only have as its object present property.

The donation and the partition may be made by separate instruments provided that the ascendant participates in both instruments.

###### Article 1197

In case of a partition donation made jointly by two spouses, the non-common child may be allotted from his parent in separate property of the latter or in common property, without the spouse being able however to be co-donor of the common property.

###### Article 1198

Property received as anticipated partition by a presumptive forced heir is imputable to his forced share, unless it has been expressly given outside the share.

###### Article 1199

The forced heir who has not participated in the partition donation, or who has received a lot less than his forced share, may exercise the action for reduction, if there does not exist at the opening of the succession property not included in the partition and sufficient to compose or complete his forced share, taking into account the liberalities from which he may have benefited.

###### Article 1200

Partition donations follow the rules of inter vivos donations for everything concerning imputation, calculation of the forced share and reduction.
The action for reduction may only be brought after the death of the disposer who made the partition. In case of a partition donation made jointly by both spouses, the action for reduction may only be brought after the death of the survivor of the disposers, except for the non-common child who may act from the death of his parent. The action is prescribed by five years from that death.

The child not yet conceived at the time of the partition donation has a similar action to compose or complete his hereditary share.

###### Article 1201

Notwithstanding the rules applicable to gifts inter vivos, the donated property shall, unless otherwise agreed, be valued at the date of the gift-partition for the purposes of imputation and calculation of the reserved portion, provided that all forced heirs alive or represented at the death of the ascendant have received a lot in the advance partition and have expressly accepted it, and that no usufruct reserve over a sum of money has been provided for.

The lot of certain donees may be formed, in whole or in part, from gifts, whether subject to collation or not, already received by them from the donor, having regard where applicable to the investments and reinvestments they may have made in the meantime.

The valuation date applicable to the advance partition shall also be applicable to prior gifts that have been thus incorporated into it. Any provision to the contrary shall be deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1203

The parties may also agree that a prior gift made outside the share shall be incorporated into the partition and imputed to the donee's reserved portion as an advancement of succession share.

###### Article 1204

The agreements referred to in the two preceding articles may take place even in the absence of new gifts from the donor. They are not regarded as liberalities between presumptive heirs, but as a partition made by the donor.

###### § 2

Gift-partitions made to descendants of different degrees Article 1205
When an ascendant proceeds with a gift-partition, his children may consent to their own descendants being allotted therein in their place and stead, in whole or in part.
Descendants of a subsequent degree may, in the advance partition, be allotted separately or jointly among themselves.

###### Article 1206

This liberality constitutes a gift-partition even where the ascendant donor has only one child, whether the partition is made between the latter and his descendants or between his descendants only.
It requires the consent, in the deed, of the child who renounces all or part of his rights, as well as of his descendants who benefit therefrom. The liberality is null and void where the consent of the renouncing party has been vitiated by error, fraud or duress.

###### Article 1207

Where descendants of different degrees participate in the same gift-partition, the partition is effected by stirpes.
Attributions may be made to descendants of different degrees in certain stirpes and not in others.

###### Article 1208

Gift-partitions made to descendants of different degrees may include the agreements provided for in articles 1202 to 1204.

###### Article 1209

In the succession of the ascendant donor, the property received by the children or their descendants as an advance partition is imputed to the reserved portion accruing to their stirps and subsidiarily to the disposable portion.
All gifts made to members of the same stirps are imputed together, regardless of the degree of relationship with the deceased.

Where all the children of the ascendant donor have given their consent to the advance partition and no usufruct reserve over a sum of money has been provided for, the property with which the donees have been allotted is valued according to the rule provided for in article 1201.

If the descendants of a stirps have not received a lot in the gift-partition or have received therein only a lot less than their reserved portion, they are made whole in their rights according to the rules provided for in articles 1199 and 1200.

###### Article 1210

In the succession of the child who has consented to his own descendants being allotted in his place and stead, the property received by them from the ascendant is treated as if they held it from their direct ancestor.
This property is subject to the rules governing gifts inter vivos for notional reunion, imputation, collation and, where applicable, reduction.
However, where all the descendants have received and accepted a lot in the advance partition and no usufruct over a sum of money has been provided for, the property with which the donees have been allotted is treated as if they had received it from their ancestor by gift-partition.

###### Article 1211

The rules laid down in article 1210 do not apply where the child who has consented to his own descendants being allotted in his place and stead subsequently proceeds himself, with the latter, to a gift-partition into which is incorporated the property previously received under the conditions provided for in article 1205.
This new gift-partition may include the agreements provided for in articles 1202 and 1203.

##### Section III: Testamentary partitions Article 1212

A testamentary partition produces the effects of a partition. Its beneficiaries may not renounce reliance on the will to claim a new partition of the succession.

###### Article 1213

The beneficiary who has not received a lot equal to his reserved portion may exercise the action for reduction in accordance with article 1200.

#### Chapter VIII

Gifts made by marriage contract to the spouses, and to children to be born of the marriage

###### Article 1214

Any gift inter vivos of present property, although made by marriage contract to the spouses, or to one of them, shall be subject to the general rules prescribed for gifts made in that capacity.
It may not take place for the benefit of children to be born, except in the cases set out in Chapter VI of this Title.

###### Article 1215

The father and mother, other ascendants, collateral relatives of the spouses, and even strangers, may, by marriage contract, dispose of all or part of the property they will leave at the day of their death, both for the benefit of the said spouses and for the benefit of the children to be born of their marriage, in the event that the donor survives the donee spouse.

Such a gift, although made for the benefit only of the spouses or one of them, shall always, in the said event of the donor's survival, be presumed to be made for the benefit of the children and descendants to be born of the marriage.

###### Article 1216

The gift in the form set out in the preceding article shall be irrevocable only in the sense that the donor may no longer dispose, by gratuitous title, of the objects included in the gift, except for modest sums, by way of reward or otherwise.

###### Article 1217

The gift by marriage contract may be made cumulatively of present and future property, in whole or in part, on condition that a statement of the donor's debts and charges existing at the day of the gift be annexed to the deed; in which case, it shall be open to the donee, upon the death of the donor, to confine himself to the present property, renouncing the remainder of the donor's property.

###### Article 1218

If the statement referred to in the preceding article has not been annexed to the deed containing the gift of present and future property, the donee shall be obliged to accept or renounce this gift as a whole.
In case of acceptance, he may claim only the property that will be found to exist at the day of the donor's death, and he shall be subject to payment of all the debts and charges of the succession.

###### Article 1219

A donation by marriage contract in favor of the spouses and children to be born of their marriage may also be made, on condition of paying indiscriminately all debts and charges of the donor's estate, or under other conditions the execution of which would depend on his will, by whatever person the donation is made: the donee shall be bound to fulfill these conditions, unless he prefers to renounce the donation; and if the donor, by marriage contract, has reserved the liberty to dispose of a specific item included in the donation of his present property or of a fixed sum to be taken from such property, the item or sum, if he dies without having disposed of it, shall be deemed included in the donation and shall belong to the donee or his heirs.

###### Article 1220

Donations made by marriage contract may not be challenged or declared null on grounds of lack of acceptance.

###### Article 1221

Any donation made in favor of the marriage shall lapse if the marriage does not take place.

###### Article 1222

Donations made to one of the spouses, under the terms of Articles 1215, 1217 and 1219 above, shall lapse if the donor survives the donee spouse and his posterity.

###### Article 1223

All donations made to the spouses by their marriage contract shall, upon the opening of the donor's estate, be reducible to the portion which the law permitted him to dispose of.

#### Chapitre IX

Des dispositions entre époux, soit par contrat de mariage, soit pendant le mariage Article 1224
The spouses may, by marriage contract, make to each other reciprocally, or one of the two to the other, such donation as they see fit, subject to the modifications hereinafter expressed.

###### Article 1225

Any inter vivos donation of present property, made between spouses by marriage contract, shall not be deemed made subject to the condition of survival of the donee, unless this condition is formally expressed; and it shall be subject to all the rules and forms prescribed above for such donations.

###### Article 1226

A donation of future property, or of present and future property, made between spouses by marriage contract, whether simple or reciprocal, shall be subject to the rules established by the preceding chapter, with regard to similar donations made to them by a third party, except that it shall not be transmissible to the children born of the marriage, in case of death of the donee spouse before the donor spouse.

###### Article 1227

A spouse, either by marriage contract or during the marriage, may, for the case where he would leave no child or descendant, dispose in favor of the other spouse in full ownership, of all that he could dispose of in favor of a stranger.

###### Article 1228

For the case where the spouse would leave children or descendants, whether or not born of the marriage, he may dispose in favor of the other spouse, either of the full ownership of what he could dispose of in favor of a stranger, or of one quarter of his property in full ownership and the other three quarters in usufruct, or again of the totality of his property in usufruct only.
Unless otherwise stipulated by the disposer, the surviving spouse may limit his emolument, that is to say accept only certain of the property disposed of in his favor. This limitation may not be considered as a liberality made to the other successors.

###### Article 1229

The children or descendants may, notwithstanding any contrary stipulation of the disposer, require, as regards property subject to usufruct, that an inventory be drawn up of movables as well as a statement of immovables, that employment be made of sums and that bearer securities be, at the choice of the usufructuary, converted into registered securities or deposited with an approved depositary.

###### Article 1230

A minor may not, by marriage contract, give to the other spouse, whether by simple donation or by reciprocal donation, except with the consent and assistance of those whose consent is required for the validity of his marriage; and, with such consent, he may give all that the law permits a spouse of full age to give to the other spouse.

###### Article 1231

A donation of future property made between spouses during the marriage is always revocable.

A donation of present property taking effect during the marriage made between spouses is revocable only under the conditions provided for in Articles 1111 to 1116.
Donations made between spouses of present property or of future property are not revoked by the birth of children.

###### Article 1232

If a spouse has made to his consort, within the limits of Article 1228, a liberality in full ownership, each of the children who are not born of both spouses shall have, as concerns him, unless contrary and unequivocal intention of the disposer, the faculty to substitute for the execution of this liberality the abandonment of the usufruct of the share of the estate that he would have received in the absence of a surviving spouse.
Those who have exercised this faculty may require that the provisions of Article 1229 be applied.

###### Article 1233

Spouses may not give to each other indirectly beyond what is permitted to them by the provisions above.
Any donation, whether disguised or made to interposed persons, shall be null.

Shall be deemed made to interposed persons, donations from one of the spouses to the children or to one of the children of the other spouse born of another marriage, and those made by the donor to relatives of whom the other spouse will be presumptive heir on the day of the donation, even though the latter did not survive his donee relative.

###### Article 1234

When a spouse acquires property with money given to him by the other for that purpose, the donation is only of the sums delivered and not of the property to which they are applied.
In this case, the rights of the donor or his heirs have as their object only a sum of money according to the current value of the property. If the property has been alienated, the value it had on the day of alienation is considered, and if new property has been subrogated to the alienated property, the value of this new property.

### Titre III : Des obligations

###### Article 1235

Obligations arise from juridical acts, from juridical facts or from the authority of law alone.

They may arise from the promise to perform a natural obligation as from the voluntary performance of such an obligation. The promise to perform a natural obligation constitutes a contract; the completed performance of a natural obligation may not give rise to restitution once the performance has been voluntarily discharged.

###### Article 1236

Juridical acts are manifestations of will intended to produce legal effects. They may be a contract or a unilateral juridical act.
Juridical acts are subject, as far as applicable, for their validity and their effects, to the rules that govern contracts.

###### Article 1237

Juridical facts are acts or events to which the law attaches legal effects.

Obligations arising from a juridical fact are governed, as the case may be, by the sub-title relating to civil liability or the sub-title relating to quasi-contracts.

Sous-titre Ier : Le contrat

Chapitre Ier : Dispositions préliminaires Article 1238
A contract is an agreement of wills between two or more persons intended to create, modify, transfer or extinguish obligations.

###### Article 1239

Everyone is free to contract or not to contract, to choose his co-contractor and to determine the content and form of the contract, within the limits set by law.
Contractual freedom does not permit derogation from rules that concern public order and good morals.

###### Article 1240

Legally formed contracts have the force of law for those who have made them. Contracts are in principle consensual.
By way of exception, the validity of solemn contracts is subject to the observance of forms determined by law, failing which the contract is null and void, subject to possible regularization.
In addition, the law makes the formation of certain contracts subject to the delivery of a thing.
On the other hand, forms required for purposes of proof or enforceability have no effect on the validity of contracts.

###### Article 1241

Where a writing is required for the validity of a contract, whether under private signature or by authentic act, it may be established and preserved in electronic form, provided that the person from whom it emanates can be duly identified and that it is established and preserved under conditions such as to guarantee not only its integrity but also the link between the electronic signature and the act to which it is attached.
The reliability of an electronic signature process is presumed until proven otherwise where that process implements a secure electronic signature, established by means of a secure electronic signature creation device and where the verification of that signature is based on the use of a qualified electronic certificate.
Where a handwritten mention by the person who binds himself is required, the latter may affix it in electronic form if the conditions of such affixing are such as to guarantee that it can only be done by himself.

###### Article 1242

Exception is made to the provisions of the preceding article for:
1° Acts under private signature relating to family law and succession;
2° Acts under private signature relating to personal or real security interests, of a civil or commercial nature.

###### Article 1243

The requirement of sending in several copies is deemed satisfied electronically if the writing can be printed by the recipient.

###### Article 1244

The requirement of a detachable form is satisfied by an electronic process that allows access to the form and its return by the same means.

###### Article 1245

Contracts must be negotiated, formed and performed in good faith. This provision is a matter of public policy.

###### Article 1246

Contracts, whether they have a specific designation or not, are subject to general rules, which are the subject of this title.
The particular rules for certain contracts are established in the provisions specific to each of them; the general rules apply subject to these particular rules.

###### Article 1247

A contract is synallagmatic or bilateral when the contracting parties mutually bind themselves to one another, modify, transfer or extinguish obligations.
It is unilateral when one or more persons are bound to one or more others, without there being any reciprocal commitment on the part of the latter.

###### Article 1248

A contract is commutative when each of the parties undertakes to provide the other with an advantage that is regarded as the equivalent of that which it receives.
It is aleatory when the equivalent consists in the chance of gain or loss for each of the parties, according to an uncertain event.

###### Article 1249

A contract is for valuable consideration when each of the parties receives from the other an advantage in return for that which it provides.
It is gratuitous or of beneficence when one of the parties provides the other with an advantage without expecting or receiving anything in return.

###### Article 1250

A contract is consensual when it is formed by the mere exchange of consents without the expression of will having to take a particular form.
A contract is solemn when it requires for its validity, in addition to the agreement of wills, compliance with forms determined by law.

A contract is real when its formation is subject to the delivery of a thing.

###### Article 1251

A contract by mutual agreement is one whose stipulations are freely negotiated between the parties.

A contract of adhesion is one whose general conditions, removed from negotiation, are determined in advance by one of the parties who proposes them to the other.

###### Article 1252

A framework contract is an agreement by which the parties agree on the general characteristics of their future contractual relations. It subsequently incorporates application contracts, which specify the terms of performance.

###### Article 1253

A contract with instantaneous performance is one whose obligations can be performed in a single performance.
A contract with successive performance is one whose obligations of at least one party are performed in several performances spread over time.

#### Chapitre II : De la formation du contrat

##### Section I : La négociation contractuelle Article 1254

The initiation, conduct and termination of pre-contractual negotiations are free. They must imperatively satisfy the requirements of good faith.
It is always possible to break off pre-contractual negotiations, except for abrupt termination or termination without legitimate reason.
In the event of fault committed in the negotiations, the reparation of the damage is of an extra-contractual nature. In the event of an agreement in principle, by which the parties undertake to continue a negotiation, in order to reach the conclusion of a contract whose conditions remain to be defined, a contractual obligation to negotiate in good faith arises. Consequently, the termination of the negotiation must be justified. Failing this, damages may be awarded on the basis of contractual liability.

In all cases, the reparation awarded cannot have the purpose of compensating for the loss of the advantages expected from the contract not concluded.

###### Article 1255

That party which knows information whose importance is decisive for the consent of the other must inform the other of it where the latter legitimately does not know this information or trusts its co-contractor. Information that has a direct and necessary link with the content of the contract or the quality of the parties is of decisive importance; on the other hand, the duty to inform does not relate to the estimation of the value of the performance.
The parties may neither limit nor exclude this duty.

It is incumbent upon the person who claims that information was owed to him to prove that the other party owed it to him, and it is for that other party to prove that it provided it.
In addition to the liability of the person who was bound by it, the breach of this duty to inform may result in the annulment of the contract under the conditions provided for in Articles 1283 and following.

###### Article 1256

Anyone who uses or discloses without authorization confidential information obtained during negotiations incurs liability under the conditions of ordinary law.

##### Section II : La rencontre des consentements

###### § 1. L'offre et l'acceptation Article 1257

A contract is formed by the meeting of an offer and an acceptance by which the parties
manifest their will to commit themselves.

A declaration of will, made expressly and without form, is sufficient to commit oneself. The will to commit oneself may also be expressed tacitly or implicitly, when it results from unequivocal conduct of its author.

###### Article 1258

A proposal to conclude a contract, addressed to one or more determined persons or to an undetermined person, constitutes an offer if it is sufficiently precise and if it indicates the will of its author to be bound in the event of acceptance.
A proposal is sufficiently precise when it contains the essential elements of the contract envisaged. Failing that, there is only an invitation to enter into negotiation.

###### Article 1259

An offer produces its effects as soon as it reaches its addressee. It is considered to have reached its addressee when it has been made verbally or when it has been delivered by any other means to the addressee himself, to his principal place of business or to his postal address.
An offer may be freely revoked, provided that the revocation reaches the addressee before the latter has dispatched his acceptance. However, an offer may not be revoked if it specifies that it is irrevocable or if it sets a specified period for its acceptance. Revocation of the offer in violation of this prohibition prevents the conclusion of the contract. It engages the extra-contractual liability of its author under the conditions of common law without obliging him to compensate for the loss of the benefits expected from the contract.

An offer, even if irrevocable, comes to an end when its rejection reaches the author of the offer.

###### Article 1260

An offer lapses upon expiry of the period fixed by its author or, in the absence thereof, after a reasonable period.
It also lapses in the event of incapacity or death of its author.

###### Article 1261

A declaration or any other conduct by the addressee indicating that he intends to be bound by the terms of the offer made constitutes an acceptance.
The silence or inaction of the person alleged to be bound cannot alone, in the absence of any other circumstance, constitute proof against him of the alleged obligation. It is otherwise when the law, usage, business relations or particular circumstances give the value of acceptance to silence maintained.

###### Article 1262

When the author of the offer has fixed a period for acceptance in a letter, that period begins to run, unless otherwise indicated in the letter, from the day of dispatch of the offer, the postmark serving as evidence. The period for acceptance that the author of the offer fixes by telephone, telex, facsimile, email or any other means of instantaneous communication begins to run at the moment when the offer reaches the addressee.

###### Article 1263

The law or the contract may provide, on the one hand, for a period of reflection for the benefit of the addressee of the offer, which is the period before the expiry of which the latter may not express his acceptance, or on the other hand, for a period of withdrawal, which is the period before the expiry of which its beneficiary may withdraw his consent.

###### Article 1264

Acceptance takes effect at the moment when the agreement expressed by the acceptor reaches the author of the offer. Acceptance does not take effect if that indication does not reach the author of the offer within the period he has stipulated or, in the absence of stipulation, within a reasonable period, taking into account the circumstances surrounding the contemplated transaction and the means of communication used by the author of the offer.

An acceptance is considered to have reached its addressee when it has been made verbally or when it has been delivered by any other means to the addressee himself, to his principal place of business or to his postal address.
A verbal offer must be accepted immediately, unless the circumstances imply otherwise.

###### Article 1265

A reply which purports to be the acceptance of an offer, but which contains additional or different elements not substantially altering the terms of the offer, constitutes an acceptance.
A reply which purports to be the acceptance of an offer, but which contains additions, limitations or other substantial modifications to the terms of the offer, must be considered as a rejection of the offer and constitutes a counter-offer.

###### Article 1266

Acceptance may be freely withdrawn, provided that the withdrawal reaches the author of the offer before the moment when the acceptance would have taken effect.

###### Article 1267

General conditions invoked by one party have effect in respect of the other only if they have been brought to the knowledge of the latter and if the latter has accepted them.
In the event of discrepancy between general conditions invoked by one and the other of the parties, the incompatible clauses have no effect.

In the event of discrepancy between general conditions and particular conditions, the latter prevail over the former.

###### Article 1268

The contract is concluded at the moment when acceptance of an offer takes effect in accordance with these provisions, thus perfecting the meeting of wills.

###### Article 1269

The contract is concluded at the place where acceptance has reached.

###### Article 1270

When it is concluded by electronic means, the contract is valid only if the addressee of the offer has had the possibility of verifying the details of his order and its total price and of correcting any errors before confirming it to express his final acceptance.
The author of the offer must acknowledge receipt without unjustified delay, by electronic means, of the order addressed to him.
The order, the confirmation of acceptance of the offer and the acknowledgement of receipt are considered to be received when the parties to whom they are addressed can have access to them.

###### § 2. Representation Article 1271

Representation is the power recognised in a person, the representative, to act in the name and on behalf of another, the represented person. The representative does not become a party to the contract.

This power is of legal, judicial or conventional origin. Conventional representation has its source in the contract of mandate.

This power is either special and for one matter or certain matters only, or general and for all the matters of the represented person. A mandate conceived in general terms embraces only acts of administration.

###### Article 1272

The legal, judicial or conventional representative is entitled to act only within the limits of the powers conferred upon him.

###### Article 1273

Representation is perfect when the representative acts within the limits of his powers and declares that he is acting in the name and on behalf of the represented person. In that case, the latter alone is bound by the commitment entered into and the contract concluded by the representative produces its effects directly, immediately and retroactively on the person of the represented person.
Representation is imperfect when the representative does not disclose to the third party the name of his principal. In that case, he alone is bound in respect of the contracting party.

###### Article 1274

The represented person is not bound by what has been done without power or beyond the power he has given to the representative. The same applies when the representative misuses his powers to the detriment of the represented person. A person who was unaware of the absence, excess or misuse of power, or could not have been unaware of it, may bring an action for relative nullity of the contract, without prejudice to damages which may, where appropriate, be claimed from the representative.
By way of exception, the represented person is bound by the act concluded when the contracting third party could legitimately believe in the reality of the representative's powers, in particular by reason of the conduct or declarations of the represented person.

These provisions do not exclude the application of the rules specific to management of another's affairs.
The represented person may ratify the act concluded without power or beyond the power given, or confirm the act accomplished by misuse of power. In these cases, the contract concluded by the representative produces its effects directly, immediately and retroactively on the person of the represented person.

###### Article 1275

The establishment of legal or judicial representation divests the represented person, for its duration, of the powers transferred to the representative.
Conventional representation leaves the represented person with the exercise of his rights.

###### Article 1276

The powers of the representative cease if he becomes incapable or is struck by incapacity during the execution of the mandate. These powers also end with the death of the representative.

###### Article 1277

A representative may not act on behalf of both parties to the contract nor contract on his own account with the represented party.
The act performed is null and void, by relative nullity, by the mere fact of breach of the rule provided for in the preceding paragraph, unless the law authorizes it or the represented party has authorized or ratified it.

##### Section III : Le pacte de préférence et la promesse unilatérale de contrat

###### Article 1278

The pact of preference is the promise made by one person to another, who accepts it, to offer him priority in concluding a contract of a specified nature, in the event that the promisor decides one day to conclude such a contract.

###### Article 1279

When a contract is concluded with a third party in violation of a pact of preference, the beneficiary of the pact may obtain compensation for the damage he suffers. If the third party knew of the existence of the pact and the beneficiary's intention to rely on it, the latter may, in addition, ask the judge to annul the contract entered into with the third party and to substitute himself for the third party in the contract concluded; he must bring this action within six months of becoming aware of the violation of the pact of preference.
The third party may request in writing that the beneficiary of the pact confirm within two months the existence of a pact of preference and whether he intends to rely on it. The writing mentions that failing a response within this period, the beneficiary of the pact may no longer seek his substitution in the contract concluded with the third party.

###### Article 1280

The unilateral promise of contract is the act by which one person, the promisor, undertakes towards another, the beneficiary, who accepts it, to grant him, for a certain period, the right to opt for the conclusion of a contract whose essential elements are already determined, and for the formation of which only the consent of the beneficiary is lacking.
The final contract is formed as soon as the option is exercised. The revocation of the promise during the time left to the beneficiary to opt does not prevent the formation of the promised contract.

The contract concluded in violation of the unilateral promise with a third party who knew of its existence is null and void. The beneficiary of the promise may, in addition to all damages compensating the prejudice he suffers, ask the judge for his substitution for the third party in the contract concluded.

#### Chapitre III : Des conditions de validité des contrats Article 1281

Four conditions are essential for the validity of a contract: 1° A real, informed and free consent of the parties;
2° Their capacity to contract; 3° A certain and lawful object;
4° A lawful cause.

##### Section I : Du consentement Article 1282

There is no contract if there is no consent.

###### Article 1283

Error, fraud and duress vitiate consent when they are of such a nature that, without them, one of the parties would not have contracted or would have contracted on substantially different terms.
Their determining character of the defect of consent is assessed having regard to the persons and the circumstances in which the consent was given.

###### Article 1284

The absence of consent and defects of consent are a cause of relative nullity of the contract.

###### Article 1285

Error of law or fact, unless it is inexcusable, is a cause of nullity of the contract when it relates to the essential qualities of the performance owed by one or the other of the parties.
Error is not a cause of nullity when it relates only to the person with whom one intends to contract, unless the consideration of that person is the principal cause of the agreement.

The essential qualities are those in consideration of which both parties contracted, or, similarly, the qualities in consideration of which one of them contracted, to the knowledge of the other. These expected qualities are those which have been expressly or tacitly agreed upon by the parties to the act.

The acceptance of a risk concerning a quality of the performance excludes error relating to that quality.

###### Article 1286

Error as to a simple motive, unrelated to the essential qualities of the performance owed or of the contracting party, is not a cause of nullity, unless the parties, rather than making this motive a condition of their agreement, have expressly made it a determining element of their consent.

###### Article 1287

Error as to value by which, without being mistaken as to the essential qualities of the performance, a contracting party merely makes an inaccurate economic assessment of it, is not a cause of nullity.

###### Article 1288

Fraud is the act by a party of surprising the consent of the other by maneuvers or lies in order to obtain the conclusion of a legal act.
Also constitutes fraud the concealment by one of the parties of information which it knows to be of determining character for the other. Nevertheless, the failure by a party to disclose to its contracting party its assessment of the value of the performance does not constitute fraud.

###### Article 1289

Fraud is also constituted if it emanates from the representative, manager of affairs, agent or surety of a party.
It is also constituted when it emanates from a third party in collusion.

###### Article 1290

Error resulting from fraud is always excusable; it is a cause of nullity even if it relates to the value of the performance or to a simple motive of the contract.

###### Article 1291

A person who is the victim of fraud may bring an action for nullity, seek only damages, or, where appropriate, both.

###### Article 1292

Duress is the act by a party or by a third party of undermining the free consent of another, by inspiring in him the fear of exposing his person, his fortune or those of his relatives to considerable harm.

###### Article 1293

Reverential fear alone towards the father, mother, or other ascendant, without violence having been exercised, is not sufficient to annul the contract.

###### Article 1294

The threat of legal proceedings does not constitute duress, except in case of abuse. Abuse is characterized when the legal proceedings are diverted from their purpose or when they are invoked or exercised to obtain a manifestly excessive advantage.

###### Article 1295

There is also duress when a party, abusing the situation of weakness in which its contracting party finds itself, obtains from him a commitment that he would not have entered into in the absence of such constraint and derives a manifestly excessive advantage from it.

###### Article 1296

The period for the action for nullity runs, in case of error or fraud, only from the day on which they were discovered and, in case of duress, only from the day on which it ceased.
A contract may no longer be challenged if, since the defect of error or fraud was discovered by the person who was the victim of it or since the duress ceased, that contract has been approved by him, either expressly, or tacitly, or by allowing the time for restitution fixed by law to pass.

##### Section II : De la capacité des parties contractantes Article 1297

Any natural person may contract except in case of incapacity provided for by law.

Legal persons contract through their representatives. In this regard, the capacity of legal persons is limited to acts useful for the realization of their object as defined by their statutes and to acts which are accessory to them, in compliance with the rules applicable to each of them.

###### Article 1298

Are incapable of contracting, to the extent defined by law:
1° Unemancipated minors;
2° Protected adults within the meaning of Article 565 of this Code.

###### Article 1299

Any person incapable of contracting may nevertheless accomplish alone routine acts authorized by law or custom.

###### Article 1300

Routine acts accomplished by a minor may be annulled for simple lesion. But nullity is not incurred when the lesion results from an unforeseeable event.

The simple declaration of majority made by the minor does not prevent annulment. Likewise, an incapable person cannot be reproached for having remained silent or for having made a false declaration about his status.

A minor cannot escape the commitments he has made in the exercise of his profession.

###### Article 1301

Acts accomplished by protected adults are governed by Articles 574, 602 and 621 without prejudice to Articles 1299, 1304 and 1581.

###### Article 1302

Incapacity to contract is a ground for relative nullity that only the incapable contracting party may invoke.

###### Article 1303

Except with judicial authorization, any person exercising a function or occupying a position in an establishment housing elderly persons or dispensing psychiatric care is prohibited, on pain of nullity, from becoming the purchaser, directly or through an intermediary, of property or assignee of a right belonging to a person admitted to the establishment, nor from taking a lease on the dwelling occupied by that person before his admission to the establishment.
For the application of this article, the spouse, ascendants and descendants of the persons to whom the prohibitions set out above apply are deemed to be intermediaries.

###### Article 1304

The contracting party of the incapable person may prevent the action for nullity brought against him by establishing that the act was useful to the protected person and free from lesion or that it benefited that person.
He may also oppose to the action for nullity the confirmation of the act by his contracting party who has become or become again capable.

###### Article 1305

The prescription of the action runs:
1° With regard to acts done by a minor, from the day of majority or emancipation;
2° With regard to acts done by a protected adult, from the day he became aware of them while he was in a position to redo them validly;
3° With regard to the heirs of the person under guardianship or curatorship or of the person subject to family authorization, from the day of death if it had not begun to run previously.

##### Section III : De l'objet et de la matière des contrats Article 1306

The object of the contract is constituted by what the parties have obligated themselves to. It may be an obligation to do, not to do, or to give.

###### Article 1307

Only things that are in commerce may be the object of a juridical act. A juridical act may not derogate from public policy either by its stipulations or by its purpose, whether or not the latter was known by all the parties.

###### Article 1308

The obligation has as its object a present or future performance. One cannot however renounce a succession not yet opened, nor make any stipulation concerning such a succession, even with the consent of the person whose succession is concerned.

The performance must be possible and determined or determinable.

The performance is determinable when it can be deduced from the contract or by reference to customs or to the prior relations of the parties, without a new agreement of the parties being necessary.

###### Article 1309

Lesion, economic imbalance between reciprocal performances, opens the way to an action for nullity only when the law so provides.

###### Article 1310

In framework contracts and contracts with successive performance, it may be agreed that the price will be fixed unilaterally by one of the parties, provided that it justifies the amount in case of dispute.
In case of abuse in fixing the price, the judge may be seized with a request seeking to obtain damages and if appropriate the resolution of the contract. Seizing the judge suspends payment of the fixed price.

###### Article 1311

In service contracts, in the absence of agreement of the parties before their performance, the price may be fixed by the creditor, provided that he justifies the amount in case of dispute.
In case of abuse in fixing the price, the judge may be seized with a request for damages. Seizing the judge suspends payment of the fixed price.

###### Article 1312

When the quality of the performance is not determined or determinable by virtue of the contract, the debtor must offer a performance of quality conforming to the legitimate expectations of the parties in consideration of its nature, customs and the amount of the consideration.

###### Article 1313

When the price or any other element of the contract must be determined by reference to an index that does not exist or has ceased to exist or to be accessible, it is replaced by the index that most closely approximates it.

##### Section IV : De la cause Article 1314

An obligation without cause, or on a false cause, or on an illicit cause, can have no effect.

###### Article 1315

Any clause that deprives the debtor's essential obligation of its substance is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1316

A contract for valuable consideration is null when, at the time of its formation, the consideration agreed upon for the benefit of the person who commits himself is illusory or derisory.

###### Article 1317

In a contract of adhesion, any clause that creates a significant imbalance between the rights and obligations of the parties to the contract is deemed unwritten.
The assessment of significant imbalance relates neither to the principal object of the contract nor to the adequacy of the price to the performance.

###### Article 1318

The agreement is no less valid, although the cause is not expressed therein.

###### Article 1319

The cause is illicit when it is prohibited by law, when it is contrary to good morals or to public policy.

##### Section V

De la sanction du non-respect des conditions de validité des contrats Sous-section 1 : La nullité

###### Article 1320

A contract that does not fulfill the conditions required for its validity is null. Nullity must be pronounced by the judge, unless the parties acknowledge it by mutual agreement.
The annulled contract is deemed never to have existed.
Performances executed give rise to restitution under the conditions provided in Articles 1577 to 1585.

Independently of the annulment of the contract, the injured party may request reparation of the damage suffered under the conditions of the general law of extra-contractual liability.

###### Article 1321

Nullity is absolute when the violated rule has as its object the safeguarding of the general interest. It is relative when the violated rule has as its sole object the safeguarding of a private interest.
When the rule that offends a private interest proceeds from a fundamental value, such as the protection of the human body, the nullity is absolute.

###### Article 1322

Absolute nullity may be requested by any person justifying an interest, as well as by the public prosecutor.
It can never be cured by confirmation of the contract.

###### Article 1323

Relative nullity may be requested only by the party that the law intends to protect. It may be cured by confirmation.
If the action for relative nullity has several holders, the renunciation of one does not prevent the others from acting.

###### Article 1324

Confirmation is the act by which a person who could rely on nullity renounces it. This act mentions the object of the obligation and the defect affecting the contract.
Confirmation can only take place after the conclusion of the contract.

Voluntary performance of the contract, with knowledge of the ground for nullity, constitutes confirmation. In case of duress, confirmation can only take place after the duress has ceased.

Confirmation entails renunciation of the means and defences that could have been raised, without prejudice however to the rights of third parties.

###### Article 1325

A party may request in writing from the party who could rely on nullity either to confirm the contract or to bring an action for nullity within six months on pain of forfeiture. The ground for nullity must have ceased.
The writing expressly mentions that in the absence of an action for nullity brought before the expiry of the six-month period, the contract shall be deemed confirmed.

###### Article 1326

Where the ground for nullity affects only one or more clauses of the contract, it entails nullity of the entire act only if that clause or those clauses constituted a determining element of the commitment of the parties or of one of them.
The contract is maintained where the law deems the clause unwritten, or where the purposes of the rule infringed require its maintenance.
Except where a provision of law confers this power upon him, the judge may not modify a clause or an amount provided for by the contract.

###### Article 1327

The defence of nullity is not subject to prescription if it relates to a contract that has received no performance.

###### Sous-section 2 : La caducité Article 1328

A validly formed contract becomes lapsed if one of its essential elements disappears.

Where the performance of several contracts is necessary for the completion of a single operation and one of them disappears, those contracts whose performance is rendered impossible by this disappearance and those for which the performance of the disappeared contract was a determining condition of the consent of a party become lapsed.

Lapse only occurs, however, if the contracting party against whom it is invoked knew of the existence of the overall operation when he gave his consent.

###### Article 1329

Lapse terminates the contract.

It may give rise to restitution under the conditions provided for in articles 1577 to 1585.

#### Chapitre IV : De l'interprétation des actes juridiques Article 1330

Where the will of the parties is expressed in a clear and precise manner, the judge may not, under cover of interpretation, modify the clauses, on pain of misrepresentation.

###### Article 1331

The judge must in agreements seek what was the common intention of the contracting parties, rather than stopping at the literal meaning of the terms.
Where this intention cannot be discerned, the contract is interpreted according to the meaning that a reasonable person placed in the same situation would give it. But even where the terms in which an

agreement is drafted are general, it includes only those things on which it appears that the parties intended to contract.

###### Article 1332

Terms capable of two meanings must be taken in the meaning that best suits the subject matter of the contract and the coherence of this act as a whole.
Where, in the common intention of the parties, several contracts contribute to a single operation, they are interpreted in light of it.

###### Article 1333

In case of doubt, a freely negotiated contract is interpreted against the creditor and in favour of the debtor, and a contract of adhesion against the party who proposed it.

###### Article 1334

Where a clause is capable of two meanings, the one that gives it effect prevails over the one that produces no effect.

#### Chapitre V : Les effets du contrat

##### Section I

Les effets du contrat entre les parties Sous-section 1 : Force obligatoire

###### Article 1335

Contracts may be modified or revoked only by mutual consent of the parties, or for the grounds that the law authorises.

###### Article 1336

Contracts bind not only to what is expressed therein, but also to all the consequences given to them by equity, usage or law.

###### Article 1337

If an unforeseeable change of circumstances at the time of conclusion of the contract renders performance excessively onerous for a party who had not agreed to assume the risk, that party may request renegotiation of the contract from its co-contracting party. It continues to perform its obligations during the renegotiation.
In case of refusal or failure of the renegotiation, the parties may agree to the termination of the contract on the date and under the conditions they determine. Failing this, one of the parties may apply to the judge to terminate the contract, on the date and under the conditions he sets.

###### Article 1338

There is simulation where the parties conclude an apparent contract that contradicts a hidden contract. In this case, the latter, also called a counter-letter, produces effect between the contracting parties.
However, any counter-letter having as its object an increase in the price stipulated in the deed of transfer of a ministerial office is null.

Likewise, any contract having the purpose of concealing part of the price is null, where it relates to a sale of immovable property, a transfer of a business or clientele, a transfer of a right to a lease, or the benefit of a promise of lease relating to all or part of an immovable property and all or part of the

balancing payment of an exchange or partition comprising immovable property, a business or a clientele.

###### Sous-section 2 : Effet translatif Article 1339

In contracts having as their object the alienation of ownership or the transfer of another right, the transfer takes place upon conclusion of the contract.
This transfer may be deferred by the will of the parties, the nature of things or by operation of law.

The transfer of ownership entails transfer of the risks of the thing. However, the debtor of the obligation to deliver recovers the burden thereof from the time of his default, either by a summons or an act containing sufficient notice, or, if the contract so provides, by the mere enforceability of the obligation, all subject to the rules provided for in article 1364, paragraph 3.

###### Article 1340
