The obligation to deliver the thing entails an obligation to preserve it until delivery, by exercising all the care of a reasonable person.
This obligation is more or less extensive in relation to certain contracts, whose effects, in this respect, are explained under the titles that concern them.

###### Article 1341

Where two successive purchasers of the same corporeal movable derive their right from the same person, the one who took possession of this movable first is preferred, even if his right is subsequent, provided that he is in good faith.
Where two successive purchasers of rights relating to the same immovable property derive their right from the same person, the one who first published his deed of acquisition executed in authentic form in the land registry is preferred, even if his right is subsequent, provided that he is in good faith.

##### Section II

Les effets du contrat à l'égard des tiers Sous-section 1 : Dispositions générales

###### Article 1342

The contract creates obligations only between the parties.

Third parties may neither request performance of the contract nor be compelled to perform it, subject to the provisions of this section and those of articles 1526 to 1529.

###### Article 1343

Third parties must respect the legal situation created by the contract, which is enforceable against them. They may rely on it in particular for evidentiary purposes.

###### Article 1344

In case of simulation, the counter-letter is not enforceable against third parties, who may nevertheless rely on it.

###### Article 1345

When a person acts on behalf of another but without informing the person with whom he enters into the contract, the latter, upon learning of the existence of the nominee agreement, may rely on the act that had been concealed from him or on the act entered into with the nominee. On the other hand, if this contracting third party participated in the establishment of the simulation, he may only rely on the concealed contract.
In such a case, in the presence of a contract transferring ownership, the nominee agreement operates a transfer directly from the estate of the nominee to that of the principal, without passing through the estate of the nominee.

###### Sous-section 2 : Le porte-fort et la stipulation pour autrui Article 1346

One may only undertake in one's own name for oneself.

###### Article 1347

One may act as guarantor by promising the act of a third party.

The promisor is released from all obligation if the third party accomplishes the promised act. Otherwise, he may be ordered to pay damages.

When the guarantee has as its object the ratification of an undertaking, the latter is retroactively validated by the ratification made by the third party, as of the date on which the guarantee was subscribed, without prejudice however to the rights of third parties.

###### Article 1348

One may stipulate for another.

One of the contracting parties, the stipulator, may have the other, the promisor, promise to perform a benefit for the benefit of a third party, the beneficiary. The third party beneficiary may be a future person but must be precisely designated or capable of being determined at the time of performance of the promise. The stipulator may reserve the right to designate the third party beneficiary when the time comes.

###### Article 1349

The third party beneficiary is vested with a direct right to the benefit against the promisor from the time of the stipulation.

Nevertheless the stipulator may freely revoke the stipulation as long as the third party beneficiary has not accepted it.

The stipulation becomes irrevocable at the moment when the acceptance reaches the stipulator or the promisor.

###### Article 1350

The revocation may only emanate from the stipulator or, after his death, from his heirs. The latter may only proceed with it upon the expiration of a period of three months from the day on which they put the third party beneficiary on notice to accept it.
If it is not accompanied by the designation of a new beneficiary, the revocation benefits, as the case may be, the stipulator or his heirs.

The revocation takes effect as soon as the third party beneficiary or the promisor has had knowledge of it. When it is made by will, it takes effect at the moment of death.

The third party initially designated as beneficiary is then deemed never to have benefited from the stipulation made for his benefit.

###### Article 1351

The acceptance may emanate from the beneficiary or, after his death, from his heirs. It may occur even after the death of the stipulator or the promisor.
The acceptance may be express or tacit.

###### Article 1352

The stipulator may himself require from the promisor the performance of his undertaking towards the beneficiary.

##### Section III : La durée du contrat Article 1353

Perpetual undertakings are prohibited.

Each contracting party may terminate them under the conditions provided for contracts of indefinite duration.

###### Article 1354

When the contract is concluded for an indefinite duration, each party may terminate it at any time, subject to respecting the contractually provided notice period or, failing that, a reasonable period.

###### Article 1355

When the contract is concluded for a fixed duration, each party must perform it until its term.
The contract may be extended if the contracting parties express their will before its expiration. The initial term of the contract is thus postponed to a later date. The extension may not, however, affect the rights of third parties.

###### Article 1356

No one may require the renewal of the contract, except by provision of law or agreement of the parties.

In case of renewal, a new contract succeeds the previous one. Their content is identical but, except where the law provides otherwise, the duration of the new contract is indefinite.

###### Article 1357

When upon the expiration of the term of a contract concluded for a fixed duration, the contracting parties continue to perform its obligations, there is tacit renewal.
This produces the same effects as the renewal of the contract.

##### Section IV : La cession de contrat Article 1358

A contracting party, the assignor, may assign his status as party to the contract to a third party, the assignee, with the agreement of his co-contracting party, the party to whom assignment is made.

This agreement may be given in advance, in particular in the contract concluded between the future assignor and the party to whom assignment is made, in which case the assignment takes effect with regard to the party to whom assignment is made when the contract concluded between the assignor and the assignee is notified to him or when he acknowledges it.
The assignment must be recorded in writing, on pain of nullity.

###### Article 1359

If the party to whom assignment is made has expressly consented thereto, the assignment of contract releases the assignor for the future.

In the absence of such express consent, the assignor is held jointly and severally liable for the performance of the contract. It is possible for the parties to exclude certain rights and obligations from the assignment.

###### Article 1360

By the effect of the assignment carried out, the assignee becomes a party to the initial contract.

The assignee may raise against the party to whom assignment is made the defenses inherent in the debt, such as payment, prescription, nullity that is not purely personal to the assignor, the defense of non-performance, termination or set-off of related debts. He may not raise against him the defenses personal to the assignor, such as incapacity or a defect of consent affecting the will of the latter.

The party to whom assignment is made may raise against the assignee all the defenses that he could have raised against the assignor.

###### Article 1361

If the assignor is not released by the party to whom assignment is made, the securities that may have been granted subsist. Otherwise, the securities granted by third parties subsist only with their agreement.
If the assignor is released, his joint and several co-debtors remain liable after deduction of his share in the debt.

##### Section V : L'inexécution du contrat Article 1362

The debtor bound by an obligation of means has undertaken to implement all the means necessary to perform his obligation, without undertaking to obtain that result. Non-performance of the contract requires that the creditor demonstrate a fault of the debtor in the accomplishment of his obligation.
The debtor bound by an obligation of result has undertaken to obtain the result provided for contractually. He is at fault by the mere demonstration of the absence of the promised result, unless he proves that the non-performance is due to an event of force majeure.

###### Article 1363

The party towards whom the undertaking has not been performed, or has been imperfectly performed, may:
-	refuse to perform or suspend the performance of his own obligation;
-	pursue the forced performance in kind of the obligation;
-	request or, when the law authorizes him to do so, notify the other party of a reduction of the price;
-	bring about the termination of the contract;
-	seek reparation for the consequences of the non-performance.
The sanctions that are not incompatible may be cumulated; forced performance of the contract and termination are not compatible. Damages may always be added to the sanction pronounced.

In case of non-performance of a contractual obligation, neither the debtor nor the creditor may evade the application of the provisions specific to contractual liability in order to opt in favor of the rules specific to extra-contractual liability.

###### Article 1364

In contractual matters, external cause may result from a fortuitous event, the act of a third party or the act of the co-contractor. External cause constitutes a case of force majeure when it prevents

the performance of his obligation by the debtor, results from an event which, escaping the control of the latter, could not reasonably have been foreseen at the time of conclusion of the contract and whose effects cannot be avoided by appropriate measures.

If the impediment is temporary, the performance of the obligation is suspended, unless the resulting delay would justify termination of the contract.

If the impediment is definitive, as the case may be, the impossibility of performing the obligation either releases the debtor to the corresponding extent, or, if it constitutes a case of force majeure, results in termination of the contract by operation of law and releases the parties from their obligations. However, the debtor remains bound if he has agreed to assume the external cause or if he has been previously given formal notice. In the latter case, when the impossibility of performance results from the loss of the thing owed, the debtor given formal notice is nevertheless released if he proves that the loss would have occurred in the same way if the obligation had been performed. In all cases, the debtor is bound to assign to his creditor the rights and actions attached to the thing.

###### Sous-section 1 : L'exception d'inexécution Article 1365

A party to a synallagmatic contract may refuse to perform his obligation, totally or partially, even though it is due, if the other does not perform his.
The refusal of performance must not be disproportionate to the breach attributed to the other.

###### Article 1366

A party may, subject to the same reservation, suspend the performance of his obligation where it is manifest that his co-contractor will not perform at the due date and that the consequences of such non-performance are sufficiently serious for him.
This suspension must be notified as soon as possible.

###### Sous-section 2 : L'exécution forcée en nature Article 1367

The creditor of an obligation may, after formal notice, pursue its performance in kind, unless such performance is impossible or there exists a manifest disproportion between its cost for the debtor and its interest for the creditor.

###### Article 1368

After formal notice, the creditor may also, within a reasonable time and at a reasonable cost, have the obligation performed himself or, upon prior authorization of the judge, destroy what has been done in violation thereof. He may demand from the debtor reimbursement of the sums committed for this purpose.
He may also request in court that the debtor advance the sums necessary for such performance or such destruction.

###### Sous-section 3 : La réduction du prix Article 1369

The creditor may, after formal notice, accept imperfect performance of the contract and request a proportional reduction of the price.
If he has not yet paid, the creditor notifies the debtor as soon as possible of his decision to reduce the price.

###### Sous-section 4 : La résolution

###### Article 1370

Termination results either from the application of a termination clause or, in case of sufficiently serious non-performance, from a notification by the creditor to the debtor or from a court decision.

###### Article 1371

The termination clause specifies the commitments whose non-performance will result in termination of the contract.

Termination is subject to an unsuccessful formal notice, if it has not been agreed that it would result from the mere fact of non-performance. The formal notice produces effect only if it expressly mentions the termination clause.

The termination clause must be implemented in good faith by the creditor. However, in case of non-performance of his commitment by the debtor, his good faith has no effect on the acquisition of the termination clause.

###### Article 1372

The creditor may, at his own risk, terminate the contract by way of notification. Except in case of urgency, he must first give formal notice to the defaulting debtor to satisfy his commitment within a reasonable time.
The formal notice expressly mentions that in default of the debtor satisfying his obligation, the creditor will be entitled to terminate the contract.

When the non-performance persists, the creditor notifies the debtor of the termination of the contract and the reasons motivating it.

The debtor may at any time seize the judge to contest the termination. The creditor must then prove the seriousness of the non-performance.

###### Article 1373

Termination may, in any event, be requested in court.

It is however possible to renounce in advance the right to request judicial termination of the contract.

###### Article 1374

The judge may, according to the circumstances, declare or pronounce termination, or order performance of the contract possibly granting a time period to the debtor, or award only damages.

###### Article 1375

Termination puts an end to the contract.

Termination takes effect, as the case may be, either under the conditions provided by the termination clause, or on the date of receipt by the debtor of the notification made by the creditor, or on the date fixed by the judge or, failing that, on the day of the summons to court.
When the exchanged performances could find their utility only through complete performance of the terminated contract, the parties must restore the entirety of what they procured from one another. When the exchanged performances found their utility progressively through reciprocal performance of the contract, there is no need for restitution for the period prior to the last performance not having received its counterpart; in this case, the termination is qualified as cancellation.

Restitutions take place under the conditions provided in articles 1577 to 1585.

###### Article 1376

Termination does not affect clauses relating to the settlement of disputes, nor those intended to produce effect even in case of termination, such as confidentiality and non-competition clauses.

###### Sous-section 5

La réparation du préjudice résultant de l'inexécution du contrat Article 1377
Reparation of prejudice resulting from non-performance of the contract falls under the provisions of articles 1403 and following.

Sous-titre II : La responsabilité civile

Chapitre Ier : Dispositions préliminaires Article 1378
Prejudices resulting from bodily harm are always repaired on the basis of the rules of extra-contractual liability, even though they may be caused on the occasion of performance of the contract.
However, the victim may invoke the express stipulations of the contract when they are more favorable to him.

###### Article 1379

When non-performance of the contract causes harm to a third party, the latter may request reparation of its consequences from the debtor only on the basis of extra-contractual liability. He must then demonstrate the reality of one of the generating facts referred to in section II of chapter II.
However, when the third party has a legitimate interest in the proper performance of a contract, he may invoke, on the basis of contractual liability, a contractual breach provided that it has caused him harm. The conditions and limits of liability that apply in relations between the contracting parties are then opposable to him. However, any clause that limits the contractual liability of a contracting party with regard to third parties is deemed unwritten.

#### Chapitre II : Les conditions de la responsabilité civile

##### Section I

Dispositions communes aux responsabilités contractuelles et extracontractuelles Sous-section 1 : Le fait générateur de responsabilité

###### Article 1380

The triggering event of extra-contractual liability is defined by articles 1391 and following. The triggering event of contractual liability is defined by articles 1403 and following.

###### Article 1381

A person who performs an act is not civilly liable:
-	prescribed or authorized by legislative or regulatory provisions;

-	ordered by legitimate authority, unless such act is manifestly illegal;
-	ordered by the necessity of legitimate defense of themselves, others, or their property;
-	necessary for the safeguarding of the person or property in response to a current or imminent danger that threatens themselves, others or property.
All subject to the limits placed on these acts by the criminal code.

###### Article 1382

Nor does a harmful act give rise to liability when it infringes a right or interest over which the victim had disposal, if the victim consented thereto.

###### Sous-section 2 : Le préjudice réparable Article 1383

Any certain harm resulting from damage and consisting of injury to a lawful interest, whether patrimonial or extra-patrimonial, is reparable.

Future harm is reparable as soon as it is certain and direct.

###### Article 1384

Expenses incurred by the claimant to prevent the imminent occurrence of damage or to avoid its aggravation, as well as to reduce its consequences, constitute reparable harm provided they were reasonably incurred.

###### Article 1385

Only the present and certain disappearance of a favorable eventuality constitutes reparable loss of a chance.
The compensation corresponds to the lost chance and not to the advantage that this chance would have provided had it materialized.

###### Sous-section 3 : Le lien de causalité Article 1386

A causal link must exist between the act imputed to the defendant and the damage. Proof of the causal link is established by any means.

###### Article 1387

When bodily harm is caused by an unidentified person among identified persons acting jointly or engaging in a similar activity, they are jointly and severally liable to answer for the whole. However, each of the co-responsible parties may demonstrate that they cannot have caused the damage.
The responsible parties contribute among themselves in proportion to the probability that each caused the damage.

###### Sous-section 4 : Les clauses limitatives ou exclusives de responsabilité Article 1388

Clauses having the object or effect of excluding or limiting liability are in principle valid, both in contractual and extra-contractual matters.

However, liability cannot be limited or excluded by contract in case of bodily harm.

###### Article 1389

In contractual matters, clauses limiting or excluding liability have no effect in case of gross or intentional fault.
They are deemed unwritten when they deprive the debtor's essential obligation of its substance.

###### Article 1390

In extra-contractual matters, one cannot exclude or limit liability for fault.

##### Section II : Dispositions propres à la responsabilité extracontractuelle

###### § 1. La responsabilité pour faute Article 1391

Any act whatsoever of man, which causes damage to another, obliges the person by whose fault it occurred to repair it.

Each person is liable for the damage they have caused not only by their act, but also by their negligence or imprudence.

###### § 2. La responsabilité du fait des choses Article 1392

Any harmful act of a thing automatically engages the liability of the person who has custody of it.

The custodian is the person who has the use, control and direction of the thing at the time of the harmful act. The owner is presumed to be the custodian of the thing.
The act of the thing and its causal role are presumed when it, in motion, has come into contact with the site of the damage. In other cases, it is for the victim to prove the act of the thing, by establishing either its defect, or the abnormality of its position, state or behavior, and its role in causing the damage.

###### Article 1393

The owner of an animal, or the person using it, while it is in their use, is liable for the damage that the animal has caused, whether the animal was under their custody, or whether it had strayed or escaped.

###### Article 1394

The owner of a building is liable for the damage caused by its collapse, when it occurred as a result of lack of maintenance or a defect in its construction.
A person who holds, under any title whatsoever, all or part of the immovable property or movable property in which a fire originated shall be liable, vis-à-vis third parties, for damage caused by that fire only if it is proved that it must be attributed to their fault or to the fault of persons for whom they are responsible.

The preceding paragraph does not apply to relations between owners and tenants, which remain governed by the laws concerning them.

###### § 3. La responsabilité du fait d'autrui

###### Article 1395

Liability for the acts of another requires proof of an act capable of engaging the personal liability of the direct author of the damage.

###### Article 1396

The following are automatically liable for the acts of a minor:
-	their parents, insofar as they exercise parental authority;
-	their guardian or guardians, insofar as they are responsible for the person of the minor;
-	the natural or legal person charged by judicial or administrative decision with organizing and controlling on a permanent basis the minor's way of life. In this case, the liability of the parents of that minor cannot be engaged.

###### Article 1397

The natural or legal person charged by judicial or administrative decision with organizing and controlling on a permanent basis their way of life is automatically liable for the acts of an adult placed under their supervision.

###### Article 1398

Other persons who, by contract, assume, in a professional capacity, such as teachers and craftsmen with regard to their pupils and apprentices, a mission of supervision of another or of organization and control of another's activity, are liable for the acts of the natural person supervised, during the time they are under their supervision.
They may be exonerated from this liability by demonstrating that, in the exercise of their mission, they did not commit any fault of supervision or of organization and control.

###### Article 1399

The principal is automatically liable for damage caused by their agent. The relationship of agency presupposes the power of the principal to give the agent orders or instructions in relation to the performance of their functions.
In case of transfer of the relationship of agency, this liability rests on the beneficiary of the transfer.

The principal or the beneficiary of the transfer is not liable if they prove that the agent acted outside the functions for which they were employed, without authorization and for purposes unrelated to their duties. Nor are they liable if they establish collusion between the agent and the victim.

The agent engages their personal liability in case of intentional fault, or when, without authorization, they acted for purposes unrelated to their duties. They engage it only in these cases.

###### § 4. La responsabilité du fait de troubles anormaux de voisinage Article 1400

No one must cause another an abnormal disturbance of neighborhood.

###### Article 1401

Neighbourhood disturbance is sanctioned by the judge as soon as it is excessive.

Where it involves a fault committed in the performance of an obligation arising from a contract, the rules of contractual liability apply between the parties to the act. In other cases, the measure of liability is that of the excessive nature of the disturbance without any regard to the existence or not of a fault of the defendant.

###### Article 1402

Where a harmful activity is carried out lawfully, the judge may nevertheless order reasonable measures to stop the disturbance and, failing the ability to do so without jeopardising the activity, award damages to the victim of the disturbance.
However, compensation for damage caused by nuisances resulting from an agricultural, industrial, artisanal, commercial or aeronautical activity that is carried out in accordance with legislation is excluded, as soon as the claimant settled in the location concerned after the activities started.

##### Section III: Provisions specific to contractual liability Article 1403

Any non-performance of the contract having caused damage to the creditor obliges the debtor to answer for it.

###### Article 1404

Unless the non-performance is final, damages are only due if the debtor has previously been given notice to perform within a reasonable time.

###### Article 1405

The debtor is condemned, if appropriate, to the payment of damages either by reason of the non-performance of the obligation, or by reason of delay in performance, if he does not prove that performance was prevented by an external cause.

###### Article 1406

The damages due to the creditor are, in general, the loss he has suffered and the gain of which he has been deprived, subject to the exceptions and modifications below.

###### Article 1407

The debtor is only liable for damages that were foreseen or could have been foreseen at the time of conclusion of the contract, except where the non-performance is due to gross or intentional fault.
Fault is gross when its author adopts behaviour of extreme gravity, bordering on fraud, and denoting his inability to fulfil his obligations.

Fault is intentional when, deliberately, the debtor refuses to perform his contractual obligations, even if this refusal is not dictated by the intention to harm his contracting party.

###### Article 1408

Even where the non-performance of the contract results from gross or intentional fault, damages only include what is an immediate and direct consequence of the non-performance.

###### Article 1409

A penalty clause is one by which a person, to ensure the performance of an agreement, undertakes to pay damages agreed in a lump sum in case of non-performance of his obligations.
In the presence of a penalty clause, no greater or lesser penalty may be awarded to the other party. Nevertheless, the judge may, even of his own motion, moderate or increase the amount thus agreed, in cases where it is manifestly excessive or derisory.

Where the undertaking has been performed in part, the agreed penalty may be reduced by the judge, even of his own motion, in proportion to the benefit that the partial performance has provided to the creditor, without prejudice to the application of the preceding paragraph.

Any stipulation contrary to the two preceding paragraphs is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1410

Whether or not the original obligation contains a term within which it must be performed, the penalty is only incurred when the person who is obliged is in default, except if the non-performance is final.

###### Article 1411

The creditor, instead of demanding the penalty stipulated against the debtor who is in default, may pursue the performance of the principal obligation. The creditor may not, however, demand at the same time, except on a subsidiary basis, the principal and the penalty, unless it was stipulated for simple delay.

###### Article 1412

The nullity of the principal obligation entails that of the penalty clause. The nullity of the latter does not entail that of the principal obligation.

###### Article 1413

The damages due by reason of delay in the payment of a monetary obligation consist of interest at the legal rate. They are only due from the day of notice, except in the case where the law makes them run automatically.
Accrued income, such as rents, arrears of perpetual or life annuities, bears interest from the day of the claim or the agreement.

These damages are due without the creditor being required to prove any loss.
The creditor to whom his debtor in default has caused harm independent of this delay, may obtain damages distinct from default interest.

###### Article 1414

In all matters, the award of compensation carries interest at the legal rate even in the absence of a request or special provision in the judgment. Unless otherwise provided by law, this interest runs from the pronouncement of the judgment, unless the judge decides otherwise.
In case of pure and simple confirmation by the court of appeal of a decision awarding compensation in reparation for damage, the latter bears interest at the legal rate automatically from the judgment at first instance. In other cases, the compensation awarded on appeal bears interest from the appeal decision. The court of appeal may always derogate from the provisions of this paragraph.

#### Chapter III: Exemption from liability Article 1415

In non-contractual matters, the external cause resides in fortuitous event, the act of a third party or of the victim. The external cause is totally exonerating if it has the characteristics of force majeure. This is the case when the event escapes the control of the defendant or the person for whom he must answer, and the occurrence or consequences of which they could not avoid by appropriate measures.
In contractual matters, force majeure and its effects are defined in Article 1364.

###### Article 1416

The victim's breach of his contractual obligations, his fault or that of a person for whom he must answer are partially exonerating when they have contributed to the occurrence of the damage.
In case of bodily injury, only gross fault may result in partial exemption.

###### Article 1417

Unless it has the characteristics of force majeure, the fault committed by the victim deprived of discernment has no exonerating effect.

###### Article 1418

The fault or contractual non-performance that may be raised against the direct victim may also be raised against victims of consequential loss.

#### Chapter IV

The effects of civil liability Section I: General rules

###### Sub-section 1: The sanction

###### § 1. Reparation Article 1419

Reparation has the purpose of erasing the consequences of the harmful act and aims at complete restoration. The victim must derive neither loss nor profit from it.
Reparation may take the form of reparation in kind or by monetary equivalent. These two forms of reparation may be combined in order to ensure complete reparation of the victim's loss.

###### Article 1420

Reparation in kind must make it possible to eliminate, reduce or compensate for the damage. It cannot be imposed on the victim.
Nor can it be ordered in case of impossibility or manifest disproportion between its cost for the person liable and its benefit for the victim. Subject to the same reservations, the judge may authorise the victim to take the measures of reparation in kind himself at the expense of the person liable. The latter may be ordered to advance the necessary sums.

###### Article 1421

Damages are assessed at the date of the judgment, taking into account all circumstances that may have affected the nature and value of the harm since the day the damage manifested, as well as its reasonably foreseeable evolution.
In the event of aggravation of the damage subsequent to the judgment, the victim may request additional compensation for the resulting harm.
Each head of damage is assessed separately.

###### Article 1422

Except in the case of bodily injury, damages are reduced whenever the victim has not taken useful and reasonable measures, particularly in light of their contributory capacity, to prevent the aggravation of their harm.

###### § 2. Cessation of the unlawful act

###### Article 1423

In non-contractual matters, independently of compensation for any harm suffered, the judge may always order reasonable measures to prevent damage or to stop the unlawful disturbance to which the plaintiff is exposed.

###### § 3. Civil fine Article 1424

In non-contractual matters, where the author of the damage has deliberately committed a fault with a view to obtaining a gain or saving, the judge may order them, at the request of the victim or the public prosecutor and by a specially reasoned decision, to pay a civil fine.

###### Article 1425

This fine is proportionate to the seriousness of the fault committed, the contributory capacity of the author and the profits they have derived from it.
The civil fine may not exceed ten times the amount of the profit realized.
If the liable party is a legal person, the fine may be increased to 5% of the amount of the highest turnover excluding taxes realized in Djibouti during one of the financial years closed since the financial year preceding that during which the fault was committed.

###### Article 1426

This civil fine is allocated to the Public Treasury. It is not insurable.

###### Sous-section 2: The effect of plurality of liable parties Article 1427

Where several persons are liable for the same damage, they are jointly and severally liable to make reparation to the victim.

###### Article 1428

If all or some of the persons liable for the same damage have committed a fault, they contribute among themselves in proportion to the seriousness and causal role of the generative act attributable to them.
If none of them has committed a fault, they contribute in proportion to the causal role of the generative act attributable to them and, failing that, in equal shares.

##### Section II: Special rules

###### Sous-section 1

Special rules for compensation for harm resulting from bodily injury

###### Article 1429

Any stipulation contrary to the provisions of this subsection is deemed unwritten, unless it is more favorable to the victim.

###### Article 1430

Harm must be assessed without taking into account any predispositions of the victim where the condition resulting therefrom was only caused or revealed by the harmful act.

###### Article 1431

Subject to special provisions, patrimonial and extra-patrimonial harm resulting from bodily injury gives rise to full compensation.

###### Article 1432

Sums paid to the victim for compensatory purposes by third-party payers give rise to no action or subrogatory recourse against the liable party or their insurer except in the cases and under the conditions provided by law.
In the event that the insolvency of the liable party would prevent full compensation of the victim, the victim shall have priority over the third-party payer for what remains owed to them by the liable party.

The fault of the victim may only reduce their right to compensation with respect to the portion of their harm that has not been compensated by the benefits of the third-party payer. The third-party payer is entitled to the balance of the debt charged to the liable party.

###### Sous-section 2

Special rules for compensation for harm resulting from material damage

###### Article 1433

In the event of damage to a corporeal thing, the compensation is the lower of the two sums representing the cost of restoration and that of replacement of the thing, without taking into account its wear and tear or any capital gain inherent in the repair.
Where the thing can be neither restored nor replaced, the compensation is the value that the thing would have had on the date of the decision, in its condition prior to the damage.

If, at the request of the victim, the damaged thing is not returned to the liable party in its current condition, its residual value is deducted from the compensation.

###### Article 1434

Where applicable, the compensation also covers the deprivation of enjoyment of the damaged thing, loss of profits or any other harm.

###### Sous-section 3

Special rules for compensation for harm resulting from environmental damage

###### Article 1435

Any person liable for ecological harm is required to repair it.

###### Article 1436

Reparable ecological harm is that which consists of a non-negligible impairment of the elements or functions of ecosystems or of the collective benefits derived by humans from the environment.

###### Article 1437

The action for reparation of ecological harm is open to any person having standing and interest to act, such as the State or any public authority and public establishments as well as approved associations or those created at least five years before the date of commencement of proceedings which have as their object the protection of nature and the defense of the environment.
Independently of the action for reparation of harm possibly suffered or in parallel with it, the judge may always order reasonable measures to prevent damage or to stop the unlawful disturbance to which the environment is exposed.

###### Article 1438

Reparation of ecological harm is effected as a priority in kind.

In the event of impossibility or insufficiency of reparation measures, the judge orders the liable party to pay damages, allocated to the reparation of the environment, to the plaintiff or, if the plaintiff cannot take the measures useful for this purpose, to the State.

The assessment of ecological harm takes into account reparation measures that may already have been taken.

###### Article 1439

In the event of a penalty payment, it is liquidated by the judge for the benefit of the plaintiff, who allocates it to the reparation of the environment or, if the plaintiff cannot take the measures useful for this purpose, for the benefit of the State, which allocates it to this same purpose.
The judge who orders a penalty payment with a view to the reparation of ecological harm has the power to liquidate it.

###### Sous-section 4

Special rules for liability and compensation of victims of bodily injury traffic accidents

###### Article 1440

Liability for land motor vehicles is governed by the provisions of the Law on liability and compensation of victims of bodily injury traffic accidents (Law No. 40/AN/99/4ème L of 8 June 1999).

###### Sous-section 5

Special rules for liability for defective products Article 1441
The provisions of this subsection apply to the reparation of damage resulting from injury to the person or that, in an amount exceeding 100,000 FD, resulting from damage to property other than the defective product itself.

###### Article 1442

A product within the meaning of this subsection is any movable property, even if it is incorporated into immovable property, including products of the soil, livestock, hunting and fishing. Electricity is considered a product.
Such a product is deemed defective within the meaning of this subsection when it does not offer the safety which one is legitimately entitled to expect having regard to all the circumstances and in particular the presentation of the product, the use to which it could reasonably be expected that the product would be put and the time when the product was put into circulation. A product may not, however, be considered defective for the sole reason that a better product was subsequently put into circulation.

###### Article 1443

The producer is liable for damage caused by a defect in a product which he has put into circulation, whether or not the producer is bound by a contract with the victim.
A product is put into circulation when the producer has voluntarily parted with it. A product is put into circulation only once.

###### Article 1444

A producer within the meaning of these provisions is, when acting in a professional capacity, the manufacturer of a finished product, the producer of a raw material, the manufacturer of a component part. Any person acting in a professional capacity who presents himself as a producer by affixing to the product his name, trademark or other distinguishing feature is assimilated to a producer for the application of this chapter;
Persons whose liability may be sought on the basis of articles 1954 to 1962 and 1819 are not considered producers within the meaning of this chapter.

If the producer cannot be identified, the seller, the lessor, with the exception of the lessor under a finance lease or a lessor similar to a lessor under a finance lease, or any other professional supplier, is liable for the lack of safety of the product, under the same conditions as the producer, unless he identifies his own supplier or the producer, within three months from the date on which the victim's claim was notified to him.

The supplier may bring a claim for indemnity against the producer, in which case his recourse against the producer is subject to the same rules as the claim brought by the direct victim of the defect. However, he must do so within one year following the date of his being summoned to court.

###### Article 1445

In the event of damage caused by a defect in a product incorporated into another product, the producer of the component part and the person who carried out the incorporation are jointly and severally liable.
The producer of the component part is not, however, liable if he establishes that the defect is attributable to the design of the product into which the component part was incorporated or to the instructions given by the producer of that product.

###### Article 1446

The claimant must prove the damage, the defect and the causal link between the defect and the damage.

The producer is liable as of right unless he proves:
1° That he had not put the product into circulation;
2° That, having regard to the circumstances, it is probable that the defect which caused the damage did not exist at the time when the product was put into circulation by him or that this defect came into being afterwards;
3° That the product was not intended for sale or any other form of distribution;
4° That the state of scientific and technical knowledge at the time when he put the product into circulation was not such as to enable the existence of the defect to be discovered; this ground of exoneration is excluded when the damage was caused by an element of the human body or by products derived from it;
5° Or that the defect is due to compliance of the product with mandatory rules of a legislative or regulatory nature.

The producer may not exonerate himself on the ground that the product was manufactured in accordance with the rules of the art or existing standards or that it was the subject of an administrative authorisation.

###### Article 1447

The liability of the producer may be reduced or excluded, having regard to all the circumstances, when the damage is caused jointly by a defect in the product and by the fault of the victim or of a person for whom the victim is responsible.

The liability of the producer towards the victim is not reduced by the act of a third party who contributed to the occurrence of the damage.

###### Article 1448

Clauses which seek to exclude or limit liability for defective products are prohibited and deemed unwritten.
However, for damage caused to property which is not used by the victim principally for his own private use or consumption, clauses stipulated between professionals are valid.

###### Article 1449

Except in the case of fault of the producer, the liability of the producer, based on the provisions of this chapter, is extinguished ten years after the putting into circulation of the actual product which caused the damage unless, during this period, the victim has brought legal proceedings.

###### Article 1450

The action for compensation based on the provisions of this subsection is prescribed within a period of three years from the date on which the claimant became aware or should have become aware of the damage, the defect and the identity of the producer.

###### Article 1451

The provisions of this chapter do not affect the rights which the victim of damage may rely on under the law of contractual or extra-contractual liability or under a special liability regime.
The producer remains liable for the consequences of his fault and that of the persons for whom he is responsible.

Sous-titre III : Les quasi-contrats Article 1452
Quasi-contracts are purely voluntary acts from which there results an obligation on the part of the person who benefits from them without being entitled to do so, and sometimes an obligation on the part of their author towards another person.
The quasi-contracts governed by this subtitle are: management of affairs, undue payment and unjust enrichment.
Chapitre Ier : La gestion d'affaires

###### Article 1453

A person who, without being obliged to do so, knowingly and usefully manages the affairs of another, without the knowledge or without the opposition of the owner of those affairs, is subject, in the performance of the legal and material acts of his management, to all the obligations of a mandatary.
The usefulness of the act of the manager is assessed at the date when it was performed.

###### Article 1454

This manager of affairs is required to bring to his management all the care of a reasonable person. He must continue the management commenced, until the owner of the affairs or his successor is in a position to provide for it.

The judge may, according to the circumstances, mitigate the damages which would result from the faults or negligence of the manager.

###### Article 1455

The person whose affairs have been usefully managed must fulfil the obligations contracted in his interest by the manager.
He reimburses the manager for the useful or necessary expenses incurred in his interest, and indemnifies him for the damage which he has suffered by reason of his management.
The sums advanced by the manager bear interest from the day of payment.

###### Article 1456

Ratification of the management by the owner is equivalent to express mandate.

###### Article 1457

The fact that the manager has a personal interest in taking charge of the affairs of another does not exclude the application of the rules of management of affairs.
In this case, the burden of obligations, expenses and damages is apportioned in proportion to the interests of each in the common affair.

###### Article 1458

If the action of the manager does not meet the conditions of management of affairs but nevertheless benefits the owner of those affairs, the latter must indemnify the manager according to the rules of unjust enrichment.

#### Chapter II: Payment of undue amount Article 1459

Every payment presupposes a debt; what has been received without being due is subject to restitution.
Restitution is not admitted with regard to natural obligations which have been voluntarily discharged.

###### Article 1460

He who receives by error or knowingly what is not due to him must restore it to him from whom he has unduly received it.

###### Article 1461

He who by error or under duress has discharged the debt of another may bring an action for restitution against the creditor.
Nevertheless this right ceases in the case where the creditor, following the payment, has destroyed his title or abandoned the securities which guaranteed his claim.
Restitution may also be claimed from him whose debt has been discharged by error.

###### Article 1462

Restitution is subject to the rules set out in articles 1577 to 1585. It may be reduced if the payment proceeds from a fault.

#### Chapter III: Unjust enrichment

###### Article 1463

Outside the cases of management of affairs and payment of undue amount, he who benefits from an enrichment without cause to the detriment of another owes, to him who finds himself impoverished thereby, an indemnity equal to the lesser of the two values of the enrichment and the impoverishment.

###### Article 1464

Enrichment is without cause when it does not proceed either from the performance of an obligation by the impoverished party or from his gratuitous intention.

###### Article 1465

There is no ground for indemnification if the impoverishment proceeds from an act performed by the impoverished party with a view to personal profit.
Indemnification may be moderated by the judge if the impoverishment proceeds from a fault of the impoverished party.

### Title IV: General regime of obligations

Chapter I: Modalities of the obligation

##### Section I: Conditional obligation Article 1466

An obligation is conditional when it depends on a future and uncertain event, or on an event which has already occurred but is still unknown to the parties.
In the first case, the condition is either suspensive, when the birth of the obligation depends on its fulfillment, or resolutory, when its fulfillment brings about the annulment of the juridical act which it concerns.
In the second case, the obligation has its effect from the day on which it was contracted.

###### Article 1467

Any condition of an impossible thing, or contrary to good morals, or prohibited by law is null, and renders null the agreement which depends on it. This nullity is absolute.
The condition not to do an impossible thing does not render null the obligation contracted under this condition.

###### Article 1468

Any obligation is null when it has been contracted under a condition the realization of which depends on the sole will of the debtor.
This nullity, which is relative, may not however be invoked when the obligation has been performed with full knowledge by him who was bound by it.

###### Article 1469

Every condition must be fulfilled in the manner that the parties probably wished and intended that it should be.
The suspensive condition is deemed fulfilled when it is the debtor, bound under this condition, who has prevented its fulfillment.

The resolutory condition is deemed to have failed if its fulfillment has been brought about by the party who had an interest therein.

###### Article 1470

When an obligation is contracted under the condition that an event will occur within a fixed time, this condition is deemed to have failed when the time has expired without the event having occurred. If there is no fixed time, the condition may always be fulfilled; and it is deemed to have failed only when it has become certain that the event will not occur.

###### Article 1471

When an obligation is contracted under the condition that an event will not occur within a fixed time, this condition is fulfilled when that time has expired without the event having occurred: it is also fulfilled, if before the term it is certain that the event will not occur; and if there is no determined time, it is fulfilled only when it is certain that the event will not occur.

###### Article 1472

A party is free to renounce the condition stipulated in his exclusive interest, as long as it is not fulfilled.

###### Article 1473

The fulfilled condition has a retroactive effect to the day on which the engagement was contracted. If the creditor died before the fulfillment of the condition, his rights pass to his heir.

###### Article 1474

Before the suspensive condition is fulfilled, the debtor must refrain from any act which would prevent the proper performance of the obligation.
The creditor may, before the condition is fulfilled, exercise all conservatory acts of his right and challenge the acts of the debtor performed in fraud of his rights.
What has been paid may be recovered as long as the suspensive condition has not been fulfilled.

###### Article 1475

When the obligation has been contracted under a suspensive condition, the thing which is the subject matter of the agreement remains at the risks of the debtor of the obligation to deliver this thing and this, until the fulfillment of the condition. He retains the administration thereof and is entitled to the fruits until the fulfillment of the condition.
If the thing has entirely perished without the fault of the debtor, the obligation is extinguished.

If the thing has deteriorated without the fault of the debtor, the creditor has the choice either to rescind the obligation, or to demand the thing in the state in which it is, without reduction of the price.
If the thing has deteriorated by the fault of the debtor, the creditor has the right either to rescind the obligation, or to demand the thing in the state in which it is, with damages.

###### Article 1476

The fulfillment of the suspensive condition gives rise to all the effects which were linked to its realization. However, the parties may provide that the fulfillment of the condition will have retroactive effect to the day of the contract.

###### Article 1477

In case of failure of the suspensive condition, the obligation is deemed never to have existed; if the suspensive condition concerned all the effects of the contract, the latter becomes lapsed.

###### Article 1478

In case of a resolutory condition, the resolution must be sought in court. The judge may grant the defendant a delay according to the circumstances.
The fulfillment of the resolutory condition extinguishes the obligation retroactively, without calling into question, where applicable, conservatory and administrative acts and the collection of fruits. If the thing has perished before the fulfillment of the condition, the risks realized are for the creditor of the obligation to deliver this thing.

Retroactivity does not take place if such is the agreement of the parties or if the exchanged performances have found their utility as the reciprocal performance of the contract progressed.

##### Section II: Obligation with a term Article 1479

An obligation is with a term when its enforceability is deferred until the occurrence of a future and certain event, even though the date thereof is uncertain.

###### Article 1480

The term may be express or tacit.

###### Article 1481

What is due only at a term, may not be demanded before the expiry of the term; but what has been paid in advance may not be recovered.
The creditor of the obligation affected by a term may exercise all conservatory acts of his right and act against the acts of the debtor performed in fraud of his rights.

###### Article 1482

The term benefits the debtor, unless it results from the law, from the will of the parties or from the circumstances that it has been established in favor of the creditor or of both parties.
The party for whose exclusive benefit the term has been fixed may renounce it without the consent of the other.

###### Article 1483

The debtor can no longer claim the benefit of the term when he has become bankrupt, or if he does not provide the security promised to the creditor or diminishes that which guarantees the obligation.

###### Article 1484

The forfeiture of the term incurred by a debtor cannot be invoked against his co-obligors, even if they are jointly and severally liable.

##### Section III: The plural obligation

###### Sous-section 1: La pluralité d'objets Article 1485

The obligation is facultative when it has as its object a certain performance but the debtor has the option, in order to discharge himself, to provide another.

The facultative obligation is extinguished if the performance of the initially agreed performance becomes impossible due to force majeure.

###### Article 1486

The obligation is alternative when it has as its object several performances and the execution of one of them discharges the debtor.
The choice between the performances to be executed belongs to the debtor, if it has not been expressly granted to the creditor. The debtor may discharge himself by delivering one of the promised things; but he cannot force the creditor to receive part of one and part of another.

If the choice is not exercised within the agreed time or within a reasonable period, the other party may, after formal notice, exercise this choice or terminate the contract.
The choice, once it is exercised, is final and causes the obligation to lose its alternative character. The alternative obligation then becomes pure and simple.

###### Article 1487

When the obligation is alternative and the choice has been exercised, the impossibility of performing the chosen performance by reason of force majeure discharges the debtor.
If the debtor has not made his choice known at the time when the impossibility materializes, he must, if one of the performances becomes impossible, perform one of the others. When the performances become impossible, the debtor is only discharged if the impossibility proceeds, for each, from a case of force majeure.

If the creditor has not made his choice known, he must, if one of the performances becomes impossible to perform as a result of force majeure, be satisfied with one of the others.

###### Article 1488

When the performances become impossible, the debtor is only discharged if the impossibility proceeds, for each, from a case of force majeure.

###### Sous-section 2: La pluralité de sujets

###### Article 1489

The obligation that binds several creditors or debtors is divided by operation of law between them. The division also takes place between their successors, even if the obligation is joint and several. If it is not otherwise regulated by law or by contract, the division takes place in equal shares.
Each of the creditors is entitled only to his share of the common claim; each of the debtors is liable only for his share of the common debt.
It is otherwise, in the relations between creditors and debtors, only if the obligation is joint and several or if the performance due is indivisible.

###### § 1. De l'obligation solidaire Article 1490

Joint and several liability is legal or contractual; it is not presumed.

###### Article 1491

Joint and several liability between creditors allows each of them to demand and receive payment of the entire claim. Payment made to one of them, who must account for it to the others, discharges the debtor with respect to all.
The debtor may pay one or the other of the joint and several creditors as long as he is not sued by one of them.
The remission granted by one of the joint and several creditors discharges the debtor only for the share of that creditor.

###### Article 1492

Any act that interrupts or suspends prescription with respect to one of the joint and several creditors benefits the other creditors.

###### Article 1493

Joint and several liability between debtors obliges each of them for the entire debt.
The obligation may be joint and several, although one of the debtors is obliged differently from the other for payment of the same thing; for example, if one is obliged only conditionally, while the engagement of the other is pure and simple, or if one has taken a term that is not granted to the other.

The creditor may demand payment from the joint and several debtor of his choice, without the latter being able to invoke against him the benefit of division.
Proceedings brought against one of the joint and several debtors do not prevent the creditor from bringing similar proceedings against the others.

Payment made by one of them discharges them all towards the creditor.

###### Article 1494

Proceedings brought against one of the joint and several debtors interrupt prescription with respect to all.

###### Article 1495

A demand for interest made against one of the joint and several debtors causes interest to run with respect to all.

###### Article 1496

The joint and several debtor sued by the creditor may raise defenses that are common to all co-debtors, such as nullity that is not purely personal to that debtor or termination, and those that are personal to him such as incapacity or a defect of consent affecting his will.
He may not raise defenses that are personal to other co-debtors, such as the granting of a term. However, when a defense personal to another co-debtor extinguishes the divided share of the latter, particularly in case of set-off or remission of debt, he may rely on it to have it deducted from the total debt.

###### Article 1497

If the thing due has perished through the fault of one or more of the joint and several debtors or at a date when one or more of the joint and several debtors were in default of performance, the other co-debtors remain liable to pay the price of the thing; but these other co-debtors are not liable to pay damages.

###### Article 1498

When one of the debtors becomes sole heir of the creditor, or when the creditor becomes the sole heir of one of the debtors, the confusion extinguishes the joint and several claim only for the part and portion of the debtor or creditor.

###### Article 1499

The creditor who consents to the division of the debt with respect to one of the co-debtors retains his joint and several action against the others, but subject to deduction of the share of the debtor whom he has discharged from joint and several liability.

###### Article 1500

The creditor who receives separately the share of one of the debtors, without reserving in the receipt joint and several liability or his rights in general, renounces joint and several liability only with respect to that debtor.
The creditor is not deemed to remit joint and several liability to the debtor when he receives from him a sum equal to the portion for which he is liable, if the receipt does not state that it is for his share.
The same applies to a simple demand made against one of the co-debtors for his share, if the latter has not acquiesced to the demand, or if a judgment of condemnation has not been rendered.

###### Article 1501

The creditor who receives separately and without reservation the portion of one of the co-debtors in the arrears or interest of the debt, loses joint and several liability only for the arrears or interest due, and not for those to become due, nor for the principal, unless the divided payment has been continued for ten consecutive years.

###### Article 1502

Among themselves, the joint and several co-debtors contribute to the debt each only for his share.

The one who has paid beyond his share has recourse against the others in proportion to their own share.
If one of them is insolvent, his share is distributed, by contribution, among the solvent co-debtors, including the one who made the payment and the one who benefited from a remission of joint and several liability.
On the other hand, if the debt proceeds from a matter that concerns only one of the joint and several co-debtors, the latter alone is liable for the debt with respect to the others; if he has paid it, he has no recourse against his co-debtors; if they have paid it, they have recourse against him.

###### Article 1503

Joint and several co-debtors are jointly and severally liable for non-performance of the obligation. The burden ultimately falls on those to whom the non-performance is attributable.

###### § 2. Divisible and indivisible obligations Article 1504

An obligation is divisible or indivisible depending on whether its object is a thing which in its delivery, or an act which in its performance, is or is not susceptible to division, whether material or intellectual.

###### Article 1505

An obligation is indivisible, even though the thing or act which is its object is divisible by its nature, if the relationship under which it is considered in the obligation does not make it susceptible to partial performance.

###### Article 1506

Each of the creditors of an indivisible obligation, whether by nature or by contract, may demand and receive full payment thereof, subject to accounting to the others; but he may not alone dispose of the claim or receive the price in place of the thing.

Each of the debtors of such an obligation is liable for the whole; but he has recourse in contribution against the others.
The same applies to each of the successors of these creditors and debtors.

#### Chapitre II

Transactions in obligations Section I: Assignment of claims

###### Article 1507

Assignment of a claim is a contract by which the assigning creditor transfers, for consideration or gratuitously, all or part of his claim against the assigned debtor to a third party called the assignee.
It may relate to one or more claims, present or future, determined or determinable. It extends to the accessories of the claim.
The consent of the debtor is not required, unless the claim has been stipulated as non-assignable.

###### Article 1508

Assignment of a claim must be evidenced in writing, on pain of nullity.

###### Article 1509

As between the parties, the transfer of the claim takes effect on the date of the instrument.

It is enforceable against third parties from that moment. In case of dispute, the burden of proving the date of the assignment lies with the assignee, who may do so by any means.
However, the transfer of a future claim takes place only on the day it comes into existence, both as between the parties and with respect to third parties.

###### Article 1510

The assignment is not enforceable against the debtor, if he has not already consented thereto, unless it has been notified to him or he has acknowledged it.
The debtor may raise against the assignee defences inherent in the debt, such as payment, prescription, nullity, exception of non-performance, termination or set-off of connected debts. He may also raise defences arising from his relations with the assignor before the assignment became enforceable against him, such as the granting of a term, remission of debt or set-off of unconnected debts.

The assignor and the assignee are jointly and severally liable for all additional costs occasioned by the assignment which the debtor need not advance. Unless otherwise stipulated, the burden of these costs falls on the assignee.

###### Article 1511

Competition between successive assignees of a claim is resolved in favour of the first in date; he has recourse against the person to whom the debtor has made payment.
The date to be taken into consideration is that of each of the assignments, proof of which may be provided by any means.

###### Article 1512

A person who assigns a claim for consideration guarantees the existence of the claim and its accessories, unless the assignee has acquired it at his own risk or was aware of the uncertain nature of the claim.
He is liable for the solvency of the debtor only when he has undertaken to do so, and up to the amount of the price he has obtained from the assignment of his claim. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.

Where the assignor has guaranteed the solvency of the debtor, this guarantee applies only to current solvency; it may however extend to solvency at maturity, but on condition that the assignor has expressly specified it.

##### Section II: Novation Article 1513

Novation is a contract whose object is to substitute for an obligation, which it extinguishes, a new obligation which it creates.
It may take place by substitution of obligation between the same parties, by change of debtor or by change of creditor.

###### Article 1514

Novation is not presumed; the intention to effect it must clearly result from the instrument.

###### Article 1515

Novation takes place only if the old obligation and the new obligation are both valid, unless its declared object is to substitute a valid undertaking for an undertaking tainted with a defect.

###### Article 1516

Novation by change of debtor may be effected without the participation of the first debtor.

###### Article 1517

Novation by change of creditor requires the consent of the debtor. The latter may, in advance, accept that the new creditor be designated by the first.
The novation is enforceable against third parties on the date of the instrument. In case of dispute as to the date of the novation, the burden of proof lies with the new creditor, who may provide it by any means.

###### Article 1518

Novation by substitution of obligation between the same parties is possible, whatever the difference established between the old and the new obligation.

###### Article 1519

The extinction of the old obligation extends to all its accessories.

By way of exception, original security interests may be reserved for the guarantee of the new obligation with the consent of third-party guarantors.

###### Article 1520

Novation agreed between the creditor and one of the joint and several co-debtors releases the others.

Novation agreed between the creditor and a surety does not release the principal debtor. It releases the other sureties up to the contributory share of the one whose obligation has been the subject of the novation.

##### Section III: Delegation Article 1521

Delegation is a transaction by which a person, the delegator, obtains from another, the delegatee, that he expressly binds himself towards a third party, the delegatory, who accepts him as debtor.
The delegatee may not, unless otherwise stipulated, raise against the delegatory any defence derived from his relations with the delegator or from the relations between the latter and the delegatory.

###### Article 1522

Where the delegator is debtor of the delegatory and the intention of the delegatory to discharge the delegator expressly results from the instrument, the delegation operates novation.
However, the delegator remains liable if he has expressly undertaken to guarantee the future solvency of the delegatee or if the latter is subject to debt settlement proceedings at the time of the delegation.

###### Article 1523

Where the delegator is debtor of the delegatory but the latter has not discharged him from his debt, the delegation gives the delegatory a second debtor.
Payment made by one of the two debtors releases the other, to the extent thereof.

###### Article 1524

Where the delegator is creditor of the delegatee, his claim is extinguished only by performance of the obligation of the delegatee towards the delegatory and to the extent thereof.
Until then, the delegator may demand or receive payment thereof only for the part which would exceed the undertaking of the delegatee. He recovers his rights only by performing his own obligation towards the delegatory.

Assignment or seizure of the claim of the delegator produces effect only under the same limitations.

However, if the delegatory has released the delegator, the delegatee is himself released with respect to the delegator, up to the amount of his undertaking towards the delegatory.

###### Article 1525

The simple indication made by the debtor of a person designated to pay in his place does not entail either novation or delegation. The same applies to the simple indication made by the creditor of a person designated to receive payment for him.

#### Chapter III: Actions Available to the Creditor Article 1526

The creditor has the right to performance of the obligation; he may compel the debtor to perform under the conditions provided by law and especially by the provisions of the code of civil procedure.

###### Article 1527

When the debtor's failure to exercise his rights and actions of a patrimonial nature compromises the rights of his creditor, the latter may, by oblique action, exercise them on behalf of his debtor,

with the exception of those which are exclusively attached to his person. Rights exclusively attached to the person of the debtor are rights and actions whose exercise is subject to personal considerations of a moral or family nature.

###### Article 1528

The creditor may also act in his own name, by way of the Paulian action, to have acts performed by his debtor in fraud of his rights declared unenforceable against him, provided he establishes, in the case of an act for valuable consideration, that the third party co-contractor had knowledge of the fraud.
The action is available when the debtor has performed an act of impoverishment aimed at organizing his insolvency or making the creditor's enforcement more difficult. It is also available when the creditor has a special right over property of the debtor and the latter performs an act which has the effect of impairing that special right.

The claim must be certain on the day the action is brought. The enforceability and liquidity of the claim are not conditions for the Paulian action.

###### Article 1529

In cases determined by law, the creditor may act directly for payment of his claim against a debtor of his debtor.

#### Chapter IV

Extinction of the Obligation Section I: Payment

###### Sub-section 1: General Provisions

###### Article 1530

Payment is the voluntary performance of the obligation due.

It must be made as soon as the debt becomes enforceable; it may be made even by a person who is not bound to do so, except in case of legitimate refusal by the creditor.
Payment releases the debtor towards the creditor and extinguishes the debt, except when the law or the contract provides for subrogation in the rights of the creditor.

###### Article 1531

Payment must be made to the creditor or to the person designated to receive it.

Payment made to a person who was not qualified to receive it is nevertheless valid if the creditor ratifies it or if he has benefited from it.
Payment made to a creditor incapable of contracting is not valid, unless he has benefited from it.

###### Article 1532

Payment made in good faith to an apparent creditor is valid.

###### Article 1533

The creditor may refuse partial payment even if the obligation is divisible. He may agree to receive in payment something other than what is owed to him.

###### Article 1534

The debtor of an obligation to deliver a specific thing is released by its delivery to the creditor in its current state, except to prove, in case of deterioration, that it is not due to his act or to that of persons for whom he must answer.

If the debt is of a thing which is determined only by its kind, the debtor shall not be required, in order to be released, to give it of the best kind; but he may not offer it of the worst kind.

###### Article 1535

In the absence of another designation by law, contract or judge, payment must be made at the domicile of the debtor.

###### Article 1536

The costs of payment are, except where otherwise provided by law or clause, borne by the debtor.

###### Article 1537

Payment is proved by any means.

###### Article 1538

The voluntary delivery by the creditor to the debtor of the original under private signature or of the enforceable copy of the title of his claim constitutes a simple presumption of release.
The same delivery to one of the joint and several co-debtors produces the same effect towards all.

###### Article 1539

The debtor of several debts may indicate, when he pays, which one he intends to discharge.

In the absence of indication by the debtor, imputation takes place as follows: first on debts due; among these, on debts which the debtor had the greatest interest in discharging. Where interests are equal, imputation is made on the oldest; all things being equal, it is made proportionally.

###### Sub-section 2: Special Provisions for Obligations of Sums of Money

###### Article 1540

The debtor of an obligation of a sum of money is released by payment of its nominal amount. The amount of the sum due may however vary through indexation or debts of value.
A debt of value is an obligation which has as its object, not a determined sum of money, but a value which may give rise, according to the times, to different estimates, such as the debt of reparation which is determined on the day of judgment and not on the day of the harmful act. The debtor of a debt of value is released by payment of the sum of money resulting from its liquidation.

###### Article 1541

When the obligation of a sum of money bears interest, the debtor is released by paying the principal and the interest. Partial payment is imputed first to interest, except by contrary agreement.
Interest is granted by law or stipulated in the contract. The rate of contractual interest must be fixed in writing. It is deemed annual by default.

###### Article 1542

Interest due, owed for at least one full year, produces interest if the contract has provided for it or if a judicial decision specifies it.

###### Article 1543

Payment, in Djibouti, of an obligation of a sum of money is made in Djibouti Francs. However, payment may take place in another currency if the obligation so denominated proceeds from an international contract or from a foreign judgment.

###### Article 1544

In the absence of another designation by law, contract or judge, the place of payment of the obligation of a sum of money is the domicile of the creditor.

###### Article 1545

The judge may, taking into account the situation of the debtor and in consideration of the needs of the creditor, postpone or spread out, within the limit of two years, the payment of sums due.
By special and reasoned decision, he may order that the sums corresponding to postponed instalments shall bear interest at a reduced rate at least equal to the legal rate, or that payments shall be imputed first to the capital.

He may make these measures subject to the performance by the debtor of acts designed to facilitate or guarantee payment of the debt.
The judge's decision suspends enforcement proceedings which would have been initiated by the creditor. Interest increases or penalties provided for in case of delay are not incurred during the period fixed by the judge.

Any contrary stipulation is deemed unwritten.
The provisions of this article are not applicable to maintenance debts.

###### Sub-section 3: Notice to Perform

###### Article 1546

Notice to perform is the act by which either the creditor clearly indicates to his debtor that he does not intend to allow a contractual non-performance to continue, or the debtor enjoins his creditor not to obstruct performance of the contract.

###### § 1. Notice to Perform to the Debtor Article 1547

The debtor is given notice to pay either by a summons or an act containing sufficient demand, or, if the contract so provides, by the mere enforceability of the obligation.

###### Article 1548

Notice to perform to pay an obligation of a sum of money causes default interest to run, at the legal rate. The creditor does not have to justify any loss.

###### Article 1549

Notice to perform to deliver a thing places the risks on the debtor, if they are not already there.

###### § 2

Formal notice to the creditor or "tender of payment" Article 1550
Where the creditor, at maturity and without legitimate reason, refuses to receive the payment due to him or prevents it by his act, the debtor may give him formal notice to accept it or to permit its performance. This formal notice constitutes a tender of payment.
