Formal notice to the creditor stops the running of interest owed by the debtor and places the risks of the thing on the creditor, if they are not already there. It is otherwise in case of gross or fraudulent fault of the debtor.

Formal notice does not interrupt prescription.

###### Article 1551

If the obstruction has not ended within two months of the formal notice, the debtor may, where the obligation relates to a sum of money, deposit it with the registry of the Court of First Instance or, where the obligation relates to the delivery of a thing, place it in custody with a professional custodian.
If custody of the thing is impossible or too costly, the judge may authorize its amicable sale or sale by public auction. After deduction of the costs of the sale, the price is deposited with the registry of the Court of First Instance.

The deposit or custody releases the debtor from the time of notification thereof to the creditor.

###### Article 1552

Where the obligation relates to another object, for example an obligation to do, the debtor is released if the obstruction has not ceased within two months of the formal notice.

###### Article 1553

The costs of formal notice and of deposit or custody are borne by the creditor.

###### Sub-section 4: Payment with subrogation

###### Article 1554

Subrogation takes place by operation of law alone in favor of one who, having a legitimate interest, makes payment provided that his payment releases, towards the creditor, the person who is bound to bear the definitive burden of all or part of the debt.

###### Article 1555

Conventional subrogation is effected at the initiative of the creditor when the latter, receiving his payment from a third person, subrogates him in his rights against the debtor.
This subrogation must be express.

It must be granted at the same time as the payment, unless, in a prior act, the subrogor has manifested the intention that his contracting party be subrogated to him upon payment. The concomitance of the subrogation and the payment may be proved by any means.

###### Article 1556

Subrogation also takes place when the debtor, borrowing a sum for the purpose of paying his debt, subrogates the lender in the rights of the creditor with the latter's concurrence. In this case, the subrogation must be express and the receipt given by the creditor must indicate the origin of the funds.
Subrogation may be granted without the concurrence of the creditor, but on condition that the debt is due or that the term is in favor of the debtor. It is then necessary that the loan agreement and the receipt be executed before a notary, that in the loan agreement it be declared that the sum has been borrowed to make the payment, and that in the receipt it be declared that the payment has been made from the sums paid for that purpose by the new creditor.

###### Article 1557

Subrogation cannot harm the creditor when he has been paid only in part; in this case, he may exercise his rights, for what remains due to him, in preference to the person from whom he has received only partial payment.
Subrogation transfers to its beneficiary, within the limit of what he has paid, the claim and its accessories, with the exception of rights exclusively attached to the person of the creditor.

However, the subrogee is entitled only to legal interest from the time of formal notice, if he has not agreed with the debtor on a new interest. These interests are guaranteed by the security interests attached to the claim, within the limits, where they have been created by third parties, of their initial commitments if they do not consent to bind themselves beyond.

###### Article 1558

The debtor may invoke subrogation as soon as he has knowledge of it but it may be set up against him only if it has been notified to him or if he has acknowledged it.
Subrogation is opposable to third parties from the time of payment.
The debtor may set up against the subrogated creditor defenses inherent in the debt, such as nullity, the defense of non-performance, termination or set-off of related debts. He may also set up against him defenses arising from his relations with the subrogor before the subrogation became opposable to him, such as the granting of a term, remission of debt or set-off of unrelated debts.

##### Section II: Set-off

###### Sub-section 1: General rules Article 1559

Set-off is the simultaneous extinction of reciprocal obligations between two persons.

It operates, subject to being invoked, to the extent applicable, on the date when its conditions are met.

###### Article 1560

Subject to the provisions set out in the following sub-section, set-off takes place only between two fungible, certain, liquidated and due obligations.
Fungible are obligations of sums of money, even in different currencies, provided they are convertible, or those which have as their object a quantity of things of the same kind.

###### Article 1561

Unseizable claims and obligations to restore a deposit, a loan for use or a thing of which the owner has been unjustly deprived are subject to set-off only if the creditor consents thereto.

###### Article 1562

A grace period does not preclude set-off.

###### Article 1563

If there are several debts subject to set-off, the rules for imputation of payments in articles 1392, 1394 and 1398 are transposable.

###### Article 1564

The debtor who has acknowledged without reservation the assignment of the claim may not set up against the assignee the set-off that he could have set up against the assignor.

###### Article 1565

The surety may set up against the creditor the set-off that occurred between the latter and the principal debtor.

The joint and several co-debtor may avail himself of the set-off that occurred between the creditor and one of his co-obligors to have the divisible share of the latter deducted from the total debt.

###### Article 1566

Set-off does not prejudice rights acquired by third parties.

###### Sub-section 2: Special rules Article 1567

Set-off may be pronounced in court even if one of the obligations, although certain, is not yet liquidated or due. Unless otherwise decided, the set-off then produces its effects on the date of the decision.

###### Article 1568

The judge may not refuse set-off of related debts on the sole ground that one of the obligations is not liquidated or due.
In this case, the set-off is deemed to have occurred on the day of the maturity of the first of them.
In the same case, the acquisition of rights by a third party over one of the obligations does not prevent its debtor from setting up the set-off.

###### Article 1569

The parties may freely agree to extinguish all reciprocal obligations, present or future, by set-off; this takes effect on the date of their agreement or, in the case of future obligations, on that of their coexistence.

##### Section III: Confusion Article 1570

Confusion results from the union of the capacities of creditor and debtor of the same obligation in the same person. It extinguishes the claim and its accessories, subject to rights acquired by or against third parties.

###### Article 1571

Where there is solidarity between several debtors or between several creditors, and the confusion concerns only one of them, the extinction takes place, with regard to the others, only for his share.
Where the confusion concerns a guaranteed obligation, the surety, even if solidary, is released. Where the confusion concerns the obligation of one of the sureties, the principal debtor is not released. The other solidary sureties are released up to the share of that surety.

##### Section IV : La remise de dette Article 1572

Release of debt is the contract by which the creditor releases the debtor from his obligation.

###### Article 1573

Release of debt granted to one of the solidary co-debtors releases the others up to his share.

Release of debt made by only one of the solidary creditors releases the debtor only for the share of that creditor.

###### Article 1574

Release of debt granted to the principal debtor releases the sureties, even if solidary.

Release granted to one of the solidary sureties does not release the principal debtor, but releases the others up to his share.

What the creditor has received from a surety for the discharge of his suretyship must be credited against the debt and discharge the principal debtor proportionally. The other sureties remain liable only after deduction of the share of the released surety or of the value provided if it exceeds that share.

##### Section V : L'impossibilité d'exécuter Article 1575

Impossibility of performing the prestation releases the debtor to the appropriate extent where it proceeds from a case of force majeure and it is definitive, unless he has agreed to take responsibility for it or he has been previously placed in default.

###### Article 1576

Where the impossibility of performance results from the loss of the thing owed, the debtor placed in default is nevertheless released if he proves that the loss would have occurred similarly if the obligation had been performed. He is however bound to assign to his creditor the rights and actions attached to the thing.

#### Chapitre V : Les restitutions

###### Article 1577

Restitution of a thing other than a sum of money takes place in kind or, where that is impossible, in value, estimated at the day of restitution.

###### Article 1578

The person who restores the thing is liable for degradations and deteriorations which have diminished its value, unless he is in good faith and they are not due to his fault.

###### Article 1579

The person who having received the thing in good faith has sold it, must restore only the price of the sale.

If he received it in bad faith, he owes its value at the day of restitution where it is greater than the price.

###### Article 1580

Restitution includes the fruits and the value of the enjoyment that the thing has provided. The value of the enjoyment is assessed by the judge at the day when he rules.
Unless otherwise stipulated, restitution of the fruits, if they are not found in kind, takes place according to a value estimated at the date of reimbursement, according to the state of the thing at the day of payment of the obligation.

###### Article 1581

Restitutions owed to an unemancipated minor or to a protected adult are reduced in proportion to the profit he has derived from the annulled act.

###### Article 1582

To fix the amount of restitutions, account is taken to the person who must restore, even if he is in bad faith, of the necessary and useful expenses for the conservation of the thing, within the limit of the increased value estimated at the day of restitution.

###### Article 1583

Restitution of a sum of money includes interest at the legal rate and taxes paid into the hands of the person who received it.

###### Article 1584

The person who has received in bad faith owes the interest, the fruits he has collected or the value of the enjoyment from the time of payment. The person who has received in good faith owes them only from the day of the demand.

###### Article 1585

Restitution of a service prestation takes place in value. This is assessed at the date at which it was provided.
Securities constituted for payment of the obligation are transferred by operation of law to the obligation to restore without however the surety being deprived of the benefit of the term.

### Titre V : De la preuve civile

###### Article 1586

The burden of proof lies on the person who claims recognition of a right or performance of an obligation.
Reciprocally, the person who claims to be released must justify the fact which produced the extinction of the right opposed to him.

Judicial administration of proof and disputes relating thereto are governed by the code of civil procedure.

Chapitre Ier : L'admissibilité des modes de preuve Article 1587
Except in cases where the law provides otherwise, proof may be adduced by any means.

###### Article 1588

A juridical act relating to a sum or value exceeding the sum or value of 100,000 FD, must be proved by writing under private signature or authentic.
It cannot be proved beyond or against a writing establishing a juridical act, even if the sum or value does not exceed that amount, except by another writing under private signature or authentic.
The person whose claim exceeds the threshold mentioned in the first paragraph cannot be dispensed from proof by writing by restricting his demand.

The same applies to the person whose demand, even less than that amount, relates to the balance or to part of a claim greater than that amount.

###### Article 1589

The rules provided for in Article 1588 are subject to exception:
-	in case of material or moral impossibility of obtaining a writing,
-	if it is customary not to establish a writing,
-	or where the writing has been lost as a result of an external cause.

###### Article 1590

Writing may also be supplemented by judicial admission, the decisive oath or a commencement of proof by writing corroborated by another means of proof.

###### Article 1591

A commencement of proof by writing constitutes any written act which has emanated from the person against whom the demand is made, or from the person he represents, and which makes the alleged fact plausible.
Declarations made by a party during his personal appearance, his refusal to answer or his absence at the appearance may be considered by the judge as equivalent to a commencement of proof by writing.

The mention of an authentic or private signature writing in a public register is equivalent to a commencement of proof by writing.

#### Chapitre II : La preuve par écrit

##### Section I : Dispositions générales

###### Article 1592

No one may constitute a title for himself.

###### Article 1593

Proof of a juridical act may be preconstituted by a writing in authentic form or under private signature.
Where a party does not know how to read, write or sign, if it is a question of an authentic act, the public officer shall have the fingerprints of that person affixed on the act after having read it to him and asked whether he consents to it. If it is a question of an act under private signature, the person who does not know how to read, write or sign, first chooses a person of his choice who reads the act to him, then affixes his fingerprint on the said act, finally the chosen person signs the act as witness.

###### Article 1594

Writing consists of a sequence of letters, characters, figures or any other signs or symbols endowed with an intelligible meaning, whatever their medium.

###### Article 1595

Electronic writing has the same probative force as writing on paper medium, provided that the person from whom it emanates can be duly identified and that it is established and preserved under conditions such as to guarantee its integrity.

###### Article 1596

The signature necessary for the perfection of a legal act identifies its author. It manifests their consent to the obligations arising from that act. When it is affixed by a public officer, it confers authenticity on the act.
When it is electronic, it consists in the use of a reliable identification process guaranteeing its link with the act to which it is attached.

###### Article 1597

In the absence of contrary provisions or agreements, the judge resolves conflicts of written evidence by determining by any means the most plausible instrument.

##### Section II : L'acte authentique Article 1598

An authentic act is one that has been received, with the required solemnities, by a public officer having the right to execute instruments in the place where the act was drawn up.

###### Article 1599

An act that is not authentic due to the incompetence or incapacity of the officer, or due to a defect of form, is valid as a privately signed writing if it has been signed by the parties.

###### Article 1600

An authentic act is evidence until impugnment for forgery of what the public officer states to have personally accomplished or observed.
Nevertheless, in case of complaints of principal forgery, the execution of the act alleged to be forged shall be suspended by the indictment; and, in case of impugnment for forgery made incidentally, the courts may, according to the circumstances, provisionally suspend the execution of the act.

##### Section III : L'acte sous signature privée

###### Article 1601

A privately signed act, acknowledged by the party against whom it is invoked or legally held to be acknowledged with regard to them, is evidence between those who subscribed to it and with regard to their heirs and successors in title.

###### Article 1602

The person against whom a privately signed act is invoked is obliged to formally acknowledge or disavow their handwriting or signature.
Their heirs or successors in title may similarly disavow the handwriting or signature of their predecessor, or may content themselves with declaring that they do not know the handwriting or signature of their predecessor. In these cases, verification of handwriting is ordered by the court.

###### Article 1603

A privately signed act that records a synallagmatic contract is evidence only if it has been made in as many originals as there are parties having a distinct interest, unless the parties have agreed to entrust to a third party the sole copy drawn up.
One original is sufficient for all persons having the same interest.

Each original must contain mention of the number of originals that have been made.

The person who has performed the contract, even partially, may not invoke the lack of plurality of originals or of mention of their number.
The requirement of a plurality of originals is deemed satisfied for contracts in electronic form when the act is established and preserved in accordance with Articles 1595 and 1596 paragraph two, and the process allows each party to have a copy on a durable medium or to have access to it.

###### Article 1604

A privately signed act by which one party alone undertakes towards another to pay them a sum of money or to deliver a fungible good to them must include the signature of the person who subscribes to this undertaking as well as the mention, written by themselves, of the sum or quantity in words and figures.
If the party declares that they do not know how or cannot sign, express mention is made in the act of their declaration, as well as of the reason preventing them from signing. The act bears their fingerprint.

###### Article 1605

When the sum expressed in the body of the act differs from that expressed by the handwritten mention, the privately signed act is evidence for the sum written in words.

###### Article 1606

A privately signed act acquires certain date with regard to third parties only from the day it was registered, from the day of death of a signatory, or from the day its substance is recorded in an authentic act.

##### Section IV : Les autres écrits Article 1607

The registers and documents that professionals must keep or establish have, against their author, the same probative force as privately signed writings; but the person who relies on them may not divide the entries to retain only those that are favorable to them.

###### Article 1608

Domestic registers and papers do not constitute evidence in favor of the person who wrote them. They constitute evidence against them:
1° In all cases where they formally state a payment received;
2° When they contain the express mention that the writing was made to make up for the lack of title in favor of the person for whom they state an obligation.

###### Article 1609

The mention of a payment or other cause of discharge entered by the creditor on an original instrument that has always remained in their possession is a simple presumption of discharge of the debtor.
The same applies to the mention entered on the duplicate of an instrument or receipt, provided that this duplicate is in the hands of the debtor.

##### Section V : Les copies des titres Article 1610

Copies, when the original instrument subsists, are evidence only of what is contained in the instrument, the presentation of which may always be required.
When the original instrument no longer exists, the reliable copy has the same probative force as the original. Reliability is left to the judge's assessment. Nevertheless, the executory or authentic copy of an authentic writing is deemed reliable; the same applies to copies that have been made by the authority of the magistrate, parties present or duly summoned, or to those that have been made in the presence of the parties and with their mutual consent.

Copies that the judge does not consider reliable may serve only as a commencement of proof in writing.
Copies of copies may, according to the circumstances, be considered as mere information.

###### Article 1611

The transcription of an act in public registers may serve only as a commencement of proof in writing; it will even be necessary for this:
1° That it be established that all the minutes of the notary, for the year in which the act appears to have been made, are lost, or that proof be given that the loss of the minute of this act was caused by a particular accident;
2° That there exist a proper repertory of the notary, which establishes that the act was made on the same date.
When, by means of the concurrence of these two circumstances, proof by witnesses is admitted, it will be necessary that those who were witnesses to the act, if they still exist, be heard.

##### Section VI : Les actes récognitifs Article 1612

An acknowledging act is a legal act that records the existence of a prior act without modifying its substance. It is valid as acknowledgment of the pre-existing obligation. The acknowledging act does not dispense with the presentation of the original instrument, unless its content is specially recited therein.

What it contains that is more or different from the original instrument has, in the absence of express intention of novation, no effect.

Nevertheless, if there were several conforming acknowledgments, supported by possession, and one of which was thirty years old, the creditor could be dispensed from producing the original instrument.

#### Chapitre III : La preuve par témoins Article 1613

The probative value of statements made by a third party under the conditions of the code of civil procedure is left to the judge's assessment.

#### Chapitre IV : Les présomptions Article 1614

Presumptions are consequences that the law or the magistrate draws from a known fact to an unknown fact.

##### Section I: Legal presumptions Article 1615

A legal presumption is one which is attached by law to certain acts or certain facts, and which holds them to be certain.

It dispenses the person for whose benefit it exists from providing proof thereof or shifts the object of proof.

The presumption is said to be simple when the law reserves proof to the contrary; it is said to be irrefragable when it cannot be overturned.

###### Article 1616

The authority of res judicata applies only with respect to what was the subject of the judgment. The thing claimed must be the same; the claim must be based on the same cause; the claim must be between the same parties, and brought by them and against them in the same capacity.

###### Article 1617

Agreements on proof are valid when they relate to rights over which the parties have free disposal.
Nevertheless, they cannot contradict irrefragable presumptions established by law, nor modify the faith attached to admission or oath. Nor can they establish an irrefragable presumption for the benefit of one of the parties.

##### Section II: Judicial presumptions Article 1618

Judicial presumptions are not established by law, but are left to the assessment of the judge, who must admit them only if they are serious, precise and concordant, and only in cases where the law admits proof by any means.

#### Chapter V: Admission by a party

###### Article 1619

Admission is the declaration by which a person acknowledges as true a fact capable of producing legal consequences against them.
The admission that is opposed to a party is either extrajudicial or judicial.

###### Article 1620

Purely verbal extrajudicial admission is received only in cases where the law permits proof by any means.
Its probative value is left to the assessment of the judge.

###### Article 1621

Judicial admission is the declaration made in court by the party or their specially mandated representative. It constitutes full proof against the person who made it.
It cannot be divided against its author.
It cannot be revoked, unless it is proved that it was the result of an error of fact; it could not be revoked on the pretext of an error of law.

#### Chapter VI: The oath Article 1622

The judicial oath is of two kinds:
1° That which one party refers to the other to make the judgment of the case depend on it: it is called decisive.
2° That which is referred ex officio by the judge to one or the other of the parties.

##### Section I: The decisive oath Article 1623

The decisive oath may be referred on any kind of dispute whatsoever.

###### Article 1624

It may be referred only on a fact personal to the party to whom it is referred.

###### Article 1625

It may be referred at any stage of the proceedings, and even when there exists no beginning of proof of the claim or exception on which it is invoked.

###### Article 1626

The oath may be referred back to the person who refers it, except when the fact which is its object is not that of both parties, but is purely personal to the person to whom the oath had been referred.

###### Article 1627

The person to whom the oath is referred, who refuses it or does not consent to refer it back to their adversary, or the adversary to whom it has been referred back and who refuses it, must fail in their claim or exception.

###### Article 1628

The oath constitutes proof only for the benefit of the person who referred it and their heirs and successors in title, or against them.

The oath referred by one of the joint and several creditors to the debtor releases the latter only for the share of that creditor.
The oath referred to the principal debtor also releases the sureties. That referred to one of the joint and several debtors benefits the co-debtors.
That referred to the surety benefits the principal debtor.
In these last two cases, the oath of the joint and several co-debtor or of the surety benefits the other co-debtors or the principal debtor only when it has been referred on the debt, and not on the fact of joint and several liability or suretyship.

##### Section II: The oath referred ex officio Article 1629

The judge may refer to one of the parties the oath, either to make the decision of the case depend on it, or only to determine the amount of the condemnation.

###### Article 1630

The judge may refer the oath ex officio, either on the claim or on the exception opposed to it, only under the following two conditions; it is necessary:
1.	That the claim or exception is not fully justified;
2.	That it is not totally devoid of proof.
Outside these two cases, the judge must either grant or purely and simply reject the claim.

###### Article 1631

The oath referred ex officio by the judge to one of the parties cannot be referred back by that party to the other.

###### Article 1632

The oath on the value of the thing claimed may be referred by the judge to the claimant only when it is otherwise impossible to establish that value.
The judge must even, in that case, determine the sum up to which the claimant will be believed on their oath.

### Title VI: Marriage contract and matrimonial property regimes

Chapter I. General provisions Article 1633
The law governs the conjugal association, as regards property, only in the absence of special agreements, which the spouses may make as they see fit, provided that they are not contrary either to good morals or to the provisions that follow.

###### Article 1634

The spouses, in the marriage certificate, indicate whether or not they have entered into a marriage contract.

They declare whether they opt for the matrimonial property regime of the civil code. Mention thereof is made in the marriage certificate.

When they opt for the regime of the civil code, they indicate the matrimonial property regime they choose. In the absence of stipulations in this regard, the spouses shall be subject to the regime of legal community (

###### article 1647

et seq.); and, with respect to third parties, the spouses shall be deemed to be married under this default regime whenever they have seized the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or accept its jurisdiction when they are in defence, unless in the acts entered into with those third parties, they have declared having made a marriage contract under such regime as they have indicated to them.

###### Article 1635

The spouses cannot derogate from the duties or rights that result for them from marriage or that are provided by law under the title of parental authority and guardianship.

###### Article 1636

The spouses cannot make any agreement or waiver the object of which would be to change the legal order of succession, without prejudice to inter vivos or testamentary gifts that may take place according to the forms and in the cases determined by this code.

###### Article 1637

The spouses can no longer stipulate in a general manner that their association will be governed by one of the customs, laws or local statutes that could govern the various parts of the Djiboutian territory, and which are repealed by this code.

###### Article 1638

All matrimonial agreements shall be drawn up, before the marriage, by notarial deed, in the presence and with the simultaneous consent of the future spouses and all persons who are parties thereto or their agents. Matrimonial agreements take effect on the day of the celebration of the marriage and cannot receive any change after that celebration.
Changes or counter-letters that could be made to these agreements before the celebration of the marriage must be recorded by deed executed before a notary and the presence and simultaneous consent of all persons who were parties thereto.

###### Article 1639

The notary shall issue to the parties, at the time of signing the contract, a certificate on plain paper and free of charge, stating his or her names and place of residence, the names, first names, capacities and residences of the future spouses, as well as the date of the contract. This certificate indicates that it must be given to the civil registrar before the celebration of the marriage, which the notary also reminds the future spouses of orally.
In case of changes made to the initial deed, the notary shall draft them following the original of the marriage contract; the notary may not issue either engrossments or copies of the marriage contract without transcribing following them the changes or counter-letters that may have been made to it. In the absence of compliance with these formalities, the changes or counter-letters shall have no effect with regard to third parties.

###### Article 1640

A minor capable of contracting marriage may consent to all the agreements of which this contract is susceptible; and the agreements and donations that he or she has made therein are valid, provided that he or she has been assisted, in the contract, by the persons whose consent is necessary for the validity of the marriage.
An adult under guardianship or curatorship may enter into matrimonial agreements if he or she is assisted, in the contract, by his or her guardian or curator.
If matrimonial agreements have been entered into without this assistance, annulment may be requested by the incapable person or by the persons whose consent was required, but only for one year from the marriage.

###### Article 1641

Once the marriage has been celebrated, no change may be made to the matrimonial regime except by effect of a judgment:

1° When one of the spouses requests judicial separation of property by reason of disorder in the affairs or misconduct of the spouse endangering his or her interests;
2° When partial and temporary modifications to the rules setting the powers of the spouses are granted by the judge, such as when the other spouse is unable to express his or her will and judicial authorization to act without the consent of the other spouse is granted (

###### article 225

of this code), or when judicial authorization to represent the other spouse has been decided (

###### article 227

of this code), or in the case of transfer of powers over ordinary or reserved community property (

###### article 1671

of this code), or transfer of powers over separate property (

###### article 1674 of this code)

3° By effect of a notarial deed, if necessary approved by the judge, in the case of article 1642.

###### Article 1642

After two years of application of the matrimonial regime, the spouses may agree, in the interest of the family, to modify it, or even to change it entirely, by a notarial deed. Mention of the modification is made on the original of the modified marriage contract and, on pain of nullity, the notarial deed contains the liquidation of the modified matrimonial regime if it is necessary.
The persons who had been parties to the modified contract and the adult children of each spouse are personally informed of the proposed modification; the creditors of the spouses are informed of it by publication of a notice in a newspaper authorized to receive legal announcements. Each of them may object to the modification within a period of three months.

In case of objection, the notarial deed is submitted to the approval of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of the domicile of the spouses. It is compulsorily so when one or the other of the spouses has minor children. The application and the decision of approval are published.

Non-objecting creditors, if fraud has been committed against their rights, may challenge the change of matrimonial regime to have this deed declared unenforceable against them, subject to establishing, if it is an onerous transaction, that the third party co-contractor had knowledge of the fraud. They must specify how the contested fraudulent acts are related to the change of matrimonial regime, which is not in itself indicative of fraud

###### Article 1643

The change of matrimonial regime takes effect between the parties on the date of the deed or judgment providing for it and, with regard to third parties, three months after mention has been made of it in the margin of the marriage certificate. However, even in the absence of this mention, the change is nonetheless enforceable against third parties if, in deeds entered into with them, the spouses have declared that they have modified their matrimonial regime.
When one or the other of the spouses is subject to a legal protection measure under the conditions provided for in Title XII of Book I of this code, the change or modification of the matrimonial regime is subject to prior authorization from the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or the family council if one has been constituted.

By exception, agreements entered into by spouses in divorce proceedings with a view to liquidating their matrimonial regime fall under the provisions provided for by this code specific to the divorce proceedings initiated.

###### Article 1644

When a change to the matrimonial regime occurs by application of a foreign law governing the effects of the union, the spouses inform the persons who had been parties to the marriage contract and each of their adult children and proceed, if necessary, with land registration. They have mention made of it in the margin of the marriage certificate.

###### Article 1645

The change of matrimonial regime takes effect between the parties from the date of the decision or deed providing for it and, with regard to third parties, three months after the publicity formalities provided for in article 1644 have been completed.

However, in the absence of completion of these formalities, the change of matrimonial regime is enforceable against third parties if, in deeds entered into with them, the spouses have declared that they have modified their matrimonial regime.

#### Chapitre II : Du régime en communauté Article 1646

Community, whether legal or conventional, begins on the day of the marriage contracted before the civil registrar: one cannot stipulate that it will begin at another time.

##### Section I : De la communauté légale Article 1647

The community that is established in the absence of a contract, or by the simple declaration that one is marrying under the community regime, is subject to the rules explained in the subsections that follow.

###### Sous-section 1 : De ce qui compose la communauté activement et passivement

###### § 1. De l'actif de la communauté Article 1648

The community is composed on the asset side of acquisitions made by the spouses together or separately during the marriage, and arising both from their personal industry and from savings made on the fruits and income of their separate property.

###### Article 1649

Any property, movable or immovable, is presumed to be a community acquisition if it is not proved that it is separate property of one of the spouses by application of a provision of the law. If the property is of those that do not bear in themselves proof or mark of their origin, the personal ownership of the spouse, if contested, must be established in writing. In the absence of an inventory or other pre-constituted proof, the judge may take into consideration all writings, including family titles, registers and domestic papers, as well as bank documents and invoices. He or she may even admit proof by testimony or presumption, if he or she finds that a spouse was in a material or moral impossibility to obtain a writing.

###### Article 1650

Each spouse retains full ownership of his or her separate property. The community is entitled only to fruits received and not consumed. But compensation may be due to it, upon dissolution of the community, for fruits that the spouse has neglected to receive or has fraudulently consumed, without any inquiry, however, being admissible beyond the last five years.

###### Article 1651

Property that is separate by nature, even if acquired during the marriage, includes clothing and linen for the personal use of one of the spouses, actions for compensation for bodily or moral injury, inalienable claims and pensions, and, more generally, all property that has a personal character and all rights exclusively attached to the person. Also separate by nature, but subject to compensation if applicable, are the work instruments necessary for the profession of one of the spouses, unless they are an accessory to a business or an operation forming part of the community.

###### Article 1652

Property of which the spouses had ownership or possession on the day of the celebration of the marriage, or which they acquire during the marriage by succession, donation or legacy, remains separate. The liberality may stipulate that the property that is the subject thereof shall belong to the community. Property falls into the community, unless otherwise stipulated, when the liberality is made to both spouses jointly. Property abandoned or transferred by father, mother or other ascendant to one of the spouses, either to fulfill what is owed to him or her, or subject to paying the donor's debts to third parties, remains separate, subject to compensation.

###### Article 1653

Property acquired as accessories to separate property as well as new securities and other increases relating to separate movable securities form separate property, subject to compensation if applicable. Also separate property, by the effect of real subrogation, are claims and indemnities that replace separate property, as well as property acquired by employment or reinvestment, in accordance with articles 1678 and 1679.

###### Article 1654

Property acquired in exchange for property that belonged separately to one of the spouses is itself separate, subject to compensation due to or by the community, if there is a balancing payment. However, if the balancing payment charged to the community exceeds the value of the property transferred, the property acquired in exchange falls into the common mass, subject to compensation in favor of the transferor.

###### Article 1655

The acquisition made, by auction or otherwise, of a portion of property of which one of the spouses was an undivided owner, does not form an acquisition, subject to compensation due to the community for the sum it may have provided.

###### § 2.Du passif de la communauté Article 1656

The community is composed on the liability side:
-	definitively, of maintenance owed by the spouses and debts contracted by them for the upkeep of the household and the education of the children, in accordance with article 228;
-	definitively or subject to compensation, depending on the case, of other debts arising during the community.

###### Article 1657

Debts for which the spouses were liable on the day of the celebration of their marriage, or with which the successions and liberalities that fall to them during the marriage are burdened, remain personal to them, both in principal and in arrears or interest.

###### Article 1658

The creditors of one or the other spouse, in the case of article 1657, may pursue their payment only against the separate property and income of their debtor.
They may, nevertheless, also seize the property of the community when the movable property that belongs to their debtor on the day of the marriage or that has fallen to him or her by succession or liberality has been merged into the common patrimony and can no longer be identified according to the rules of article 1649.

###### Article 1659

Compensation is due to the community that has discharged the personal debt of a spouse.

###### Article 1660

Payment of debts for which each spouse is liable, for whatever cause, during the community, may always be pursued against the common property, unless there has been fraud by the debtor spouse and bad faith by the creditor, subject to compensation due to the community if applicable.

###### Article 1661

The earnings and wages of a spouse may be seized by the creditors of his or her spouse only if the obligation was contracted for the upkeep of the household or the education of the children, in accordance with article 228.

###### Article 1662

Each of the spouses may only bind his or her separate property and income by a guarantee or a loan, unless these have been contracted with the express consent of the other spouse who, in that case, does not bind his or her separate property.

###### Article 1663

The community that has discharged a debt for which it could be pursued under the preceding articles is nevertheless entitled to compensation, whenever that commitment had been contracted in the personal interest of one of the spouses, such as for the acquisition, preservation or improvement of separate property.

###### Article 1664

The community is entitled to compensation, after deduction, where applicable, of the profit derived by it, when it has paid fines incurred by a spouse, by reason of criminal offenses, or the damages and costs to which he or she had been sentenced for civil delicts or quasi-delicts. It is likewise entitled to compensation if the debt it has discharged had been contracted by one of the spouses in disregard of the duties imposed on him or her by marriage.

###### Article 1665

When a debt has entered the community on behalf of only one of the spouses, it may not be pursued against the separate property of the other. If there is joint and several liability, the debt is deemed to enter the community on behalf of both spouses.

###### Sous-section 2 : De l'administration de la communauté et des biens propres Article 1666

Each of the spouses has the power to administer the common property alone and to dispose of it, subject to being liable for faults he or she may have committed in his or her management. Acts accomplished without fraud by one spouse are binding on the other. The spouse who exercises a separate profession alone has the power to accomplish the acts of administration and disposition necessary for it. All subject to articles 1667 to 1670.

###### Article 1667

The spouses may not, one without the other, dispose inter vivos, gratuitously, of community property. Nor may they, one without the other, assign one of these properties as security for the debt of a third party.

###### Article 1668

The legacy made by a spouse may not exceed his or her share in the community. If a spouse has bequeathed an item of the community, the legatee may claim it in kind only insofar as the item, by the event of the

partition, falls into the lot of the testator's heirs; if the item does not fall into the lot of these heirs, the legatee has compensation for the total value of the bequeathed item, against the share, in the community, of the heirs of the testator spouse and against the personal property of the latter.

###### Article 1669

The spouses may not, one without the other, alienate or encumber with real rights the immovable property, businesses and operations belonging to the community, nor the non-negotiable partnership rights and corporeal movables whose alienation is subject to publicity. They may not, without their spouse, collect the capital proceeds from such operations. Likewise, they may not, one without the other, transfer community property into a fiduciary patrimony.

###### Article 1670

The spouses may not, one without the other, lease a rural property or an immovable property for commercial, industrial or artisanal use belonging to the community. Other leases on common property may be entered into by one spouse alone and are subject to the rules provided for leases entered into by the usufructuary.

###### Article 1671

If one of the spouses finds himself or herself, in a lasting manner, unable to express his or her will, or if his or her management of the community demonstrates inaptitude or fraud, the other spouse may apply to the court to be substituted in the exercise of his or her powers. The provisions of Articles 1689 to 1692 are applicable to this application.
The spouse, thus authorized by the court, has the same powers as the spouse he or she replaces would have had; he or she performs with judicial authorization the acts for which his or her consent would have been required if there had been no substitution. The spouse deprived of his or her powers may, subsequently, apply to the court for their restitution, by establishing that their transfer to the other spouse is no longer justified.

###### Article 1672

If one of the spouses has exceeded his or her powers over the common property, the other, unless he or she has ratified the act, may apply for its annulment. The action for nullity is open to the spouse for two years from the day on which he or she became aware of the act, without ever being able to be brought more than two years after the dissolution of the community.

###### Article 1673

Each spouse has the administration and enjoyment of his or her separate property and may dispose of it freely.

###### Article 1674

If one of the spouses finds himself or herself, in a lasting manner, unable to express his or her will, or if he or she endangers the interests of the family, either by allowing his or her separate property to deteriorate, or by dissipating or misappropriating the income derived therefrom, he or she may, at the request of his or her spouse, be divested of the rights of administration and enjoyment recognized to him or her by Article 1673. The provisions of Articles 1689 to 1691 are applicable to this application.
Unless the appointment of a judicial administrator appears necessary, the judgment confers upon the applicant spouse the power to administer the separate property of the divested spouse, as well as to collect the fruits thereof, which must be applied by him or her to the charges of the marriage and the surplus used for the benefit of the community. From the date of the application, the divested spouse may dispose alone only of the bare ownership of his or her property. He or she may, subsequently, apply to the court to be restored to his or her rights, if he or she establishes that the causes which had justified the divestment no longer exist.

###### Article 1675

If, during the marriage, one of the spouses entrusts the other with the administration of his or her separate property, the rules of mandate are applicable. The mandatary spouse is, however, dispensed from accounting for the fruits, when the power of attorney does not expressly require it.

###### Article 1676

When one of the spouses takes in hand the management of the separate property of the other, with the knowledge of the latter, and nevertheless without opposition on his or her part, he or she is deemed to have received a tacit mandate, covering acts of administration and enjoyment, but not acts of disposition. This spouse is liable for his or her management towards the other as a mandatary. He or she is, however, accountable only for existing fruits; for those which he or she has neglected to collect or fraudulently consumed, he or she may be pursued only within the limit of the last five years.
If it is in defiance of a recorded opposition that one of the spouses has interfered in the management of the separate property of the other, he or she is liable for all the consequences of his or her interference and accountable without limitation for all the fruits which he or she has collected, neglected to collect or consumed.

###### Article 1677

The community owes compensation to the owner spouse whenever it has derived benefit from separate property. This is the case, in particular, when it has received separate funds or funds from the sale of separate property, without employment or reinvestment having been made.
If a dispute is raised, proof that the community has derived benefit from separate property may be administered by all means, even by testimony and presumptions.

###### Article 1678

Employment or reinvestment is deemed made with regard to a spouse whenever, at the time of an acquisition, he or she has declared that it was made with separate funds or funds from the alienation of separate property, and to serve as employment or reinvestment for him or her. In the absence of this declaration in the act, employment or reinvestment takes place only by agreement of the spouses, and it produces its effects only in their mutual relations.

###### Article 1679

If employment or reinvestment is made by anticipation, the property acquired is separate, on the condition that the sums expected from the separate patrimony are paid to the community within five years from the date of the act.

###### Article 1680

When the price and costs of the acquisition exceed the sum for which employment or reinvestment has been made, the community is entitled to compensation for the excess.
If, however, the contribution of the community is greater than that of the acquiring spouse, the property acquired falls into the community, subject to the compensation due to the spouse.

###### Article 1681

Whenever a sum is taken from the community, either to discharge debts or charges personal to one of the spouses, such as the price or part of the price of property separate to him or her or the redemption of feudal services, or for the recovery, preservation or improvement of his or her personal property, and generally whenever one of the two spouses has derived a personal benefit from the property of the community, he or she owes compensation therefor.

###### Article 1682

If the father and mother have jointly endowed the common child without expressing the portion for which they intended to contribute, they are deemed to have endowed each for half, whether the dowry was provided or promised in property of the community, or whether it was provided in property personal to one of the two spouses. In the second case, the spouse whose personal property was constituted as dowry, has, against the property of the other, an

action for indemnity for half of said dowry, having regard to the value of the property given at the time of the endowment.

###### Article 1683

The dowry constituted to the common child, in property of the community, is chargeable to the community. It must be borne for half by each spouse, upon the dissolution of the community, unless one of them, in constituting it, has expressly declared that he or she would bear it for the whole or for a share greater than half.

###### Article 1684

The guarantee of the dowry is owed by any person who has constituted it; and its interest runs from the day of the marriage, even though there is a term for payment, if there is no stipulation to the contrary.

###### Sous-section 3 : De la dissolution de la communauté

###### § 1. Des causes de dissolution et de la séparation de biens Article 1685

The community is dissolved:
1° by the death of one of the spouses; 2° by declared absence;
3° by divorce;
4° by separation from bed and board; 5° by separation of property;
6° by change of matrimonial regime.

###### Article 1686

There can be no continuation of the community, notwithstanding any stipulations to the contrary.

The spouses may, either one, apply, if appropriate, that, in their mutual relations, the effect of the dissolution be carried back to the date when they ceased to cohabit and collaborate.

###### Article 1687

If, by the disorder of the affairs of a spouse, his or her bad administration or his or her misconduct, it appears that the maintenance of the community endangers the interests of the other spouse, the latter may pursue separation of property in court. Any separation, without the intervention of the judge, is null and void.

###### Article 1688

Separation of property, although pronounced by the court, is null if proceedings tending to liquidate the rights of the parties have not been commenced within three months of the judgment having become res judicata and if the final settlement has not occurred within one year of the opening of liquidation operations.
This period of one year may be extended by the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance ruling in summary proceedings.

###### Article 1689

The application and the judgment of separation of property must be published under the conditions and subject to the penalties provided for by the Code of Civil Procedure.
The judgment pronouncing the separation of property takes effect, as to its effects, from the day of the application.

Mention of the judgment shall be made in the margin of the marriage certificate as well as on the original of the marriage contract.

###### Article 1690

The creditors of a spouse may not request separation of property on his or her behalf.

###### Article 1691

When an action for separation of property has been initiated, creditors may summon the spouses by lawyer-to-lawyer notice to communicate to them the application and supporting documents. They may even intervene in the proceedings for the preservation of their rights.
If the separation was pronounced in fraud of their rights, they may challenge it by way of third-party opposition, under the conditions provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure.

###### Article 1692

The spouse who has obtained separation of property must contribute, in proportion to his or her means and those of his or her spouse, both to household expenses and to the costs of educating the children. He or she must bear these costs entirely if nothing remains to the other.

###### Article 1693

Separation of property pronounced by a court has the effect of placing the spouses under the regime of Articles 1739 and following. The court, in pronouncing the separation, may order that one spouse pay his or her contribution to his or her spouse, who shall henceforth assume alone with respect to third parties the settlement of all marriage charges.

###### Article 1694

Agreements entered into pursuant to Article 293 are suspended, as to their effects, until the divorce is pronounced; they may not be executed, even in relations between spouses, until the judgment has become res judicata. Either spouse may request that the divorce judgment modify the agreement if the consequences of the divorce fixed by that judgment call into question the basis of the liquidation and partition.

###### § 2. De la liquidation et du partage de la communauté Article 1695

Once the community is dissolved, each of the spouses takes back those properties that had not entered the community, if they exist in kind, or the properties that have been subrogated thereto. Liquidation of the common mass, assets and liabilities, must then take place.

###### Article 1696

An account is established in the name of each spouse of the compensation that the community owes him or her and the compensation that he or she owes to the community, according to the rules prescribed in the preceding sections.

###### Article 1697

Compensation is, in general, equal to the lesser of the two sums represented by the expenditure made and the profit remaining. It may not, however, be less than the expenditure made when the latter was necessary. It may not be less than the profit remaining when the borrowed value was used to acquire, preserve or improve a property that is found, on the day of liquidation of the community, in the borrowing estate. If the property acquired, preserved or improved was alienated before liquidation, the profit is valued on the day of alienation; if a new property has been subrogated to the alienated property, the profit is valued on that new property.

###### Article 1698

If, on balance, the account shows a balance in favor of the community, the spouse returns the amount to the common mass. If it shows a balance in favor of the spouse, the latter has the choice either to demand payment or to withdraw common properties up to the corresponding amount.

###### Article 1699

Withdrawals are made first from cash, then from movables, and subsidiarily from immovables of the community. The spouse making the withdrawal has the right to choose the movables and immovables that he or she will withdraw. He or she may not, however, prejudice by his or her choice the rights that his or her spouse may have to request maintenance of indivision or preferential attribution of certain properties. If the spouses wish to withdraw the same property, the matter is resolved, except for demonstration of abuse by the one who opposes the withdrawal of a particular property by the other, by drawing lots.

###### Article 1700

In case of insufficiency of the community, the withdrawals of each spouse are proportional to the amount of compensation owed to him or her. However, if the insufficiency of the community is attributable to the fault of one of the spouses, the other spouse may exercise his or her withdrawals before the former on all common properties; he or she may exercise them subsidiarily on the separate properties of the responsible spouse.

###### Article 1701

Compensation owed by the community or to the community bears interest by operation of law from the day of dissolution. However, when the compensation is equal to the profit remaining, interest runs from the day of liquidation.

###### Article 1702

Withdrawals in common properties constitute a partition operation. They do not confer on the spouse exercising them any right to be preferred over the creditors of the community.

###### Article 1703

After all withdrawals have been made from the mass, the surplus is divided in half between the spouses. If an immovable of the community is an annex to another immovable belonging separately to one of the spouses, or if it is contiguous to that immovable, the spouse owner has the option of having it attributed to him or her by imputation on his or her share or in exchange for an equalizing payment, according to the value of the property on the day the attribution is requested.

###### Article 1704

The partition of the community, with respect to all matters concerning its forms, the maintenance of indivision and preferential attribution, the sale by auction of properties, the effects of partition, the warranty and equalizing payments, is subject to all the rules that are established in the title On Successions for partitions among co-heirs.
However, for communities dissolved by divorce, legal separation or separation of property, preferential attribution is never by right, and it may always be decided that the totality of any equalizing payment due shall be payable in cash.

###### Article 1705

The spouse who has misappropriated or concealed any effects of the community is deprived of his or her share in said effects. Likewise, the one who has knowingly concealed the existence of a common debt must assume it definitively.

###### Article 1706

After partition is completed, if one of the two spouses is a personal creditor of the other, as when the price of his or her property was used to pay a personal debt of his or her spouse, or for any other cause, he or she exercises his or her claim on the share that has fallen to the latter in the community or on his or her personal properties.

###### Article 1707

Personal claims that spouses have to exercise against each other do not give rise to withdrawal and bear interest only from the day of formal demand.

Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, these personal claims that spouses have to exercise against each other are valued according to the rules of Article 1697, in the cases provided for therein; interest then runs from the day of liquidation.

###### Article 1708

Gifts that one of the spouses may have made to the other are executed only on the donor's share in the community and on his or her personal properties.

###### § 3

De l'obligation et de la contribution au passif après la dissolution Article 1709
Each of the spouses may be sued for the totality of debts existing, on the day of dissolution, that had entered the community on his or her behalf.

###### Article 1710

Each spouse may be sued only for half of the debts that had entered into the community on account of his or her spouse.
After partition and except in case of concealment, the spouse who is not personally bound is liable only up to the amount of his or her emolument, that is to say up to the amount of the active share of the community that he or she receives, provided that there has been an inventory, and subject to accounting for both the contents of that inventory and what has fallen to him or her by partition as well as the common liabilities already discharged.

###### Article 1711

The inventory provided for in Article 1710 must take place in the forms prescribed by the code of civil procedure, adversarially with the other spouse or with him or her duly summoned. It must be closed within nine months from the day on which the community was dissolved, except for an extension granted by the judge in summary proceedings. It must be affirmed sincere and true before the public officer who received it.

###### Article 1712

Each spouse contributes half to the community debts for which no compensation was due, as well as to the costs of sealing, inventory, sale of movables, liquidation, licitation and partition.
When the debt was definitively incumbent only on one of the spouses and the other spouse nevertheless contributed, the latter is entitled to corresponding compensation.

###### Article 1713

The spouse who may avail himself or herself of the benefit of Article 1710, second paragraph, does not contribute for more than the active share of the community that he or she receives, to the debts that had entered into the community on account of the other spouse, unless they are debts for which he or she would have owed compensation.

###### Article 1714

The spouse who has paid beyond the portion for which he or she was liable by application of the preceding articles has, against the other, recourse for the excess.

###### Article 1715

He or she has no claim, for that excess, against the creditor, unless the receipt expresses that he or she intends to pay only within the limit of his or her obligation.

###### Article 1716

The one of the two spouses who, by the effect of the mortgage exercised on the immovable fallen to him or her in partition, is sued for the totality of a community debt, has by right his or her recourse against the other for half of that debt.

###### Article 1717

The provisions of the preceding articles do not prevent a clause of the partition from obliging one or the other of the spouses to pay a quota of debts other than that which is fixed above, or even to discharge the liabilities entirely, without prejudice to the rights of third parties.

###### Article 1718

The heirs of the spouses exercise, in case of dissolution of the community, the same rights as the spouse whom they represent and are subject to the same obligations.

##### Section II : De la communauté conventionnelle Article 1719

The spouses may, in their marriage contract, modify the legal community by any kind of agreements not contrary to Articles 1633, 1635 and 1636.
They may, in particular, agree:
1° That the community shall include movables and acquests; 2° That the rules concerning administration shall be derogated from;
3° That one of the spouses shall have the power to withdraw certain property subject to compensation; 4° That one of the spouses shall have received sums or property outside the succession share;
5° That the spouses shall have unequal shares;
6° That there shall be universal community between them.

The rules of the legal community remain applicable in all points that have not been the subject of the agreement of the parties.

###### Sous-section 1 : De la communauté de meubles et acquêts Article 1720

When the spouses agree that there shall be between them community of movables and acquests, the common assets include, in addition to the property that would form part of it under the legal community regime, the movable property of which the spouses had ownership or possession on the day of marriage or which has fallen to them since by succession or liberality, unless the donor or testator has stipulated otherwise.

Nevertheless, those of these movable properties that would have formed separate property by their nature under Article 1651, under the legal regime, if they had been acquired during the community, remain separate.
If one of the spouses had acquired an immovable since the marriage contract, containing a stipulation of community of movables and acquests, and before the celebration of the marriage, the immovable acquired in that interval shall enter into the community, unless the acquisition was made in execution of some clause of the marriage contract, in which case it would be governed according to the agreement.

###### Article 1721

Enter into the common liabilities, under this regime, in addition to the debts that would form part of it under the legal regime, a fraction of those with which the spouses were already burdened when they married, or with which the successions and liberalities that fall to them during the marriage are charged.
The fraction of liabilities that the community must bear is proportional to the fraction of assets that it receives according to the rules of Article 1720, either in the patrimony of the spouse on the day of marriage, or in all the property that is the subject of the succession or liberality.

For the establishment of this proportion, the composition and value of the assets are proved in accordance with Article 1649.

###### Article 1722

The debts for which the community is liable in consideration of the property it receives are its definitive charge.

###### Article 1723

The distribution of liabilities prior to the marriage or burdening successions and liberalities may not prejudice creditors. They retain, in all cases, the right to seize the property that previously formed their security. They may even pursue their payment on the whole of the community when the movables of their debtor have been merged into the common patrimony and can no longer be identified according to the rules of Article 1649.

###### Sous-section 2 :De la clause d'administration conjointe Article 1724

The spouses may agree that they shall jointly administer the community.
In that case acts of administration and disposition of common property are made under the joint signature of both spouses. This double signature entails by operation of law joint and several liability for the obligations subscribed. Conservatory acts may be made separately by each spouse.

###### Sous-section 3 : De la clause de prélèvement moyennant indemnité Article 1725

The spouses may stipulate that the survivor of them or one of them if he or she survives, or even one of them in all cases of dissolution of the community, shall have the power to withdraw certain common property, subject to accounting for it to the community according to the value they shall have on the day of partition, if it has not been otherwise agreed.

###### Article 1726

The marriage contract may fix bases of valuation and terms of payment of the possible balancing payment. Taking into account these clauses and in the absence of agreement between the parties, the value of the property shall be fixed by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 1727

The power of withdrawal lapses if the beneficiary spouse has not exercised it by a notification made to the other spouse or to his or her heirs within a period of one month from the day on which they shall have put him or her on notice to take a position. This notice itself may not take place before the expiration of the time limits provided for in Article 906 for making an inventory and deliberating.

###### Article 1728

The withdrawal is a partition operation: the property withdrawn is charged against the share of the beneficiary spouse; if their value exceeds that share, there is occasion for the payment of a balancing payment.
The spouses may agree that the compensation due by the author of the withdrawal shall be charged subsidiarily against his or her rights in the succession of the predeceased spouse.

###### Sous-section 4

The attribution, to the spouse, of sums or property outside the succession share Article 1729
It may be agreed, in the marriage contract, that the survivor of the spouses, or one of them if he or she survives, shall be authorized to withdraw from the community, before any partition, either a certain sum, or certain property in kind, or a certain quantity of a specified type of property.

###### Article 1730

This attribution outside the succession share is not regarded as a donation, either as to substance or as to form, but as a marriage contract and between partners.

###### Article 1731

When the community is dissolved during the lifetime of the spouses, there is no place for the delivery of the sums and property whose attribution is provided for outside the succession share; but the spouse in whose favor it has been stipulated retains his or her rights in the event of survival, subject to Article 291.
He or she may require security from his or her spouse as a guarantee of his or her rights.

###### Article 1732

The creditors of the community always have the right to have the property included outside the succession share sold, subject to the spouse's recourse against the remainder of the community.

###### Sous-section 5: On the stipulation of unequal shares Article 1733

The spouses may derogate from the equal partition established by law.

###### Article 1734

When it has been stipulated that the spouse or his or her heirs shall have only a certain share in the community, such as one-third or one-quarter, the spouse thus reduced or his or her heirs bear the debts of the community only in proportion to the share they take in the assets.
The agreement is null if it obliges the spouse thus reduced or his or her heirs to bear a greater share, or if it exempts them from bearing a share in the debts equal to that which they take in the assets.

###### Article 1735

The attribution of the entire community may be agreed upon only in the event of survival, either in favor of a designated spouse, or in favor of whichever one survives. The spouse who thus retains the totality of the community is obliged to pay all the debts thereof.
It may also be agreed, in the event of survival, that one of the spouses shall have, in addition to his or her half, the usufruct of the share of the predeceased. In this case, he or she shall contribute to the debts, as to the usufruct, according to the rules of Articles 714 and following of this code.
The provisions of Article 1731 are applicable to these clauses when the community is dissolved during the lifetime of both spouses.

###### Article 1736

The stipulation of unequal shares and the clause of integral attribution are not deemed to constitute donations, either as to substance or as to form, but simply marriage contracts and between partners. Unless otherwise stipulated, they do not prevent the heirs of the predeceased spouse from recovering the contributions and capital that fell into the community from their predecessor.

###### Sous-section 6: On universal community

The spouses may establish by their marriage contract a universal community of their property, both movable and immovable, present and future. However, unless otherwise stipulated, the property that Article 1651 declares separate by its nature does not fall into this community.

The universal community definitively bears all the debts of the spouses, present and future.

##### Section III

Provisions common to the first two sections of Chapter II Article 1738
The advantages that either of the spouses may derive from the clauses of a conventional community, as well as those that may result from the merger of movable property or debts, are not regarded as constituting donations.

Nevertheless, in the event that there are children who are not issue of both spouses, any agreement that would have the consequence of giving to one of the spouses beyond the portion regulated by Article 1228, under the title Of Donations Inter Vivos and Testaments, shall be without effect for the entire excess; but the simple benefits resulting from common work and savings made from the respective incomes, although unequal, of the two spouses, are not considered as an advantage made to the prejudice of children of another marriage.

#### Chapter III: On the regime of separation of property Article 1739

When the spouses have stipulated in their marriage contract that they would be separated as to property, each of them retains the administration, enjoyment and free disposal of his or her personal property.

Each of them remains solely liable for debts arising in his or her person before or during the marriage, except in the case of Article 228.

###### Article 1740

The spouses contribute to the charges of the marriage according to the agreements contained in their contract; and, if none exist in this regard, in the proportion determined in Article 222.

###### Article 1741

Both with regard to his or her spouse and to third parties, a spouse may prove by all means that he or she has the exclusive ownership of property.
The presumptions of ownership stated in the marriage contract have effect with regard to third parties as well as in relations between spouses, unless otherwise agreed. Proof to the contrary shall be permitted, and it shall be made by all means proper to establish that the property does not belong to the spouse whom the presumption designates, or even, if it belongs to him or her, that he or she acquired it by a liberality from the other spouse.

Property over which neither of the spouses can establish exclusive ownership is deemed to belong to them jointly, to each for one-half.

###### Article 1742

If, during the marriage, one of the spouses entrusts to the other the administration of his or her personal property, the rules of mandate are applicable. The spouse acting as mandatory is, however, dispensed from accounting for the fruits, when the power of attorney does not expressly oblige him or her to do so.

When one of the spouses takes in hand the management of the property of the other, with the knowledge of the latter, and nevertheless without opposition on his or her part, he or she is deemed to have received a tacit mandate, covering acts of administration and management, but not acts of disposition.

This spouse is responsible for his or her management toward the other as a mandatory. He or she is, however, accountable only for existing fruits; for those that he or she has neglected to collect or fraudulently consumed, he or she may be pursued only within the limit of the last five years.

If it is in defiance of a recorded opposition that one of the spouses has interfered in the management of the property of the other, he or she is responsible for all the consequences of his or her interference, and accountable without limitation for all the fruits that he or she has collected, neglected to collect or consumed.

###### Article 1744

A spouse is not guarantor of the failure to invest or reinvest the property of the other, unless he or she has interfered in the operations of alienation or collection, or unless it is proved that the monies were received by him or her, or have turned to his or her profit.

###### Article 1745

After the dissolution of the marriage by the death of one of the spouses, the partition of undivided property between spouses separated as to property, with respect to all that concerns its forms, the maintenance of the indivision and the preferential attribution, the sale by auction of the property, the effects of the partition, the warranty and the balancing payments, is subject to all the rules that are established under the title Of Successions for partitions between co-heirs.
The same rules apply after divorce or legal separation. However, the preferential attribution is never of right. It may always be decided that the totality of any balancing payment due shall be payable in cash.

###### Article 1746

The rules of Article 1707 are applicable to claims that one of the spouses may have to exercise against the other.

#### Chapter IV: Of the participation in acquisitions regime Article 1747

When spouses have declared that they are marrying under the participation in acquisitions regime, each of them retains the administration, enjoyment and free disposal of their personal property, without distinguishing between that which belonged to them on the day of marriage or came to them since by succession or liberality and that which they acquired during the marriage for valuable consideration. During the marriage, this regime functions as if the spouses were married under the separation of property regime. Upon dissolution of the regime, each spouse has the right to participate for half in value in the net acquisitions found in the patrimony of the other, and measured by the double valuation of the original patrimony and the final patrimony.
