The lender may not take back the thing lent until after the agreed term, or, in the absence of such provision, until after it has served the purpose for which it was borrowed.

He is required to reimburse the sums expended by the borrower under the conditions of Article 2094, second paragraph.

###### Article 2099

Nevertheless, if, during the agreed period or before the borrower's need has ceased, there arises for the lender a pressing and unforeseen need for his thing, the judge may, depending on the circumstances, compel the borrower to return it to him without waiting.

###### Article 2100

When the thing lent has defects such that it risks causing harm to the person using it, the lender is liable as soon as he knew of the defects and did not warn the borrower.

#### Chapter II: Loan for consumption

##### Section I: Nature of the loan for consumption

###### Article 2101

The loan for consumption is a contract by which one of the parties delivers to the other a certain quantity of things that are consumed by use, on condition that the latter return as much of the same kind and quality.

###### Article 2102

By the effect of this loan, the borrower becomes the owner of the thing lent.

If it perishes, it is he who, independently of the cause of this event, suffers the loss, except for his recourse against the person by whose fault it occurred

###### Article 2103

One cannot give by way of loan for consumption things which, although of the same kind, differ as individuals, such as animals: then it is a loan for use.

###### Article 2104

The obligation resulting from a loan of money is always only for the sum stated in the contract.

If there has been an increase or decrease in currency before the time of payment, the debtor must return the sum lent, and must return only that sum in the currency having legal tender at the time of payment.

This rule does not apply if the loan was made in bullion or commodities, in which cases the debtor must always return the same quantity and quality, and must return only that regardless of the variation in value that may have affected the property.

##### Section II: Obligations of the lender Article 2105

In the loan for consumption, the lender is subject to the liability established by Article 2100 for the loan for use.

###### Article 2106

The lender cannot demand back the things lent before the agreed term.

###### Article 2107

If no term has been fixed for restitution, the judge may grant the borrower a period depending on the circumstances.

###### Article 2108

If it has only been agreed that the borrower would pay when he could, or when he had the means, the judge shall fix a term of payment for him depending on the circumstances.

##### Section III: Obligations of the borrower Article 2109

The borrower is required to return the things lent, in the same quantity and quality, and at the agreed term.
If he is unable to satisfy this on that date, he must pay the value:
-	on the day and at the place of repayment when the contract has provided the time and place of restitution;
-	on the day and at the place where the loan was made.

If the borrower does not return the things lent or their value at the agreed term and failing that, from the formal notice addressed to him, he owes interest from the day of the summons or the legal claim.

#### Chapter III: Loan at interest Article 2111

The stipulation of interest is authorized both for the loan of money, commodities, and other movable things.

###### Article 2112

If the borrower has paid interest when it was not stipulated, he cannot obtain reimbursement. Nor can he impute it to the principal.

###### Article 2113

Interest is legal or conventional. Legal interest is fixed by law. Conventional interest may exceed that of the law, whenever the law does not prohibit it.
The rate of conventional interest must be fixed in writing. Failing that, the loan is granted gratuitously and interest at the legal rate runs only from the formal notice to return the principal.

###### Article 2114

The receipt for the principal given without reservation of interest creates a presumption of payment and operates a discharge.

###### Article 2115

It may also be provided that, in consideration for making capital available, which the lender undertakes not to demand, the borrower undertakes to pay him periodically an annuity.
In this case, the loan takes the name of constitution of annuity.
It may also be constituted, on a purely gratuitous basis, by gift inter vivos or by will. It must then be clothed in the forms required by law.

###### Article 2116

This annuity may be constituted in two ways, in perpetuity or for life.

###### Article 2117

The annuity constituted in perpetuity is redeemable. This possibility of redemption is imprescriptible and implied in these kinds of contracts.
The parties may only agree that redemption shall not be made before a certain period. This period takes the form:
-	either of a waiting period, which shall be fixed by the parties for a maximum duration of ten years, from the loan;
-	or of a notice period, which the debtor must give to the creditor when he notifies him of his intention to redeem.

###### Article 2118

The debtor of an annuity constituted in perpetuity may be compelled to redeem: 1° If he ceases to fulfill his obligations for two years;
2° If he fails to provide the lender with the securities promised by the contract.

The principal of the annuity constituted in perpetuity also becomes due in case of bankruptcy of the debtor.

###### Article 2120

The rules concerning life annuities are established in the title on Aleatory Contracts.

### Title XIII: On Deposit

Chapter I: On the Two Types of Deposits Article 2121
Deposit is an act by which a person receives the property of another, with the obligation to keep it and to return it in kind.

###### Article 2122

There are two types of deposit: deposit properly so-called and sequestration.

#### Chapter II: On Deposit Properly So-Called

##### Section I: On the Nature and Essence of the Contract of Deposit Article 2123

Deposit properly so-called is an essentially gratuitous contract.

###### Article 2124

It may only have movable property as its object.

###### Article 2125

It is perfected only by the actual or constructive delivery of the thing deposited.
Constructive delivery suffices when the depositary is already in possession, under some other title, of the thing which one consents to leave with him as a deposit.

###### Article 2126

Deposit is voluntary or necessary.

##### Section II: On Voluntary Deposit Article 2127

Voluntary deposit is formed by the reciprocal consent of the person making the deposit and the person receiving it.
Voluntary deposit presupposes persons capable of contracting. Nevertheless, if a person capable of contracting accepts a deposit made by an incapable person, he is bound by all the obligations of a true depositary; he may be sued by the tutor or administrator of the person who made the deposit.

Conversely, if the deposit was made by a capable person to an incapable person, the person who made the deposit has only the action for revendication of the thing deposited, as long as it exists in the hands of the depositary, or the action for restitution up to the amount that has turned to the profit of the latter.

###### Article 2128

Voluntary deposit may only be validly made by the owner of the thing deposited, or with his express or tacit consent.

###### Article 2129

Voluntary deposit must be proved in writing. Proof by witness is not admissible when the value of the thing deposited exceeds 20,000 FD.

###### Article 2130

When the deposit, being above the amount provided for in the preceding article, is not proved in writing, the person who is sued as depositary is believed on his declaration, whether as to the fact of the deposit itself, or as to the thing which was its object, or as to the fact of its restitution.

##### Section III: On the Obligations of the Depositary Article 2131

The depositary must exercise, in the safekeeping of the thing deposited, the same care that he exercises in the safekeeping of things belonging to him.

This obligation must be applied more rigorously:
1° If the depositary offered himself to receive the deposit; 2° If he stipulated a salary for the safekeeping of the deposit;
3° If the deposit was made solely for the interest of the depositary;
4° If it was expressly agreed that the depositary would be liable for any kind of fault.

###### Article 2132

The depositary is not liable, in any case, for accidents of force majeure, unless he has been placed in default to return the thing deposited.

###### Article 2133

He may not use the thing deposited without the express or presumed permission of the depositor.

###### Article 2134

He must not seek to know what things have been deposited with him if they were entrusted to him in a closed container or under a sealed envelope.

###### Article 2135

When the thing deposited is a specific thing, the depositary must return the very thing he received. Otherwise, he must return a thing of the same kind, and identical in quantity and quality.

###### Article 2136

The depositary returns the thing deposited in the state in which it is at the moment of restitution. Deteriorations that did not occur through his act are at the expense of the depositor.

###### Article 2137

If the thing deposited comes to disappear as a result of a case of force majeure, the depositary who has received a price or something in its place must return what he has received in exchange.

###### Article 2138

The heir of the depositary, who has sold in good faith the thing of whose deposit he was unaware, is only bound to return the price he received, or to assign his action against the purchaser, if he has not received the price.

###### Article 2139

If the thing deposited has produced fruits that have been collected by the depositary, he is obliged to return them. He owes no interest on money deposited, except from the day on which he was placed in default to make restitution.

###### Article 2140

The depositary must return the thing deposited only to the person who entrusted it to him, or to the person in whose name the deposit was made, or to the person who was designated to receive it.

###### Article 2141

He may not require from the person who made the deposit proof that he was the owner of the thing deposited.

Nevertheless, if he discovers that the thing was stolen, and who the true owner is, he must notify the latter of the deposit that was made with him with summons to claim it within a determined and sufficient period. If the person to whom the notification was made neglects to claim the deposit, the depositary is validly discharged by returning it to the person from whom he received it.

###### Article 2142

In case of death of the person who made the deposit, the thing deposited may only be returned to his heir. If there are several heirs, it must be returned to each of them for their share and portion.
If the thing deposited is indivisible, the heirs must agree among themselves to receive it.

###### Article 2143

If the person who made the deposit has been divested of his powers of administration, for example when an adult depositor is struck by an incapacity, the deposit may only be returned to the person who has the administration of the property of the depositor.

###### Article 2144

If the deposit was made by a tutor or an administrator, in one of these capacities, it may only be returned to the person whom that tutor or that administrator represented, if their tutorship or their administration has ended.

###### Article 2145

If the contract of deposit designates the place in which restitution must be made, the depositary is bound to take the thing deposited there. If there are transportation costs, they are at the expense of the depositor.
If the contract does not designate the place of restitution, it must be made in the very place of the deposit.

###### Article 2146

The deposit must be returned to the depositor as soon as he claims it, even if the contract had fixed a determined period for restitution; unless there exists, in the hands of the depositary, a seizure or an opposition to the restitution and displacement of the thing deposited.

###### Article 2147

The depositary who misappropriates the thing entrusted to him or who, through his fault, cannot return the thing deposited must pay its value, at the choice of the depositor, either on the day of the deposit or on the day when the judge rules, without prejudice to damages that may be awarded.

###### Article 2148

All obligations of the depositary cease if he comes to discover and to prove that he is himself the owner of the thing deposited.

##### Section IV: On the Obligations of the Depositor Article 2149

The depositor must reimburse the depositary for the expenses he incurred for the preservation of the thing deposited, and indemnify him for all losses that the deposit may have occasioned him.

###### Article 2150

The depositary may retain the thing deposited until full payment of what is owed to him by reason of the deposit.

##### Section V: Necessary Deposit Article 2151

Necessary deposit results from the constraint suffered by a person, by reason of an unforeseen event, for example, a fire, a ruin, a pillage, or a shipwreck, to deposit their effects in the hands of a third party to ensure their safekeeping.

Except for special provisions, necessary deposit is governed by all the rules previously stated.

###### Article 2152

Proof by witnesses may be received for necessary deposit, even when it concerns a value exceeding the amount provided for in Article 2129.

###### Article 2153

Hotel deposit is assimilated to necessary deposit: innkeepers or hoteliers are liable, as depositaries, for clothing, luggage and various objects brought into their establishment by the traveler who lodges with them.
They are liable for theft or damage to the traveler's effects, whether the theft was committed or the damage was caused by their employees, or by third parties coming and going in the hotel or any establishment assimilated to a hotel.

When an object, whatever its nature or value, has been deposited in their hands or they have refused to receive it without legitimate reason, their liability in case of theft or deterioration is entire, notwithstanding any contrary clause. In all other cases, the damages owed to the traveler are, to the exclusion of any lower contractual limitation, limited to the equivalent of twenty times the rental price of the accommodation per day, except when the traveler demonstrates that the harm they suffered results from a fault of the person who accommodates them or persons for whom the latter must answer.

They are not, however, liable for thefts committed with armed force or other cases of force majeure.

#### Chapter III: Sequestration Article 2154

Sequestration is conventional or judicial.

##### Section I: Conventional Sequestration

###### Article 2155

Conventional sequestration is the deposit made by one or more persons, of a contentious thing, in the hands of a third party who undertakes to return it, after the dispute is terminated, to the person who is judged to be entitled to obtain it.

###### Article 2156

Sequestration may not be gratuitous.
When it is gratuitous, it is subject to the rules of deposit properly so-called, provided that:
1° Sequestration may have as its object, not only movable effects, but also immovables. 2° The depositary charged with sequestration cannot be discharged before the dispute is terminated, except with the consent of all interested parties, or for a cause judged legitimate such as a long absence or a failing state of health, and obtain, if applicable, the designation of a replacement.

##### Section II: Sequestration or "Judicial Deposit" Article 2157

Justice may order sequestration:
1° Of movables seized from a debtor;

2° Of an immovable or a movable thing whose ownership or possession is disputed between two or more persons;
3° Of things, according to what they owe, that a debtor offers for their release.

###### Article 2158

The establishment of a judicial guardian produces, between the seizing party and the guardian, reciprocal obligations:
1° The guardian must:
-	exercise, for the preservation of the seized effects, the care of a good father of a family;
-	produce said effects, either at the discharge of the seizing party for the sale, or to the party against whom the executions were made, in case of release of the seizure.
2° The seizing party must pay the guardian the salary determined by the judge.

###### Article 2159

Judicial sequestration is given, either to a person whom the interested parties have agreed upon among themselves, or to a person appointed ex officio by the judge.
In both cases, the person to whom the thing has been entrusted is subject to all the obligations entailed by conventional sequestration.

### Title XIV: Aleatory Contracts

Chapter I: Gaming and Wagering Article 2160
The law grants no action for a gaming debt or for the payment of a wager.

###### Article 2161

However, the loser can never recover what they have voluntarily paid, unless there has been, on the part of the winner, fraud, trickery or swindling.

#### Chapter II: Life Annuity Contract

##### Section I: Conditions Required for the Validity of the Contract Article 2162

An annuity is a claim whose object is a periodic income obtained by a person, called the annuitant, from another person, the debtor of the annuity; when it is for life, the annuity is paid throughout the life of its beneficiary.

###### Article 2163

The annuity may be constituted for valuable consideration, by means of a sum of money, or for an appreciable movable thing, or for an immovable.

###### Article 2164

It may also be constituted, as a purely gratuitous title, by gift inter vivos or by will. It must then be clothed with the forms required by law. Such is especially the case for annuities constituted by way of gift-partition.
When it is constituted as a purely gratuitous title, the annuity is reducible if it exceeds what one is permitted to dispose of; it is null if it is for the benefit of a person incapable of receiving.

###### Article 2165

The annuity may be constituted either on the head of the person who furnishes the price, or on the head of a third party, although the price of the annuity is furnished in that case by another person.
It may also be constituted on one or more heads.

###### Article 2166

When an annuity is constituted on the head of a third party, although it has the characteristics of a liberality, it is not subject to the forms required for gifts; except to be reduced if it exceeds what one is permitted to dispose of or to be annulled if it is made for the benefit of a person incapable of receiving.
In contracts for the constitution of life annuity, the clause by which the purchaser stipulates that after their death, the annuity will be continued to a third party during the life of the latter, is valid, although that third party did not intervene in the contract.

When, constituted by spouses or one of them, the annuity is stipulated reversible for the benefit of the surviving spouse, the reversibility clause may have the characteristics of a liberality or those of an act for valuable consideration. In the latter case, the compensation or indemnity owed by the beneficiary of the reversion to the community or to the succession of the predeceased is equal to the value of the reversion of the annuity. Except for contrary intent of the spouses, the reversion is presumed to have been granted gratuitously.

###### Article 2167

Any life annuity contract, created on the head of a person who was dead on the day of the contract, produces no effect.
The same applies to the contract by which the annuity was created on the head of a person suffering from the illness from which they died within twenty days of the date of the contract.

###### Article 2168

Life annuity may be constituted at the rate that the contracting parties are pleased to fix.

##### Section II: Effects of the Contract Between the Contracting Parties Article 2169

The person for whose benefit the life annuity has been constituted by means of a price may demand the rescission of the contract, if the debtor of the annuity does not give them the securities that may have been stipulated for its execution.

###### Article 2170

The mere failure to pay the arrears of the annuity does not authorize the person in whose favor it is constituted to demand the reimbursement of the capital, or to re-enter the property alienated by them: they have only the right to seize and have sold the property of their debtor and to have ordered or consented, on the proceeds of the sale, the use of a sum sufficient for the service of the arrears.

###### Article 2171

The debtor of the annuity cannot discharge himself from payment of the annuity by offering to reimburse the capital and renouncing recovery of arrears paid: he is bound to provide the annuity during the entire life of the person or persons upon whose life the annuity was constituted, whatever the duration of the life of those persons, and however onerous the provision of the annuity may have become.

###### Article 2172

The life annuity is acquired by the owner only in proportion to the number of days he has lived.

Nevertheless, if it has been agreed that it would be paid in advance, the term that was to be paid is acquired from the day when payment was to be made.

###### Article 2173

The life annuity may be stipulated unseizable only when it has been constituted gratuitously.

###### Article 2174

The holder of a life annuity may claim arrears thereof only by proving his existence, or that of the person upon whose life it was constituted.

### Titre XV: Of mandate

Chapitre Ier: Of the nature and form of mandate Article 2175
Mandate, or power of attorney, is an act by which a person called the principal gives to another, the agent, the power to do something for the principal and in his name.
The contract is formed only by acceptance of the agent.

###### Article 2176

Mandate may be given by authentic act or by private written instrument, even by letter. It may also be given verbally; but testimonial proof thereof is admissible only in accordance with the title Of obligations.
Acceptance of the mandate may be merely tacit, and result from the execution given to it by the agent.

###### Article 2177

Mandate is gratuitous, unless otherwise agreed.

###### Article 2178

It is special when it is given for one matter or certain matters only; it is general when it is given for all the affairs of the principal.
When it is general, the mandate permits only acts of administration.

If it concerns alienation or mortgaging, or any other act of ownership, the mandate must be express.

###### Article 2179

The agent may do nothing beyond what is contained in his mandate. The power to settle does not include the power to submit to arbitration.

###### Article 2180

In case of absence, exceeding or misuse of power by the agent, the rules of article 1274 are applicable.

###### Article 2181

An unemancipated minor may be chosen as agent; but the principal shall have action against him only according to the general rules relating to obligations of minors.

#### Chapitre II: Of the obligations of the agent Article 2182

The agent is bound to perform the mandate as long as he remains charged with it, and is liable for damages that may result from his non-performance.
He is likewise bound to complete the matter begun at the death of the principal, if there is peril in delay.

###### Article 2183

The agent is liable not only for fraud, but also for faults he commits in his management.

Nevertheless, liability relating to faults is applied less rigorously to one whose mandate is gratuitous than to one who receives remuneration.

###### Article 2184

Every agent is bound to render account of his management, and to account to the principal for all that he has received by virtue of his power of attorney, even in the case where what he has received is not due to the principal.

###### Article 2185

The agent is liable for the person he has substituted in the management:
1° when he has not received the power to substitute someone;
2° when that power has been conferred upon him without designation of a person, but the one he has chosen was notoriously incapable or insolvent.
In all cases, the principal may act directly against the person whom the agent has substituted.

###### Article 2186

When there are several holders of power or agents established by the same act, there is solidarity between them only insofar as it is expressed.

###### Article 2187

The agent owes interest on sums he has used for his own use from the date of that use; and on those for which he is debtor under his mission, from the day he is placed in default.

###### Article 2188

The agent who has given to the party with whom he contracts in that capacity sufficient knowledge of his powers is bound to no warranty for what has been done beyond, unless he has personally submitted thereto.

#### Chapitre III: Of the obligations of the principal Article 2189

The principal is bound to perform the engagements contracted by the agent, in accordance with the power given to him.

He is bound for what may have been done beyond, only insofar as he has ratified it expressly or tacitly.

###### Article 2190

The principal must reimburse to the agent the advances and expenses that the latter has made for the execution of the mandate, and pay him his remuneration when it has been promised.
If there is no fault attributable to the agent, the principal cannot dispense with making these reimbursements and payment, even in the case where the matter he hoped to conclude has not succeeded, nor have the amount of expenses and advances reduced on the pretext that they could have been less.

###### Article 2191

Unless otherwise agreed, the principal must also indemnify the agent for losses that the latter has suffered on the occasion of his management, without imprudence attributable to him.

###### Article 2192

Advances made by the agent bear interest against the principal, from the date of the established advances.
These interests are due by the principal from the day when the advances were made, and not from the day when they were established by judicial decision or from the day of the demand for payment.

###### Article 2193

When the agent has been appointed by several persons for a common matter, each of them is bound solidarily towards him for all the effects of the mandate.

#### Chapitre IV: Of the different ways in which mandate ends Article 2194

Mandate ends notably:
1° By revocation of the agent;
2° By renunciation by the latter of the mandate;
3° By death, guardianship of adults or bankruptcy, either of the principal or of the agent.

###### Article 2195

The principal may revoke his power of attorney when he sees fit and compel, if necessary, the agent to restore to him the instrument containing the power of attorney. This restitution must occur without delay, as soon as the agent is required to do so by the principal.

The appointment of a new agent for the same matter constitutes revocation of the first, from the day when it has been notified to the latter.

In all cases, from revocation, the rendering of accounts becomes immediately due.

###### Article 2196

Revocation notified to the agent alone is presumed unknown to third parties who have dealt in ignorance of that revocation, except for the principal to prove that, taking into account the circumstances, the third party should have had knowledge thereof.

###### Article 2197

The agent may renounce the mandate, by notifying the principal of his renunciation.

Nevertheless, if this renunciation prejudices the principal, he must be indemnified by the agent, unless the latter finds himself unable to continue the mandate without himself suffering considerable prejudice.

###### Article 2198

If the agent is unaware of the death of the principal or one of the other causes that terminate the mandate, what he has done in that ignorance is valid.

###### Article 2199

In the above cases, the engagements of the agent are performed with regard to third parties who are in good faith.

###### Article 2200

In case of death of the agent, his heirs must give notice thereof to the principal, and provide, in the meantime, for what the circumstances require for the interest of the latter.

### Title XVI: On certain patrimonies by appropriation

Chapter I: On the foundation Article 2201
A foundation results from an act by which a person irrevocably appropriates all or part of their property to a purpose of social utility having a lasting character.

The foundation may not have as its essential object the realization of a profit or the operation of an enterprise.

###### Article 2202

The property of the foundation constitutes either an autonomous patrimony distinct from that of the disposer and any other person, or the patrimony of a legal person.
In the first case, the foundation is governed by the provisions of this title relating to the trust of social utility, subject to the provisions of the law; in the second case, it is governed by the laws applicable to legal persons of its kind.

###### Article 2203

The foundation created by trust is established by donation or by will, according to the rules governing these acts.

###### Article 2204

Unless otherwise stipulated in the constitutive act of the foundation, the property which forms the initial patrimony of the foundation created by trust, or the property which is subrogated or added to it, must be preserved and allow the intended purpose to be achieved either by the distribution of the income alone which derives from it, or by a use which does not substantially modify the consistency of the patrimony.

#### Chapter II: On the trust

##### Section I: On the nature of the trust and its constitution

###### § 1. On the nature of the trust Article 2205

A trust results from an act by which one or more persons, called the settlor, transfer from their patrimony property, rights or security interests, or a set of property, rights or security interests, present or future, to one or more patrimonies which they constitute for a determined purpose for the benefit of one or more beneficiaries, and which a trustee undertakes, by the fact of their acceptance, to hold and administer.

###### Article 2206

The trust patrimony, formed of the property referred to in the preceding article and transferred in trust, constitutes an autonomous patrimony by appropriation distinct from that of the settlor, the trustee or the beneficiary, over which none of them has a real right. In particular, the opening of a judicial reorganization or liquidation proceeding, personal bankruptcy and fraudulent bankruptcy, or an equivalent proceeding abroad concerning the trustee does not affect the trust patrimony.
Without prejudice to the rights of the settlor's creditors holding a right of pursuit attached to a security interest published prior to the trust contract and except in cases of fraud against the rights of the settlor's creditors, the trust patrimony may only be seized by holders of claims arising from the preservation or management of that patrimony.
In case of insufficiency of the trust patrimony, the obligation for trust liabilities is limited to the trust patrimony alone.

###### Article 2207

A trust is established by contract, for consideration or gratuitously, by will or by law. It may also, when the law authorizes it, be established by judgment.

###### Article 2208

A trust is constituted upon acceptance by the trustee or, if there are several, by one of them. The settlor may revoke the trust contract as long as it has not been accepted by the beneficiary; after acceptance by the beneficiary, the contract may only be modified or revoked with their consent or by court decision.
When the trust is established by will, the effects of acceptance retroact to the day of death.

###### Article 2209

Acceptance of the trust divests the settlor of the property, charges the trustee with ensuring their appropriation and the administration of the trust patrimony, and makes certain the right of the beneficiary.

###### § 2. On the trust contract

###### Article 2210

The trust contract determines, on pain of nullity:
1° The property, rights or security interests transferred. If they are future, they must be determinable;
2° The duration of the transfer, which may not exceed ninety-nine years from the signing of the contract;
3° The identity of the settlor or settlors; 4° The identity of the trustee or trustees;
5° The identity of the beneficiary or beneficiaries or, failing that, the principles or rules allowing their designation; 6° The mission of the trustee or trustees and the extent of their powers of administration and disposition.
The trust contract also defines the conditions under which the trustee accounts for their mission to the settlor. However, when during the execution of the contract the settlor becomes subject to a guardianship measure, the trustee, as soon as they are informed, accounts for their mission to the guardian at the latter's request at least once a year, without prejudice to the periodicity fixed by the contract. When during the execution of the contract the settlor becomes subject to a curatorship measure, the trustee accounts for their mission, under the same conditions, to the settlor and their curator.

###### Article 2211

When the trust contract provides that the settlor retains the use or enjoyment of a business or professional real property transferred into the trust patrimony, the agreement concluded for this purpose is not subject to chapters 2 and 4 of title I of book II of the commercial code, unless otherwise stipulated.

###### Article 2212

The assignment of claims carried out within the framework of a trust is enforceable against third parties on the date of the trust contract or the amendment recording it. It only becomes enforceable against the debtor of the assigned claim by notification made to them by the assignor or the trustee.

###### Article 2213

On pain of nullity, the trust contract and its amendments are registered in a public register, within one month from their date, with the register of real property security interests.
When they relate to real property or real property rights, they are also published in the Land Register. The trustee is, in case of default by the settlor, subject to the rules relating to the exercise of mortgage rights as set forth by this code.

The transmission of rights resulting from the trust contract and, if the beneficiary is not designated in the trust contract, their subsequent designation must, on pain of nullity, give rise to a written act registered under the same conditions.

###### Article 2214

A national register of trusts is constituted and maintained by the Central Bank of Djibouti.

##### Section II: On the various kinds of trust Article 2215

Trusts are constituted for personal purposes, or for purposes of private or social utility.
They may, to the extent that a mention indicates that it is a trust, be identified under the name of the disposer, the trustee or the beneficiary or, if they are constituted for purposes of private or social utility, under a name which designates their object.

###### Article 2216

A personal trust is constituted gratuitously, for the purpose of procuring an advantage to a determined person or one who may be determined.

###### Article 2217

A trust of private utility is one which has as its object the construction, maintenance or preservation of corporeal property, or the use of property appropriated to a determined use, either for the indirect advantage of a person or in their memory, or for another purpose of a private nature.

###### Article 2218

Also of private utility is a trust constituted for consideration for the purpose, in particular, of allowing the realization of a profit by means of placements or investments, of providing for a retirement or of procuring another advantage to the settlor or to the persons they designate, to members of a company or an association, to employees or to security holders.

###### Article 2219

A fiducie established by contract for valuable consideration may also have as its object to guarantee the performance of an obligation.

###### Article 2220

A fiducie for social utility is one that is established for a purpose of general interest, in particular of a cultural, educational, philanthropic, religious or scientific nature.
Its essential object is not to make a profit or to operate a business.

###### Article 2221

A personal fiducie established for the benefit of several persons successively may not comprise more than two orders of beneficiaries of the fruits and income, in addition to that of the beneficiary of the capital.
Accretions, between the co-beneficiaries of the fruits and income of the same order.

###### Article 2222

The right of the beneficiary of the first order opens at the latest upon the expiration of ninety-nine years following the establishment of the fiducie, even if a longer term has been stipulated. That of the beneficiaries of subsequent orders may open subsequently, but only for the benefit of beneficiaries who have the required qualification to receive upon the expiration of ninety-nine years following the establishment of the fiducie.
Legal persons may never be beneficiaries for a period exceeding ninety-nine years, even if a longer term has been stipulated.

###### Article 2223

A fiducie for private or social utility may be perpetual.

##### Section III : De l'administration de la fiducie

###### § 1. De la désignation et de la charge du fiduciaire Article 2224

Only banking or financial institutions, investment firms, and insurance companies may have the capacity of fiduciaries. Members of the legal profession may also have the capacity of fiduciary.

The settlor or the beneficiary may be a fiduciary, but must act jointly with a fiduciary who is neither settlor nor beneficiary.

###### Article 2225

The settlor may designate one or more fiduciaries or provide for the method of their designation or replacement.
In the absence of contractual stipulations providing for the conditions of replacement or if it is impossible to provide for the replacement of a fiduciary, the court may, at the request of an interested party and after notice given to the persons it indicates, proceed with the replacement. It may also, when the conditions of administration so require, designate one or more other fiduciaries.
When the fiduciary fails in its duties or endangers the interests entrusted to it, or if it is subject to safeguard or judicial reorganization proceedings, the settlor, the beneficiary or the third party designated pursuant to Article 2234 may apply to the court for the appointment of a provisional fiduciary or request the replacement of the fiduciary. The judicial decision granting the application automatically divests the original fiduciary and vests its replacement.

###### Article 2226

The fiduciary has complete and exclusive control and administration of the fiduciary patrimony and the titles relating to the property composing it are established in its name; it exercises all rights pertaining to the patrimony and may take any measure appropriate to ensure its allocation.
When the fiduciary acts on behalf of the fiducie, it must expressly mention this.

In its relations with third parties, the fiduciary is deemed to have the most extensive powers over the fiduciary patrimony, unless it is demonstrated that the third parties were aware of any limitations affecting its powers.

###### § 2. Du bénéficiaire et de ses droits Article 2227

The settlor or the fiduciary may be the beneficiary or one of the beneficiaries of the fiducie contract.

###### Article 2228

The beneficiary of a fiducie established gratuitously must have the qualifications required to receive by donation or by will at the opening of its right.
The beneficiary of a fiducie must, in order to receive, fulfill the conditions required by the constitutive instrument.

###### Article 2229

The settlor may reserve the right to receive the fruits and income or, as the case may be, the capital of a fiducie, even established gratuitously, or to participate in the advantages it provides.

###### Article 2230

The settlor may reserve or confer upon the fiduciary or a third party the power to elect the beneficiaries or to determine their share.
In the case of a fiducie for social utility, the power of the fiduciary to elect the beneficiaries and determine their share is presumed. In the case of a personal fiducie or a fiducie for private utility, the power to elect may only be exercised by the fiduciary or the third party if the category of persons from among whom they must choose the beneficiary is clearly determined in the constitutive instrument.

The person who has the power to elect the beneficiaries or to determine their share exercises it as they see fit; they may modify or revoke their decision for the needs of the fiducie. The person who exercises the power may not do so for their own benefit.

###### Article 2231

During the duration of the fiducie, the beneficiary has the right to require:
1° According to the periodicity fixed by the contract, the account by the fiduciary of its mission. The third party designated pursuant to Article 2234 has the same power.
2° According to the constitutive instrument, either the provision of an advantage granted to them, or the payment of the fruits and income and of the capital or of only one of them.

###### Article 2232

The beneficiary of a fiducie established gratuitously is presumed to have accepted the right granted to them and may dispose of it.
They may also renounce it at any time. The renunciation must be made by notarial act if they are the beneficiary of a personal fiducie or a fiducie for private utility.

###### Article 2233

In the case of a plurality of beneficiaries, when one of them renounces their right or the latter becomes without effect, that right passes, in proportion to the shares of each, to the co-beneficiaries of the fruits and income or of the capital, according to whether they themselves are beneficiaries of the fruits and income or of the capital.
If they are the sole beneficiary of the fruits and income in their order, the right of the renouncing party passes, in proportion to the shares of each, to the beneficiaries of the fruits and income of the second order or, failing that, to the beneficiaries of the capital.

###### § 3. Des mesures de surveillance et de contrôle Article 2234

Unless otherwise stipulated in the fiducie contract, the settlor may, at any time, designate a third party responsible for ensuring the preservation of their interests in the context of the performance of the contract and who may have the powers that the law grants to the settlor.

When the settlor is a natural person, they may not renounce this power.

###### Article 2235

The administration of the fiducie is subject to the supervision of the settlor or their heirs, if deceased, and of the beneficiary, even if contingent. It is also subject to the supervision of the third party designated by the settlor pursuant to Article 2234.
In addition, in the cases provided for by law, the administration of fiducies for private or social utility is subject, according to their object and purpose, to the supervision of the persons and bodies designated by law.

###### Article 2236

Upon the establishment of a fiducie for private or social utility subject to the supervision of a person or body designated by law, the fiduciary must file with the person or body a declaration indicating, in particular, the nature and object of the fiducie, its duration, as well as the name and address of the fiduciary.
It must, at the request of the person or body, permit the examination of the fiducie files and provide any account, report or information requested of it.

###### Article 2237

The rights of the beneficiary of a personal trust are exercised, if he is not yet conceived, by the person who, having been designated by the settlor to act as curator, accepts that office or, failing that, by the person appointed by the court at the request of the trustee or any interested person.

In the case of a trust for private purposes of which no person, even determinable or contingent, may be a beneficiary, the rights that this paragraph grants to the beneficiary may be exercised by the public prosecutor.

###### Article 2238

The settlor, the beneficiary or another interested person may, notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, bring action against the trustee to compel him to perform his obligations or to do an act necessary for the trust, to enjoin him from any act detrimental to the trust or to obtain his removal.
He may also challenge acts done by the trustee in fraud of the trust patrimony or of the rights of the beneficiary.

###### Article 2239

The court may authorize the settlor, the beneficiary or another interested person to bring legal action in place of the trustee, when the latter, without sufficient reason, refuses to act, neglects to do so or is prevented from doing so.

###### Article 2240

The trustee, the settlor and the beneficiary are, if they participate therein, solidarily liable for acts performed in fraud of the rights of the creditors of the settlor or of the trust patrimony.

##### Section IV: Modification and termination of the trust

###### § 1. Modification of the trust Article 2241

Any person may increase the trust patrimony by transferring property to it by contract or by
will and by following, for such increases, the rules specific to the constitution of a trust. He does not thereby acquire the rights of a settlor.
The property transferred is merged into the trust patrimony and is administered in accordance with the provisions of the constitutive instrument and those of this chapter.

###### Article 2242

When a trust has ceased to correspond to the original intention of the settlor, in particular when the court finds the occurrence of unforeseeable circumstances which make the pursuit of the purpose of the trust too onerous or the impossibility of achieving that purpose, that court may, at the request of an interested person, terminate the trust.
If the trust still corresponds to the intention of the settlor, but new measures would better respect his intention or would facilitate the accomplishment of the trust, the court may modify the provisions of the constitutive instrument.

In all the situations referred to in the preceding paragraphs, notice of the application must be given to the settlor and to the trustee and, as the case may be, to the beneficiary, to the liquidator of the succession of the settlor or to the heirs, and to any other person or body designated by law whenever the trust is subject to their supervision. Those persons must be heard by the court if they so request.

###### § 2. Termination of the trust

###### Article 2243

A trust terminates by:
1° the lapse of the right of all the beneficiaries, both of the capital and of the fruits and revenues;
2° the renunciation by all of the beneficiaries of the trust, except stipulations of the contract providing the conditions under which it continues;
3° the arrival of the term or the occurrence of the condition if one is provided;
4° the fact that the purpose of the trust has been achieved or by the impossibility found by the court of achieving it.

###### Article 2244

The trustee must, at the termination of the trust, deliver the property to those who are entitled to it.

In the absence of a beneficiary, the property remaining at the termination of the trust devolves by operation of law to the settlor or to his heirs.

###### Article 2245

The property of a trust for social purposes which terminates by reason of the impossibility of accomplishing it returns to the settlor. If he is deceased, that property devolves to a trust, to a legal person or to any other group of persons having a purpose approximating as closely as possible that of the trust. The designation thereof is made by the court, on the recommendation of the trustee. The court also takes the opinion of the person or body designated by law, if the trust was subject to their supervision.

### Title XVII: Transactions

###### Article 2246

A transaction is a contract by which the parties, by reciprocal concessions, terminate a dispute that has arisen, or prevent a dispute from arising.
This contract must be drawn up in writing.

###### Article 2247

To enter into a transaction, one must have the capacity to dispose of the objects included in the transaction.

The tutor may not enter into a transaction for the minor or the major under tutorship except in accordance with article 604 of the title On minority, tutorship and emancipation; and he may not enter into a transaction with the minor who has become of age, on the tutorship account, except in accordance with article 609 of the same title.

Communes and public establishments may not enter into transactions except with the express authorization of the President of the Republic.

###### Article 2248

One may enter into a transaction on the civil interest arising from an offence.
The transaction does not prevent prosecution by the public prosecutor.

###### Article 2249

One may add to a transaction the stipulation of a penal clause against the person who fails to perform it.

###### Article 2250

Transactions are confined to their object: the renunciation made therein of all rights, actions and claims is understood only as relating to the dispute which gave rise to it.

###### Article 2251

Transactions settle only the disputes included therein, whether the parties have manifested their intention by special or general expressions, or whether that intention is recognized by a necessary consequence of what is expressed.

###### Article 2252

If a person who had entered into a transaction on a right which he had in his own capacity, and has thus abandoned it in part, subsequently acquires a similar right in the capacity of another person, he is not, as to the newly acquired right, bound by the prior transaction.

###### Article 2253

A transaction made by one of the interested persons does not bind the other interested persons and may not be invoked by them.

###### Article 2254

A transaction bars the institution or continuation between the parties of a legal action having the same object. The judge may raise of his own motion this ground of inadmissibility arising from the existence of a transaction.
A transaction may not be challenged on the ground of error of law, nor on the ground of lesion.

###### Article 2255

Nevertheless, a transaction may be annulled when there is error as to the person or as to the object of the dispute.
It may be annulled in all cases where there is fraud or duress.

###### Article 2256

There is also ground for an action for annulment against a transaction when it was made in execution of a void title, unless the parties, when they have the power to do so, have expressly confirmed the cause of nullity.

###### Article 2257

A transaction made on documents which have since been recognized as false is entirely void.

###### Article 2258

A transaction on a lawsuit terminated by a judgment having acquired the force of res judicata, of which the parties or one of them had no knowledge, is void.
If the judgment unknown to the parties was susceptible of appeal, the transaction is valid.

###### Article 2259

When the parties have settled generally all matters they could have between them, documents that were then unknown to them and that were subsequently discovered are not grounds for annulment, unless they were withheld by the act of one of the parties.
However, the settlement would be null if it had only one subject matter on which it would be established, by newly discovered documents, that one of the parties had no right.

###### Article 2260

Calculation errors in a settlement must be corrected.

### Titre XVIII: Arbitration

###### Article 2261

Arbitration is governed by the provisions of articles L.710-1 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure.

### Titre XIX: Securities

###### Article 2262

Whoever has personally obligated himself is bound to fulfill his commitment on all his movable and immovable property, present and future.

###### Article 2263

The debtor's property may be seized even if it is held by third parties. Seizure is carried out according to the rules specific to the nature of each of them.

###### Article 2264

Property referred to in articles L.511-4 to L.511-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot be seized.

Furthermore, any individual entrepreneur who is a natural person may render unseizable the rights he holds over the immovable property forming his principal residence, to protect his family home from a failure of his business. The unseiability is effected by a declaration before a notary which, to be enforceable against third parties, must be published in a journal authorized to receive legal publications.

###### Article 2265

Seized property is unavailable.

Leases granted by the person whose property is seized are, whatever their duration, unenforceable against pursuing creditors. The same rules apply to property seized, mortgaged or pledged on a conservatory basis.

###### Article 2266

The debtor's property is the common pledge of his creditors; and the proceeds are distributed among them by contribution, unless there are legitimate causes of preference among the creditors.

###### Article 2267

With regard to real securities, the legitimate causes of preference are privileges and mortgages.
Sous-Titre I: Personal Securities Chapitre I: Suretyship

##### Section I: Nature and Extent of Suretyship

###### Article 2268

Civil suretyship is a contract by which the surety undertakes towards the creditor to perform the debtor's obligation if the debtor does not satisfy it himself.

###### Article 2269

Suretyship can only exist on a valid obligation.

However, it is possible to guarantee, with full knowledge, an obligation, even though it could be annulled by an exception purely personal to the obligor; for example, the commitments of an incapable person. The confirmation by the debtor of an obligation tainted with relative nullity does not, however, bind the surety, except express waiver by the surety of this nullity.
The lack of authority of the representative to bind the legal person who is the principal debtor may be invoked by the surety of that person under the conditions provided in the preceding paragraph.

###### Article 2270

The surety's commitment cannot be contracted under more onerous conditions than the principal obligation, nor exceed what is owed by the debtor at the time of proceedings.
The principal debtor cannot aggravate the surety's commitment by an agreement subsequent to the suretyship.
Suretyship that exceeds the debt, or that is contracted under more onerous conditions, is not null; it is reduced to the extent of the principal obligation.
The surety's commitment may be contracted for only part of the debt, and under less onerous conditions.

###### Article 2271

A suretyship may be contracted without the debtor's instruction and even without his knowledge.

One may also become surety, not only for the principal debtor, but also for the person who has guaranteed him.

###### Article 2272

Suretyship is not presumed, whatever the nature of the guaranteed obligation.

It must be express, and it cannot be extended beyond the limits within which it was contracted.
Suretyship must be recorded in a document bearing the surety's signature and the mention of the maximum sum guaranteed in words and figures. In case of difference, the suretyship is valid for the sum expressed in words.

The surety who does not know how or cannot write affixes his fingerprint in the presence of a witness who attests in the suretyship document his identity, his presence and that the nature and effects of the document have been specified to the surety.

The provisions of this article also apply to suretyship required by law.

###### Article 2273

Suretyship of an obligation may extend, in addition to the principal and within the limit of the maximum sum guaranteed, to the accessories of the debt and to the costs of recovering the claim, including those subsequent to the notice given to the surety, provided that this commitment results from a handwritten mention by the surety in accordance with the provisions of the preceding article.
The document constituting the principal obligation must be annexed to the suretyship agreement.

###### Art.2274

General suretyship of the principal debtor's debts, in the form of a suretyship of all commitments, of the debit balance of a current account, or in any other form, is understood, except express provision to the contrary, only as a guarantee of direct contractual debts.

It must be concluded, on pain of relative nullity, for a maximum sum freely determined between the parties, including the principal and all accessories.

General suretyship may be renewed when the maximum sum is reached. Renewal must be express; any provision to the contrary is deemed unwritten.

It may be revoked, at any time, by the surety before the maximum guaranteed sum has been reached. All commitments of the guaranteed debtor arising before the revocation remain guaranteed by the surety.
Unless otherwise provided, general suretyship does not guarantee the principal debtor's debts prior to the date of the suretyship.

###### Article 2275

Debts incumbent on the deceased in his capacity as surety remain, like all other debts, the responsibility of his successors.
However, only debts arising prior to the surety's death are transmitted to his successors. Nevertheless, debts arising before death or universal transmission remain their responsibility, regardless of when they become due.

###### Article 2276

The debtor obligated to provide a surety must present one who has the capacity to contract, who has sufficient property to answer for the object of the obligation, and whose domicile is within the jurisdiction where it must be given, unless waived by the creditor or the competent court.
The debtor who cannot find a surety may replace it with any real security giving the same guarantees to the creditor.

###### Article 2277

The solvency of a civil surety is estimated only with regard to his landed property, except in commercial matters, or when the debt is modest.
No regard is had to litigious immovable property, or property whose discussion would become too difficult due to the remoteness of their location.

###### Article 2278

When the surety received by the creditor, voluntarily or in court, subsequently becomes insolvent, the debtor must provide another or provide a real security giving the same guarantees to the creditor.
This rule is excepted only in the case where the surety was given by virtue of an agreement by which the creditor required a particular person as surety.

##### Section II: Effect of suretyship

###### § 1

Effect of suretyship between the creditor and the surety Article 2279
The creditor must notify the surety of any default by the debtor, forfeiture or extension of the term, indicating the amount remaining due by the debtor in principal, interest and costs at the date of default, forfeiture or extension of the term.

In case of extension of the term granted to the principal debtor, the surety is entitled to refuse the benefit of this extension and to pursue the debtor to compel payment or obtain a guarantee or a conservatory measure.

In case of forfeiture of the term affecting the principal debtor, this does not automatically extend to the surety who may only be required to pay at the maturity date fixed at the time when the suretyship was provided. Any clause to the contrary is unwritten. However, the surety incurs forfeiture of the term if, after formal notice, it does not satisfy its own obligations at the fixed maturity date.

###### Article 2280

Civil suretyship is simple, unless otherwise provided by law or conventional stipulation of solidarity.

The joint and several surety is bound to perform the principal obligation under the same conditions as a joint and several debtor subject to the special provisions of this code.
Unless otherwise provided by law or stipulation, the simple surety, unlike the judicial surety and the joint and several surety, has the benefit of discussion and division.
However, the creditor may only pursue the surety, whether simple, joint and several or judicial, by joining the principal debtor as a party.

###### Article 2281

The creditor may only bring legal action against the surety after a formal notice to pay addressed to the debtor has remained without effect.
The surety is only bound to pay the creditor if the principal debtor does not perform its obligation. It is bound in the same manner as the principal debtor.

###### Article 2282

Any surety may raise against the creditor all defenses belonging to the principal debtor, which are inherent to the debt and tend to reduce, extinguish or defer the debt, subject to contrary legislative provisions. But the surety may not raise against the creditor defenses that are purely personal to the debtor.
The simple or joint and several surety is discharged when subrogation to the creditor's rights and guarantees can no longer operate in its favor, by act of the creditor. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.

If the act imputed to the creditor only limits this subrogation, the surety is discharged to the extent of the insufficiency of the preserved guarantee.

###### Article 2283

The surety who, upon first proceedings brought against it, requests the benefit of discussion must indicate to the creditor the property of the principal debtor capable of being immediately seized on national territory and, if the creditor so requests, advance sufficient sums to conduct the discussion.

###### Article 2284

Whenever the surety has made the indication of property authorized by the preceding article, and has provided sufficient sums for the discussion, the creditor is, up to the value of the property indicated, liable to the surety for the insolvency of the principal debtor arising from failure to pursue.

###### Article 2285

If there are several sureties for the same debtor and the same debt, unless there is a stipulation of solidarity between them or waiver by them of this benefit, each of them may, upon first proceedings by the

creditor, request division of the debt among the solvent sureties on the day the defense is invoked.

The surety is not liable for the insolvencies of other sureties arising after the division.
The creditor who voluntarily divides its action when it could have avoided doing so, may not reverse this division and bears the insolvency of the sureties pursued without being able to transfer it to the other sureties.

###### § 2. Effect of suretyship between the debtor and the surety Article 2286

As soon as it is pursued the surety must notify the principal debtor or join it as a party before paying the debt to the pursuing creditor.
If the surety has paid without having notified or joined the principal debtor as a party, it loses its recourse against the debtor if, at the time of payment by it or subsequent to this payment, the debtor had the means to have the debt declared extinguished or if it had paid in ignorance of the surety's payment. Nevertheless, the surety retains its action for restitution against the pursuing creditor.

###### Article 2287

The surety who has paid has recourse against the principal debtor, even if the suretyship was given without the debtor's knowledge.
This recourse applies both to the principal and to interest and costs; nevertheless the surety only has recourse for costs incurred by it since it notified the principal debtor of the proceedings brought against it.
It also has recourse for damages, if applicable in case of prejudice it may have suffered from the creditor's proceedings.

###### Article 2288

The surety who has paid the debt is subrogated to all the rights and guarantees of the pursuing creditor against the debtor.
If there are several principal debtors jointly and severally liable for the same debt, the surety is subrogated against each of them for all that it has paid, even if it only stood surety for one. If the debtors are joint, it must divide its recourses.

###### Article 2289

The surety, even before having paid, may act against the debtor to be indemnified by it, or request preservation of its rights in the debtor's patrimony:
1° As soon as it is pursued in court for payment; 2° When the debtor is in cessation of payments;
3° When the debtor has not discharged it within the agreed period;
4° When the debt has become due by expiry of the term under which it was contracted.

###### § 3. Effect of suretyship among the various sureties Article 2290

When several persons have stood surety for the same debtor for the same debt, the surety who has discharged the debt has recourse against the other sureties, each for its share and portion;

But this recourse only applies when the surety has paid in one of the cases set out in the preceding article.

##### Section III: Extinction of suretyship Article 2291

The obligation resulting from suretyship is extinguished by the same causes as under the general law of contracts.
Payment in kind definitively releases the surety, even if the creditor is subsequently evicted from the thing accepted by it. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.
Novation of the principal obligation by change of object or cause releases the surety unless it agrees to transfer its guarantee to the new debt. Any clause to the contrary stipulated before the novation is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2292

The surety's undertaking is extinguished independently of the principal obligation:
-	when in proceedings brought against it, the surety pleads set-off for a personal claim against the pursuing creditor;
-	when the creditor has granted a release of debt to the surety alone;
-	when confusion occurs between the person of the creditor and the surety;
-	when the creditor has voluntarily accepted immovable property or any item in payment of the principal debt, even if subsequently the creditor were to be evicted therefrom;
-	for debts arising after the death of the surety;
-	in the case of article 2282.

###### Article 2293

The simple extension of time granted by the creditor to the principal debtor, or the modification of the security interests accompanying the principal obligation into new equivalent security interests, does not discharge the surety, who may, in such case, pursue the debtor to compel payment.

#### Chapitre II : De la lettre de garantie ou « garantie autonome » Article 2294

A letter of guarantee or autonomous guarantee is a necessarily written undertaking by which the guarantor binds himself, in consideration of an obligation entered into by a third party giving the order, to pay a sum either on first demand or according to agreed terms.
Such a contract may not be entered into, on pain of nullity, by natural persons; and may not, for legal persons, be stipulated for a purpose unrelated to the commercial or professional activity of the borrower. In such case, the letter of guarantee is governed by articles L.2281-201 et seq. of the Commercial Code.

#### Chapitre III : De la lettre d'intention

###### Article 2295

A letter of intent is an undertaking to do or not to do having as its object the support provided to a debtor in the performance of his obligation towards his creditor.

Sous-Titre II : Les sûretés réelles Chapitre I : Dispositions générales

###### Article 2296

Any real security interest may be created, registered, managed and enforced on behalf of the creditors of the guaranteed obligation by a person whom they designate for that purpose in the instrument evidencing such obligation.

###### Article 2297

A privilege is a right which the quality of the claim gives to a creditor to be preferred over other creditors, even secured creditors. It may be over movables or over immovables.
As between privileged creditors, preference is determined by the different qualities of the privileges. When they are of the same rank, privileged creditors are paid proportionately.

###### Article 2298

The privilege in respect of rights of the Public Treasury and the order in which it is exercised are governed by the laws concerning them.
The Public Treasury may not, however, obtain a privilege to the prejudice of rights previously acquired by third parties.

###### Article 2299

Privileges, like security interests, may be over movables or over immovables.

#### Chapitre II : Des sûretés sur les meubles Article 2300

Real security interests over movables comprise: the right of retention, the pledge, privileges and ownership retained or transferred by way of security.

##### Section I : Du droit de rétention Article 2301

A creditor who lawfully holds property of the debtor may retain it until full payment of what is owed to him, independently of any other security interest.
Where the same property is the subject of several successive pledges without dispossession, the rank of creditors is determined by the order of their registration. Where property given in pledge without dispossession is subsequently the subject of a pledge with dispossession, the right of preference of the prior pledgee is enforceable against the subsequent pledgee when it is duly published notwithstanding the latter's right of retention.

###### Article 2302

The right of retention may only be exercised:
-	before any seizure;
-	if the claim is certain, liquidated and due;
-	if there exists a connection between the arising of the claim and the thing retained.

##### Section II : Du nantissement Article 2303

A pledge is a contract by which a debtor delivers a thing to his creditor as security for the debt.

Pledges without dispossession which relate to: rights of partners and securities; business goodwill; professional equipment; stocks of raw materials and merchandise, are governed by the provisions of the Commercial Code.
The pledge of a movable thing is called a gage. That of an immovable thing is called an immovable pledge.

###### Article 2304

Heavy equipment purchased by a private individual may be the subject of a pledge for the benefit of the seller, of the third party having guaranteed the purchaser's commitments towards the seller, or of any person having lent the sums necessary for the purchase.
Such a security interest is enforceable against third parties only if it is registered in the Movable Security Interests Register.

###### Article 2305

A gage is a contract by which a debtor delivers a thing or a set of things of a movable nature to his creditor as security for the debt.
The secured claims may be present, future or contingent; in the latter two cases, they must be determinable and not be tainted with nullity.

The gage confers on the creditor the right to be paid from the thing which is its object, by privilege and in preference to other creditors.

###### Article 2306

A gage may be granted by the debtor or by a third party; in the latter case, the creditor has recourse only against the property assigned as security.
Except for a gage granted by a third party, a gage over another's property is null and may give rise to damages when the creditor was unaware that the thing belonged to another. If the thing does not belong to the grantor, the pledgee in good faith may oppose the owner's claim for recovery under the conditions provided for a possessor in good faith.

###### Article 2307

Any movable property, corporeal or incorporeal, is capable of being given in gage.

Movable security interests subject to publicity are the subject of registration, at the initiative of the creditor, in the Movable Security Interests Register.

###### Article 2308

The parties may agree to the substitution during performance of the pledge contract of the pledged thing by another thing.
The gage may also relate to sums or securities deposited as security by civil servants, ministerial officers or any other person to guarantee abuses for which they might be liable and loans granted for the constitution of such security.

###### Article 2309

A pledge contract provided with dispossession produces effect only if the pledged thing is actually delivered to the creditor or to a third party agreed between the parties.

A promise of pledge, in particular of future things, obliges the promisor to deliver the thing under the agreed conditions.

###### Article 2310

Where it is without dispossession of the debtor, the gage is enforceable against third parties by the publicity given to it. This is effected at the initiative of the creditor in the Movable Security Interests Register.

###### Article 2311

A pledge contract is enforceable against third parties only if it is evidenced by a writing, authentic or under private signature, duly registered, and containing indication of the sum owed as well as the kind, nature and quantity of the movable property given in pledge, unless otherwise provided by law.
The drafting of the instrument in writing and its registration are nevertheless required only in matters exceeding the value of 100,000 FD.
The gage is also enforceable against third parties by the dispossession into the hands of the creditor or of an agreed third party of the property which is its object.
If the gage is created over incorporeal movable property, such as a movable claim, the instrument, once registered, is served on the debtor of the claim given in pledge.

###### Article 2312

A debtor who pledges his claim against a named third party must deliver to the pledgee creditor his title to the claim and notify his own debtor of the transfer of his claim in that capacity; failing this, the pledgee creditor may proceed with such notification.
This pledge is realized by the demand for payment that the pledgee creditor addresses to the transferred debtor. The latter may raise against the pledgee creditor defenses based on his personal relations with his own creditor as well as defenses which he may assert against the pledgee creditor. It is otherwise if the transferred debtor has made a written commitment to pay the pledgee creditor directly, in which case he may not raise against the pledgee creditor defenses based on his personal relations with his own creditor.

The creditor of the transferred debtor remains liable, jointly and severally with the latter, for payment of the pledged claim.
The pledgee creditor who has obtained payment must account for it to his own debtor.

###### Article 2313

In other areas, if there are no specific legal provisions or contractual stipulations defining the methods of pledging the intangible property given as security, delivery to the creditor of the document evidencing the existence of the right operates dispossession of the grantor.

###### Article 2314

The deposit or consignment of sums, instruments or securities, ordered judicially as security or as a conservatory measure, entails special allocation and privilege under Article 2305 paragraph 3.

###### Article 2315

The pledgee creditor retains or causes to be retained the pledged thing by the agreed third party until full payment, in principal, interest and costs, of the debt for which the pledge was constituted.
If there arises on the part of the same debtor towards the same creditor, one or more other debts contracted subsequent to the pledging, and becoming due before payment of the first debt, the creditor may retain or cause to be retained the pledged thing until complete payment of all debts, even in the absence of any stipulation to that effect.

###### Article 2316

The privilege subsists on the pledge only insofar as the pledge has been placed and remains in the possession of the creditor, or of a third party agreed between the parties.
But if he has been dispossessed against his will, the creditor may claim the pledged thing as a possessor in good faith.

###### Article 2317

Until the expropriation of the debtor, if applicable, the grantor remains owner of the pledge, which is, in the hand of the creditor, only a deposit ensuring the latter's privilege.

###### Article 2318

The creditor or the agreed third party must watch over the thing and ensure its preservation, as must a remunerated depositary. He is liable for the loss or deterioration of the pledge that would have occurred through his negligence.
He may not, except by contrary stipulation, use the pledged thing or collect its fruits. If he is authorized to collect the fruits, he must apply them, except by contrary clause, to what is owed to him in interest and capital. When the pledged thing is a claim, the provisions of Article 2320 apply.

If the thing threatens to perish, the creditor or the agreed third party may, upon authorization, as the case may be, from the Civil Chamber or the Commercial Chamber of the Court of First Instance, sell it and the effects of the pledge are then transferred to the price.
The agreed third party and, if applicable, the purchaser in bad faith of the pledged thing are jointly and severally liable with the pledgee creditor for non-performance of these obligations.
The pledging of a consumable thing authorizes the creditor or the agreed third party to return an equivalent thing.

When the pledge has as its object fungible things, the creditor or the agreed third party may alienate them only if the agreement so provides, subject to replacing them with the same quantity of equivalent things. In the absence of a stipulation to that effect, he must keep them separate from things of the same nature belonging to him. Failing this by the creditor or the agreed third party, the grantor may claim restitution of the pledged property, without prejudice to damages, if the creditor or the agreed third party does not satisfy his obligation to preserve the pledge. When the agreement exempts the creditor from the obligation to separate the pledged property from his things of the same nature, he acquires ownership thereof subject to returning the same quantity of equivalent things.

###### Article 2319

For his part, when he has fully paid him the capital, interest and costs, the debtor must account to the creditor for the useful and necessary expenses that the latter has incurred for the preservation of the pledge.

###### Article 2320

When the thing given in pledge is a claim:
-	if the maturity of the claim given in pledge is prior to the maturity of the secured claim, the pledgee creditor is entitled to collect the amount thereof in capital and interest, except by contrary clause;
-	if the maturity of the secured claim is prior to the maturity of the claim given in pledge, the pledgee creditor is required to wait for the maturity of the latter to collect the amount thereof.
In both cases, the pledgee creditor collects the amount of the pledged claim subject to accounting, in the capacity of agent, for the surplus collected in favor of the grantor of the pledge.
