In addition, except by contrary agreement, if this claim bears interest, the creditor applies this interest to that which may be owed to him in interest and capital.
If the debt for the security of which the claim was given in pledge does not itself bear interest, the application is made to the capital of the debt.

###### Article 2321

In the absence of payment at maturity, the pledgee creditor may, eight days after simple notification made to the debtor and to the third party who holds the thing delivered in pledge, if there is one, have the pledged thing sold at public sale.
The sale is conducted by a bailiff at least eight days after publication of a notice in a newspaper authorized to receive legal announcements mentioning the date, time and place of the sale, the place where the objects may be viewed, the reserve price or prices, the description of the object and the costs.

The creditor may also apply to, as the case may be, the Civil Chamber or the Commercial Chamber of the Court of First Instance to request that the pledge be awarded to him or sold to a third party up to the amount of his claim and according to valuation following market rates or by expert opinion.
Any clause that would authorize the creditor to appropriate the pledge or to dispose of it without the above formalities is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2322

In case of sale or loss or destruction of the pledged thing, the pledgee creditor has priority over the price of the thing sold or over the insurance indemnity for the amount of the secured claim in principal, interest and costs.
He exercises his right of preference in accordance with Article 2331 of this code. If there are several pledgee creditors, they are ranked in the order of registration of successive pledges or, in the absence of registration, in the order of constitution.

###### Article 2323

The pledge is indivisible notwithstanding the divisibility of the debt towards the heirs of the debtor or those of the creditor.
The heir of the debtor who has paid his portion of the debt may not demand restitution of his portion in the pledge, even if it were divisible by nature, as long as the debt is not entirely discharged.

Reciprocally, the heir of the creditor who has received his share of the claim may not release the pledge, even if it were divisible, to the prejudice of those of his co-heirs who are not paid.

###### Article 2324

The commercial pledge is governed by the provisions of the commercial code.

###### Article 2325

The pledge relating to a registered motor vehicle or trailer is governed by this article and articles 2326 to 2329 below.
This pledge is enforceable against third parties by the declaration made to the Mining Service. This declaration is recorded in a special register with counterfoils and mentions the creation of the pledge to which the vehicle or trailer is subject, the name of the owner of the property and that of the creditor, and the date of registration of the contract.

A receipt for this declaration is issued to the pledgee creditor, repeating verbatim the particulars appearing on the counterfoil. By possession of this receipt, the pledgee creditor is deemed to have retained the vehicle or trailer in his possession.

###### Article 2326

In the case of a pledge relating to a new vehicle or trailer, the registration of the pledge by the seller, assignee of the debt, discounter or lender of money for the purchase made, must be done within three months from the issue of the receipt for the declaration of putting the vehicle into circulation.

###### Article 2327

The cancellation of the pledge notation may be requested either by the creditor or by the debtor.

When it is done by the creditor, indication of the cancellation is recorded on the receipt that was issued to him. In this case, the debtor may request to obtain a certificate of cancellation.
When it is done by the debtor, the latter must justify the extinction of the guaranteed debt or produce the deed giving release of the registration. A certificate of cancellation is then issued to him.

###### Article 2328

In the absence of payment of the guaranteed debt, the creditor may have the sale of the pledged property ordered by the court. This sale takes place according to the procedures provided for enforcement methods without the pledge agreement being able to derogate therefrom.
The creditor may also have it ordered by the court that the property shall remain with him in payment. When the value of the property exceeds the amount of the guaranteed debt, the sum equal to the difference is paid to the debtor or, if there are other pledgee creditors, is deposited.

###### Article 2329

It may be agreed, at the time of creation of the pledge or subsequently, that in the absence of performance of the guaranteed obligation the creditor shall become owner of the pledged property.
The value of the property is determined on the day of transfer by an expert appointed amicably or judicially. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.
When this value exceeds the amount of the guaranteed debt, the sum equal to the difference is paid to the debtor or, if there are other pledgee creditors, is deposited.

##### Section III: Privileges over movable property

###### Article 2330

Privileges are either general, or particular over certain movable property.

###### § 1. General privileges over movable property Article 2331

Privileged claims over all movable property are those expressed below, and are exercised in the following order, without formality of publicity:
1° Court costs; 2° Funeral expenses;
3° Any costs of the last illness preceding the seizure of property, whatever its outcome, concurrently among those to whom they are owed;
4° Without prejudice to the possible application of the provisions of articles 152 to 155 of the labour code, the privileges of wages, which relate to:
-	sums owed to workers and apprentices for performance and termination of their contract during the last six months preceding the death of the debtor, the seizure of property or the judicial decision opening collective proceedings;
-	compensation owed for paid leave;
-	severance compensation owed;

5° Supplies of subsistence provided to the debtor and his family during the last year

6° Sums owed to authors of intellectual, literary and artistic works for the last three years preceding the death of the debtor, the seizure of property or the judicial decision opening collective proceedings;

7° Up to a limit of one million Djibouti Francs, the sums for which the debtor is liable in respect of tax and customs claims and to the National Social Security Fund.

###### Article 2332

It is recalled that, in accordance with article 2298, the privilege, by reason of the rights of the Public Treasury and the order in which it is exercised, are regulated by the laws concerning them. The same applies to claims for contributions to the National Social Security Fund.
Special texts creating general privileges must specify the rank of these by determining it in relation to the provisions of this article. Failing this, the rank of these privileges is the last of that established by this article.

###### § 2. Privileges over certain movable property Article 2333

Creditors holding special privileges have, over the movable property assigned to them as a basis by law, a right of preference.

This right of preference is also exercised, by subrogation, over the insurance indemnity for the movable property that has perished or disappeared, as long as it is not paid.

###### Article 2334

Privileged claims over certain movable property are, without prejudice to special texts establishing others, those:
1° Of the lessor of immovable property, who has a privilege over the fruits and income of the year, and over the price of everything that furnishes the leased property.
This privilege guarantees, in addition to the damages that may be awarded to him, the claims of the lessor against the lessee for the twelve months elapsed preceding the seizure and for the twelve months to fall due after it.
The lessee or any person who, by fraudulent manoeuvres, deprives the lessor of his privilege totally or partially, commits a criminal offence punished by the penalties for breach of trust.
The owner may seize the movable property furnishing his house or farm, when they have been moved without his consent, and he retains his privilege over them, provided that he has made the claim in the deed of seizure; however, the lessor who thus claims the movable property moved without his consent must reimburse the purchaser the price they cost him.
2° Of the pledgee creditor, over the pledge he realizes;

3° Of the person who has incurred expenses or provided services for the preservation of the thing;

4° Of the seller, who has, over the movable property sold, a privilege to guarantee payment of the unpaid price, if it is still in the possession of the debtor or over the price still owed by the sub-purchaser.
5° The hotelier for his supplies, over the effects of the traveller that have been transported to his hotel; 6° The carrier, for carriage costs and ancillary expenses, over the thing transported;
7° Holders of claims resulting from abuses and malfeasance committed by public officials in the exercise of their functions, over the funds of their security deposit and over the interest that may be owed thereon;
8° Holders of claims arising from an accident for the benefit of third parties injured by this accident or their successors in title, over the indemnity for which the civil liability insurer acknowledges itself or has been judicially recognized as debtor by reason of the insurance agreement.

No payment made to the insured shall be liberatory as long as the privileged creditors have not been satisfied.

##### Section V: Ownership retained or transferred as security

###### § 1. Ownership retained as security Article 2335

Ownership of a property may be retained as security by the effect of a retention of title clause. The effect of a retention of title clause is to suspend the transfer effect of a contract until complete payment of the obligation that constitutes its consideration.

The ownership thus reserved is accessory to the claim whose payment it guarantees.

###### Article 2336

Retention of title must necessarily be agreed in writing.

###### Article 2337

Reserved ownership of a fungible good may be exercised, up to the amount of the debt remaining due, over goods of the same nature and same quality held by the debtor or on his account.

###### Article 2338

The incorporation of a movable subject to a reservation of ownership into another good does not prevent the creditor's rights when these goods can be separated without suffering damage.

###### Article 2339

In the absence of full payment at maturity, the creditor may demand the restitution of the good in order to recover the right to dispose of it.
The value of the good taken back is imputed, as payment, on the balance of the secured debt.

When the value of the good taken back exceeds the amount of the secured debt still due, the creditor owes the debtor a sum equal to the difference.

###### Article 2340

The right of ownership transfers to the debtor's claim against the sub-purchaser or to the insurance indemnity subrogated to the good.

###### § 2. Ownership transferred as security Article 2341

Ownership of a movable good or of a right may be transferred as security for an obligation by virtue of a fiduciary contract concluded in application of articles 2205 to 2245.

###### Article 2342

In case of a fiduciary concluded as security, the contract mentions on pain of nullity, in addition to the provisions provided for in article 2210, the secured debt and the estimated value of the good or right transferred into the fiduciary patrimony.

###### Article 2343

In the absence of payment of the secured debt and unless otherwise stipulated in the fiduciary contract, the fiduciary, when he is the creditor, acquires free disposal of the good or right transferred as security.
When the fiduciary is not the creditor, the latter may require from him the delivery of the good, which he may then freely dispose of, or, if the fiduciary contract so provides, the sale of the good or right transferred and the delivery of all or part of the price.

The value of the good or right transferred is determined by an expert appointed amicably or judicially, unless the good is a sum of money. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2344

If the beneficiary of the fiduciary has acquired free disposal of the good or right transferred in application of article 2343, he pays to the settlor, when the value mentioned in the last paragraph of that article exceeds the amount of the secured debt, a sum equal to the difference between that value and the amount of the debt, subject to prior payment of debts arising from the conservation or management of the fiduciary patrimony.
Subject to the same reservation, if the fiduciary proceeds with the sale of the good or right transferred in application of the fiduciary contract, he restores to the settlor the part of the proceeds of that sale exceeding, as the case may be, the value of the secured debt.

###### Article 2345

The ownership transferred in application of article 2341 may be subsequently assigned as security for debts other than those mentioned in the constitutive instrument provided that the latter expressly provides for it.
The settlor may offer it as security, not only to the original creditor, but also to a new creditor, even though the first has not been paid. When the settlor is a natural person, the fiduciary patrimony may then be assigned as security for a new debt only within the limit of its value estimated on the day of the recharge.

On pain of nullity, the agreement established according to the provisions of article 2342 is registered in the form provided for in article 2213. The date of registration determines, among them, the rank of creditors.

The provisions of this article are of public policy and any clause contrary to them is deemed unwritten.

#### Chapter III: Securities over immovables Article 2346

Securities over immovables are: privileges, immovable pledge (or antichresis), and mortgages.
Ownership of the immovable may also be retained or transferred as security.

##### Section I: Immovable pledge or "antichresis" Article 2347

Immovable pledge, or antichresis, is the assignment, by the debtor or by a third party for the debtor, of an immovable as security for an obligation; it entails dispossession of the one who constitutes it.
Immovable pledge is established only in writing.

The creditor acquires by this contract only the faculty to collect the fruits of the immovable, with the obligation to impute them annually on the interest, if any is due to him, and then on the principal of his debt. He may for this purpose, without losing possession of the good, lease the immovable, either to a third party or to the debtor himself.

###### Article 2348

The creditor is bound, unless otherwise agreed, to pay the contributions and annual charges of the immovable that he holds as immovable pledge.
He must also, on pain of damages, provide for the maintenance and useful and necessary repairs of the immovable, and may deduct for this purpose, from the fruits, all expenses relating to these various matters. He may, at any time, free himself from this obligation by restoring the good to its owner.

###### Article 2349

The debtor may not claim enjoyment of the immovable that he has delivered as immovable pledge before the full discharge of his debt.

###### Article 2350

The creditor does not become owner of the immovable by the mere default of payment at the agreed term; any clause to the contrary is null.

The creditor, in case of default of payment at the agreed term may however pursue the expropriation of his debtor by legal means.

###### Article 2351

The provisions of article 2323 apply to immovable pledge.

###### Article 2352

Everything provided in this chapter does not prejudice the rights that third parties might have over the land of the immovable delivered as immovable pledge. Indeed, immovable pledge being only a delegation of fruits as and when they fall due or are collected, third parties may acquire and exercise their rights over the pledged immovable.
If the creditor, provided with this title, has over the land privileges or mortgages legally established and preserved, he exercises them in his order and like any other creditor.

###### Article 2353

The rights of the creditor holding an immovable pledge right are extinguished notably: 1° By the extinction of the principal obligation;
2° By the early restitution of the immovable to its owner.

##### Section II: Privileges over immovable property

###### § 1. Special privileges over immovable property Article 2354

Privileged creditors over immovable property are:

1° The seller, over the immovable property sold, for payment of the price;

If there are several successive sales for which the price is owed in whole or in part, the first seller is preferred to the second, the second to the third, and so on;
2° Those who have provided funds for the acquisition of immovable property, provided that it is authentically established, by the loan agreement, that the sum was intended for that use and, by the seller's receipt, that payment was made from the borrowed funds;

3° Co-heirs, over the immovable property of the estate, for the guarantee of partitions made between them, and of balancing payments or equalization of shares;

4° Architects, contractors and artisans who have built, reconstructed or repaired buildings, canals or any other works whatsoever, provided however that, by an expert appointed ex officio by the court of first instance within whose jurisdiction the buildings are located, a report has been drawn up beforehand, for the purpose of establishing the state of the premises in relation to the works that the owner declares he intends to have carried out, and that the works have been, within six months at most of their completion, accepted by an expert also appointed ex officio. But the amount of the privilege cannot exceed the values established by the second report, and it is reduced to the increase in value existing at the time of alienation of the immovable property and resulting from the works that have been carried out thereon;

5° Those who have lent funds to pay or reimburse the workers enjoy the same privilege, provided that this use is authentically established by the loan agreement, and by the workers' receipt, as stated above for those who have lent funds for the acquisition of immovable property;

6° The creditors of the deceased and legatees of sums of money over the immovable property of the estate, as well as the personal creditors of the heir over the immovable property of the latter, for the guarantee of the rights they hold under article 1028.

###### Article 2355

The privileges enumerated in articles 2331 and 2354 of the civil code, with the exception however of the privilege for legal costs incurred for the realization of the immovable property and the distribution of the price, only grant a right of preference to the beneficiaries called upon to exercise them over the immovable property mass over unsecured creditors.

###### § 2. General privileges over immovable property Article 2356

The privileges that extend over movable property and immovable property are those set out in article 2331.

###### Article 2357

When, for lack of movable property, the privileged creditors set out in the preceding article present themselves to be paid from the price of immovable property in competition with other privileged creditors over the immovable property, payments are made in the following order:
1° Legal costs and others set out in article 2331; 2° The claims designated in article 235

###### 4. §

3. How privileges over immovable property are preserved Article 2358
As between creditors, privileges only produce effect with regard to immovable property insofar as they are made public by registration in the registers of the keeper of mortgages, in the manner determined by law, and from the date of that registration, subject only to the following exceptions.

###### Article 2359

The claims enumerated in article 2331 are excepted from the formality of registration.

###### Article 2360

If their privilege is established by a notarial deed to be published in the land register:
1° The privileged seller preserves his privilege by the transcription of the instrument that transferred ownership to the purchaser, and which establishes that all or part of the price is owed to him; for this purpose, the transcription of the contract made by the purchaser shall be valid as registration for the seller and for the lender who has provided him with the sums paid, and who will be subrogated to the seller's rights by the same contract. In this case, the keeper of mortgages shall nevertheless be required, on pain of all damages and interest towards third parties, to make ex officio the registration in his register, of the claims resulting from the instrument transferring ownership, both in favor of the seller and in favor of the lenders, who may also have made, if it has not been done, the transcription of the sale contract, for the purpose of acquiring registration of what is owed to them on the price.

2° The co-heir or co-partitioner preserves his privilege over the property of each share or over the property sold by licitation for the balancing payments and equalization of shares or for the price of the licitation, by registration made at his initiative, within sixty days, from the date of the partition deed or the adjudication by licitation; during which time no mortgage may take place over the property charged with the balancing payment or adjudicated by licitation, to the prejudice of the creditor of the balancing payment or of the price.

###### Article 2361

Architects, contractors, masons and other workers employed to build, reconstruct or repair buildings, canals, or other works, and those who have, to pay and reimburse them, lent the sums whose use has been established, preserve by the double registration made:

1° Of the report establishing the state of the premises;

2° Of the acceptance report, their privilege at the date of registration of the first report.

###### Article 2362

Creditors and legatees who request the separation of the deceased's estate, in accordance with article 665 of the title On Successions, preserve, with regard to the creditors of the heirs or representatives of the deceased, their privilege over the immovable property of the estate, by registrations made on each of these properties, within six months from the opening of the succession.
Before the expiration of this period, no mortgage may be established with effect on these properties by the heirs or representatives to the prejudice of these creditors or legatees.

###### Article 2363

The assignees of these various privileged claims exercise all the same rights as the assignors in their place and stead.

###### Article 2364

All privileged claims subject to the formality of registration, with regard to which the conditions prescribed above to preserve the privilege have not been fulfilled, do not nevertheless cease to be secured by mortgage, but the mortgage only dates, with regard to third parties, from the time of the registrations that must have been made as will be explained hereinafter.

##### Section III: Mortgages Article 2365

The provisions of Law No. 177/AN/91/2nd L on the organization of land ownership are applicable, in a general manner and subject to the provisions that follow, to registered immovable property and to the real rights relating thereto.

###### Article 2366

A mortgage is a real right over immovable property assigned to the discharge of an obligation.

It is, by its nature, indivisible, and subsists in its entirety over all the immovable property assigned, over each and over each portion of this immovable property.

It follows them into whatever hands they pass.

###### Article 2367

A mortgage only takes place in the cases and according to the forms authorized by law.

###### Article 2368

Only the following are susceptible to mortgages:
1° Land whether built upon or not which is in commerce and with them, their accessories deemed to be immovable property;
2° The usufruct of the same property, during the time of its duration;
3° The rights of emphyteusis, during the time of its duration, and of superficies, established over the same property. Movable property does not have a right of pursuit by mortgage.

Ships and seagoing vessels are subject to the provisions specific to them.


This excerpt sits under: REPUBLIC OF DJIBOUTI > BOOK III. THE DIFFERENT WAYS IN WHICH PROPERTY IS ACQUIRED > Title XIX: Securities > Chapter III: Securities over immovable property Article 2346

###### Article 2369

A mortgage is either legal, judicial, or conventional. A legal mortgage is one which results from the law.
A judicial mortgage is one which results from judgments or judicial acts. A mortgage may likewise result from judgments rendered in foreign countries, if they have been declared enforceable by a Djiboutian court, subject to special laws or treaties. Similarly, arbitral awards give rise to a mortgage only insofar as they are vested with the exequatur.
A conventional mortgage is one which results from contracts and other juridical acts. It is granted by notarial deed; the transfer and release of the mortgage take place in the same forms.

###### Article 2370

A conventional mortgage may be granted only by those who have the capacity to alienate the immovable property which they subject to it. The property of minors, adults under guardianship, and that of absentees as long as possession is conferred only provisionally, may be mortgaged only for the causes and in the forms established by law, or by virtue of judgments; those who have over the immovable property only a right suspended by a condition, or resolvable in certain cases, or subject to rescission, may grant only a mortgage subject to the same conditions or to the same rescission.
The authentic instrument specifically declares the nature and location of each of the immovable properties presently belonging to the debtor, over which he grants the mortgage of the debt.

###### Article 2371

Future property cannot be mortgaged.

Nevertheless, if the present and unencumbered property of the debtor is insufficient for the security of the debt, he may, by acknowledging this insufficiency, consent that each of the properties which he shall acquire thereafter be specially assigned thereto as acquisitions are made.

###### Article 2372

If the immovable property or immovable properties presently subject to the mortgage perish or suffer deterioration in such a manner that they become insufficient for the security of the creditor, the latter may obtain a supplementary mortgage or, failing that, pursue his reimbursement forthwith.

###### Article 2373

A conventional mortgage is valid only insofar as the sum for which it is granted is certain and determined by the deed: if the debt resulting from the obligation is conditional as to its existence, or indeterminate in its value, the creditor may require the registration of which mention will be made hereinafter, only up to an estimated value expressly declared by him, and which the debtor shall have the right to have reduced, if appropriate.

###### Article 2374

Mortgages and privileges which have given rise to registration are extinguished: 1° By the extinction of the obligation of which they constitute the guarantee;
2° By the renunciation by the creditor of his right;
3° By the completion of the procedure for purging mortgages by the third-party holder upon forced expropriation or upon expropriation for reasons of public utility, in accordance with the requirements of Article 51 of Law No. 177/AN/91/2nd L on the organization of land ownership.

##### Section IV: Immovable property transferred as security

###### Article 2375

The provisions of this chapter are not applicable to fiducies constituted as security by legal persons.

###### Article 2376

The ownership of immovable property may be transferred as security for an obligation by virtue of a fiducie contract concluded in application of Articles 2205 to 2245.

###### Article 2377

In the case of a fiducie concluded as security, the contract mentions on pain of nullity, in addition to the provisions provided for in Article 2210, the secured debt and the estimated value of the immovable property transferred into the fiduciary patrimony.

###### Article 2378

In the absence of payment of the secured debt and unless otherwise stipulated in the fiducie contract, the fiduciary, when he is the creditor, acquires the free disposal of the property transferred as security.
When the fiduciary is not the creditor, the latter may require from him the delivery of the property, which he may then freely dispose of, or, if the agreement so provides, the sale of the property and the delivery of all or part of the price.

The value of the property is determined by an expert appointed amicably or judicially. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2379

If the beneficiary of the fiducie has acquired the free disposal of the property in application of Article 2378, he pays to the settlor, when the value mentioned in the last paragraph of that article exceeds the amount of the secured debt, a sum equal to the difference between that value and the amount of the debt, subject to the prior payment of debts arising from the conservation or management of the fiduciary patrimony.
Subject to the same reservation, if the fiduciary proceeds with the sale of the property in application of the fiducie contract, he restores to the settlor the portion of the proceeds of that sale exceeding, where applicable, the value of the secured debt.

###### Article 2380

The ownership transferred in application of Article 2376 may be subsequently assigned to the security of debts other than those mentioned in the constitutive deed provided that the latter expressly provides for it.
The settlor may offer it as security, not only to the original creditor, but also to a new creditor, even though the first has not been paid. When the settlor is a natural person, the fiduciary patrimony may then be assigned as security for a new debt only within the limit of its value estimated on the day of the recharge.

On pain of nullity, the agreement established according to the provisions of Article 2377 is published in the form provided for in Article 2213. The date of publication determines, among them, the rank of the creditors.
The provisions of this article are of public order and any clause contrary to them is deemed unwritten.

### TITLE XX: Immovable revendication and forced sale of immovable property

###### Article 2381

The action for revendication of an immovable property and the forced sale of immovable property is pursued in compliance with the provisions of the code of civil procedure and those of Law No. 177/AN/91/2nd L on the organization of land ownership.

### Title XXI: Prescription

Chapter I: General provisions Article 2382
Prescription is a means of acquiring or of being released by a certain lapse of time, and under the conditions determined by law.

Time limits for forfeiture are not, except for contrary provisions provided by law, governed by this title.

The provisions of this title do not preclude the application of special rules provided by other texts or special laws.

###### Article 2383

Extinctive prescription is a mode of extinction of a right resulting from the inaction of its holder for a time defined by law.
It is subject to the law governing the right which it affects.

###### Article 2384

Acquisitive prescription is a means of acquiring property or a right by the effect of possession, when the law authorizes such an effect.

###### Article 2385

Prescription may in no case constitute a mode of acquisition of real rights over immovable property or of release from charges encumbering the same immovable property.

###### Article 2386

In movable matters, possession may produce an acquisitive effect of right under the conditions set out in Article 686 and following.

###### Article 2387

One cannot, in advance, renounce prescription; one may renounce prescription acquired.

Renunciation of prescription is express or tacit; tacit renunciation results from a fact which presupposes the abandonment of the acquired right.

One who cannot exercise his rights by himself cannot alone renounce prescription acquired.

###### Article 2388

Except in case of waiver, prescription may be raised at any stage of proceedings, even before the court of appeal.

Creditors, or any other person having an interest in the prescription being acquired, may raise it, even if the debtor or the owner has stated that he waives it.
Judges may not raise the defense of prescription of their own motion.

###### Article 2389

Payment made to extinguish a debt may not be reclaimed on the sole ground that the prescription period had expired.

###### Article 2390

The State, public establishments and communes are subject to the same prescriptions as private individuals, and may also raise them.

###### Article 2391

However, the following are imprescriptible, subject to the texts governing them:
1° Property belonging to the public domain within the meaning of the law (specifically referred to here are Law No. 171/AN/91/2nd L establishing and organizing the public domain and Law No. 173/AN/91/2nd L organizing the private domain of the State);
2° Things that are not in commerce;
3° In accordance with Article 674, the right of ownership as well as the rights and actions that are attributes of the right of ownership, such as for example the right to acquire joint ownership of a wall, the right to use running water of which one is a riparian owner, the right to claim passage for the owner of an enclosed land, the right to enclose oneself, or the right to request partition.

#### Chapitre II : Des causes qui empêchent la prescription mobilière Article 2392

One cannot change for oneself the cause and principle of one's possession, so that one prescribes according to the obligation one has contracted. Thus, those who possess for others never prescribe by any lapse of time whatsoever. Such is the case, for example, of the depositary or the usufructuary, and all others who hold the thing of the owner precariously, cannot prescribe it.

The heirs of those who held the thing from someone under such precarious titles cannot prescribe either.

###### Article 2393

It is otherwise in case of interversion of title, namely when the person whom the owner designates as precarious holder considers that his detention has been changed into possession or ownership.

###### Article 2394

Those to whom the thing has been transferred by a precarious holder by a title transferring ownership may nevertheless prescribe it when the conditions of possession are fulfilled.

#### Chapitre III

Du cours de la prescription Section I : Dispositions générales

###### Article 2395

Prescription runs against all persons, unless they are within some exception established by law.

###### Article 2396

Prescription is counted by days, and not by hours.

It is acquired when the last day of the term is completed.

###### Article 2397

When a new law extends the duration of a prescription period or a forfeiture period, it has no effect on a prescription or forfeiture already acquired. Subject to any transitional provisions it may provide, such a law applies immediately to the situation when the prescription period or forfeiture period had not expired on the date of its entry into force; account is then taken of the time already elapsed.

If the new law reduces the duration of a prescription period or a forfeiture period, this new period runs from the day of entry into force of this new law, without the total duration being able to exceed the duration provided for by the former law.

###### Article 2398

The prescription period may be interrupted or suspended according to the causes indicated by law.

Interruption of prescription erases the period already acquired and starts a new period running. This new period is of the same duration as the old one.
Suspension of prescription temporarily stops its running without erasing the time already elapsed.

##### Section II : Du délai de droit commun et de certains délais particuliers Article 2399

Except where otherwise provided:

1° Personal or movable actions are prescribed after three years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling him to exercise it;

2° Real immovable actions are prescribed after thirty years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling him to exercise it.

3° The prescription period is:
a.	10 years in case of bodily injury for the victim, from the date of consolidation of the injury;
b.	10 years for ecological damage;
c.	20 years in case of harm related to an act of torture or barbarity, or violence or sexual assault against minors.
d.	Architects, contractors and other persons bound to the owner by a contract for work are discharged from the warranty of works they have made or directed after ten years if they are major works, after two years for minor works.
e.	The action of bailiffs, for the salary of acts they serve and commissions they execute; the action of notaries for payment of their acts; the action of doctors, surgeons, dental surgeons, midwives and pharmacists, for their visits, operations and medicines, are prescribed after two years.
f.	The action of lawyers, for payment of their costs and fees, is prescribed after two years, from the judgment of proceedings or the settlement of the parties, or since the revocation of said lawyers. With regard to unfinished matters, they may not make claims for their costs and fees going back more than five years.
g.	Prescription, in the above cases, takes place, even though there has been continuation of supplies, deliveries, services and works.
It ceases to run only when there has been a settled account, note or obligation, or citation in court not lapsed.
h.	Nevertheless, those against whom these prescriptions are raised may defer the oath to those who raise them, on the question of whether the thing has actually been paid.
The oath may be deferred to widows and heirs, or to the guardians of the latter, if they are minors, so that they may declare whether they do not know that the thing is due.

i.	Judges, bailiffs as well as persons who have represented or assisted the parties are discharged from documents five years after the judgment or the cessation of their involvement.
j.	The action of workers for payment of salary, salary accessories, bonuses and allowances of any kind as well as, more generally, any sum due by the employer to the worker, and that for provision of benefits in kind and possibly their reimbursement, are prescribed after one year. Prescription runs from the date from which the salary is payable. It is suspended or interrupted under the conditions provided for in Section III below.

###### Article 2400

All actions, both real and personal, are prescribed after thirty years, without the person alleging this prescription being obliged to produce a title or being able to be met with the exception derived from bad faith.
The thirty-year extinctive prescription established by the preceding paragraph is not applicable to cases where the law sets a shorter period running from the day of knowledge of the fact, act or event.

##### Section III : Des causes qui interrompent ou suspendent la prescription

###### § 1. Des causes qui interrompent le cours de la prescription Article 2401

Prescription is interrupted:
1° When the possessor is deprived for more than one year of the enjoyment of the thing, either by the alleged owner, or even by a third party;
2° By the acknowledgment that the debtor or possessor makes of the right of the person against whom he was prescribing.

###### Article 2402

A legal claim, even in summary proceedings, a formal demand or a seizure, served on the person one wishes to prevent from acquiring by prescription, also interrupts the limitation period as well as the foreclosure period.
The same applies when the legal claim is brought before an incompetent court, or when the summons is void by reason of a defect in form.
The interruption resulting from the legal claim produces its effects until the extinction of the proceedings.

###### Article 2403

The interruption is regarded as void:
-	if the claimant withdraws his claim;
-	if he allows the proceedings to lapse;
-	or if his claim is definitively rejected.

###### Article 2404

The formal demand made to one of the joint and several debtors by a legal claim, or by an act of forced execution, or the acknowledgment by the debtor of the right of the person against whom he was acquiring by prescription, interrupts prescription against all the others, even against their heirs.
On the other hand, the formal demand made to one of the heirs of a joint and several debtor, or the acknowledgment of that heir, does not interrupt prescription with regard to the other co-heirs, even in the case of a mortgage debt, if the obligation is divisible. This formal demand or this acknowledgment interrupts prescription, with regard to the other co-debtors, only for the share for which that heir is liable.
To interrupt prescription for the whole, with regard to the other co-debtors, the formal demand made to all the heirs of the deceased debtor, or the acknowledgment of all those heirs, is required.

###### Article 2405

The formal demand made to the principal debtor, or his acknowledgment, interrupts prescription against the surety.

###### § 2. Des causes qui suspendent le cours de la prescription Article 2406

By way of exception to Article 2395, prescription does not run against a person who cannot validly act, by reason of an impediment resulting from the law, from an agreement, or from force majeure.

###### Article 2407

Prescription does not run against unemancipated minors and adults under guardianship, with the exception of cases determined by law.
Thus and by way of exception, prescription runs against unemancipated minors and adults under guardianship, subject to their recourse against their guardians: prescriptions relating to the payment or recovery of salaries, arrears of annuities, maintenance payments, rents, rental charges, interest on sums lent and, generally, actions for payment of everything that is payable by years or at shorter periodic terms.

###### Article 2408

Prescription does not run between spouses, one against the other.

###### Article 2409

Prescription does not run:
-	with regard to a claim that depends on a condition, until the condition occurs;
-	with regard to an action in warranty, until eviction has taken place;
-	with regard to a claim at a fixed date, until that date has arrived.

###### Article 2410

Prescription does not run against the beneficiary heir, with regard to claims he has against the estate.
On the other hand, it runs against a vacant estate, even in the case where it is not provided with a curator.

###### Article 2411

When the law grants a person a grace period, the prescription of the property and rights concerned is suspended during that legally granted time.

Article final Dispositions transitoires générales

All texts contrary to the provisions of this code are repealed, except when they create texts derogating from common law, in consideration of their field.
References to provisions repealed, amended or moved by this code and contained in provisions of any nature, legislative as well as regulatory, are replaced by references to provisions having the same subject matter.

Contracts and other legal acts that were entered into under the previous code are valid if they complied with the conditions then required.

Prescriptions begun at the time of publication of this code are governed in accordance with the former texts. Nevertheless, prescriptions then begun, and for which, according to the former laws, more than thirty years would still be required from the same time, shall be completed by that period of thirty years, all subject to Article 2400, paragraph 2.

This law shall be executed upon its promulgation.
